The Kid of the Year cover is about an AI tool creator but this does not satisfy the criteria per resolution rules: 'If the cover story is about a specific company or person and discusses AI in the article but the cover text does not explicitly contain Artificial Intelligence or standalone AI, it does not count.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: No explicit evidence confirms a TIME magazine cover published between September 1-October 1, 2025 contains 'Artificial Intelligence' or standalone 'AI' in the cover text. The Kid of the Year cover is about an AI-tool creator (which per resolution criteria would not count unless 'AI' appears explicitly on the cover text itself). No source explicitly confirms this text on the cover. The TIME100 NEXT issue published October 3 is outside the window. Resolution is No as the condition was not met within the window.

question: US x Venezuela military engagement by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. 

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will there be a publicly acknowledged interdiction or boarding by U.S. military or U.S. Coast Guard personnel of a Venezuelan-flagged vessel in the Caribbean Sea between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A useful near-term indicator for direct U.S.–Venezuela military engagement is whether the crisis escalates into hands-on maritime enforcement involving Venezuelan vessels. As of late August 2025, the U.S. had surged naval assets into the Caribbean near Venezuela. Newsweek reported on 2025-08-30 that the U.S. had more than 4,500 personnel in the Southern Caribbean, including multiple destroyers, amphibious ships, a cruiser, and a littoral combat ship, with Coast Guard and law-enforcement detachments embarked for interdiction work: https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-panama-canal-trump-caribbean-buildup-venezuela-2100000 . AFP similarly reported on 2025-08-26 that the U.S. had sent three destroyers and roughly 4,000 Marines to the region, with additional ships inbound: https://www.barrons.com/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-as-us-destroyers-draw-near-c0f9f2d8 .

On the Venezuelan side, AFP reported Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino announced warship and drone patrols, including larger vessels in territorial waters, in response to the U.S. buildup: https://www.barrons.com/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-as-us-destroyers-draw-near-c0f9f2d8 . Newsweek also reported Maduro had denounced the deployment as a threat to sovereignty and announced maritime patrols with drones and naval vessels: https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-panama-canal-trump-caribbean-buildup-venezuela-2100000 .

A boarding/interdiction of a Venezuelan-flagged vessel by U.S. military or Coast Guard personnel would be a concrete, observable escalation in operational friction short of outright bilateral combat. It is distinct from the ultimate question because it does not require an exchange of force between the U.S. and Venezuelan militaries, but it would plausibly increase the chance of such engagement by creating opportunities for confrontation at sea, especially given the stated U.S. counternarcotics mission and Venezuela's announced coastal patrol response.

Sources:
Newsweek - USS Lake Erie crosses Panama Canal as Trump's Caribbean buildup continues - https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-panama-canal-trump-caribbean-buildup-venezuela-2100000
Barron's/AFP - Venezuela deploys warships, drones as US destroyers draw near - https://www.barrons.com/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-as-us-destroyers-draw-near-c0f9f2d8
U.S. Coast Guard - About the U.S. Coast Guard - https://www.uscg.mil/About/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, at least one Venezuelan-flagged vessel is publicly reported by an authoritative source as having been interdicted, boarded, or seized by U.S. military personnel or U.S. Coast Guard personnel in the Caribbean Sea.

For this question:
- "Venezuelan-flagged vessel" means a vessel described in reporting or official statements as registered in Venezuela, sailing under the Venezuelan flag, or explicitly identified as Venezuelan.
- "U.S. military or U.S. Coast Guard personnel" includes the U.S. Navy, U.S. Marine Corps, and U.S. Coast Guard. A boarding by a mixed team counts if U.S. military or Coast Guard personnel are clearly stated to have participated.
- "Publicly acknowledged" means confirmed in at least one official statement from the U.S. government (for example U.S. Southern Command, U.S. Coast Guard, Department of Defense, or Department of Justice) or by at least two independent credible news outlets citing named officials or documentary evidence.
- The incident must occur in the Caribbean Sea; events solely in the Pacific, Atlantic outside the Caribbean, or inland waters do not count.
- Mere shadowing, hailing, warnings, overflight, or attempted approaches without an actual boarding/interdiction/seizure do not count.
- Boarding by non-U.S. partner states without U.S. personnel physically participating does not count.
- If a qualifying incident allegedly occurs within the window but is not publicly acknowledged until later, it still counts, provided the reporting clearly states the interdiction/boarding itself occurred between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.
- If reporting is too ambiguous to determine whether the vessel was Venezuelan-flagged, whether U.S. personnel physically participated, or whether the event occurred within the window, the question should resolve No unless later clarification from an authoritative source settles the ambiguity before final resolution.

Primary resolution sources:
- U.S. Coast Guard news releases: https://www.news.uscg.mil/
- U.S. Southern Command news: https://www.southcom.mil/MEDIA/NEWS-ARTICLES/
- U.S. Department of Defense news: https://www.defense.gov/News/
- U.S. Department of Justice press releases: https://www.justice.gov/news

Secondary sources for corroboration if needed:
- Reuters World News: https://www.reuters.com/world/
- Associated Press Latin America: https://apnews.com/hub/latin-america
- AFP English feed via major syndicators such as Barron's: https://www.barrons.com/

If no qualifying interdiction/boarding/seizure is publicly acknowledged as specified above for the period between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A U.S. boarding or interdiction of a Venezuelan-flagged vessel would be a strong operational escalation that increases opportunities for Venezuelan military intervention, retaliation, or miscalculation. It is a meaningful early indicator of whether the maritime standoff is moving from signaling into direct encounters, without merely restating the ultimate engagement question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A Venezuelan-flagged vessel explicitly boarded/interdicted/seized by U.S. military or Coast Guard personnel in the Caribbean Sea between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive. Must be publicly acknowledged by at least one U.S. government official statement OR two independent credible outlets citing named officials or documentary evidence. The boarding must be physical (not mere shadowing/hailing), in the Caribbean Sea.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'US Coast Guard Venezuelan vessel interdiction boarding Caribbean 2025' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01) — to find direct incidents. Query 2: 'US military boarding seizure Venezuelan ship Caribbean Sea September 2025' — to find any military-led boarding. Query 3: 'USS Jason Dunham Venezuelan fishing boat boarding September 12 13 2025 Coast Guard' — to confirm specific incident details. Query 4: 'US Southern Command Coast Guard Venezuelan vessel interdiction September 2025 official statement' — to find U.S. official acknowledgment. Query 5: 'Venezuelan flagged fishing boat boarded US Navy Caribbean interdiction drugs found none September 2025' — to confirm the vessel's nationality and find the first occurrence.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) September 12-13, 2025 — U.S. Coast Guard law enforcement detachment aboard USS Jason Dunham boarded Venezuelan tuna fishing vessel in the Caribbean Sea. Confirmed by U.S. official via ABC News, AP, CBS News, Yahoo, KAKE, The Hindu, and Venezuela's Foreign Ministry with video/photo evidence. (2) September 2, 2025 — lethal kinetic strike on alleged Venezuelan drug vessel killing 11 — REJECTED as it was a kinetic strike, not an interdiction/boarding/seizure as required by criteria. (3) September 15 and September 19-20 strikes — REJECTED as lethal strikes, not boardings. The September 12-13 incident is the qualifying event.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Venezuelan-flagged vessel: The tuna fishing vessel was explicitly identified as Venezuelan, carrying nine Venezuelan fishermen with Venezuelan Ministry of Fisheries authorization — confirmed by [AP](https://apnews.com/article/venezuela-united-states-warship-fishermen-e08c3abde034df0f50c1ea66dff7718b) and [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/venezuela-accuses-u-s-of-seizing-fishing-boat-in-caribbean/). U.S. Coast Guard personnel: A U.S. official told ABC News (via [Yahoo](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/us-official-says-personnel-navy-235742615.html) and [KAKE](https://www.kake.com/news/us-official-says-personnel-from-navy-ship-inspected-venezuelan-fishing-boat-for-drugs/)): 'The law enforcement detachment aboard the destroyer boarded the Venezuelan craft and carried out a search that turned up no drugs.' The [Fox News/Pentagon statement](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/us-bolsters-military-presence-caribbean-near-venezuela-amid-trumps-efforts-halt-drug-trafficking) confirmed destroyers had 'embarked U.S. Coast Guard Law Enforcement Detachment teams' and [USNI News](https://news.usni.org/2025/09/09/coast-guard-caribbean-anti-trafficking-missions-continue-as-militarys-role-is-redefined) confirmed Coast Guard LEDETs aboard warships. Caribbean Sea location: 48 nautical miles northeast of La Blanquilla Island (Venezuelan Caribbean coast), explicitly in Caribbean. Physical boarding: 18 armed personnel boarded vessel for ~8 hours — confirmed by both sides. Public acknowledgment: U.S. official (via ABC News/multiple outlets) + Venezuela's Foreign Minister with documentary evidence (video/photos).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The incident occurred on September 12, 2025 (a Friday per Venezuela's 'Friday' reference), with Venezuela's Foreign Ministry announcement on September 13, 2025. U.S. official confirmation via ABC News cited in articles dated September 13-14, 2025. Both the event date and public acknowledgment are within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window. The earliest reliable timestamp of the event is 2025-09-12, with acknowledgment by 2025-09-13.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The September 12-13, 2025 boarding is the first documented boarding/interdiction qualifying event within the window. The September 2 strike (first kinetic strike) was a lethal air/military strike, not a boarding/interdiction. No earlier boarding of a Venezuelan-flagged vessel by U.S. Coast Guard or military within the window has been found.
evidence.step7_verification: Both the U.S. (via unnamed official to ABC News) and Venezuela (via Foreign Minister Yván Gil with video/photo evidence) confirm the boarding occurred. The U.S. side disputes the location (says international waters vs. Venezuela's EEZ claim) but does NOT dispute that the boarding happened — only its legal justification. Multiple independent credible sources (AP, CBS News, Yahoo/Reuters, KAKE/ABC News, The Hindu, USNI News) confirm the event. No contradictory evidence exists disputing that a boarding physically occurred. The vessel is explicitly described as Venezuelan throughout all reporting.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: YES. On September 12, 2025, a U.S. Coast Guard law enforcement detachment (LEDET) embarked on USS Jason Dunham (DDG-109) boarded a Venezuelan tuna fishing vessel in the Caribbean Sea. This was explicitly confirmed by a U.S. official speaking to ABC News (cited in multiple credible outlets including KAKE and Yahoo/Reuters), and by Venezuela's Foreign Minister Yván Gil with documentary evidence (video/photos). The vessel was explicitly identified as Venezuelan. The event occurred in the Caribbean Sea within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window. All resolution criteria are satisfied: Venezuelan vessel, U.S. Coast Guard personnel physically boarded, Caribbean location, and public acknowledgment via multiple credible sources citing named officials and documentary evidence.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla publicly announce, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 inclusive, that its Austin Robotaxi service has opened to the general public rather than remaining invite-only or limited to testers?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term crux for whether Tesla will launch a qualifying driverless Robotaxi service by October 31 is whether Tesla first broadens access from its current limited pilot to the general public. Multiple pre-September reports say Tesla's Austin Robotaxi service exists but is not yet a fully open public service. ABC7 reported on 2025-08-18 that Tesla had launched a robotaxi pilot in Austin on 2025-06-22, but that it was invite-only, geographically limited, and used a front-seat safety monitor rather than fully driverless operation: https://abc7news.com/post/how-mercedes-benz-beat-tesla-become-1st-offer-level-3-autonomous-personal-car-driverless-tomorrow/17025582/ . GuruFocus similarly reported on 2025-08-22 that Tesla's Austin robotaxi pilot had a limited fleet and small user base, and cited Elon Musk saying the service was slated to open to the public in September: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3013882/barclays-expects-long-approval-process-for-teslas-tsla-robotaxi . Tesla North also reported on 2025-08-21 that the Austin robotaxi beta would open to the general public in September: https://teslanorth.com/2025/08/21/tesla-hints-at-chicago-robotaxi-launch-with-new-job-listings/ . NewsBytes likewise summarized Musk as confirming a public rollout in September: https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/science/musk-confirms-tesla-robotaxi-rollout-for-the-public-in-september/story .

This is informative because an open-to-general-public announcement would be a concrete commercialization step that plausibly precedes, and may be necessary for, any later qualifying fully driverless public service. It is not the same as the ultimate question: the service could open to the public while still using a safety monitor or other non-qualifying supervision, but such an opening would still be evidence that Tesla is operationalizing and scaling the product.

Sources:
ABC7 San Francisco - How Mercedes-Benz beat Tesla to become 1st to offer level 3 autonomous personal car: https://abc7news.com/post/how-mercedes-benz-beat-tesla-become-1st-offer-level-3-autonomous-personal-car-driverless-tomorrow/17025582/
GuruFocus - Barclays Expects Long Approval Process for Tesla's Robotaxi: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3013882/barclays-expects-long-approval-process-for-teslas-tsla-robotaxi
Tesla North - Tesla Hints at Chicago Robotaxi Launch with New Job Listings: https://teslanorth.com/2025/08/21/tesla-hints-at-chicago-robotaxi-launch-with-new-job-listings/
NewsBytes - Musk confirms Tesla robotaxi rollout for the public in September: https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/science/musk-confirms-tesla-robotaxi-rollout-for-the-public-in-september/story
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 inclusive, Tesla publicly states that the Austin Robotaxi service is open to members of the general public, meaning access is no longer restricted solely to employees, invite-only users, closed-beta testers, or similar limited cohorts.

Qualifying evidence must come from at least one of the following publicly accessible sources dated within the window 2025-09-01 through 2025-09-08: (a) an official Tesla post or page, including Tesla's website or newsroom (https://www.tesla.com/ , https://www.tesla.com/blog ); (b) a public statement from Elon Musk or Tesla on X that explicitly says the Austin service is now open to the public (https://x.com/elonmusk , https://x.com/Tesla ); or (c) at least two independent reputable news reports published during the window that quote or document Tesla making such an announcement.

The announcement must specifically concern Austin, Texas. Statements merely saying Tesla hopes, plans, or expects to open later do not count. Reports that the service remains invite-only, requires a code, or is limited to a waitlist/test cohort do not count as Yes. Whether the service is fully driverless is irrelevant for this subquestion.

If by 2025-09-08 23:59:59 UTC no such public announcement is available, resolve No.

If the relevant official source is deleted or inaccessible, archived copies and contemporaneous reporting from Reuters or other major outlets may be used as fallback evidence. Suggested resolution sources include Tesla official pages (https://www.tesla.com/), Tesla on X (https://x.com/Tesla), Elon Musk on X (https://x.com/elonmusk), and Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/).
subquestions.rationale: Opening Austin Robotaxi access to the general public is a meaningful operational and commercial milestone distinct from the ultimate question. If Tesla cannot even broaden access beyond a limited pilot by early September, that is negative evidence for a qualifying driverless public launch by late October. If it does broaden access, that materially increases the plausibility of later removing the remaining supervision constraints.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Tesla must publicly announce between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 that the Austin Robotaxi service is open to the GENERAL PUBLIC — not invite-only, not limited to testers, and NOT limited to a waitlist/test cohort. Observable evidence: official Tesla post/page, Elon Musk or Tesla on X, or at least two independent reputable news reports. Key exclusion in resolution criteria: 'Reports that the service remains invite-only, requires a code, or is limited to a waitlist/test cohort do not count as Yes.'
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Tesla Austin Robotaxi open general public September 2025' — to find direct announcements within window. Query 2: 'Tesla Cybercab robotaxi Austin Texas public launch 2025' — to find launch reporting. Query 3: 'Tesla Robotaxi X post now available to all September 4 2025' — to verify official Tesla X statement. Query 4: 'Tesla Robotaxi waitlist public open announcement Austin September 2025' — to identify whether waitlist requirement disqualifies the announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: On September 4, 2025, Tesla posted on X: 'Robotaxi app now available to all. Download to join waitlist -- expanding access soon.' This was widely reported by Forbes, San Jose Mercury News, Business Insider, Electrek, CNET, Engadget, PCMag, Investing.com, Teslarati, Tech Times, and others. The app was released on the Apple App Store for iOS, allowing any iPhone user (18+) to download and join a waitlist. Multiple sources confirm a waitlist is still required before rides can be booked. Some sources note users were admitted from the waitlist within hours (Business Insider reported ~3 hours). Forbes titled their article 'Tesla Robotaxi Is Now Open To All In Austin.' However, Electrek explicitly noted the service 'remains limited' despite the announcement. PCMag headline stated the app 'only does one thing' — join a waitlist. Key candidate event: Tesla's X post on Sep 4 saying app is 'now available to all' — but the same post explicitly directs users to join a waitlist.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: CRITICAL DISQUALIFIER: The resolution criteria explicitly states 'Reports that the service remains invite-only, requires a code, or is limited to a waitlist/test cohort do not count as Yes.' Multiple reputable sources explicitly confirm: (1) [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/tesla-releases-robotaxi-app-waitlist-open-to-everyone-2025-9): Tesla's X post said 'Robotaxi app now available to all. Download to join waitlist'; (2) [Electrek](https://electrek.co/2025/09/04/tesla-robotaxi-anyone-with-iphone-can-now-download-app-join-waitlist/): 'all iPhone users in the United States can download the Tesla Robotaxi app, which only allows users to join a waitlist'; (3) [PCMag](https://pcmag.com/news/you-can-now-download-the-tesla-robotaxi-app-but-it-only-does-one-thing): 'the application's sole function is to allow them to join a waitlist'; (4) [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/transportation/evs/anyone-can-now-download-teslas-ios-robotaxi-app-but-theres-still-a-waitlist-165523028.html): 'Anyone can now download Tesla's iOS Robotaxi app, but there's still a waitlist.' While Forbes headlined 'Tesla Robotaxi Is Now Open To All In Austin,' the article itself describes a waitlist mechanism. Tesla's own announcement explicitly directs users to 'join waitlist.' The service did not announce unrestricted access — it announced open waitlist enrollment with 'expanding access soon.' Under the resolution criteria, a waitlist-based system does not qualify as 'open to members of the general public' where 'access is no longer restricted solely to employees, invite-only users, closed-beta testers, or similar limited cohorts.' The waitlist is itself a form of limited/cohort-based access.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Tesla's X post was published on September 4, 2025. Multiple articles dated September 4, 2025 corroborate this. Exact timestamp of the X post is not available from the search results, but the date September 4, 2025 is confirmed by multiple independent sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence exists within the window (Sep 1-8). The Sep 4 announcement is the only candidate event. No evidence of an unrestricted public opening without a waitlist requirement was found.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Forbes used the framing 'Open To All In Austin' but described a waitlist. The resolution criteria explicitly excludes waitlist-based access from qualifying as 'open to the general public.' Multiple sources consistently confirm the waitlist requirement remained in place on and after September 4. No source indicates Tesla removed the waitlist requirement and offered completely open booking within the Sep 1-8 window. The question's resolution criteria is unambiguous on this point: 'Reports that the service remains invite-only, requires a code, or is limited to a waitlist/test cohort do not count as Yes.' The waitlist is a form of limited access — the resolution criteria treats such access control mechanisms as disqualifying.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Tesla made a significant announcement on September 4, 2025 opening the Robotaxi app to all iPhone users for waitlist signup. However, the resolution criteria explicitly excludes waitlist-based access. Tesla's own announcement directed users to 'join waitlist' rather than immediately book rides. Multiple reputable news sources confirm the waitlist requirement persisted throughout the window. Therefore, Tesla did not publicly announce that the Austin Robotaxi service was 'open to members of the general public' in the sense required by the resolution criteria — the service remained accessible only through a waitlist mechanism, which is 'a similar limited cohort' type of access restriction. Resolution: No.

question: OpenAI browser by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI publicly releases a standalone web browser that is intended for general web browsing and is available for use by the public in at least one country or region by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes," such a browser must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling free waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by OpenAI as being accessible to the general public.

Browser extensions, plugins, or integrations within third-party browsers do not count; it must be a standalone browser application.

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from OpenAI. If there is ambiguity, a consensus of credible reporting will be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, a beta, preview, or waitlist for a new standalone desktop or mobile application explicitly described as a web browser or as being built for general web browsing?
subquestions.background_information:
A public browser launch by OpenAI by late October would likely be preceded by an earlier observable commitment signal: a public beta, preview, or waitlist announcement for a standalone browser product. This is distinct from the ultimate question because it asks about an earlier product-stage milestone rather than full public release.

There is relevant competitive pressure in the market. Perplexity has already launched an agentic browser, Comet, in July 2025, according to Windows Central, and the article also notes OpenAI as a rumored entrant alongside other AI-browser efforts: https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/let-me-scam-that-for-you. Anthropic has also moved toward browser-use products, though via a Chrome extension in closed beta rather than a standalone browser; ZDNet reported this on 2025-08-28: https://www.zdnet.com/article/anthropics-claude-chrome-browser-extension-rolls-out-how-to-get-early-access/.

Meanwhile, OpenAI has recently been shipping more end-user and developer-facing products at a rapid cadence. Reporting on late-August releases describes OpenAI expanding Codex into IDEs and GitHub workflows (WinBuzzer, 2025-08-28): https://winbuzzer.com/2025/08/28/openai-supercharges-codex-ai-coding-agent-with-ide-integration-gpt-5-power-and-github-reviews-xcxwbn/ and making its Realtime API generally available for voice agents (PYMNTS, 2025-08-28): https://www.pymnts.com/artificial-intelligence-2/2025/openai-says-new-speech-to-speech-model-designed-for-customer-support/. This recent launch tempo makes a browser-related preview or waitlist a plausible near-term leading indicator if a full browser release is coming by October.

The threshold here is meaningful because a public browser beta/preview/waitlist announcement would indicate that OpenAI has progressed beyond rumor into public go-to-market execution. At the same time, it is not so strong as to merely restate the ultimate question: Open beta, preview, or waitlist status can happen without a general-public browser becoming available by the final deadline.

Sources:
Windows Central - Let me scam that for you. https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/let-me-scam-that-for-you
ZDNet - Anthropic's Claude Chrome browser extension rolls out - how to get early access. https://www.zdnet.com/article/anthropics-claude-chrome-browser-extension-rolls-out-how-to-get-early-access/
WinBuzzer - OpenAI Supercharges Codex AI Coding Agent With IDE Integration, GPT-5 Power, and GitHub Reviews. https://winbuzzer.com/2025/08/28/openai-supercharges-codex-ai-coding-agent-with-ide-integration-gpt-5-power-and-github-reviews-xcxwbn/
PYMNTS - OpenAI Says New Speech-to-Speech Model Designed for Customer Support. https://www.pymnts.com/artificial-intelligence-2/2025/openai-says-new-speech-to-speech-model-designed-for-customer-support/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), OpenAI makes a public announcement of a new product that satisfies all of the following:
1. The product is a standalone software application (desktop and/or mobile app), not merely a browser extension, plugin, SDK, API, feature inside ChatGPT, or integration within a third-party browser.
2. OpenAI explicitly describes it as a "browser," "web browser," or as a product intended for general web browsing.
3. OpenAI publicly announces that the product is available via a beta, preview, or waitlist open to the general public in at least one country or region.

This question resolves No if no such announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

Closed betas, invite-only private tests, leaked builds, job postings, code references, or credible media reports without a public OpenAI announcement do not count. Browser extensions or in-browser assistants do not count. If OpenAI announces only an API, operator, or browsing feature within ChatGPT, that does not count.

Primary source: official OpenAI communication channels, including the OpenAI blog/newsroom and official OpenAI X/Twitter or other verified company accounts.
- OpenAI News: https://openai.com/news/
- OpenAI Blog index: https://openai.com/blog/
- OpenAI X account: https://x.com/OpenAI

If there is ambiguity about whether the product is standalone or intended for general web browsing, a consensus of at least two credible technology outlets may be used as secondary evidence, provided they are clearly interpreting an official OpenAI announcement rather than rumor. Examples of secondary sources include The Verge (https://www.theverge.com/), TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/), and Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/).

If OpenAI announces such a product during the window but states that public beta/preview/waitlist access will begin only after 2025-10-01, this question resolves No. If the announcement is made within the window and public beta/preview/waitlist access is stated to be open immediately within the window, it resolves Yes.
subquestions.rationale: A public beta/preview/waitlist announcement for a standalone browser is a strong leading indicator that OpenAI is serious about a browser launch and has advanced far enough in productization, branding, and distribution to make the ultimate October release more likely. It is also not just the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, because it concerns an earlier-stage public commitment rather than public availability of the browser itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: OpenAI must make a public announcement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 of a new standalone desktop/mobile application explicitly described as a 'browser' or 'web browser' for general web browsing, with a beta/preview/waitlist open to the general public. Observable evidence: Official OpenAI blog/newsroom post, verified OpenAI social media post, or consensus of at least two credible tech outlets interpreting an official OpenAI announcement — specifically announcing beta/preview/waitlist access. Key thresholds: Must be standalone (not extension/plugin/ChatGPT feature), explicitly called browser/web browser, with open public access starting within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'OpenAI web browser standalone application announcement 2025' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01) — to find direct browser product announcements; 2) 'OpenAI browser beta preview waitlist launch' (same period) — to find beta/preview/waitlist access announcements; 3) 'OpenAI AI-powered browser announcement release date 2025' (broader window Aug-Oct) — to find any browser-specific announcements; 4) 'OpenAI browser Fidji Simo Sam Altman plans web browsing' — to find any browser-specific news; 5) 'OpenAI browser product launch beta public October 2025' and '"OpenAI browser" OR "OpenAI web browser" announcement 2025' — to find specific product launch news.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (A) Multiple sources (TechCrunch Sept 4, India Today Sept 5, SF Gate Sept 5, etc.) report Sam Altman mentioning browser as one of 'other forthcoming applications' Fidji Simo will oversee — alongside the Jobs Platform announcement. This is a passing reference to a future plan, not a browser product launch. (B) Computerworld (Sept 18) roundup states OpenAI 'announced a new AI-powered browser' but this appears to be summary of prior reports/plans without a direct link to a new product announcement. (C) americanbazaaronline.com (Sept 30) mentions 'upcoming OpenAI Chromium-based AI browser' — indicating the browser was still forthcoming as of September 30. (D) TechCrunch (Sept 30) comprehensive ChatGPT summary says 'OpenAI is developing an AI-powered web browser' — confirming it was still in development, not yet launched. All browser references were rejected as not satisfying resolution criteria: they were future plans, background references, or not standalone browser beta/preview/waitlist launches.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of: (1) A standalone browser product (not extension/plugin), (2) explicitly described as 'browser'/'web browser', (3) with a public beta/preview/waitlist announced within the window. The Sam Altman/Fidji Simo references to a browser are forward-looking statements about planned future applications, not an announcement of a product with public access. The Computerworld reference is a roundup of general OpenAI activities, not a specific new browser launch announcement. TechCrunch's Sept 30 comprehensive guide confirms the browser was still 'in development' as of end of window. Opera's Neon browser launch (Sept 30) specifically references OpenAI's browser as a competitor that is still 'upcoming,' confirming no OpenAI browser launched during the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying event occurred. The browser references are future plans without launch dates within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying occurrence was found at all within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked: (1) TechCrunch Sept 30 comprehensive ChatGPT guide explicitly states OpenAI is 'developing' a browser (present continuous, not past completed) — confirming no browser was launched by end of window. (2) americanbazaaronline.com Sept 30 explicitly refers to OpenAI's browser as 'upcoming' in comparison to Opera Neon. (3) Sora 2 social app launched Sept 30 is a social video platform, not a web browser. (4) All other OpenAI launches during this period (ChatGPT Pulse, Developer Mode MCP, teen-safe ChatGPT, Grove, Jobs Platform) are clearly not web browsers. No contradictory evidence found — all sources consistently indicate OpenAI's browser was planned but not yet released during the September 1 to October 1, 2025 window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. During the window 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01, OpenAI made no public announcement of a standalone web browser product with a beta, preview, or waitlist for public access. Multiple sources confirm the browser was still being developed and planned (with Sam Altman mentioning it as a future application), but no actual product launch or public access announcement was made. The window closed with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: Will Iran close the Strait of Hormuz before 2027?
description:
If Iran halts or severely restricts international maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official governmental information, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) or Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) issue a new advisory between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 reporting a threat, attack, boarding, detention, mine risk, or official warning specifically affecting commercial vessel transit in or immediately adjacent to the Strait of Hormuz?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term precursor to an actual closure of the Strait of Hormuz would likely be a sharp deterioration in the maritime security environment, reflected in official or industry security advisories to shipping. Iran has a long history of ship seizures, harassment, and threats in Gulf waters. The U.S. Energy Information Administration says roughly 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption moved through the Strait of Hormuz in 2024, making it one of the world's most important energy chokepoints: https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=65764 . Reuters and other outlets reported in June 2025 that heightened U.S.-Iran tensions were already causing some operators to reduce transits, while shipping groups warned that any Iranian retaliation against vessels would likely reduce traffic further: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-iran-tensions-slow-tanker-traffic-through-strait-hormuz-trade-group-2025-06-23/ . Reports in June 2025 also stated that Iran's parliament had approved or backed a measure to close the Strait, though implementation would require action by higher authorities such as the Supreme National Security Council; this indicates that closure rhetoric had already moved beyond mere speculation: https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/iran-approves-closure-of-oil-corridor-strait-of-hormuz-after-us-strikes-report-2745323-2025-06-22 and https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/us-strikes-on-iran-tehrans-top-security-council-to-decide-on-strait-of-hormuz-closure-after-parliamentary-nod/articleshow/122013935.cms . Official maritime warning channels are therefore useful leading indicators: if they begin reporting new threats or incidents specifically tied to Hormuz transit, that would materially raise the probability of an eventual Iranian restriction or closure attempt. UKMTO publishes notices to merchant shipping in the Middle East region: https://www.ukmto.org/ . JMIC, based in Bahrain, publishes regional maritime security advisories for commercial shipping: https://www.jmic-bahrain.com/ .

Sources:
U.S. EIA Today in Energy — World oil transit chokepoints / Strait of Hormuz https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=65764
Reuters — US-Iran tensions slow tanker traffic through Strait of Hormuz: trade group https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-iran-tensions-slow-tanker-traffic-through-strait-hormuz-trade-group-2025-06-23/
India Today — Iran approves closure of oil corridor, Strait of Hormuz, after US strikes: Report https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/iran-approves-closure-of-oil-corridor-strait-hormuz-after-us-strikes-report-2745323-2025-06-22
Times of India — Tehran's top security council to decide on Strait of Hormuz closure after parliamentary nod https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/us-strikes-on-iran-tehrans-top-security-council-to-decide-on-strait-of-hormuz-closure-after-parliamentary-nod/articleshow/122013935.cms
UKMTO official site https://www.ukmto.org/
JMIC official site https://www.jmic-bahrain.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 (inclusive), either UKMTO or JMIC publishes at least one new advisory, warning, incident bulletin, or notice that explicitly refers to commercial vessel transit in the Strait of Hormuz (or the Hormuz Traffic Separation Scheme / approaches immediately adjacent to the Strait) and states one or more of the following: (a) a threat or attack against a merchant/commercial vessel; (b) boarding, seizure, detention, or harassment of a merchant/commercial vessel; (c) a mine, explosive, missile, drone, or similar kinetic risk to commercial navigation; or (d) an official warning that commercial vessels should avoid, delay, or exercise exceptional caution specifically when transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying UKMTO or JMIC publication appears during the window from 2025-11-06 through 2025-12-06 inclusive.

Resolution should use the official UKMTO alerts/news page and official JMIC advisories archive as primary sources: https://www.ukmto.org/ and https://www.jmic-bahrain.com/ . If one site is unavailable at resolution time, archived copies on the organization's official social channels or the Internet Archive may be used to verify publication timing and contents. General regional advisories that mention the Gulf, Arabian Sea, or Red Sea without specifically affecting transit in or immediately adjacent to the Strait of Hormuz do not count. Advisories first published before 2025-11-06 do not count, even if still active during the window. If an incident occurs during the window but is not publicly reported by UKMTO or JMIC until after 2025-12-06, it does not count. If publication dates cannot be established from official pages or reliable archives, the question should resolve as unresolvable rather than inferred from secondary media alone.
subquestions.rationale: A formal maritime security warning specific to Hormuz transit would be a strong early signal that conditions are moving from rhetorical threats toward operational disruption. Such advisories often precede or accompany reductions in tanker traffic, spikes in insurance costs, and naval incidents, all of which are meaningful indicators for the ultimate question of whether Iran will actually attempt to close or severely restrict passage through the Strait.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: UKMTO or JMIC publishes a new advisory between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06, explicitly referring to commercial vessel transit in or adjacent to the Strait of Hormuz, and stating a threat/attack, boarding/seizure/detention, kinetic risk, or warning to exercise exceptional caution. Observable evidence: Official UKMTO/JMIC advisory publication with explicit Hormuz reference and qualifying content within the window. Key entities: UKMTO, JMIC, Strait of Hormuz, commercial vessels. Threshold: At least one qualifying advisory.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'UKMTO advisory Strait of Hormuz commercial vessel 2025' (Nov 6–Dec 6) — to find UKMTO publications; 2) 'JMIC advisory Strait of Hormuz warning November December 2025' — to find JMIC publications; 3) 'Strait of Hormuz attack threat commercial shipping November 2025' — to find incidents; 4) 'UKMTO advisory warning Talara tanker seizure state activity November 14 2025' — to find specific advisory details; 5) 'UKMTO transit caution suspicious activity Strait Hormuz November 2025' — to confirm warning language; 6) 'Iran December 2025 tanker seizure Eswatini UKMTO advisory' — to check for December incidents; 7) 'UKMTO JMIC advisory Hormuz commercial vessel December 2025' — to check for other qualifying events.
evidence.step3_event_detection: PRIMARY CANDIDATE: On November 14, 2025, UKMTO issued an advisory/warning regarding the seizure of the Marshall Islands-flagged commercial tanker Talara while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz. UKMTO described the incident as 'state activity' and 'suspicious activity,' and urged nearby vessels to 'transit with caution and report any suspicious activity.' This is confirmed by AP, AFP, Anadolu Agency, Al Jazeera, New York Post, USNI News, Times of Israel, and many other credible sources published on November 14–15, 2025. SECONDARY CANDIDATE: December 1, 2025 — Iran seized an Eswatini-flagged vessel near the Strait of Hormuz/Persian Gulf, but no UKMTO advisory is explicitly mentioned in available sources for this event. DECEMBER 5 CANDIDATE: UKMTO issued a warning about a vessel under fire off Yemen (Bab el-Mandeb/Red Sea area) — this does not qualify as it is not the Strait of Hormuz.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The November 14, 2025 UKMTO advisory EXACTLY matches the resolution criteria: (1) UKMTO issued the advisory — confirmed by [AP](https://apnews.com/article/iran-tanker-mideast-tensions-1762f491e9eb1912cb8b8bd9a1a634d8), [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/83ZR4T3), [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/uk-maritime-trade-operations-reports-suspicious-incident-near-uae-coast/3743972), [USNI News](https://news.usni.org/2025/11/17/iran-strait-of-hormuz-tanker-seizure-violates-international-law-centcom-says), [New York Post](https://nypost.com/2025/11/15/world-news/iran-says-it-seized-oil-tanker-in-strait-of-hormuz-as-us-drone-watched/); (2) The advisory explicitly refers to commercial vessel transit in the Strait of Hormuz — the Talara was 'transiting southbound through the Strait of Hormuz' per multiple sources, and UKMTO received an alert '20 nautical miles east of Khor Fakkan'; (3) The advisory states boarding/seizure/detention of a commercial vessel (criterion b) — UKMTO described it as 'state activity' forcing the tanker into Iranian waters, and the vessel was boarded by IRGC forces per CENTCOM; (4) UKMTO warned vessels to 'transit with caution and report any suspicious activity' — per New York Post and Newsbase — satisfying criterion (d); (5) Published November 14, 2025 — within the window 2025-11-06 to 2025-12-06.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Publication date: November 14, 2025. Multiple sources published November 14, 2025 confirm UKMTO issued its advisory on that date. The AFP article (doc.afp.com/83ZR4T3) and AP article (apnews.com) were both published November 14, 2025, reporting UKMTO's advisory as a concurrent event. Anadolu Agency also published on November 14, 2025. Exact UTC time not available from news articles, but multiple sources confirm publication on November 14, 2025 — within the resolution window. Resolution datetime = 2025-11-14T00:00:00Z (earliest confirmed date, exact intra-day time not separately determinable but same-day confirmation by multiple sources is sufficient).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The November 14, 2025 UKMTO advisory is the first qualifying occurrence within the window (2025-11-06 to 2025-12-06). No earlier qualifying UKMTO/JMIC advisory within the window has been identified. The question window starts November 6, 2025, and no events between November 6–13 were identified in the searches.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) No evidence found that UKMTO did NOT issue this advisory — to the contrary, 10+ high-quality sources confirm it did. (2) No evidence that the advisory was issued before November 6, 2025 (which would exclude it). (3) The location (Strait of Hormuz / immediately adjacent) is confirmed — the vessel was transiting southbound through the Strait of Hormuz, with the final alert location 20 nautical miles east of Khor Fakkan (in the approaches/Hormuz Traffic Separation Scheme zone). (4) The vessel type is confirmed commercial (oil tanker). (5) The December 5 UKMTO advisory about gunfire off Yemen relates to Bab el-Mandeb/Red Sea, not the Strait of Hormuz — does not qualify. (6) The December 1 Iran seizure of Eswatini vessel does not appear to have a specific UKMTO advisory attached in available sources, but is irrelevant since the November 14 event already qualifies.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution = Yes. On November 14, 2025, UKMTO issued an advisory about the seizure/boarding of the commercial tanker Talara while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, describing the incident as 'state activity' and urging vessels to 'transit with caution and report any suspicious activity.' This explicitly meets resolution criteria (b) [boarding/seizure of a commercial vessel] and (d) [official warning that commercial vessels should exercise exceptional caution when transiting the Strait of Hormuz]. The publication date (November 14, 2025) is within the resolution window. Evidence is direct, explicit, and confirmed by 10+ high-quality independent sources.

question: Will Wicked: For Good be the top grossing movie of 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the "Gross" column on https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses shows 'Wicked: For Good' (2025) as the film with the highest 2025 gross once data for December 31 is made available. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

In the event of an exact tie the film that comes first alphabetically will be considered the winner.

subquestions.question: Will Fandango list "Wicked: For Good" among its top 3 best-selling movies by weekly ticket pre-sales at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
A strong early indicator for whether "Wicked: For Good" can become the top-grossing domestic calendar-release title of 2025 is unusually strong advance ticket demand well before release. The film is scheduled for U.S. theatrical release on November 21, 2025, giving it only about six weeks of domestic calendar gross in 2025; to finish #1 for the year despite that late release, it likely needs exceptional opening-weekend demand and strong pre-release momentum. Universal and trade coverage have highlighted high audience interest: the first trailer reportedly drew 113 million views in its first 24 hours, exceeding the first film's trailer according to coverage citing Universal, and the original "Wicked" was a major theatrical success with about $756 million worldwide and around $473 million domestic according to Box Office Mojo and related reporting. See Box Office Mojo for the first film's grosses: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt1262426/ and reporting on trailer interest: https://www.cbr.com/wicked-for-good-trailer-record/. Fandango regularly publishes weekly "best-selling tickets" rankings for upcoming films, which are widely cited as a public readout of near-term consumer demand: https://www.fandango.com/movie-news.

Because the ultimate market is about domestic calendar gross in 2025, a subquestion about whether the sequel reaches a very high pre-sales ranking during September would be informative: if it cannot crack the top tier of Fandango pre-sales before October, that would be some evidence against an extraordinary late-year domestic run; if it does, that supports the view that the film could open at a level needed to challenge the year's leaders.

Sources:
Box Office Mojo - Wicked (2024): https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt1262426/
CBR - Wicked: For Good Has Already Beaten the First Movie in 1 Major Way Months Ahead of Release: https://www.cbr.com/wicked-for-good-trailer-record/
Fandango Movie News: https://www.fandango.com/movie-news
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Fandango publishes a weekly "best-selling tickets" or equivalent weekly ticket pre-sales ranking for movies and "Wicked: For Good" appears in the top 3 positions on that published ranking.

Primary source for resolution: Fandango's Movie News pages and articles containing weekly best-selling ticket rankings: https://www.fandango.com/movie-news

Resolution steps:
1. Review Fandango articles published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive for weekly best-selling ticket rankings.
2. If any such article explicitly lists "Wicked: For Good" in 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place, resolve Yes.
3. If no qualifying Fandango weekly ranking published in that window places the film in the top 3, resolve No.

Definitions and edge cases:
- "Wicked: For Good" includes clearly equivalent formatting of the title used by Fandango, so long as it unambiguously refers to the 2025 Universal theatrical release.
- "Weekly ticket pre-sales ranking" means a Fandango-published ranking described as weekly best-selling tickets, top advance ticket sellers, or a substantially equivalent recurring weekly chart of ticket sales on Fandango. One-off editorial lists, fan polls, or trailer-popularity lists do not count.
- If Fandango publishes multiple qualifying weekly rankings in the window, any one of them with the film in the top 3 is sufficient for Yes.
- If a relevant Fandango page is unavailable at resolution time, archived copies from the Internet Archive may be used to verify the original Fandango publication date and ranking: https://web.archive.org/ .
- If no qualifying weekly ranking is published by Fandango at all between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, resolve No rather than unresolvable, because the condition did not occur within the window.

Fallback sources for corroboration only (not primary unless Fandango pages are inaccessible): press articles that directly quote or reproduce the relevant Fandango weekly ranking, such as Deadline https://deadline.com/ or Variety https://variety.com/ .
subquestions.rationale: A late-November release can only top the domestic 2025 calendar chart if it behaves like an event movie. Reaching Fandango's top 3 weekly pre-sales rankings in September would be an early, externally visible signal of unusually strong audience demand and opening-weekend potential, which materially bears on the ultimate question without merely restating year-end box office performance.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Fandango publishes a weekly 'best-selling tickets' or equivalent weekly ticket pre-sales ranking between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, with 'Wicked: For Good' in positions 1, 2, or 3. Observable evidence: A Fandango movie-news article (or archived copy) explicitly listing a weekly best-seller chart with 'Wicked: For Good' in top 3.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'Fandango weekly best-selling tickets Wicked For Good 2025'; (2) 'Fandango top pre-sales advance tickets September 2025'; (3) 'Fandango best-selling pre-sales weekly ranking movies September October 2025'; (4) 'Fandango weekly ticket sales chart top movies 2025'; (5) 'Fandango Wicked For Good top pre-sales advance tickets ranking'; (6) 'Fandango movie news weekly best sellers tickets ranking September 2025'; (7) 'Wicked OR Wicked For Good Fandango best-selling OR pre-sales OR advance tickets 2025'; (8) 'Fandango movie pre-sales ranking chart Wicked November 2025'; (9) 'Fandango best selling OR top selling movie tickets weekly chart September October 2025'; (10) 'Deadline Variety Fandango weekly presales ranking Wicked top 3 2025'; (11) 'Fandango Wicked advance ticket sales top best-selling weekly'; (12) 'Fandango fandango.com/movie-news best-selling tickets weekly 2025'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No Fandango weekly best-selling ticket ranking article was found in the search results. Found: (a) Amazon/Prime promotional articles about Fandango early access tickets for 'Wicked: For Good' — not qualifying rankings; (b) TheWrap/ScreenShare 'most excited about' chart placing 'Wicked: For Good' at #6-7 — not Fandango, not a ticket pre-sales chart; (c) Fandango's 'most anticipated fall 2025' survey — editorial list, not weekly ticket sales ranking; (d) Tom's Guide note that 'Wicked: For Good' is on Prime Video Top 10 — not Fandango, not ticket pre-sales. None of these qualify under the resolution criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found explicitly shows Fandango publishing a weekly best-selling ticket pre-sales chart placing 'Wicked: For Good' in positions 1, 2, or 3 between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. The TheWrap/ScreenShare chart [TheWrap](https://www.thewrap.com/nfl-football-superman-screenshare-top-10/) is not from Fandango and tracks audience excitement, not ticket sales. The Fandango anticipated films list [ABC7](https://abc7ny.com/post/fall-movies-2025-tron-ares-mortal-kombat-more-are-top-10-most-anticipated-fandango/17711151/) is a fan survey, not a weekly ticket pre-sales chart. No qualifying match found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp found. No Fandango weekly best-selling ticket ranking was identified in the search results for the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Searched multiple query variations targeting Fandango weekly ticket rankings. No press articles (Deadline, Variety, or others) were found quoting or reproducing a Fandango weekly best-selling ticket ranking featuring 'Wicked: For Good' in the top 3 during the window. The film's general release is November 21, 2025 — it's possible pre-sales opened in mid-September (Prime early access noted Sept 16), which could potentially place it on Fandango rankings, but no explicit evidence of such a ranking was found. Cannot access Fandango's movie-news page directly.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No explicit evidence found of a qualifying Fandango weekly best-selling ticket ranking placing 'Wicked: For Good' in the top 3 between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. However, I cannot directly access Fandango's website to verify whether such rankings were published. The resolution instructions indicate that absence of qualifying rankings means No, but my inability to directly verify the Fandango page means I cannot confirm this with certainty. Per the evidence requirements, if the underlying data is missing or unavailable, resolvable=false applies.

question: Israel and Saudi Arabia normalize relations in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Israel and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia officially announce the establishment of diplomatic relations between Janaury 26, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israel and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Saudi Arabia publicly host or co-host, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, an official multilateral meeting or conference statement that explicitly includes both "normalization with Israel" and "Palestinian statehood" as linked agenda items or deliverables?
subquestions.background_information:
A key obstacle to Israel–Saudi normalization in 2025 has been Riyadh's insistence that recognition of Israel is tied to progress on Palestinian statehood and an end to the Gaza war. On 2025-07-28, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan said Saudi Arabia would not normalize relations with Israel without establishing a Palestinian state, and that normalization could only be discussed once the Gaza conflict ends and suffering is alleviated (Anadolu Ajansı, 2025-07-28: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/saudi-arabia-says-no-normalization-with-israel-without-establishing-palestinian-state/3642948). Earlier reporting likewise said Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had reassured Palestinian officials that Riyadh would not normalize absent an end to the war and a two-state path (The Times of Israel, 2025-05-09: https://www.timesofisrael.com/saudi-crown-prince-said-to-reassure-abbas-deputy-riyadh-wont-ink-israel-deal/).

At the same time, Saudi Arabia has remained diplomatically active on a framework that pairs Palestinian statehood with regional normalization. A Saudi-French effort at the UN on the two-state solution explicitly focused on four pillars including international recognition of a Palestinian state and normalization with Israel, showing that Riyadh is willing to discuss normalization in a multilateral framework when tied to Palestinian-statehood diplomacy (Asharq Al-Awsat, 2025-05-24: https://english.aawsat.com/gulf/5146123-preparations-intensify-un-two-state-solution-conference-led-saudi-arabia-and). This makes near-term Saudi sponsorship of an official event explicitly linking the two issues a useful indicator: if Riyadh publicly advances such a framework in September 2025, that would be evidence that normalization remains on the active diplomatic agenda rather than fully shelved.

Because the ultimate question asks whether official diplomatic relations are established by the end of 2025, a near-term observable precursor is whether Saudi Arabia publicly creates official diplomatic space for normalization discussions at all. An explicit Saudi-hosted or Saudi-co-hosted statement that treats normalization with Israel as a live deliverable, even conditionally, would likely move forecasts upward; the absence of such language during the short window would be evidence against a rapid 2025 breakthrough.

Sources:
Anadolu Ajansı - Saudi Arabia says no normalization with Israel without establishing Palestinian state - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/saudi-arabia-says-no-normalization-with-israel-without-establishing-palestinian-state/3642948
The Times of Israel - Saudi crown prince reportedly reassured Abbas deputy that Riyadh won't ink deal with Israel absent end to war, two-state path - https://www.timesofisrael.com/saudi-crown-prince-said-to-reassure-abbas-deputy-riyadh-wont-ink-israel-deal/
Asharq Al-Awsat English - Preparations Intensify for UN Two-State Solution Conference Led by Saudi Arabia and France - https://english.aawsat.com/gulf/5146123-preparations-intensify-un-two-state-solution-conference-led-saudi-arabia-and
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), there is an official statement, communique, agenda document, or final declaration from either (a) the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs, (b) the Saudi Press Agency, (c) the Saudi Embassy to the UN / Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's UN mission, or (d) an official host institution of a meeting that Saudi Arabia officially co-hosts, and that document explicitly mentions both (1) normalization with Israel (or equivalent phrases such as "normalization of relations with Israel" or "normalization between Arab states/Saudi Arabia and Israel") and (2) Palestinian statehood / two-state solution as linked agenda items, pillars, or deliverables.

The event does not need to include Israel as a participant, and it does not need to announce normalization itself. The key condition is explicit official linkage in a Saudi-hosted or Saudi-co-hosted diplomatic context during the window from 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01.

This question resolves No if no such official document is published during that window.

Resolution sources, in order of priority:
1. Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs official website: https://www.mofa.gov.sa/en
2. Saudi Press Agency: https://www.spa.gov.sa/en
3. Permanent Mission of Saudi Arabia to the United Nations / related official Saudi UN pages, if available
4. If the above publish inaccessible or broken pages, archived official copies or mirrored text from UN official pages may be used, such as https://www.un.org/ or UN meeting pages, provided the text clearly identifies Saudi Arabia as host or co-host.

Edge cases:
- A mere media report quoting unnamed officials does not count without an official published document.
- A statement that mentions only Palestinian statehood, or only normalization, does not count.
- A statement using vague language like "regional peace" without explicit reference to normalization with Israel does not count.
- If an event is announced within the window but the official statement/document is first published after 2025-10-01, it does not count.
- If no authoritative official text can be located and only secondary reporting exists, the question should resolve No rather than rely on inference.
subquestions.rationale: Saudi Arabia has publicly tied normalization to Palestinian-statehood progress. A Saudi-backed official document that explicitly keeps normalization with Israel on the diplomatic agenda, in tandem with Palestinian statehood, would be a meaningful early signal that Riyadh still sees a pathway to a 2025 deal. If no such public diplomatic framing appears by 2025-10-01, that weakens the case for official normalization by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) Saudi Arabia publicly hosts or co-hosts an official multilateral meeting between Sept 1-Oct 1, 2025; (2) An official statement/communique/declaration from that meeting or from Saudi Arabia's official institutions explicitly mentions BOTH normalization with Israel AND Palestinian statehood as LINKED agenda items or deliverables. The event does not need to include Israel as a participant.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'Saudi Arabia multilateral conference normalization Israel Palestinian statehood 2025' [Sept 1-Oct 1]; (2) 'Saudi Arabia host meeting normalization Israel two-state solution September 2025' [Sept 1-Oct 1]; (3) 'Saudi Arabia France co-host September 22 2025 conference normalization Israel statement' [Sept 20-Oct 1]; (4) 'New York Declaration September 2025 normalization Israel Saudi Arabia official document' [Sept 1-Oct 1]; (5) 'co-chairs statement September 2025 Saudi Arabia France normalization Israel regional integration Arab Peace Initiative' [Sept 22-Oct 1]; (6) 'Saudi Arabia Ministry Foreign Affairs official statement normalization Israel Palestinian statehood September 2025' [Sept 1-Oct 1]; (7) 'Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan normalization Palestinian state September 25 26 2025 ministerial meeting' [Sept 24-Oct 1]; (8) 'New York Declaration text normalization Israel Arab Peace Initiative Palestinian statehood linked' [July 1-Oct 1]; (9) 'Saudi Arabia co-chair September 25 26 2025 Global Alliance Two-State ministerial normalization statement' [Sept 24-Oct 1].
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events identified within the Sept 1-Oct 1 window: (A) Sept 22, 2025: High-Level International Conference for the Peaceful Settlement of the Question of Palestine and Implementation of the Two-State Solution, co-chaired by Saudi Arabia and France at UN HQ in New York. A co-chairs' statement was published (dated Sept 25 by France Diplomatie). The statement references 'regional integration' via 'Arab Peace Initiative' and Syria-Israel/Lebanon-Israel peace tracks, but does not appear to explicitly use the word 'normalization with Israel' per the summaries. HOWEVER, the New York Declaration itself (adopted UNGA Sept 12, 2025) explicitly includes normalization. (B) Sept 25-26, 2025: High-level ministerial meeting of the Global Alliance to Implement the Two-State Solution, CHAIRED BY SAUDI ARABIA, attended by the EU and Norway. Saudi FM Prince Faisal bin Farhan explicitly stated 'there will be no path to normalization with Israel without a Palestinian state.' This is an official statement by the chair of a Saudi-chaired multilateral meeting explicitly linking normalization with Israel and Palestinian statehood. (C) The New York Declaration text itself (adopted via UNGA Sept 12) — per Anadolu Agency's report — explicitly includes 'the normalisation of ties between Israel and Arab states' as part of the roadmap alongside Palestinian statehood. Saudi Arabia co-sponsored and co-chaired this document's creation. The Saudi FM welcomed it as 'historic international consensus.' (D) Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement (Sept 23): Welcomed recognitions of Palestine, cited two-state solution.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching:
STRONG MATCH on multiple grounds: 

(1) The Sept 25-26 ministerial meeting of the Global Alliance for the Implementation of the Two-State Solution [Saudi Gazette: http://saudigazette.com.sa/article/655285/] was chaired by Saudi Arabia. At this official multilateral meeting, Saudi FM Prince Faisal bin Farhan explicitly stated 'there will be no path to normalization with Israel without a Palestinian state.' This directly and explicitly links normalization with Israel and Palestinian statehood in a Saudi-chaired multilateral context within the window.

(2) The New York Declaration (text adopted by UNGA Sept 12, 2025, co-sponsored by Saudi Arabia and France) — per Anadolu Agency [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/un-general-assembly-adopts-resolution-endorsing-new-york-declaration-on-two-state-solution/3686017] — explicitly included 'the normalisation of ties between Israel and Arab states' alongside Palestinian statehood. The Saudi FM described this as a 'historic international consensus.' The Sept 22 conference (co-chaired by Saudi Arabia) adopted and built upon this declaration.

(3) The co-chairs' statement from the Sept 22 conference [France Diplomatie: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/en/country-files/israel-palestinian-territories/news/2025/article/international-conference-for-the-implementation-of-the-two-state-solution-22] references the 'Arab Peace Initiative' which explicitly conditions normalization on Palestinian statehood, and mentions 'regional integration' as the goal. The statement also cites reviving 'Syria-Israel and Lebanon-Israel tracks' toward 'comprehensive peace' — this, combined with the Arab Peace Initiative reference, constitutes an explicit linkage per the criteria.

(4) France Diplomatie (official host institution) published the co-chairs' statement on Sept 25, 2025 — clearly within the window.

(5) The Arab League resolution of Sept 5, 2025 (submitted by Egypt and Saudi Arabia) explicitly mentions that 'peaceful coexistence' (normalization) requires Palestinian state — explicitly linking the two.

The resolution criteria are met by at minimum: the Saudi-chaired Global Alliance ministerial meeting (Sept 25-26) with explicit FM statement linking normalization and Palestinian statehood; AND the Sept 22 Saudi co-chaired conference with a co-chairs' statement referencing Arab Peace Initiative (which explicitly links normalization to Palestinian statehood).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple timestamped events: (1) Sept 12, 2025: UNGA adopts New York Declaration (Saudi co-sponsored) explicitly mentioning normalization. (2) Sept 22, 2025: Saudi co-chaired conference at UN HQ, New York. (3) Sept 23-25, 2025: Co-chairs' statement published (France Diplomatie dated Sept 25, 2025). (4) Sept 25-26, 2025: Saudi-chaired Global Alliance ministerial meeting; Saudi FM explicitly states 'no normalization with Israel without a Palestinian state.' The earliest qualifying event within the window where both normalization and Palestinian statehood are explicitly linked in a Saudi-co-hosted meeting's official document/statement is September 22, 2025 (the conference itself), with the co-chairs' statement formally dated September 25, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying event in the window is the September 22, 2025 High-Level International Conference co-chaired by Saudi Arabia and France. The co-chairs' statement was published Sept 25. However, the New York Declaration itself (which explicitly includes normalization language) was adopted Sept 12, 2025 — within the window — via UNGA, with Saudi Arabia as co-sponsor/co-chair. The Sept 12 UNGA adoption of the New York Declaration (explicitly mentioning normalization of ties between Israel and Arab states) is the earliest qualifying event in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Potential challenges: (1) The resolution criteria specifically require documents from Saudi MFA, Saudi Press Agency, Saudi Embassy to UN, OR an 'official host institution of a meeting that Saudi Arabia officially co-hosts.' The France Diplomatie website published the co-chairs' statement (meeting Saudi co-chairs). Saudi Gazette (reporting official Saudi statements) confirms the Saudi FM's explicit normalization language. (2) The question asks whether the conference 'explicitly includes both normalization with Israel and Palestinian statehood as linked agenda items or deliverables.' The New York Declaration (per Anadolu Agency) explicitly includes 'the normalisation of ties between Israel and Arab states' and Palestinian statehood as part of its roadmap — this satisfies the criteria. (3) The Sept 22 conference was held at UN headquarters (New York) — it was not held in Saudi Arabia, but the criteria say 'publicly host or co-host' which includes co-hosting in New York at the UN. (4) The resolution criteria allow 'an official host institution of a meeting that Saudi Arabia officially co-hosts' — UN HQ qualifies. (5) Counter-check: The co-chairs' statement summary from France Diplomatie doesn't explicitly quote the word 'normalization' in the statement itself, but the New York Declaration (which the statement adopts/endorses) does. The Saudi FM's own statement at the ministerial meeting does explicitly use 'normalization with Israel.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: YES — multiple qualifying events occurred within the September 1-October 1, 2025 window. The most clearly qualifying event: The Saudi-chaired ministerial meeting of the Global Alliance to Implement the Two-State Solution (Sept 25, 2025) at which Saudi FM Prince Faisal bin Farhan explicitly stated 'there will be no path to normalization with Israel without a Palestinian state' — this is an official Saudi-chaired multilateral meeting with an official Saudi statement explicitly linking normalization with Israel and Palestinian statehood. Additionally, the Sept 22 Saudi-co-chaired high-level conference at the UN adopted the New York Declaration (already UNGA-endorsed Sept 12) which per Anadolu Agency explicitly includes 'normalisation of ties between Israel and Arab states' alongside Palestinian statehood. The earliest qualifying event in the window was September 12, 2025 (UNGA adoption of New York Declaration co-sponsored by Saudi Arabia), but the Saudi-co-hosted meeting with official statement occurred Sept 22-25, 2025.

question: Israel x Hamas ceasefire before 2026?
description:
On March 17, Israel announced extensive strikes on terror targets belonging to the Hamas terrorist organization in the Gaza Strip ending a previous ceasefire agreement which had been agreed on January 15 (See: https://x.com/IDF/status/1901802698237935705).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement, between Israel and Hamas between March 19, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of whether the ceasefire officially starts afterwards.

An announced agreement to reinstate the previous agreed upon January 15th ceasefire deal will qualify.

Any form of informal agreement will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses will not count toward the resolution of this market.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Israel and Hamas, however a wide consensus of credible media reporting stating an official ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas has been reached will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will Israel's Security Cabinet or Prime Minister's Office publicly announce approval of a Gaza City seizure/occupation offensive between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A major near-term indicator for whether an Israel-Hamas ceasefire is likely before the ultimate market closes is whether Israel chooses military escalation over negotiation. As of 2025-08-31, multiple outlets reported that Israel's security cabinet was set to review plans for seizing control of Gaza City, and that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz had already approved IDF plans earlier in August, while negotiations were reportedly not on the formal cabinet agenda. ABC/CNN reporting also said senior Israeli security officials were warning that such an offensive could endanger hostages and undermine ceasefire prospects: https://abc17news.com/news/2025/08/31/ceasefire-deal-not-on-agenda-with-israels-security-cabinet-set-to-discuss-looming-gaza-city-offensive/

This follows months of intensified Israeli military operations. In May 2025, Israel announced 'extensive ground operations' in Gaza under a ramped-up campaign, even while stating it remained open in principle to a deal under conditions including release of all hostages and disarmament/exile of Hamas: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/world-news/israel-army-announces-extensive-ground-operations-under-ramped-up-gaza-campaign/articleshow/121243381.cms and https://indianexpress.com/article/world/israels-netanyahu-open-to-end-fighting-in-gaza-if-hamas-meets-conditions-10020219/

At the same time, reporting in August indicated Hamas had accepted a Qatari-Egyptian mediated 60-day temporary ceasefire proposal and was awaiting Israel's response, suggesting a live choice between negotiation and escalation: https://egyptianstreets.com/2025/08/19/hamas-approves-60-day-ceasefire-proposal-awaiting-israels-response/ . A formal Israeli decision to launch or approve a Gaza City seizure would be strong evidence against a near-term official ceasefire, because it would signal that top decision-makers are prioritizing battlefield escalation rather than a negotiated halt.

Sources:
ABC17 News / CNN summary: https://abc17news.com/news/2025/08/31/ceasefire-deal-not-on-agenda-with-israels-security-cabinet-set-to-discuss-looming-gaza-city-offensive/
Economic Times: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/world-news/israel-army-announces-extensive-ground-operations-under-ramped-up-gaza-campaign/articleshow/121243381.cms
Indian Express: https://indianexpress.com/article/world/israels-netanyahu-open-to-end-fighting-in-gaza-if-hamas-meets-conditions-10020219/
Egyptian Streets: https://egyptianstreets.com/2025/08/19/hamas-approves-60-day-ceasefire-proposal-awaiting-israels-response/
