subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), either (a) Israel's Prime Minister's Office or Security Cabinet publicly announces approval of a plan to seize, occupy, or take control of Gaza City, or (b) the Israel Defense Forces publicly announces the launch of an operation explicitly described as aimed at seizing, occupying, or taking control of Gaza City.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

Primary resolution sources will be official Israeli government or military channels, including the Prime Minister's Office (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office/govil-landing-page), the PMO/X account if used for official statements (https://x.com/IsraeliPM), and the IDF official site/newsroom (https://www.idf.il/en/) or IDF official X account (https://x.com/IDF).

If official primary sources are unavailable or ambiguous, the market will use a broad consensus of at least two credible international news reports describing an official Israeli approval/announcement of such an offensive, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news), or CNN (https://www.cnn.com/).

For avoidance of doubt: mere media reports that plans are under consideration, leaks, or reports that a meeting occurred do not qualify without a public announcement of approval or launch. General references to 'expanded operations' do not qualify unless they explicitly state Gaza City is to be seized, occupied, or taken under Israeli control. If an announcement is made before 2025-09-01 or after 2025-10-01, it does not count. If purported approval is reported but later denied and no authoritative source confirms it within the window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A formal decision to seize or occupy Gaza City would be a concrete signal of Israeli escalation and reduced willingness to conclude a near-term ceasefire with Hamas. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question; rather, it tracks a strategic choice by Israel that should materially update forecasts about whether an official ceasefire agreement will be reached before the ultimate deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: (a) PM Office or Security Cabinet publicly announces approval of plan to seize/occupy/take control of Gaza City between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, OR (b) IDF publicly announces launch of operation explicitly aimed at seizing/occupying/taking control of Gaza City within the same window. Key entities: PM Office, Security Cabinet, IDF. Timing: strictly within Sept 1–Oct 1 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Israel Security Cabinet approve Gaza City seizure occupation offensive 2025' (Sept 1–Oct 1) — to find any within-window approval announcement. 2) 'IDF Israel Gaza City operation launch announcement September 2025' (Sept 1–Oct 1) — to find IDF launch announcements. 3) 'Israel Security Cabinet approve Gaza City plan August 2025' (Aug 1–Sept 10) — to establish when the Security Cabinet approval occurred. 4) 'IDF Netanyahu announce Gaza City ground operation September 16 2025' (Sept 14–20) — to confirm ground offensive launch details. 5) 'Israel IDF official announcement Gaza City operation Gideon's Chariots launch September 2 2025' (Sept 1–5) — to find earliest within-window qualifying event.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Security Cabinet approval on August 8, 2025 — confirmed by Straits Times, CNN, Rediff, TASS, etc. BUT this is BEFORE the Sept 1 window, so it does NOT qualify under the resolution criteria. (B) IDF Chief Zamir announcement on September 3, 2025 of 'launch of second phase of Operation Gideon's Chariots to occupy Gaza City' — confirmed by Anadolu Agency, Daily Sabah, Yeni Safak. This IS within the window. (C) IDF ground offensive launch announcement on September 15–16, 2025 — confirmed by ABC News, CNBC, Times of Israel, RT, AP, ABC Australia, The Forward, etc. This is also within the window. Events B and C qualify under criterion (b). Event A does not qualify due to being before the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Event B (Sept 3, 2025): IDF Chief of Staff Zamir told troops: 'We have entered the second phase of Operation Gideon's Chariots to fulfill the objectives of the war. Returning our hostages is both a moral and national mission.' [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/israel-launches-2nd-phase-of-offensive-to-occupy-gaza-city/3677538) explicitly described as aimed at 'occupying Gaza City.' This is an IDF public announcement of the launch of an operation aimed at seizing/occupying Gaza City within the Sept 1–Oct 1 window — satisfying criterion (b). Event C (Sept 16, 2025): IDF stated it 'has begun expanding ground operations in Gaza City as part of Operation Gideon's Chariots II' [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/16/gaza-is-burning-israel-launches-ground-invasion-of-gaza-city.html); described by Australian ABC as 'ground offensive to occupy Gaza City' [abc.net.au](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-09-16/idf-launches-military-offensive-to-occupy-gaza/105777948); PM Netanyahu publicly confirmed 'We have begun a powerful operation in Gaza' [Christian Post](https://www.christianpost.com/news/israels-gaza-city-ground-operation-officially-begins.html). Both events satisfy criterion (b).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First qualifying event in window: September 3, 2025 — IDF Chief of Staff Zamir announced the launch of Phase 2 of Operation Gideon's Chariots aimed at occupying Gaza City. Published by Anadolu Agency on 2025-09-03. Exact time not specified in article, but date is September 3, 2025. Second qualifying event: September 15–16, 2025 — IDF announced expansion of ground operations in Gaza City. RT article timestamp: 2025-09-16 08:53. ABC News article: Sept 16, 2025. CNBC: Sept 16, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The Security Cabinet approval was on August 8, 2025 (before the window). The first qualifying IDF announcement within the window was September 3, 2025 (Zamir's Phase 2 announcement). No earlier qualifying event within the Sept 1–Oct 1 window was found. The Sept 1 IDF statement by Zamir about 'reservists preparing to deepen the fight in Gaza City in October' (Worthy Christian News) does not constitute a launch announcement.
evidence.step7_verification: The August 8 Security Cabinet approval is well-documented and clearly before the window. The September 3 announcement by Zamir is reported by Anadolu Agency and other outlets as an explicit launch of a new phase aimed at occupying Gaza City — this meets criterion (b). The September 16 ground offensive launch is confirmed by AP, ABC News, CNBC, Times of Israel, and multiple other credible outlets. No contradictory evidence was found denying these announcements. The resolution criteria explicitly states that 'If official primary sources are unavailable or ambiguous, the market will use a broad consensus of at least two credible international news reports' — this condition is clearly satisfied for both Sept 3 and Sept 16 events.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves YES. The IDF publicly announced the launch of an operation explicitly aimed at seizing/occupying/taking control of Gaza City on September 3, 2025 (Zamir's Phase 2 announcement), which is within the Sept 1–Oct 1 window. This satisfies criterion (b). Additionally, on September 15–16, 2025, the IDF launched the main ground offensive with Netanyahu's and the IDF's explicit public announcements. Multiple credible international sources (Anadolu Agency, ABC News, CNBC, AP, Times of Israel, RT) confirm these within-window announcements. The first qualifying event in the window is September 3, 2025.

question: Will James Talarico be the Democratic nominee for Senate in Texas?
description:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Democratic Primary for United States Senator from Texas.

If no 2026 Texas Democratic Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Texas Democratic party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

subquestions.question: Will James Talarico report raising at least $8.0 million in total receipts for his 2026 Texas U.S. Senate campaign in his next FEC filing covering activity through 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
Fundraising is a key early indicator of primary strength because it measures donor enthusiasm, campaign viability, and ability to communicate with voters before the March 2026 Texas Democratic Senate primary. Talarico launched his campaign on 2025-09-09. By late October, The Dallas Morning News reported that his campaign had raised $6.2 million in under four weeks since launch, compared with Colin Allred's $4.1 million in his first three months of this cycle, suggesting unusually strong early momentum for Talarico (https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/2025/10/28/james-talarico-targets-rival-colin-allreds-home-turf-in-senate-primary-fight/). The Texas Democratic Senate candidate filing period runs from 2025-11-08 to 2025-12-08, making the next disclosure period especially relevant because it captures whether Talarico can sustain his launch momentum during the formal filing window (same source). Candidate financial reports for federal candidates are published by the Federal Election Commission and are a standard source for measuring campaign strength (https://www.fec.gov/data/). Because Talarico is running against a well-known former congressman, continued fundraising strength above his already-high launch baseline would be meaningful evidence that he remains a top contender for the nomination.

Sources:
Dallas Morning News - James Talarico targets rival Colin Allred's home turf in Senate primary fight - https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/2025/10/28/james-talarico-targets-rival-colin-allreds-home-turf-in-senate-primary-fight/
Federal Election Commission data portal - https://www.fec.gov/data/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
Start date: 2025-11-13. End date: 2025-12-13.

This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13 inclusive, the first publicly available FEC filing by James Talarico's principal campaign committee for the 2026 Texas U.S. Senate race that covers a reporting period ending on 2025-11-30 or later shows total receipts of at least $8,000,000 for the election cycle to date.

It resolves No if, between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13 inclusive, such a filing becomes publicly available and shows cycle-to-date total receipts below $8,000,000.

If no qualifying FEC filing for Talarico's principal campaign committee covering a period ending on 2025-11-30 or later is publicly available by 2025-12-13, this question resolves Unresolvable.

Primary source: the FEC candidate/committee filings and financial summary pages for James Talarico's Senate campaign at https://www.fec.gov/data/ and the FEC electronic filings search at https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/forms/. Resolution should use the committee's reported "total receipts" / cycle-to-date receipts as shown in the filing or FEC summary. If the FEC site is temporarily unavailable, the same filed report as republished by an authoritative mirror such as OpenSecrets may be used as a fallback, but the FEC filing controls if later accessible: https://www.opensecrets.org/.

Amendments: if multiple filings are posted within the resolution window for the same reporting period, use the latest filing posted by 2025-12-13. Filings posted after 2025-12-13 do not count.
subquestions.rationale: Talarico's nomination chances depend heavily on whether his early fundraising surge is real and sustainable. Crossing $8 million by the next filing would be strong evidence that he can compete with or surpass better-known rivals like Colin Allred in organization and message resonance.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) A FEC filing by Talarico's principal campaign committee for the 2026 Texas Senate race; (2) The filing must cover a reporting period ending on 2025-11-30 or later; (3) The filing must be publicly available between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13; (4) The filing must show cycle-to-date total receipts of at least $8,000,000. If no such filing is available by 2025-12-13, the question resolves Unresolvable rather than Yes or No.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'James Talarico FEC filing 2026 Texas Senate campaign fundraising' (Nov-Dec 2025) — to find FEC filings. 2. 'James Talarico Texas Senate campaign total receipts 2025' (Nov-Dec 2025) — to find fundraising totals. 3. 'James Talarico FEC quarterly report November 2025 total receipts million' — to find specific November filing. 4. 'Talarico FEC filing November 30 2025 monthly report quarterly' — to find monthly filing. 5. 'James Talarico campaign fundraising $8 million Senate 2025' (Oct-Dec 2025) — to check $8M threshold. 6. 'James Talarico Texas Senate fundraising total raised November December 2025' — to find updated totals.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key data found: (1) As of Q3 2025 (ending September 30), Talarico's campaign raised approximately $6.2-6.3 million and had $5.0 million cash on hand. (2) As of December 2025, news reports consistently cite '$6.2 million' or 'over $6 million' as the campaign total — with no mentions approaching $8 million. (3) No news reports mention any FEC filing by Talarico covering a period ending November 30, 2025. (4) The standard FEC quarterly schedule would have Q4 (October 1-December 31, 2025) due on January 31, 2026 — outside the resolution window. No monthly filing for a November 30 period is mentioned.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: CRITERIA NOT MET on multiple grounds: (1) No evidence of a Talarico FEC filing covering a period ending 2025-11-30 or later becoming publicly available by 2025-12-13. News sources from December 2025 only reference the Q3 filing data ($6.2M), not any subsequent filing. Under standard FEC quarterly filing schedules, the next filing after Q3 (September 30) would cover Q4 (December 31) and not be due until January 31, 2026. (2) Even if such a filing existed, all reporting indicates total receipts of approximately $6.2-6.5 million — well below the $8 million threshold. [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/colin-allred-texas-senate-democratic-primary-dallas/) stated Talarico 'raised $6.2 million' as of December 8, 2025. [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/congressional/3910362/jasmine-crockett-running-texas-senate-colin-allred-drop-out/) confirmed '$6.2 million in the first three weeks.' No source mentions reaching $8 million.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp for a qualifying FEC filing could be extracted because no such filing was found in any news source or search result within the resolution window (2025-11-13 to 2025-12-13). The question therefore resolves as Unresolvable per the stated criteria.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying FEC filing covering a period ending 2025-11-30 or later was found. The question's own resolution criteria state that if no qualifying filing is publicly available by 2025-12-13, the question resolves Unresolvable.
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checked multiple sources from December 2025: All consistently reference Talarico's $6.2 million figure from Q3 2025. No source mentions a new FEC filing covering a post-September 30 period. The FEC's standard filing schedule for non-election year Senate campaigns requires only quarterly reports, with Q4 not due until January 31, 2026. Monthly filers would have an October monthly (due November 20) but not a 'November 30' period filing due by December 13. The resolution window explicitly includes an 'Unresolvable' outcome if no qualifying filing appears.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question is Unresolvable. No qualifying FEC filing by Talarico's principal campaign committee covering a period ending 2025-11-30 or later became publicly available between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13. The standard FEC quarterly schedule would place the next filing (Q4 ending December 31, 2025) as due on January 31, 2026, outside the resolution window. All available evidence from December 2025 indicates Talarico's total cycle receipts were approximately $6.2-6.5 million — well below the $8 million threshold — but this is irrelevant because the primary resolution condition (existence of a qualifying FEC filing within the window) is not satisfied.

question: Will Gemini 3.0 be released by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve according to the date (ET) Google's Gemini 3.0 model is made available to the general public. 

For this market to resolve to "Yes," Gemini 3.0 must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by Google as being accessible to the general public.

Gemini 3.0 refers to a product explicitly named Gemini 3.0 (e.g. Gemini 3.0 pro would count), or one that is recognized as a successor to Gemini 2.0, similar to the progression from Gemini 1.0 to Gemini 2.0. Products labeled as Gemini 2.5 or similar will not count for this market's resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Google, with additional verification from a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Google publicly announce a Gemini for Home early-access sign-up or rollout date in October 2025 by 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term public rollout commitment for a major Gemini-powered consumer product would be a meaningful indicator that Google is in active launch mode for the Gemini family, which may correlate with readiness to introduce a new flagship model generation such as Gemini 3.0 before the end of October. At Google's August 2025 hardware event, multiple outlets reported that "Gemini for Home" would enter early access in October on Nest speakers and displays, but Google had not yet given a specific public date or full rollout plan as of late August. Engadget reported that Google said Gemini for Home would launch in early access on smart displays and speakers in October, with more rollout details to come: https://www.engadget.com/ai/gemini-is-coming-to-google-home-in-october-with-both-free-and-paid-versions-120050080.html . Trusted Reviews similarly reported October early access without a precise date: https://www.trustedreviews.com/news/gemini-is-finally-making-its-way-to-googles-smart-home-devices-4637094 . Business Standard also said Google would release a detailed rollout plan later: https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/google-to-offer-gemini-for-home-early-access-from-october-what-to-expect-125082200238_1.html .

Separately, Google has continued shipping Gemini 2.5-branded capabilities rather than a 3.0-branded model. Digital Trends said Gemini 2.5 Pro had been released to all users by August 2025, indicating that the currently public flagship naming remains on the 2.5 line rather than 3.0: https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-gemini-everything-you-need-to-know/ . Google also launched Gemini 2.5 Flash Image in preview through developer channels in late August, showing continued product activity and deployment velocity in the Gemini ecosystem: https://developers.googleblog.com/en/introducing-gemini-2-5-flash-image/ .

Because Google had already publicly signaled an October consumer rollout for Gemini for Home, a further public announcement by October 1 that specifies sign-up mechanics or a concrete date would be a useful leading indicator of whether Google is accelerating Gemini releases and marketing ahead of the ultimate October 31 Gemini 3.0 deadline.

Sources:
Engadget - Gemini is coming to Google Home in October with both free and paid versions - https://www.engadget.com/ai/gemini-is-coming-to-google-home-in-october-with-both-free-and-paid-versions-120050080.html
Trusted Reviews - Gemini is finally making its way to Google's smart home devices - https://www.trustedreviews.com/news/gemini-is-finally-making-its-way-to-googles-smart-home-devices-4637094
Business Standard - Google to offer 'Gemini for Home' early access from October - https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/google-to-offer-gemini-for-home-early-access-from-october-what-to-expect-125082200238_1.html
Digital Trends - Google Gemini: everything you need to know - https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-gemini-everything-you-need-to-know/
Google Developers Blog - Introducing Gemini 2.5 Flash Image - https://developers.googleblog.com/en/introducing-gemini-2-5-flash-image/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Google publicly announces either: (a) a specific calendar date in October 2025 for Gemini for Home early access, launch, or rollout; or (b) a public sign-up mechanism for Gemini for Home early access that is available to the general public or to an openly defined public customer class (for example, all Nest Aware subscribers), with Google stating that access begins in October 2025.

For clarity, qualifying announcements must be publicly accessible and attributable to Google, such as on the Google Blog, The Keyword, official Google Help pages, official Google social media accounts, store/listing pages, or support documentation. Closed-door comments, leaks, or reporting that merely cites unnamed sources do not count unless corroborated by an official Google public source.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public Google announcement appears between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

Primary resolution sources: official Google channels, including but not limited to https://blog.google/ , https://blog.google/products/ , https://support.google.com/ , and official @Google or @madebygoogle posts on https://x.com/ . Secondary verification may come from credible reporting such as Engadget (https://www.engadget.com/), 9to5Google (https://9to5google.com/), or The Verge (https://www.theverge.com/) if needed to identify the relevant official Google source.

If an announcement is made within the window but the actual rollout is later delayed, the question still resolves Yes, because this market is about the public announcement of the October sign-up or rollout date, not successful execution. If only a vague statement such as "coming in October" is repeated without a specific date or public sign-up mechanism, that does not qualify. If Google content appears within the window but is inaccessible at resolution time, archived versions or contemporaneous credible reports quoting the official Google announcement may be used as fallback evidence.
subquestions.rationale: A concrete public rollout announcement for Gemini for Home would indicate active launch readiness, coordinated marketing, and confidence in Gemini deployment cadence. That is not the same as releasing Gemini 3.0, but it is an observable near-term sign that Google is pushing major Gemini initiatives into public access ahead of the ultimate deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, Google must publicly announce on an official channel (a) a specific calendar date in October 2025 for Gemini for Home early access/launch/rollout, OR (b) a public sign-up mechanism for early access available to the general public or a defined customer class, with Google stating access begins in October 2025. Observable evidence: official Google X post, blog.google post, or support page specifying October 2025 rollout date. Key entities: 'Gemini for Home,' 'early access,' 'October 2025,' official Google channels.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Google Gemini for Home early access announcement 2025' (Sept 1 – Oct 1): to find the announcement. 2) 'Google Gemini Home smart home rollout October 2025' (Sept 1 – Oct 1): to find rollout details. 3) 'Google Made by Google X post Gemini is coming to Google Home October 1' (Sept 1 – Oct 1): to confirm official X post. 4) 'Google Gemini Home early access sign-up Nest Aware subscribers October 2025' (Sept 1 – Oct 1): to check for sign-up mechanism. 5) 'Google blog.google Gemini for Home launch announcement September 2025' (Sept 1 – Oct 1): to confirm official blog post.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: Official @madebygoogle X post (~September 2, 2025) reading 'Gemini is coming to Google Home' and 'Come back October 1st,' announcing October 1, 2025 as the rollout/early-access date. Confirmed by PCWorld (Sept 2), Android Central (Sept 2), MacRumors (Sept 3), The Verge (Sept 3), Engadget (Sept 3), Forbes (Sept 3), CNET (Sept 3), TechRadar (Sept 4), and many others — all citing the official @madebygoogle X post. MacRumors explicitly: 'Google announced that its Gemini for Home generative-AI assistant will start rolling out on October 1 through an early-access program.' The Verge confirms: 'early access beginning in October as promised at the Made by Google event.' Candidate event 2: blog.google post dated October 1, 2025 (URL: https://blog.google/products/google-nest/gemini-for-home-launch/) — falls on the boundary date. No candidates rejected from within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The @madebygoogle X post (official Google social media account) on ~September 2, 2025 announced a specific calendar date — October 1, 2025 — for Gemini for Home early-access rollout. This satisfies criterion (a): 'a specific calendar date in October 2025 for Gemini for Home early access, launch, or rollout.' Confirmed by [MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/2025/09/03/gemini-for-home-rolling-out-october-1/), [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/769848/google-teases-new-nest-cam-gemini-home), [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/home/smart-home/google-will-reveal-more-gemini-smart-home-plans-and-devices-on-october-1-133601777.html), [PCWorld](https://www.pcworld.com/article/2896569/google-sets-date-for-nest-cam-gemini-for-home-reveal.html), [CNET](https://www.cnet.com/home/smart-home/google-is-bringing-gemini-ai-to-its-smart-home-lineup-starting-oct-1/). The source is an official @madebygoogle X post — qualifying under 'official Google social media accounts.' The date (October 1, 2025) is a specific calendar date in October 2025. Criteria fully satisfied.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The @madebygoogle X post was reported by PCWorld on September 2, 2025 and by Engadget, MacRumors, The Verge on September 3, 2025. The post itself was published on or about September 2, 2025. This is within the resolution window (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 inclusive). Exact timestamp of the X post is September 2, 2025 (reported as 'Tuesday' by CNET on Sept 3, which places it September 2, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest credible reports of Google's announcement are from September 2, 2025 (PCWorld, Android Central). No earlier qualifying announcement within the window (September 1–2 gap is small, and no Sept 1 reports found). This is the first qualifying occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources consistently report the same official @madebygoogle X post stating October 1, 2025 as the Gemini for Home rollout/early-access date. No contradictory evidence found — the October 1, 2025 blog.google launch post (https://blog.google/products/google-nest/gemini-for-home-launch/) confirms the announced date was followed through. No conflicting reports exist about the announcement being postponed, retracted, or altered before October 1. The blog.google post on October 1 itself states 'Early access is available via the Google Home app (version 4.0+), with full rollout beginning in October 2025,' corroborating the September announcement.
evidence.step8_final_decision: YES. Google's official @madebygoogle X post on September 2, 2025 publicly announced that Gemini for Home early access would begin on October 1, 2025 — a specific calendar date in October 2025. This is an official Google social media announcement within the resolution window (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01), directly satisfying resolution criterion (a). The announcement was corroborated by numerous credible secondary sources and ultimately confirmed by the official blog.google launch post on October 1, 2025. Resolution: YES, with resolution datetime of 2025-09-02T00:00:00Z (date of the @madebygoogle X post).

question: Will the U.S. invade Venezuela by December 31, 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of Venezuela between September 6 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, land de facto controlled by Venezuela or the United States as of September 6, 2025, 12:00 PM ET, will be considered the sovereign territory of that country.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible sources.

subquestions.question: Will either chamber of the U.S. Congress introduce a joint resolution or bill between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06 that would specifically require congressional authorization for U.S. military action against Venezuela or direct the termination of such action under the War Powers Resolution?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term congressional move to constrain or authorize force against Venezuela would be a meaningful indicator of whether U.S. decision-makers believe a Venezuela operation is plausible or imminent. Such legislation would not itself constitute an invasion, but it would signal that the issue has become salient enough in Washington to trigger formal war-powers contestation.

Recent reporting indicates a sharp rise in U.S.-Venezuela military tensions. AP reported on 2025-09-17 that Nicolás Maduro publicly warned of a U.S. invasion threat and called for Venezuelan unity in response to recent U.S. actions: https://apnews.com/ . Reporting from bne IntelliNews on 2025-09-11 said Colombian President Gustavo Petro rejected the use of Colombian territory for any invasion of a neighboring country, indicating regional concern that a cross-border military operation was conceivable: https://www.intellinews.com/colombia-rules-out-use-of-its-territory-for-venezuela-invasion-petro-says-396981/ .

On 2025-10-03, multiple outlets reported that the Trump administration had notified Congress of military operations against Venezuelan cartel-linked groups and that some lawmakers were preparing a War Powers response. TASS summarized that a document sent to Congress said the Pentagon had been directed to conduct operations against alleged Venezuelan drug cartels and described the situation as a "non-international armed conflict": https://tass.com/world/ . The user-provided article summary from The US Sun likewise states that Democrats in Congress were drafting a War Powers Resolution to block further unilateral action.

Formal congressional introduction of a Venezuela-specific war-powers measure would be informative because it implies legislators perceive a real risk of hostilities escalating beyond maritime interdiction or isolated strikes. If no such measure is introduced by early November, that modestly suggests the crisis may remain below the threshold where Congress expects an invasion or major ground-seizure operation.

Sources:
Congress.gov https://www.congress.gov/
AP News https://apnews.com/
bne IntelliNews article https://www.intellinews.com/colombia-rules-out-use-of-its-territory-for-venezuela-invasion-petro-says-396981/
TASS https://tass.com/world/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06 inclusive, either the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate formally introduces a joint resolution, concurrent resolution, simple resolution, or bill that explicitly references Venezuela and either: (a) requires prior congressional authorization for U.S. military action against Venezuela; or (b) directs, demands, or requires the termination/removal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Venezuela or from hostilities in/over/around Venezuelan territory pursuant to the War Powers Resolution.

This question resolves No if no such measure is formally introduced during the window from 2025-10-07 through 2025-11-06.

Primary resolution source: Congress.gov legislative records and search results, especially bill/resolution text and introduction dates: https://www.congress.gov/

Suggested search pages for resolution:
- Congress.gov search for Venezuela: https://www.congress.gov/search?q=%7B%22source%22%3A%22legislation%22%2C%22search%22%3A%22Venezuela%22%7D
- Congress.gov search for War Powers and Venezuela: https://www.congress.gov/search?q=%7B%22source%22%3A%22legislation%22%2C%22search%22%3A%22War%20Powers%20Venezuela%22%7D

Interpretation rules:
1. "Formally introduces" means the measure receives an official Congress.gov entry with an introduction date in the qualifying window.
2. The measure must specifically mention Venezuela in the title, summary, or legislative text; a generic war-powers bill not specifically tied to Venezuela does not count.
3. A nonbinding press release, draft, leaked text, or announced intention to introduce legislation does not count unless an official legislative entry appears on Congress.gov within the window.
4. A measure focused solely on sanctions, humanitarian aid, elections, recognition policy, counternarcotics in general, or cartel designations does not count unless it also explicitly addresses U.S. military action against Venezuela as described above.
5. If Congress.gov is temporarily unavailable, official House or Senate clerk records may be used as fallback, but only if they clearly show the measure text/title and formal introduction date: https://clerk.house.gov/ and https://www.senate.gov/ .
6. If conflicting sources exist, Congress.gov controls.

If a qualifying measure is introduced after 2025-11-06, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: Congressional war-powers activity is a distinct observable indicator of perceived invasion risk. A Venezuela-specific attempt to authorize or restrain force would signal that U.S. elites view major military action as live and near-term, which should meaningfully update forecasts on whether the U.S. invades Venezuela by the end of 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06 inclusive, either chamber formally introduces a joint resolution, concurrent resolution, simple resolution, or bill that (a) explicitly references Venezuela AND (b) requires congressional authorization for U.S. military action against Venezuela OR directs termination of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Venezuela under the War Powers Resolution. Observable evidence: A Congress.gov legislative entry (or equivalent official record) with an introduction date in the window. Key entities: U.S. Senate, U.S. House, Venezuela, War Powers Resolution. Threshold: Formal introduction (not mere announcement or press release). Timing: Oct 7–Nov 6, 2025 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Congress bill resolution Venezuela military War Powers Resolution 2025' (Oct 7–Nov 6) — to find legislation introduced. Query 2: 'congressional legislation Venezuela military action authorization 2025' (Oct 7–Nov 6) — to find bills. Query 3: 'Kaine Schiff Paul War Powers Resolution Venezuela Senate introduced October 2025' — for specific resolution details. Query 4: 'House Representatives Venezuela military bill resolution introduced October November 2025' — to find House action. Query 5: 'Senate Venezuela war powers resolution vote November 2025' — to find end-of-window activity. Query 6: 'Schiff Kaine Venezuela war powers resolution Senate introduced October 8 2025' — to verify earliest date. Query 7: 'Ilhan Omar House Venezuela war powers resolution bill introduced 2025' — to check House action. Query 8: 'Senate Joint Resolution 83 Venezuela war powers Schiff Kaine introduced date' — to verify the exact SJR 83 introduction date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Senate Joint Resolution 83 introduced by Schiff/Kaine – voted down Oct 8-9, 2025 (51-48). The White House opposed it on Oct 7, 2025, suggesting introduction was on or just before Oct 7. However, The Hill article from Oct 6 suggests they were preparing to force a vote 'this week,' indicating introduction may have been Oct 7-8. (2) New bipartisan war powers resolution introduced October 17, 2025 by Kaine, Paul, and Schiff — explicitly blocking U.S. military force 'within or against' Venezuela without congressional authorization. Multiple major sources confirm Oct 17 introduction date. (3) Rep. Ilhan Omar introduced a House resolution, per The Intercept (Oct 9 article), no specific introduction date given. (4) A third Senate resolution voted on Nov 6, 2025 (49-51) requiring congressional authorization before military strikes on Venezuelan territory. (5) A resolution reportedly introduced Nov 1, 2025 per EntornoInteligente.com. Rejected events: None — all above qualify; the October 17 resolution is the clearest qualifying event within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The October 17, 2025 resolution introduced by Senators Kaine, Paul, and Schiff [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/world/senators-look-block-trump-from-engaging-hostilities-venezuela), [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/10/17/kaine-bill-war-venezuela/5291760706542/), [Raw Story](https://www.rawstory.com/trump-war-2674210487/), [Common Dreams](https://www.commondreams.org/news/venezuela-senate): (a) explicitly references Venezuela — YES, the resolution specifically targets U.S. military force 'within or against' Venezuela; (b) requires prior congressional authorization for U.S. military action against Venezuela — YES, the resolution prohibits U.S. military force against Venezuela without explicit congressional authorization (declaration of war or AUMF); (c) invokes the War Powers Resolution — YES, senators cited the 1973 War Powers Act. It was formally introduced in the U.S. Senate on October 17, 2025. Interpretation rule #4 concern: The measure is not solely about sanctions, humanitarian aid, elections, recognition policy, counternarcotics in general, or cartel designations — it explicitly addresses U.S. military action against Venezuela as a sovereign state. The Common Dreams article specifically states the resolution would 'prevent U.S. military force within or against Venezuela unless explicitly authorized.' This directly matches criteria (a) and (b). Additionally, Senate Joint Resolution 83 (voted Oct 8-9) also qualifies if introduced within the window on Oct 7-8.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The October 17, 2025 resolution: Multiple sources published on October 17, 2025 confirm introduction on that date. Fox News article dated 2025-10-17 states senators 'introduced a War Powers Resolution on October 17, 2025.' UPI article dated 2025-10-17 states senators 'introduced a bipartisan bill on October 17, 2025.' Raw Story article dated 2025-10-17 states senators 'introduced a bipartisan war powers resolution on October 17, 2025.' Reliable timestamp: 2025-10-17 (exact date, multiple high-quality sources agree). For SJR 83: Articles from Oct 7-8 reference it as already introduced/being voted on, suggesting introduction on or just before Oct 7. The White House formally opposed it on Oct 7, 2025, per Washington Examiner. The Hill article from Oct 6 describes senators planning to 'force a vote this week,' suggesting formal introduction may have occurred on Oct 7 or Oct 8.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question asks whether any qualifying measure was introduced in the window. The earliest qualifying event within the window appears to be Senate Joint Resolution 83 — which was introduced on or around October 7-8, 2025 (the window starts Oct 7). The White House formally opposed it on Oct 7, suggesting it was already introduced. The Oct 6 Hill article says senators were 'pushing to force a vote this week,' strongly suggesting formal introduction occurred on Oct 7 or Oct 8. If SJR 83 was introduced before Oct 7 (e.g., on Oct 6), then SJR 83 might not count, but the October 17 resolution by Kaine/Paul/Schiff is definitively within the window. Multiple subsequent resolutions were also introduced within the window (Oct 17, Nov 1 area, voted Nov 6). The first qualifying occurrence within the window is most likely Oct 7-8 (SJR 83) or definitively Oct 17 (Kaine/Paul/Schiff resolution).
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove: (1) Could SJR 83 have been introduced before Oct 7? The Hill article from Oct 6 says senators were planning to 'force a vote this week,' suggesting formal introduction hadn't yet occurred on Oct 6. The Washington Examiner opposition article is dated Oct 7. The vote occurred Oct 8-9. This strongly suggests introduction was on Oct 7 or Oct 8 — within the window. (2) Could the Oct 17 resolution not specifically reference Venezuela? No — multiple sources explicitly state it targets U.S. military force 'within or against' Venezuela, making Venezuela a central, explicit focus. (3) Could this be a counternarcotics bill not addressing military action? No — the resolution explicitly addresses U.S. military hostilities against Venezuela, not merely drug enforcement. (4) Contradictory evidence? None found — all sources consistently confirm multiple qualifying resolutions were introduced in the Oct 7–Nov 6 window. (5) Rep. Ilhan Omar also reportedly introduced a House resolution per The Intercept (mentioned in Oct 9 article), though the exact introduction date is unclear from available sources.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly supports a Yes resolution. Multiple qualifying legislative measures were formally introduced in the U.S. Senate between October 7 and November 6, 2025 that explicitly reference Venezuela and require congressional authorization for U.S. military action against Venezuela under the War Powers Resolution. The first confirmed qualifying event within the window is Senate Joint Resolution 83 (introduced approximately Oct 7-8, 2025, voted down Oct 8-9), and a second distinct resolution was introduced on October 17, 2025 by Senators Kaine, Paul, and Schiff. Both are explicitly Venezuela-focused war powers measures requiring congressional authorization for military action — directly matching the resolution criteria. The October 17 resolution is the most clearly documented qualifying event with multiple high-quality sources confirming the introduction date.

question: Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”  if, Ukraine signs any written instrument (e.g., treaty, ceasefire/armistice, framework/“roadmap,” exchange of letters, or mediated agreement text) that: (i) includes both Ukraine and the Russian Federation as parties, and (ii) either ends hostilities/establishes a ceasefire or commits both sides to a defined process toward ending the war (i.e., stated objective of peace/normalization plus principles, steps, and/or a timetable) by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

Only Ukraine’s signature is required; Russia’s signature or ratification is not.

Localized, temporary, or issue-specific arrangements—such as airstrike-limitation or deconfliction protocols, humanitarian pauses, evacuation corridors, prisoner-exchange or trade/export arrangements, border/DMZ adjustments, or ceasefires limited to a particular sector/front/municipality—will not qualify.

The document must bear a wet-ink or officially issued electronic signature of an authorized Ukrainian representative. Unsigned agreements (e.g., the 2023 Ohrid arrangement) will not qualify regardless of if they are otherwise officially enacted. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine and Russia hold at least one publicly acknowledged in-person meeting at the foreign-minister level or higher between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
A key near-term indicator for whether Ukraine may sign a qualifying peace instrument by the end of 2025 is whether the parties escalate diplomacy to direct, senior-level in-person talks. As of late August 2025, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Vladimir Putin was prepared to meet Volodymyr Zelenskyy, but only after major issues were 'well worked out' and after questions about the legitimacy of the Ukrainian signatory were resolved, indicating that Moscow sees senior-level meetings as contingent on prior diplomatic progress rather than impossible in principle. Reuters reporting syndicated by MarketScreener summarized Lavrov's remarks on 2025-08-21: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Putin-prepared-to-meet-Zelenskiy-but-legitimacy-an-issue-Lavrov-says-50825485/ .

At the same time, Ukrainian and allied positions suggest a ceasefire-first approach and continued insistence that Ukraine be directly involved in any settlement. A Canada-Ukraine joint communiqué on 2025-08-24 called for an 'immediate, complete, and unconditional ceasefire as a first step toward launching a genuine peace process': https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/statement-joint-communique-between-canada-and-ukraine-843421705.html . Reporting in Ukrainska Pravda on 2025-08-18, citing the Financial Times, said Ukraine rejected territorial concessions and insisted on a ceasefire as the first step toward a full peace agreement: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/18/7522502/ .

This makes a publicly acknowledged in-person meeting at foreign-minister level or above a meaningful crux. Such a meeting would not itself be a peace deal, but it would be a concrete sign that preparatory issues have advanced enough for direct political negotiation. Conversely, the absence of any such meeting through October would be evidence that the process remains too stalled for a signed written peace instrument by year-end.

Sources:
MarketScreener / Reuters summary on Lavrov comments: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Putin-prepared-to-meet-Zelenskiy-but-legitimacy-an-issue-Lavrov-says-50825485/
Canada-Ukraine joint communiqué (CNW): https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/statement-joint-communique-between-canada-and-ukraine-843421705.html
Ukrainska Pravda on Ukraine rejecting territorial concessions: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/18/7522502/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if at least one in-person meeting between representatives of Ukraine and the Russian Federation at the rank of foreign minister or higher occurs between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, and the meeting is publicly acknowledged by credible reporting or official statements from either government during or after the window.

Qualifying participants on each side include: head of state, head of government, foreign minister, defense minister, or another official explicitly described by credible reporting as leading the country's delegation at equivalent or higher rank. At least one qualifying Ukrainian official and at least one qualifying Russian official must both be physically present at the same meeting.

A meeting counts whether bilateral or as part of a mediated format, summit, or multilateral gathering, so long as credible reporting states that Ukrainian and Russian qualifying officials met in person. Mere attendance at the same event without a reported meeting does not count. Telephone calls, video conferences, exchanged messages, shuttle diplomacy without face-to-face contact, lower-level technical talks, or meetings involving only non-state intermediaries do not count.

Primary sources for resolution will be consensus of credible reporting from major international news organizations such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), AFP (https://www.afp.com/), BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news), or official readouts from the Ukrainian presidency/government (https://www.president.gov.ua/en, https://www.kmu.gov.ua/en) and the Russian presidency/foreign ministry (http://en.kremlin.ru/, https://mid.ru/en/). If these sources conflict on whether an in-person meeting occurred, the question resolves according to the preponderance of detailed, specific reporting. If a meeting is announced for the window but is postponed beyond 2025-10-31, this question resolves No. If reporting is insufficient to determine whether a qualifying in-person meeting occurred, the question should be treated as unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Senior direct diplomacy is a strong process indicator for a possible signed peace instrument by year-end. A publicly acknowledged foreign-minister-or-higher in-person meeting would suggest that bargaining has progressed beyond public posturing and that political principals are actively shaping terms, increasing the likelihood of a later written agreement. Its absence through October would be negative evidence for a 2025 signing.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: at least one in-person meeting between (1) a qualifying Ukrainian official (head of state, head of government, foreign minister, defense minister, or equivalent delegation leader) AND (2) a qualifying Russian official at the same rank, both physically present at the same location, during October 1-31, 2025. Observable evidence: credible reporting from major international news organizations or official government readouts confirming the meeting occurred.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Ukraine Russia foreign minister meeting in-person October 2025' — to find direct bilateral meetings; Query 2: 'Zelensky Putin meeting October 2025' — to find head-of-state level contacts; Query 3: 'Ukraine Russia direct talks negotiations meeting October 2025' — to find any diplomatic meeting format; Query 4: 'Sybiha Lavrov meeting bilateral talks 2025' — to find FM-level bilateral meetings; Query 5: 'Ukraine Russia peace talks Istanbul bilateral meeting October 2025' — to find negotiation-format meetings; Query 6: 'Zelensky Putin direct meeting summit October 2025' — to find summit-level contacts
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Istanbul negotiation process rounds — declared 'on hold' by Kremlin as of early October 2025, no new round in October; (2) Planned Budapest Trump-Putin summit — canceled/postponed before end of October, and even if held would not be a Ukraine-Russia direct meeting; (3) Ukrainian FM Sybiha attended EU Foreign Affairs Council on October 20 — met EU officials, not Russian officials; (4) Russian FM Lavrov met with Morocco FM (Oct 16), Ethiopia FM (Oct 21), Kazakhstan FM (Oct 22), North Korea FM (Oct 27) — none involving Ukraine; (5) Remains transfer announced October 23 — humanitarian/technical exchange, not a high-level political meeting; (6) Planned trilateral Budapest meeting (Zelensky+Trump+Putin) — never materialized within October window; All candidates rejected as not meeting criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event satisfies the criteria. The Kremlin explicitly stated that 'a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy can only be prepared through expert-level talks' and that 'the negotiation process between Moscow and Kyiv is currently paused' [Kremlin via APA.AZ, Oct 1](https://en.apa.az/cis-countries/kremlin-expert-level-talks-needed-before-any-putin-zelenskyy-meeting-479374). The Istanbul process was 'on hold' as of October 10 [Yahoo News, Oct 10](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/kremlin-says-istanbul-negotiation-process-114522204.html). The Kremlin ruled out 'direct talks with Zelensky until a peace deal is practically agreed upon' [Macau Business, Oct 21](https://www.macaubusiness.com/russia-downplays-swift-meeting-to-prepare-for-trump-putin-summit/). Ukrainian FM Sybiha briefed EU council on October 20 but met no Russian officials [Ukrainska Pravda, Oct 20](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/10/20/8003548/). Russian FM Lavrov's meetings in October were exclusively with non-Ukrainian counterparts.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found for any in-person Ukraine-Russia meeting at the required level during October 1-31, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found in the window. The previous direct talks occurred in the Istanbul/Alaska format prior to October 2025 (last mentioned round: August 15, 2025 at Alaska military base), and those were on pause during the entire October 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked multiple angles: (1) No contradictory evidence found suggesting a Ukraine-Russia in-person meeting at FM level or higher occurred in October 2025; (2) Multiple sources consistently confirm talks were paused; (3) The only 'meeting' discussions during October involved a potential Trump-Putin-Zelensky trilateral in Budapest that was never scheduled and ultimately did not happen; (4) The remains transfer on October 23 was a humanitarian/technical exchange, not a qualifying high-level political meeting; (5) All FM Lavrov meetings in October were with non-Ukrainian counterparts.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence conclusively shows that no in-person meeting between qualifying Ukrainian and Russian officials at foreign minister level or higher occurred during October 1-31, 2025. The Istanbul negotiation process was explicitly on pause, the Kremlin ruled out direct Zelensky-Putin talks, and Ukrainian/Russian foreign ministers were engaged in meetings exclusively with third-party officials during this period. The window closed on October 31, 2025 with no qualifying meeting having occurred.

question: Will Eric Adams drop out?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Eric Adams withdraws from or officially announces his withdrawal from the 2025 New York City Mayoral election, or announces the suspension of his 2025 NYC Mayoral campaign, by November 3, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Eric Adams or his official/legal representatives, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Eric Adams publicly endorse or sign on to a candidate-consolidation plan that commits him to withdraw if he is not the leading anti-Mamdani candidate by 2025-09-25?
subquestions.background_information:
A key live issue in the 2025 NYC mayoral race is whether non-Democratic candidates will consolidate to avoid splitting the anti-Mamdani vote. Multiple reports say Andrew Cuomo and Jim Walden have expressed willingness to step aside under certain conditions, while Eric Adams has notably declined to join such a pledge. NY1 / Spectrum News reported on 2025-07-18 that Cuomo and Adams were each calling on the other to drop out, and that Walden had proposed a poll-driven consolidation mechanism; Adams said instead that Cuomo and Curtis Sliwa should rally behind him. https://nystateofpolitics.com/state-of-politics/new-york/politics/2025/07/18/adams--cuomo-call-on-each-other-to-drop-out

A 2025-07-25 report said Cuomo and Walden had pledged to drop their independent bids if they were not leading in polls by early September, but Adams had declined to join that pledge. https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/andrew-cuomo-jim-walden-pledge-to-drop-independent-bids-in-nyc-mayoral-race-if-not-leading-come-fall

Separately, reporting on 2025-08-06 described Adams and Cuomo as still refusing to drop out, despite pressure to coalesce around a single challenger to Zohran Mamdani. https://www.wbap.com/2025/08/06/adams-cuomo-refuse-to-drop-out-of-nyc-mayoral-race/

This matters for the ultimate question because a public commitment by Adams to a measurable consolidation mechanism would be a strong early indicator that he is open to exiting the race if he lacks a viable path. Conversely, continued refusal to join any such plan suggests a lower likelihood of withdrawal by the ultimate market deadline.

Sources:
Spectrum News NY1 / State of Politics: https://nystateofpolitics.com/state-of-politics/new-york/politics/2025/07/18/adams--cuomo-call-on-each-other-to-drop-out
DonaldJTrump.com article mirror: https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/andrew-cuomo-jim-walden-pledge-to-drop-independent-bids-in-nyc-mayoral-race-if-not-leading-come-fall
WBAP 820 AM: https://www.wbap.com/2025/08/06/adams-cuomo-refuse-to-drop-out-of-nyc-mayoral-race/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-25 inclusive, Eric Adams or his official campaign publicly states that he is joining, endorsing, or signing a candidate-consolidation arrangement under which he would withdraw, suspend, or support another non-Mamdani candidate if he is not the leader under a specified metric (for example: a named poll, a polling average, a head-to-head survey, or another explicitly defined determination method).

Qualifying statements must be attributable to at least one of the following: (a) Eric Adams directly, via a public speech, interview, debate, press release, campaign website post, or official social-media account; or (b) an official Adams campaign spokesperson or legal representative speaking on the record. Mere discussion of unity, attacks on vote-splitting, or calls for others to drop out do NOT qualify unless Adams explicitly commits himself to a plan that could require his own withdrawal.

The primary sources for resolution will be Eric Adams's official campaign website and official social-media accounts, plus on-the-record reporting from major NYC outlets. Relevant sources include:
- Eric Adams campaign / official statements if available
- Eric Adams X account: https://x.com/ericadamsfornyc
- Eric Adams campaign website: https://www.ericadamsfornyc.com/
- NY1 / Spectrum News political coverage: https://nystateofpolitics.com/
- Gothamist: https://gothamist.com/
- THE CITY: https://www.thecity.nyc/
- New York Daily News: https://www.nydailynews.com/

If no qualifying public commitment is made between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-25 inclusive, resolve No.

If reporting claims Adams joined such a plan but no public statement or attributable on-the-record confirmation from Adams or his official campaign can be found, resolve based on the best consensus of at least two credible outlets quoting the commitment. If the evidence remains too ambiguous to determine whether Adams actually committed himself to a withdrawal-triggering plan, this question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Adams agrees in advance to a clear consolidation mechanism is a strong crux for whether he will later drop out. Joining such a plan would indicate willingness to subordinate his candidacy to coalition strategy, substantially increasing the chance of eventual withdrawal; refusing to do so is evidence in the opposite direction.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Eric Adams or official campaign must publicly commit (via speech, interview, press release, social media, or on-record spokesperson) to a candidate-consolidation arrangement specifying he would withdraw if he is NOT the leading anti-Mamdani candidate per a defined metric (poll, polling average, head-to-head survey, etc.). Period: Sept 1-25, 2025. Mere calls for others to drop out or vague unity language does NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Eric Adams candidate consolidation withdrawal plan Mamdani NYC mayor 2025' — to find any formal consolidation plan Adams joined; 2) 'Eric Adams drop out withdraw NYC mayor race 2025 unity plan' — to find any withdrawal commitment; 3) 'Eric Adams consolidation agreement sign withdraw poll leading anti-Mamdani September 2025' — to find a specific metric-based commitment; 4) 'Eric Adams suspend campaign endorse another candidate anti-Mamdani pact September 2025' — to find any formal endorsement of consolidation; 5) 'Eric Adams drops out NYC mayor race September 2025' — to check if he dropped out (which might imply prior commitment); 6) 'Eric Adams poll numbers metric withdrawal commitment signed agreement September 2025' — to find any signed agreement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) Jim Walden dropped out Sept 2 and called on others including Adams to consolidate — Adams REJECTED this; (b) Trump allegedly floated job offers to Adams to get him to drop out — Adams denied any formal offers and rejected the idea; (c) Adams mentioned an internal poll at a private ABNY meeting saying 'if my poll numbers don't improve, I would prioritize the interests of the city' — this was vague, private, not a formal commitment; (d) Adams repeatedly held press conferences affirming he was staying in the race (Sept 5, 12, 15-16); (e) Adams was MIA from events Sept 19-24 sparking rumors, but no formal announcement made. All candidate events for a 'Yes' resolution were REJECTED as not satisfying criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of Adams explicitly committing to a consolidation plan with a withdrawal trigger. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/nyc-mayor-jim-walden-zohran-mamdani-729776ee8294a3f18ad5258cb0f22fa8): 'none accepted the proposal' referring to Walden's consolidation challenge. [NBC New York](https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/politics/adams-no-formal-job-offers-from-trump-says-hes-still-in-running-for-nyc-mayor/6385249/): Adams said 'No pressure, no diamonds' and rejected calls to drop out. [Daily News](https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/09/12/as-mayor-adams-tours-the-bronx-he-blasts-reports-hes-considering-dropping-out-of-the-race/): internal poll was for 'messaging' not to decide withdrawal. [News 12](https://longisland.news12.com/spokesperson-for-mayor-adams-denies-he-will-drop-out-of-race): spokesperson called dropout rumors 'complete bullshit' on Sept 15. No source documents Adams signing or endorsing a conditional withdrawal pact with a defined metric.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no qualifying event occurred within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event was found at all during the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: Yahoo article mentioned Adams privately said at an ABNY event 'if my poll numbers don't improve, I would prioritize the interests of the city' — but this falls short of the resolution criteria because: (1) it was at a private meeting, not a public speech/interview/press release/social media post; (2) it didn't specify a metric, named poll, or consolidation arrangement; (3) it didn't constitute a commitment to support or defer to another specific anti-Mamdani candidate. Adams' own public statements consistently denied consolidation pacts. Through Sept 24-25, Adams had still not dropped out or committed to any formal plan.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Adams repeatedly and explicitly rejected all consolidation challenges, denied dropout rumors, and made no public commitment to any withdrawal-triggering plan during Sept 1-25, 2025. Resolution is No. Since no qualifying event occurred and Adams was still in the race at the end of the window, the No conclusion is confirmed at the window close of Sept 25, 2025.

question: Will Taylor Swift be the top Spotify artist for 2025?
description:
Spotify releases an annual report of its most streamed artist (see: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2024-12-04/top-songs-artists-podcasts-audiobooks-albums-trends-2024/). This market refers to the most streamed Spotify artist for 2025. 

If the above-listed artists are the most streamed Spotify artist for 2025, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Spotify does not release who their top artist for 2025 is by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No". 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Spotify, typically released as part of Spotify Wrapped.

subquestions.question: Will Taylor Swift's album "The Life of a Showgirl" debut with at least 250 million Spotify streams worldwide in its first 7 full days after release?
subquestions.background_information:
Taylor Swift is the reigning top global Spotify artist for 2024, with Spotify reporting 26.6 billion streams for her across the year, which makes her a natural contender to repeat in 2025 if a major late-year release performs strongly. Spotify's 2024 Wrapped announcement names her the year's top artist: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2024-12-04/top-songs-artists-podcasts-audiobooks-albums-trends-2024/

A major new album is especially relevant because the ultimate question concerns total 2025 Spotify streams, and late-year blockbuster releases can add very large volumes quickly. Multiple 2025 reports state that Swift's new album, "The Life of a Showgirl," is scheduled for release on 2025-10-03 and had already become the most pre-saved album in Spotify Countdown Page history before release, suggesting unusually strong launch demand. See Euronews: https://www.euronews.com/culture/2025/09/02/taylor-swift-already-breaks-spotify-record-before-release-of-new-album and Digital Music News: https://www.digitalmusicnews.com/2025/09/02/taylor-swift-new-album-breaks-spotify-pre-save-record/

Swift's prior album, "The Tortured Poets Department," set extremely high Spotify launch benchmarks: Spotify said it became the first album to cross 300 million streams in a single day, and other reporting cited 1 billion streams within five days. Spotify announced the 300 million one-day mark here: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2024-04-19/taylor-swifts-the-tortured-poets-department-breaks-records-on-spotify/ . Euronews summarizes both milestones here: https://www.euronews.com/culture/2025/09/02/taylor-swift-already-breaks-spotify-record-before-release-of-new-album

A threshold of 250 million streams in the first 7 full days is therefore meaningful but not trivial. It is lower than the extraordinary launch pace of "The Tortured Poets Department," while still high enough that a Yes outcome would be evidence that Swift is generating enough late-2025 Spotify volume to remain highly competitive for the full-year top-artist title.

Sources:
Spotify Newsroom - 2024 Wrapped top artists: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2024-12-04/top-songs-artists-podcasts-audiobooks-albums-trends-2024/
Spotify Newsroom - The Tortured Poets Department breaks records: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2024-04-19/taylor-swifts-the-tortured-poets-department-breaks-records-on-spotify/
Euronews - Swift breaks Spotify pre-save record: https://www.euronews.com/culture/2025/09/02/taylor-swift-already-breaks-spotify-record-before-release-of-new-album
Digital Music News - New album breaks Spotify pre-save record: https://www.digitalmusicnews.com/2025/09/02/taylor-swift-new-album-breaks-spotify-pre-save-record/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if authoritative public reporting from Spotify states that Taylor Swift's album "The Life of a Showgirl" accumulated at least 250,000,000 Spotify streams worldwide during its first 7 full days after release, where the qualifying release and measurement window must begin between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive. For avoidance of doubt, because the album is reportedly scheduled for release on 2025-10-03, the relevant 7-day measurement window would ordinarily be the first 7 full days following that release.

Primary resolution source: official Spotify communications, including Spotify Newsroom posts or official Spotify social accounts: https://newsroom.spotify.com/ and https://x.com/Spotify

If Spotify does not publish a clear 7-day total, the question resolves Yes based on a report from a major music-industry outlet that explicitly attributes the 7-day Spotify total to Spotify, Universal, Republic, or another rights-holder with direct access to the data. Acceptable secondary sources include Billboard (https://www.billboard.com/), Variety (https://variety.com/), Music Business Worldwide (https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/), or Digital Music News (https://www.digitalmusicnews.com/).

This question resolves No if, by 2025-10-31 23:59:59 UTC, no qualifying authoritative source reports a first-7-days Spotify total of at least 250,000,000 streams for the album.

If the album's Spotify release is postponed to after 2025-10-31, or if no authoritative source publishes sufficient information to determine whether the threshold was met by 2025-10-31, this question should be considered unresolvable.

subquestions.background_information:
A key near-term indicator for whether Governor Tim Walz might resign is whether he escalates from rhetorical accountability to personnel accountability. As of late December 2025, Walz has publicly acknowledged responsibility for fraud occurring "on my watch" and announced a new statewide fraud-prevention program led by Tim O’Malley on December 12, 2025, but reporting indicates critics argue that no senior officials had yet been fired over the scandal. See Alpha News' Dec. 12 report on the program and appointment of O’Malley: https://alphanews.org/walz-creates-new-fraud-prevention-program-says-i-just-fix-these-things-amid-widening-scandal/ . The scandal environment had intensified by late December. House Oversight Chair James Comer said on Dec. 23 that a federal investigation was expanding, involving subpoenas and whistleblower testimony, while more than 100 Minnesota mayors and state legislators had signed a letter criticizing fiscal mismanagement: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/comer-warns-walls-caving-tim-walz-minnesota-fraud-probe-widens . Secretary of Education Linda McMahon publicly called on Walz to resign in a Dec. 15 letter over alleged fraud involving 1,834 "ghost students" and $12.5 million in grants and loans, according to the U.S. Department of Education press release page: https://www.ed.gov/ . A public escalation by Walz against top appointees would be a meaningful signal that the crisis is worsening internally and that he is under acute political pressure; such moves often precede, or reduce the need for, a leader’s own resignation.

This subquestion is not a restatement of whether Walz resigns. Instead, it tracks a distinct observable event: whether Walz takes highly visible disciplinary action against top executive officials. If he does, forecasters may update upward on the seriousness of the scandal and instability of his governorship. If he does not, that may suggest he still expects to remain in office and manage the controversy politically.

question: Ukraine recognizes Russian sovereignty over its territory by December 31, 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to formally recognize Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement. 

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory for any amount of time will count.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995, “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia, which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement, is an example of a qualifying agreement.

An official unilateral pledge by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution even if not part of an agreement with Russia.

The April 19, 2013, Brussels Agreement between Serbia and Kosovo, in which Serbia recognized Kosovo’s de facto administration but did not formally grant de jure recognition, would not be considered a qualifying agreement under this market, as this market requires formal recognition of sovereignty rather than acknowledgment of administrative control.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will President Volodymyr Zelenskyy or Ukraine's Verkhovna Rada publicly state between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that a nationwide referendum would be required before Ukraine could formally recognize Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory?
subquestions.background_information:
A key obstacle to the ultimate question is not just diplomatic willingness, but whether Ukrainian leaders frame formal territorial recognition as constitutionally or politically impossible without a referendum. In April 2025, President Zelenskyy publicly rejected recognizing Crimea as Russian, and multiple reports noted that Ukrainian officials viewed formal territorial surrender as incompatible with Ukraine's constitution and political red lines. Euronews reported on 2025-04-23 that Zelenskyy opposed a proposal involving recognition of Russian control over Ukrainian land and that the EU reaffirmed that 'Crimea is Ukraine' (https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/04/23/brussels-rejects-russian-recognition-of-crimea-and-sanctions-relief). Yahoo reported on 2025-04-27 that Ukrainian officials said the government had 'no constitutional means' to accept violation of territorial integrity and that altering Ukraine's territory requires a nationwide referendum (https://www.yahoo.com/news/shocked-us-peace-proposal-ukrainians-040834020.html). The Kyiv Independent likewise reported unanimous opposition among Ukrainian lawmakers to de jure recognition of Crimea and quoted lawmakers saying the constitution does not provide for recognizing seized territories as belonging to another country (https://kyivindependent.com/dangerous-and-cruel-trumps-reported-crimea-proposal-sparks-horror-among-ukraines-lawmakers/). 

If, in the next month, Zelenskyy or the Rada publicly reiterates that a referendum is required for any formal recognition of Russian sovereignty, that would be evidence that institutional and domestic constraints remain strong, reducing the near-term chance of the ultimate event. Conversely, the absence of such statements would not by itself imply recognition is likely, but an affirmative statement would be a meaningful crux because it points to a concrete procedural barrier that would make a 2025 recognition deal harder.

Sources:
Euronews - Brussels rejects Russian recognition of Crimea and sanctions relief - https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/04/23/brussels-rejects-russian-recognition-of-crimea-and-sanctions-relief
Yahoo News - Shocked by US peace proposal, Ukrainians say they will not accept any formal surrender of Crimea - https://www.yahoo.com/news/shocked-us-peace-proposal-ukrainians-040834020.html
Kyiv Independent - 'Dangerous and cruel' — Trump's reported Crimea proposal sparks horror among Ukraine's lawmakers - https://kyivindependent.com/dangerous-and-cruel-trumps-reported-crimea-proposal-sparks-horror-among-ukraines-lawmakers/
President of Ukraine official website - https://www.president.gov.ua/en
Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine official website - https://www.rada.gov.ua/

For Yes, the statement must clearly connect the referendum requirement to formal recognition of Russian sovereignty over Ukrainian territory; general statements about constitutional constraints, territorial integrity, or red lines are not sufficient unless they specifically say a referendum is required for such recognition.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying statement is published during the window from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 inclusive.

Primary sources for resolution are the official website of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en) and the official Verkhovna Rada website (https://www.rada.gov.ua/). As a fallback, if a qualifying statement is first made in a live appearance and the official transcript is delayed or unavailable, resolution may rely on at least two concordant reports from major credible outlets quoting the statement directly, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), or BBC (https://www.bbc.com/), provided the statement itself clearly satisfies the wording standard above. If publication timing is ambiguous, Kyiv local time controls for whether the statement occurred within 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 inclusive.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends heavily on whether Ukraine can politically and legally make a formal sovereignty concession. A fresh public insistence that a referendum is required would signal that any recognition deal faces a major domestic procedural hurdle, making the ultimate Yes less likely by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Zelenskyy (via president.gov.ua or official statement) OR Verkhovna Rada (via rada.gov.ua or official statement) explicitly states that a NATIONWIDE REFERENDUM IS REQUIRED before Ukraine can FORMALLY RECOGNIZE RUSSIAN SOVEREIGNTY over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory.
