evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Putin (September 3-5, 2025) cited Ukraine's constitution saying territorial questions require referendum — REJECTED: this is Putin/Russia's statement, not Zelenskyy/Verkhovna Rada. (2) Zelenskyy September 26 Axios interview: 'We will never recognize these territories that are temporarily occupied by Russia. We cannot do this.' — REJECTED: this is a refusal to recognize, not a statement that a referendum is required for such recognition. (3) Verkhovna Rada Chairman Stefanchuk said 'concessions on territory or sovereignty are unacceptable' — REJECTED: general statement about concessions, not specifically about referendum requirement for recognition. (4) An opinion piece cited Ukraine's constitution requiring a referendum for territorial change — REJECTED: not an official statement by Zelenskyy or Verkhovna Rada. No candidate event found that explicitly connects a referendum requirement to formal recognition of Russian sovereignty from the qualifying sources.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No statement found from Zelenskyy ([president.gov.ua](https://www.president.gov.ua/en)) or the Verkhovna Rada ([rada.gov.ua](https://www.rada.gov.ua/)) that explicitly states 'a nationwide referendum is required before Ukraine could formally recognize Russian sovereignty over any part of Ukrainian territory.' The referendum language in September 2025 came exclusively from Putin and Russian officials. Ukrainian officials categorically refused recognition but did not frame their position in terms of a referendum requirement. Zelenskyy's September 26 statement ('We will never recognize these territories') does not satisfy the criteria because it doesn't specifically say a referendum is required for such recognition.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying statement with a reliable timestamp was found within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at all within the window, making the first-occurrence check moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: Putin repeatedly cited Ukraine's constitution's referendum requirement for territorial changes, but this was Putin's argument — not a statement from Ukrainian officials. Zelenskyy's statements during the window consistently rejected recognition outright without framing it as a referendum requirement. Stefanchuk (Verkhovna Rada Chairman) made similar statements about territorial integrity without invoking a referendum requirement for recognition. The Daily Sabah opinion piece mentioned Ukraine's constitution requires a referendum for territorial change, but this is an opinion piece — not an official statement from qualifying sources. No qualifying statement exists from Zelenskyy or the Verkhovna Rada within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Despite extensive searching, no statement was found from either Zelenskyy or the Verkhovna Rada within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window explicitly stating that a nationwide referendum is required before Ukraine could formally recognize Russian sovereignty over any Ukrainian territory. Ukrainian officials during this period uniformly took a position of outright refusal to recognize Russian sovereignty rather than framing the issue as requiring a referendum. The referendum language came exclusively from Putin and Russian officials. The window closed on October 1, 2025 with no qualifying statement published.

1. Taylor Swift makes at least one new in-person public appearance documented by date-stamped photo or video coverage from a major reputable outlet (for example AP, Getty Images, Reuters, People, Vogue, Billboard, ELLE, TMZ, or equivalent major entertainment/news outlet); and
2. Within 72 hours of that appearance, at least two distinct major reputable entertainment/news outlets explicitly state that the appearance is fueling, prompting, or renewing pregnancy speculation about Swift, with the claim tied specifically to her clothing, silhouette, or apparent attempt to conceal her midsection.

This question resolves No if no such appearance-and-coverage combination occurs between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

Resolution should rely first on publicly accessible coverage from major outlets and image-wire services such as Getty Images (https://www.gettyimages.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), People (https://people.com/), Billboard (https://www.billboard.com/), and ELLE (https://www.elle.com/). Fact-check outlets such as Snopes (https://www.snopes.com/) may be used secondarily to determine whether speculation was widespread but false.

Interpretation notes:
- The question is about media interpretation, not whether Swift is actually pregnant.
- Mere social-media fan chatter, TikTok speculation, tabloid comment sections, or isolated low-credibility blogs do not count.
- The outlets must explicitly connect the appearance to pregnancy speculation; vague statements like 'fans are talking' without mention of pregnancy do not count.
- If purported coverage is based on AI-generated or manipulated imagery later debunked by a credible fact-check, it does not count.
- If an appearance begins before 2025-10-01 or after 2025-10-31 UTC-equivalent local date, it does not count unless the qualifying documented appearance itself occurs within the window.
- If source pages become unavailable, archived versions and substantially similar reports from other major outlets may be used as fallback evidence.

Primary sources for resolution methodology:
AP News: https://apnews.com/
Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
Getty Images: https://www.gettyimages.com/
People: https://people.com/
Billboard: https://www.billboard.com/
ELLE: https://www.elle.com/
Snopes: https://www.snopes.com/
subquestions.rationale: A credible burst of pregnancy speculation tied to a new October public appearance would be an early observable signal that often precedes celebrity pregnancy announcements, while still being distinct from the ultimate question of whether Swift herself announces a pregnancy in 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes resolution, need: (1) A dated public appearance by Taylor Swift between Oct 1-31, 2025, documented by a major outlet with Swift wearing a visibly loose or concealing outfit; AND (2) within 72 hours of that appearance, at least two distinct major reputable entertainment/news outlets explicitly stating the appearance is fueling/prompting/renewing pregnancy speculation tied specifically to her clothing, silhouette, or apparent attempt to conceal her midsection. Key constraint: outfit must be 'visibly loose or concealing' — not fitted/tight. Outlets must be major (AP, Getty, Reuters, People, Vogue, Billboard, ELLE, TMZ, or equivalent). Social media chatter alone does not count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Taylor Swift pregnancy speculation October 2025 outfit' - to find any pregnancy-speculation stories tied to her appearance; 2) 'Taylor Swift public appearance October 2025' - to catalog her October appearances; 3) 'Taylor Swift pregnancy bump concealing outfit October 2025 entertainment outlets' - to find explicit major-outlet coverage; 4) 'Taylor Swift tight black top miniskirt pregnancy rumors October 12 2025' - to investigate The Blast article; 5) 'Taylor Swift pregnancy baby bump October 12 NYC night out outfit fueling speculation People Billboard' - to find second outlet; 6) 'Taylor Swift oversized concealing outfit pregnancy speculation clothing midsection 2025' - to find qualifying appearance; 7) 'Taylor Swift pregnancy video restaurant October 22 2025 baby bump figure' - to investigate the Oct 22-23 viral video event; 8) 'Taylor Swift Chiefs game oversized jersey pregnancy speculation October 2025' - to check game appearances.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Oct 12 NYC night out - The Blast article 'Taylor Swift Pregnant in Tight Top And Schoolgirl Miniskirt' - REJECTED because outfit is described as TIGHT, not loose/concealing; (B) Oct 9 TVOvermind article about TikTok doctor speculating pregnancy from facial appearance - REJECTED because (1) not tied to clothing/midsection concealment, (2) TikTok doctor is social media figure not major outlet; (C) Oct 22-23 MARCA/The News International viral video of Swift leaving restaurant after Chiefs win, fans speculating on changed figure - PARTIALLY QUALIFYING but: outfit not described as loose/concealing, articles frame it as debunking fan speculation not as fueling it, outlets may not meet the 'major reputable' threshold matching the criteria; (D) Oct 12 Chiefs game - Swift wore 'oversized mini dress' by Ganni - REJECTED because coverage focused on her engagement ring and team tribute, NOT pregnancy speculation; (E) Oct 3 Distractify article about fans convinced Swift is pregnant - REJECTED because it does not connect a specific appearance with a concealing/loose outfit as the trigger.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Blast article [https://theblast.com/734220/taylor-swift-pregnant-in-top-and-schoolgirl-miniskirt/] - published Oct 12, 2025 - describes a tight black top and miniskirt, NOT a loose or concealing outfit. This fails the 'visibly loose or concealing outfit' requirement. MARCA article [https://www.marca.com/en/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/2025/10/22/68f942a922601d6e058b45ff.html] and The News International [https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1353013-is-taylor-swift-pregnant-fans-ignite-internet-debate] (both published Oct 22-23) cover viral video pregnancy speculation, but (1) neither article explicitly describes the outfit as loose or concealing, (2) both articles actually debunk the speculation rather than promulgate it, (3) the specification requires two outlets explicitly stating the appearance is 'fueling, prompting, or renewing' pregnancy speculation. TVOvermind [https://tvovermind.com/doctor-suggests-taylor-swift-pregnant-visible-changes-viral-video/] is about facial appearance, not clothing/midsection. No appearance in the window with a visibly loose/concealing outfit that two major outlets explicitly connected to pregnancy speculation tied to her clothing/silhouette/midsection within 72 hours was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp was found. The closest event (Oct 12 The Blast article) fails the outfit description criteria. The Oct 22-23 viral video event lacks clear outfit documentation as 'loose or concealing' and is covered by only one outlet (MARCA + The News International, which appears to aggregate the same story).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found in the window. All candidate events fail one or more mandatory criteria.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Swift's October appearances throughout the month were extensively covered by major outlets (Harper's BAZAAR, Us Weekly, People, HELLO!, E! Online, Cosmopolitan) with detailed outfit descriptions - all described fitted, tight, or form-fitting outfits (mini dresses, tight bodices, silver chainmail dress, turtleneck with leather skirt). None of these coverage pieces connected her outfits to pregnancy speculation. The only pregnancy speculation tied to an outfit was The Blast's Oct 12 article about a tight top and miniskirt - which explicitly fails the 'loose or concealing' criteria. Multiple sources (Distractify, TVOvermind) address pregnancy speculation but not tied to loose/concealing clothing triggering the speculation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No qualifying appearance-and-coverage combination occurred within the Oct 1-31, 2025 window. Swift made numerous public appearances documented by major outlets, but none involved a 'visibly loose or concealing outfit' that two distinct major reputable outlets explicitly connected to pregnancy speculation about her midsection within 72 hours. The window closed without the required criteria being met.

question: Will Russia capture Kupiansk by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the Kup'yans'k-Pivdennyi railroad station located on Pryvokzalna vulytsia by October 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET.

The railroad station will be considered captured if any part of the train station icon is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to “No”.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of if it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement which gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

Once Russia captures the railroad station, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

Train Station Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/Kupiansk+train+station.jpeg

Kupiansk Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/Kupiansk+location.jpeg

Location on Google maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/9Pt8PPbQvWLerHLr6

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map which will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will the ISW control map show any part of Kupiansk's city-center administrative district west of the Oskil River shaded red by 2025-10-26?
subquestions.background_information:
This is an early-indicator question for whether Russia can capture the Kupiansk-Pivdennyi railroad station by the end of October. The station is in the urban area of Kupiansk, and meaningful Russian progress into the city center west of the Oskil River would be strong evidence that Russian forces are overcoming Ukrainian defenses in the parts of the city they would likely need to traverse or suppress to take and hold the station. Recent reporting suggests Russian forces have been active in and around Kupiansk, including infiltration routes and contested urban footholds, but that claims of broad control remain disputed. DeepState-linked reporting on 2025-09-12 said Russian forces had used a gas pipeline network to infiltrate toward the outskirts of Kupiansk and reach the railway area, indicating at least some operational intent toward rail-linked objectives in the city (https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/09/12/7510145/). On 2025-09-17, Ukrainian Pravda reported DeepState-assessed Russian advances in eastern Kupiansk and near Holubivka, while also noting Ukraine's General Staff said Ukrainian forces still controlled Kupiansk and surrounding areas (https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/09/17/7510840/). Reuters-syndicated reporting from early September described Russian claims of having captured 'about half' of Kupiansk, but noted Ukraine denied those claims and that independent verification was lacking (https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-says-it-captures-about-half-ukrainian-city-kupiansk-kyiv-denies-report-2025-09-03/). The Moscow Times, summarizing open-source and satellite-based assessments, reported on 2025-09-17 that Russia controlled only about 6.3% of the built-up areas of Kupiansk and that much of the city remained a contested 'grey zone,' which implies city-center west-bank penetration would be a nontrivial additional step beyond the status quo (https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2025/09/17/russia-inflates-battlefield-gains-after-a-costly-summer-offensive-a90444). The ISW map is the same primary source used by the ultimate market and therefore provides a consistent observable for a crux question about near-term battlefield geometry (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375).

Sources:
ISW Ukraine map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
Ukrainska Pravda (pipeline infiltration / railway): https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/09/12/7510145/
Ukrainska Pravda (DeepState advances near Kupiansk): https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/09/17/7510840/
Reuters (Russian claim about half of Kupiansk): https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-says-it-captures-about-half-ukrainian-city-kupiansk-kyiv-denies-report-2025-09-03/
The Moscow Times (6.3% built-up area assessment): https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2025/09/17/russia-inflates-battlefield-gains-after-a-costly-summer-offensive-a90444
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-26 (inclusive), the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) Ukraine control-of-terrain map shows any red-shaded Russian-controlled area west of the Oskil River inside the built-up central Kupiansk urban area that includes the city-administration/city-center blocks. For operational clarity, resolvers should use the ISW interactive/story map at https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 and compare it against standard basemaps (e.g. Google Maps, OpenStreetMap) to determine whether any red polygon overlaps the dense central urban area west of the river around central Kupiansk streets and municipal core. 

This question resolves No if no such red-shaded overlap appears on any ISW map update published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-26 (inclusive).

Primary source: ISW Ukraine map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375

Interpretation notes:
1. 'West of the Oskil River' means the portion of Kupiansk on the west bank of the river visible on standard maps.
2. 'City-center administrative district' is intended to exclude tiny isolated western-bank footholds on peripheral industrial or forested edges and instead capture meaningful penetration into the central built-up urban core. If ISW's red shading clearly overlaps blocks around the municipal center of west-bank Kupiansk, resolve Yes.
3. Yellow/contested, hatch marks, arrows, reported claims, or unit icons without red territorial shading do not count.
4. A temporary rendering glitch on ISW that is later corrected should not count.
5. If ISW becomes permanently unavailable before 2025-10-26, the fallback source is DeepStateMap at https://deepstatemap.live/. Under fallback, resolve Yes if DeepState's Russian-control coloring clearly shows control in the same west-bank central urban area during the same window. If both maps become permanently unavailable, use a consensus of credible reporting plus archived map captures.
6. If available evidence is insufficient to determine whether the red area reached the defined central west-bank urban core during the 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-26 window, the question should be treated as unresolvable rather than guessed.

Auxiliary location references:
Google Maps (Kupiansk): https://maps.app.goo.gl/9Pt8PPbQvWLerHLr6
OpenStreetMap (Kupiansk): https://www.openstreetmap.org/
DeepStateMap fallback: https://deepstatemap.live/
subquestions.rationale: A visible Russian move into the west-bank city center would be a strong crux for the ultimate station-capture question without merely restating it. It measures whether Russia is converting infiltration and edge advances into consolidated urban control in the part of Kupiansk that matters for broader city seizure. If this happens by October 26, forecasters should update upward on the chance that the railroad station falls by October 31; if it does not, that is evidence the offensive is stalling short of decisive urban penetration.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: ISW Ukraine control-of-terrain map must show red-shaded Russian-controlled area west of Oskil River inside the built-up central Kupiansk urban area during Oct 1–26, 2025. Observable evidence required: direct citation of ISW map showing red polygon overlapping Kupiansk city-center blocks on west bank. Key entities: ISW ArcGIS map, Kupiansk city center (west bank), Oskil River, red shading (not grey/contested). The question excludes peripheral footholds and requires meaningful penetration into the municipal core.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Kupiansk Russian forces west bank Oskil River October 2025' — to find ground situation; 2) 'Kupiansk city center Russian control ISW map 2025' — to find ISW-specific map evidence; 3) 'ISW Kupiansk Russian control west bank city center October 2025' — ISW-specific; 4) 'Kupiansk Yubileyny district west bank Russian occupation ISW 2025' — specific district search; 5) 'ISW daily update Kupiansk October 2025 territorial control map' — ISW daily reports; 6) 'Kupiansk right bank west bank Russian troops occupied city center 2025' — geographic specificity; 7) 'ISW Kupiansk northern half high-rise buildings control October 2025' — UK MoD/ISW specific; 8) 'Kupiansk city center Russian control October 2025 DeepState ISW' — both sources.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) DeepState Oct 20 report of 'expanded control in central part of Kupiansk' [Interfax-Ukraine, Ukrainska Pravda]; (B) British MoD Oct 16 'captured most high-rise buildings in northern half' of Kupiansk; (C) RT Oct 24 claims Russian control of 'city center, railway station, and Yubileyny district'; (D) DW Oct 9 'Russian soldiers now occupy the city'; (E) Ukraine General Staff Oct 16 counter-sabotage ops with ~80 Russian personnel inside city. REJECTED as insufficient: RT (Russian state media, credibility concerns); DW report uses 'occupy' loosely; General Staff report emphasizes Ukrainian counter-operations preventing consolidation. The DeepState and UK MoD reports are strongest but still don't directly confirm ISW map red shading.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria specifically require the ISW map (primary source) to show red shading in the city-center west bank area. No source directly reports what the ISW ArcGIS storymaps link shows during the Oct 1–26 window. [Interfax-Ukraine Oct 20](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1114051.html) cites DeepState (fallback source) showing 'expanded control in the central part' — this is the strongest evidence but uses the fallback source, not the primary ISW source. [Newsweek Oct 16](https://www.newsweek.com/ukraine-war-russia-advances-update-territory-10887749) cites UK MoD saying 'contesting the majority of Kupiansk, having captured most high-rise buildings in the northern half' — 'contesting' and 'captured' are different from ISW red-shading. The ISW typically distinguishes confirmed control (red) from contested (grey/yellow). Ukrainian forces conducting active counter-sabotage operations through Oct 21 [Ukrinform Oct 21] suggest ISW would not shade as confirmed Russian control. Evidence does not directly confirm ISW map shows red in the defined area.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for the ISW map showing red shading in the Kupiansk west-bank city center, as no source explicitly describes the ISW map's depiction during this window. DeepState expanded control report: October 20, 2025 (Interfax-Ukraine). This is the fallback source, not the primary ISW source.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: N/A — cannot confirm the event occurred at all from available evidence (ISW map showing red in specified area).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Ukraine General Staff (Oct 16) stated forces are 'doing everything possible to clear Kupiansk of Russian invaders and prevent enemy consolidation' — suggesting ISW would not show consolidated red control. The Sept 17 Moscow Times article noted satellite imagery showed Russia controls 'only 6.3% of the built-up areas of Kupiansk.' The nature of the infiltration (small groups crossing river via pipeline/boats, counter-sabotage operations ongoing) is more consistent with grey/contested shading on ISW than solid red. ISW is known to be more conservative than DeepState in showing Russian control.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence establishes that Russian forces were present in and had expanded their footprint in central Kupiansk's west bank during October 2025 (supported by DeepState, UK MoD, field reporting). However, the question specifically requires the ISW map to show red shading in the city-center west-bank area — and no article directly cites the ISW ArcGIS map as showing this. The distinction between 'Russian forces present/infiltrating' and 'ISW showing confirmed territorial control (red)' is critical. Given that: (1) Ukrainian counter-sabotage was active throughout the window; (2) ISW is more conservative than DeepState; (3) no source directly describes the ISW map's depiction; (4) the resolution criteria explicitly require the ISW map specifically — the evidence is insufficient to confirm Yes, but also insufficient to definitively confirm No. The question should be treated as unresolvable per the instruction: 'If available evidence is insufficient to determine whether the red area reached the defined central west-bank urban core during the 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-26 window, the question should be treated as unresolvable rather than guessed.'

question: Israel strikes Iran by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an Israeli missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Israel publicly issue an evacuation warning for civilians at any location in Iran or at any official Iranian diplomatic facility between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-29?
subquestions.background_information:
Public evacuation warnings have often preceded overt Israeli air operations in the region, especially when Israel seeks to signal imminent strikes while reducing civilian presence. Such warnings are a materially different observable from an actual strike, but they would be a strong near-term indicator that Israeli decision-makers are preparing or threatening aerial action. The ultimate question concerns whether Israel will conduct a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or an official Iranian embassy/consulate by October 31, 2025. A public warning directed at civilians near a site in Iran would suggest elevated operational readiness, target selection, and willingness to acknowledge a coming attack.

Current regional context is highly escalatory. The Houthis, an Iran-backed group, have continued firing missiles and drones at Israel in late September 2025; The Times of Israel reported on 2025-09-29 that since March 18, 2025, the Houthis had launched nearly 90 ballistic missiles and dozens of drones at Israel, while Israel had repeatedly retaliated in Yemen. https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-intercepts-yemen-ballistic-missile-houthis-say-it-had-cluster-bomb-warhead/ The Times of Israel also reported on 2025-09-16 that Israel struck Hodeida port in Yemen after repeated Houthi attacks, part of a broader pattern of overt Israeli long-range retaliation against Iran-backed actors. https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-strikes-houthi-held-port-of-hodeida-in-response-to-drone-and-rocket-fire/

CSIS noted on 2025-09-16 that Israel had faced major direct Iranian missile and drone salvos in 2024 and a June 2025 conflict involving roughly 550 ballistic missiles and 1,000 drones, while Israeli officials emphasized the challenge of interceptor stockpiles. This indicates that direct Israel-Iran escalation is no longer a remote scenario but an active strategic risk. https://www.csis.org/analysis/enduring-role-fires-modern-battlefield

Because an evacuation warning is a public, attributable, pre-strike signal rather than the strike itself, it is a good crux: if it occurs, forecasters should substantially update upward on the probability that Israel will strike Iran by October 31; if it does not occur, that is some evidence against imminent overt action, though not conclusive.

Sources:
The Times of Israel - IDF intercepts Yemen ballistic missile; Houthis say it had cluster bomb warhead - https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-intercepts-yemen-ballistic-missile-houthis-say-it-had-cluster-bomb-warhead/
The Times of Israel - Israel strikes Houthi-held port of Hodeida in response to drone and rocket fire - https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-strikes-houthi-held-port-of-hodeida-in-response-to-drone-and-rocket-fire/
CSIS - The Enduring Role of Fires on the Modern Battlefield - https://www.csis.org/analysis/enduring-role-fires-modern-battlefield
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-29 inclusive, an official Israeli government or Israeli military communication publicly instructs civilians to evacuate, leave, or avoid a specified site/zone located on Iranian sovereign territory, or any official Iranian embassy or consulate anywhere in the world, because of impending Israeli military action or for wording clearly equivalent to that.

Qualifying communications include statements or posts from the Israel Defense Forces, the Israeli Prime Minister's Office, the Israeli Ministry of Defense, the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or verified official accounts of those bodies. The warning must be public and attributable; anonymous media claims without publication of the official warning do not count.

Examples that count:
- An IDF Arabic/Persian/X/Telegram post naming a facility in Tehran and telling nearby civilians to evacuate immediately.
- A formal Israeli government statement warning civilians to leave an Iranian consulate before military action.

Examples that do not count:
- General travel advisories for Israelis.
- Warnings about missile alerts inside Israel.
- Third-party reports that Israel "may strike" without an actual official evacuation warning.
- Warnings concerning Yemen, Lebanon, Syria, Gaza, or any non-Iranian/non-Iranian-diplomatic site.

Primary resolution sources will be official Israeli channels, including:
- IDF website: https://www.idf.il/en/
- IDF X account: https://x.com/IDF
- Prime Minister's Office: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office
- Israeli Ministry of Defense: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/ministry_of_defense
- Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/ministry_of_foreign_affairs

Secondary confirmation sources may include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), and The Times of Israel (https://www.timesofisrael.com/).

If no qualifying public warning is issued between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-29 inclusive, resolve No.

If a purported warning is reported but no text, image, recording, or direct quotation from an official Israeli channel can be located, and credible reporting remains insufficient to establish that an official public warning actually occurred within the window, resolve No.

If evidence is so contradictory that it cannot be determined whether a qualifying warning occurred within the window, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A public evacuation warning for a site in Iran would be a strong leading indicator of an overt Israeli aerial attack, while still being clearly distinct from the ultimate question. It captures operational preparation and political willingness to telegraph imminent action.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition for Yes: An official Israeli government or military body (IDF, PM Office, MoD, MoFA, or verified official accounts) must have issued a PUBLIC warning between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-29 instructing civilians to evacuate, leave, or avoid a site located on Iranian sovereign territory OR at an Iranian embassy/consulate anywhere in the world, because of impending Israeli military action. The warning must be attributable with a direct quote, post, image, or recording from an official Israeli channel.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'Israel evacuation warning Iran civilians 2025' [Oct 1–29] — to find any general evacuation warnings directed at Iran; (2) 'IDF warning Iran strike evacuation October 2025' [Oct 1–29] — to find specific IDF communications about Iran strikes; (3) 'Israel IDF evacuation warning Tehran Iranian embassy consulate October 2025' [Oct 1–29] — to find warnings targeted at specific Iranian locations; (4) 'Israel strike Iran attack October 2025' [Oct 1–29] — to find any Israeli military operations against Iran; (5) 'IDF Persian warning civilians evacuate Iran October 2025' [Oct 1–29] — to find Persian-language IDF communications; (6) 'Israel military operation Iran diplomatic facility 2025' [Oct 1–29] — to find warnings about Iranian diplomatic sites.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Multiple Israeli evacuation warnings directed at Gaza City residents — REJECTED: These are not about Iran or Iranian diplomatic facilities. (2) IDF releasing footage of October 2024 strikes in Iran (Oct 26, 2025) — REJECTED: This is retrospective footage, not a current evacuation warning. (3) Liberman (opposition leader) warning about possible Iranian attack on Israel (Oct 4 and Oct 8, 2025) — REJECTED: This is an Israeli politician warning Israelis about Iran attacking Israel, not Israel warning Iranian civilians to evacuate. (4) Iran references to a '12-day military campaign' against Iran in October 2025 by Iran International — NOTE: One Iranian source (Tehran Times, Oct 22) mentions an 'Israel's 12-day military campaign against Iran in October 2025,' but this appears to be a confused/inaccurate reference to the June 2025 conflict; no other source corroborates a new military campaign in October 2025. No official Israeli evacuation warning for Iran was found in any source.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate events found in any search that match the resolution criteria. All evacuation warnings found from Israeli officials during Oct 1–29, 2025 were directed at Gaza (specifically Gaza City residents). No official Israeli government or military communication publicly instructing civilians to evacuate from Iranian sovereign territory or Iranian diplomatic facilities was found. The Tehran Times reference to a '12-day military campaign against Iran in October 2025' appears to be a misattribution or editorial error — no corroborating sources confirm a new Israeli-Iran military campaign in October 2025, and no evacuation warning was cited in that context.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. No official Israeli evacuation warning for Iran or Iranian diplomatic facilities was identified within the Oct 1–29, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The Tehran Times article (Oct 22, 2025) mentions 'Israel's 12-day military campaign against Iran in October 2025' which could suggest military action in October 2025. However: (a) Multiple other reliable sources indicate the 12-day war occurred in June 2025, not October 2025; (b) No Israeli official source announced any new military campaign against Iran in October 2025; (c) The IDF's anniversary content (Oct 26-27) refers to October 2024 strikes and June 2025 operations, with no mention of current October 2025 Iran operations; (d) The Gaza ceasefire deal was being finalized in October 2025, making a new Iran campaign extremely unlikely per the overall geopolitical context. question: Israel strikes Iran before 2026?
description:

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

question: Apple Vision Pro 2 released by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Apple releases a new Vision Pro product by December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying product must be named "Apple Vision" and be recognized as a successor to the original Apple Vision Pro product, similar to the relationship between iPhone 14 and iPhone 15. A new Apple Vision product released without a number, under a designation other than Apple Vision Pro 2 will qualify if it retains the original functions of the Apple Vision Pro and expands on them in such a way that it is clear that this product is a successor.

In order to be considered released, the product must be available for purchase by the general public within the specified timeframe. An announcement or unveiling alone is not sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from Apple. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Apple publicly list the current Apple Vision Pro as unavailable for purchase on its U.S. online store due to discontinuation or replacement at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether Apple will release a Vision Pro successor by the end of 2025 is whether Apple begins clearing the way in its retail lineup for a replacement. Apple often stops selling older Pro-tier hardware when a new Pro successor is introduced; press coverage ahead of the September 2025 Apple event explicitly notes that Apple "never sells two generations of Pro models at the same time" for iPhone Pro models, illustrating a broader Apple pattern of simplifying the premium lineup when a successor arrives (Economic Times, 2025-08-28: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/apples-iphone-17-event-is-here-and-6-popular-products-may-be-killed-off-for-good/articleshow/123558676.cms). Multiple pre-September 2025 reports also say a refreshed Vision Pro is expected in the coming months, possibly with an M5 chip, suggesting that any change in store availability could be an early public signal that Apple is preparing or has prepared a successor (9to5Mac, 2025-08-31: https://9to5mac.com/2025/08/31/future-generations-of-apple-vision-pro-roadmap/). Macworld likewise reported expectations of new Vision Pro hardware during Apple's September product cycle (Macworld, 2025-09-01: https://www.macworld.com/article/2793032/get-ready-for-a-packed-month-of-apple-releases-with-a-new-iphone-and-a-whole-lot-more.html).

As of launch, the original Apple Vision Pro was sold through Apple's retail channels in the U.S. and positioned as Apple's flagship spatial-computing headset (Apple newsroom launch materials: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2024/01/apple-vision-pro-available-in-the-us-on-february-2/). Apple product pages remain the most authoritative public source for whether the device is still offered for general purchase in the U.S. (Apple Vision Pro product page: https://www.apple.com/apple-vision-pro/; Apple Store Vision Pro buy page: https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-vision/apple-vision-pro).

This is not the same as asking whether Vision Pro 2 itself launches by October 1. Rather, it asks whether Apple visibly changes retail availability of the incumbent headset in a way that would be consistent with an impending successor or replacement. Such a move would be meaningful evidence toward the ultimate question because Apple usually manages premium hardware transitions centrally through its own store.

Sources:
- Apple Newsroom: Apple Vision Pro available in the U.S. on February 2 — https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2024/01/apple-vision-pro-available-in-the-us-on-february-2/
- Apple Vision Pro product page — https://www.apple.com/apple-vision-pro/
- Apple Store Vision Pro buy page — https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-vision/apple-vision-pro
- 9to5Mac roadmap report — https://9to5mac.com/2025/08/31/future-generations-of-apple-vision-pro-roadmap/
- Macworld September 2025 Apple releases report — https://www.macworld.com/article/2793032/get-ready-for-a-packed-month-of-apple-releases-with-a-new-iphone-and-a-whole-lot-more.html
- Economic Times on Apple discontinuation patterns — https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/apples-iphone-17-event-is-here-and-6-popular-products-may-be-killed-off-for-good/articleshow/123558676.cms
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Apple publicly indicates on its U.S. online store that the original Apple Vision Pro is no longer available for purchase by the general public because it has been discontinued, replaced, or removed from sale. Qualifying evidence includes any of the following on Apple's U.S. website: (a) the Apple Vision Pro buy page https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-vision/apple-vision-pro is removed or redirects to a different current Apple Vision purchasing page; (b) Apple marks the product as unavailable in a way that clearly reflects end-of-sale rather than a temporary stock shortage; or (c) Apple publishes an official statement or newsroom item saying the current Vision Pro has been replaced or discontinued.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public indication appears between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

Temporary inventory outages, delivery delays, appointment unavailability, or region-specific stock shortages do NOT count as Yes unless Apple clearly signals discontinuation/replacement. Refurbished availability does not prevent a Yes if the new-product listing is ended. Third-party retailer actions do not count.

Primary sources for resolution will be Apple's U.S. online store and official newsroom pages: https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-vision/apple-vision-pro, https://www.apple.com/apple-vision-pro/, and https://www.apple.com/newsroom/. Archival verification may use the Internet Archive if needed: https://web.archive.org/. If Apple's pages are ambiguous or changed after the fact, a consensus of credible contemporaneous reporting from major Apple-focused outlets such as MacRumors (https://www.macrumors.com/) and 9to5Mac (https://9to5mac.com/) may be used as secondary evidence, but only if it specifically describes Apple's public U.S. store status during the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window. If the evidence does not clearly distinguish discontinuation/replacement from a temporary outage, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: If Apple removes or clearly sunsets the current Vision Pro from its own U.S. store in September 2025, that would be strong evidence that a successor release by year-end is more likely. Apple-controlled retail availability is a concrete, near-term observable that can update beliefs about the ultimate launch question without merely restating it.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition for Yes: Apple publicly indicates on its U.S. online store between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) that the original Apple Vision Pro is no longer available for purchase because it has been discontinued, replaced, or removed from sale. Qualifying evidence must be from Apple's official U.S. pages (buy-vision page, main Vision Pro page, or newsroom). Temporary stock outages do NOT qualify. The observable evidence needed would be: buy page removed/redirected, product marked as end-of-sale (not temporary), or Apple's official statement/newsroom saying discontinued/replaced.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Apple Vision Pro discontinued unavailable purchase 2025' (Sept–Oct 2025 window) — to find explicit end-of-sale events; 2. 'Apple Vision Pro removed from sale store September 2025' — to find any store removal; 3. 'Apple Vision Pro online store purchase available September 2025' — to check continued availability; 4. 'Apple Vision Pro out of stock unavailable buy page September October 2025' — to distinguish stock shortage from discontinuation; 5. '"Apple Vision Pro" discontinued "no longer available" OR "end of sale" 2025' — to find explicit discontinuation language.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple articles throughout September 2025 discuss: (a) Apple releasing visionOS 26 on September 15, 2025 for existing Vision Pro hardware — indicating the product is actively supported; (b) Apple announcing new immersive films for Vision Pro (Sept 22–24, 2025) — confirming active sales engagement; (c) Rumors about a Vision Pro 2 refresh (M4/M5 chip) expected 'before end of 2025' or 'in October/November 2025' — but no actual launch or replacement occurred within the window; (d) FCC leaks about a new Vision Pro model (A3416) confirmed by MacRumors on September 30, 2025 — but this is a leaked document, not a product launch; (e) A MacRumors article from October 11, 2025 says Apple paused all headset development and the original Vision Pro production ceased, but this is OUTSIDE the Sept 1–Oct 1 window; (f) No article reports Apple removing the Vision Pro buy page, marking it discontinued, or issuing a discontinuation newsroom post within the Sept 1–Oct 1 window. REJECTED: All articles discussing Vision Pro 2 rumors describe future plans, not present discontinuation of the original. The October 11 MacRumors article about paused development and ceased production is outside the window and describes a future/ongoing state, not a Sept 1–Oct 1 store change.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found within Sept 1–Oct 1, 2025 explicitly states that: (a) Apple's buy-vision page was removed/redirected; (b) Apple marked the Vision Pro as end-of-sale rather than temporarily out of stock; or (c) Apple published a newsroom item saying the Vision Pro was discontinued/replaced. To the contrary, articles confirm the Vision Pro remained actively supported (visionOS 26 launched Sept 15), actively sold (immersive films announced for Vision Pro, Sept 22–24), and remained available in multiple countries including the U.S. ([MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/2025/09/22/apple-vision-pro-immersive-films/) says 'Apple Vision Pro is available for purchase in... the U.S.'). The FCC leak about a Vision Pro 2 on September 30 indicates a new model was upcoming — but the original was not yet removed from sale within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window. The closest relevant event (paused headset development, production cessation) is referenced in October 11, 2025 articles — outside the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window. The question resolves No.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence AGAINST Yes: (1) visionOS 26 launched September 15, 2025 specifically for Vision Pro hardware, indicating Apple was still actively supporting and implicitly selling the device; (2) Apple announced new immersive content for Vision Pro in late September 2025, actively marketing the product; (3) MacRumors' September 22 article explicitly states Vision Pro 'is available for purchase' in the U.S.; (4) Multiple analyst reports from September 29–30, 2025 describe the Vision Pro 2 as 'coming soon' but not yet launched, meaning the original hadn't been replaced yet. The only evidence of production cessation and development pauses comes from articles published AFTER October 1, 2025 (October 2, 10, 11), outside the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is unambiguous: throughout September 1–October 1, 2025, the original Apple Vision Pro remained available for purchase on the U.S. store, was actively supported with new software (visionOS 26), and was actively marketed with new content. No qualifying end-of-sale indication appeared within the resolution window. The question resolves No. The window closed with no qualifying event, so the resolution_datetime is 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z.

question: Will TIME's Person of the Year for 2025 be a woman?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the individual named as TIME's Person of the Year for 2025 is a woman. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

In the event that multiple individuals are named TIME's 2025 Person of the Year, this market will resolve to "Yes" if at least one of them is a woman.

If for any reason the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is not announced by January 31, 2026 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on Time's cover. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will TIME publish, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, a cover story or homepage feature naming a woman as one of its annual 2025 honorees (excluding Person of the Year)?
subquestions.background_information:
TIME often publishes several annual recognition franchises in the months before announcing Person of the Year, including categories such as Kid of the Year, Athlete of the Year, CEO of the Year, and various TIME100-related recognitions. These choices can indicate which individuals and themes TIME's editors are elevating in a given year. In 2025, TIME had already named Tejasvi Manoj, a 17-year-old girl, as Kid of the Year by September 2025, showing that women and girls are already prominent in TIME's annual honors ecosystem this year: https://time.com/collections/time-for-kids-kid-of-the-year-2025/ and reporting summarized here: https://www.moneycontrol.com/education/meet-tejasvi-manoj-the-indian-american-named-times-kid-of-the-year-2025-for-protecting-seniors-from-cybercrime-article-13416636.html

Historically, Person of the Year is announced in early December, so November editorial choices can be a useful near-term indicator of whether TIME is foregrounding female figures or narratives heading into its biggest annual selection. TIME's main site regularly publishes cover stories and special-project landing pages that are publicly visible and timestamped: https://time.com/ . If TIME spotlights a woman in a major annual-honor feature during November 2025, that may increase the odds that a woman is also strongly in contention for Person of the Year.

This is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it asks about a different observable event—TIME's publication of another annual-honors feature involving a woman—before the Person of the Year announcement window.

TIME Kid of the Year 2025 collection https://time.com/collections/time-for-kids-kid-of-the-year-2025/
Moneycontrol on Tejasvi Manoj as TIME's Kid of the Year 2025 https://www.moneycontrol.com/education/meet-tejasvi-manoj-the-indian-american-named-times-kid-of-the-year-2025-for-protecting-seniors-from-cybercrime-article-13416636.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, TIME publishes on its website a clearly labeled annual-honors feature, cover story, or homepage-promoted special package that explicitly names a woman as one of its 2025 honorees, excluding any Person of the Year announcement.

For this question:
- The qualifying window is strictly from 2025-10-31 through 2025-11-30 inclusive.
- "A woman" includes any individual described by TIME or by the feature itself as female/woman/girl.
- "Annual 2025 honorees" includes franchises such as Kid of the Year, Athlete of the Year, CEO of the Year, TIME100 Next, Women of the Year, or comparable recurring annual TIME recognitions for 2025.
- The item must be published by TIME itself on https://time.com/ or an official TIME subpage, and must be publicly accessible or archived in a way that preserves the publication date.
- Person of the Year content does not count.
- Re-publication or reposting of content first published before 2025-10-31 does not count unless TIME clearly presents it as a newly published 2025 annual-honors feature within the window.

Primary source for resolution: TIME's official website and archives at https://time.com/ .
Fallback sources: TIME's official collection/tag pages and the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine if publication timing on TIME is unclear: https://web.archive.org/ . If TIME's site becomes unavailable, credible secondary reporting that quotes and links the TIME feature may be used to confirm publication date and content.

If no such qualifying TIME-published feature appears between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, resolve No. If the publication date cannot be established from TIME, archived snapshots, or credible secondary reports, the question should be considered unresolvable.

question: Will Eric Adams endorse Cuomo?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Eric Adams announces that he will vote for Andrew Cuomo or endorses Cuomo for the 2025 NYC Mayor election between June 25, and November 4, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

If  Eric Adams announces that he will vote for another candidate or endorses another candidate for NYC Mayor this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Eric Adams or one of his representatives, or a consensus of credible reporting of Adams' endorsement.

subquestions.question: Will Eric Adams publicly rule out dropping out of the 2025 NYC mayoral race before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Whether Adams stays in the race is a meaningful indicator for whether he might later endorse Andrew Cuomo. If Adams clearly says he will not drop out, that makes a Cuomo endorsement less likely; if he declines to rule it out, that leaves more room for consolidation behind Cuomo. This is distinct from the ultimate question because it tracks Adams' willingness to remain an active candidate rather than directly asking whether he will endorse Cuomo.

Current reporting indicates intense pressure on anti-Mamdani candidates to consolidate. After Cuomo lost the Democratic primary, reporting described calls for either Cuomo or Adams to drop out and support the other. CBS reported on August 13 that Paterson suggested Adams or Cuomo should drop their independent campaign to unify against Zohran Mamdani, while Adams publicly projected confidence despite weak polling: https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/david-paterson-endorsing-eric-adams-reelection-nyc-mayor/ . The Hill similarly reported that Cuomo had called for candidates to coalesce behind the strongest opponent, while Adams had refused to drop out: https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5447898-former-ny-governor-endorsing-eric-adams-for-nyc-mayor/ .

A proposed October consolidation mechanism also exists. The Wave reported on July 18 that Jim Walden proposed a ranked-choice poll among non-Democratic candidates, and Cuomo had already joined the pledge while Adams had not yet done so: https://www.rockawave.com/articles/editorial-jim-walden-to-the-rescue/ . If Adams instead explicitly says he is staying in through Election Day, that would be evidence against a later Cuomo endorsement.

Adams also received a visible boost from former Gov. David Paterson, who endorsed him in August. Newsmax reported Paterson endorsing Adams while noting polling that had Mamdani leading, Cuomo second, and Adams far behind: https://www.newsmax.com/newsfront/paterson-adams-endorsement/2025/08/13/id/1221706/ . This combination—low polls but fresh elite support—makes Adams' public posture toward staying in the race especially informative.

Sources:
CBS News New York – David Paterson endorsing Eric Adams for reelection: https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/david-paterson-endorsing-eric-adams-reelection-nyc-mayor/
The Hill – Former NY governor endorsing Eric Adams for NYC mayor: https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5447898-former-ny-governor-endorsing-eric-adams-for-nyc-mayor/
The Wave – Jim Walden To The Rescue?: https://www.rockawave.com/articles/editorial-jim-walden-to-the-rescue/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Eric Adams or an authorized campaign/spokesperson makes a public statement that clearly indicates he will remain in the 2025 NYC mayoral race and will not withdraw, drop out, suspend his campaign, or step aside before the election. Examples that count include statements such as "I am not dropping out," "I will stay on the ballot and continue my campaign," or equivalent unambiguous language.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

For resolution, use in order of priority: (1) official statements from Eric Adams' campaign website or official social media accounts; (2) official statements from Adams himself in video, transcript, press release, or interview format; (3) reporting from credible outlets quoting Adams or an authorized spokesperson directly. Primary sources include Adams campaign/official accounts if available. Credible secondary sources may include CBS New York, The New York Times, Gothamist, Politico, NY1, AP, or similar outlets.

If Adams makes only ambiguous statements such as saying he is "focused on campaigning today" or "taking it one day at a time," that does not count. If a statement is later contradicted within the window, the existence of an earlier qualifying unambiguous statement is still sufficient for Yes. If no reliable public source remains available at resolution time, a consensus of at least two credible news reports quoting the statement will suffice.

Suggested sources for resolution:

Eric Adams X account: https://x.com/ericadamsfornyc
CBS New York: https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/

subquestions.rationale: Adams endorsing Cuomo becomes much less likely if Adams explicitly commits to staying in the race. A firm public refusal to drop out is an early observable signal about whether Adams sees himself as a continuing candidate versus a potential coalition partner for Cuomo.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Eric Adams or authorized spokesperson makes an unambiguous public statement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) clearly indicating he will remain in the race and will not drop out, withdraw, or suspend. evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate qualifying events: (1) September 5, 2025 — Adams press conference at Gracie Mansion: 'I am running for reelection,' 'I'm running, and I'm going to beat Mamdani,' 'I am in this race. And I am the only one who can beat Mamdani.' Confirmed by AP, PBS, Gothamist, Daily Caller, Washington Examiner, NDTV, Yahoo, Townhall, Yeshiva World. September 28 dropout — disqualifies for Yes on its own but does not negate earlier statements per criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: September 5, 2025 press conference satisfies criteria exactly. Adams stated 'I am running for reelection' and 'I'm running, and I'm going to beat Mamdani' — this is equivalent to 'I will stay on the ballot and continue my campaign.' Confirmed by [AP](https://apnews.com/article/eric-adams-trump-job-offer-nyc-mayor-1005e2938a564324fe07206fc16dc164), [PBS NewsHour](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/watch-nyc-mayor-eric-adams-announces-he-is-continuing-his-reelection-campaign), [Gothamist](https://gothamist.com/news/mayor-adams-vows-to-say-in-nyc-mayors-race-calling-mamdani-and-cuomo-2-spoiled-brats), [Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2025/09/05/eric-adams-nyc-mayoral-race-zohran-mamdani/), [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/state/3795603/eric-adams-to-stay-in-new-york-city-mayoral-race/). Resolution criteria explicitly states that if a qualifying statement is later contradicted within the window, the earlier qualifying statement is still sufficient for Yes. Adams' September 28 withdrawal does not negate the September 5 qualifying statement.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 5, 2025 press conference at Gracie Mansion. Multiple sources published their reports on September 5–6, 2025. The AP report is dated September 5, 2025. Fox4 News reports Adams had declared he was 'all in' a week before September 28 (i.e., ~September 21). The September 5 press conference is the earliest qualifying event in the window. Exact time not specified in all sources, but the press conference was announced for 4:30 PM ET on September 5, 2025, as reported by Hindustan Times. The September 5 statement is clearly unambiguous ('I am running for reelection,' 'I'm running, and I'm going to beat Mamdani') and explicitly within the window.
