evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution = Yes. Eric Adams made multiple unambiguous public statements between September 1–October 1, 2025 that he would remain in the race. The first qualifying statement was on September 5, 2025, when he held a press conference at Gracie Mansion and declared 'I am running for reelection' and 'I'm running, and I'm going to beat Mamdani.' This is explicitly confirmed by multiple top-tier sources (AP, PBS, Gothamist). Per the resolution criteria, this earlier qualifying statement is sufficient for Yes even though Adams later dropped out on September 28.

question: Will tariffs generate >$250b in 2025?
description:
The U.S. government collected $82.2b in customs duties in FY 2025 (See: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/files/reports-statements/financial-report/2024/notes-to-the-financial-statements19.pdf).

This market will resolve to "Yes"  if the value of costumes duties collected in FY 2025 according to the Financial Report of the United States Government published by the Treasury Department for FY 2025 (See: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/financial-report/) is greater than $250b. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No". 

If the Treasury Department does not publish relevant data  for FY 2025 by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No". 

The resolution source will be the Treasury Department.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury's Monthly Treasury Statement for August 2025 report at least $20 billion in net customs duties for that month?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful near-term indicator for whether FY 2025 customs-duty collections could exceed $250 billion. The ultimate question depends on total FY 2025 customs duties in the Treasury's FY 2025 Financial Report, and August 2025 is the penultimate month of that fiscal year. Very high August receipts would be evidence that the late-summer tariff revenue surge is continuing strongly enough to make an exceptionally high full-year total more plausible.

Recent data suggest customs-duty collections have risen sharply in FY 2025. Reuters reported, citing Treasury data, that net customs duties were about $108.0 billion through the first nine months of FY 2025, with June 2025 alone at about $26.6 billion net, and gross customs duties at $113.3 billion through June. https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-customs-duties-top-100-billion-first-time-fiscal-year-2025-07-11/ . Reuters also reported that July 2025 customs duties reached roughly $27-28 billion, bringing FY 2025 tariff revenue to around $150 billion so far, according to Treasury data. https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-july-tariff-revenues-hit-record-bring-fiscal-year-haul-150-bln-2025-07-30/ .

The U.S. Treasury publishes monthly federal receipts in the Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS). The MTS contains a line for Customs Duties in both gross and net terms and is the most authoritative short-horizon public source for tracking the same revenue stream relevant to the ultimate question. https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/americas-finance-guide/government-revenue/ and https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mts/ .

A threshold of $20 billion for August 2025 is informative rather than trivial: it is below the reported June/July record levels, but still high by historical standards, so resolution either way should update beliefs about whether FY 2025 finishes anywhere near the very high $250 billion bar.

Sources:
Reuters - U.S. customs duties top $100 billion for first time in a fiscal year: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-customs-duties-top-100-billion-first-time-fiscal-year-2025-07-11/
Reuters - U.S. July tariff revenues hit record, bring fiscal-year haul to $150 bln: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-july-tariff-revenues-hit-record-bring-fiscal-year-haul-150-bln-2025-07-30/
U.S. Treasury - Monthly Treasury Statement: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mts/
Fiscal Data - Government Revenue overview: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/americas-finance-guide/government-revenue/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Treasury's Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) covering August 2025, first published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), reports net customs duties for August 2025 of at least $20.0 billion. It resolves No if that MTS reports net customs duties for August 2025 below $20.0 billion.

Primary source: the official Monthly Treasury Statement published by the U.S. Treasury at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mts/ . Resolvers should use the statement or accompanying tables for the single month of August 2025, specifically the net amount for Customs Duties, not a cumulative fiscal-year total and not the gross amount unless net is unavailable.

If the Treasury publishes both PDF tables and machine-readable tables and they conflict, the PDF MTS table takes precedence. If the standard MTS page is unavailable, a materially identical Treasury-hosted copy or Treasury Fiscal Data release may be used as a fallback, provided it clearly gives August 2025 net customs duties: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/ .

Only publications released between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) count. If no official Treasury MTS for August 2025 containing the needed August customs-duties figure is published by 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC, this question resolves No.

If Treasury later revises the August 2025 figure after 2025-10-01, such later revisions do not affect resolution; the first qualifying official publication within the window governs.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether FY 2025 customs-duty collections exceed an extremely high $250 billion threshold. August 2025 monthly customs-duty receipts are a direct, observable leading indicator of whether the late-FY2025 revenue run-rate is strong enough to keep that possibility alive. A very strong August print would support the idea that tariff collections are still accelerating; a weak print would make a >$250 billion annual total less plausible.

evidence.step1_decompose: The exact condition for Yes is: The U.S. Treasury's Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) covering August 2025, published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, must report net customs duties for August 2025 of at least $20.0 billion. Key entities: U.S. Treasury, MTS publication. Key threshold: $20.0 billion net customs duties. Timing: published within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'U.S. Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement August 2025 customs duties' - to find the MTS publication and its customs duties figure; 2) 'Monthly Treasury Statement MTS August 2025 published September' - to find the publication date; 3) 'Treasury MTS 29.5 billion customs' - to confirm specific figure; 4) 'Treasury budget statement August 2025 September 11 customs duties record' - to verify the report date and figure.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: U.S. Treasury released the August 2025 Monthly Treasury Statement on September 11, 2025, reporting net customs duties of $29.5 billion for August 2025. This is reported by Reuters (via Investing.com), Bloomberg Law, Yahoo Finance, The Hill, Newsmax, Market Screener, InstaForex, and Devdiscourse — all citing the U.S. Treasury Department's release. No candidate events were rejected; all sources are consistent.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The MTS for August 2025 was published on September 11, 2025 (within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window). Multiple sources explicitly report 'net customs receipts' of $29.5 billion for August 2025, directly from the Treasury's monthly statement. [Reuters/Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/us-august-deficit-falls-to-345-billion-as-tariff-revenues-rise-4235923): 'Net customs receipts for August also hit an all-time monthly record of $29.5 billion, up from $7 billion a year earlier.' [Newsmax](https://www.newsmax.com/finance/financenews/u-s-august-deficit/2025/09/11/id/1226092/): 'Net customs receipts hit an all-time monthly record of $29.5 billion.' [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/tariffs-revenue-neared-30-billion-this-august--the-first-month-of-trumps-full-reciprocal-tariff-regime-194619123.html): '$29.5 billion in customs duties in August...according to the Treasury's latest monthly statement.' $29.5 billion >> $20.0 billion threshold. Criteria fully satisfied.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple sources dated September 11, 2025 report the MTS publication. The Treasury MTS for August 2025 was released on September 11, 2025, which is within the resolution window. ISO 8601 approximate: 2025-09-11T00:00:00Z (exact time of day not specified, but the date is confirmed by multiple independent news outlets).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: All sources consistently cite the same September 11, 2025 release as the first and only publication of the August 2025 MTS. No earlier publication within the window was found. This is the first qualifying occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources agree: net customs receipts for August 2025 were $29.5 billion (with The Hill and Bloomberg Law rounding to ~$30 billion, and Mises Institute citing $31 billion, but the consensus precise figure from Reuters, Newsmax, and multiple financial outlets is $29.5 billion). All figures are far above the $20 billion threshold. No contradictory evidence found. The figure is explicitly labeled 'net customs receipts' for August 2025, not a cumulative or gross amount.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. Treasury's Monthly Treasury Statement for August 2025 was published on September 11, 2025 (within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window). It reported net customs duties of $29.5 billion for August 2025, which exceeds the $20.0 billion threshold by a wide margin. The resolution is definitively Yes.

question: Macron out in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Emmanuel Macron ceases to be President of France for any length of time between January 2 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET (inclusive). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Macron departs from office before the expiry date, the market should resolve immediately.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the government of France, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Prime Minister François Bayrou cease to hold office as Prime Minister of France between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-15 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term loss of the prime minister would be a strong indicator of escalating political instability around Emmanuel Macron, even though it is distinct from the ultimate question of whether Macron himself leaves office in 2025. As of late August 2025, multiple outlets reported that Bayrou was heading into a confidence vote scheduled for 8 September 2025, with opposition from both the left and the National Rally making his position precarious. Reuters-reported coverage said Macron publicly ruled out resigning even if Bayrou falls, while acknowledging that a failed confidence vote could force Bayrou and his government out and leave Macron needing to appoint yet another prime minister or take other destabilizing steps. See Yahoo/Reuters, 2025-08-30: https://www.yahoo.com/news/macron-rules-out-resigning-loses-155859652.html and Reuters, 2025-08-29: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/macron-vows-serve-out-term-despite-budget-crisis-2025-08-29/ . France has experienced repeated government instability since the 2024 legislative turmoil, making another prime-ministerial fall a meaningful signal about whether the presidency may come under greater pressure. The office of Prime Minister is officially tracked by the French government at Gouvernement.fr: https://www.gouvernement.fr/ .

Sources:
Reuters - Macron vows to serve out term despite budget crisis - https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/macron-vows-serve-out-term-despite-budget-crisis-2025-08-29/
Yahoo/Reuters - Macron rules out resigning if he loses sixth prime minister - https://www.yahoo.com/news/macron-rules-out-resigning-loses-155859652.html
Government of France - Gouvernement.fr - https://www.gouvernement.fr/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if François Bayrou ceases to hold the office of Prime Minister of France at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-15 inclusive. This includes resignation, dismissal, replacement by another prime minister, or any official end of his tenure during that window. It resolves No if Bayrou remains Prime Minister continuously throughout the entire period from 2025-09-01 through 2025-09-15 inclusive.

Primary source: official announcements or the official listing of the Prime Minister on the Government of France website, https://www.gouvernement.fr/ and related official communiqués from the French presidency at https://www.elysee.fr/ .

Secondary/fallback sources: Reuters coverage of French government changes, including Reuters' France politics pages or specific reports such as https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ . A consensus of at least two credible major news outlets may be used only if the official sites are unavailable or materially delayed.

For resolution purposes, the qualifying event is the actual cessation of Bayrou's tenure, not merely a failed vote, announced intention to resign, or submission of a resignation that is not accepted/effective within the window. If Bayrou announces he will resign after 2025-09-15, that does not count. If a confidence vote is postponed beyond 2025-09-15 and Bayrou remains in office through that date, resolve No. If source material is contradictory and no authoritative determination is possible, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Macron leaving office in 2025 becomes more plausible if the government collapses again and the political crisis worsens. Bayrou's fall would not directly answer the ultimate question, but it is a concrete, observable indicator of mounting instability that could increase pressure on Macron to resign or trigger extraordinary constitutional developments.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: François Bayrou must have actually ceased to hold office as Prime Minister of France at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-15 inclusive. Observable evidence: official resignation accepted, dismissal, or confirmed replacement by another PM within that window. Key entities: Bayrou, Macron, French National Assembly, Elysée Palace.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'François Bayrou Prime Minister France resign September 2025' — to detect resignation or dismissal events. 2) 'Bayrou Premier ministre démission France septembre 2025' — French-language sources for official announcements. 3) 'Bayrou resignation accepted Macron September 9 2025 official' — to confirm acceptance. 4) 'France new prime minister appointed after Bayrou September 2025' — to confirm successor appointment confirming Bayrou's exit.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) September 8, 2025: National Assembly confidence vote fails 364–194 against Bayrou. (2) September 9, 2025: Bayrou submits resignation to Macron at ~13:30 CET; Macron accepts it. (3) September 9, 2025: Macron appoints Sébastien Lecornu as new PM. (4) September 10, 2025: Formal handover of powers at Hôtel Matignon. All events confirmed by multiple credible sources. The confidence vote failure on Sept 8 triggered the constitutional obligation to resign; formal resignation and acceptance occurred Sept 9.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Bayrou's tenure definitively ended on September 9, 2025, when his resignation was submitted and accepted by President Macron — confirmed by [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2014557): 'On September 9, 2025, French Prime Minister Francois Bayrou submitted his resignation to President Emmanuel Macron, who accepted it.' Also confirmed by [France 24](https://www.france24.com/en/france/20250909-live-president-macron-new-pm-bayrou-resignation-confidence-vote-austerity-budget), [Euronews](http://www.euronews.com/2025/09/09/emmanuel-macron-names-sebastien-lecornu-as-new-prime-minister-of-france), [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/french-pm-francois-bayrou-ousted-in-parliament-confidence-vote), and [KTVZ/CNN](https://ktvz.com/news/national-world/cnn-world/2025/09/09/sebastien-lecornu-appointed-as-new-french-prime-minister/). Lecornu was appointed successor, confirmed by the Elysée. The formal handover occurred Sept 10 per [ANSA](https://www.ansa.it/sito/photogallery/primopiano/2025/09/10/lecornu-a-matignon-per-passaggio-di-consegne-con-bayrou_fd1f7307-16f6-4e06-8665-fc98b6a0207c.html). This exactly matches the resolution criteria: actual cessation of tenure (resignation accepted), within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 9, 2025 — Bayrou tendered resignation to Macron (France 24 reported it was scheduled for 13:30 CET = 11:30 UTC on Sept 9), and Macron accepted it the same day. ISO 8601 UTC: 2025-09-09T11:30:00Z (confirmed time from France 24 live blog indicating 13:30 CET). Lecornu formally took over at noon on September 10, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence exists — the window opens September 1 and the confidence vote occurred September 8, with resignation on September 9. No evidence of an earlier end to Bayrou's tenure within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: All searched sources are consistent: Bayrou lost confidence vote Sept 8, resigned Sept 9 (accepted by Macron), Lecornu appointed Sept 9–10. No contradictory evidence found. One source (The Independent) mentioned 'August 25' but this appears to be an error in that article's summary — all other sources consistently confirm Sept 8 vote and Sept 9 resignation. The resolution criteria specifies 'actual cessation' not merely 'announced intention,' and Macron's acceptance of the resignation on Sept 9 constitutes actual cessation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Bayrou ceased to hold office as Prime Minister on September 9, 2025, when his resignation was submitted and accepted by President Macron, followed by the appointment of Sébastien Lecornu as successor. This is a definitive Yes resolution, with the qualifying event occurring within the September 1–15, 2025 window. Multiple high-quality international news sources confirm the exact date.

question: Will Hezbollah disarm in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Hezbollah officially announces it will disarm in Lebanon by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only announcements supported by the Secretary-General of Hezbollah (currently Naim Qassem), a direct successor, or, if the position of Secretary-General of Hezbollah is vacant, the widely acknowledged leadership of Hezbollah will qualify. 

For the purposes of this market, "disarm" refers to a public commitment to relinquish or dismantle its military, whether partially or completely, in Lebanon.

Announcements of partial disarmament (e.g., surrendering a class of weapons or agreeing to disarm in stages or a certain region) will qualify as long as it is part of an acknowledged disarmament process.

Only official announcements will qualify. Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

Primary resolution sources will include official statements from Hezbollah leadership; however, a wide consensus of credible reporting confirming a policy of disarmament has been instituted will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the Lebanese Council of Ministers publicly approve a formal time-bound implementation plan for bringing all non-state weapons under exclusive state control by 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term crux for whether Hezbollah might officially announce disarmament by the end of 2025 is whether the Lebanese state moves from general rhetoric to an adopted implementation plan. In August 2025, Lebanon's government reportedly ordered the military to draft a plan to disarm Hezbollah by the end of the year, with Prime Minister Nawaf Salam saying the decision to limit arms to the state is "irreversible" and that decisions of war and peace must rest solely with the legitimate government. See Khaama Press, 2025-08-06: https://www.khaama.com/lebanese-government-orders-military-to-disarm-hezbollah/

Reuters reported on 2025-08-25 that the Lebanese cabinet had tasked the army with developing a plan to establish state control over arms by year-end, while Israel tied a phased pullback to Lebanese progress on disarmament. See Reuters via ThePrint: https://theprint.in/world/israel-ties-pullback-from-south-lebanon-to-hezbollah-disarmament-group-repeats-refusal/2770360/

At the same time, Hezbollah's leadership has repeatedly rejected disarmament. On 2025-09-27, Naim Qassem reportedly said, "We will never abandon our weapons, nor will we relinquish them." See Reuters pick-up in The Express Tribune: https://tribune.com.pk/story/2554920/hezbollah-refuses-to-be-disarmed. This makes a formal Lebanese cabinet move especially informative: if the government adopts a concrete plan with deadlines, jurisdictions, and implementing bodies, that would increase pressure and make a later Hezbollah announcement more plausible; failure to do so would point the other way.

The issue is grounded in current institutions. The Council of Ministers is the executive body that would ordinarily approve a national implementation plan. A public cabinet statement, decision record, or official government communiqué would be a clear observable signal. Official Lebanese government communications are typically published through the Prime Minister's office or cabinet-related channels, such as https://www.pcm.gov.lb/ and the National News Agency at https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/.

3. It is not the same as the ultimate question: it asks about state action, not Hezbollah's own formal commitment. But it is a strong indicator because an adopted plan would likely reflect sustained domestic and international pressure, create a focal point for negotiations, and raise the odds of a later Hezbollah announcement of partial or staged disarmament.

question: Israel x Iran ceasefire broken by March 31, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if either Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate, or Iran initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Israeli soil or any official Israeli embassy or consulate, by 11:59 PM ET on the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli or Iranian military forces that impact the other party’s ground territory or any official embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an Israeli missile, or an Israeli air base is hit by an Iranian drone, this market will resolve to "Yes") that is officially acknowledged by the relevant government or a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Iran or Israel publicly announce, between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-05, that it has raised military readiness specifically in response to the other side, including by mobilizing reserve forces, placing air defenses on heightened alert, or beginning a named military exercise explicitly tied to possible conflict with the other state?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term public move to heightened military readiness would be a meaningful indicator that the June 24, 2025 ceasefire is under renewed strain, even if no qualifying strike has yet occurred. The recent baseline is already tense. After the June 2025 Israel-Iran war and subsequent ceasefire, senior Iranian and Israeli officials continued issuing threatening statements rather than signaling durable de-escalation. Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson said on 2026-01-05 that Iran was intensifying efforts to safeguard its territorial integrity and remained highly vigilant: https://en.trend.az/iran/3994503.html . Israel’s army chief said on 2025-12-21 that the IDF would strike “wherever required” and reporting in The Times of Israel said Israeli officials were concerned about Iranian ballistic missile rebuilding: https://www.timesofisrael.com/army-chief-hinting-at-potential-new-iran-war-says-idf-will-strike-wherever-required/ .

Public readiness measures are often observable precursors to direct interstate attacks because they reflect both political intent and operational preparation. During and after the 2025 conflict, reporting described extensive prior planning and large-scale force employment by both sides, including hundreds of attacks by Israel and mass missile/drone launches by Iran, suggesting that any renewed conflict would likely be preceded by visible military posturing rather than emerge wholly without warning. France 24’s retrospective on the 12-day war summarizes the scale of the June 2025 campaign and ceasefire context: https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20250626-looking-back-at-israel-and-iran-s-12-day-war-direct-conflict-breaks-out-between-arch-enemies .

Because the ultimate question resolves on an actual strike, a public move to heightened readiness is useful as an earlier indicator rather than a restatement: it captures escalation in the political-military environment that should increase the chance of a later strike before late February 2026.

Sources:
Trend - Iran intensifies its initiatives for safeguarding its territorial integrity - spokesman: https://en.trend.az/iran/3994503.html
The Times of Israel - Army chief, hinting at potential new Iran war, says IDF will strike 'wherever required': https://www.timesofisrael.com/army-chief-hinting-at-potential-new-iran-war-says-idf-will-strike-wherever-required/
France 24 - Looking back at Israel and Iran's '12-day war': https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20250626-looking-back-at-israel-and-iran-s-12-day-war-direct-conflict-breaks-out-between-arch-enemies

This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-05 inclusive, at least one of the following occurs and is publicly reported by an official government or military source of Iran or Israel, or by at least two credible international news outlets citing such an official source: (1) Iran or Israel announces mobilization or call-up of reserve forces explicitly in response to the other country; (2) Iran or Israel announces that relevant air defense, missile, or broader military forces have been placed on heightened alert explicitly because of possible action by the other country; or (3) Iran or Israel begins a named military exercise that official statements explicitly describe as preparation for possible conflict, retaliation, or defense against the other country.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying announcement or officially acknowledged action occurs between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-05 inclusive.

For clarity, general hostile rhetoric alone does not count. Routine exercises, routine troop movements, or unspecified “readiness” statements do not count unless the announcement explicitly ties the measure to Israel/Iran as the relevant adversary. Secret or anonymously sourced claims without later official acknowledgement do not count.

Primary resolution sources will be official statements from the Israel Defense Forces, Israeli Prime Minister’s Office, Iranian Foreign Ministry, Iran’s armed forces, or Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, plus corroboration from Reuters and the Associated Press. If those are unavailable, BBC News or Agence France-Presse may be used as fallbacks.

Relevant source pages for resolution:
IDF official site: https://www.idf.il/en/
Israeli Prime Minister's Office: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office
Iranian Foreign Ministry: https://en.mfa.gov.ir/

AP Middle East: https://apnews.com/hub/middle-east
BBC News Middle East: https://www.bbc.com/news/world/middle_east

If a purported readiness step begins within the window but is only publicly disclosed after 2026-02-05, it will count only if reliable reporting clearly states that the qualifying action occurred within the 2026-01-06 to 2026-02-05 window. If reporting remains too ambiguous to determine timing or whether the step was explicitly tied to the other state, the question should resolve No rather than rely on discretion.
subquestions.rationale: Visible military readiness moves are a plausible leading indicator of whether the ceasefire will later break. Forecasters who disagree on the ultimate strike question are likely to disagree partly because they differ on whether current rhetoric will convert into operational preparation. Resolving this subquestion should therefore update beliefs about the probability of a direct strike before the ultimate deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-05, Iran or Israel must (1) mobilize reserve forces explicitly in response to the other, (2) place air defense/missile/military forces on heightened alert explicitly due to the other country, or (3) begin a named military exercise explicitly tied to conflict with the other state. Evidence must come from official government/military sources, or at least two credible international news outlets citing such official sources. General rhetoric does not count; the announcement must explicitly tie the measure to Israel/Iran as the adversary.

REJECTED: December 2025 events fall outside the window. REJECTED: General rhetoric statements (e.g., Jan 12 IDF 'prepared defensively' without explicit tie to Iran-specific alert increases) are borderline but the Jan 13-14 events go further with explicit air defense alert increases. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: CRITERION 2 (air defense/military forces placed on heightened alert explicitly due to the other country): — Iran (Jan 6, 2026): [Mehr News Agency](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/240522/400-units-of-IRGC-Army-on-full-alert-to-confront-threats) reports IRGC Brig. Gen. Ghorbani (official IRGC source) stating 400 IRGC/Army units on 'full alert' to confront 'potential aggression from the United States or Israel,' explicitly naming Israel and stating forces would 'level [Israel] to the ground.' Corroborated by [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/iran-puts-military-high-alert-11319549) and [NEWS.am](http://news.am/eng/news/923862.html). — Israel (Jan 13-14, 2026): [Arutz Sheva](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/420860) reports IDF increased alert levels 'across multiple systems, including air defense and the Iron Dome' amid tensions with Iran. [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2071427) cites IDF Spokesman Effie Defrin confirming IDF 'put on high alert,' instructed to 'strengthen defensive readiness.' [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-warns-against-misinformation-as-it-boosts-readiness-over-iran-threats/) confirms 'in response to reports of a potential U.S. strike on Iran and Iranian threats of retaliation against Israel,' at 19:15 Jan 14, 2026. — Iran Army Chief (Jan 31, 2026): [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/94N98NQ) directly reports Army Chief Hatami warning US and Israel, stating forces on 'high alert' following increased U.S. deployments in Gulf. Explicitly ties alert to US and Israel as adversaries. All three events satisfy Criterion 2 from the resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: FIRST QUALIFYING EVENT: January 6, 2026 — Mehr News Agency published at January 6, 2026 (exact date confirmed by article metadata). IRGC Brig. Gen. Ghorbani statement was made on January 6, 2026, confirmed by multiple corroborating sources including Newsweek (published January 7, 2026) and NEWS.am (January 6, 2026). Exact hour not available in sources, but date is reliably January 6, 2026, within the window start date. SECOND QUALIFYING EVENT: January 13-14, 2026 — Times of Israel specifies '19:15' on January 14, 2026 for the IDF statement. Arutz Sheva reports IDF raised alert on January 13, 2026.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest qualifying event is January 6, 2026 (Iran IRGC full alert statement explicitly naming Israel/US as adversaries). Pre-window evidence from December 2025 shows general readiness statements but these are outside the window. The December 2025 searches returned events from Dec 1-Dec 23 that predate the window but are not qualifying anyway. Within the window, no qualifying event appears before January 6, 2026 (the window start date itself). The January 6, 2026 event is the first qualifying occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: POTENTIAL ISSUES: (1) The Jan 6 IRGC statement mentions both US and Israel jointly — the criteria require explicit tie to Israel specifically. However, the statement explicitly names Israel ('level [Israel] to the ground') and lists Israel by name as one of two adversaries, which satisfies 'explicitly ties the measure to Israel/Iran as the relevant adversary.' (2) The criteria state 'official government or military source of Iran or Israel' — Brig. Gen. Morteza Ghorbani as 'senior adviser to the Commander-in-Chief of the IRGC' is an official Iranian armed forces source. (3) Corroboration: Newsweek, NEWS.am both report the same Jan 6 statement. This exceeds the 'two credible international news outlets' threshold. (4) The IDF Jan 13-14 statements: IDF Spokesman Brig. Gen. Effie Defrin is clearly an official IDF source, and multiple outlets (TASS, Times of Israel, Arutz Sheva) cite him — this satisfies both the official source and two-outlet corroboration requirements. (5) CONTRADICTION CHECK: No evidence contradicts these events occurring. Iran's actions were widely reported by AP, Reuters affiliate coverage, AFP (primary resolution sources). No source disputes these announcements occurred. CONCLUSION: Multiple qualifying events occurred, all within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: RESOLUTION: YES. Multiple qualifying events occurred within the 2026-01-06 to 2026-02-05 window. The FIRST qualifying event is January 6, 2026: Iran's IRGC senior adviser officially stated 400 IRGC/Army units are on 'full alert' explicitly to confront 'potential aggression from the United States or Israel,' naming Israel as the explicit adversary. This satisfies Criterion 2 (military forces placed on heightened alert explicitly because of possible action by the other country). This is reported by official Iranian armed forces sources (IRGC senior adviser Brig. Gen. Ghorbani) and corroborated by Mehr News Agency, Newsweek, and NEWS.am — satisfying the 'two credible international news outlets' corroboration requirement. Additional qualifying events include IDF air defense/Iron Dome alert increases on January 13-14, 2026 (official IDF spokesman statement confirmed by TASS, Times of Israel, Arutz Sheva), and Iran Army Chief's 'high alert' declaration on January 31 (AFP primary source + multiple corroborators). The resolution_datetime is set to 2026-01-06T00:00:00Z (the date of the first qualifying event, exact time not available in sources but within the window).

question: Starmer out in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Keir Starmer ceases to be the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom for any period of time between February 2 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement of Keir Starmer's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/removal goes into effect.

The resolution source for this market will be the government of the UK, however a consensus of credible reporting will also suffice.

subquestions.question: Will a Labour MP publicly submit a letter of no confidence in Keir Starmer to the chair of the Parliamentary Labour Party between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term pathway for a sitting UK prime minister to leave office is a loss of support within their own parliamentary party. For Labour, an early observable indicator of serious internal destabilisation would be an MP publicly confirming that they have submitted a no-confidence letter in the prime minister to the chair of the Parliamentary Labour Party (PLP), or that such a letter has been submitted on their behalf. This is not the same as Starmer actually leaving office, but it would be a concrete sign that discontent has escalated from anonymous briefings and poor polling into formal internal action.

By mid-2025, media reporting had already described significant Labour unease around Starmer’s leadership. Reuters reported in July 2025 that Starmer had backed Chancellor Rachel Reeves after market turmoil and political pressure, underscoring concerns about government stability: https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uk-pm-starmer-backs-finance-minister-reeves-after-tears-market-selloff-2025-07-02/ . Around the same time, Ipsos reported very poor public satisfaction numbers for Starmer, with dissatisfaction at historically high levels for a first-year prime minister: https://www.ipsos.com/en-uk/ipsos-political-monitor-starmer-satisfaction-july-2025 . The House of Commons website shows Labour remains the governing party with a large parliamentary presence, meaning internal Labour unrest matters more for Starmer’s position than opposition pressure alone: https://members.parliament.uk/parties/Commons .

Because Labour’s internal leadership processes are less mechanically transparent to the public than, for example, a statutory parliamentary confidence vote, a public declaration by an MP that they have submitted a no-confidence letter is a useful and observable proxy for whether elite support is beginning to fracture. If such letters start appearing in public before October 2025, forecasters should substantially raise the probability that Starmer could be out by year-end.

Sources:
Reuters - UK PM Starmer backs finance minister Reeves after tears, market selloff: https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uk-pm-starmer-backs-finance-minister-reeves-after-tears-market-selloff-2025-07-02/
Ipsos Political Monitor July 2025: https://www.ipsos.com/en-uk/ipsos-political-monitor-starmer-satisfaction-july-2025
UK Parliament - House of Commons parties and members: https://members.parliament.uk/parties/Commons
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), at least one sitting Labour MP publicly states that they have submitted a letter of no confidence in Keir Starmer to the chair of the Parliamentary Labour Party, or publicly states that such a letter has been formally submitted on their behalf, and this statement is reported by at least one credible UK national news outlet or appears in the MP’s own public communication.

This question resolves No if no such public statement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

For avoidance of doubt:
- Anonymous sourcing alone does not count.
- General criticism of Starmer, calls for him to resign, or discussion of plots/challenges do not count unless there is a public statement that a no-confidence letter has actually been submitted.
- Statements by peers, councillors, party members, trade union figures, or former MPs do not count; the person must be a sitting Labour MP during the resolution window.
- If a public statement says only that a letter is being considered, drafted, or may be submitted later, that does not count.
- If the only evidence is a claim by a journalist that a letter was submitted, without attribution to the MP or another on-record identifiable source, that does not count.

Primary resolution sources will be the MP’s own public statements (official website, X/Twitter, Facebook, press release), plus reporting from BBC News, Reuters, PA Media, Financial Times, Sky News, The Guardian, or The Times.

Suggested source URLs for resolution:
UK Parliament MPs directory: https://members.parliament.uk/
BBC News UK politics: https://www.bbc.com/news/politics
Reuters UK: https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/
PA Media: https://www.pa.media/
Financial Times UK politics: https://www.ft.com/uk-politics
Sky News Politics: https://news.sky.com/politics
The Guardian Politics: https://www.theguardian.com/politics
The Times Politics: https://www.thetimes.com/politics

If, by the end date, credible reporting indicates a qualifying public statement occurred within the window but the exact wording cannot be recovered, resolve according to the preponderance of the cited reporting. If reports conflict and no underlying public statement can be verified, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A publicly acknowledged no-confidence letter from a Labour MP would be an early, concrete sign of internal parliamentary revolt. Since Starmer’s removal before year-end would most plausibly come from Labour deciding he is politically unsustainable, this is a high-value indicator that is meaningfully distinct from the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A sitting Labour MP must publicly state (attributed, on-record) that they have submitted a formal letter of no confidence in Keir Starmer to the chair of the Parliamentary Labour Party (Anna Turley from Sep 6, 2025), reported by credible UK national media or the MP's own public communication, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Anonymous sourcing, general criticism, calls to resign, or letters 'being considered' do not count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Labour MP no confidence letter Keir Starmer Parliamentary Labour Party chair 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) — to find any formal submission; 2) 'Labour MP submits no confidence Starmer letter September 2025' — to find specific submission events; 3) 'Labour MP formally submits no confidence letter PLP chair Starmer' — direct criteria match; 4) 'no confidence letter Parliamentary Labour Party chair submitted MP September October 2025' — exact criteria; 5) 'Labour MP publicly submits no-confidence letter Starmer PLP chair Anna Turley' — named chair; 6) 'Richard Burgon Andy McDonald Kim Johnson no confidence letter Starmer submitted' — specific likely MPs.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (a) i-News (Sep 17): 'Rebel Labour MPs warn whips they have no confidence in Starmer' — describes MPs telling whips informally, anonymously, not submitting letters to PLP chair. REJECTED: anonymous, told to whips not PLP chair, no public statement of formal submission. (b) Express (Sep 15): 'party insiders suggest a no-confidence vote could be possible' — speculative, not a formal submission. REJECTED. (c) Burgon (Sep 15): warns Starmer has 8 months, calls leadership inevitable to end — criticism and prediction, not a formal submission. REJECTED. (d) McDonald, Lewis, Johnson: criticism and calls for change — no mention of submitting formal letters to PLP chair. REJECTED. No qualifying event was identified.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article from BBC News, Reuters, PA Media, FT, Sky News, The Guardian, The Times, or any credible outlet explicitly reports that a sitting Labour MP publicly stated they had submitted a formal letter of no confidence to the PLP chair (Anna Turley) during the window. The i-News article [https://inews.co.uk/news/politics/rebel-labour-mps-warn-whips-they-have-no-confidence-in-starmer-3922248] describes MPs privately telling whips — anonymous sources, not formal public submissions to the PLP chair. This does not meet the resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found; no timestamp can be extracted.
evidence.step7_verification: Extensive search found consistent reporting of internal discontent, criticism, and speculation about leadership challenges throughout September 2025. The Labour Party chair Anna Turley was appointed Sep 6 and urged unity Sep 26. No reporting from any source describes a named MP publicly confirming submission of a formal no-confidence letter to the PLP chair. The distinction between 'telling whips informally' and 'formally submitting a no-confidence letter to the PLP chair' is critical here — the former was reported, the latter was not.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution window closed (Oct 1, 2025) with no qualifying event having occurred. There was substantial internal Labour dissent and informal expressions of no confidence to whips, but no Labour MP publicly stated — on the record, attributed — that they had formally submitted a letter of no confidence to the PLP chair. The question resolves No, with resolution_datetime = 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z.

question: Bank of Japan decreases interest rates after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The Statement on Monetary Policy for the Bank of Japan's Monetary Policy meeting for January is scheduled to be released on January 23, 2026 (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm).

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the short-term policy interest rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Bank of Japan's January 2026 meeting.

If the short-term policy interest rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Bank of Japan (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market may resolve as soon as the Bank of Japan's statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the Bank of Japan leave the short-term policy interest rate unchanged at around 0.5% at its December 2025 Monetary Policy Meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful leading indicator for whether the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will cut rates after its January 2026 meeting, because a December hold would suggest the BOJ is still in a wait-and-see posture rather than urgently tightening or responding to a downturn before January. If the BOJ instead hikes in December, that would usually make a January cut less likely absent a sharp adverse shock; if it cuts in December, that would strongly increase the chance of further easing or at least a dovish shift by January.

As of late 2025, the BOJ’s policy rate is around 0.5%. Reuters- and press-based coverage before 2025-11-08 indicates the BOJ kept its key rate unchanged at the October 30, 2025 meeting, with a 7-2 vote and two members still favoring a hike to around 0.75% rather than a cut, implying the internal debate was between hold and hike, not imminent easing. See bne IntelliNews, 2025-10-30: https://www.intellinews.com/bank-of-japan-keeps-key-rate-unchanged-as-takaichi-takes-office-397937/ .

Other contemporaneous reporting also suggested that analysts widely expected an October hold and were focused on whether the next move would be a hike in December or January 2026, not a cut. Investing.com’s 2025-10-29 BOJ preview reported expectations for rates to remain on hold at 0.5% in October, with some analysts pointing to December 2025 or January 2026 as the next plausible hike window: https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/boj-preview-oct-rates-to-remain-on-hold-outlook-in-focus-amid-sticky-inflation-3694596 . Reuters-based reporting cited by Investing.com on 2025-10-06 said yen swaps implied only a 41% chance of a rate hike by December 2025, down from 68% earlier, again framing the near-term question as hold vs. hike: https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/takaichi-could-tolerate-another-boj-rate-hike-by-january-economic-adviser-says-3918554 .

The BOJ’s official meeting schedule shows regular Monetary Policy Meetings, including the January 2026 meeting relevant to the ultimate question; the December 2025 meeting occurs before that and is therefore a natural crux. Official schedule: https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm .

Sources:
BOJ meeting schedule: https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm
bne IntelliNews - Bank of Japan keeps key rate unchanged as Takaichi takes office: https://www.intellinews.com/bank-of-japan-keeps-key-rate-unchanged-as-takaichi-takes-office-397937/
Investing.com - BOJ preview Oct: rates to remain on hold, outlook in focus amid sticky inflation: https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/boj-preview-oct-rates-to-remain-on-hold-outlook-in-focus-amid-sticky-inflation-3694596
Investing.com - Takaichi could tolerate another BOJ rate hike by January, economic adviser says: https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/takaichi-could-tolerate-another-boj-rate-hike-by-january-economic-adviser-says-3918554
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Bank of Japan announces, between 2025-11-08 and 2025-12-08 inclusive, the result of a Monetary Policy Meeting in which it leaves the target level for the uncollateralized overnight call rate / short-term policy interest rate unchanged at approximately 0.5% (i.e., no change from the level in place immediately before that meeting).

This question resolves No if, between 2025-11-08 and 2025-12-08 inclusive, the BOJ announces a Monetary Policy Meeting outcome in which the short-term policy interest rate is changed to any level other than approximately 0.5%.

Primary source: the BOJ’s official Statements on Monetary Policy and meeting materials on its website, especially the Monetary Policy Meeting pages and schedule: https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm and https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/index.htm .

If the BOJ publishes the December 2025 meeting decision within the resolution window, that published decision governs resolution. If the BOJ has not published any December 2025 Monetary Policy Meeting decision by 2025-12-08, this question resolves Unresolvable, because the qualifying event would have been postponed beyond the resolution window.

If BOJ pages are temporarily unavailable, a consensus of credible financial reporting quoting the BOJ decision (for example Reuters, Bloomberg, Nikkei, or the BOJ-linked statement mirrored by major outlets) may be used as a fallback, but the official BOJ statement controls whenever available.

If the BOJ changes its operating framework or terminology but clearly states the effective short-term policy rate target or equivalent policy rate setting, resolution will be based on whether that effective setting is unchanged from the pre-meeting level of about 0.5%.
subquestions.rationale: The December 2025 policy decision is the most direct near-term observable about BOJ reaction function before the January 2026 meeting. A December hold points to continued patience; a December hike suggests residual hawkishness and lowers the odds of a January cut; a December cut would be strong evidence favoring further dovishness by January.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: BOJ announces a Monetary Policy Meeting result between Nov 8 - Dec 8, 2025 where the short-term policy rate is left unchanged at ~0.5%. Observable evidence: Official BOJ statement or credible financial reporting confirming a meeting decision in this window. Key threshold: rate must remain at ~0.5%. Timing constraint: announcement must occur within Nov 8 - Dec 8, 2025 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Bank of Japan monetary policy meeting December 2025 interest rate decision' (to find any meeting results in window). Query 2: 'BOJ policy rate unchanged 0.5% December 2025' (to find evidence of unchanged rate). Query 3: 'Bank of Japan monetary policy meeting schedule November 2025' (to determine meeting schedule). Query 4: 'BOJ interest rate decision November 2025 meeting result' (to check if any meeting occurred in window). Query 5: 'Bank of Japan October 2025 policy meeting held maintained rate 0.5%' (to confirm last pre-window meeting). Query 6: 'BOJ monetary policy meeting December 18 19 2025 schedule next meeting' (to confirm next meeting is outside window).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) BOJ October 28-30, 2025 meeting — held BEFORE the resolution window, result: rate held at 0.5%. (2) BOJ December 18-19, 2025 meeting — scheduled AFTER the resolution window closes (Dec 8, 2025). No meeting was held or announced within the November 8 - December 8, 2025 window. Multiple sources from Nov 10, Nov 18, Nov 21, Nov 29, Dec 1, Dec 4, Dec 5, Dec 6, 2025 all consistently state 'the next BOJ meeting is December 18-19, 2025,' confirming no meeting occurred in the resolution window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require the BOJ to announce a Monetary Policy Meeting outcome between Nov 8-Dec 8, 2025. No such announcement occurred. Multiple credible sources confirm: [Yahoo Finance Dec 5](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/boj-said-likely-raise-interest-042746923.html) states December 19 is the decision date; [Japan Times Nov 29](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2025/11/29/economy/boj-senior-officials-rate-hike/) states 'The BOJ's next decision is scheduled for December 18–19, 2025'; [Nikkei Asia Dec 6](https://asia.nikkei.com/economy/bank-of-japan/as-boj-rate-decision-nears-takaichi-government-signals-openness-to-hike) confirms decision is scheduled for later in December. The resolution criteria explicitly state: 'If the BOJ has not published any December 2025 Monetary Policy Meeting decision by 2025-12-08, this question resolves Unresolvable.' No qualifying BOJ Monetary Policy Meeting decision was published within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event (BOJ MPM decision) occurred within the November 8 - December 8, 2025 window. The last meeting was October 28-30, 2025 (before the window). The next scheduled meeting is December 18-19, 2025 (after the window closes). Therefore, no timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying occurrence was found within the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: All searched sources consistently confirm that no BOJ Monetary Policy Meeting was scheduled between November 8 and December 8, 2025. The October 30 meeting held rates steady at 0.5%, but that was before the resolution window. The December 18-19 meeting is after the resolution window. No contradictory evidence was found suggesting any additional meeting was held or announced in November or early December 2025. The resolution criteria explicitly address this scenario: 'If the BOJ has not published any December 2025 Monetary Policy Meeting decision by 2025-12-08, this question resolves Unresolvable.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BOJ held no Monetary Policy Meeting between November 8 and December 8, 2025. The last meeting (October 28-30) was before the window; the next meeting (December 18-19) is after the window closes. The resolution criteria explicitly state this scenario makes the question 'Unresolvable.' Therefore, resolvable=false.

question: Will Trump's approval rating hit 40% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump’s approval rating according to Silver Bulletin is equal to or below the listed value for any date between April 14 and December 31 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Note that the approval ratings for this date must be finalized before it is considered for this market (namely once the next data point is available, the previous one is finalized).

This market's resolution source will be Silver Bulletin' approval rating poll aggregator, https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin, specifically the approval rating indicated by the green trend line for the resolution date. Changes in the methodology by which Silver Bulletin calculates the approval rating will have no bearing on the resolution of this market. If Silver Bulletin's approval rating becomes permanently unavailable, RealClearPolitics will be used.

If the approval rating for December 31 is not published by January 4, 2026, 12:00 PM ET (noon), this market will resolve according to all previous datapoints.

subquestions.question: Will the Silver Bulletin net approval trend for Donald Trump be at or below -10.0 percentage points on any finalized date between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful leading indicator for whether Trump’s approval rating might later hit 40% in 2025, because sustained deterioration in net approval usually reflects either falling approval, rising disapproval, or both. As of spring and summer 2025, Trump’s ratings were underwater and fairly stable but weak. New York Magazine reported that Silver Bulletin had Trump at roughly -9.1 net approval on 2025-04-28, with 53.2% disapproving: https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/trump-approval-rating-100-days-second-term.html . By 2025-05-15, Silver Bulletin’s net approval had improved somewhat to about -6.2, but he remained underwater: https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/polls-trump-job-approval-stabilizing-but-still-underwater.html . Reuters coverage summarized by WBMA on 2025-06-03 said Silver Bulletin showed Trump at 45.8% overall approval and negative on the economy, trade, and inflation: https://abc3340.com/news/nation-world/trumps-approval-ratings-positive-for-immigration-negative-on-economy-polls-show .

By mid-summer, the picture worsened again. Newsweek reported Nate Silver saying Trump’s net approval had fallen from -6.9 on 2025-07-10 to about -8.9 by 2025-07-21, nearing his prior low of -9.7: https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-started-drop-more-quickly-nate-silver-2102276 . Another Newsweek piece on 2025-08-11 said Trump’s net approval had become “very boring,” fluctuating narrowly between about -8.5 and -8.9 since August 1, suggesting a plateau at a weak level rather than a rebound: https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-very-boring-nate-silver-2108252 . A move to -10.0 or worse by late September would signal a clear break below that recent plateau and would make a later 40% approval print more plausible.

This is not the same as the ultimate question: it tracks net approval rather than raw approval, and it asks whether sentiment deteriorates further in the near term. Because disapproval has often been in the mid-50s while approval has been in the low-to-mid 40s, crossing -10 net approval would likely correspond to pressure on the approval trend even if 40% itself is not yet reached.

Sources:
- New York Magazine, At 100 Days, Trump Approval Rating Is As Low As First Term: https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/trump-approval-rating-100-days-second-term.html
- New York Magazine, Polls: Trump Job Approval Stabilizing, But Still Underwater: https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/polls-trump-job-approval-stabilizing-but-still-underwater.html
- WBMA / Reuters summary, Trump's approval ratings positive for immigration, negative on economy, polls show: https://abc3340.com/news/nation-world/trumps-approval-ratings-positive-for-immigration-negative-on-economy-polls-show
- Newsweek, Trump's approval rating has "started to drop more quickly" -- Nate Silver: https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-started-drop-more-quickly-nate-silver-2102276
- Newsweek, Donald Trump approval rating numbers have become "very boring" -- Nate Silver: https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-very-boring-nate-silver-2108252
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Silver Bulletin Trump approval page shows a finalized net approval trend value (approval minus disapproval, in percentage points) of -10.0 or lower for any date between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, inclusive. It resolves No if no such finalized date exists in that window.

Primary source: Nate Silver / Silver Bulletin Trump approval ratings page: https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin

Use the net approval trend value displayed by Silver Bulletin for each date in the window. A date counts only once its value is finalized, following the same convention as the ultimate market: namely, once the next data point is available, the previous one is considered finalized. If the value for 2025-10-01 is not finalized by 2025-10-04 12:00 PM ET, resolve using all earlier finalized datapoints from the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window.

If Silver Bulletin becomes permanently unavailable before resolution, use the RealClearPolitics Trump job approval average as a fallback and compute net approval as approval minus disapproval from its published average for dates between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, inclusive: https://www.realclearpolitics.com/epolls/other/president_trump_job_approval-7320.html . If neither source provides sufficient date-specific data for the full window, the question should be considered unresolvable.

Only dates within the explicit window from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 inclusive count toward resolution; earlier or later dates do not count.
subquestions.rationale: If Trump’s net approval breaks below -10 in September, that would indicate broadening weakness beyond the August plateau around -8.5 to -8.9. Such a deterioration would be a meaningful early warning sign that his raw approval trend could later slip to 40% before year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Silver Bulletin net approval trend (approval minus disapproval) ≤ -10.0 percentage points for any finalized date in 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 inclusive. question: Will Hamas agree to disarm by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Hamas officially announces it will disarm in the Gaza Strip by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only credible announcements, for example by the widely acknowledged leadership of Hamas, will qualify.

For the purposes of this market, "disarm" refers to a public commitment to relinquish or dismantle its military, whether partially or completely, in the Gaza Strip.

Announcements of partial disarmament (e.g., surrendering a class of weapons or agreeing to disarm in stages or a certain region) will qualify as long as it is part of an acknowledged disarmament process.

Only official announcements will qualify. Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

Primary resolution sources will include official statements from Hamas leadership; however, a wide consensus of credible reporting confirming a policy of disarmament has been instituted will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Qatar, Egypt, or Turkey publicly state between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 that Hamas has accepted in principle a disarmament or demilitarization framework for Gaza?
subquestions.background_information:
A key indicator for whether Hamas will officially agree to disarm by year-end is whether its main mediators begin publicly characterizing Hamas as having accepted disarmament in principle. Recent reporting suggests this is a live but unresolved issue. On 2025-11-26, Arutz Sheva reported that Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem said Hamas would not disarm except through internal Palestinian dialogue and a broader political process, while also reporting that Qatar's prime minister said Qatar was pressuring Hamas to accept disarmament and that Hamas appeared ready to relinquish governance of Gaza. https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/400084 (site path may differ at publication, but Arutz Sheva report dated 2025-11-26 is the relevant cited item). Earlier reporting in The Boston Globe on 2025-10-08 said Arab mediators believed Hamas could be open to partial disarmament, though not full disarmament, as part of indirect talks. https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/10/08/world/hamas-partial-disarmament-gaza-talks/ The Hill reported on 2025-10-14 that Hamas's consolidation of power in Gaza was clouding prospects for the second phase of the Trump peace plan, which hinges on Hamas disarming and relinquishing authority; it also noted senior US officials cautioned that private negotiations may differ from Hamas's public messaging. https://thehill.com/policy/international/ Middle East diplomacy around Gaza has often been mediated through Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey, so a public statement from one of these mediators that Hamas has accepted disarmament in principle would be strong near-term evidence that an official Hamas disarmament announcement is becoming more likely.

Because the ultimate market requires an official Hamas announcement, mediator statements are not sufficient for final resolution there. But they are highly informative as a crux: if mediators publicly say Hamas has accepted a disarmament framework, that would suggest negotiations have crossed an important threshold from outright rejection toward formalization.

Sources:
Arutz Sheva / Israel National News report on Hamas refusal to disarm and Qatari pressure: https://www.israelnationalnews.com/
The Boston Globe report on possible partial disarmament openness: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/10/08/world/hamas-partial-disarmament-gaza-talks/
The Hill report on peace deal prospects and unresolved second phase: https://thehill.com/policy/international/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), at least one of the following occurs: (1) Qatar's foreign ministry, prime minister, emir, or another clearly official Qatari government channel; (2) Egypt's presidency, foreign ministry, State Information Service, or another clearly official Egyptian government channel; or (3) Turkey's presidency, foreign ministry, or another clearly official Turkish government channel publicly states that Hamas has accepted, agreed to, or consented in principle to a framework involving disarmament, demilitarization, surrender of weapons, putting weapons beyond use, or equivalent language regarding Gaza. Direct official statements count, as do on-record statements quoted by at least two independent major news organizations.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement is made between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive).

For avoidance of doubt, statements merely saying mediators are urging, pressuring, or hoping Hamas will disarm do NOT count. Statements that Hamas is discussing disarmament, considering it, or linking it to conditions do NOT count unless the statement clearly says Hamas has accepted or agreed in principle. Anonymous-source reports alone do NOT count. Statements by U.S., Israeli, or Hamas officials do NOT count unless they are explicitly relaying an attributable public statement from Qatar, Egypt, or Turkey meeting the criteria above.

Primary resolution sources: official government websites and official social-media accounts of Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey, plus Reuters and AP coverage of attributable public statements. Useful source pages include Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs https://www.mofa.gov.qa/ ; Egypt State Information Service https://www.sis.gov.eg/ ; Republic of Turkey Ministry of Foreign Affairs https://www.mfa.gov.tr/default.en.mfa ; Reuters world news https://www.reuters.com/world/ ; AP News Middle East coverage https://apnews.com/hub/middle-east

If a qualifying statement is first made within the window but only widely reported afterward, it still counts so long as the underlying statement can be verified as having occurred between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29. If no verifiable timestamp can establish that the statement occurred within that window, the statement does not count.
subquestions.rationale: Mediator public messaging is a strong leading indicator for whether Hamas is nearing a formal disarmament announcement. Since Hamas has recently reiterated resistance to disarmament, a shift by key mediators from pressuring Hamas to saying Hamas has accepted disarmament in principle would meaningfully update forecasts on the ultimate question without merely restating it.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: At least one official Qatari, Egyptian, or Turkish government channel publicly stating that Hamas has accepted/agreed/consented in principle to a disarmament, demilitarization, or weapons-surrender framework for Gaza. Excluded: statements about urging/pressuring/hoping Hamas disarms; statements that Hamas is 'discussing' or 'considering' disarmament; anonymous sources; statements by U.S./Israeli/Hamas officials.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Hamas disarmament demilitarization framework Qatar Egypt Turkey statement 2025' (Nov 30–Dec 29, 2025). Query 2: 'Hamas accepts disarmament Gaza ceasefire deal December 2025' (Nov 30–Dec 29). Query 3: 'Qatar Egypt Turkey official statement Hamas agreed accepted disarmament December 2025' (Dec 1–29). Query 4: 'Hamas weapons freeze disarmament agreement accepted mediators statement' (Nov 30–Dec 29). Query 5: 'Qatar Turkey Egypt Hamas accepted agreed disarmament weapons framework Gaza late December 2025' (Dec 20–29). Query 6: 'Miami meeting mediators Hamas disarmament agreement December 19 2025' (Dec 18–29).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Dec 6 Doha Forum statements by Qatar PM, Turkey FM Fidan, Egypt FM Abdelatty — REJECTED: these discuss sequencing, governance prerequisites, and call for restraint, not Hamas acceptance of disarmament; Fidan explicitly says disarmament is 'not realistic' in first phase; (2) Dec 7 Hamas official Bassem Naim says Hamas open to 'freezing or storing' weapons — REJECTED: this is a Hamas statement (not Qatar/Egypt/Turkey), and it is about 'discussing' not accepting, and is a freeze not disarmament; (3) Dec 10–11 Hamas leader Meshaal explicitly rejects disarmament, proposes weapons freeze — REJECTED: this is Hamas rejecting disarmament; (4) Dec 19–20 Miami meeting joint statement by US/Qatar/Egypt/Turkey — REJECTED: statement says 'little progress,' notes second phase requires 'compromises on Hamas disarmament,' no statement that Hamas accepted; (5) Dec 26–27 mediator meeting statement — REJECTED: again states second phase requires compromises on Hamas disarmament, confirming no acceptance by Hamas.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No qualifying statement found. The Miami joint statement (Dec 20) by Qatar/Egypt/Turkey [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/gaza-mediators-urge-israel-hamas-to-keep-truce-after-meeting-yields-little-progress/) explicitly states 'little progress' and that the second phase requires Hamas to make compromises on disarmament — the opposite of Hamas having accepted. Turkey's FM Fidan at the Doha Forum [Reuters/Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/turkeys-fidan-gaza-governance-must-precede-hamas-disarmament-in-ceasefire-deal-4394679) said disarmament cannot happen yet and depends on governance structures. Egypt's FM Abdelatty confirmed ISF focus would be on 'monitoring the ceasefire and border crossings,' not disarmament enforcement per [Gatestone](https://www.gatestoneinstitute.org/22124/gaza-peacekeepers-monitors). Qatar PM stated ceasefire is at 'critical moment' and called for next steps, not that Hamas accepted disarmament [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/87AY2KJ).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found within the window, so no timestamp to extract for a Yes resolution.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at all within the window 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-29.
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checked: (1) Multiple sources (AFP, Times of Israel, Asharq Al-Awsat, Daily Sabah, Foreign Policy, Reuters) consistently show that Hamas explicitly rejected full disarmament throughout the window; (2) Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey consistently described disarmament as a future goal contingent on other steps, not as something Hamas had accepted; (3) The Dec 19–20 Miami joint mediator meeting produced a statement that explicitly noted lack of progress and that Hamas disarmament remained a sticking point; (4) No contradictory evidence showing any of the three countries (Qatar, Egypt, Turkey) made a statement that Hamas had accepted a disarmament framework was found in any source. The Gatestone article explicitly quotes Egypt's FM confirming ISF would NOT do disarmament. All evidence corroborates the No resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence within the window (Nov 30–Dec 29, 2025) shows that Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey made NO public statement that Hamas had accepted a disarmament or demilitarization framework. On the contrary, official statements from all three countries consistently described Hamas disarmament as a future requirement still to be achieved, and Hamas itself publicly rejected disarmament throughout this period. The condition for Yes resolution was never met. Resolution: No.

A drop below $200 would represent a conspicuous deterioration in Tesla’s market valuation and therefore likely pressure Musk’s net worth materially. question: Will USA win the 2025 Ryder Cup?
description:
In the 2025 Ryder Cup, scheduled for September 25-28, 2025.

If Team USA wins the 2025 Ryder Cup by finishing with more total points than Team Europe, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If the Ryder Cup is postponed, this market will remain open until the tournament has been completed.

If the Ryder Cup is canceled entirely, with no make-up tournament, this market will resolve “Tie”.

subquestions.question: Will Team Europe be listed as the betting favorite over Team USA by FanDuel Sportsbook for the 2025 Ryder Cup winner market at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26 inclusive?
subquestions.background_information:
Pre-tournament betting markets are a compact indicator of aggregated information about expected team strength, injuries, course fit, home advantage, and public/news sentiment. For the 2025 Ryder Cup, Team Europe enters as the defending champion from 2023, while Team USA has home advantage at Bethpage Black in New York. The 2025 event is scheduled for September 26-28, 2025, and the competition format requires 14.5 points to win; a 14-14 tie means Europe, as the holder, retains the Cup. Several late-August previews identify the venue, format, and likely lineups, including major U.S. names such as Scottie Scheffler, Xander Schauffele, and Bryson DeChambeau, and European stars such as Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm, Viktor Hovland, and Ludvig Åberg in media coverage of the event context. See Ryder Cup schedule/format summaries from Yahoo Sports Canada and Jagran Josh: https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/2025-ryder-cup-format-rules-203745515.html and https://www.jagranjosh.com/general-knowledge/ryder-cup-2025-team-usa-vs-team-europe-dates-format-and-venue-1820000506-1. FanDuel publicly posts golf outrights, including Ryder Cup winner markets, making it a plausible observable summary of market expectations: https://sportsbook.fanduel.com/navigation/golf.

Because the ultimate question is whether the USA wins, a shift to Europe being the market favorite before play starts would be evidence against a U.S. win. This is especially informative in a short-window sports forecast where direct pre-event indicators are limited and betting markets quickly incorporate lineup announcements, injury news, and sentiment.

Sources:
Yahoo Sports Canada – 2025 Ryder Cup format, rules: https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/2025-ryder-cup-format-rules-203745515.html
Jagran Josh – Ryder Cup 2025 Team USA vs Team Europe: Dates, Format and Venue: https://www.jagranjosh.com/general-knowledge/ryder-cup-2025-team-usa-vs-team-europe-dates-format-and-venue-1820000506-1
FanDuel Sportsbook Golf page: https://sportsbook.fanduel.com/navigation/golf
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26 inclusive, FanDuel Sportsbook lists Team Europe with shorter outright odds than Team USA in a market clearly labeled for the 2025 Ryder Cup winner (or equivalent winner market for USA vs Europe in the 2025 Ryder Cup). It resolves No if, throughout the entire window from 2025-09-01 through 2025-09-26 inclusive, Team Europe is never listed with shorter outright odds than Team USA.

Primary source: FanDuel Sportsbook golf pages and/or the specific Ryder Cup market page, if available: https://sportsbook.fanduel.com/navigation/golf

For American odds, a more negative number is shorter (e.g., Europe -120 vs USA +100 means Europe is favorite). For decimal odds, a smaller number is shorter. For fractional odds, a smaller implied probability denominator/ratio should be interpreted in the standard way; if needed, convert to implied probability.

If both teams are exactly tied in price at all observed times, that does not count as Europe being the favorite. Europe must be strictly shorter than USA.

If the specific market is temporarily unavailable on some dates, resolution should use archived snapshots from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine for FanDuel pages: https://web.archive.org/ and reliable odds aggregators that archive bookmaker-specific odds and clearly identify FanDuel as the quoted bookmaker, such as Oddschecker Ryder Cup pages: https://www.oddschecker.com/golf/ryder-cup. Fallback evidence should only count if it clearly shows FanDuel's quoted odds during the window.

If no reliable record of FanDuel Ryder Cup odds can be found for the relevant window, the question should resolve Unresolvable.

subquestions.background_information:
A renewed nationwide internet shutdown would be a useful early indicator of acute regime instability in Iran. Large-scale shutdowns are often used by the Iranian state during major protest waves or security crises, and such crises could increase the chance that Ali Khamenei is removed, incapacitated, or attempts to flee Iran before the ultimate question's deadline. The user-provided reporting says Iran imposed a major internet blackout beginning on 2026-01-08 amid nationwide protests and that officials were discussing restoration around 2026-01-24 to 2026-01-25. Those same reports describe unusually severe unrest, thousands of deaths, and rumors that Khamenei had delegated day-to-day operations to his son while sheltering in a bunker, all of which suggest the regime may still be under exceptional pressure if another national shutdown is imposed. See News.com.au coverage from 2026-01-25: https://www.news.com.au/world/middle-east/iranian-leader-hiding-son-left-in-charge/news-story/ and Republic World from 2026-01-25: https://www.republicworld.com/world-news/iran-supreme-leader-khamenei-reportedly-sheltering-in-underground-bunker-as-us-naval-forces-head-to-middle-east .

Independent monitoring organizations regularly track Iranian connectivity.
