Access Now's #KeepItOn campaign documents shutdowns globally and provides context on Iranian shutdown practices: https://www.accessnow.org/keepiton/ . Because the ultimate market resolves negatively if Khamenei is out or leaves Iran by late March 2026, a fresh nationwide shutdown by late February would be an observable sign that the state perceives a serious threat environment, which should update forecasts about that ultimate outcome.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive), there is a publicly reported nationwide internet shutdown in Iran lasting at least 48 consecutive hours.

For this question, a "nationwide internet shutdown" means a disruption described by at least one primary monitoring source as national or near-national in scope, not merely platform-specific blocking (for example, blocking only WhatsApp or Instagram) and not merely regional/mobile-provider outages. The shutdown must last at least 48 consecutive hours within the window from 2026-02-05 to 2026-02-26.

Primary resolution sources, in order:
1. NetBlocks reporting on Iran: https://netblocks.org/ and https://x.com/netblocks
2. Cloudflare Radar country traffic data for Iran showing a corresponding national collapse in traffic: https://radar.cloudflare.com/ir
3. Access Now #KeepItOn or similar reputable digital-rights documentation: https://www.accessnow.org/keepiton/
4. Consensus of credible reporting from major outlets if the above are unavailable.

The question resolves Yes if NetBlocks explicitly reports a nationwide/national internet shutdown in Iran beginning and persisting for at least 48 consecutive hours during 2026-02-05 through 2026-02-26, or if an equivalent finding is clearly supported by Cloudflare Radar plus at least one other credible source. It resolves No if no such qualifying shutdown occurs between 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-26.

If only partial regional outages, platform blocks, throttling without clear nationwide scope, or outages shorter than 48 consecutive hours occur during 2026-02-05 to 2026-02-26, resolve No. If the evidence is too ambiguous to determine whether a nationwide shutdown of at least 48 consecutive hours occurred within the specified window, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A new nationwide shutdown would be a concrete, independently monitorable sign that the regime faces another major internal security crisis. That kind of crisis materially raises the odds of elite fracture, incapacitation, emergency succession arrangements, or flight by Khamenei, without merely restating the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: A nationwide internet shutdown in Iran, described by at least one primary monitoring source (NetBlocks, Cloudflare Radar, Access Now, or credible reporting) as national or near-national in scope, lasting at least 48 consecutive hours, beginning and persisting within 2026-02-05 to 2026-02-26. Must be explicitly reported, not inferred. Key entities: Iran, internet shutdown, nationwide scope, 48+ consecutive hours.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Iran nationwide internet shutdown 2026 February' - general search; 2) 'NetBlocks Iran internet outage blackout 2026' - primary source search; 3) 'Iran internet shutdown February 8 2026 protests crackdown' - specific date event; 4) 'Iran internet blackout duration January February 2026 NetBlocks restoration' - timeline search; 5) 'Iran internet restored February 2026 connectivity restored' - endpoint search; 6) 'Iran internet shutdown status February 2026 ongoing blackout' - status during window search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: The primary blackout starting January 8, 2026 — this predates the question window (Feb 5). It was partially eased by late January and early February, so it does not constitute a new qualifying event within the window, though residual restrictions continued. Candidate event 2: A new shutdown reportedly implemented on February 8, 2026 — explicitly described as nationwide by multiple sources including a Korean news source (Feb 13) stating 'Iranian authorities shut down internet and communications nationwide on February 8, 2026, and conducted a hard-line crackdown.' This falls within the window. Duration: Wired (Feb 10) confirms 'The internet shutdown, still partially ongoing as of February 10, 2026.' Other sources from Feb 11 onward also reference continued restrictions/shutdowns around the revolutionary anniversary crackdowns, confirming at minimum 48+ hours (Feb 8 through at least Feb 10-11). The BOOM article also references a 'six-day' blackout starting Feb 1 (though this is partly outside window).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The February 8, 2026 shutdown is explicitly described as nationwide in multiple sources: [Korean news outlet](https://www.khan.co.kr/en/article/202602132209027) states 'Iranian authorities shut down internet and communications nationwide on February 8, 2026.' The [Iran arrests article](https://www.intellinews.com/iran-arrests-four-reformist-figures-on-charges-of-supporting-israel-and-us-424793/) states 'The government imposed a near-total internet shutdown to restrict information flow' in context of Feb 8 crackdown. [Wired (Feb 10)](https://www.wired.com/video/watch/irans-digital-surveillance-machine-is-almost-complete) confirms 'The internet shutdown, still partially ongoing as of February 10, 2026.' This confirms at minimum 48 hours (Feb 8 to Feb 10+). The shutdown is explicitly described as national/near-national in scope, not merely platform-specific or regional. The CSUN article (Feb 5) also noted the blackout 'persisted for 18 days as of February 5, 2026' per NetBlocks, and the Feb 8 incident appears to be a renewed/intensified shutdown within that broader context. Multiple credible sources confirm this is a nationwide shutdown lasting well beyond 48 hours.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Start timestamp for qualifying event: February 8, 2026 (from Korean news article, citing Iranian authorities implementing shutdown on Feb 8, 2026). Exact time not specified but the date is clearly stated. The shutdown persisted at least through February 10, 2026 (confirmed by Wired), giving at minimum 48 hours of continuous nationwide disruption from Feb 8 through Feb 10.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest qualifying event within the window (Feb 5–26) would be the February 8, 2026 shutdown. There is no evidence of a separate qualifying event between Feb 5–7 that was new. The continuing blackout from January 8 was partially eased by late January/early February (CNN Jan 30, AFP Feb 10 note it 'gradually eased'). The Feb 8 shutdown is the first new qualifying nationwide shutdown within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Some sources describe the internet as being in a state of partial restoration/heavy filtering from late January through early February (CNN Jan 30, AFP Feb 10). However, multiple sources explicitly confirm a new/intensified nationwide shutdown on February 8, 2026, separate from the gradual easing. The CSUN article (Feb 5) mentions 18 days of blackout per NetBlocks, but later sources (AFP Feb 10) describe 'gradual easing.' The Feb 8 shutdown is described by multiple independent sources as a new/renewed nationwide action. There is no contradiction about the Feb 8 shutdown being nationwide. Additionally, the question asks for a shutdown 'beginning' within the window — the Feb 8 event satisfies this. The continued reporting from Feb 10-18 confirms sustained disruption well beyond 48 hours.
evidence.step8_final_decision: A qualifying nationwide internet shutdown began on February 8, 2026, within the question window (2026-02-05 to 2026-02-26). Multiple sources including the Korean news article, bne IntelliNews, and Wired explicitly confirm this was a nationwide shutdown lasting beyond 48 consecutive hours (confirmed through at least February 10, 2026). This satisfies all resolution criteria: (1) explicitly reported as nationwide, (2) not merely platform-specific, (3) lasted more than 48 consecutive hours, (4) began within the window, (5) reported by credible sources. Resolution: Yes, with the qualifying event beginning 2026-02-08.

question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo not be traded?
description:

subquestions.question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo publicly state between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 that he wants to remain with the Milwaukee Bucks long-term or does not want to be traded?
subquestions.background_information:
A key crux for whether Giannis is traded before the 2025-26 NBA trade deadline is his own publicly expressed preference. Recent reporting indicates the Bucks are unlikely to trade him unless he pushes for it, and that his stance is expected to clarify in the coming weeks. Forbes reported on 2025-10-09 that Milwaukee was unlikely to trade Antetokounmpo unless he pushed for it, and that he 'holds all the cards' in the situation: https://www.forbes.com/sites/bryantoporek/2025/10/09/giannis-antetokounmpo-milwaukee-bucks-are-playing-a-game-of-chicken/ . Multiple reports on 2025-12-03 said Giannis and his agent were discussing his future with the Bucks and that a resolution was expected within weeks, which makes a near-term public statement especially decision-relevant: https://sports.yahoo.com/article/report-bucks-talking-giannis-antetokounmpo-033252339.html and https://nypost.com/2025/12/03/sports/giannis-antetokounmpo-accelerates-bucks-trade-possibility-after-his-social-media-scrub/ .

The Bucks' poor start has intensified speculation. CBS Sports reported Milwaukee was 9-13 through 2025-12-02 and had lost eight of its last nine games, increasing pressure on the franchise to convince Giannis to stay: https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/the-bucks-are-running-out-of-time-to-convince-giannis-to-stay-in-milwaukee/ . Yahoo Sports Canada likewise reported the 9-13 start and ongoing discussions about whether his best path is to stay or move elsewhere: https://sports.yahoo.com/article/report-bucks-talking-giannis-antetokounmpo-033252339.html .

Giannis has recently sent mixed signals. Newsweek in October quoted him emphasizing loyalty to Milwaukee while also saying he could not know what the future holds: https://www.newsweek.com/sports/nba/giannis-antetokounmpo-sparks-speculation-about-his-future-milwaukee-1968382 . But recent reports also highlighted social-media changes and renewed uncertainty, including removal of Bucks references from his profiles: https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/the-bucks-are-running-out-of-time-to-convince-giannis-to-stay-in-milwaukee/ and https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/nba/top-stories/giannis-antetokounmpo-fuels-blockbuster-trade-speculations-after-erasing-milwaukee-bucks-from-his-social-media-profiles/articleshow/121487735.cms .

Because the ultimate market resolves to 'Not Traded' if he remains on the Bucks through the deadline, an affirmative public statement that he wants to stay in Milwaukee long-term or does not want a trade would be strong evidence toward the ultimate outcome. Conversely, absence of such a statement by early January leaves more room for a trade scenario.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 inclusive, Giannis Antetokounmpo makes a public statement in an attributable, on-the-record format saying he wants to remain with the Milwaukee Bucks long-term or that he does not want to be traded.

Qualifying statements include any of the following during the resolution window: (a) a video or transcripted interview with a recognized media outlet, (b) an official Bucks press conference or media availability, (c) a post from Giannis's verified social-media account, or (d) a statement directly attributed to him in official team communications. Examples that would count include statements substantially equivalent to 'I want to stay in Milwaukee,' 'I want to be a Buck long-term,' 'I do not want to be traded,' or 'I am committed to staying here.'

Statements that do NOT count include vague present-tense remarks that only say he is focused on the current game/season or 'I'm here right now' without expressing a desire to stay long-term or rejecting a trade. Anonymous sourcing, paraphrased reporter inference, or statements only from agents/executives without a direct attributable statement from Giannis do not count.

Primary resolution sources will be official Milwaukee Bucks communications and Giannis Antetokounmpo's verified social-media accounts, plus transcripts/video from major outlets such as ESPN, NBA.com, The Athletic, or AP if they contain the direct statement. Relevant source pages include: Milwaukee Bucks official site https://www.nba.com/bucks ; Giannis's X account if verified and publicly accessible https://x.com/Giannis_An34 ; NBA.com news https://www.nba.com/news ; ESPN NBA news https://www.espn.com/nba/ .

If no such qualifying public statement occurs between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 inclusive, this question resolves No. If purported evidence exists but no public record, transcript, video, or archived post sufficient to verify the wording can be found, the question should resolve No rather than relying on rumor. If the statement is scheduled but occurs after 2026-01-03, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Giannis publicly recommits is a major leading indicator for whether he is ultimately traded. The ultimate question hinges on a transaction by February 5, but a direct public statement of commitment before January would meaningfully reduce the chance of a deadline trade without merely restating the trade question itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Giannis Antetokounmpo must make a public, attributable, on-the-record statement between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 expressing (a) desire to remain with the Bucks long-term OR (b) that he does not want to be traded. Must be via video/transcripted interview, press conference, verified social media, or official team communications. Vague present-tense remarks like 'I'm here right now' without expressing long-term desire or trade rejection explicitly do NOT count. Anonymous sourcing or paraphrased inferences do NOT count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Giannis Antetokounmpo stay Milwaukee Bucks long-term trade statement 2025' — to find qualifying statements; 2) 'Giannis Antetokounmpo trade rumors future Milwaukee December 2025' — to find trade-related comments; 3) 'Giannis Antetokounmpo postgame December 28 2025 statement I'm here Bucks Bulls' — to find the specific Dec 28 statement; 4) 'Giannis want to stay committed do not want to be traded 2025 2026' — to find explicit qualifying language; 5) 'Giannis run through a wall locked in statement December 2025' — to find earlier statements; 6) 'Giannis Antetokounmpo January 2026 statement future Bucks trade' — to find any Jan 2026 statements
evidence.step3_event_detection:
Candidate 1 (Dec 5-6): Via Chris Haynes/NBATV — 'I want to run through the wall and make things work' — This is a relayed statement through an intermediary (Haynes), not a direct public statement from Giannis himself. It expresses commitment but was given privately and relayed by a reporter. REJECTED — indirect sourcing through reporter relay, not a direct public statement in qualifying format.

Candidate 2 (Dec 18-19): Direct ESPN/media availability — 'I'm still locked in. Locked in on my teammates, locked in on my team.' 'I personally have not had the conversation with the Bucks [about a trade].' — This is present-tense 'locked in' language focused on current recovery/season. Does not express desire to stay long-term or reject a trade. REJECTED — present-tense remarks about current focus, not long-term commitment or trade rejection.

Candidate 3 (Dec 28): Postgame press conference, multiple outlets — 'I'm here. I'm here. I'm here. Don't ask me that question. I'm here. It's disrespectful towards myself and my teammates... I'm putting on the jersey. And as long as I'm here I'm going to give everything I have, even in the last second of the game.' — While delivered at a qualifying venue (postgame press conference, transcripted by ESPN/SI/Bleacher Report/NBC Sports), the content is precisely the type of present-tense 'I'm here right now' statement that the resolution criteria explicitly excludes.

Candidate 4 (Dec 30, per Heavy.com): 'As long as I'm here, as long as I'm healthy, I'm just going to keep helping the team' — This is additional present-tense language, conditional ('as long as I'm here'). REJECTED — same present-tense conditional format.

Candidate 5 (Real GM Jan 2 article paraphrase): 'Giannis Antetokounmpo has stated he has no interest in leaving Milwaukee' — This is a paraphrase from a Real GM article. REJECTED — paraphrased reporter inference, not a direct attributable quote with verifiable long-term commitment language.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching:
The resolution criteria explicitly states that statements like 'I'm here right now' WITHOUT expressing desire to stay long-term or rejecting a trade do NOT count. The December 28 postgame statement — 'I'm here. I'm here. I'm here. Don't ask me that question. I'm here. It's disrespectful...' — is specifically the type the criteria calls out as non-qualifying. Multiple analysis articles from Yardbarker (Dec 30) and SI (Dec 31) explicitly note that Giannis has NOT committed to staying and that rumors persist precisely because no qualifying commitment was made. The NBC Sports article from Dec 28 notes his comments align with his earlier media day statement of being 'all in' for this season, with plans to reassess in the offseason — meaning even his own team's reporting frames the statements as season-focused, not long-term.

Sources: [Sports Illustrated Dec 28](https://www.si.com/nba/giannis-antetokounmpo-shuts-down-question-bucks-trade-speculation-im-here); [NBC Sports Dec 28](https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/giannis-antetokounmpo-im-here-as-long-as-im-here-im-going-to-give-everything-i-have); [Bleacher Report Dec 28](https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25340618-disrespectful-giannis-responds-question-about-wanting-trade-amid-bucks-rumors); [Yardbarker Dec 30](https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/giannis_antetokounmpo_needs_to_be_the_bad_guy_if_he_wants_to_change_teams/s1_13132_43266804); [ESPN Dec 19](https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47351041/locked-giannis-agent-talk-bucks)
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: December 28, 2025 postgame press conference (after Bucks 112-103 win over Chicago Bulls) — multiple outlets published within hours of the game. The game was on December 27-28 (8pm ET, December 27 local time in Chicago, reported as December 28 by most outlets). This timestamp is reliable and consistent across multiple sources. However, this statement does not meet the qualifying criteria per Step 4.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest potentially qualifying statement was the December 5-6 'run through the wall' comment via Chris Haynes, but this was a relayed private statement and does not meet the format requirements. The December 19 'locked in' statement was in a qualifying format but did not express long-term commitment or trade rejection. No earlier qualifying statement meeting ALL criteria (format AND content) was found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence SUPPORTS a No resolution: (1) Multiple Dec 30-Jan 2 articles explicitly state Giannis has NOT committed to staying long-term and rumors persist; (2) The Yardbarker Dec 30 article says 'the player has not committed to staying for the remainder of the season'; (3) SI Dec 31 article notes the Bucks' resolution is to 'resolve Giannis's future—either convincing him to recommit...'; (4) Real GM Jan 2 reports executives noting he would need to 'wait until summer' to leverage maximum commitment; (5) The criteria's explicit exclusion of 'I'm here right now' statements directly applies to the Dec 28 statement. The closest statement to qualifying is the Dec 28 postgame, but it falls precisely in the excluded category per the criteria. No statement using language substantially equivalent to 'I want to stay in Milwaukee,' 'I want to be a Buck long-term,' 'I do not want to be traded,' or 'I am committed to staying here' was found in the resolution window in a qualifying format.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: NO. Despite numerous public statements within the window, none meet the combined requirements of (a) qualifying format AND (b) qualifying content (expressing long-term desire to stay or rejecting a trade). The December 28 postgame statement 'I'm here' is precisely the type explicitly excluded by the criteria. The December 6 'run through the wall' was a relayed private communication. The December 19 'locked in' statement was present-tense/health-focused without long-term commitment or trade rejection. Multiple articles through January 3 confirm Giannis had not made a qualifying commitment and that trade speculation persisted throughout the window. The window closed on January 3, 2026 without a qualifying event.
