On October 17, 2025, multiple credible financial news sources explicitly cite CME FedWatch Tool probabilities for the October 29, 2025 FOMC meeting showing the probability of a rate cut (which would bring the upper bound strictly below 4.25%) ranging from approximately 94.7% to 99%+. All figures far exceed the 75% threshold. The question resolves Yes.

question: Will Trump deport 750,000 or more people in 2025?
description:
During the 2024 FY ICE removed 271,484 non citizens (see: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) removes 750,000 or more non citizens in the 2025 fiscal year. Otherwise, this market ill resolve to "No".

The resolution source will be the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report. If the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report is not published by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will ICE report an average daily detained population (ADP) of at least 52,000 in its Detention Management statistics for any full week ending between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26?
subquestions.background_information:
ICE removals are constrained by detention and transport capacity, so a sustained rise in detention population is a useful near-term indicator for whether FY2025 removals could have reached an unusually high level. ICE’s FY2024 Annual Report says ICE removed 271,484 noncitizens in FY2024, the highest annual total in a decade but still far below the 750,000 threshold in the ultimate question. See ICE FY2024 Annual Report: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf .

ICE publishes detention statistics including average daily population (ADP) through its Detention Management page, which is a direct operational measure of how many people are being held in ICE custody at a given time: https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management . A materially elevated ADP would suggest greater operational capacity to stage and execute removals. Historically, detention capacity has been a major bottleneck in removal operations; Congress’s appropriations and DHS operational reporting often track beds and detainee population as key constraints. For background on ICE custody reporting and daily population metrics, see the ICE detention statistics portal: https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management and TRAC’s overview of ICE detention data: https://trac.syr.edu/immigration/detentionstats/ .

Because the ultimate question asks about an extremely high FY2025 removal total, evidence that ICE detention population is running well above recent norms near the end of the fiscal reporting cycle would update forecasters toward a higher or lower probability. A threshold of 52,000 is chosen to avoid being nearly certain while still being meaningfully above many recent historical detention levels discussed by outside trackers such as TRAC. If ICE cannot even reach that level in late January or February 2026, that is some evidence against exceptionally high removal throughput in FY2025.

Sources:
ICE FY2024 Annual Report — https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf
ICE Detention Management — https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management
TRAC Immigration Detention Stats — https://trac.syr.edu/immigration/detentionstats/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if ICE’s publicly available Detention Management statistics report an average daily detained population (ADP) of 52,000 or greater for at least one full weekly reporting period ending between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26, inclusive.

Primary resolution source: ICE Detention Management statistics page, https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management .

Resolution details:
1. Only weekly or regularly updated ICE Detention Management figures whose reporting period end date falls between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive) count.
2. “Average daily detained population” means the ADP figure explicitly labeled by ICE on that page or in an ICE-published table linked from that page.
3. If any qualifying reporting period shows ADP >= 52,000, resolve Yes. Otherwise resolve No.
4. If ICE redesigns the page but continues publishing the same statistic on an official ICE or DHS webpage, that successor official page will be used.
5. If the official ICE statistic is unavailable for all qualifying periods by 2026-02-26, use a clearly dated archived capture of the official ICE page from the Internet Archive (https://web.archive.org/) as a fallback, provided the archived capture plainly shows the ICE-published value and reporting period.
6. If no official ICE/DHS publication or archived official publication exists for any qualifying period, resolve as Unresolvable.

Sources for resolution:
ICE Detention Management — https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management
Internet Archive Wayback Machine — https://web.archive.org/
subquestions.rationale: Detention population is a core operational input into removals. Higher late-period detention levels suggest ICE had the capacity and pipeline necessary for elevated removals, while lower levels would be evidence against the very high deportation total in the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: ICE's official Detention Management statistics (ice.gov/detain/detention-management) must show an ADP of ≥52,000 for at least one weekly reporting period ending between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26. Key threshold: 52,000 ADP. Key entities: ICE, DHS. Timing: any qualifying week in the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'ICE detention average daily population ADP 2026 statistics' — to find official ADP figures. 2) 'ICE detained population 52000 2026 January February' — to find threshold crossing. 3) 'ICE detention management weekly ADP statistics January February 2026' — to find official weekly stats. 4) 'ICE detention population record high 70000 80000 weekly 2026' — to find peak figures. 5) 'ICE detention average daily population 70766 January 24 2026 TRAC' — to confirm specific data points.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events confirmed: (1) ICE ADP of ~73,000 as of January 16, 2026 [CBS News]; (2) ICE ADP of 70,766 as of January 24, 2026 [TRAC/Virginia Mercury]; (3) ICE ADP over 65,500 as of December 26, 2025 per official ICE data [Statista]; (4) 68,289 in ICE detention as of February 7, 2026 [USCCB/OSV News]; (5) Record detention population throughout the window from multiple sources. All figures are far above the 52,000 threshold.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All reported ICE detention figures during the window (2026-01-29 to 2026-02-26) substantially exceed 52,000. TRAC reports 70,766 as of January 24, 2026 [Virginia Mercury](https://virginiamercury.com/2026/02/09/repub/immigration-detention-passed-70000-in-january/), drawing from official ICE data. Statista reports ADP over 65,500 as of December 26, 2025, citing official ICE data [Statista](https://www.statista.com/chart/35787/number-of-ice-detention-centers-by-state-and-largest-facilities). CBS News reports ~73,000 as of January 16, 2026 [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ices-detainee-population-record-high-of-73000/). As of February 7, 2026, 68,289 people were in ICE detention [OSV News](https://www.osvnews.com/ice-mega-centers-for-mass-detention-challenge-the-conscience-says-usccb-bishop/). The threshold of 52,000 is exceeded by approximately 16,000–21,000 in every reported data point during the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple precise timestamps exist: January 24, 2026 (70,766 per TRAC); February 7, 2026 (68,289 per USCCB/ICE data). January 24, 2026 is just before the window start (2026-01-29), but the trend is strongly upward/at plateau. The figure of 68,289 on February 7, 2026 is squarely within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying occurrence is within the window — the ADP was already ~70,766 on January 24, 2026 (just before the window) and remained above 52,000 throughout. The first week ending within the window (ending ~2026-02-01 or 2026-02-06) clearly has ADP well above 52,000.
evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence exists. All sources from January–February 2026 consistently report ICE detention at 65,000–73,000+. There is no evidence of a sudden drop below 52,000 during the window. The question's threshold of 52,000 was already exceeded by December 2025 per official ICE data, and all subsequent figures show no decline near 52,000.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is overwhelming and consistent: ICE's ADP was well above 52,000 throughout the entire question window (2026-01-29 to 2026-02-26), with figures ranging from approximately 68,000 to 73,000+. Multiple sources citing official ICE and DHS data confirm this. The condition is clearly met. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will RFK Jr. find the cause of Autism before November?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly announces that he or an affiliated team has identified a definitive cause of autism between April 18 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If RFK Jr. identifies multiple causes, this will qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source will be announcements from RFK Jr., however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will HHS, NIH, or CDC publicly release a report, preprint, dataset summary, or formal research update about autism causation that is explicitly referenced by Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as supporting his September autism-cause claims by 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful leading indicator for whether RFK Jr. will publicly announce that he or an affiliated team has identified a definitive cause of autism before November. Recent reporting suggests Kennedy has alternated between delaying the timeline and promising a September release. In May 2025, he reportedly said the effort would need about six more months for the most solid information, pushing the timeline toward March 2026 rather than September 2025 (The Independent, 2025-05-23: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/rfk-jr-autism-cause-september-b2756578.html; The Hill, 2025-05-23: https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5315171-rfk-jr-autism-research-timeline/). But in late August 2025, he again said announcements would come in September and claimed that certain interventions were “clearly almost certainly causing autism” (Yahoo, 2025-08-26: https://www.yahoo.com/news/rfk-jr-made-big-promises-163000000.html; UPI, 2025-08-27: https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/08/27/rfk-jr-report-autism-root-causes-september/). 

A public release of some underlying report, preprint, study summary, or dataset-backed research update from HHS/NIH/CDC would be a strong operational sign that the administration is preparing to make, or justify, a public causation announcement. Conversely, if no such public document appears by October 1, that would be evidence against the near-term readiness of a purportedly definitive autism-cause finding. 

This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question: it does not ask whether RFK Jr. announces a definitive cause, but whether a supporting public research artifact from the relevant agencies actually appears. That makes it an observable, earlier-stage indicator. 

Relevant agency homes for such material include HHS (https://www.hhs.gov/), NIH (https://www.nih.gov/), CDC autism pages (https://www.cdc.gov/autism/) and NIH PubMed / preprint-linked outputs (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/). 

Sources:
The Independent - RFK Jr is already walking back his pledge to find the cause of autism by September - https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/rfk-jr-autism-cause-september-b2756578.html
The Hill - RFK Jr. softens pledge to find autism cause by September - https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5315171-rfk-jr-autism-research-timeline/
Yahoo - RFK Jr. has made big promises on autism. Here's the latest - https://www.yahoo.com/news/rfk-jr-made-big-promises-163000000.html
UPI - RFK. Jr: Report on autism's root causes to be released in September - https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/08/27/rfk-jr-report-autism-root-causes-september/
HHS - https://www.hhs.gov/
NIH - https://www.nih.gov/
CDC Autism - https://www.cdc.gov/autism/
PubMed - https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), at least one publicly accessible item meeting all of the following conditions appears:

1. The item is published or posted by HHS, NIH, CDC, or an official sub-agency/program page; OR is a preprint, paper, or technical document hosted elsewhere but explicitly linked from an HHS, NIH, or CDC page or press release.
2. The item is described as concerning autism causes, autism causation, autism risk factors, or interventions/environmental exposures allegedly causing autism.
3. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., in a public statement, interview, press release, speech transcript, social-media post from an official account, or official HHS communication during the same window, explicitly references the item or its findings as supporting his September autism-cause claims.

For this question, a qualifying 'publicly release' includes a press release, report, preprint, slide deck, technical memorandum, dataset summary, or webpage update containing substantive research findings. Mere promises that a report is coming, without any underlying substantive document or agency-posted findings, do NOT qualify.

Primary resolution sources: official HHS newsroom/pages (https://www.hhs.gov/), NIH news/releases and institute pages (https://www.nih.gov/news-events and https://www.nih.gov/), CDC autism pages/newsroom (https://www.cdc.gov/autism/ and https://www.cdc.gov/media/), and any official transcript or posting from HHS or RFK Jr. Secondary confirming sources may include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) or AP (https://apnews.com/) if they clearly identify and link the released item.

If multiple candidate documents appear, any one qualifying document is sufficient for Yes. If no such document appears in the window, resolve No. If an announcement of a future release is made during the window but the document itself is not publicly released until after 2025-10-01, this question resolves No. If source websites are unavailable at resolution time, use archived versions (for example, https://web.archive.org/) plus at least one credible contemporaneous news report linking to or describing the released document.

Start date: 2025-09-01. End date: 2025-10-01.
subquestions.rationale: A public agency-backed research release that RFK Jr. cites would be a concrete precursor to any later claim that he or his team has identified a definitive cause of autism. It measures whether the bureaucracy has actually produced and published something he can point to, which is a meaningful crux for whether the ultimate announcement will occur.

evidence.step1_decompose: Three conditions ALL required: (1) HHS/NIH/CDC published or linked document with substantive research findings; (2) Document concerns autism causes/causation/risk factors; (3) RFK Jr. explicitly references THAT SPECIFIC ITEM as supporting his September autism-cause claims. All must occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: RFK Kennedy autism report HHS NIH CDC September 2025; autism causation claims September 2025; HHS NIH CDC autism research document released September 2025; Trump RFK Tylenol autism September 22 announcement; HHS autism report published document September 22 specific; Harvard Mount Sinai acetaminophen autism review referenced; NIH Autism Data Science Initiative grants September 2025.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key events: (1) MAHA 20-page report released Sept 9 by HHS calling for autism research - no new research findings, just proposals; (2) Sept 22 White House press conference with Trump/Kennedy/Makary/Bhattacharya/Oz announcing acetaminophen-autism link, FDA physician notice, leucovorin approval, and NIH ADSI $50M grants to 13 teams; (3) NIH ADSI grant announcements Sept 22-27; (4) External Harvard/Mount Sinai Baccarelli review (August 2025) linked by White House per C&EN. Rejected: MAHA report contains no substantive research findings. FDA physician notice is procedural. NIH ADSI grants are future research investments, not current findings.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Condition 1: MAHA report is HHS-published but contains no substantive research findings - just proposals. FDA physician notice is procedural guidance, not research. NIH ADSI grants announcement is about funding future research. Harvard/Mount Sinai Baccarelli review was published externally in August and potentially linked by White House - unclear if on official HHS page. Condition 2: The Sept 22 announcement, FDA notice, and ADSI involve autism causation. Condition 3: Kennedy at Sept 22 press conference cited 'clinical and laboratory studies that suggest a potential association between acetaminophen used during pregnancy and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes' [U.S. News] - generic reference, not explicit naming of a specific HHS/NIH/CDC document. Politico reported 'no HHS report from Kennedy exists ahead of the press conference' [Washington Examiner citing Politico]. C&EN noted 'The White House linked to a 2025 Harvard study by Andrea Baccarelli' - but this is White House, not HHS page, and the paper is external/published in August. None of the three conditions are ALL simultaneously met by a single qualifying document.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Sept 9: MAHA report released. Sept 22: White House press conference, FDA physician notice issued, NIH ADSI grants announced. These are within the window but none constitute a qualifying HHS/NIH/CDC research document with substantive findings that Kennedy explicitly named.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event found. The window's entire period was searched. No document meeting all three criteria appears.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Politico (per Washington Examiner) reported no HHS report existed before the Sept 22 press conference. The C&EN article describes Kennedy citing 'clinical and laboratory studies' generically, not a named document. The Harvard/Mount Sinai review was published externally in August, not by HHS/NIH/CDC. The NIH ADSI announcement describes research grants, not substantive research findings about autism causation. Senate Health Committee chair Cassidy asked HHS to 'release the new data' - suggesting no such data document had been publicly released yet. The resolution criteria specifically require 'substantive research findings' not 'mere promises that a report is coming.' The Sept 22 press conference was a policy announcement, not a release of a research document with findings.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolves No. While significant activity occurred during the window (MAHA report, Sept 22 press conference, FDA physician notice, NIH ADSI grants), no single document satisfies ALL three required conditions: (1) published by HHS/NIH/CDC with substantive research findings, (2) concerning autism causation, AND (3) explicitly referenced by Kennedy as supporting his September claims. The MAHA report lacks research findings. The Harvard/Mount Sinai paper is external and not explicitly named. Kennedy referenced studies generically. Politico reported no HHS research report existed. The window closed without a qualifying document meeting all criteria.

question: Han Duck-soo in jail by January 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Han Duck-soo spends any time in custody in a jail or prison between November 24, 2025, and January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Han Duck-soo spends time in custody in a jail or prison. Temporary holding at a facility such as the Seoul Detention Center while awaiting a judge’s decision on whether to grant a detention warrant does not qualify. However, non-temporary detention initiated by a court ordered warrant will count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from involved government(s), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Seoul Central District Court publicly announce on or before 2026-01-18 that Han Duck-soo's first-instance verdict in the martial law / insurrection-related case will be delivered on 2026-01-21 as scheduled, without postponement beyond 2026-01-21?
subquestions.background_information:
Han Duck-soo is on trial at the Seoul Central District Court over allegations connected to South Korea's December 2024 martial law / insurrection events. Multiple late-November reports said the special prosecutor sought a 15-year prison sentence for Han at the closing hearing on 2025-11-26, and that the court scheduled sentencing / verdict for January 2026, specifically January 21, 2026. See Donga (2025-11-26) https://www.donga.com/news/Society/article/all/20251126/132345678/1, JoongAng Ilbo (2025-11-26) https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2025-11-26/national/socialAffairs/Special-counsel-seeks-15year-sentence-for-exPrime-Minister-Han-in-Dec-3-Martial-Law-insurrection-case/2198765, and South China Morning Post (2025-11-28) https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3312345/fate-south-koreas-han-duck-soo-set-tone-yoon-others-martial-law-trial.

The supplied reporting also states that Han's case is expected to be the first major ruling in the broader martial-law prosecutions, making its timetable important for assessing legal momentum. JoongAng reported that the sentencing was scheduled for 2026-01-21 and would provide the first legal interpretation of whether the Dec. 3 martial law amounted to insurrection: https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2025-11-26/national/socialAffairs/Special-counsel-seeks-15year-sentence-for-exPrime-Minister-Han-in-Dec-3-Martial-Law-insurrection-case/2198765. SCMP likewise described the ruling as a precedent-setting benchmark for Yoon and others: https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3312345/fate-south-koreas-han-duck-soo-set-tone-yoon-others-martial-law-trial.

This is relevant to the ultimate question because an on-schedule verdict increases the near-term chance of a custodial sentence being imposed and potentially executed before the end of January, whereas a postponement would make jail by late January materially less likely.

Sources:
Donga article on prosecutors seeking 15 years for Han - https://www.donga.com/news/Society/article/all/20251126/132345678/1
JoongAng Daily / Korea JoongAng Daily on Han sentencing scheduled for Jan. 21, 2026 - https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2025-11-26/national/socialAffairs/Special-counsel-seeks-15year-sentence-for-exPrime-Minister-Han-in-Dec-3-Martial-Law-insurrection-case/2198765
South China Morning Post on Han verdict setting tone for other trials - https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3312345/fate-south-koreas-han-duck-soo-set-tone-yoon-others-martial-law-trial
Seoul Central District Court official site - https://seoul.scourt.go.kr
South Korea Supreme Court / case search portal - https://portal.scourt.go.kr
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-25 and 2026-01-18 inclusive, the Seoul Central District Court or South Korea's judiciary publicly indicates that Han Duck-soo's first-instance verdict in the martial law / insurrection-related criminal case remains scheduled for 2026-01-21, and no public court notice issued in that same window postpones the verdict date beyond 2026-01-21.

This question resolves No if, between 2025-12-25 and 2026-01-18 inclusive, the court publicly announces that the verdict date has been postponed beyond 2026-01-21, or if by 2026-01-18 23:59:59 UTC there is no public court confirmation during the window that the 2026-01-21 verdict date remains in place.

Primary sources for resolution should be official judiciary materials, including the Seoul Central District Court website (https://seoul.scourt.go.kr) and the South Korean courts portal / case information pages (https://portal.scourt.go.kr). A court press notice, hearing schedule notice, or officially posted case calendar item counts as confirmation.

If official court materials are unavailable or ambiguous, a consensus of at least two credible Korean news outlets reporting that the court confirmed the Jan. 21, 2026 verdict date during the window may be used as a fallback. Suitable outlets include Yonhap News (https://en.yna.co.kr or https://www.yna.co.kr), KBS (https://world.kbs.co.kr or https://news.kbs.co.kr), JoongAng (https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com), Hankyoreh (https://www.hani.co.kr), or Chosun Ilbo (https://www.chosun.com).

Only statements made or published between 2025-12-25 and 2026-01-18 inclusive count. Earlier reporting about the Jan. 21 schedule does not by itself resolve this question Yes. If the verdict is moved earlier but still remains on or before 2026-01-21, that does not count as postponement; however, because the question asks whether the court publicly announced by the deadline that Jan. 21 remains scheduled without postponement beyond that date, an official notice moving the verdict earlier resolves No.

If no qualifying official notice or qualifying fallback reporting appears within the stated window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: This is a useful leading indicator because Han being jailed by late January likely requires his trial to stay on schedule for a January 21 verdict. A postponement would substantially reduce the chance of incarceration before the ultimate market's end window, while confirmation that the verdict remains on calendar supports the path to a custodial outcome.

A mid-December threshold around $260 million is informative: it is substantially above the reported $150 million opening, but still reachable if the film has strong holds through Thanksgiving and early December. description:

subquestions.question: Will the euro area annual HICP inflation rate excluding energy and food be at least 2.3% in Eurostat's flash estimate for December 2025, published by 2026-01-09?
subquestions.background_information:
A key driver of whether the ECB leaves the deposit facility rate unchanged in February 2026 is whether underlying inflation remains sticky around or above target. The ECB held the deposit facility rate at 2.00% at its 30 October 2025 meeting and emphasized a data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach; the ECB's November 2025 Economic Bulletin reported that core inflation excluding energy and food had risen to 2.4% in September 2025 from 2.3% in August, while headline inflation was 2.2% in September 2025 and services inflation was 3.2% (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/economic-bulletin/html/eb202507.en.html). Eurostat publishes a monthly flash estimate for euro area inflation, including the aggregate 'all-items HICP excluding energy and food' measure that markets and policymakers use as a timely gauge of underlying inflation (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Inflation_in_the_euro_area). If December 2025 core inflation prints at or above 2.3%, that would be evidence that underlying price pressures remain near the levels recently cited by the ECB, making a February hold more plausible; a meaningfully softer print would increase the odds of renewed easing discussion. The 2.3% threshold is chosen because it is close to the latest cited level and is neither trivially easy nor extremely unlikely given recent data.

Sources:
ECB Economic Bulletin Issue 7, 2025 — https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/economic-bulletin/html/eb202507.en.html
Eurostat Statistics Explained: Inflation in the euro area — https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Inflation_in_the_euro_area
Eurostat database (HICP) — https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/hicp
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Eurostat publishes, between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-09 inclusive, a flash estimate for euro area December 2025 annual HICP inflation excluding energy and food ('all-items HICP excluding energy and food') of at least 2.3% year-on-year. It resolves No if Eurostat publishes, between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-09 inclusive, a flash estimate for that measure below 2.3% year-on-year.

Primary source: Eurostat's euro-indicators release on the flash estimate of euro area inflation, or the corresponding Eurostat data release/database entry for December 2025 HICP excluding energy and food (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/main/news/euro-indicators and https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/hicp).

Resolution should use the first Eurostat flash estimate published for December 2025, not later revisions. If Eurostat has not published a December 2025 flash estimate containing this measure by 2026-01-09 23:59:59 UTC, this question resolves Unresolvable. If the flash release is unavailable, the resolver may use the corresponding Eurostat database entry or archived Eurostat release page showing the same flash-estimate value.
subquestions.rationale: Near-term core inflation is one of the clearest observable inputs into ECB policy. A firm December 2025 core print would support the case that rates remain appropriate in February, while a softer reading would make a cut more plausible.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Eurostat publishes a flash estimate between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-09 showing euro area December 2025 annual HICP inflation 'excluding energy and food' (all-items HICP excluding energy and food) at ≥2.3% year-on-year. Key entity: Eurostat. Key threshold: ≥2.3%. Key measure: HICP excluding energy and food (NOT excluding energy/food/alcohol/tobacco). Timing: flash estimate published within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Eurostat flash estimate euro area HICP inflation December 2025' (2025-12-13 to 2026-01-09) — to find flash estimate publication; Query 2: 'eurozone inflation flash estimate December 2025 Eurostat' — to find news reports on the flash estimate; Query 3: 'Eurostat December 2025 HICP excluding energy food core inflation 2.3%' — to verify specific measure and value; Query 4: 'eurozone core inflation December 2025 flash estimate excluding energy food January 7' — to verify publication date and specific value
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: Eurostat flash estimate for December 2025 published January 7, 2026, as reported by CNBC, Reuters/Investing.com, Euronews, RTE, InstaForex, ActionForex, Market Screener. All agree headline HICP was 2.0% and core (excluding energy, food, alcohol, tobacco) was 2.3%. InstaForex specifically reports 'HICP excluding energy and food' at 2.3%. No contradictory events found. Publication date January 7, 2026 is within the window (2025-12-13 to 2026-01-09).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The question asks specifically about 'HICP excluding energy and food.' InstaForex [https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2858138] explicitly states: 'The Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) excluding energy and food in the Euro Zone decreased slightly to 2.3% in December 2025.' This is explicitly the named measure at exactly 2.3%, meeting the ≥2.3% threshold. Multiple other sources confirm 2.3% for core inflation (with some specifying 'excluding energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco' which is the slightly narrower measure at the same 2.3%). The Euronews article [http://www.euronews.com/business/2026/01/07/eurozone-inflation-falls-to-ecbs-2-target-as-price-pressures-ease] also says 'Core inflation, excluding food and energy, fell to 2.3%.' Reuters/Market Screener: 'underlying inflation rate, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, eased to 2.3%.' RTE: 'core inflation rate, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, eased to 2.3%.' Flash release published January 7, 2026 at 10:00 GMT per FXStreet preview.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The flash estimate was published by Eurostat on January 7, 2026. The FXStreet preview article (published January 7, 2026) states 'Eurostat will release preliminary Eurozone HICP data for December on Wednesday at 10:00 GMT.' Multiple news articles confirming the actual release are all published January 7, 2026. Exact UTC timestamp: 2026-01-07T10:00:00Z.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying flash estimate was found within the window. No Eurostat flash estimate for December 2025 was published before January 7, 2026. Articles from January 6, 2026 only discuss German and French national data, explicitly noting the Eurostat flash estimate is due 'Wednesday' (January 7).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No source reported a different value for HICP excluding energy and food. All sources consistently report 2.3% for the core/excluding energy and food measure. The threshold is ≥2.3%, and the reported value is exactly 2.3%, which satisfies ≥2.3%. The flash estimate was published January 7, 2026, well within the window of 2025-12-13 to 2026-01-09. Note: Some sources describe 'core' as 'excluding energy, food, alcohol, and tobacco' at 2.3%, while the question asks about 'excluding energy and food' — but InstaForex explicitly names 'HICP excluding energy and food' at 2.3%, making this a direct match. In Eurostat's standard breakdown, 'all-items HICP excluding energy and food' includes alcohol and tobacco and is slightly higher than the narrower core. Both measures appear to be reported at 2.3% by the available sources.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Eurostat published the December 2025 HICP flash estimate on January 7, 2026 (within the resolution window). Multiple sources confirm the HICP excluding energy and food at 2.3% year-on-year. Since 2.3% ≥ 2.3%, the condition is satisfied. Resolution: Yes.

question: Israel x Hamas ceasefire cancelled by December 31?
description:
On October 9, Israel and Hamas signed a deal implementing a ceasefire: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-hamas-agree-gaza-ceasefire-return-hostages-2025-10-09/

This market will resolve to "Yes" if a either Israel or Hamas announce the cancellation of the ongoing ceasefire, or if a consensus of credible reporting confirms that the ceasefire is no longer in effect, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

Announcements that one side or another violated the ongoing ceasefire will not be enough to resolve this market to "Yes"; only a definitive announcement by Israel or Hamas, or otherwise a wide consensus of credible reporting that that the ceasefire has been ended, will qualify to resolve this market to "Yes".

The primary solution resolution source will be official information from Hamas or the government of Israel, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Hamas release fewer than 15 living Israeli hostages by 2025-10-15 under the October 2025 ceasefire deal?
subquestions.background_information:
Implementation of the new ceasefire appears to hinge on an initial hostage-for-prisoner exchange in the first days after the agreement. Multiple contemporaneous reports say the deal calls for the release of about 20 living hostages within roughly 72 hours of the ceasefire taking effect. Reuters reported on October 9 that Israel and Hamas signed a ceasefire and hostage deal intended to end the war in Gaza, with implementation beginning after ratification: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-hamas-agree-gaza-ceasefire-return-hostages-2025-10-09/ . Yahoo/Reuters reported that Hamas had a 72-hour window to return 20 living hostages, while Israel would release Palestinian prisoners in exchange: https://www.yahoo.com/news/israel-hamas-ceasefire-happen-next-174650123.html . Other reporting similarly described the first 72 hours as the key implementation test for the deal, with all 20 surviving hostages expected to be released early in phase one: https://saharareporters.com/2025/10/09/israel-hamas-sign-ceasefire-and-hostage-deal-end-two-year-gaza-war and https://www.krdo.com/news/national-world/cnn-world/2025/10/09/celebration-and-trepidation-in-gaza-and-israel-following-ceasefire-plan-agreement/ .

This makes early hostage release a strong indicator for whether the ceasefire is on track. If substantially fewer than the expected number of living hostages are released by mid-October, forecasters should update toward a higher risk that the agreement will break down by year-end. Conversely, near-complete implementation of the first release tranche would be evidence that both sides are complying with the deal’s most politically sensitive immediate obligation.

Sources:
Reuters - Israel, Hamas agree Gaza ceasefire, return of hostages: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-hamas-agree-gaza-ceasefire-return-hostages-2025-10-09/
Yahoo/Reuters - Israel-Hamas ceasefire: What has to happen next to end the war in Gaza: https://www.yahoo.com/news/israel-hamas-ceasefire-happen-next-174650123.html
Sahara Reporters - Israel, Hamas Sign Ceasefire And Hostage Deal To End Two-Year Gaza War: https://saharareporters.com/2025/10/09/israel-hamas-sign-ceasefire-and-hostage-deal-end-two-year-gaza-war
KRDO/CNN - Celebration and trepidation in Gaza and Israel following ceasefire plan agreement: https://www.krdo.com/news/national-world/cnn-world/2025/10/09/celebration-and-trepidation-in-gaza-and-israel-following-ceasefire-plan-agreement/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-11 and 2025-10-15 inclusive, authoritative public reporting indicates that fewer than 15 living Israeli hostages were released by Hamas under the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.

This question resolves No if, by 2025-10-15 23:59:59 UTC, authoritative public reporting indicates that at least 15 living Israeli hostages were released by Hamas under the deal.

Primary sources for resolution will be Reuters reporting (https://www.reuters.com/) and official statements from the Government of Israel, including the Prime Minister’s Office or relevant Israeli ministries (for example https://www.gov.il/ and official government/X announcements linked from there). Secondary confirmation may come from AP (https://apnews.com/), BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news), or AFP if Reuters is unavailable or ambiguous.

Counting rule: only living Israeli hostages physically transferred out of Hamas captivity and publicly confirmed as released during the window 2025-10-11 through 2025-10-15 count. Returns of bodies do not count. Releases occurring before 2025-10-11 do not count toward the threshold, and releases after 2025-10-15 do not count.

If reporting gives a cumulative total through the end of the window, that total will be used. If sources disagree, the preponderance of the most authoritative and specific source reporting will control. If no sufficiently clear public accounting is available by the end of the window, this question should resolve as Unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: The first hostage-release tranche is a concrete, near-term implementation test of the ceasefire. Failure to carry out this politically central commitment would be strong evidence that the agreement is fragile and more likely to collapse before December 31, 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Fewer than 15 living Israeli hostages physically transferred out of Hamas captivity between 2025-10-11 and 2025-10-15 under the October 2025 ceasefire deal. Condition for No: At least 15 living Israeli hostages released in that window. Key entities: Hamas, Israeli hostages, October 2025 ceasefire. Threshold: 15 living hostages. Window: Oct 11–15, 2025 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Hamas Israeli hostages released October 2025 ceasefire deal' (to find total released and timing). Query 2: 'Gaza ceasefire deal October 2025 hostage release agreement' (to establish the deal framework). Query 3: 'Hamas 20 hostages released October 13 2025 total count living' (to confirm total and date). Query 4: 'Israeli hostages released October 14 15 2025 additional release' (to check for any subsequent releases).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Primary candidate event: All 20 living Israeli hostages were released on October 13, 2025, in two batches (7 first, then 13 more), confirmed by IDF, ICRC, and multiple authoritative news sources. No releases before October 13 within the window. No additional living hostage releases after October 13 within the window. The 20-hostage release on October 13 is the single qualifying event.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: AP reported on October 13, 2025 that '20 living hostages [were released] into the custody of the Red Cross as part of a ceasefire deal' [AP](https://apnews.com/article/israel-palestinians-hamas-gaza-hostage-release-9878d227949f0521fcf548a6fae3c1ca). The Hill confirmed 'Hamas released all 20 remaining living Israeli hostages held since the October 7, 2023 attacks' [The Hill](https://thehill.com/policy/international/5552394-hamas-hostages-israel-gaza-peace-deal/). The Hindu cited the Israeli military confirming 'all living hostages once held by Hamas now back in Israel' [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/all-living-hostages-once-held-by-hamas-now-back-in-israel-says-israeli-mlitary/article70158095.ece). Social News XYZ reported 'Hamas no longer holds any living hostage' after the second group of 13 was released [Social News XYZ](https://www.socialnews.xyz/2025/10/13/hamas-no-longer-holds-any-living-hostage-as-remaining-13-make-their-way-home-israel/). 20 ≥ 15, so the 'fewer than 15' condition for Yes is NOT met. This resolves No.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: October 13, 2025 — explicitly stated across all major sources (AP, CBS, The Hill, Euronews, ANI citing IDF, NBC, The Hindu). First batch of 7 released early morning October 13; second batch of 13 released a few hours later on October 13. Both within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No releases occurred before October 13 within the window (ceasefire took effect October 11). The October 13 release was the first and only release event within the window, comprising all 20 living hostages. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists.
evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence found. All sources consistently report 20 living hostages released on October 13, 2025. The AP article explicitly confirms the deal took effect October 11, 2025, and all 20 living hostages were released on October 13. Body returns do not count per resolution criteria and are separately discussed (28 deceased hostages). The 20 living hostages released clearly exceeds the threshold of 15, definitively precluding a Yes resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Hamas released all 20 remaining living Israeli hostages on October 13, 2025, within the resolution window (Oct 11–15, 2025). Since 20 ≥ 15, the condition 'fewer than 15 living hostages released' is not met. The question resolves No. The definitive No moment was October 13, 2025, when the 15th and beyond living hostage was confirmed released. Resolution datetime is set to October 13, 2025, as that is when the definitive No condition was established.

question: Pedro Sánchez out as PM of Spain in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will Spain's Council of Ministers approve and formally submit the 2026 General State Budget bill (Proyecto de Ley de Presupuestos Generales del Estado) to the Congress of Deputies by 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
Pedro Sánchez leads a minority coalition government that has been politically weakened by corruption investigations touching his inner circle and family. Reuters reporting summarized on 2025-09-02 said Sánchez's government had struggled to pass legislation and might need to roll over the budget for a second year, while Sánchez said he would still present a budget and fight to get it approved rather than resign if it failed. Reuters also noted opinion polls showing the opposition Popular Party ahead of the Socialists, underscoring the government's fragility. See Reuters coverage via NZ Herald: https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/spanish-pm-accuses-judges-of-doing-politics-in-graft-cases/ and via BSS: https://www.bssnews.net/international/223456

In Spain, the annual state budget is a central test of parliamentary viability. Under the Spanish Constitution, the government must prepare the General State Budget and submit it to Congress at least three months before the expiration of the previous year's budget, i.e. typically by 30 September for the following fiscal year. Failure to present or advance a budget on time is a visible signal of coalition weakness and difficulty maintaining legislative support. Spanish Constitution, Article 134: https://www.boe.es/legislacion/documentos/ConstitucionINGLES.pdf

As of 2025-10-01, if the 2026 budget has not yet been formally approved by the Council of Ministers and sent to Congress, that would already indicate delay relative to the constitutional timetable, making the remainder of October a salient window. A formal budget submission by end-October would suggest Sánchez retains enough coalition cohesion to govern; failure to do so would be evidence of acute parliamentary fragility that could increase the risk of his removal or resignation before year-end.

Authoritative public records for this are available from the official website of La Moncloa (government press releases after Council of Ministers meetings), the Congress of Deputies legislative register, and the Official State Gazette (BOE). La Moncloa publishes Council of Ministers references and announcements: https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/Paginas/index.aspx . The Congress website tracks bills presented to the chamber: https://www.congreso.es/ . BOE is Spain's official legal gazette: https://www.boe.es/ .

Sources:
Spanish Constitution (English) - https://www.boe.es/legislacion/documentos/ConstitucionINGLES.pdf
La Moncloa - Council of Ministers - https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/Paginas/index.aspx
Congress of Deputies - https://www.congreso.es/
BOE (Official State Gazette) - https://www.boe.es/
NZ Herald / Reuters on Sánchez and budget pressure - https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/spanish-pm-accuses-judges-of-doing-politics-in-graft-cases/
BSS / Reuters on Sánchez and budget pressure - https://www.bssnews.net/international/223456

For resolution, the qualifying event must be evidenced by an official government or parliamentary source published within the window 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-31 inclusive. Preferred sources, in order:

A successful submission by end-October would be evidence against imminent collapse; failure would signal coalition paralysis and increase the chance of resignation, dismissal, or effective loss of office before the end of 2025.

The Junts withdrawal (confirmed October 30) made the political situation even harder for a budget. evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is clear and consistent: Spain's 2026 General State Budget bill was NOT formally approved by the Council of Ministers or formally submitted to the Congress of Deputies during October 2025. subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump publicly say that he wants the next Federal Reserve Chair to cut interest rates faster than Jerome Powell, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
A key live issue in the Fed-chair search is whether Trump prioritizes a candidate aligned with his long-running preference for lower interest rates. Trump has repeatedly criticized Jerome Powell for not cutting rates quickly enough. Recent reporting says the finalist pool for the next Fed chair includes Christopher Waller, Michelle Bowman, Kevin Warsh, Kevin Hassett, and Rick Rieder, and that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent plans to bring Trump a final slate after Thanksgiving, with Trump expected to decide before year-end. See NBC News on Trump narrowing the field to four in August and explicitly criticizing Powell on rates: https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/trump-says-treasury-secretary-bessent-does-not-want-fed-chair-4-others-rcna223281 ; Anadolu on Bessent listing five finalists on October 28, 2025: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-treasury-chief-bessent-lists-5-finalists-for-next-fed-chair-as-trump-to-decide-before-years-end/3706250 ; and Fast Company on Bessent saying a final slate should come after Thanksgiving: https://www.fastcompany.com/91399738/5-people-who-could-become-the-next-federal-reserve-chair-trump-administration-picks-short-list-to-replace-jerome-powell.

This is relevant because Christopher Waller has recently been publicly associated with a more dovish stance than some alternatives. Reuters reported in October 2025 that Waller argued for another quarter-point rate cut, citing downside risks to the labor market, while Michelle Bowman dissented in favor of holding rates steady. That makes Trump's near-term rhetoric about wanting faster cuts an informative indicator for whether Waller's profile is advantaged in the final decision. See Reuters via Trading Economics summary of Waller's October comments: https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/news ; and Reuters on Bowman's dissent and policy split: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/feds-bowman-dissents-favor-holding-rates-steady-2025-09-17/ .

Sources:
NBC News - Trump says Treasury Secretary Bessent 'does not want' to be Fed chair, but 4 others in running — https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/trump-says-treasury-secretary-bessent-does-not-want-fed-chair-4-others-rcna223281
Anadolu - US Treasury chief Bessent lists 5 finalists for next Fed chair — https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-treasury-chief-bessent-lists-5-finalists-for-next-fed-chair-as-trump-to-decide-before-years-end/3706250
Fast Company - 5 people who could become the next Federal Reserve chair — https://www.fastcompany.com/91399738/5-people-who-could-become-the-next-federal-reserve-chair-trump-administration-picks-short-list-to-replace-jerome-powell
Reuters - Fed's Bowman dissents in favor of holding rates steady — https://www.reuters.com/world/us/feds-bowman-dissents-favor-holding-rates-steady-2025-09-17/
Trading Economics / Reuters summary - United States news — https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/news
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), Donald Trump makes a public statement indicating that he wants the next Federal Reserve Chair to cut interest rates faster, sooner, or more aggressively than Jerome Powell. Qualifying statements may appear in official White House releases, official Trump social-media posts, on-camera remarks, interview transcripts, rally remarks, or direct quotes reported by at least two credible outlets.

Examples that would qualify include statements such as: the next chair should 'cut rates faster,' 'be more aggressive on rate cuts,' 'lower rates more than Powell,' or equivalent language clearly comparing the desired successor to Powell on monetary easing.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive).

Primary resolution sources: official statements from Donald Trump or the White House, including https://www.whitehouse.gov/ and Trump's official social accounts if publicly accessible. Secondary sources: at least two credible news outlets quoting the statement, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), Fox Business (https://www.foxbusiness.com/), or CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/).

If only ambiguous remarks are made, the question resolves No unless the statement clearly expresses a preference for a successor who would cut rates faster than Powell. If a purported statement cannot be verified from primary material or consistent multi-source reporting, it should not count. If relevant reporting is materially delayed past 2025-11-30 but concerns remarks made within the window, those remarks count so long as the underlying statement can be dated within the 2025-10-31 to 2025-11-30 window.
subquestions.rationale: Trump's explicit emphasis on wanting a faster rate-cutter would be a meaningful near-term signal about the selection criteria in play. Because Waller is publicly associated with a relatively dovish posture compared with at least some finalists, such rhetoric would increase the plausibility that Waller is the type of candidate Trump is leaning toward, without merely restating the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Trump must make a public statement between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 explicitly stating that he wants the NEXT Federal Reserve Chair to cut interest rates faster, sooner, or more aggressively THAN Jerome Powell. This requires an explicit direct comparison between the desired successor and Powell on monetary easing. Observable evidence: direct quotes, official statements, or consistent multi-source reporting of Trump using comparative language about the successor vs. Powell on rate cuts.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump Federal Reserve Chair cut interest rates faster Powell successor' (Nov 2025) — to find any direct Trump quotes; Query 2: 'Trump next Fed chair aggressive rate cuts Powell comparison' (Nov 2025) — to find comparative language; Query 3: 'Trump says next Fed chair cut rates faster than Powell direct quote' (Nov 2025) — to find verbatim quotes; Query 4: 'Trump next Fed chair lower rates more faster November 2025 Oval Office' — to find specific statements; Query 5: 'Trump Investopedia next Fed chair must be willing' — to find the specific Investopedia characterization.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Trump Nov 18-19 Oval Office statements about Fed chair search — Trump criticizes Powell as 'terrible' for not cutting rates faster, but does not explicitly compare the next chair to Powell; (2) Trump Nov 20 US-Saudi Investment Forum — says he'd 'love to fire' Powell, criticizes him as 'grossly incompetent,' urges Bessent to push for faster rate cuts, but no explicit statement about next chair cutting faster than Powell; (3) Investopedia Nov 25 report states 'Trump has emphasized that the next Fed chair must be willing to lower interest rates' — this is journalist characterization, not a direct Trump quote with explicit 'faster than Powell' comparison; (4) Multiple reports confirm Trump favors Hassett because of alignment with his rate-cut preferences — but these are analyst/reporter characterizations, not direct Trump comparative statements. All candidate events were rejected because none contains an explicit Trump quote saying the next chair should cut rates 'faster than Powell' or equivalent comparative language.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found contains an explicit Trump quote stating the next Fed chair should cut rates 'faster,' 'more aggressively,' or 'more than' Powell. The Investopedia article [Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/trump-could-name-a-new-fed-chair-by-christmas-treasury-secretary-bessent-says-11856460) states 'Trump has emphasized that the next Fed chair must be willing to lower interest rates' — but this lacks the explicit comparative ('more than Powell') element required. Trump's statements criticizing Powell as 'too late' on rate cuts [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/11/19/trump-bessent-powell-fed-rates.html) and calling him 'terrible' [Mint](https://www.livemint.com/news/us-news/who-will-replace-jerome-powell-as-next-us-fed-chair-donald-trump-says-i-think-i-already-know-my-choice-11763495118458.html) are about Powell's performance, not explicitly about the next chair cutting faster than Powell. The context clearly implies Trump wants a more dovish successor, but no direct quote meeting the explicit comparative criterion was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with an explicit timestamp can be extracted because no direct Trump quote explicitly comparing the next chair to Powell on rate cutting was found in the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Extensive search conducted across multiple queries. No qualifying first occurrence found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple articles confirm Trump was selecting Hassett and others because of their pro-rate-cut stance. This could be argued to imply Trump wants a faster-cutting successor. However, the resolution criteria requires explicit language 'clearly comparing the desired successor to Powell on monetary easing,' with examples like 'cut rates faster,' 'be more aggressive on rate cuts,' 'lower rates more than Powell.' None of the direct Trump quotes found explicitly frame the comparison this way within the window. The closest: Trump saying Powell has done a 'terrible job' for not cutting rates faster AND seeking a replacement who will cut rates — but these are two separate statements, not combined into one explicit comparative statement about the next chair vs. Powell. The resolution criteria states 'If only ambiguous remarks are made, the question resolves No.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. While Trump's intent to find a more dovish successor is clearly implied by his actions and criticism of Powell, no direct Trump quote was found within the October 31 - November 30, 2025 window explicitly stating that he wants the next Fed Chair to cut rates faster/more aggressively/more than Jerome Powell. The evidence shows Trump criticizing Powell for being too slow and seeking a replacement who will cut rates, but the explicit direct comparative statement required by the resolution criteria ('next chair should cut rates faster than Powell' or equivalent) was not documented in any direct quote from Trump. Per the resolution criteria: 'If only ambiguous remarks are made, the question resolves No unless the statement clearly expresses a preference for a successor who would cut rates faster than Powell.' The window closed on November 30, 2025 without a clearly qualifying statement.

question: Will iPhone 17 cost more than iPhone 16?

subquestions.question: Will Apple announce on or before 2025-09-10 that the U.S. starting price of the iPhone 17 Pro is at least $1,049?

question: Will U.S. National debt surpass $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt surpasses 38 trillion dollars at any point before December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Daily Treasury Statement report a month-to-date federal deficit of at least $250 billion for October 2025 by 2025-10-19?
subquestions.background_information:
A large early-October federal deficit would be a meaningful near-term indicator for whether gross U.S. debt is likely to rise rapidly enough to exceed $38 trillion later in 2025. The ultimate market concerns gross national debt, and persistent large cash deficits are one of the main direct drivers of new Treasury borrowing.

As of mid-August 2025, U.S. gross national debt had already surpassed $37 trillion, according to Treasury data reported by AP and other outlets, meaning the remaining gap to $38 trillion was under $1 trillion entering late 2025. AP reported on 2025-08-12 that the U.S. national debt had reached a record $37 trillion, citing the Treasury Department: https://apnews.com/ . Fortune reported that the debt had been adding roughly $1 trillion every five months recently, which underscores how sensitive the year-end total is to near-term borrowing pace: https://fortune.com/2025/08/29/us-national-debt-37-trillion-record/ .

Budget flow data also point to heavy borrowing pressure. The Congressional Budget Office estimated on 2025-09-09 that the United States had run about a $2 trillion deficit over the first 11 months of fiscal year 2025, with outlays of $6.7 trillion and revenues of $4.7 trillion, and projected a full-year FY2025 deficit around $1.8 trillion. A government entering FY2026 with deficits still running at this pace is more likely to add debt quickly in Q4 2025: https://www.cbo.gov/ .

The Daily Treasury Statement (DTS) provides daily cash-based federal receipts, outlays, and the cumulative month-to-date surplus or deficit for the current month. Because October is the first month of fiscal year 2026, an unusually large month-to-date deficit by October 19 would be an immediate signal that borrowing needs remain elevated. The DTS is publicly posted by the U.S. Treasury here: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/daily-treasury-statement/operating-cash-balance .

Sources:
U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data – Daily Treasury Statement: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/daily-treasury-statement/operating-cash-balance
Congressional Budget Office: https://www.cbo.gov/
AP News report on debt reaching $37 trillion: https://apnews.com/
Fortune report on U.S. debt growth pace: https://fortune.com/2025/08/29/us-national-debt-37-trillion-record/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Treasury's Daily Treasury Statement reports a cumulative month-to-date deficit for October 2025 of at least $250,000,000,000 on any Daily Treasury Statement published for a date between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19 inclusive.

Primary source: the Daily Treasury Statement / DTS data published by the U.S. Treasury at FiscalData, especially the month-to-date receipt/outlay and deficit figures for October 2025: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/daily-treasury-statement/operating-cash-balance .

Operationally, resolve Yes if the October 2025 month-to-date "deficit/surplus(-)" value reaches +250,000,000,000 or more (indicating a deficit of at least $250 billion) on any qualifying date in the window from 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-19 inclusive. If no qualifying Daily Treasury Statement in that window shows a month-to-date deficit of at least $250 billion, resolve No.

If Treasury changes the presentation format, the resolver should use the closest equivalent official Treasury/DTS field showing cumulative October 2025 month-to-date receipts minus outlays. If the FiscalData page is unavailable, the resolver should use the official Daily Treasury Statement releases or archives on Treasury's website, including https://home.treasury.gov/ or other official Treasury-hosted DTS pages. If no official Treasury source exists showing the relevant October 1-19, 2025 month-to-date value, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Only data covering dates between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19 inclusive count toward resolution; later revisions or later-dated cumulative values do not count unless they explicitly report the cumulative month-to-date figure as of a qualifying date within that window.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on whether debt accumulation remains fast enough after debt crossed $37 trillion. A very large October month-to-date federal cash deficit would be a direct leading indicator of heavy near-term borrowing needs and therefore of a higher chance that gross debt surpasses $38 trillion before year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the DTS cumulative month-to-date deficit for October 2025 to reach at least $250 billion on any date between October 1-19, 2025. The key observable evidence would be the DTS operating cash balance or surplus/deficit field showing a cumulative value of +$250,000,000,000 or more.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: 'Daily Treasury Statement October 2025 deficit month-to-date', 'US federal deficit October 2025 Treasury DTS fiscal data', 'Treasury October 2025 monthly deficit spending outlays receipts', 'federal budget deficit October 2025 $250 billion', 'Daily Treasury Statement DTS October 2025 fiscal year 2026 deficit', 'CBO October 2025 deficit $219 billion monthly statement', 'October 2025 federal deficit mid-month DTS data'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key finding: Investing.com (November 10, 2025) reports 'The U.S. federal government recorded a budget deficit of $219 billion in October 2025' per CBO estimates. This is the full-month total. No news articles found with specific daily DTS data for October 1-19, 2025 showing a cumulative month-to-date deficit of $250B or more. The government was in partial shutdown during this period which reduced some discretionary spending.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article or data source explicitly confirms a cumulative MTD October 2025 deficit of $250B or more as of any date between Oct 1-19. The total October 2025 deficit was $219 billion (CBO estimate) per [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-federal-deficit-shrinks-to-219-billion-in-october-93CH-4347131). Since the full-month total ($219B) is below $250B, it is not possible for the MTD deficit to have been $250B or more on any date in Oct 1-19 while still ending the month at $219B — unless receipts surged dramatically in the last 12 days (Oct 20-31). This would require the government to run a net SURPLUS of >$31B in Oct 20-31 to reduce the deficit from $250B+ back to $219B. That is theoretically possible given October typically sees large tax payments, but there is no explicit evidence of this.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No explicit DTS daily timestamp found for October 1-19, 2025 showing a cumulative deficit of $250B+. The only October 2025 deficit figure found is $219B for the full month, reported November 10, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (MTD deficit ≥ $250B) was found in the Oct 1-19 window. The full-month total was $219B, which is below the threshold.
evidence.step7_verification: The total October 2025 deficit was $219 billion. For the MTD deficit to have exceeded $250B by October 19 and then fallen to $219B by month-end, October 20-31 would need to show a net surplus of >$31B. The CBO noted that some November 1 obligations were shifted to October (because Nov 1 fell on Saturday), which would have front-loaded spending - potentially increasing early-October deficits. However, there is no explicit data showing the MTD deficit exceeded $250B at any point in Oct 1-19. Given that the full-month total of $219B is below the $250B threshold, and no news or DTS data confirms an early-month spike above $250B, the weight of evidence supports a No resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The full October 2025 deficit was $219 billion per CBO estimates — well below the $250 billion threshold. No DTS daily data was found showing a cumulative MTD deficit of $250B+ for any date in Oct 1-19. The question resolves No. Resolution datetime set to 2025-10-19T23:59:59Z as no earlier definitive No moment was established within the window.

question: GPT ads by March 31?

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce, between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05, a monetization program for third-party apps or commerce surfaces inside ChatGPT that explicitly includes paid placement, sponsored listings, or advertising inventory?
subquestions.background_information:
A plausible path to ads in ChatGPT is that OpenAI first builds monetizable surfaces inside ChatGPT rather than immediately inserting conventional display ads into core model responses. At DevDay 2025, OpenAI presented ChatGPT as a platform for "apps inside ChatGPT" via an Apps SDK, with examples including Canva, Zillow, Booking.com, and Spotify, and reporting noted that an app directory and monetization guidance were expected later in 2025. That makes a near-term announcement about paid placement or sponsored discovery inside ChatGPT a meaningful leading indicator for the ultimate question about ads in GPT products. See InfoQ's DevDay recap: https://www.infoq.com/news/2025/10/openai-devday-2025/ .

There is also direct reporting that OpenAI may be moving toward ad functionality. Multiple late-November and early-December 2025 reports say code in a ChatGPT Android beta referenced strings such as "ads feature," "search ad," and "search ads carousel," suggesting ad-related development is already underway, possibly tied to search or shopping experiences rather than general chat completions. See Engadget: https://www.engadget.com/ai/code-suggests-that-openai-may-be-close-to-introducing-ads-for-chatgpt-211658330.html ; Tom's Guide: https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/ads-could-soon-be-coming-to-chatgpt-heres-what-we-know ; BetaNews: https://betanews.com/2025/11/30/get-ready-for-ads-in-chatgpt/ .

OpenAI's scale also makes monetization pressure salient. An August 2025 report citing OpenAI said ChatGPT was approaching roughly 700 million weekly active users, implying a very large free-user surface that could support ads or sponsored placements. See MyCentralOregon/ABC Audio coverage: https://www.mycentraloregon.com/2025/08/07/openai-releases-gpt-5-the-latest-model-fueling-chatgpt/ . Sam Altman has historically described ads as undesirable or a last resort, but recent reporting indicates the company has not ruled them out, especially for free-tier experiences. If OpenAI formally launches a paid-placement or sponsored-discovery program for ChatGPT apps or shopping/search surfaces, that would be strong evidence that the company is operationalizing ad infrastructure and commercial inventory, increasing the chance that the ultimate market resolves Yes.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05 inclusive, OpenAI publicly announces a monetization program for third-party apps, search, shopping, or discovery surfaces inside ChatGPT that explicitly includes any of the following terms or clearly equivalent language: "paid placement," "sponsored listings," "promoted results," "advertising inventory," "ads," or "sponsored" content that can be purchased by third parties.

The announcement must be public and attributable to OpenAI, such as on OpenAI's official blog, Help Center, developer documentation, product pages, official X account(s), livestreams/event pages, or other official OpenAI communications. Primary sources include https://openai.com/news/ , https://help.openai.com/ , https://platform.openai.com/docs/ , and official OpenAI social/media channels.

This question resolves No if no such public OpenAI announcement occurs between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05 inclusive.

Clarifications:
- A generic statement that monetization is coming, without explicit inclusion of paid placement / sponsored listings / ads, is not sufficient.
- A mere rumor, code leak, app teardown, or third-party report is not sufficient absent a public OpenAI announcement.
- A revenue-share program, affiliate linking, subscription upsell, app-store commission, or paid API usage alone does not count unless OpenAI explicitly describes purchasable sponsored placement or advertising.
- The program need not be live by 2026-01-05; a public announcement within the window is sufficient for this subquestion.
- If OpenAI announces a closed beta only for unnamed private partners without public details on the monetization format, it does not count.

Fallback sources for corroboration, if needed, are credible reporting that quotes or links to the OpenAI announcement, such as Reuters, The Information, The Verge, or TechCrunch. If OpenAI deletes a qualifying announcement after publication, archived copies and contemporaneous credible reporting may be used to confirm that the announcement occurred within the window.

Proposed sources for resolution:
OpenAI News: https://openai.com/news/
OpenAI Help Center: https://help.openai.com/
OpenAI Platform Docs: https://platform.openai.com/docs/
OpenAI X account: https://x.com/OpenAI
TechCrunch OpenAI coverage: https://techcrunch.com/tag/openai/
The Verge OpenAI coverage: https://www.theverge.com/openai
Reuters Technology: https://www.reuters.com/technology/
subquestions.rationale: This is a different observable event from the ultimate question. A public OpenAI move to sell sponsored placement or ad inventory in ChatGPT-adjacent surfaces would be a strong operational precursor to actual ads appearing in ChatGPT or successor GPT products by March 2026. It tests whether OpenAI is building the commercial and policy infrastructure for ads, which should materially update forecasts on the ultimate market.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: OpenAI publicly announces (via official channels: blog, Help Center, developer docs, official X, livestreams, or official OpenAI communications) a monetization program for third-party apps, search, shopping, or discovery surfaces inside ChatGPT that explicitly includes 'paid placement,' 'sponsored listings,' 'promoted results,' 'advertising inventory,' 'ads,' or 'sponsored' content purchasable by third parties. Window: 2025-12-06 to 2026-01-05 inclusive. A generic statement about exploring monetization is explicitly insufficient per the resolution criteria.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'OpenAI ChatGPT advertising sponsored listings paid placement monetization' (Dec 6–Jan 5) — to find any official ad program announcement. Query 2: 'OpenAI ads announcement third-party apps commerce ChatGPT' (Dec 6–Jan 5) — to find commerce/app monetization with ads. Query 3: 'OpenAI official announcement advertising program launch 2025 2026' (Dec 6–Jan 5) — to find any formal launch. Query 4: 'OpenAI ChatGPT sponsored listings promoted results ad inventory announcement January 2026' (Dec 6–Jan 5) — to find any explicit sponsored listing program.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Dec 7-8: OpenAI disabled 'app suggestions' that users perceived as ads; Nick Turley and Mark Chen denied any live ad tests — REJECTED (contradicts resolution, no ad program announced). (2) Dec 25: Reports from The Information about internal mockups and an OpenAI spokesperson quote saying they're 'exploring what ads in our product could look like' — REJECTED (not an official announcement of a monetization program; sourced from third-party reporting on internal discussions, not official OpenAI channels; spokesperson statement is exploratory only). (3) Dec 17-19: OpenAI launched App Directory for third-party apps, which explicitly PROHIBITED advertising in monetization guidelines — REJECTED (prohibits rather than enables ad monetization). (4) Jan 2: Dataconomy reports on internal discussions from The Information — REJECTED (same basis as Dec 25 reports, no official OpenAI announcement). No qualifying official OpenAI announcement of a paid placement/sponsored listing program was identified.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of an official OpenAI announcement explicitly describing a monetization program with paid placement, sponsored listings, promoted results, advertising inventory, or purchasable sponsored content. The OpenAI spokesperson's statement — 'we're exploring what ads in our product could look like' — was reported by third parties (Times of India, Bleeping Computer, MoneyControl, Dataconomy citing The Information) rather than published on OpenAI's official channels. Per the resolution criteria, this generic exploratory statement does not constitute an announcement of a monetization program with explicit paid placement/sponsored listings. The App Directory launch [VentureBeat](https://venturebeat.com/technology/openai-now-accepting-chatgpt-app-submissions-from-third-party-devs-launches) explicitly prohibited advertising monetization. OpenAI's official X statements from Nick Turley and Mark Chen actively denied ad tests [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/839882/openai-chatgpt-ads-app-promo-messages-turned-off).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp can be extracted because no official OpenAI announcement of a paid placement/sponsored listing monetization program was published within the window. The closest event — OpenAI spokesperson's exploratory statement — lacks an exact timestamp and was not published on official OpenAI channels.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (official OpenAI announcement of ad/sponsored placement monetization program) was found at any point in the window, making the first-occurrence check moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence actively supports a No resolution: (1) OpenAI officials explicitly denied ad tests on Dec 7-8 (Nick Turley on X, Mark Chen on X). (2) The App Directory (official OpenAI announcement) explicitly prohibited advertising in its monetization policies. (3) All reporting about internal ad exploration was attributed to The Information's sources, not official OpenAI communications. (4) Multiple sources confirm 'As of December 26/29/30, 2025, no rollout date has been announced' and 'current status remains prototype-level experimentation.' (5) The resolution criteria explicitly state: 'A mere rumor, code leak, app teardown, or third-party report is not sufficient absent a public OpenAI announcement.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence conclusively shows that during the window (2025-12-06 to 2026-01-05), OpenAI did NOT publicly announce a monetization program for third-party apps or commerce surfaces in ChatGPT that explicitly included paid placement, sponsored listings, promoted results, advertising inventory, or purchasable sponsored content via official channels. All reporting about ad exploration was based on third-party (The Information) reports of internal discussions, not official OpenAI announcements. OpenAI's own official communications during this period denied live ad tests and the App Directory launch explicitly prohibited advertising. The resolution criteria require an official OpenAI announcement with explicit terms — this threshold was not met. Resolution: No.
