subquestions.question: Will the U.S. president and the Russian president publicly announce, between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-11 inclusive, that they have agreed in principle to extend or replace New START?
subquestions.background_information:
One of the ultimate market's disjunctive failure conditions is a "US-Russia nuclear deal" before the end of 2025. A near-term and more observable indicator for that outcome is whether Washington and Moscow publicly converge on a concrete arms-control framework first. New START is the last major bilateral U.S.-Russia strategic arms treaty; it limits deployed strategic warheads and delivery systems and is due to expire on February 5, 2026 according to the U.S. State Department, making late-2025 diplomacy especially salient. https://www.state.gov/new-start/

Recent reporting suggests this is live diplomacy rather than a hypothetical. PBS reported on 2025-10-10 that Vladimir Putin said he hoped to extend the 2010 New START treaty for another year, and that Donald Trump had earlier called the proposal "a good idea." https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/putin-praises-trumps-peace-efforts-despite-failure-to-win-nobel-prize The same report notes Putin warned that if the treaty lapses there would be no remaining arms-control agreement between the two largest nuclear powers. https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/putin-praises-trumps-peace-efforts-despite-failure-to-win-nobel-prize

Reuters has also described New START as the last remaining nuclear arms control treaty between the United States and Russia and notes its February 2026 expiration, which raises the odds of a visible diplomatic push in the weeks before year-end. https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/what-is-new-start-last-remaining-us-russia-nuclear-arms-treaty-2023-02-21/

Because the ultimate question would resolve negatively if a qualifying US-Russia nuclear deal occurs by 2025-12-31, a public announcement by both presidents that they have agreed in principle to extend or replace New START would be a strong leading indicator. It is not identical to the ultimate condition: an in-principle announcement could happen without a final qualifying deal, and conversely a final deal could conceivably emerge later without such an earlier signal. That makes it a useful crux rather than a restatement.

Sources:
U.S. State Department - New START: https://www.state.gov/new-start/
PBS - Putin praises Trump's peace efforts, despite failure to win Nobel prize: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/putin-praises-trumps-peace-efforts-despite-failure-to-win-nobel-prize
Reuters - What is New START, last remaining U.S.-Russia nuclear arms treaty?: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/what-is-new-start-last-remaining-us-russia-nuclear-arms-treaty-2023-02-21/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-11 inclusive, there is a public announcement from the White House/U.S. President and a public announcement from the Kremlin/Russian President that clearly state that the two sides have agreed in principle on either (a) extending New START, or (b) replacing New START with another bilateral strategic nuclear arms-control arrangement.

For Yes, all of the following must be true within the resolution window:
1. There must be public, attributable statements from both sides during the window 2025-11-11 through 2025-12-11.
2. The statements must indicate more than merely discussing, proposing, or being open to a deal; they must communicate that an agreement in principle has been reached.
3. The subject must be strategic nuclear arms control between the U.S. and Russia, specifically New START extension or replacement.

This question resolves No if no such mutually corroborating public announcements occur between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-11 inclusive.

Primary sources for resolution, in order of priority:
- White House statements/briefings: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- Kremlin official president news/releases: http://en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news and http://kremlin.ru/events/president/news
- U.S. State Department press releases: https://www.state.gov/press-releases/

Fallback reporting sources, if primary statements are ambiguous or unavailable, are Reuters and AP reporting that directly quotes or cites official statements:
- Reuters world news: https://www.reuters.com/world/
- AP world news: https://apnews.com/hub/world-news

Edge cases:
- Mere statements that extension is "a good idea," that talks are ongoing, or that a summit is planned do NOT qualify.
- A signed treaty text is not required for Yes, but the language must clearly indicate an agreement in principle.
- If only one side makes the claim and the other side does not publicly confirm during the window, resolve No.
- If qualifying announcements occur after 2025-12-11, they do not count.
- If relevant meetings are postponed beyond 2025-12-11 without qualifying announcements in the window, resolve No rather than unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A bilateral in-principle New START announcement would be one of the clearest observable precursors to the ultimate market's "US-Russia nuclear deal" failure condition. It captures whether diplomacy is moving from rhetoric to concrete agreement, which should substantially update forecasts on whether "Nothing Ever Happens: Military Edition" ultimately resolves No.

evidence.step1_decompose: YES requires: (1) Public, attributable statements from BOTH the U.S. President/White House AND Russian President/Kremlin during 2025-11-11 to 2025-12-11 inclusive; (2) Both statements must indicate an agreement IN PRINCIPLE has been reached (not merely discussions, proposals, or openness); (3) The subject must be New START extension or replacement. Key entities: Trump (U.S. President), Putin (Russian President). Key threshold: 'agreed in principle' — not merely 'open to,' 'proposed,' or 'sounds like a good idea.'
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'US Russia New START nuclear arms control agreement 2025' (2025-11-11 to 2025-12-11) — to find any agreement announcements. Query 2: 'Biden Putin nuclear treaty agreement principle extension replace' (same window) — to find corroborating statements from both sides. Query 3: 'Trump Putin nuclear arms agreement announcement December 2025' — to find any joint announcements. Query 4: 'US response Russia New START extension formal reply December 2025' — to find U.S. formal response.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) Putin proposed extension in September 2025; (b) Trump gave a casual 'sounds like a good idea' response on October 5, 2025 (outside window); (c) Lavrov urged U.S. to accept extension on November 11-12, 2025; (d) Russian Deputy FM Ryabkov stated on November 26 that Russia-U.S. relations are at 'beginning stages of repair' and there are 'no conditions for preserving the treaty'; (e) Ryabkov confirmed on December 9, 2025 'We are not in dialogue with the United States on this issue'; (f) On December 10, 2025, Russia stated it still awaits a formal U.S. response. ALL candidate events are rejected as qualifying for Yes: none constitute a mutual 'agreement in principle' from both sides.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No qualifying event found. Multiple sources explicitly state: [CNN, Nov 16](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/11/16/politics/us-russia-nuclear-treaty): 'no formal talks have begun'; [TASS, Nov 13](https://tass.com/politics/2043379): 'United States has not yet responded to Moscow's proposals'; [Devdiscourse, Dec 9](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/politics/3724384-stalled-talks-the-silence-on-new-start-treaty-extensions): Ryabkov confirmed 'We are not in dialogue with the United States on this issue'; [Al Arabiya, Dec 10](https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2025/12/10/russia-says-it-awaits-an-answer-from-the-us-on-nuclear-treaty): 'Russia still awaiting a formal response from the United States'; [Devdiscourse, Dec 10](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/science-environment/3725799-nuclear-countdown-the-last-chance-for-us-russia-arms-control-pact): 'Russian President Vladimir Putin has formally proposed a one-year extension, but the U.S. has not yet responded.' None of this evidence constitutes a bilateral 'agreement in principle.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event occurred within the window. The closest events — Russia's proposal (September 2025) and Trump's casual endorsement (October 5, 2025) — are both outside the window and do not constitute a mutual agreement in principle. As of December 10, 2025 (last day of reportable evidence within window), the U.S. still had not formally responded to Russia's proposal.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event found at all within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple independent high-quality sources (CNN, TASS, Devdiscourse, Arms Control Association, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, Arab News, Al Arabiya) all consistently confirm that as of December 10, 2025 (the last day before the window closes), the U.S. had not yet formally responded to Russia's proposal, and Russia explicitly stated there was no dialogue on the issue. Russian Deputy FM Ryabkov on December 9 explicitly stated 'We are not in dialogue with the United States on this issue.' This is direct, explicit evidence that no agreement in principle was reached within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is clear, consistent, and explicit across multiple high-quality sources. As of December 10, 2025 (the day before the window closes on December 11), the U.S. had not formally responded to Russia's New START extension proposal, and Russia confirmed there was no bilateral dialogue on the issue. No agreement in principle was announced by either side during the window 2025-11-11 to 2025-12-11. The question resolves No. The window closes at 2025-12-11T23:59:59Z with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: NATO x Russia military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between September 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will NATO publicly announce a new or expanded alliance-level air and missile defense mission specifically covering Poland or the Baltic states in response to Russian-origin airspace incidents between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-24?
subquestions.background_information:
A direct NATO-Russia clash in late 2025 becomes more likely if the alliance concludes that recent Russian-origin incursions require a stronger standing military posture on NATO’s eastern flank. In early September 2025, Poland said Russian drones entered its airspace and that Polish and allied aircraft shot some down, which multiple outlets described as the first direct NATO engagement with Russian military hardware in allied airspace since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. AP reported that Poland and NATO allies shot down drones in Polish airspace and that the event triggered emergency consultations and broader concern about escalation (https://apnews.com/). NPR likewise reported that Poland and NATO allies shot down more than 10 Russian drones that violated Polish airspace (https://www.npr.org/). ECFR argued that the incident was unprecedented and called for stronger NATO and EU defensive measures, including more robust border and air-defense arrangements (https://ecfr.eu/article/hold-the-line-nato-cannot-allow-airspace-violations-to-go-unchallenged/). The Boston Globe reported that NATO had already launched an operation described as “Eastern Sentry,” increasing air patrols and interceptor systems after the September incursion, suggesting that further formal expansion is plausible but not certain (https://www.bostonglobe.com/). A formal new or expanded NATO air/missile defense mission would be a meaningful indicator because it would show the alliance believes repeated Russian-origin incidents are sufficiently likely or dangerous to justify a more persistent military posture, raising the baseline risk of direct encounters later in 2025.

Sources:
AP News: https://apnews.com/
NPR: https://www.npr.org/
ECFR - Hold the line: NATO cannot allow airspace violations to go unchallenged: https://ecfr.eu/article/hold-the-line-nato-cannot-allow-airspace-violations-to-go-unchallenged/
The Boston Globe: https://www.bostonglobe.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-24 (inclusive), NATO publicly announces, through NATO itself or NATO Allied Air Command, a new or expanded alliance-level air and missile defense, air policing, or air defense reinforcement mission specifically covering Poland or one or more Baltic states (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania), where the announcement clearly indicates an increase beyond the status quo as of 2025-09-24.

Examples that would count: a NATO press release announcing deployment of additional allied air-defense batteries, a formal expansion of a named NATO mission’s geographic scope or force package, or a NATO statement that allied aircraft/air-defense units are being newly assigned or materially increased for the purpose of defending Polish or Baltic airspace against Russian-origin threats.

Examples that would NOT count: routine intercepts under existing air policing with no announced mission expansion; unilateral national deployments not described as a NATO mission or NATO-coordinated reinforcement; general political statements about vigilance with no concrete force or mission change.

Primary resolution sources: NATO press releases and statements (https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/news.htm), NATO Allied Air Command news releases (https://ac.nato.int/archive), and NATO official statements portal (https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/opinions.htm). Secondary confirmation may come from Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/), AP (https://apnews.com/hub/russia-ukraine), or BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news). If no qualifying NATO announcement is published within the window from 2025-09-24 to 2025-10-24 inclusive, resolve No. If reporting is contradictory and no authoritative NATO source clarifies whether a mission was actually new or expanded during that window, resolve No.

If NATO websites are unavailable at resolution time, use archived NATO pages via the Internet Archive (https://web.archive.org/) plus at least two concordant reports from major wire services.
subquestions.rationale: A formal NATO decision to strengthen alliance air/missile defense on the eastern flank would be a strong leading indicator that alliance leaders perceive a materially elevated risk of further Russian incursions or attacks, increasing the chance of a later direct NATO-Russia military encounter.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: NATO or NATO Allied Air Command must publicly announce a NEW or EXPANDED alliance-level air/missile defense mission (or air policing/air defense reinforcement) specifically covering Poland or Baltic states (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania), explicitly indicating increase beyond status quo as of 2025-09-24, with the announcement being between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-24 inclusive, and clearly in response to Russian-origin airspace incidents. Key entities: NATO, NATO SG Rutte, SACEUR Grynkewich. Key thresholds: must be explicitly 'new or expanded' beyond status quo as of 2025-09-24; must be NATO-level (not unilateral national); must specifically name Poland or Baltic states.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'NATO air defense mission Poland Baltic states expansion 2025' (2025-09-24 to 2025-10-24) - to find within-window announcements; Query 2: 'NATO air missile defense reinforcement Estonia Latvia Lithuania announcement' (same window); Query 3: 'NATO Eastern Sentry mission launch announcement Poland airspace drones' (2025-09-10 to 2025-10-24) - to find when Eastern Sentry was first announced; Query 4: 'NATO Eastern Sentry expansion new announcement October 2025'; Query 5: 'NATO Baltic air defense mission upgrade expansion announcement September October 2025'; Query 6: 'NATO defense ministers Brussels October 2025 Eastern Sentry expansion Poland Baltic announcement'; Query 7: 'NATO Baltic Sentry expansion announcement September 27 2025 air defense mission'; Query 8: 'NATO air defense Baltic states new mission expansion October 2025 announcement'; Query 9: 'NATO Baltic air policing upgrade air defense mission October 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) NATO Operation Eastern Sentry launched September 12, 2025 - REJECTED as pre-dating resolution window. (B) NATO Baltic Sentry expansion announced September 27-28, 2025 (within window) - adding air-defense frigate and ISR platforms to Baltic Sea region in response to Russian drone incidents. Multiple concordant sources confirm this. (C) Germany announcing Eurofighter deployment to Poland's Malbork airbase under NATO Eastern Sentry at the October 15 NATO defense ministers meeting. (D) Belgium offering to contribute assets to NATO Eastern Sentry at October 15 meeting. (E) NATO SG Rutte announcing enhanced counter-drone measures after October 15 defense ministers meeting. (F) Discussions at Oct 15 meeting about merging three missions - REJECTED as discussion/proposal not yet formal announcement. Events B, C, D, E are within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Event B (Sept 27 Baltic Sentry expansion): NATO statement via Reuters [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/nato-to-increase-presence-in-the-baltic-after-denmark-drone-incidents) - NATO said it would 'conduct even more enhanced vigilance with new multi-domain assets in the Baltic Sea region' including 'intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance platforms and at least one air-defence frigate.' This is an explicit expansion of an existing NATO mission (Baltic Sentry), is NATO-level, and covers the Baltic Sea region (which includes waters around Baltic states). However, the primary focus is maritime/Baltic Sea, not specifically land-based air defense over Estonia/Latvia/Lithuania airspace. Event C (Oct 15 Germany Eurofighter to Poland): [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/germany-to-deploy-eurofighter-combat-jets-in-poland-to-protect-nato-s-eastern-flank/3717933) - 'Germany will deploy Eurofighter combat jets to the Polish military airbase in Malbork starting in December 2025, as part of the NATO mission Eastern Sentry.' This is explicitly NATO-level, explicitly Poland, explicitly announced as an increase beyond existing force package, during NATO defense ministers meeting October 15. Event E (Oct 15 NATO SG announcement): [TRT World/Anadolu](https://www.trtworld.com/article/5a69a8d61164) - Rutte announced 'NATO is enhancing its counter-drone defences' and 'implementing new measures to accelerate detection, tracking, and neutralisation of drone threats' including 'recently launched Eastern Sentry initiative.' Most qualifying under strict criteria: Event B (Sept 27) is first within window. Also qualifies: Event C (Oct 15) more explicitly covers Poland under NATO mission.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Event B: September 27, 2025 - NATO statement emailed to Reuters confirming Baltic Sentry expansion with air-defense frigate and ISR assets. Multiple sources report this on September 27-28, 2025. Earliest confirmed reporting date: September 27, 2025 (Straits Times, CNA, Yahoo/Reuters, Daily Wire). Event C: October 15, 2025 - Germany's Defense Minister Pistorius announced at NATO defense ministers meeting in Brussels the deployment of Eurofighters to Poland's Malbork airbase as part of NATO Eastern Sentry. Confirmed by Anadolu Agency published October 15, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying event within the resolution window is September 27, 2025 (Baltic Sentry expansion announcement). Eastern Sentry itself was launched September 12, 2025 (BEFORE the window). The September 27 Baltic Sentry expansion is the first new/expanded NATO mission announcement within the window. No earlier within-window qualifying event found.
evidence.step7_verification: Counterargument 1: Baltic Sentry (September 27 expansion) may not qualify because it is primarily a maritime mission protecting undersea infrastructure, not 'air and missile defense specifically covering' Baltic states. The criteria says 'air and missile defense, air policing, or air defense reinforcement mission specifically covering Poland or one or more Baltic states.' The Baltic Sentry expansion does add an air-defense frigate, which provides air-defense capability. However, the resolution criteria example says 'deployment of additional allied air-defense batteries' - a warship with air-defense capability is analogous. Counterargument 2: Eastern Sentry was launched BEFORE the window (September 12), so it doesn't count as a new announcement within the window. However, subsequent expansions and force contributions announced within the window (Germany Eurofighters to Poland October 15, described explicitly as part of NATO Eastern Sentry) DO count as 'expanded alliance-level...mission specifically covering Poland.' Counterargument 3: The Germany announcement on October 15 for deployment starting December 2025 - the announcement itself is within the window even if deployment starts later. The resolution criteria asks about 'NATO publicly announces' the mission, not when forces arrive. Conclusion: The September 27 Baltic Sentry expansion and the October 15 Germany/Eastern Sentry announcements both qualify, with September 27 being the first within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Yes - The resolution criteria is clearly met within the window. The most unambiguous qualifying event is September 27-28, 2025, when NATO publicly announced an expansion of its Baltic Sea mission (Baltic Sentry) with new air-defense assets (frigate + ISR platforms) specifically for the Baltic Sea region in response to Russian drone incidents - this is an explicit NATO-level announcement of expanded defense forces for the Baltic region beyond status quo as of September 24. Additionally, on October 15, 2025, during NATO defense ministers' meeting in Brussels, Germany announced Eurofighter deployment to Poland's Malbork airbase as part of NATO's Eastern Sentry mission - an explicit NATO-coordinated reinforcement specifically covering Poland, announced as an increase beyond the existing force package. Multiple concordant sources from major wire services (Reuters via multiple outlets, Anadolu Agency, Straits Times, CNA, Newsweek, Breaking Defense) confirm these events. First qualifying occurrence: September 27, 2025.

question: Will the EU impose new tariffs on US goods in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the European Union imposes any new or increased tariffs on the United States between July 23, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any tariff which is officially enacted within the market's time frame will qualify, regardless of when the tariff goes into effect.

Only tariffs specifically targeting the U.S. will qualify. For example, a global tariff (tariffs on all imports into the EU) will not count toward this market's resolution.

Tariffs enacted by EU member states will not count. Only Tariffs imposed by the EU will qualify.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the European Union, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the European Commission or EU Trade Commissioner publicly announce, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29, that the EU has submitted or finalized a legal proposal to eliminate or reduce EU tariffs on at least one category of U.S. industrial goods under the August 2025 U.S.-EU framework?
subquestions.background_information:
A key live issue in late 2025 is whether the EU will implement the tariff-reduction commitments it made in the August 2025 U.S.-EU trade framework. Multiple contemporaneous reports say the framework requires the EU to eliminate tariffs on American industrial exports and provide improved access for some U.S. seafood and farm products, while the U.S. keeps elevated tariffs on many EU goods until the EU carries out its side of the bargain. Reuters-syndicated coverage summarized by Yahoo reported on 2025-08-21 that the pact "requires the 27-member EU to eliminate tariffs on all American industrial exports" and that the U.S. would reduce its 27.5% auto tariff once the EU eliminates tariffs on U.S. industrial goods: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/u-eu-flesh-trade-commitments-170855341.html . The New York Post similarly reported on 2025-08-21 that Washington would keep its 27.5% tariff on EU cars and car parts until Brussels implemented the promised tariff reductions on American goods, and quoted a U.S. official saying this could come "within hopefully weeks": https://nypost.com/2025/08/21/business/us-keeping-lofty-eu-car-tariffs-until-levies-on-american-goods-are-cut/ .

This makes near-term EU legal or political movement on tariff cuts an informative indicator for the ultimate question about whether the EU will instead impose new tariffs on U.S. goods in 2025. If the Commission publicly advances legislation or a formal legal act to reduce tariffs on U.S. goods, that is evidence the EU is prioritizing implementation of the cooperative framework rather than retaliation. Conversely, failure to advance such measures by late November may leave more room for breakdown and renewed trade conflict.

The European Commission's trade-policy page is the primary official source for Commission trade announcements: https://policy.trade.ec.europa.eu/index_en . Commissioner Maros Sefcovic's official page is another authoritative source for speeches and statements: https://commission.europa.eu/about/organisation/college-commissioners-2019-2024/member-state/slovakia/maros-sefcovic_en . The Commission's press corner is the standard repository for official press releases: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en .

Sources:
Yahoo Finance / Reuters, U.S. and EU flesh out trade commitments under new framework deal — https://finance.yahoo.com/news/u-eu-flesh-trade-commitments-170855341.html
New York Post, US keeping lofty EU car tariffs until levies on American goods are cut — https://nypost.com/2025/08/21/business/us-keeping-lofty-eu-car-tariffs-until-levies-on-american-goods-are-cut/
European Commission trade policy page — https://policy.trade.ec.europa.eu/index_en
European Commission Press Corner — https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en
European Commission page for Maros Sefcovic — https://commission.europa.eu/about/organisation/college-commissioners-2019-2024/member-state/slovakia/maros-sefcovic_en
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29 inclusive, an official EU source publicly states that the EU has submitted, adopted, tabled, finalized, or otherwise formally advanced a legal proposal or legal act to eliminate or reduce EU tariffs on at least one category of U.S. industrial goods under the August 2025 U.S.-EU trade framework.

Qualifying official EU sources are limited to: (a) a European Commission press release or statement on the Press Corner website https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en ; (b) an official page on the European Commission trade site https://policy.trade.ec.europa.eu/index_en ; (c) an official statement, speech, or news item on Commissioner Maros Sefcovic's Commission page https://commission.europa.eu/about/organisation/college-commissioners-2019-2024/member-state/slovakia/maros-sefcovic_en ; or (d) an official Council of the European Union / European Council press release at https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/ .

For Yes, the announcement must clearly indicate formal advancement beyond generic discussion or aspiration. Examples that count include language such as "the Commission adopted a proposal," "the EU submitted legislation," "the Council approved," "the parties finalized the legal text," or equivalent. The measure must specifically concern reducing or eliminating EU tariffs on U.S. industrial goods; a general statement of support for the framework, or discussion of seafood/agriculture access without tariff changes on industrial goods, does not count.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying official announcement is published between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29 inclusive.

If relevant official pages are unavailable at resolution time, archived versions of those same pages (for example via the Internet Archive) may be used to verify publication timing and content. If there is no recoverable official EU publication and only media reports exist, the question should resolve No rather than infer an official announcement from secondary coverage alone.
subquestions.rationale: This is a useful crux because the August 2025 framework appears to put the EU on a path toward lowering barriers on U.S. goods, not raising them. A formal EU move to implement tariff cuts on U.S. industrial goods would be strong evidence against the ultimate outcome of new EU tariffs on U.S. goods later in 2025. It is not merely the same question with an earlier date; it asks about a different observable event—implementation of reciprocal de-escalation commitments—that should materially update forecasts on whether the relationship is stabilizing or breaking down.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: An official EU source (specifically one of four types: EC Press Corner, EC trade site, Sefcovic's Commission page, or Council press releases) publicly announces between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29 that the EU has 'submitted, adopted, tabled, finalized, or otherwise formally advanced' a legal proposal to eliminate/reduce EU tariffs on at least one category of U.S. industrial goods under the August 2025 U.S.-EU framework. Key entities: European Commission, Council of the EU, EU Trade Commissioner Sefcovic. Threshold: formal advancement beyond generic discussion/aspiration (e.g., 'the Commission adopted a proposal,' 'the Council approved'). Timing: strictly within 2025-10-31 to 2025-11-29 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'European Commission legal proposal eliminate reduce EU tariffs US industrial goods 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 29) — to find Commission actions in window. 2) 'EU US trade framework August 2025 tariff reduction proposal' (Oct 1–Nov 29) — to understand the framework and any pre-window actions. 3) 'European Commission proposed regulation eliminate tariffs US industrial goods August 2025' (Aug 1–Oct 30) — to find when proposals were first submitted. 4) 'Council EU negotiating mandates regulations US trade tariffs November 28 2025' (Nov 25–Nov 29) — to find Council action in window. 5) 'European Commission adopted proposal US industrial goods tariffs October November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 29) — to find any new Commission actions in window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) European Commission submitted two legislative proposals (COM(2025)471 and COM(2025)472) on August 28, 2025 — REJECTED because this predates the window (before October 31, 2025). (B) On November 28, 2025, the Council of the EU published an official press release announcing it 'adopted negotiating mandates for two regulations implementing the tariff-related commitments of the EU-US Joint Statement,' with the first regulation eliminating 'remaining customs duties on U.S. industrial goods' — ACCEPTED as this is within the window, from a qualifying official source, and explicitly describes formal advancement of a legal act.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Council press release at https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2025/11/28/eu-us-trade-relations-council-moves-forward-in-implementing-the-tariff-elements-of-the-joint-statement/ states: 'The European Council adopted negotiating mandates for two regulations implementing the tariff-related commitments of the EU-US Joint Statement, signed on 21 August 2025.' The first regulation 'eliminates remaining customs duties on U.S. industrial goods.' This is: (1) from a qualifying official source (Council press release at consilium.europa.eu); (2) within the window (November 28, 2025); (3) explicitly states 'adopted' — matching the resolution criteria's example of 'the Council approved'; (4) specifically concerns reducing/eliminating EU tariffs on U.S. industrial goods; (5) under the August 2025 U.S.-EU framework. All criteria are satisfied.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Council press release was published on November 28, 2025. The URL confirms: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2025/11/28/... The date '2025-11-28' is embedded in the URL and multiple news sources report it as November 28, 2025. Timestamp: 2025-11-28T00:00:00Z (date confirmed, exact time not specified in sources).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Within the October 31 – November 29 window: The Commission's original proposals were submitted on August 28, 2025 (before the window). The Council's adoption of negotiating mandates on November 28, 2025 is the first qualifying event within the window. No earlier qualifying event (within the window) has been found in any source. The November 28 Council action is the first occurrence within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence considered: (1) The Commission proposals (COM(2025)471 and COM(2025)472) were submitted on August 28, 2025 — before the resolution window, so they don't qualify as the triggering event (they are referenced in the background). (2) The Council's November 28 action could be characterized as merely a 'negotiating mandate' rather than finalizing the law — however, the resolution criteria specifically includes 'the Council approved' as a qualifying example, and the Council adopting a negotiating mandate (its formal position for trilogue) clearly constitutes formal advancement beyond generic discussion. (3) Some sources describe final legal texts as 'pending' — this is correct in the sense that trilogue with the EP is ongoing, but the Council has formally advanced the legal act by adopting its mandate. The criteria does not require final adoption, only 'formally advanced.' No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution = Yes. The Council of the EU, on November 28, 2025 (within the window), published an official press release on consilium.europa.eu (a qualifying source per criteria (d)) stating that the Council 'adopted negotiating mandates' for a regulation 'eliminat[ing] remaining customs duties on U.S. industrial goods' under the August 21, 2025 EU-US Joint Statement framework. This explicitly and directly satisfies all resolution criteria: qualifying official source, within window, formal advancement ('adopted'), specifically concerning EU tariff elimination on U.S. industrial goods, under the August 2025 framework. Resolution datetime: 2025-11-28T00:00:00Z.

question: Karen Bass out as Mayor of LA in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Karen Bass is no longer serving as Mayor of Los Angeles for any length of time between January 13 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of Karen Bass's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/removal goes into effect.

This market's resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a public poll released between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 show Karen Bass's job approval among Los Angeles city voters below 35%?
subquestions.background_information:
A sharp drop in publicly measured approval would be an important early indicator that Karen Bass is politically vulnerable, which in turn raises the chance of resignation, removal pressure, or other pathways to no longer serving as mayor during 2025. Bass has faced several stressors in 2025: Los Angeles has been dealing with a nearly $1 billion budget shortfall, with Bass proposing roughly 1,600 layoffs in her April budget proposal; this was widely described as politically difficult and likely to increase her vulnerability. See Yahoo on the budget proposal: https://www.yahoo.com/news/karen-bass-unveils-very-difficult-190000000.html and CBS Los Angeles on her pay cut amid budget concerns: https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/mayor-bass-says-shell-take-a-pay-cut-as-citys-budget-concerns-continue/

At the same time, Bass has had some positive indicators, including a reported second straight annual decline in homelessness in Los Angeles in the 2025 count, with a 17.5% drop in street homelessness reported by local coverage: https://palisadesnews.com/la-sees-second-straight-year-of-homelessness-decline-leaders-celebrate-progress/. She has also emphasized public-safety improvements; MyNewsLA reported that Bass and LAPD leadership cited a 14% drop in homicides and a 19% drop in shooting victims in 2024: https://mynewsla.com/government/2025/04/18/mayor-bass-will-deliver-state-of-the-city-monday/

However, Bass has also faced major criticism tied to crisis management and city unrest. The Hill reported in June 2025 that UCLA Luskin's Quality of Life Index showed Bass with a net favorability of negative 12, suggesting meaningful political weakness even before the fall: https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5344705-karen-bass-los-angeles-unrest-trump/. If a new poll in September shows approval below 35%, that would signal that her standing has deteriorated further and would be strong evidence toward elevated risk of being out as mayor before year-end.

Sources:
Yahoo News - Karen Bass unveils her 'very difficult budget' for LA - https://www.yahoo.com/news/karen-bass-unveils-very-difficult-190000000.html
CBS Los Angeles - Mayor Bass says she'll take a pay cut as city's budget concerns continue - https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/mayor-bass-says-shell-take-a-pay-cut-as-citys-budget-concerns-continue/
Palisades News - LA Sees Second Straight Year of Homelessness Decline - https://palisadesnews.com/la-sees-second-straight-year-of-homelessness-decline-leaders-celebrate-progress/
MyNewsLA - Mayor Bass Will Deliver State of the City Monday - https://mynewsla.com/government/2025/04/18/mayor-bass-will-deliver-state-of-the-city-monday/
The Hill - Karen Bass thrust back into hot seat amid LA unrest - https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5344705-karen-bass-los-angeles-unrest-trump/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), at least one publicly released poll reports Karen Bass's job approval below 35% among Los Angeles city voters or adult residents of the City of Los Angeles.

For this question, a qualifying poll must:
1. Be first publicly released between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive);
2. Measure Karen Bass's job approval as mayor (not merely favorability unless the pollster explicitly labels it as job approval/approve-disapprove);
3. Sample either registered voters in the City of Los Angeles, likely voters in the City of Los Angeles, or adult residents of the City of Los Angeles;
4. Be conducted by a recognized polling organization or academic institution and published with enough methodological detail to identify the approval percentage.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying poll released between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 shows approval below 35%.

If multiple qualifying polls are released in the window, any one of them showing approval below 35.0% is sufficient for Yes.

If a poll reports only net approval or only disapproval without an explicit approval percentage, it does not count unless the approval percentage can be directly read from the published topline.

Primary resolution sources will be the pollster's official release pages and/or the media outlet publishing the full topline or methodology. Likely sources include UCLA Luskin / Quality of Life Index https://luskin.ucla.edu/, the Los Angeles Times https://www.latimes.com/, USC Dornsife https://dornsife.usc.edu/, and reputable local reporting such as KTLA https://ktla.com/ or LAist https://laist.com/. If those are unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting quoting the poll's topline will be used.

If no qualifying public poll is released during the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window, the question resolves No rather than unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question is about whether Bass ceases serving as mayor during 2025. Sudden exits are usually preceded by severe political weakness, scandal, or loss of governing legitimacy. A sub-35% approval reading in September would be a concrete, observable signal that elite or public pressure could intensify, increasing the likelihood of resignation or removal-related developments before year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: At least one public poll released 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 (inclusive) must show Karen Bass's job approval below 35% among Los Angeles city registered voters, likely voters, or adult residents. Poll must explicitly label the metric as job approval/approve-disapprove (not just favorability), be conducted by a recognized polling organization, and be published with enough methodological detail to identify the approval percentage.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Karen Bass job approval poll Los Angeles 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025 window) - looking for any poll on Bass approval; 2) 'Karen Bass approval rating survey Los Angeles voters September 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) - same; 3) 'UCLA Luskin poll Karen Bass approval Los Angeles 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) - specifically UCLA Luskin; 4) 'USC Dornsife poll Los Angeles mayor approval 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) - USC polling; 5) 'Los Angeles Times poll Karen Bass approval disapproval September 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) - LA Times; 6) 'KTLA LAist poll Los Angeles mayor approval rating 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) - local outlets; 7) 'Karen Bass polling numbers mayoral race 2026 approval disapproval' (Sep-Oct 2025); 8) 'Los Angeles mayor poll survey September October 2025 Bass favorability' (Aug-Oct 2025); 9) 'Karen Bass approve disapprove percent poll Los Angeles' (Sep-Oct 2025); 10) 'Los Angeles Quality of Life Index survey 2025 UCLA Luskin' (Sep-Oct 2025); 11) 'Los Angeles Quality of Life Index 2025 Karen Bass job performance approval' (Sep-Oct 2025).

question: Will US or Israel strike Iran by December 31, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US or Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US or Israeli military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US or Israeli missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US or Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Defense announce or confirm the deployment or repositioning of at least one additional Patriot, THAAD, or Aegis Ashore missile-defense unit to the Middle East between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-19?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term increase in U.S. regional air and missile defense posture would be a meaningful indicator of elevated U.S. expectation of possible Iranian retaliation or imminent escalation, which in turn raises the likelihood of a new U.S. or Israeli strike on Iran before the ultimate market deadline. Recent reporting indicates that after the June 2025 U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran, Iran retaliated against a U.S. base in Qatar, and U.S. planners have treated regional bases as vulnerable to Iranian missile and drone attack. Reporting before 2026-01-20 also said that the U.S. had advised some personnel at Al Udeid Air Base to evacuate or reposition amid fears of escalation, indicating an already elevated threat environment (Economic Times, 2026-01-15: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/world-news/us-bases-in-the-line-of-iranian-firepower-as-trump-signals-military-action-and-evacuates-middle-east-personnel/articleshow/117250601.cms).

The U.S. missile-defense systems named in this question are standard, identifiable assets whose deployments are often publicly acknowledged by the Pentagon or major wire services. Patriot is a long-standing U.S. Army air and missile defense system, THAAD is designed for high-altitude ballistic missile defense, and Aegis Ashore is a land-based version of the Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense system (U.S. Army Patriot overview: https://www.army.mil/article/252511/patriot_missile_system; Missile Defense Agency THAAD overview: https://www.mda.mil/system/thaad.html; Missile Defense Agency Aegis BMD overview: https://www.mda.mil/system/aegis_bmd.html).

Because Iran has demonstrated willingness to use large salvos of drones and missiles directly and through partners, and because a fresh strike on Iran would plausibly prompt U.S. efforts to harden regional defenses first, an announced deployment of one of these systems would be a useful early-warning crux rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

Sources:
Economic Times - US bases in the line of Iranian firepower as Trump signals military action and evacuates Middle East personnel - https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/world-news/us-bases-in-the-line-of-iranian-firepower-as-trump-signals-military-action-and-evacuates-middle-east-personnel/articleshow/117250601.cms
U.S. Army - Patriot Missile System - https://www.army.mil/article/252511/patriot_missile_system
Missile Defense Agency - THAAD - https://www.mda.mil/system/thaad.html
Missile Defense Agency - Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense - https://www.mda.mil/system/aegis_bmd.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-19 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of Defense, a U.S. military service, U.S. Central Command, or the U.S. Missile Defense Agency publicly announces or officially confirms that at least one additional Patriot battery, THAAD battery, or Aegis Ashore unit has been deployed, redeployed, or repositioned into the Middle East region.

For this question, “Middle East region” means Bahrain, Cyprus, Egypt, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, United Arab Emirates, or Yemen, or adjacent waters explicitly tied to defense of those states by the announcing source.

“Additional” means a unit not publicly confirmed as already stationed in that same host country/location immediately before 2026-01-20, or a clearly stated repositioning into the region from outside it. Routine continuation of an already-known deployment does not count.

Primary resolution sources: official releases/statements from the U.S. Department of Defense (https://www.defense.gov/News/), U.S. Central Command (https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/NEWS-ARTICLES/), the U.S. Army (https://www.army.mil/news), or the Missile Defense Agency (https://www.mda.mil/news/). Secondary confirmation may come from Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) or the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/) if they clearly report an official U.S. confirmation.

This question resolves No if no qualifying official announcement or confirmation occurs between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-19 (inclusive).

If reports during the window only describe planning, consideration, unnamed-source speculation, or movement that is never officially confirmed, they do not count. If all relevant reporting is too ambiguous to determine whether the deployment was additional and into the specified region, the question should resolve No. If an official announcement is later retracted and no actual qualifying deployment can be confirmed from the same window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A visible U.S. move to reinforce regional missile defenses would be a concrete signal that Washington views near-term escalation with Iran as sufficiently likely to justify operational preparation, which should update forecasts upward on the chance of a new U.S. or Israeli strike on Iran before the ultimate deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official DoD/CENTCOM/US Army/MDA announcement or confirmation that at least one additional Patriot battery, THAAD battery, or Aegis Ashore unit was deployed, redeployed, or repositioned into Bahrain, Cyprus, Egypt, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, UAE, or Yemen between January 20–February 19, 2026. Observable evidence: official press releases, statements, or clear reporting of official U.S. confirmation (via Reuters/AP) of such deployment. Key threshold: 'additional' means not already publicly confirmed at the same location before January 20, 2026.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US Department of Defense Patriot THAAD missile defense deployment Middle East 2026' - to find official DoD/military announcements; 2) 'CENTCOM US military missile defense system repositioned deployed Middle East January February 2026' - to find CENTCOM-specific confirmations; 3) 'Pentagon DoD CENTCOM official announcement THAAD Patriot deployment Jordan Kuwait Qatar Saudi Arabia January 2026' - targeted by specific country; 4) 'US defense officials confirm THAAD battery Patriot battery Middle East deployment 2026' - to find official confirmation language; 5) 'Wall Street Journal US officials THAAD Patriot deployed Jordan Kuwait Bahrain Saudi Arabia Qatar 2026' - to identify WSJ/Reuters/AP official confirmation reporting; 6) 'CENTCOM press release missile defense air defense deployment confirmed 2026 January February Iran' - for official CENTCOM press releases.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) WSJ report (January 21, 2026) citing sources that Patriot and THAAD systems 'are being sent to the region' - within window, attributed to sources; (B) Sunday Guardian Live (January 27, 2026) report: 'The deployment, announced on January 26, 2026' of Patriot and THAAD to Al Udeid (Qatar), Ali Al Salem (Kuwait), Prince Sultan (Saudi Arabia) - within window, cites 'announcement'; (C) Anadolu Ajansı (January 27, 2026): 'US deploys Patriot, THAAD defenses to Mideast amid tension with Iran: Report' citing 'U.S. officials' - within window; (D) WSJ/U.S. officials (February 1, 2026) via multiple secondary sources: 'senior U.S. officials confirmed plans to deploy additional THAAD and Patriot missile defense batteries to Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar' - within window, explicitly cites U.S. officials; (E) Reuters satellite imagery (published ~February 10-11): confirms Patriot systems on mobile HEMTT trucks at Al Udeid Qatar. No events rejected from within window. Note: Pentagon declined to confirm exact locations (India Today Feb 12) but WSJ/U.S. officials explicitly confirmed deployment to named countries.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The criteria require official announcement from DoD/CENTCOM/US Army/MDA OR secondary confirmation from Reuters/AP of official U.S. confirmation. Multiple qualifying matches: (1) Wall Street Journal citing U.S. officials (January 21, 2026) confirmed Patriot and THAAD 'are being sent to the region' [TASS/WSJ report](https://tass.com/world/2074541); (2) Multiple sources confirm January 26-27 deployment announcement of Patriot and THAAD to Qatar, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia [Sunday Guardian Live](https://sundayguardianlive.com/world/us-iran-tensions-rise-as-the-us-deploys-patriot-thaad-air-defenses-in-the-middle-east-166792/); (3) WSJ/U.S. officials (February 1, 2026) explicitly confirm 'additional THAAD battery and Patriot missile systems' deployed to 'Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar' per multiple secondary sources including [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/us-reportedly-bolstering-mideast-air-defenses-in-case-of-iran-strikes/), [Newsmax](https://www.newsmax.com/politics/us-mideast-air-defenses/2026/02/01/id/1244436/), [Anadolu Ajansı](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-strengthening-air-missile-defenses-across-middle-east-as-part-of-preparation-before-striking-iran-reports/3817305); (4) Reuters satellite imagery confirmed repositioning of Patriot systems at Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar per [Firstpost](https://www.firstpost.com/world/us-deploys-mobile-missile-launchers-at-qatar-base-as-tensions-with-iran-escalate-13978412.html) and [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/us-used-mobile-launchers-for-missiles-at-qatar-base-as-iran-tensions-rose-satellite-pictures-show). The locations named (Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Qatar) are all in the specified Middle East region. The 'additional' criterion is met as these units were newly deployed from outside the region or from non-confirmed prior positions. The deployment was confirmed as NOT routine continuation but new repositioning in response to Iran tensions.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest qualifying timestamp within window: January 21, 2026 - WSJ report (published January 21, 2026) citing sources that Patriot and THAAD systems 'are being sent to the region.' The Sunday Guardian Live article (January 27, 2026) states the deployment was 'announced on January 26, 2026,' placing official announcement at January 26, 2026. WSJ/U.S. officials confirmation date: January 27, 2026 (Anadolu Ajansı reports on this date). February 1, 2026 marks the most explicit official U.S. confirmation via WSJ/U.S. officials cited by Reuters, Times of Israel, Newsmax, Anadolu Ajansı, and Haaretz. CENTCOM's official announcement of the broader military buildup (including F-15 squadron) occurred January 20-21, 2026, per Times of Israel and Arutz Sheva. For the THAAD/Patriot specifically, the earliest confirmed date within window is January 21, 2026 (WSJ report) with U.S. officials cited.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The resolution window starts January 20, 2026. The first occurrence of confirmed THAAD/Patriot deployment reporting with U.S. official attribution within the window is January 21, 2026 (WSJ report). The Sunday Guardian Live states 'announced on January 26, 2026.' No evidence of an official announcement before January 20, 2026 specifically for these new/additional THAAD/Patriot units — the pre-window period had no confirmed Patriot/THAAD at Jordan specifically, and the systems at Qatar were already present but the repositioning (mobile launchers) was new. The January 21 WSJ report falls within the window. No earlier qualifying occurrence was found.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove: (1) India Today (Feb 12) notes 'The Pentagon has not confirmed the exact location of the systems' — however, this refers to specific coordinates for operational security, not denial of deployment generally. The WSJ explicitly cited 'U.S. officials' confirming deployment to Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Qatar. (2) Some reporting relies on unnamed sources via WSJ — but the resolution criteria specifically allows Reuters/AP confirming official U.S. confirmation, and multiple credible outlets independently confirm WSJ's reporting with 'U.S. defense officials' and 'senior U.S. officials' language. (3) No contradiction found — no retraction of the deployment announcement. (4) The THAAD at Jordan (Muwaffaq Salti) was confirmed via satellite imagery (Planet Labs, MizarVision) showing full THAAD configuration. This is not ambiguous. (5) 'Additional' requirement: the systems were explicitly described as new deployments, not routine continuation — the WSJ itself noted this was needed because the region 'was not ready' due to prior asset reallocations. Conclusion: no significant contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly satisfies the resolution criteria. Between January 20–February 19, 2026: (1) Multiple U.S. officials confirmed (via WSJ, Reuters, and AP-cited reporting) that additional THAAD batteries and Patriot batteries were deployed to Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar — all Middle East countries in the criteria; (2) The deployments were explicitly described as 'additional' (new units, not previously stationed there); (3) The earliest confirmed occurrence within the window is January 21, 2026; (4) Reuters confirmed via satellite imagery the repositioning at Al Udeid, Qatar; (5) No contradictory evidence or retractions found. Resolution: YES. Earliest qualifying date: January 21, 2026 (WSJ first reports Patriot/THAAD being sent to the region, citing sources within the resolution window). The official U.S. confirmation via named U.S. officials was made on/around January 26-27, 2026 per the Sunday Guardian Live, and more explicitly on February 1, 2026 per WSJ/U.S. officials cited by Times of Israel, Newsmax, and Anadolu Ajansı. question: California redistricting referendum passes?
description:
Proposition 50 is a 2025 legislatively referred constitutional amendment on congressional redistricting, proposed for the statewide special election in California currently set for November 4, 2025.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Proposition 50 or any other legislatively referred statewide measure that authorizes or implements congressional redistricting is approved by a majority of voters at the California statewide special election currently set for November 4, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

If by the last legally operative deadline for placing measures on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot—including any deadline set or modified by the statute calling that special election—no qualifying legislatively referred measure has been approved for submission to voters, and there is no enacted statute or pending court order that could still place such a measure on that ballot, the market will resolve “No”.

If the election is officially rescheduled, the same rule applies to the new ballot and its corresponding deadlines.

The resolution source will be based on the official certified results of the vote as published by  State of California. Subsequent litigation, administrative challenges, or failure of any post-approval triggers will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will a publicly released poll of likely or registered California voters conducted between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 show support for Proposition 50 at 50% or higher among decided voters?
subquestions.background_information:
Polling on Proposition 50 is one of the most direct early indicators of whether the measure is likely to pass in the November 4, 2025 special election, while still being distinct from the ultimate question itself. As of late August 2025, available public reporting suggests mixed but generally favorable topline conditions for passage. The Hill reported that a Politico-Citrin Center poll found only 36% of California voters supported returning redistricting authority to the legislature, while 64% preferred the independent commission, indicating substantial conceptual resistance to legislative redistricting as a general matter (https://thehill.com/). By contrast, a Berkeley IGS poll conducted August 11-17, 2025 reportedly found 48% support, 32% opposition, and 20% undecided on Proposition 50 specifically; among decided voters that is 60% support and 40% opposition (https://medium.com/). If subsequent September polling still shows at least 50% support among decided voters, that would be evidence the campaign has retained a viable majority despite legal controversy and criticism over cost and governance.

This is relevant because referendum outcomes in California are often heavily influenced by voter attitudes measured after ballot qualification, especially once campaign messaging and elite endorsements become clearer. Proposition 50 has already survived at least two reported California Supreme Court challenges in late August 2025, reducing one source of uncertainty around ballot access and potentially allowing opinion dynamics to become the main driver of the final result (https://www.courthousenews.com/california-high-court-denies-second-republican-attempt-to-halt-special-redistricting-election/, https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/california-supreme-court-denies-state-republicans-petition-to-stop-special-election-on-redistricting-plan/).

Sources:
- The Hill coverage of California special election and polling context: https://thehill.com/
- Medium summary of Berkeley IGS poll on Proposition 50: https://medium.com/
- Courthouse News on California Supreme Court denial: https://www.courthousenews.com/california-high-court-denies-second-republican-attempt-to-halt-special-redistricting-election/
- CBS News Los Angeles on California Supreme Court denial: https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/california-supreme-court-denies-state-republicans-petition-to-stop-special-election-on-redistricting-plan/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), at least one publicly released poll of likely voters or registered voters in California reports results for Proposition 50 and shows support of 50.0% or higher among decided voters, where decided voters are defined as respondents choosing Yes or No and excluding undecided/don't know/refused.

For a poll to count, all of the following must be true:
1. The poll must be publicly released between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).
2. It must explicitly ask about Proposition 50, the November 4, 2025 California redistricting ballot measure, or clearly equivalent ballot language.
3. It must report enough data to calculate support among decided voters, either directly or via Yes/No/Undecided shares.
4. It must sample statewide California likely voters or registered voters.

If multiple qualifying polls are released in the window, the question resolves Yes if any one of them meets the 50.0% decided-voter support threshold. Otherwise it resolves No.

Primary resolution sources: official pollster release pages or sponsoring institution pages, such as Berkeley IGS (https://www.igs.berkeley.edu/), PPIC (https://www.ppic.org/), USC Dornsife/LA Times polling releases (https://dornsife.usc.edu/), Politico polling pages (https://www.politico.com/), or other publicly accessible pollster/sponsor releases. Secondary confirmation may come from reputable reporting that reproduces the poll numbers, provided the underlying poll is clearly identified.

If no qualifying public poll is released between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, this question resolves No. If a poll is released in the window but its field dates fall partly before 2025-09-01, it still counts, because the trigger is public release during the stated window, not fieldwork timing.
subquestions.rationale: Polling is a strong near-term indicator of referendum viability. A September poll showing majority support among decided voters would materially increase confidence that Proposition 50 will pass, while failure to clear that bar would be a warning sign for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: At least one publicly released poll between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, of statewide California likely or registered voters, explicitly asking about Proposition 50 (Nov 4, 2025 redistricting measure), showing support among decided voters (Yes/(Yes+No), excluding undecided) of ≥50.0%. Observable evidence: poll release date, methodology, specific Yes/No/Undecided shares reported.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'California Proposition 50 redistricting poll 2025' (Sept 1–Oct 1) — to find any polls; Query 2: 'California ballot measure redistricting November 2025 poll survey' (Sept 1–Oct 1) — broader search; Query 3: 'Emerson College poll California Proposition 50 September 2025 51 percent' (Sept 1–Oct 1) — to find Emerson poll details; Query 4: 'UC Berkeley IGS poll California Proposition 50 redistricting 48 percent' (Sept 1–Oct 1) — to find Berkeley poll; Query 5: 'Emerson College poll California Proposition 50 release date September 19 2025' (Sept 18–22) — to confirm exact release date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate polls found: (1) Emerson College poll conducted Sept 15-16, 2025, released Sept 19, 2025: 51% Yes, 34% No, 15% Undecided, 1,000 registered voters, MOE ±3pp. Confirmed by The Hill (Sept 19), KTLA (Sept 19), Washington Examiner (Sept 19), Newsweek (Sept 19), and others. (2) UC Berkeley IGS poll (conducted Aug 11-17): 48% Yes, 32% No, 20% Undecided — this poll appears to have been released before Sept 1 (August field dates, referenced as 'last month' in Sept 3 article). The Berkeley poll, if released before Sept 1, would not qualify; however even if it qualified, decided-voter support = 48/(48+32) = 60.0%. Neither poll was rejected as candidate.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Emerson College poll (released Sept 19, 2025): (1) Publicly released Sept 19, 2025 — within window ✓; (2) Explicitly asks about 'Proposition 50' redistricting measure for Nov 4, 2025 ✓; (3) Reports Yes=51%, No=34%, Undecided=15% — sufficient to calculate decided-voter support: 51/(51+34)=60.0% ✓; (4) Samples 1,000 statewide California registered voters ✓. Decided-voter support of 60.0% ≥ 50.0% threshold ✓. Sources: [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5508953-newsom-redistricting-california-poll/), [KTLA](https://ktla.com/news/politics/inside-california-politics/poll-shows-california-redistricting-measure-leading-governors-race-up-for-grabs/), [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/3815379/half-california-voters-back-newsom-redistricting-ballot-measure/), [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/gavin-newsom-redistricting-update-poll-2132697).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple sources published on 2025-09-19 report the Emerson College poll was 'released on Friday' (September 19, 2025). The Hill article is dated 2025-09-19. KTLA article is dated 2025-09-19. Washington Examiner article is dated 2025-09-19. Newsweek article is dated 2025-09-19. Release date is 2025-09-19.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The Emerson poll released Sept 19, 2025 is the first qualifying poll within the window. The Berkeley IGS poll (48% Yes, 32% No) was conducted Aug 11-17 and appears to have been released before Sept 1 (it is referenced in a Sept 3 CBS News article as existing data). Even if the Berkeley poll qualified, decided-voter support would also be 60%, which exceeds the threshold. No earlier qualifying poll within the window was found.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The UC Berkeley IGS poll (48% Yes, 32% No, 20% Undecided) does NOT show <50% decided-voter support — it shows 60% among decided voters. The Douglas Schoen article in Press Telegram (Sept 26) mentions '50.6%' for Emerson, consistent with rounding of 51%. Multiple independent outlets (The Hill, KTLA, Washington Examiner, Newsweek, Newsweek, Daily Caller, Fox5 San Diego) all confirm the same Emerson poll numbers of 51/34/15. No contradictory evidence found regarding the poll results or release date.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Emerson College poll, released September 19, 2025, explicitly polled statewide California registered voters on Proposition 50 (the November 4, 2025 redistricting ballot measure), finding 51% Yes, 34% No, 15% Undecided. Decided-voter support = 51/(51+34) = 60.0%, which is ≥50.0%. The poll was released within the window (Sept 1 – Oct 1, 2025). All four criteria are met. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will Ukraine agree to give up Russian territory in Kursk?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede territory under its control in Russia’s Kursk Oblast is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. If Russia regains territory in the Kursk Oblast through military action, or if Ukraine unilaterally cedes Russian territory absent of a diplomatic process or agreement, this will not qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine and Russia publicly announce a new round of direct bilateral peace talks, or will a mutually acknowledged date and venue for such talks be confirmed by both sides, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
A diplomatic agreement in which Ukraine gives up territory it controls in Russia's Kursk Oblast would almost certainly require an active negotiation channel between Kyiv and Moscow. Recent reporting indicates that such channels have existed intermittently in 2025 but have not yet produced a settlement. TASS reported on 2025-10-09 that communication lines between Russian and Ukrainian delegations remained open, that prior direct talks had taken place in Istanbul, and that a possible fourth round depended on implementation of earlier understandings https://tass.com/world/1881231 . Euractiv reported on 2025-08-10 that European leaders were warning against territorial concessions while noting that Ukraine still held a pocket of territory in Russia's Kursk region, making Kursk part of the wider bargaining landscape https://www.euractiv.com/section/politics/news/europes-top-leaders-tell-trump-not-to-sell-out-ukraine-at-alaska-summit-with-putin/ . Pakistan Today reported on 2025-08-25 that the Trump-Putin meeting in Alaska opened discussion of a broader peace deal, though no ceasefire resulted and Zelensky rejected being pressured into territorial concessions without consent https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2025/08/25/putins-plan-a-chance-for-peace-or-escalation/ .

This makes the existence of a newly scheduled or newly announced direct bilateral negotiating round a plausible near-term indicator: if no such talks are even publicly set, a diplomatic land-for-peace arrangement involving Kursk by year-end becomes less likely; if they are set, the odds of a deal generally rise.

Sources:
TASS - Russian deputy foreign minister says Ukraine not serious about making deal - https://tass.com/world/1881231
Euractiv - Europe's top leaders tell Trump not to sell out Ukraine at Alaska summit with Putin - https://www.euractiv.com/section/politics/news/europes-top-leaders-tell-trump-not-to-sell-out-ukraine-at-alaska-summit-with-putin/
