subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, either: (a) an official Ukrainian government source and an official Russian government source each publicly state that a new round of direct bilateral peace/settlement negotiations between Ukraine and the Russian Federation will occur, with a stated or clearly implied shared upcoming meeting; or (b) there is an official public announcement by one side of a specific date and venue for such direct bilateral talks and no public denial from the other side within 72 hours, plus at least two credible international news outlets report that both sides have agreed to the meeting.

For clarity, qualifying talks must be direct Ukraine-Russia talks on war settlement, ceasefire, peace, territorial, political, military, or humanitarian issues. Routine prisoner-exchange coordination alone does not count unless it is explicitly described by both sides or by consensus reporting as a new round of broader bilateral negotiations. Talks mediated by a third party still count if they are clearly a direct bilateral negotiating round between Ukraine and Russia.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement or mutually acknowledged scheduling occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive.

Primary sources for resolution: official statements from the President of Ukraine, Ukraine's Foreign Ministry, the Kremlin, or Russia's Foreign Ministry; and reporting from Reuters and AP. Useful official sites include https://www.president.gov.ua/en , https://mfa.gov.ua/en , http://en.kremlin.ru/ , and https://mid.ru/en/ . Preferred news wires are Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ and AP https://apnews.com/ .

Fallback criteria: if official sites are unavailable or ambiguous, resolution should rely on a consensus of at least two major international outlets with strong sourcing, prioritizing Reuters and AP, and secondarily BBC https://www.bbc.com/news or Financial Times https://www.ft.com/ . If reports conflict and there is no clear mutual acknowledgment by 2025-11-30, resolve No. If an announcement is made for talks but is explicitly postponed beyond 2025-11-30 before they are mutually acknowledged as scheduled, that does not qualify for Yes.
subquestions.rationale: A Kursk-for-peace concession would likely emerge only through an active bilateral diplomatic track. Public confirmation that a new direct negotiation round is scheduled is an early indicator that the parties are seriously exploring a deal structure in which territorial tradeoffs, including Ukrainian-held territory in Kursk, could be discussed.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Both Ukraine and Russia official sources (President, Foreign Ministry) publicly state a new round of direct bilateral peace/settlement negotiations will occur with a stated or clearly implied shared upcoming meeting; OR one side officially announces specific date and venue with no denial from the other within 72 hours plus at least two credible international outlets report both sides agreed. Key constraint: must occur between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive. Routine prisoner exchange alone does not count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Ukraine Russia peace talks direct bilateral negotiations 2025' (Oct 31-Nov 30) - to find any announced talks; 2) 'Ukraine Russia ceasefire negotiations announcement November 2025' (Oct 31-Nov 30) - to find ceasefire deal announcements; 3) 'Ukraine Russia direct talks Istanbul fourth round scheduled announced' (Oct 31-Nov 30) - to find specific Istanbul fourth round; 4) 'Putin Zelensky both sides confirm peace negotiations meeting date' (Oct 31-Nov 30) - to find mutual confirmation; 5) 'Zelensky Medinsky Umerov direct negotiations Russia Ukraine meeting November 2025' - to find specific delegations meeting.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Ukraine officially halted/suspended direct peace talks with Russia - Nov 12, 2025, Ukrainian Deputy FM Kyslytsya. (B) Russia signaled readiness to resume Istanbul talks - Nov 12, 2025, Russian diplomat Polishchuk/Ivanov (unilateral, not mutual). (C) Turkey offered to host 4th round - Nov 1-2, 2025 (Turkey offer only, no agreement from either party). (D) US-Ukraine talks in Geneva - Nov 23-24, 2025 (US-mediated, not direct Ukraine-Russia). (E) Abu Dhabi 'secret talks' Putin confirmed Russian and Ukrainian officials met - Nov 27, 2025. (F) Ukraine delegation headed to US - Nov 29, 2025 (US-Ukraine talks, not Russia-Ukraine). All events are REJECTED as not meeting criteria: either Ukraine unilaterally suspended talks, Russia unilaterally expressed readiness without Ukraine's agreement, or talks are US-mediated multi-party negotiations not direct bilateral rounds mutually acknowledged by both sides.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Rejected: (A) Ukraine formally suspended talks [Anadolu Agency Nov 12](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/ukrainian-deputy-foreign-minister-says-kyiv-suspended-peace-talks-with-russia/3742359), [TASS Nov 12](https://tass.com/world/2042933) — explicitly against a Yes resolution. (B) Russia unilaterally said ready to restart [Washington Times Nov 12](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/nov/12/russia-signals-ready-restart-peace-talks-ukraine-istanbul/), [B92 Nov 12](https://www.b92.net/english/world/180850/ivanov-russia-is-ready-to-hold-negotiations-with-ukraine-in-istanbul-at-any-moment/vest) — unilateral, not mutual. (E) Abu Dhabi 'secret talks' - Putin confirmed Nov 27 [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/putin-confirms-russian-ukrainian-secret-talks-in-abu-dhabi/3755899) that a Russian-Ukrainian meeting occurred in Abu Dhabi at Ukraine's initiative — but no official Ukrainian government source publicly confirmed this as a direct bilateral negotiation round, and Putin himself on Nov 28 ruled out talks with Zelenskyy [Medium.com Nov 28]. The Abu Dhabi talks were not accompanied by mutual public official confirmation nor described by either side as a new round of broader bilateral negotiations. No specific date and venue confirmed by both sides for any future round. Criteria NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found within the window. Ukraine suspended talks Nov 12, 2025. The Abu Dhabi talks were secret and not publicly acknowledged by Ukraine as a new negotiating round. No mutual official announcement existed.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event occurred at any point in the window. The evidence consistently shows talks were suspended or only unilaterally offered, never mutually agreed upon.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Putin on Nov 28 confirmed Russian-Ukrainian officials met secretly in Abu Dhabi, but (1) Ukraine did not officially confirm this as a new round of bilateral talks, (2) Putin simultaneously ruled out direct talks with Zelenskyy, (3) the meeting was described as Ukraine-initiated and US-participated secret contact, not a publicly announced new round. Macron on Nov 25 explicitly stated Russia showed 'no willingness to agree ceasefire.' French and other leaders confirmed Russia had not engaged on revised peace plan. Ukraine's delegation was headed to the US (Nov 29) for US-Ukraine talks, not Russia-Ukraine talks. No scenario exists where both official Ukrainian and Russian sources publicly confirmed a new round of direct bilateral talks with a shared upcoming meeting.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Ukraine officially suspended direct bilateral peace talks on Nov 12, 2025. Russia expressed readiness unilaterally but Ukraine did not reciprocate. All major diplomatic activity in November 2025 involved US-mediated multi-party talks (Geneva, Abu Dhabi) rather than direct mutually acknowledged Ukraine-Russia bilateral negotiations. Putin on Nov 28 ruled out direct talks with Zelenskyy. No official announcement from both sides of a scheduled direct bilateral round was made during the entire Oct 31 - Nov 30 window. The window closed with no qualifying event.

question: Will Trump try to fire Powell in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump publicly and unequivocally announces that he is removing Jerome Powell as Chair of the Federal Reserve before his term is up, or takes formal action toward doing so, such as issuing a directive or formal request by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, will Donald Trump publicly state that Jerome Powell should resign or that the Federal Reserve Board should remove or override him as Chair?
subquestions.background_information:
This is an informative leading indicator for whether Trump will later try to fire Powell outright. Trump has already escalated his rhetoric toward Powell in 2025. On 2025-08-01, Yahoo Finance reported that Trump wrote on Truth Social: "Jerome 'Too Late' Powell, a stubborn MORON, must substantially lower interest rates, NOW. IF HE CONTINUES TO REFUSE, THE BOARD SHOULD ASSUME CONTROL, AND DO WHAT EVERYONE KNOWS HAS TO BE DONE!" https://finance.yahoo.com/ . That kind of public pressure on Powell short of a formal firing attempt is plausibly one of the clearest near-term precursors to the ultimate event.

A second relevant development is Trump's attempt to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook in late August 2025. CBS News reported on 2025-08-26 that Trump announced he had fired Cook and posted a letter saying he had determined there was sufficient cause to remove her from the Board of Governors. https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-says-hes-fired-federal-reserve-board-member-lisa-cook/ This matters because it shows Trump is already willing to test the boundaries of presidential removal power over the Federal Reserve, making further escalatory rhetoric toward Powell more consequential than ordinary political criticism.

Market commentary has also treated Trump's prior comments about Powell as a meaningful signal. The Business Times reported on 2025-07-17 that markets were rattled by what investors viewed as a "credible threat" of Trump trying to fire Powell, even though Trump subsequently downplayed the possibility. https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/ That suggests a renewed call for Powell to resign, or for the Board to strip Powell of authority, would likely be interpreted as evidence that the administration is moving closer to an actual removal attempt.

This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it asks about an earlier rhetorical or political escalation that falls short of publicly and unequivocally announcing Powell's removal or taking formal action. If resolved Yes, it would increase the odds that Trump later attempts to fire Powell; if No, it would suggest reduced near-term momentum toward that outcome.

Sources:
Yahoo Finance - Trump Demands Fed Board Remove Chair Jerome Powell, But Polymarket Traders Aren't Buying It - https://finance.yahoo.com/
CBS News - Trump says he's fired Federal Reserve board member Lisa Cook - https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-says-hes-fired-federal-reserve-board-member-lisa-cook/
The Business Times - Markets rattled by 'credible threat' of Trump trying to fire Jerome Powell - https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Donald Trump makes a public statement that clearly and directly says at least one of the following about Jerome Powell: (a) Powell should resign; (b) the Federal Reserve Board should remove Powell as Chair; or (c) the Board should take control from, override, or otherwise strip Powell of his effective leadership as Chair.

Qualifying statements may be made on Truth Social, White House releases/transcripts, official campaign or presidential social-media accounts, televised remarks, speeches, or interviews, provided the wording is publicly available in a primary source or reliably quoted by multiple credible outlets.

This question resolves No if no such public statement is made between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

Important exclusions: a statement that Trump may fire Powell, is considering firing Powell, is planning to fire Powell, or criticism of Powell's rate policy alone does not qualify unless it explicitly says Powell should resign or that the Board should remove/override him. A statement that already constitutes an unequivocal firing announcement or formal removal action would not be used to resolve this subquestion Yes unless it also independently contains one of the narrower qualifying statements above; if the only relevant event is the ultimate question event itself, this subquestion should still be resolved based on whether the qualifying rhetoric occurred.

Primary resolution sources: Trump's Truth Social posts and official White House transcripts/releases if available. Secondary sources: consensus of credible reporting from outlets such as CBS News, Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, or similar.

Suggested sources for resolution:
- Truth Social / Trump's account or mirrored official posts if publicly accessible
- White House remarks and statements: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- Reuters U.S. markets/economy coverage: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- CBS News: https://www.cbsnews.com/

If no sufficiently public record of Trump's exact words is available, the market should resolve according to the balance of credible contemporaneous reporting quoting the statement. If reporting is irreconcilably contradictory and no primary source can be found, the question should be treated as unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A public demand that Powell resign, or that the Board remove or override him, would be a meaningful escalation that stops short of an actual firing attempt. It is a plausible intermediate step in the path to the ultimate question and would materially update forecasts about whether Trump will later try to fire Powell in 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Trump must make a PUBLIC statement EXPLICITLY saying (a) Powell should resign, (b) the Fed Board should remove Powell as Chair, OR (c) the Board should take control from/override/strip Powell of leadership. Key EXCLUSIONS: statements about Trump firing Powell, considering firing Powell, planning to fire Powell, or rate policy criticism alone do NOT qualify. Observable evidence: direct primary-source quote or clear, verbatim reporting from multiple credible outlets of Trump using qualifying language. Window: 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump Powell resign Federal Reserve Board remove override September 2025' (finding qualifying statements); Query 2: 'Trump Jerome Powell fire criticism Federal Reserve September 2025' (broad search); Query 3: 'Trump Powell resign Truth Social statement September 2025 exact quote' (finding primary-source quotes); Query 4: 'Trump explicitly called urged Powell resign speech interview statement September 2025' (finding verbal statements); Query 5: 'Trump Federal Reserve Board override strip Powell leadership control September 2025' (finding override/strip statements); Query 6: 'Trump You're Fired Powell meme cartoon Truth Social September 27 2025 meaning' (analyzing the cartoon post).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) September 27-28, 2025: Trump posted a 'You're Fired!' cartoon/meme on Truth Social depicting himself firing Powell — REJECTED as qualifying because the resolution criteria explicitly excludes 'a statement that Trump may fire Powell.' (2) Multiple secondary articles characterize Trump as 'pressuring Powell to resign' or having 'called for Powell's resignation' — REJECTED as primary qualifying evidence because these are reporters' characterizations/summaries, not direct quotes of Trump explicitly saying 'Powell should resign.' (3) Trump's actual direct quotes found: 'Too Late must lower the RATE, BIG, right now. Powell is a total disaster, who doesn't have a clue!!!'; 'Too Late MUST CUT INTEREST RATES, NOW, AND BIGGER THAN HE HAD IN MIND'; announcing Powell successor candidates — these are rate policy criticism and discussion of succession, NOT qualifying statements. (4) Opinion columnists (Stephen Moore, Power Line, RealClearPolitics) calling for Powell's resignation — these are third parties, not Trump.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires Trump's OWN statement explicitly saying Powell should resign or the Board should remove/override him. Key evidence reviewed: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/27/trump-cartoon-firing-powell-fed.html) reports Trump posted a cartoon saying 'YOU'RE FIRED!' — this depicts Trump firing Powell, which falls under the explicit exclusion. [Market Screener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/trump-says-fed-chair-powell-should-make-big-rate-cut-now-ce7d59ddd88af025) reports Trump's direct quote: 'Powell is a total disaster, who doesn't have a clue!!!' — rate policy criticism only, not a qualifying statement. Secondary characterizations in [NewsBytes](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/trump-anticipates-major-interest-rate-cut-but-federal-reserve/story), [KSL](https://www.ksl.com/article/51376374/fed-expected-to-cut-rates-update-views-of-trump-economic-plan-with-new-projections), [MedPage Today](https://www.medpagetoday.com/washington-watch/washington-watch/117658), [New Indian Express](https://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2025/Sep/26/trump-to-put-100-import-taxes-on-pharmaceutical-drugs-kitchen-cabinets-furniture-and-heavy-trucks) describe Trump as 'pressuring Powell to resign' or having 'urged Powell to resign,' but none provide a direct verbatim quote of Trump explicitly saying the qualifying words. The distinction between 'Trump said Powell should resign' (qualifying) vs. 'Trump has pressured Powell to resign' (reporter characterization) is critical. No primary source with verbatim qualifying language was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp of a qualifying verbatim statement from Trump could be extracted. The 'You're Fired!' cartoon was posted on September 27, 2025, but falls under the explicit exclusion. Reporter characterizations of Trump 'calling for Powell to resign' lack accompanying verbatim primary-source quotes with reliable timestamps.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was identified within the window because no direct, verbatim primary-source qualifying statement from Trump was found that explicitly says Powell should resign or the Board should remove/override him.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification attempts: (1) The 'You're Fired!' cartoon clearly depicts firing, not resignation, and the resolution criteria explicitly excludes firing statements. (2) Secondary reporting characterizations of Trump 'calling for resignation' are not accompanied by direct quotes. This could reflect reporters' interpretation of his overall posture (threats to fire, pressure campaign) rather than explicit 'resign' statements. (3) Trump's own verified direct quotes during this period (Truth Social posts) are rate policy criticism and the 'You're Fired' cartoon — none explicitly say 'Powell should resign' or 'the Board should remove Powell.' (4) No evidence found of Trump calling on the Board specifically to remove or override Powell. (5) The resolution criteria explicitly sets a high bar: 'clearly and directly says' one of the qualifying things — secondary characterizations without verbatim quotes do not meet this standard under the 'prefer precision over recall' instruction.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: No. While Trump made many inflammatory statements about Powell during this period (calling him a disaster, posting a 'You're Fired' meme, pressuring him on rates), none of Trump's verified direct statements within the window explicitly said Powell should resign or that the Federal Reserve Board should remove or override Powell as Chair. The 'You're Fired' cartoon falls under the explicit exclusion. Secondary reporter characterizations of Trump 'pressuring Powell to resign' lack accompanying verbatim quotes meeting the 'clearly and directly says' standard. The window closed on 2025-10-01 without a confirmed qualifying statement.

question: Will Donald Trump visit Germany in 2025?
description:
If U.S. President Donald Trump visits a listed country between January 15 and December 31, 2025 11:59 PM ET, the relevant market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial or maritime territory of the listed country. Whether or not Trump enters the country's airspace during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the White House publicly announce between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-22 that President Donald Trump will attend an event in Germany in 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A formal public announcement of a presidential trip is a strong near-term indicator for whether the trip will actually occur, especially when the ultimate question's deadline is only weeks away. Germany is a plausible destination because Trump has already engaged Germany's leadership in Washington in 2025: the Council on Foreign Relations noted on June 5, 2025 that Germany's chancellor was set to meet Trump in the Oval Office to discuss trade and Ukraine, showing active high-level bilateral engagement between the two governments (https://www.cfr.org/article/germany-chancellor-visits-washington). Germany is also a country Trump has visited before, though not frequently; Statista reported on September 16, 2025 that Trump had visited Germany once previously for the 2017 G20 summit and had not yet made a bilateral visit to Germany (https://www.statista.com/chart/35262/trumps-international-travels-mapped/). Recent NATO-related tensions in Central Europe may also raise the salience of a Germany visit, as reporting on September 17, 2025 highlighted Operation Eastern Sentry and Germany's role in allied deployments on NATO's eastern flank (https://herald-review.com/news/world/article_drones-over-poland-test-nato-trump.html). Because presidential foreign travel is usually preceded by official scheduling notices, a White House announcement during October 1-22 would materially increase the chance that Trump physically enters Germany before the ultimate market closes on October 25.

Sources:
Council on Foreign Relations - Germany Chancellor Visits Washington - https://www.cfr.org/article/germany-chancellor-visits-washington
Statista - Trump's International Travels Mapped - https://www.statista.com/chart/35262/trumps-international-travels-mapped/
Herald-Review - Drones over Poland test NATO, Trump - https://herald-review.com/news/world/article_drones-over-poland-test-nato-trump.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-22 (inclusive), the White House or another official U.S. government source publicly states that President Donald Trump is scheduled or expected to attend an event in Germany at any time in 2025. Qualifying announcements include, for example: a White House schedule, press guidance, statement, proclamation, readout, or official travel announcement; or an official U.S. embassy / State Department / administration release explicitly saying Trump will be in Germany. The announcement must specifically indicate Germany as a destination for Trump; a generic Europe trip announcement without naming Germany does not count.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying official announcement is published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-22 (inclusive).

- White House Briefing Room: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- White House Presidential Actions / Statements: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/
- White House Live / Schedule-related postings: https://www.whitehouse.gov/live/

If an announcement is made outside the window, including before 2025-10-01 or after 2025-10-22, it does not count. If reports only say planning is under discussion, or that an invitation exists, without an official U.S. government announcement that Trump will attend in Germany, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A public White House announcement of a Germany event is a concrete preparatory step that should sharply update forecasts about whether Trump will physically visit Germany by October 25. It is not the same as the ultimate question, because it asks about an earlier scheduling signal rather than the visit itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The White House or an official U.S. government source must publicly announce between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-22 (inclusive) that President Trump is scheduled to attend an event in Germany at any time in 2025. Required: explicit naming of Germany as a destination, from an official U.S. source. Observable evidence: White House briefing room post, press guidance, official travel statement, or State Department release naming Germany.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump Germany trip 2025 White House announcement' (Oct 1–22) — to find any official announcement; 2) 'Trump visit Germany schedule travel announcement official' (Oct 1–22) — broader search; 3) 'Trump Germany travel White House official announcement October 2025' — targeted to window; 4) 'Trump Europe trip Germany Berlin 2025' — to catch any Europe trip naming Germany; 5) 'Trump Germany visit scheduled 2025 invitation Merz' — to check if Merz invitation was confirmed officially; 6) 'White House travel schedule Germany announcement October 2025' — direct search for WH source; 7) 'Trump Bad Durkheim Germany trip visit 2025' — specific Germany destination; 8) 'Trump Ukraine peace meeting Hungary Germany Europe summit' — covering diplomatic travel; 9) Site-specific search for whitehouse.gov/state.gov Germany announcement.

All candidates rejected as not meeting criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event satisfies the resolution criteria. Trump's travel announcements within the window (Israel/Egypt Oct 13, Asia Oct 21+) do not name Germany. The Merz invitation from June 2025 [Chosun.com](https://www.chosun.com/english/world-en/2025/10/21/H6RHIUOSDZBFBBPZL43LIRWOIQ/) is an invitation from a foreign leader, not an official White House or U.S. government announcement that Trump will attend an event in Germany. The AfD honorary citizenship proposal [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/afd-calls-trump-made-honorary-054021101.html) is a foreign political party motion, not a qualifying announcement. No White House Briefing Room, State Department, or official U.S. government source named Germany as a Trump destination during the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying event was found within the window. The window closes at 2025-10-22T23:59:59Z.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at any point in the Oct 1–22 window. Extensive searches across multiple query types returned no evidence of a White House or U.S. government announcement specifically naming Germany as a Trump travel destination.

There is a standing invitation from Merz for Trump to visit Bad Dürkheim, but this has not been followed by any U.S. government confirmation of a Germany trip. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Despite multiple searches, no evidence was found of the White House or any official U.S. government source announcing between October 1–22, 2025 that Trump would attend an event in Germany in 2025. question: Will NVIDIA be the second-largest company in the world by market cap on December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to the second-largest company in the world by market cap on December 31, 2025, as of market close.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will NVIDIA Corporation close at a market capitalization at least 15% higher than Apple Inc.'s on any U.S. trading day between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13?
subquestions.background_information:
NVIDIA's chance of finishing 2025 as the world's second-largest company by market cap depends importantly on whether it can maintain a substantial cushion over Apple, one of the most plausible rivals for the #2 spot. As of late September / early October 2025, multiple financial outlets reported that Nvidia had become the world's largest public company, with a market capitalization above $4.5 trillion after a September 30, 2025 close around $186.58 per share, surpassing Microsoft and far exceeding earlier thresholds such as $4 trillion reached in July 2025. See Yahoo! Finance coverage: https://finance.yahoo.com/ and the related article summary provided by the user. Contemporary reporting also described Apple as around $3.9 trillion and Microsoft around $3.4 trillion in August 2025, indicating that Apple remained in the same broad range as the principal comparator for a #2 ranking contest; see The Motley Fool article summary and site: https://www.fool.com/ .

A subquestion about whether Nvidia can build and hold a double-digit lead over Apple by mid-November is informative because the ultimate question asks about the year-end rank on December 31, 2025. If Nvidia is already materially ahead of Apple in the near term, that is evidence it is more likely to remain at least #2 at year end; if not, the race is tighter. This is not a restatement of the final question because it asks about a relative spread versus a specific rival during an earlier window, rather than Nvidia's exact global rank on December 31.

For market-cap comparisons, authoritative and publicly accessible daily data can be obtained from CompaniesMarketCap, which publishes end-of-day market capitalizations for listed companies and rank tables. Nvidia page: https://companiesmarketcap.com/nvidia/marketcap/ . Apple page: https://companiesmarketcap.com/apple/marketcap/ . The site's global ranking page also provides context for the leading firms: https://companiesmarketcap.com/ .

CompaniesMarketCap - Apple market cap: https://companiesmarketcap.com/apple/marketcap/
CompaniesMarketCap - Global ranking by market cap: https://companiesmarketcap.com/
Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/
The Motley Fool: https://www.fool.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Operationally, for each trading day in the window from 2025-10-14 through 2025-11-13 inclusive, compute the ratio using CompaniesMarketCap's daily historical market-cap series:

subquestions.rationale: Nvidia's odds of being #2 on December 31 rise if it can establish a clear near-term valuation cushion over Apple, one of the most likely competing firms for that slot. evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: On at least one U.S. trading day between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 inclusive, NVIDIA's end-of-day market cap / Apple's end-of-day market cap >= 1.15. (f) Oct 29: NVDA ~$5.03T (closed $207.04), Apple ~$3.99T → ratio ~1.261. (g) Nov 1: NVDA $4.92T, Apple $4.01T → ratio 1.227. (h) Nov 3-6: NVDA ~$5T, Apple ~$4T → ratio ~1.25. All candidate dates yield ratios above 1.15.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple sources confirm the ratio exceeded 1.15 throughout the window: [Visual Capitalist/CompaniesMarketCap](https://www.visualcapitalist.com/ranked-the-worlds-50-most-valuable-companies-in-october-2025/) states Oct 24: NVDA $4.53T, Apple $3.9T → ratio 1.162 (>1.15). Since the window starts October 14 and the ratio was already well above 1.15 on Oct 20 (and evidence suggests it was above 1.15 from day one), the earliest verifiable qualifying date is 2025-10-20T00:00:00Z (end of trading day).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question window opens October 14, 2025. evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition (NVDA market cap / Apple market cap >= 1.15) was met on multiple days within the window. The earliest explicitly confirmed day with both market caps stated for the same date is October 20, 2025 (NVDA $4.4T, Apple $3.7T, ratio=1.189). Earlier dates within the window (Oct 14-19) also appear to qualify based on NVDA data and Apple trajectory, but the October 20 date is the most explicitly supported. The resolution is Yes.

question: GOP uses 'Nuclear Option' to break filibuster by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US Senate passes a motion to invoke cloture and end debate on any part of the legislative process, with such a cloture motion receiving Yea votes from fewer than three-fifths of the Senators by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve "No".

Confirmations are considered part of the Senate’s “advice and consent” function, not part of the Senate’s “legislative process,” and will therefore not count towards this market's resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the U.S. government.

subquestions.question: Will Senate Majority Leader John Thune publicly say between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 that he supports, is considering, or is open to using a simple-majority rules change to pass government funding legislation or a continuing resolution?
subquestions.background_information:
A key near-term indicator for whether Senate Republicans might use the legislative 'nuclear option' by year-end is whether Majority Leader John Thune shifts his public stance. As of late October 2025, multiple reports say Thune has ruled out using the nuclear option to end the government shutdown, even though some Republicans outside the Senate and a few senators have urged it. Spectrum News reported that Thune dismissed using the nuclear option to end the shutdown and defended the filibuster as something that 'makes the Senate the Senate' https://baynews9.com/fl/tampa/politics/2025/10/21/shutdown-sparks-new-conversations-on--nuclear-option- . Townhall similarly reported on 2025-10-09 that Senate Republicans were 'not yet considering' changing filibuster rules for legislation and quoted Sen. Roger Marshall strongly rejecting the idea https://townhall.com/tipsheet/saraharnold/2025/10/09/republicans-not-yet-considering-changing-filibuster-rules-to-end-government-shutdown-n2664768 .

At the same time, pressure inside the GOP ecosystem has risen. The Hill reported on 2025-10-20 that Rep. Chip Roy explicitly floated the nuclear option for funding legislation, while Speaker Mike Johnson cautioned against it and Thune had ruled it out for the continuing resolution https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5561813-chip-roy-floats-nuclear-option-on-senate-filibuster-to-end-shutdown/ . Other reports note calls from Marjorie Taylor Greene and discussion of a possible carve-out for funding bills, with Sen. Susan Collins reportedly leaving open the possibility of considering proposals to reopen the government and Sen. John Fetterman supporting a funding carve-out https://www.easternprogress.com/news/greene-calls-for-nuclear-option-to-end-government-shutdown-what-is-it/article_0f9a0f5e-8f61-11f0-9e58-7f1a3f08d7d3.html .

This matters because the ultimate question is specifically about a Senate legislative cloture precedent being set with fewer than 60 votes by 2025-12-31. A public shift by Thune would be a strong leading indicator: he controls the floor and would almost certainly need to authorize any such procedural escalation. This is not a restatement of the ultimate question, because it asks about an observable signaling event rather than the procedural vote itself.

Sources:
Spectrum News Bay News 9 - Shutdown sparks new conversations on 'nuclear option' - https://baynews9.com/fl/tampa/politics/2025/10/21/shutdown-sparks-new-conversations-on--nuclear-option-
Townhall - Republican's Not Yet Considering Changing Filibuster Rules To End Government Shutdown - https://townhall.com/tipsheet/saraharnold/2025/10/09/republicans-not-yet-considering-changing-filibuster-rules-to-end-government-shutdown-n2664768
The Hill - Chip Roy floats nuclear option on Senate filibuster to end shutdown - https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5561813-chip-roy-floats-nuclear-option-on-senate-filibuster-to-end-shutdown/
Eastern Progress - Greene calls for ‘nuclear option’ to end government shutdown. What is it? - https://www.easternprogress.com/news/greene-calls-for-nuclear-option-to-end-government-shutdown-what-is-it/article_0f9a0f5e-8f61-11f0-9e58-7f1a3f08d7d3.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), Senate Majority Leader John Thune makes a public statement that clearly indicates he supports, is considering, or is open to using a simple-majority Senate precedent/rules change for government funding legislation or a continuing resolution. Examples that count include statements such as: 'I support using the nuclear option for a CR,' 'we are considering all options including a simple-majority path for funding,' or 'I am open to a carve-out from the filibuster for appropriations/shutdown-ending legislation.'

This question resolves No if no such public statement is made during that window.

For resolution, use on-the-record statements reported by major outlets or official transcripts/posts from Thune's office. Primary sources preferred, in order:
1. Thune's official Senate site: https://www.thune.senate.gov/
2. Thune's official press releases/newsroom pages on that site.
3. Thune's official X account or other verified official social-media accounts, if archived and publicly viewable.
4. Congressional press conference video/transcripts carried by C-SPAN: https://www.c-span.org/
5. If no primary-source text is available, reporting from Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ , AP https://apnews.com/ , The Hill https://thehill.com/ , Punchbowl News https://punchbowl.news/ , Politico https://www.politico.com/ , or major national newspapers may be used.

Statements do NOT count if they only reaffirm opposition to the nuclear option, discuss prior nominee precedent changes only, or refer solely to confirmations rather than legislation. Ambiguous comments like 'we'll keep talking' do not count unless they explicitly mention a simple-majority rules change, nuclear option, carve-out, or ending the 60-vote threshold for funding legislation.

If conflicting paraphrases appear, the resolver should defer to the clearest verbatim quote or official video/transcript. If no sufficiently clear public statement can be verified from the listed sources, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Thune changes his public position is a high-value crux because he is the pivotal agenda-setter for any legislative rules confrontation. A move from ruling out the nuclear option to even saying he is 'open' to it would materially increase the probability of the ultimate event by December 31.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: John Thune makes a public on-the-record statement between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 indicating he supports, is considering, or is open to using a simple-majority Senate rules change (nuclear option, carve-out, ending 60-vote threshold) for government funding legislation or a continuing resolution. Observable evidence: verbatim quotes or official reports from major outlets/Thune's office showing such openness. Key entities: John Thune, Senate Majority Leader. Timing: within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'John Thune nuclear option simple majority continuing resolution government funding 2025' — to find any statement of support or openness; 2) 'Thune filibuster carve-out appropriations CR Senate rules change November 2025' — to find specific carve-out language; 3) 'Thune open to nuclear option filibuster carve-out funding bill November 2025' — to find any shift in position; 4) 'Thune considering simple majority rules change appropriations shutdown November 2025' — to find any consideration; 5) 'Thune filibuster position change support nuclear option late November 2025' — to check for late-window shift; 6) 'Senate rules change 60 vote threshold government funding November 2025' — to find any Senate rules change discussion.
evidence.step3_event_detection: All candidate events found show Thune consistently OPPOSING the nuclear option and simple-majority rules change throughout the window: (a) Oct 31: Thune's position 'unchanged,' called it a 'bad idea'; (b) Nov 4: 'The votes aren't there'; (c) Nov 5: Ending filibuster is 'not happening'; (d) Nov 8: Multiple sources confirm Thune downplayed Trump's nuclear option push; (e) Nov 10-12: Shutdown ended via 60-vote bipartisan deal, not rules change; (f) Nov 24-28: Treasury Secretary Bessent called for ending filibuster, but Thune still resisted, saying he wants to 'ensure that the Senate stays the Senate' and that Republicans would 'own all the crap' Democrats do later. No candidate event shows Thune expressing support, consideration, or openness to a simple-majority rules change for funding legislation.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All evidence explicitly contradicts the Yes condition. [The Hill, Oct 31](https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5583744-gop-leader-thune-defends-filibuster-trump/): 'Leader Thune's position on the importance of the legislative filibuster is unchanged.' [Yahoo/AP, Nov 5](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/thune-reiterates-filibuster-changes-not-175456775.html): Thune says ending filibuster 'not happening.' [Newsday, Nov 28](https://www.newsday.com/long-island/politics/trump-senate-filibuster-thfrcofx): Thune continued to resist, emphasizing 'one of my priorities as leader will be to ensure that the Senate stays the Senate.' [Scott Bessent/Benzinga, Nov 24](https://www.benzinga.com/news/politics/25/11/49024359/scott-bessent-says-if-radical-left-again-shuts-down-government-in-january-gop-should-immediately-end-the-filibuster): 'Republican leaders, including Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) and House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.), have resisted.' No statement matching the Yes criteria was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. The condition for Yes was never met within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence exists at any point in the window. Extensive searching found only statements of opposition to, not support for or openness to, a simple-majority rules change for government funding.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: Attempted to find any late-window shift in Thune's position (especially after the shutdown ended Nov 12 and Scott Bessent's Nov 24 op-ed calling for filibuster elimination). Even after Bessent's op-ed, Thune continued to publicly oppose changing the filibuster, per the Nov 28 Newsday article. No conflicting evidence exists. All sources consistently report Thune maintaining opposition throughout the window. The government shutdown was ultimately resolved via the existing 60-vote threshold (bipartisan deal), not a rules change — further confirming Thune never moved toward the nuclear option for funding.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is clear, direct, explicit, and consistent throughout the entire window. Thune repeatedly and publicly stated opposition to using a simple-majority rules change for government funding. He called it a 'bad idea,' said it was 'not happening,' said 'the votes aren't there,' and emphasized his priority to keep the Senate as it is. No statement of support, consideration, or openness to a nuclear option or carve-out for appropriations was found from any source. Resolution: No.

question: Will the federal government be shut down for 10–29 days in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve according to how many days the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announces that the U.S. federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse in appropriations by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM.

Days are counted based on notices checked at 10:00 AM ET each day. If the Office of Personnel Management announces a partial shutdown, this will count; however, announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather will not qualify. 

If there are multiple government shutdowns during the relevant period, this market only applies to the first shutdown, as the market will resolve after the end of the first shutdown. Notices of emergency furloughs or impacted government operations count toward the shutdown days.  

If no shutdown occurs during the period, this market will resolve to "No shutdown".

The resolution source for this market will be the website of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

subquestions.question: Will Congress pass, and President Trump sign, a continuing resolution or full-year appropriations law that extends federal discretionary funding beyond October 1, 2025, by October 1, 2025 11:59 PM ET?
subquestions.background_information:
A lapse in appropriations that triggers a federal shutdown would ordinarily begin when the new fiscal year starts on October 1 if Congress has not enacted either regular appropriations or a continuing resolution (CR). That makes enactment of any funding measure before the deadline a strong leading indicator for whether a shutdown occurs at all, and therefore for whether the first shutdown could last 10–29 days. Congress has reportedly completed only a small subset of the 12 annual appropriations bills so far, increasing reliance on a CR as the most plausible shutdown-avoidance path. For example, reporting in early September said the Senate had passed only three appropriations bills and the House only two, with a CR viewed as the most likely near-term outcome if a shutdown is avoided (National Law Review, 2025-09-03: https://natlawreview.com/article/potential-outcomes-if-congress-misses-federal-funding-deadline). Contemporary reporting also noted that the federal funding cycle ends at midnight on September 30, 2025, and that a partial shutdown could begin on October 1 absent enacted funding; Republicans hold narrow majorities, while the Senate's 60-vote threshold means bipartisan support is likely needed (AOL, 2025-09-04: https://www.aol.com/could-government-shutdown-occur-affect-090000000.html). Additional reporting described the situation as unusually risky because most appropriations bills remained unfinished and lawmakers were under pressure to negotiate a bipartisan stopgap bill before October 1 (New Hampshire Bulletin, 2025-09-03: https://newhampshirebulletin.com/2025/09/03/every-fall-theres-a-government-shutdown-warning-this-time-it-could-happen/). If such a funding law is enacted on time, the chance of any October 1 shutdown falls sharply; if it is not, the probability of a shutdown—and potentially one lasting more than a token 1–2 days—rises materially.

Sources:
National Law Review – Potential Outcomes If Congress Misses the Federal Funding Deadline — https://natlawreview.com/article/potential-outcomes-if-congress-misses-federal-funding-deadline
AOL – When could a government shutdown occur? How would it affect you? — https://www.aol.com/could-government-shutdown-occur-affect-090000000.html
New Hampshire Bulletin – Every fall there’s a government shutdown warning. This time it could happen. — https://newhampshirebulletin.com/2025/09/03/every-fall-theres-a-government-shutdown-warning-this-time-it-could-happen/
Congress.gov — https://www.congress.gov/
White House Presidential Actions — https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-17 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), both of the following occur by 2025-10-01 11:59 PM ET: (1) Congress finally passes a bill that provides appropriations or a continuing resolution covering at least some discretionary federal agencies for a period extending beyond 2025-10-01 12:00 AM ET; and (2) the President signs that bill into law. For resolution, the primary source will be Congress.gov legislative status pages showing final passage in both chambers and the White House Presidential Actions page or the enrolled public law record showing presidential signature: https://www.congress.gov/ and https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/ . A bill qualifies whether it is a short-term CR, omnibus, minibus, or full-year appropriations law, so long as it prevents a lapse in appropriations for at least some discretionary agencies past the start of October 1, 2025. Budget resolutions that do not themselves provide budget authority do not count. Passage in only one chamber does not count. If a bill is passed by Congress before the deadline but is signed after 2025-10-01 11:59 PM ET, this question resolves No. If Congress.gov is unavailable, official House Clerk and Senate roll-call records plus the public law record on GovInfo may be used as fallback sources: https://clerk.house.gov/ , https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm , https://www.govinfo.gov/ .
subquestions.rationale: The most direct early crux for a 2025 shutdown lasting 10–29 days is whether lawmakers avert the initial funding lapse at the key fiscal deadline. If a CR or appropriations law is enacted on time, the ultimate market is very likely to resolve to no shutdown; if not, the odds of a shutdown beginning on October 1 increase substantially, making a 10–29 day duration much more plausible.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes: (1) Congress must pass (both chambers) a bill providing appropriations or a CR covering at least some federal discretionary agencies for a period extending beyond October 1, 2025 12:00 AM ET; AND (2) President Trump must sign that bill into law — all by 2025-10-01 11:59 PM ET. The bill must provide actual budget authority (not just a budget resolution). Observable evidence: Congressional vote records showing final passage in both chambers and a White House presidential signature record, all timestamped within the window (2025-09-17 to 2025-10-01 inclusive).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'continuing resolution government funding October 2025 Congress signed' (2025-09-17 to 2025-10-01) — to find any signed CR; 2) 'government shutdown October 2025 federal funding deadline' (2025-09-17 to 2025-10-01) — to find whether shutdown occurred; 3) 'government shutdown ended October 2025 continuing resolution signed Trump' (2025-10-01) — to see if any last-minute deal was reached on Oct 1; 4) 'Senate vote continuing resolution passed October 1 2025 government funding' (2025-09-30 to 2025-10-01) — to check Senate vote outcomes; 5) 'government shutdown deal October 1 2025 CR signed Trump reopened' (2025-10-01) — to see if shutdown was resolved same day.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) House passed 'clean' CR on September 19, 2025 (funding through November 21) — passed only one chamber, does not qualify. (B) Senate vote on Republican CR (House-passed bill) on September 30 — FAILED, did not reach 60-vote threshold. (C) Senate vote on Democratic alternative CR — also FAILED. (D) House Democrats attempted unanimous consent for their own CR on September 30 — failed/blocked by Republicans. (E) Government shutdown commenced at 12:01 AM on October 1, 2025 — confirming no CR was enacted. No event found of any CR being passed by both chambers and signed by President Trump within the window. All searches for a last-minute October 1 deal returned no results.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event satisfies both criteria: (1) Congress finally passing a bill through both chambers AND (2) President Trump signing it, by October 1, 2025 11:59 PM ET. Multiple sources confirm the government shut down at 12:01 AM on October 1, 2025 [politomix.com](https://politomix.com/foxnews/2293121/government-shuts-down-after-congress-deadlocks-spending/), [apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/government-shutdown-chuck-schumer-20e54a0f5e4fee909d0f9ea2c07c15e1), [breakingnews.ie](https://www.breakingnews.ie/world/us-government-shutdown-begins-as-nation-faces-new-period-of-uncertainty-1813235.html), [businessday.ng](https://businessday.ng/world/article/us-government-shuts-down-after-senate-deadlock/). The Senate rejected both CRs on September 30, 2025, and no further legislative action was taken by midnight. The House was on recess until October 7, 2025 [jdsupra.com](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/healthcare-preview-for-the-week-of-1596875/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The shutdown definitively began at 12:01 AM ET on October 1, 2025 (04:01 UTC on October 1, 2025), confirmed by multiple sources. The Senate's final votes on both CRs occurred around 5:30–6:30 PM EDT on September 30, 2025 (approximately 21:30–22:30 UTC on September 30, 2025), both failing. No subsequent votes or presidential signatures occurred within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (both chambers passing + presidential signature) was found at any point in the window 2025-09-17 to 2025-10-01. The only bill that passed one chamber was the House's clean CR on September 19, which the Senate failed to pass. No earlier qualifying event exists.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No source reports a CR or appropriations bill being passed by both chambers and signed by Trump within the window. Sources from the morning of October 1 (SBS, Fox2 Detroit, Politomix/Fox News, Businessday NG) confirm the shutdown was underway, with no mention of a last-minute deal being signed. The search for 'government shutdown deal October 1 2025 CR signed Trump reopened' returned no articles, confirming no resolution occurred on October 1 itself. AP News confirms the shutdown began and outlines what happens 'now that a government shutdown is underway.' No contradictory evidence exists.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves NO. The U.S. government shut down at 12:01 AM ET on October 1, 2025, because Congress failed to pass any CR or appropriations bill that both chambers agreed on, and no such bill was signed by President Trump. The Senate voted on September 30, 2025 to reject both the Republican clean CR (which had passed the House on September 19) and the Democratic alternative — both failing the 60-vote cloture threshold. The condition for Yes was definitively foreclosed when the Senate's votes failed and the fiscal year deadline passed at midnight, causing the shutdown to commence. The definitively impossible moment is when the Senate votes failed and the shutdown began at 12:01 AM ET October 1, 2025 = 2025-10-01T04:01:00Z.

question: Taylor Swift holds top ten spots on the Billboard Hot 100 for the week of October 18th?
description:

subquestions.question: Will Taylor Swift's album "The Life of a Showgirl" debut at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart dated October 18, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A full top-10 sweep of the Billboard Hot 100 typically requires an unusually dominant album release week with very high U.S. streaming and sales across many tracks. Taylor Swift has shown this kind of chart power before: in November 2022 she became the first artist ever to occupy the entire Hot 100 top 10 with songs from "Midnights," and in 2024 she held the top 14 spots after the release of "The Tortured Poets Department". See Billboard's historical coverage of her 2022 sweep at https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/taylor-swift-entire-top-10-hot-100-midnights-1235166570/ and Billboard coverage of the 2024 top-14 feat at https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/taylor-swift-top-14-hot-100-tortured-poets-department-1235664225/ .

Swift's new album, "The Life of a Showgirl," is reported to be released on October 3, 2025, which places the first full tracking week squarely in the period relevant to the ultimate question. Multiple outlets reported unusually strong pre-release demand: Spotify said the album became the most pre-saved project ever on its countdown page, surpassing Swift's own prior record. See Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2025/09/03/taylor-swifts-new-album-makes-history-on-spotify----a-month-before-it-drops/ and Euronews: https://www.euronews.com/culture/2025/09/02/taylor-swift-already-breaks-spotify-record-before-release-of-new-album .

Current Billboard conditions also show meaningful competition rather than a guaranteed Swift takeover. Billboard's Hot 100 coverage for the week of October 4, 2025 shows non-Swift songs currently dominating the singles chart, including HUNTR/X's "Golden" at No. 1 and Alex Warren at No. 2, indicating Swift will need a very strong launch to displace entrenched hits. See Billboard's October 4 Hot 100 countdown summary: https://www.billboard.com/video/billboard-hot-100-top-10-countdown-for-october-4-2025-billboard-news/ . NPR also reported in late August that the "KPop Demon Hunters" soundtrack had four simultaneous Hot 100 top-10 hits, underscoring the strength of current competitors: https://www.npr.org/2025/08/27/nx-s1-5514880/kpop-demon-hunters-conan-gray-billboard-charts .

A No. 1 Billboard 200 debut for Swift's new album would be a strong early indicator that her release week is large enough to generate many high-charting tracks, which would increase the odds of a Hot 100 top-10 sweep on the following relevant chart week. It is not sufficient on its own, but it is a meaningful crux because a failure to debut at No. 1 would make a full Hot 100 top-10 takeover much less likely.

Sources:
- Billboard: Taylor Swift Makes History as First Artist Ever to Claim Entire Top 10 of Hot 100: https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/taylor-swift-entire-top-10-hot-100-midnights-1235166570/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Billboard publishes the Billboard 200 chart dated October 18, 2025, and "The Life of a Showgirl" by Taylor Swift is listed at No. 1 on that chart, with the qualifying publication/release of that chart occurring between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-11 (inclusive). Otherwise, it resolves No.

Primary resolution source: Billboard's Billboard 200 chart page at https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-200/ .

The resolver should use the chart page specifically labeled for the week of October 18, 2025. If Billboard's main chart page is difficult to navigate, archived or article coverage on Billboard.com explicitly stating the No. 1 album for the Billboard 200 dated October 18, 2025 may be used as a backup source, provided it is on Billboard.com. Example Billboard domain: https://www.billboard.com/ .

If Billboard does not publish the Billboard 200 chart dated October 18, 2025 by 2025-10-11, this question should be considered unresolvable rather than inferred from other sources. If the album title appears with minor stylization differences but is clearly the same Taylor Swift album, it counts. Deluxe, clean, or explicit variants count toward the same album entry if Billboard lists them under the same charting album entry.
subquestions.rationale: A No. 1 Billboard 200 debut is a strong signal that Swift's release week is powerful enough to drive massive track-level consumption across the album. Since a Hot 100 top-10 sweep requires many songs to chart extremely high simultaneously, album-level dominance is a useful early indicator and a meaningful crux distinct from simply asking about the Hot 100 outcome earlier.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Taylor Swift's 'The Life of a Showgirl' must be listed at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart specifically dated October 18, 2025. Billboard must publish this chart between October 1–11, 2025. Key entities: Taylor Swift, album title 'The Life of a Showgirl', Billboard 200 chart, chart date October 18, 2025. Observable evidence: Billboard.com or equivalent reliable coverage explicitly stating the album is No. 1 on the Billboard 200 dated October 18, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Taylor Swift The Life of a Showgirl album Billboard 200' (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-11) — to find general coverage. evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Billboard.com article from October 10, 2025 explicitly states 'The Life of a Showgirl is set to debut on the Billboard 200 on Oct. 18'; (2) Collider article from October 8, 2025 states the album 'debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200'; (3) Multiple sources from October 8–10, 2025 confirm 3.5 million equivalent album units for the debut tracking week (Oct 3–9), which maps to the Oct 18 chart date; (4) Forbes article from October 9, 2025 confirms Swift now has 14 No. 1 albums, with this being her most recent. One source (Rolling Stone Brasil) states a debut at No. 25 — this is clearly erroneous, contradicting all other sources including Billboard.com itself, and appears to be low-quality AI-generated content. Rejected: the Rolling Stone Brasil claim due to direct contradiction with Billboard.com's own reporting.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Billboard.com article from October 10, 2025 [Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/taylor-swift-the-fate-of-ophelia-record-start-radio-charts-1236086740/) explicitly states: 'The album The Life of a Showgirl is set to debut on the Billboard 200 on Oct. 18, with Hot 100 chart highlights expected on Oct. 13, and all charts updating on Oct. 14.' The Collider article from October 8, 2025 [Collider](https://collider.com/taylor-swift-life-of-a-showgirl-beatles-record/) explicitly states: 'Taylor Swift's twelfth studio album, The Life of a Showgirl, was released on October 8, 2025, and debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.' The Yahoo/Billboard article from October 10, 2025 [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/music/articles/taylor-swift-life-showgirl-breaks-183000823.html) states: 'Final figures...will determine the album's debut on the Billboard 200 chart (dated October 18).' Multiple sources confirm 3.5 million equivalent album units — an unprecedented figure that makes No. 1 certain. The criteria requires the chart to be published between October 1–11; Billboard typically releases charts about a week ahead of chart date, and the October 10 Billboard article is anticipating the October 18 chart, consistent with standard practice.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Billboard.com article confirming the album 'is set to debut on the Billboard 200 on Oct. 18' was published on October 10, 2025. The Collider article explicitly stating it 'debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200' was published on October 8, 2025. The Yahoo/Billboard article was published October 10, 2025. All are within the resolution window (October 1–11, 2025). The formal chart publication by Billboard would occur around October 11, 2025 (Friday), which is within the resolution window per standard Billboard chart publication practice.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: There is no earlier qualifying event — the chart dated October 18, 2025 is the debut chart for 'The Life of a Showgirl,' which was released October 3, 2025. The tracking week for the October 18 chart was October 3–9, 2025. No earlier Billboard 200 chart could show this album at No. 1 for this specific chart date.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: One source (Rolling Stone Brasil, October 8, 2025) claims the album 'debuted at number 25 on the Billboard 200 chart, earning 200,000 equivalent album units.' This directly contradicts: (a) Billboard.com's own reporting of 3.5 million equivalent album units, (b) the Collider article stating No. 1 debut, (c) the Forbes article confirming 14 No. 1 albums for Swift, and (d) universal coverage of record-breaking 3.5M unit sales. The Rolling Stone Brasil claim appears to be AI hallucination or error within that article — it's internally inconsistent (claiming record-breaking streams but only 200K units). This single outlier source is rejected in favor of the consensus of high-quality sources including Billboard.com itself. All other evidence strongly and consistently confirms No. 1 debut on the Billboard 200 dated October 18, 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is clear and explicit: Taylor Swift's 'The Life of a Showgirl' debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart dated October 18, 2025. This is confirmed by: (1) Billboard.com itself (October 10, 2025) stating the album 'is set to debut on the Billboard 200 on Oct. 18'; (2) Collider (October 8, 2025) explicitly stating the album 'debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200'; (3) Forbes (October 9, 2025) confirming Swift's 14th No. 1 album; (4) record-breaking 3.5 million equivalent units making any chart position other than No. 1 impossible. The chart was published within the required window (October 1–11, 2025). Resolution: YES.

question: Will Michael Jackson be named in newly released Epstein files?

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Justice or FBI publicly release a searchable/downloadable tranche of previously unreleased Jeffrey Epstein investigative records totaling at least 1,000 pages between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-17?
subquestions.background_information:
A major near-term driver of whether any specific person is newly named in Epstein files is whether there is a substantial federal release at all before the ultimate market closes. Multiple late-November reports say the Epstein Files Transparency Act requires the Justice Department to release unclassified Epstein-related materials by December 19, 2025, including FBI reports, witness interview transcripts, flight logs, travel records, and internal communications, in a searchable and downloadable format. See PBS (2025-11-21): https://www.pbs.org/ and Global News (2025-11-21): https://globalnews.ca/ . The law was reportedly signed in November 2025 and gives the DOJ 30 days to comply, implying a deadline very close to the ultimate question’s end date. The same reports note that tens of thousands of pages had already become public through lawsuits, FOIA, court dockets, and estate disclosures, so the key uncertainty is whether the federal government releases genuinely new material rather than merely republishing old material. PBS notes that the release may still face delays due to active-investigation claims or other withholding grounds: https://www.pbs.org/ . Chicago Tribune similarly reports that the DOJ is under a legal obligation to release unclassified materials by December 19, 2025, but may withhold some files tied to ongoing investigations or classified matters: https://www.chicagotribune.com/ . Because the ultimate question hinges on Michael Jackson being named in newly released files, the existence of a sizable, genuinely new federal tranche before mid-December is a strong indicator: without such a release, the chance of any newly surfaced mention is much lower; with such a release, the chance rises materially.

Sources:
PBS, "7 things to know about the Justice Department's Epstein files" — https://www.pbs.org/
Global News, "The Epstein files: What to know ahead of their release" — https://globalnews.ca/
Chicago Tribune, "What to know about the Justice Department's Jeffrey Epstein files" — https://www.chicagotribune.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-17 inclusive, the U.S. Department of Justice or the Federal Bureau of Investigation publicly posts or officially distributes a set of Jeffrey Epstein-related records that satisfy all of the following: (1) the records are described by the releasing agency or by a consensus of credible reporting as previously unreleased or newly released to the public; (2) the release is publicly accessible online in searchable and/or downloadable form; and (3) the release totals at least 1,000 pages of documents, as stated by the agency or by credible reporting. It resolves No otherwise.

For this subquestion, 'previously unreleased' excludes releases that are merely mirrors, repostings, reformatting, de-redactions of already public documents, or compilations of materials already publicly available before 2025-11-30. If the tranche mixes old and new material, it counts only if credible reporting or agency statements indicate that the tranche includes previously unreleased records and the tranche as released totals at least 1,000 pages.

Primary resolution sources: official DOJ and FBI websites/newsrooms, including https://www.justice.gov/ and https://www.fbi.gov/ . Secondary sources: Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ , AP https://apnews.com/ , PBS https://www.pbs.org/ , and major U.S. newspapers of record. If page count is disputed, the resolver should use the lowest figure supported by the official release materials or the consensus of the most authoritative credible reporting. If no clear page count is available, the question should resolve based on whether the released files are explicitly characterized by official sources or consensus reporting as totaling at least 1,000 pages. If an announced release is postponed beyond 2025-12-17, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This is not a restatement of whether Michael Jackson is named. Instead, it tracks the key upstream bottleneck: whether a substantial new federal disclosure actually happens in time. A large new release would significantly increase the probability that additional names—including Michael Jackson—surface in novel material.

question: U.S. Government funding lapse on October 1?

subquestions.question: Will all 12 regular FY2026 appropriations bills still not have passed both chambers of Congress by 2025-09-20?
subquestions.background_information:
A failure to complete the regular appropriations process by late September is a strong indicator that Congress will need a continuing resolution (CR) or face a funding lapse on October 1. Recent reporting indicates Congress is far behind the normal schedule. As of late August, Democrats wrote that the Senate had passed only three regular appropriations bills and the House only two, while warning that bipartisan negotiations had not yet been meaningfully launched https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5473560-schumer-jeffries-call-on-gop-leaders-to-meet-to-avoid-government-shutdown/ . Other coverage similarly states that the House had passed only a handful of bills and the Senate only a minibus before recess, with the chambers still needing to reconcile differences before sending anything to the president https://www.thecentersquare.com/national/article_0e62c4f0-86f9-11f0-bf5f-7f2b3bb0a8b4.html . Analysts and lawmakers have publicly expressed skepticism that all appropriations can be enacted before September 30, making a stopgap CR the most likely path and raising shutdown risk if that CR fails https://talkbusiness.net/2025/07/womack-sees-potential-for-government-shutdown/ ; https://www.notus.org/congress/appropriations-rescissions-bill-government-funding-process .

This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it asks about legislative progress on regular appropriations by September 20, an earlier procedural indicator that meaningfully bears on whether a funding lapse becomes likely by October 1. If by September 20 all 12 bills still have not passed both chambers, Congress would have little time left to conference bills, pass a CR, and obtain presidential signature.
