No ISW map evidence, DeepState evidence, or credible reporting confirms Russian-controlled territory touching Myrnohrad's eastern administrative boundary during September 1-28, 2025. Resolution: No.

question: Will Ghislaine Maxwell testify before Congress in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Ghislaine Maxwell provides live or recorded testimony before either chamber of the United States Congress (House of Representatives or Senate), or any of their official committees or subcommittees by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform publicly state by 2025-10-31 that it has scheduled, re-scheduled, or is actively negotiating a specific date for Ghislaine Maxwell's deposition or interview?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful near-term indicator for whether Maxwell will ultimately testify before Congress in 2025 because the main obstacle appears to be procedural and legal negotiation rather than simple congressional interest. In July 2025, the House Oversight Committee moved to subpoena Maxwell regarding Jeffrey Epstein-related matters, and reporting indicated a deposition had at one point been contemplated for August 11, 2025. However, Maxwell's attorneys said she would testify only if several conditions were met, including immunity, advance access to questions, and timing after the resolution of her Supreme Court petition; they also said that absent those concessions she would invoke the Fifth Amendment. CNN reported that the committee rejected immunity, while Maxwell's lawyer said they remained open to finding a path forward. These facts suggest that a concrete public update from the committee in October 2025 that a date is being set or negotiated would be meaningful evidence that talks have advanced beyond the July standoff and therefore would raise the odds of actual testimony before the end of 2025. See CNN's reporting on Maxwell's conditions and the committee's rejection of immunity: https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/29/politics/ghislaine-maxwell-testify-congress-immunity ; and Yahoo/AFP on the subpoena push and broader congressional effort: https://www.yahoo.com/news/us-congress-subpoena-ghislaine-maxwell-2025-07-22.html . Additional contemporaneous reporting indicated the committee had subpoenaed Maxwell for an August 11 deposition and that her counsel was still seeking concessions: https://www.politico.com/ (as quoted in secondary coverage summarized at https://boingboing.net/2025/07/29/sex-trafficker-ghislaine-maxwell-wants-new-conditions-met-before-shell-testify-to-congress.html ).

Sources:
CNN Politics - Maxwell offers to testify before Congress but with major conditions, including immunity - https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/29/politics/ghislaine-maxwell-testify-congress-immunity
Yahoo News / AFP - US Congress will subpoena Ghislaine Maxwell to testify about Jeffrey Epstein amid political firestorm - https://www.yahoo.com/news/us-congress-subpoena-ghislaine-maxwell-2025-07-22.html
Boing Boing summary citing Politico - Sex trafficker Ghislaine Maxwell wants new conditions met before she'll testify to Congress - https://boingboing.net/2025/07/29/sex-trafficker-ghislaine-maxwell-wants-new-conditions-met-before-shell-testify-to-congress.html
House Oversight Committee official site - https://oversight.house.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (or its official chair, ranking member, official spokesperson, or official website/social-media account) publicly states that: (a) a specific date has been scheduled or re-scheduled for Ghislaine Maxwell's deposition, interview, or testimony before the committee or a subcommittee; or (b) the committee and Maxwell/her counsel are actively negotiating or finalizing a specific date for such a deposition, interview, or testimony.

This question resolves No if no such public statement is made between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive.

Qualifying statements must be attributable to an official committee source or be reported by at least one credible outlet quoting an on-record committee spokesperson or member acting in an official capacity. General statements that the committee still wants testimony, without mention of scheduling, re-scheduling, or active date-setting negotiations, do not qualify. Mere repetition in October of a previously announced August plan does not qualify unless the October statement makes clear that a date is currently scheduled, being re-scheduled, or actively negotiated during the resolution window.

Primary resolution sources: the House Oversight Committee official website https://oversight.house.gov/ and official X account https://x.com/GOPoversight . Secondary sources, if needed, include credible reporting such as CNN https://www.cnn.com/politics , NBC News https://www.nbcnews.com/politics , The Hill https://thehill.com/homenews/house/ , Politico https://www.politico.com/ , and Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ . If no primary-source statement is available but multiple credible reports consistently quote an official committee source on the record, those reports may be used. If reporting is contradictory and no consensus can be established, the question should be considered unresolved rather than forced to Yes or No.
subquestions.rationale: A public October update that a date is scheduled or actively being negotiated would be a strong operational signal that the congressional process is moving toward actual testimony. It is not the same as asking whether Maxwell testifies; instead, it measures whether the stalled subpoena/negotiation process has materially advanced.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: An official House Oversight Committee source publicly states that (a) a specific date has been scheduled/re-scheduled for Maxwell's deposition/interview, OR (b) the committee and Maxwell's counsel are actively negotiating/finalizing a specific date for such proceedings. Timing window: 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-31 inclusive. Key entities: Chairman James Comer, Ranking Member (Garcia or Raskin per reports), official committee spokesperson, official website/social media. The condition requires explicit mention of scheduling, re-scheduling, or active date-setting negotiations — not merely general expressions of intent to obtain testimony.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'House Oversight Committee Ghislaine Maxwell deposition interview 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find core reporting on committee actions; 2. 'Ghislaine Maxwell Congress testimony scheduled date October 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find any announcement of a specific date; 3. 'House Oversight Committee Maxwell deposition date scheduled October 2025' (Oct 10-31) — to find post-SCOTUS scheduling news; 4. 'Comer Maxwell deposition negotiating specific date testimony 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find evidence of active date negotiation; 5. 'Maxwell deposition date scheduled committee spokesperson statement October 2025' (Oct 10-31) — to find specific spokesperson statements; 6. 'House Oversight Epstein Maxwell testimony update November 2025' (Oct 15-31) — to find late-October updates; 7. 'Comer Epstein Maxwell hearing date set scheduled late October 2025' (Oct 20-31) — specifically for late-October scheduling announcements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Washington Examiner (Oct 10, 2025): Committee spokesperson confirmed staff reached out to Maxwell's attorneys 'soon after' SCOTUS decision and 'expected to provide an update soon.' This is an official committee spokesperson statement about contact/outreach but does NOT confirm active date negotiation or scheduling of a specific date. REJECTED — does not meet the specific threshold of scheduled date or active date-setting negotiation. (2) Forbes (Oct 9, 2025): Committee stated it will provide an update 'soon' on whether Maxwell will appear. REJECTED — no specific date mentioned, no active negotiation confirmed. (3) Raw Story (Oct 9, 2025): Reports the August 11 deposition was 'paused,' awaiting SCOTUS decision. REJECTED — no new date set or negotiated. (4) ukrainetoday.org (Oct 17): Government shutdown halted investigation; DOJ not responding to subpoenas. Complicating factor suggesting no active scheduling occurred. (5) No late-October reports (Fox News Oct 23, Mediaite Oct 28) mention any Maxwell deposition date scheduled or actively negotiated. All rejected for lack of specific date or active negotiation language.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The closest qualifying statement comes from [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/house/3845304/oversight-committee-ghislaine-maxwell-testify/) (Oct 10, 2025), citing a Comer spokesperson: staff 'reached out soon after' the SCOTUS decision and 'expected to provide an update soon.' This is an official committee spokesperson statement. However, the resolution criteria explicitly requires either (a) a specific date scheduled/re-scheduled, or (b) active negotiation/finalizing of a specific date. The statement confirms only that initial outreach was made — not that a specific date was scheduled, re-scheduled, or actively being negotiated. The [Forbes article](https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2025/10/09/will-ghislaine-maxwell-speak-with-congress-supreme-court-rejection-clears-way-for-her-to-testify/) similarly indicates only that the committee would provide an update 'soon.' No source within the window reports a specific date being set or confirmed active date-setting negotiations. The criteria's explicit exclusion of 'general statements that the committee still wants testimony, without mention of scheduling, re-scheduling, or active date-setting negotiations' applies directly here.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with an exact timestamp was found within the window. The closest action (committee outreach to Maxwell's attorneys after Oct 7 SCOTUS ruling) is reported by Washington Examiner on Oct 10, 2025, but does not constitute a qualifying statement under the resolution criteria (no specific date scheduled or actively negotiated).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (specific date scheduled/re-scheduled, or active date-setting negotiation publicly stated) was found at any point in the October 2025 window. The search comprehensively covered Oct 1-31 with multiple targeted queries.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: A government shutdown reported beginning October 1, 2025 (ukrainetoday.org, Oct 17) complicated DOJ-committee cooperation during the window. This supports the absence of active scheduling. The committee made initial contact with Maxwell's attorneys post-SCOTUS but no follow-up reports confirm scheduling of a specific date. Late-October reporting (Oct 23, Oct 28) focused on other aspects of the Epstein investigation without mention of Maxwell deposition scheduling. The Babylon Bee article (Oct 27) is satirical and not evidence. No credible source within the window reports a specific Maxwell deposition date being set, re-scheduled, or actively negotiated.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence shows the committee made initial contact/outreach to Maxwell's attorneys after the SCOTUS October 7 ruling, as confirmed by a Comer spokesperson (Washington Examiner, Oct 10). However, this does not satisfy the resolution criteria, which explicitly requires either a specific date scheduled/re-scheduled, or a public statement that the committee and Maxwell's counsel are actively negotiating or finalizing a specific date. The language 'reached out soon after' and 'expected to provide an update soon' constitutes general outreach, not active date negotiation. The government shutdown also hampered scheduling. No credible report within the October 2025 window confirms the required level of specificity (scheduled date or actively negotiated specific date). The question resolves No, with the window closing at 2025-10-31.

question: Nothing Ever Happens: US Strike Edition
description:

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Defense announce between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-05 that additional U.S. military forces or assets are being deployed to the U.S. Southern Command area of responsibility in response to the Venezuela operation?
subquestions.background_information:
A key near-term indicator for whether the U.S. could expand military action beyond Venezuela is whether Washington visibly reinforces the regional military posture. The ultimate market concerns possible U.S. strikes on Iran, Colombia, Mexico, or Cuba after the already-reported Venezuela strike. Following the January 2026 Venezuela operation, multiple reports say President Trump publicly threatened possible further military action involving Colombia, Mexico, and Cuba, and suggested readiness for additional strikes if Venezuelan authorities do not comply. See FXStreet (Jan. 5, 2026): https://www.fxstreet.com/news/dow-jones-futures-steady-ahead-of-us-ism-manufacturing-pmi-202601050933 and Newsquawk summaries via Zero Hedge (Jan. 5, 2026): https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/crude-falls-following-us-strike-venezuela-european-equity-futures-point-positive-open and https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/crude-benchmarks-trade-choppy-following-us-strike-venezuela-us-equity-futures-are

The Department of Defense regularly publicizes notable force posture changes through official releases and statements. U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) is the combatant command responsible for Latin America and the Caribbean, including Colombia, Venezuela, and Cuba: https://www.southcom.mil/About/ . A fresh deployment of naval, air, marine, or special-operations assets into SOUTHCOM after the Venezuela strike would be a concrete and observable escalation signal, more informative than rhetoric alone. Such deployments would not guarantee another strike, but they would materially increase the plausibility of one by improving readiness, logistics, and deterrence posture.

This is different from merely restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline: it tracks a military-preparatory step that should update forecasters on the probability of additional U.S. strikes in the region. It is grounded in current events because the reported Venezuela operation has already occurred and public threats against Colombia, Mexico, and Cuba have been reported in major market coverage on Jan. 4-5, 2026.

Sources:
- FXStreet, Dow Jones futures steady ahead of US ISM Manufacturing PMI: https://www.fxstreet.com/news/dow-jones-futures-steady-ahead-of-us-ism-manufacturing-pmi-202601050933
- Zero Hedge / Newsquawk, Crude falls following US strike on Venezuela: https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/crude-falls-following-us-strike-venezuela-european-equity-futures-point-positive-open
- Zero Hedge / Newsquawk, Crude benchmarks trade choppy following US strike on Venezuela: https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/crude-benchmarks-trade-choppy-following-us-strike-venezuela-us-equity-futures-are
- U.S. Southern Command, About SOUTHCOM: https://www.southcom.mil/About/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-05 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of Defense, a U.S. military service branch, or U.S. Southern Command publicly announces a new deployment, movement, or positioning of additional military forces or assets into the U.S. Southern Command area of responsibility explicitly connected to the Venezuela situation, regional deterrence, bordering states, counternarcotics pressure related to the crisis, or protection/contingency operations stemming from the January 2026 Venezuela operation.

Qualifying announcements include official press releases, statements, transcripts, or readouts on .mil or defense.gov websites that specify at least one additional asset or force package, such as naval vessels, combat aircraft, ISR aircraft, Marines, Army units, Special Operations forces, or air-defense/logistics enablers, being sent to or newly positioned within SOUTHCOM's area of responsibility. SOUTHCOM's AOR includes Latin America and the Caribbean; see https://www.southcom.mil/About/ .

The question resolves No if no such qualifying official announcement is published between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-05.

Clarifications:
- Routine previously scheduled exercises or rotations do not count unless the official announcement explicitly ties them to the Venezuela crisis or regional escalation after the January 2026 strike.
- Mere media speculation or unnamed-official reporting does not count without an official U.S. government announcement.
- Redeployments outside SOUTHCOM's area of responsibility do not count.
- If an announcement is first published within the window and later corrected, the corrected official record governs.
- If no authoritative official source remains available, fallback sources are archived official pages or contemporaneous Pentagon press briefings on https://www.defense.gov/ and official SOUTHCOM releases on https://www.southcom.mil/Newsroom/ .

Primary resolution sources:
- U.S. Department of Defense news: https://www.defense.gov/News/
- DoD Releases: https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/
- U.S. Southern Command newsroom: https://www.southcom.mil/Newsroom/
- U.S. Southern Command about page (for AOR definition): https://www.southcom.mil/About/
subquestions.rationale: Additional force deployments into SOUTHCOM would be an observable preparatory move that should meaningfully raise the odds of further U.S. military action against Colombia or Cuba and, more broadly, indicate a willingness to continue regional coercive operations after Venezuela.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official U.S. DoD/military/SOUTHCOM announcement between Jan 6–Feb 5, 2026, of NEW/ADDITIONAL military forces or assets being deployed TO SOUTHCOM's AOR explicitly connected to Venezuela situation, regional deterrence, counternarcotics related to crisis, or contingency operations from January 2026 Venezuela operation. The announcement must specify at least one additional asset/force package (naval vessels, aircraft, Marines, Army, SOF, air defense) being SENT TO or NEWLY POSITIONED within SOUTHCOM's AOR.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US military deployment SOUTHCOM Venezuela 2026' — to find general deployment news; 2) 'Venezuela military operation US strike January 2026' — to find context; 3) 'Pentagon DoD announcement SOUTHCOM additional forces deployment Caribbean Venezuela January 2026' — to find qualifying official announcements; 4) 'US Navy warships aircraft carrier SOUTHCOM Caribbean deployment announcement 2026' — to find naval asset announcements; 5) 'Operation Southern Spear USS Gerald Ford additional assets SOUTHCOM January 2026' — for specific operation news; 6) 'US military forces withdrawal reduction Caribbean Venezuela after January operation 2026' — to find counter-evidence; 7) 'SOUTHCOM official announcement new forces deployment January February 2026' — to find official releases
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) DVIDS Jan 9 release: Marines/Sailors from USS Gerald R. Ford seized tanker Olina — official SOUTHCOM publication confirming Venezuela-related operations, but this involves EXISTING forces, not new additions. (B) DVIDS Jan 15 release: Operation Southern Spear seizure of Veronica — same, existing forces. (C) DVIDS Jan 20 release: Operation Southern Spear seizure of Sagitta — same. (D) Jan 12 SOUTHCOM/News18: USS Gerald R. Ford and ARG 'remain deployed' — explicitly continuation of existing. (E) Jan 30 Aviationist: F-35As that were in Puerto Rico for Venezuela moving AWAY from SOUTHCOM to Atlantic/CENTCOM — counter-evidence. (F) Jan 12 aerotechnews: 'some US military assets departed the Caribbean' after Operation Absolute Resolve — counter-evidence. (G) Jan 19 Washington Examiner: Admiral Daryl Caudle 'expressed concern about extending USS Gerald R. Ford from the Caribbean' — continuation, not addition. REJECTED: The DVIDS/SOUTHCOM announcements confirm operations but do not announce NEW/ADDITIONAL forces being sent to SOUTHCOM AOR. All represent continuation of pre-existing deployments ordered in late 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require an announcement specifying forces/assets 'being SENT TO or NEWLY POSITIONED within SOUTHCOM's AOR.' The evidence shows: (1) USS Gerald R. Ford CSG (deployed to SOUTHCOM Oct 2025) and Iwo Jima ARG continue operations under SOUTHCOM — EXISTING, not new [News18, Jan 12](https://www.news18.com/world/us-deploys-its-largest-aircraft-carrier-in-western-hemisphere-amid-venezuela-pressure-ws-l-9826311.html). (2) Some assets DEPARTED the Caribbean after Operation Absolute Resolve [aerotechnews, Jan 12](https://www.aerotechnews.com/blog/2026/01/12/headlines-january-12-3/). (3) F-35As from Puerto Rico moved toward Atlantic/CENTCOM [Aviationist, Jan 30](https://theaviationist.com/2026/01/30/f-35as-puerto-rico-moving-across-the-atlantic/). (4) USS Abraham Lincoln redirected FROM Caribbean/Pacific TO Middle East (CENTCOM), not SOUTHCOM [Forbes, Jan 15](https://www.forbes.com/sites/petersuciu/2026/01/15/us-navy-supercarrier-uss-abraham-lincoln-heading-to-the-middle-east/). (5) Rubio stated Jan 28 'no current plans to use military force in Venezuela' and only a Marine security detail at embassy [Fox News, Jan 28](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/rubio-says-us-has-no-plan-use-force-venezuela-warns-imminent-threat-could-change). No qualifying announcement of NEW/ADDITIONAL forces being sent TO SOUTHCOM AOR found within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with exact timestamp found. The continuation of existing forces (USS Gerald R. Ford, Iwo Jima ARG) in SOUTHCOM has official DVIDS releases dated Jan 9, 15, 20, but these do not announce NEW deployments. The overall trajectory shows assets redeploying OUT of SOUTHCOM to CENTCOM for Iran tensions.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence of a NEW/ADDITIONAL force deployment announcement to SOUTHCOM explicitly connected to Venezuela was identified. The January 3, 2026 operation (Operation Absolute Resolve) occurred BEFORE the resolution window. All forces documented within the window are continuations of pre-existing deployments.
evidence.step7_verification: Counter-check: Could the Operation Southern Spear DVIDS releases count? The releases describe existing forces conducting operations in SOUTHCOM AOR tied to Venezuela — but they are not announcing NEW/ADDITIONAL forces. The question requires forces 'being SENT TO or NEWLY POSITIONED.' The USNI Fleet Tracker (Jan 26) shows Iwo Jima ARG still in Caribbean under SOUTHCOM, and Gerald R. Ford under SOUTHCOM — but these were pre-existing. Defense Secretary Hegseth on Jan 7 stated the presence was 'not a new cost' since troops were already deployed. This directly contradicts any reading that these were new deployments within the window. The post-operation strategic shift was toward the Middle East (CENTCOM). The Jan 22, 2026 Congressional War Powers resolution (which narrowly failed) was aimed at preventing further military action in Venezuela, with Republicans arguing 'no U.S. troops are currently on the ground in Venezuela' — consistent with no new SOUTHCOM deployments being announced.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly shows: (1) The massive U.S. military buildup in SOUTHCOM was ordered in late 2025 and executed for the Jan 3, 2026 Operation Absolute Resolve — BEFORE the resolution window. (2) Within the window (Jan 6–Feb 5), the official DoD/SOUTHCOM narrative was continuation/persistence of existing forces, not new additions. (3) Multiple sources confirm post-operation redeployment of some assets OUT of SOUTHCOM (F-35As to Atlantic, Abraham Lincoln to CENTCOM). (4) No official U.S. government announcement of NEW/ADDITIONAL forces being sent TO SOUTHCOM AOR explicitly connected to Venezuela was found. The resolution criteria are not met. Resolution: No.

question: Nikita Bier out as Head of Product at X by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Nikita Bier ceases to be Head of Product of X for any length of time between October 14, and December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of Nikita Bier's resignation/firing before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/firing goes into effect.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from X and/or Nikita Bier, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will X publicly announce or launch a new user-facing core product feature primarily associated with Nikita Bier between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14?
subquestions.background_information:
Nikita Bier was announced as X's Head of Product at the end of June / start of July 2025, with coverage emphasizing that he was brought in to revamp product and improve engagement. TechCrunch reported on 2025-07-01 that Bier joined X as Head of Product and planned to help create more personalized timelines using Grok, while Elon Musk publicly welcomed him to X. https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/01/nikita-bier-joins-x-as-head-of-product-ive-officially-posted-my-way-to-the-top/ Business Insider reported on 2025-09-05 that Bier was still publicly acting as X's product head and giving detailed advice about how X's recommendation system promotes users, indicating active involvement in product strategy as of early September 2025. https://www.businessinsider.com/x-product-head-nikita-bier-playbook-getting-rich-posting-2025-9

This makes near-term evidence of continued product execution a meaningful indicator for whether Bier is likely to remain in role through the end of 2025. A visible launch or official announcement of a new user-facing feature tied to Bier would suggest organizational support, continued authority, and active tenure; the absence of such evidence would be weaker, but a launch would be a strong positive signal against near-term departure. The threshold is framed around a "new user-facing core product feature" rather than generic posting, because X staff frequently post informal ideas, and many posts would not indicate meaningful retained authority. Requiring public launch/announcement and a clear association with Bier aims to capture substantive product leadership.

Sources:
TechCrunch — Nikita Bier joins X as Head of Product: https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/01/nikita-bier-joins-x-as-head-of-product-ive-officially-posted-my-way-to-the-top/
Business Insider — X's head of product says this is the playbook for getting rich by posting: https://www.businessinsider.com/x-product-head-nikita-bier-playbook-getting-rich-posting-2025-9
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 inclusive, X publicly announces or launches at least one new user-facing core product feature and the public announcement materially associates the feature with Nikita Bier.

For this question:
- "Publicly announces or launches" means the feature is described in an official X source (such as an @X, @XEng, @Support, @Safety, @elonmusk, or Nikita Bier account post), an official X blog/newsroom post, or a credible media report quoting X or Bier directly.
- "New user-facing core product feature" means a feature available to, or explicitly planned for, X users on the main platform/app/web product (examples: timeline/recommendation changes, posting/reply/DM/community/creator/discovery/profile features, Grok integration into the X product). It does not include purely backend changes, policy-only changes, staffing announcements, moderation statistics, bug fixes, or marketing copy without a specific feature.
- "Materially associates" means the official announcement or quoted report explicitly attributes the feature to Bier's leadership, e.g. by naming him as announcing it, describing it as his initiative, or quoting him explaining the launch.

Primary sources for resolution will be official X communications and Nikita Bier's public posts, including https://x.com/nikitabier , https://blog.x.com/ , and official X platform accounts if available. Secondary sources may include TechCrunch, Business Insider, or similar credible reporting if they quote X/Bier directly.

This question resolves No if no qualifying announcement or launch occurs between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 inclusive.

If an announcement is made within the window but is clearly embargoed, retracted, or shown to be fake, it does not count. If evidence is ambiguous, resolution should favor official X-authored materials over third-party characterization. If no relevant official pages remain accessible at resolution time, archived copies plus consensus of credible reporting may be used as fallback.
subquestions.rationale: A publicly launched or announced feature tied to Bier would be evidence that he retains real product authority and internal backing, making his exit by 2025-12-31 less likely. It is a different observable event from the ultimate question and serves as an early operational indicator rather than a restatement of whether he leaves.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14, X publicly announces or launches at least one new user-facing core product feature where the official announcement materially associates the feature with Nikita Bier. Observable evidence: official X post by Bier, or credible media report directly quoting/attributing the feature to Bier's leadership. Key entities: Nikita Bier (X Head of Product), X platform. Timing: October 15 – November 14, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Nikita Bier X Twitter product feature launch 2025' (Oct 15–Nov 14) — to find any feature launches. 2. 'Nikita Bier X platform announcement feature' (Oct 15–Nov 14) — to find all feature announcements. 3. 'Nikita Bier X transparency profile feature country origin announcement October 15 2025' — to confirm earliest event. 4. 'X Bangers account feature Nikita Bier November 2025' — to check November features.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Oct 15: 'About this account' / transparency profile feature — Bier announced profile transparency feature (country of origin, join date, username history, access method) in a post on Oct 15, 2025. Reported by TheRegister, TechCrunch, Mashable, India Today, MediaPost, all on Oct 15. (B) Oct 17: 'X Links' teaser — Bier confirmed X Links feature coming soon. (C) Oct 19-20: iOS in-app browser link engagement feature — Bier announced new way to display links, collapsing post to bottom of screen while browsing. Reported by LatestLY, Fast Company, Digital Trends, Social Media Today. (D) Nov 9-12: 'Bangers'/'Certified Bangers' badge — Bier announced/launched feature awarding top posts. None rejected — all directly attributed to Bier as head of product.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Event A (Oct 15): The Register explicitly states 'Nikita Bier, X Head of Product, announced the feature in a post on October 15, 2025' — new user-facing profile feature (displaying country, join date, username changes, access method on profiles). This is a user-facing core product feature (profile display changes), publicly announced by Bier directly, reported by [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/15/x-plans-to-show-more-information-about-user-profiles-to-help-improve-trust/), [TheRegister](https://www.theregister.com/2025/10/15/twitter_x_bot_show_user_info/), [Mashable](https://mashable.com/article/elon-musk-x-new-user-information-testing-location-data), [India Today](https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/x-to-reveal-your-location-and-username-history-to-curb-fake-engagement-online-2803500-2025-10-15). The feature is materially associated with Bier as he personally announced it. Criteria fully satisfied.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: TheRegister states 'Nikita Bier, X Head of Product, announced the feature in a post on October 15, 2025.' Multiple credible sources (TechCrunch, Mashable, India Today) published on October 15, 2025 confirming the announcement. One source (Cryptopolitan) suggests Bier announced it on Oct 14 but its publication date is Oct 15. TheRegister's explicit reference to 'October 15, 2025' as the announcement date from Bier's post is the most direct timestamp. Date: 2025-10-15 (within window).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The Oct 15, 2025 announcement is the first qualifying event within the window. The Engadget article (dated Oct 14) references this same announcement but the sources that most explicitly timestamp it as Bier's X post date it to Oct 15. The window begins Oct 15 so even if the post was made late Oct 14, the majority of credible reporting places the announcement on Oct 15. Regardless, later events (Oct 17, Oct 19-20, Nov 9-12) also qualify. No earlier qualifying event (before Oct 15) found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: One article (Cryptopolitan) mentions Bier 'announced the update on October 14, 2025' — this could place the announcement one day before the window opens. However, TheRegister specifically states the announcement was 'in a post on October 15, 2025,' and the vast majority of credible coverage (TechCrunch, Mashable, India Today, MediaPost) published on October 15. Even if the first qualifying announcement occurred on Oct 14 (outside the window), the Oct 19-20 iOS link feature and Nov 9-12 Certified Bangers feature are unambiguously within the window and directly attributed to Bier. No retraction or embargo found for any of these features.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Multiple qualifying events exist firmly within the window. At minimum: (1) Oct 15, 2025 — profile transparency 'About this account' feature announced by Bier (per TheRegister, TechCrunch, Mashable); (2) Oct 19-20, 2025 — iOS in-app browser link engagement feature announced by Bier (per Fast Company, Digital Trends, Social Media Today); (3) Nov 9-12, 2025 — 'Certified Bangers' badge feature launched by X with Bier credited (per Social Media Today, NDTV, Mint). All are new user-facing core product features with public announcements explicitly attributing them to Bier. Resolution: Yes.

subquestions.question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo publicly request a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03?
subquestions.background_information:
A public trade request by Giannis would be one of the clearest near-term indicators that he is more likely to be traded before the 2025-26 NBA trade deadline. Recent reporting indicates that Giannis and his agent Alex Saratsis have already begun discussions with the Bucks about his future, and multiple outlets have reported that a resolution—either recommitment or a trade request—could come in the coming weeks. ESPN reporting relayed by the New York Post said Giannis and his agent had started talks with Milwaukee about whether his best fit is staying or moving, with a resolution expected before the February 5, 2026 trade deadline: https://nypost.com/2025/12/03/sports/giannis-antetokounmpo-accelerates-bucks-trade-possibility-after-social-media-move/ . RealGM similarly summarized that talks with the Bucks had begun and that a trade request was a plausible outcome: https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/279123/Giannis-Antetokounmpo-Opens-Talks-With-Bucks-About-His-Future .

Milwaukee's poor start appears to be a key driver. The Times of India reported that the Bucks were 9-13 and that Giannis had removed much Bucks-related content from his social media, which fueled speculation about dissatisfaction: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/nba/top-stories/giannis-antetokounmpo-fuels-blockbuster-trade-speculations-after-erasing-milwaukee-bucks-from-his-social-media-profiles/articleshow/122987654.cms . Earlier season reporting also suggested that the team's early performance would heavily influence whether Giannis pushed for a move. Newsweek described the first quarter of the season as effectively make-or-break for Milwaukee with respect to Giannis's future: https://www.newsweek.com/sports/nba/bucks-have-giannis-antetokounmpo-concern-before-regular-season-1964768 . question: Will Amazon acquire Warner Bros. Discovery?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if it is announced that Warner Bros. Discovery will be, has been, or is being acquired by or merged with the listed entity by 11:59 PM ET on May 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If no merger or acquisition takes place by the specified date, this market will resolve to "No Acquisition by May 31, 2026".

An official announcement will qualify for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether the merger or acquisition is ultimately completed. 

Any merger or acquisition will qualify regardless of whether it regards Warner Bros Discovery's entire company or separate transactions for its Warner Bros. or Discovery Global businesses.

The primary resolution source for this market is official information from the listed individual and/or Warner Bros. Discovery; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Amazon be named in credible reporting as a participant in Warner Bros. Discovery's strategic review process by 2025-11-23?
subquestions.background_information:
Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) said on 2025-10-21 that it had begun a strategic review after receiving unsolicited interest from multiple parties, and that it was considering options including a sale of all or part of the company. Reporting also noted that WBD is being advised by Allen & Company, J.P. Morgan, and Evercore, indicating a live M&A process rather than mere market rumor. See Yahoo Finance's summary of the announcement: https://finance.yahoo.com/ and Cord Cutters News' recap of the company statement and advisers involved: https://cordcuttersnews.com/warner-bros-discovery-confirms-it-has-received-multiple-offers-to-buy-the-company/

WBD had previously announced a plan to split into two publicly traded companies in 2026, separating 'Streaming & Studios' from 'Global Networks.' That planned separation creates a near-term alternative to a full sale, so evidence that Amazon is specifically engaging with the process would meaningfully increase the odds of an Amazon-WBD transaction relative to the status quo. CNET covered the split plan here: https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/warner-bros-discovery-to-split-into-two-companies-by-2026/

Recent media reporting has already speculated that Amazon could be among logical buyers because of strategic fit with MGM and Prime Video, but this appears to be speculation rather than confirmed involvement. For example, Cord Cutters News reported that WBD was seeking interest from Amazon, Apple, and Netflix: https://cordcuttersnews.com/warner-bros-discovery-hopes-amazon-apple-or-netflix-will-buy-its-struggling-company/ . Motley Fool also discussed Amazon as a potential acquirer in market commentary: https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/10/12/warner-bros-discovery-too-late-to-catch-this-risin/

Because the ultimate question is whether Amazon acquires WBD, a strong early indicator is whether Amazon is reported as actually participating in the sale process, submitting or preparing an indication of interest, conducting diligence, or holding management talks. That is materially different from the final acquisition question itself, but would be a major update toward it.

Cord Cutters News - WBD confirms it has received multiple offers to buy the company: https://cordcuttersnews.com/warner-bros-discovery-confirms-it-has-received-multiple-offers-to-buy-the-company/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23 (inclusive), at least two of the following credible business/financial news organizations report that Amazon is participating in WBD's strategic review process: Reuters, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, CNBC, or The New York Times. 'Participating' means any of the following are explicitly reported: (a) Amazon has submitted a bid or indication of interest; (b) Amazon is in talks with WBD or its advisers about a possible acquisition or merger; (c) Amazon has been granted access to a data room or is conducting due diligence; or (d) Amazon has been invited into, or is actively engaged in, a formal sale or strategic-review process for WBD or a major WBD business unit relevant to the ultimate question.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying reporting appears by 2025-11-23.

Reporting that only says Amazon is a 'logical buyer,' is 'speculated to be interested,' or is named in generic lists of possible bidders without claiming active participation does not qualify. A single-source rumor repeated by many outlets does not count unless at least two qualifying outlets independently publish the claim as their own reporting or clearly attribute it to sufficiently specific sourcing.

Primary sources for resolution will be the websites/search archives of Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), The Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com/), Financial Times (https://www.ft.com/), CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/), and The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com/). If those are unavailable, archived versions or Factiva/Lexis reproductions of the same articles may be used. If qualifying reporting is first published within the window but later corrected to retract Amazon's participation before 2025-11-23, the corrected record will control and the question will resolve No unless other qualifying unretracted reporting remains.

If no qualifying report is published within the stated window, or if publication is delayed until after 2025-11-23, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: If Amazon is credibly reported to be actively participating in WBD's sale process, that is a direct near-term indicator that an Amazon-WBD acquisition has become live rather than merely speculative. It should substantially update forecasts on the ultimate question while remaining distinct from the acquisition event itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: At least two of Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, Financial Times, CNBC, or NYT must explicitly report (between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23) that Amazon is actively participating in WBD's strategic review — meaning Amazon has submitted a bid, is in talks, has data room access, or has been formally engaged. Reports only calling Amazon a 'logical buyer' or 'speculated to be interested' or listing it in generic lists of possible bidders do NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: (1) 'Amazon Warner Bros Discovery strategic review acquisition merger 2025', (2) 'Warner Bros Discovery WBD strategic review process bidders 2025', (3) 'Amazon bid Warner Bros Discovery data room due diligence formal process November 2025', (4) 'Amazon WBD Warner Bros Discovery indication of interest acquisition talks advisers', (5) 'Amazon MGM Warner Bros Discovery bid formal process Reuters Bloomberg WSJ CNBC', (6) 'Bloomberg Amazon Warner Bros Discovery acquisition bid interest November 2025', (7) 'Warner Bros Discovery bids submitted November 20 Amazon Apple excluded bidders'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Bloomberg reported ~Oct 24 that Netflix, Amazon, and Apple were considering acquiring parts/all of WBD — but secondary sources describe this as Amazon 'considering' or being interested, not actively participating. (2) Deadline (Nov 10) mentioned 'Amazon MGM exploring bids' alongside Netflix and Comcast. (3) Deadline (Nov 15) noted 'Amazon MGM has shown interest, though its current position remains unclear.' (4) Washington Examiner (Nov 20) stated 'Apple and Amazon were also reportedly interested but have not confirmed bids.' (5) On Nov 20-21, Bloomberg, NYT, CNBC, Bloomberg Law all reported only Paramount, Comcast, and Netflix submitted bids — Amazon was not among them. None of these constitute explicit reporting of Amazon's active participation from two qualifying outlets.

Amazon was consistently placed in the category of 'reportedly interested but have not confirmed bids.' The Deadline article mentioning 'Amazon MGM exploring bids' is vague, does not attribute to a qualifying outlet, and was not corroborated by any of the six qualifying outlets. The initial Bloomberg report about Netflix, Amazon, and Apple 'considering' WBD describes speculative interest, not active participation (no bid, no talks, no data room access attributed specifically to Amazon by Bloomberg itself).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying event occurred — no qualifying outlet explicitly reported Amazon's active participation in the WBD strategic review process during the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: N/A — no qualifying event found at all.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for any contradictory evidence suggesting Amazon DID actively participate: The Washington Examiner (Nov 20) said 'Apple and Amazon were also reportedly interested but have not confirmed bids.' The AMC CEO article (Deadline, Nov 6) said WBD is 'considering offers from Amazon MGM, Comcast, and Netflix' — but this is from Deadline, not a qualifying outlet, and appears to use 'considering offers from' loosely. The Deadline (Nov 15) article only said 'Amazon MGM has shown interest, though its current position remains unclear' — not a qualifying outlet and not confirming active participation. None of the six qualifying outlets (Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, CNBC, NYT) published reporting that Amazon submitted a bid, was in talks, had data room access, or was formally engaged as an active participant in WBD's strategic review process. The absence of Amazon from the list of actual bidders on November 20-21 (confirmed by Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ via secondary sources, NYT) further confirms Amazon was not actively participating as defined.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: No. The evidence clearly shows that while Amazon was frequently mentioned as a possible or speculative bidder/suitor, none of the six qualifying outlets (Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, CNBC, NYT) explicitly reported Amazon as actively participating in WBD's strategic review process as defined by the resolution criteria. The confirmed bidders who submitted formal non-binding bids by the November 20 deadline were Paramount Skydance, Comcast, and Netflix — not Amazon. Amazon is absent from the formal bidder lists confirmed by qualifying outlets. The resolution criteria's explicit exclusion of 'generic lists of possible bidders without claiming active participation' applies here. The question resolves No as of the end of the window (2025-11-23).

question: Will Italy win the third most gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the third most gold medals at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most gold medals won will use most overall medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most gold medals won, and Norway wins more overall medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the gold medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

Host nations often outperform their baseline due to home advantage, and Italy's ability to accumulate multiple early-to-mid Games golds is a meaningful indicator of whether it can contend for an unusually high final gold ranking such as third place. The provided news coverage suggests Italy is generally viewed as a longshot for topping the gold table, with pre-Games betting markets focusing on Norway, Germany, and the United States as the leading contenders; for example, Sportsbook Review summarized Kalshi market pricing with Norway, the U.S., and Germany as the only countries with double-digit implied chances to win the most gold medals, while Italy was listed far behind at around 2% for most golds. This makes an early milestone like reaching 3 golds by February 19 potentially informative: if Italy hits that threshold with several medal events still remaining before the Feb. 22 close, its chances of ending third in golds would rise materially relative to pre-Games expectations.
