question: Will Rodrigo Paz Pereira win by 15–20%?
description:
A second-round (runoff) vote for the Bolivia Presidential election is scheduled to take place on October 19, 2025 

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the 2025 Bolivian Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the 'margin of victory' is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first and second-place candidate. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the second round of the Bolivian Presidential Election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the results of the election aren’t known by March 31, 2026 ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve solely based on the first official vote count released by the Bolivian Government, specifically the Plurinational Electoral Body (Órgano Electoral Plurinacional, OEP) (https://www.oep.org.bo/).

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

subquestions.question: Will Samuel Doria Medina publicly endorse Rodrigo Paz Pereira for the runoff between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Rodrigo Paz Pereira led Bolivia's first-round presidential election with about 32.1% of the vote, while Jorge "Tuto" Quiroga received about 26.9%, sending both to the October 19, 2025 runoff. Third-place finisher Samuel Doria Medina won about 20% of the first-round vote, making his supporters one of the most important available vote pools for the runoff. Several reports published after the first round explicitly noted that Paz could benefit from a Doria Medina endorsement, making such an endorsement a plausible and informative near-term indicator for whether Paz will build a broad anti-MAS / centrist-right coalition large enough to win by a substantial margin. See AS/COA's post-election analysis noting that Paz "may get a boost in the runoff due to the endorsement of third-place finisher Samuel Doria Medina, who captured 20 percent of the vote" (https://www.as-coa.org/articles/three-things-know-about-bolivias-2025-first-round-election-results). CounterPunch likewise reported first-round shares of 32.1% for Paz, 26.9% for Quiroga, and 20% for Doria Medina (https://www.counterpunch.org/2025/08/22/bolivia-elections-restore-established-order-socialists-are-dismissed/). AFP also reported Paz's first-round total at 32.1% and described his surprise rise and runoff positioning (https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/latin-america/from-tiktok-to-frontrunner-inside-pazs-presidential-campaign-in-bolivia.phtml). Because the ultimate market is specifically about Paz winning by a large 15-20 point margin, coalition formation matters more than merely whether he remains competitive. A public endorsement by a candidate who just won roughly one-fifth of the vote would be evidence that elite and voter coordination are breaking toward Paz rather than Quiroga.

Sources:
AS/COA - Three Things to Know About Bolivia's 2025 First-Round Election Results - https://www.as-coa.org/articles/three-things-know-about-bolivias-2025-first-round-election-results
CounterPunch - Bolivia Elections Restore Established Order, Socialists are Dismissed - https://www.counterpunch.org/2025/08/22/bolivia-elections-restore-established-order-socialists-are-dismissed/
Buenos Aires Times / AFP - From TikTok to Frontrunner, inside Paz's presidential campaign in Bolivia - https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/latin-america/from-tiktok-to-frontrunner-inside-pazs-presidential-campaign-in-bolivia.phtml
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Samuel Doria Medina makes a clear public statement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) explicitly endorsing Rodrigo Paz Pereira for president in the 2025 Bolivian runoff. Qualifying statements include: (a) an endorsement published on Doria Medina's official website or official social media accounts; (b) an interview, press conference, or written statement reported by at least one major news outlet quoting him directly as endorsing Paz; or (c) a joint public event or signed communique in which Doria Medina explicitly calls for voting for Paz. 

This question resolves No if no such qualifying endorsement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

For resolution, preference should be given to primary sources from Samuel Doria Medina's official channels if available. Suggested primary sources include his official website and verified social media accounts. If primary sources are unavailable or ambiguous, use reporting from major outlets such as Reuters, AFP, AP, or AS/COA. An endorsement of a generic anti-Quiroga or anti-MAS position does not count unless Doria Medina explicitly endorses Rodrigo Paz Pereira by name or unmistakable reference as the candidate voters should support in the runoff. Mere rumors, unnamed-source reports, negotiations, or statements that he is "leaning toward" Paz do not count. An endorsement announced before 2025-09-01 does not count; it must occur within the window from 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01. If purported endorsement evidence only appears after 2025-10-01 but clearly documents a statement made within the window, it counts. If the available evidence remains genuinely contradictory or insufficient to determine whether an explicit endorsement occurred within the window, resolve based on the preponderance of authoritative evidence; if still indeterminate, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Proposed sources for resolution:
Samuel Doria Medina official site - https://samueldoriamedina.com/
Samuel Doria Medina on X - https://x.com/SamuelDoriaMed
AS/COA - https://www.as-coa.org/
Reuters World - https://www.reuters.com/world/
AP News Latin America - https://apnews.com/hub/latin-america
subquestions.rationale: Doria Medina's voters are the largest identifiable transferable bloc from the first round. A public endorsement for Paz would be a meaningful signal that center-right and anti-incumbent elites are consolidating behind him, which would increase the odds not just of a Paz win, but of a comfortable multi-point margin in the runoff. If instead Doria Medina stays neutral or backs Quiroga, that would weaken the case for Paz winning by as much as 15-20%.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Samuel Doria Medina makes a clear public statement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) explicitly endorsing Rodrigo Paz Pereira for president. Observable evidence: direct quote from Doria Medina endorsing Paz on his official channels or in major news reports, with a timestamp within the window. Key entities: Samuel Doria Medina, Rodrigo Paz Pereira, Bolivia runoff. Threshold: explicit endorsement (not rumors/leaning), within the time window only.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Samuel Doria Medina endorse Rodrigo Paz Pereira Bolivia runoff 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 1) — to find direct endorsement in window; 2) 'Bolivia segunda vuelta elecciones 2025 Doria Medina apoyo' (Sep 1–Oct 1) — Spanish-language sources; 3) 'Doria Medina apoyo endorsement Rodrigo Paz Bolivia octubre 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 1); 4) 'Bolivia runoff endorsements October 2025 Quiroga Paz coalition' (Sep 1–Oct 1); 5) 'Samuel Doria Medina Bolivia election 2025 support candidate' (Aug 1–Oct 1) — to find timing of endorsement; 6) 'Bolivia election August 18 2025 Doria Medina concedes endorses Paz second round' (Aug 18–Aug 31) — to verify the endorsement happened before the window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event identified: Doria Medina endorsed Paz on August 18, 2025 (election night). Multiple sources confirm this: AFP reported 'Doria Medina immediately threw his support behind Paz, citing the need for change'; Adnkronos reported 'Entrepreneur Samuel Doria Medina...has announced his support for Paz Pereira in the second round'; KPVI reported 'Millionaire businessman Samuel Doria Medina threw his support behind Paz, saying it was a vote for change'; AS/COA (Aug 19) references 'the endorsement of third-place finisher Samuel Doria Medina'. All of these are dated August 18-19, 2025, BEFORE the September 1 window opens. No evidence found of any repeat endorsement within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The endorsements found — [AFP August 18](https://afp.com/), [Adnkronos August 18](https://www.adnkronos.com/internazionale/akieng/bolivia-elections-there-will-be-a-runoff-challenge-between-rodrigo-paz-and-tuto-quiroga_44zMKQaP0EXCxNrALcsIzC), [AS/COA August 19](https://www.as-coa.org/articles/three-things-know-about-bolivias-2025-first-round-election-results) — satisfy criteria (a) and (b) of the resolution criteria in terms of form (direct quotes/reported statements from Doria Medina endorsing Paz by name), but they FAIL the temporal criterion: the resolution criteria explicitly states 'An endorsement announced before 2025-09-01 does not count.' These endorsements all occurred on August 17-18, 2025. No qualifying endorsement within the Sep 1–Oct 1 window was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The endorsement timestamp is August 18, 2025 (election night), as reported by multiple major outlets (AFP, Adnkronos, KPVI, AS/COA on Aug 19). This is before the window opens on 2025-09-01T00:00:00Z. No timestamp within the required window was found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first (and only found) qualifying endorsement occurred on August 18, 2025 — before the window. No earlier occurrence within the window exists because there is no occurrence within the window at all.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempts to find any subsequent, separate endorsement by Doria Medina within September 1–October 1, 2025 returned no results. The AS/COA article from August 19 notes the endorsement as already having occurred. No September or October news reports reference a new or reaffirmed endorsement by Doria Medina within the window. The evidence is consistent: the endorsement predates the question window. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Samuel Doria Medina did endorse Rodrigo Paz Pereira, but this endorsement occurred on August 18, 2025 — before the question's window of September 1–October 1, 2025. The resolution criteria explicitly disqualifies endorsements made before September 1, 2025. No evidence was found of a separate, qualifying endorsement within the required window. Therefore, the question resolves No. The window closed on October 1, 2025 without a qualifying event.

question: Will India strike Pakistan by Dec 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if India initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Pakistani territory by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Indian military forces that impact Pakistani territory (e.g., if an Indian missile or drone hits a target within Pakistan’s borders, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted before reaching Pakistani territory, as well as surface-to-air missile strikes, will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether debris lands on Pakistani soil or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or any operation conducted by Indian ground forces will not qualify as a strike under this market.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a Pakistan-based militant attack kill at least 5 people in India between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14?
subquestions.background_information:
A major near-term driver of renewed India-Pakistan escalation is the risk of another mass-casualty militant attack in India that New Delhi attributes to Pakistan-based groups. India’s 2025 Operation Sindoor was launched in response to the Pahalgam terror attack, and senior Indian leaders have continued to signal that India may strike again if provoked. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on 2025-11-07 that Operation Sindoor was launched against terrorist hideouts in Pakistan and that India would act again if needed; Prime Minister Modi similarly said the operation is not over and that India will act again if required (Firstpost, https://www.firstpost.com/india/we-didnt-kill-pakistani-citizens-rajnath-on-how-india-carried-operation-sindoor-13898466.html). Public Indian military commentary in October also emphasized that Pakistan had sought a ceasefire after suffering losses, while warning that future Pakistani actions would be met firmly (Moneycontrol, https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/india/indian-navy-had-sailed-into-arabian-sea-dgmo-lt-gen-rajiv-ghais-big-statement-on-operation-sindoor-13469659.html; ThePrint, https://theprint.in/defence/pakistan-alleges-india-trying-to-mould-history-by-inventing-outlandish-bollywood-style-scripts/2859670/).

Separately, security reporting suggests an elevated terrorism and infiltration threat. The Tribune reported on 2025-10-28 that Punjab police had seized an RPG launcher and that officials were warning of a rising terror threat linked to Pakistan-backed smuggling and drone drops; BSF recoveries in Punjab by 2025-10-23 reportedly included 215 drones, 180 weapons, and explosives (The Tribune, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/rpg-seizure-signals-rising-terror-threat-in-state/). A fresh deadly attack inside India, especially if credibly linked by Indian authorities to Pakistan-based militants, would be a strong indicator increasing the odds of an Indian cross-border aerial strike before year-end.

Sources:
Firstpost - 'We didn't kill Pakistani citizens': Rajnath on how India carried Operation Sindoor — https://www.firstpost.com/india/we-didnt-kill-pakistani-citizens-rajnath-on-how-india-carried-operation-sindoor-13898466.html
Moneycontrol - 'Indian Navy had sailed into Arabian Sea...': DGMO Lt Gen Rajiv Ghai's big statement on Operation Sindoor — https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/india/indian-navy-had-sailed-into-arabian-sea-dgmo-lt-gen-rajiv-ghais-big-statement-on-operation-sindoor-13469659.html
ThePrint - Pakistan alleges India trying to 'mould' history by 'inventing outlandish, Bollywood-style scripts' — https://theprint.in/defence/pakistan-alleges-india-trying-to-mould-history-by-inventing-outlandish-bollywood-style-scripts/2859670/
The Tribune - RPG seizure signals rising terror threat in state — https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/rpg-seizure-signals-rising-terror-threat-in-state/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 (inclusive), there is at least one militant attack on Indian territory that satisfies all of the following: (1) at least 5 people are reported killed; (2) the attack is publicly attributed by the Government of India, India’s Ministry of Home Affairs, India’s Ministry of Defence, Indian Army, National Investigation Agency, or a consensus of at least two major reputable news outlets to a Pakistan-based militant group, Pakistan-backed militants, or infiltrators entering from Pakistan; and (3) the deaths are directly caused by the attack itself, not solely by later security operations.

The question resolves No if no such attack occurs between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 (inclusive).

For casualty counts, use the highest officially confirmed death toll reported within 7 days of the attack by Indian authorities; if no official toll is available, use a consensus of Reuters, AP, BBC, or The Hindu. For attribution, priority is given to explicit statements by Indian authorities. If attribution remains materially disputed and no such official attribution or two-outlet consensus exists by 2025-12-21, the attack does not count.

If a qualifying attack begins within the window but casualty/attribution confirmation is delayed, it still counts so long as the attack itself occurred between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 inclusive. If source reporting is too contradictory to determine whether the threshold was met, resolve based on the preponderance of the listed authoritative sources; if still impossible, the market should be considered unresolvable.

Primary resolution sources: official releases from India’s Press Information Bureau (https://pib.gov.in/), Ministry of Home Affairs (https://www.mha.gov.in/), Ministry of Defence (https://mod.gov.in/), Indian Army public channels (https://indianarmy.nic.in/), and NIA (https://www.nia.gov.in/). Secondary sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news), and The Hindu (https://www.thehindu.com/).
subquestions.rationale: A mass-casualty militant attack in India that is linked to Pakistan-based actors is one of the clearest observable triggers that could prompt India to launch the kind of aerial strike described in the ultimate question. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question; rather, it tracks a key escalation trigger that would substantially update forecasts.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: (1) Attack on Indian territory between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 inclusive; (2) At least 5 people killed directly by the attack; (3) Attribution to Pakistan-based militant group by Indian authorities (GOI, MHA, MOD, Indian Army, NIA) or two-outlet consensus. Observable evidence: news reports and official statements confirming all three criteria.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Multiple searches conducted: 'Pakistan militant attack India killed 2025 November December'; 'terrorist attack India Kashmir casualties November December 2025'; 'Delhi Red Fort car blast November 10 2025 Pakistan NIA attribution'; 'Nowgam Srinagar police station blast November 14 2025'; 'Jammu Kashmir terrorist attack killed security forces November December 2025'; 'India militant attack 5 killed Pakistan-based group NIA attribution December 2025'; 'India attack Pakistan Jaish Lashkar Hizbul TRF killed November 15 December 2025'; 'India terror attack killed December 2025 militants'; 'India terrorist attack November December 2025 civilians killed 5 deaths'; 'Rajouri Poonch Kupwara attack killed India December 2025'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Delhi Red Fort blast on November 10, 2025 - killed 10-15, linked to JeM/Pakistan-based handlers. REJECTED: Occurred before the resolution window starts (Nov 14). (B) Nowgam police station blast on November 14, 2025 (~11:20 PM) - killed 9. REJECTED: Indian authorities (DGP, MHA) explicitly classified as accidental explosion while handling confiscated explosives, not a militant attack. Police rejected militant group's (PAFF) responsibility claim as 'patently false, baseless and mischievous.' Does not meet criterion (3) - not directly caused by a militant attack. (C) All other violent events found within window were in Pakistan, not on Indian territory.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event within the window (2025-11-14 to 2025-12-14) satisfies all three resolution criteria simultaneously. The Delhi blast meets criteria 2 and 3 but fails criterion 1 (timing). The Nowgam blast meets criteria 1 and 2 but fails criterion 3 (not an attack - accidental). No other events on Indian territory with 5+ deaths attributed to Pakistan-based militants were found in this period. BSF noted 120 terrorists at 69 launch pads but no successful qualifying attack was reported. Infiltration attempts in 2025 involved only 4 incidents with 13 infiltrators, 8 eliminated.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Nowgam accidental blast timestamp: 2025-11-14T23:20:00+05:30 (approximately 2025-11-14T17:50:00Z). Delhi blast: 2025-11-10T13:22:00Z (6:52 PM IST). Neither qualifies for resolution.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (attack on Indian territory, 5+ killed, Pakistan-based attribution) was found within the window. The first occurrence check is therefore moot - no qualifying event exists.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: PAFF (linked to JeM) claimed responsibility for Nowgam blast, but J&K police, DGP Nalin Prabhat, and MHA explicitly rejected this and confirmed it was accidental. Multiple authoritative sources (AFP, Reuters, The Hindu, Yahoo/Reuters) confirmed the accidental nature. The Red Fort blast was definitively before the window (Nov 10). No other qualifying attacks on Indian territory found. BSF reports indicate successful prevention of infiltration. NIA investigations continued but focused on the Nov 10 attack.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying event occurred within the resolution window of 2025-11-14 to 2025-12-14. The two major events near the window - the Delhi Red Fort blast (before window) and the Nowgam police station accidental explosion (within window but explicitly not a militant attack) - do not satisfy all resolution criteria. No other attacks on Indian territory resulting in 5+ deaths attributed to Pakistan-based militants were reported. The question resolves No.

question: Will Norway win the second most gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the second most gold medals at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most gold medals won will use most overall medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most gold medals won, and Norway wins more overall medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the gold medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

subquestions.question: Will Norway have won at least 4 gold medals in cross-country skiing and biathlon combined at the 2026 Winter Olympics by the end of 2026-02-19 UTC?
subquestions.background_information:
Norway's path to finishing near the top of the Winter Olympic gold table is heavily concentrated in Nordic endurance events, especially cross-country skiing and biathlon. Pre-Games coverage specifically noted that Norway was expected to rely heavily on biathlon and cross-country skiing for medals, with additional support from ski jumping and alpine events (Bleacher Report, 2026-02-05: https://bleacherreport.com/articles/medal-tally-olympics-2026-predictions-for-milano-cortinas-final-winter-medal-count). Norway was the clear pre-Games favorite to win the most gold medals overall, reflecting its recent dominance: 16 golds at Beijing 2022, 14 at PyeongChang 2018, and 11 at Sochi 2014 (Sports Illustrated, 2026-02-02: https://www.si.com/betting/odds-to-win-most-gold-medals-at-2026-winter-olympics; Olympics historical medal tables: https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/beijing-2022/medals and https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/pyeongchang-2018/medals). Because the ultimate question asks whether Norway will finish specifically second in golds, an early read on whether Norway is converting in its strongest disciplines is informative: a strong early gold haul in cross-country skiing and biathlon makes it more likely Norway finishes first or near-first, while a weak start increases the chances that countries such as the United States or Germany overtake or separate from Norway in the final gold ranking. The Milano Cortina 2026 program runs through February 22, with many Nordic events scheduled before the final weekend, making February 19 a meaningful checkpoint before the overall medal table is settled (Olympics schedule hub: https://olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/schedule).

Sources:
Bleacher Report - Medal Tally Olympics 2026 Predictions for Milano Cortina's Final Winter Medal Count - https://bleacherreport.com/articles/medal-tally-olympics-2026-predictions-for-milano-cortinas-final-winter-medal-count
Sports Illustrated - Odds to Win Most Gold Medals at 2026 Winter Olympics - https://www.si.com/betting/odds-to-win-most-gold-medals-at-2026-winter-olympics
Olympics Beijing 2022 medal table - https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/beijing-2022/medals
Olympics PyeongChang 2018 medal table - https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/pyeongchang-2018/medals
Milano Cortina 2026 schedule - https://olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/schedule
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Norway is officially credited with at least 4 gold medals in events classified by the official Olympics results/medal pages as cross-country skiing or biathlon, with those medals awarded between 2026-02-07 and 2026-02-19 inclusive, as shown on the official Milano Cortina 2026 results or medal pages at https://olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/results or the relevant sport pages on https://olympics.com/.

It resolves No if, by the end of 2026-02-19 UTC, Norway has fewer than 4 such gold medals awarded during that window.

Only medals awarded within the resolution window from 2026-02-07 through 2026-02-19 inclusive count. Medals awarded before 2026-02-07 or after 2026-02-19 do not count. Relay and team events count if the IOC/Olympics medal table credits the gold to Norway. Mixed-team events count only if the medal is officially credited to Norway in the national medal table. If an event is delayed beyond 2026-02-19 UTC, it does not count toward resolution. If an event is completed within the window but the official Olympics site has not yet updated the medal attribution by the resolution time, the resolver should wait for the official update; if no official update is available within 7 days, use the official IOC/Olympics results PDF or archived results pages as fallback.

Primary source: official Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics results pages, including the medal table and sport-specific results pages: https://olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/results
Fallback source: official Olympics main site results and medal pages: https://olympics.com/
Additional fallback if needed: IOC official site: https://www.olympics.com/ioc
subquestions.rationale: This is a strong crux because Norway's gold-medal ceiling depends heavily on its core Nordic sports. If Norway underperforms in cross-country skiing and biathlon by February 19, its chance of finishing second rather than first or third changes materially. Conversely, a strong early haul in these sports is evidence that Norway may remain too strong for the 'second-most-golds' outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Norway officially credited with at least 4 gold medals in cross-country skiing or biathlon events between 2026-02-07 and 2026-02-19 inclusive on the official Olympics results pages. Key entities: Norway, cross-country skiing, biathlon, gold medals, threshold of 4. Observable evidence: official results from Olympics.com or credible sports news reporting confirmed gold medals in those disciplines.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Norway gold medals cross-country skiing biathlon 2026 Winter Olympics Milano Cortina' — to find all relevant gold medals; 2) '2026 Winter Olympics Norway medal count results February' — to confirm medal totals; 3) 'Norway biathlon gold medal 2026 Olympics results' — specific biathlon golds; 4) 'Norway cross-country skiing gold medal Klaebo 2026 Olympics first gold' — to identify earliest qualifying events; 5) 'Norway biathlon mixed relay gold medal 2026 Olympics February' — to check mixed relay; 6) 'Norway biathlon relay gold women men February 15 2026 Olympics pursuit' — to identify later biathlon golds; 7) 'Norway cross-country skiing team sprint relay gold February 18 2026' — to identify team events; 8) 'Norway biathlon men relay gold February 15 2026 Olympics results' — biathlon relay specifics
evidence.step3_event_detection: Confirmed Norway gold medals in cross-country skiing and biathlon within Feb 7-19 window: (1) Feb 8 - Men's skiathlon cross-country [Klaebo, reported by CNA and multiple sources]; (2) Feb 10 - Men's sprint classic cross-country [Klaebo, reported by AP Daily Medals List and multiple sources]; (3) Feb 10 - Men's 20km individual biathlon [Johan-Olav Botn, reported by AP and multiple sources]; (4) Feb 13 - Men's 10km interval start freestyle cross-country [Klaebo, reported by AP and multiple sources as his 8th career gold]; (5) Feb 14 - Women's 7.5km sprint biathlon [Maren Kirkeeide, reported by multiple sources]; (6) Feb 15 - Men's 4x7.5km relay cross-country [Norway, Klaebo anchoring, reported by AP Daily Medals List and multiple sources]; (7) Feb 18 - Men's team sprint free cross-country [Klaebo & Hedegård, reported by AP/Yahoo/WTOP]. Note: Women's biathlon relay on Feb 18 went to France (Norway got bronze). Men's biathlon relay on Feb 17 went to France (Norway got silver). Note: Mixed biathlon relay on Feb 8 went to France (Norway 4th). These were rejected as Norway did NOT win gold in those events. Nordic combined (Feb 11, Oftebro) was also identified as a Norway gold but is NOT in cross-country skiing or biathlon per standard classification, so excluded.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require at least 4 gold medals in 'cross-country skiing or biathlon' events within the window. Confirmed qualifying Norway golds: (1) Feb 8 - Men's skiathlon (cross-country skiing) [CNA: https://www.channelnewsasia.com/sport/crosscountry-norways-klaebo-wins-gold-in-mens-skiathlon-after-explosive-finish-5915901]; (2) Feb 10 - Men's sprint classic (cross-country skiing) [AP Daily Medals List: https://apnews.com/20250a9e5f35710c91b07b8cc0e6a215]; (3) Feb 10 - Men's 20km individual biathlon [AP via NBC Chicago: https://www.nbcchicago.com/olympics/2026-milan-cortina/see-the-latest-2026-winter-olympics-medal-count-as-team-usa-has-huge-day/3890795/]; (4) Feb 13 - Men's 10km freestyle (cross-country skiing) [AP: https://apnews.com/article/milan-cortina-olympics-cross-country-klaebo-6d712004bd9250bf8921d3c1a8333312]. These four alone satisfy the ≥4 threshold. Additional golds (5)-(7) further confirm. All events are clearly categorized as cross-country skiing or biathlon. All medals were awarded to Norway during the Feb 7-19 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The 4th qualifying gold medal was awarded on February 13, 2026, when Klaebo won the men's 10km interval start freestyle cross-country skiing race. Multiple AP and news sources report this as occurring on February 13, 2026, in Tesero, Italy. The question's threshold of ≥4 was reached on this date. Earlier golds (#1 Feb 8, #2 Feb 10, #3 Feb 10) were all within the window. The exact moment of the 4th gold can be established as February 13, 2026 (during the race in Tesero, Italy).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying gold was Norway's men's skiathlon (cross-country skiing) won by Klaebo on February 8, 2026 — the first full competition day of the Games (Day 2). The second was Feb 10 (men's sprint), third was also Feb 10 (men's 20km biathlon individual), and the fourth was Feb 13 (men's 10km). No earlier qualifying occurrences outside this sequence were found. The biathlon mixed relay on Feb 8 went to France, not Norway.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictions: (1) The mixed biathlon relay (Feb 8) was won by France, not Norway — Norway placed 4th, so this does NOT count as a Norway gold. (2) Women's biathlon relay (Feb 18) was won by France — Norway placed 3rd. (3) Men's biathlon relay (Feb 17) was won by France — Norway placed 2nd. These were correctly excluded. (4) Nordic combined (Oftebro, Feb 11) is NOT biathlon or cross-country skiing — correctly excluded. No sources contradict the four qualifying Norway golds in cross-country skiing and biathlon. Multiple independent sources (AP, TSN, Yahoo Sports, Heavy, NBC, CNA) confirm the same results. The evidence clearly shows Norway exceeded 4 gold medals in cross-country skiing and biathlon well within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Norway won at least 4 gold medals in cross-country skiing and biathlon combined within the Feb 7-19, 2026 window. The 4th qualifying gold was awarded on February 13, 2026 (Klaebo's men's 10km freestyle cross-country). Prior to that, Norway had also won: (1) men's skiathlon (cross-country, Feb 8), (2) men's sprint classic (cross-country, Feb 10), (3) men's 20km individual biathlon (Feb 10). All four are clearly within the window. The threshold of ≥4 was definitively reached. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will A Minecraft Movie be the second highest grossing movie of 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to the movie with the second highest 2025 gross once data for December 31 is made available.

Data from the "Gross" column on https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses will be used to resolve this market.

Note: This market is about the movie's domestic calendar gross in 2025 - dates outside of 2025 will not count toward this movie's gross.

In the event of an exact tie the film that comes first alphabetically will be considered the winner.

If there is no final data available by January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

subquestions.question: Will Box Office Mojo list "A Minecraft Movie" with a 2025 domestic calendar gross of at least $424.0 million as of the 2025-10-01 daily update?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, trade coverage indicates that A Minecraft Movie is narrowly ahead of Lilo & Stitch in 2025 domestic gross, with Box Office Mojo figures cited at about $423.9 million for A Minecraft Movie versus about $421.7 million for Lilo & Stitch. This suggests Minecraft's year-end rank is vulnerable to small late-year changes by competitors, especially major Q4 releases, and that even a modest additional increase in Minecraft's 2025 calendar gross could matter as a signal of staying power. See ScreenRant (2025-08-20): https://screenrant.com/lilo-stitch-box-office-record-minecraft-domestic/ .

The ultimate market resolves from Box Office Mojo's 2025 domestic calendar grosses, so a near-term indicator based on the same reporting source but on Minecraft crossing a specific round-number threshold is relevant without simply restating the final ranking question. Box Office Mojo's 2025 calendar grosses page is the key public source: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses .

A threshold of $424.0 million is chosen because reporting before 2025-09-01 places Minecraft at roughly $423.9 million domestically, making the question nontrivial but plausible within a one-month window. Crossing that mark would indicate at least some continued domestic gross accumulation during September 2025, which slightly improves Minecraft's cushion against films already close behind and reduces the set of plausible paths by which it falls below second place.

Sources:
ScreenRant - Disney's $1 Billion Hit Will Fall Just Shy Of A Final Box Office Record — https://screenrant.com/lilo-stitch-box-office-record-minecraft-domestic/
Box Office Mojo - 2025 Domestic Calendar Grosses — https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Box Office Mojo's page for 2025 domestic calendar grosses shows "A Minecraft Movie" with a value in the "Gross" column of at least $424,000,000 on the first publicly accessible daily update dated 2025-10-01, reflecting grosses accumulated between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive. It resolves No if, on that 2025-10-01 update, the listed 2025 domestic calendar gross for "A Minecraft Movie" is below $424,000,000.

Primary resolution source: Box Office Mojo 2025 domestic calendar grosses page: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses .

If Box Office Mojo instead shows the figure only on the film's title page or a linked yearly breakdown page, those Box Office Mojo pages may be used so long as they clearly report the film's 2025 domestic calendar gross as of the 2025-10-01 update. If Box Office Mojo is temporarily unavailable on 2025-10-01, resolve using the earliest subsequent Box Office Mojo snapshot or archive capture that clearly corresponds to the 2025-10-01 daily standings. If no reliable Box Office Mojo page or archive corresponding to 2025-10-01 is available by 2025-10-08, the question should be considered unresolvable rather than inferred from later totals.

For avoidance of doubt, only the reported 2025 domestic calendar gross counts; worldwide gross, lifetime domestic gross outside the 2025 calendar accounting, and non-Box Office Mojo estimates do not determine resolution.
subquestions.rationale: Minecraft's final placement depends partly on whether it continues to add domestic calendar gross after September begins. Clearing a modest threshold by October 1 would indicate continued box-office legs and a slightly stronger buffer against close competitors, making it a useful early signal for whether it can hold a top-two domestic rank for all of 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Box Office Mojo's 2025 domestic calendar grosses page must show 'A Minecraft Movie' with a gross value of at least $424,000,000 as of the October 1, 2025 daily update. Observable evidence: explicit BOM-sourced domestic figure for the film at or above $424,000,000. Key threshold: $424,000,000 exactly. Timing: must be reflected in the Oct 1, 2025 BOM update.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'A Minecraft Movie box office domestic gross 2025' (Sept-Oct 2025) - to find current domestic figures. Query 2: 'Minecraft Movie total domestic box office earnings United States 2025' (Aug-Oct 2025) - to find latest figures. Query 3: 'Minecraft Movie domestic gross late September 2025 final total' - to find most recent figure before Oct 1. Query 4: '"Minecraft Movie" "$424" OR "424 million" domestic 2025' - to find threshold-matching evidence. Query 5: 'Box Office Mojo 2025 domestic calendar grosses Minecraft' - to find BOM-specific data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple sources cite domestic gross for A Minecraft Movie: (1) Statista (Sept 5): '$424 million domestically'; (2) Koimoi (Sept 16): '$424 million'; (3) Businessday NG (Sept 20, citing BOM data as of Sept 17): '$423.9 million'; (4) ScreenRant (Aug 20, citing BOM): '$423.9 million'; (5) Kirsten Dunst article (Yahoo, Aug 20): '$955.1 million worldwide'. The figures cluster around $423.9M-$424M. Key question is whether the exact BOM figure meets the $424M threshold. The Businessday NG article explicitly cites Box Office Mojo data showing $423.9M as of approximately September 17, 2025. Koimoi (Sept 16) and Statista (Sept 5) round to $424M.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires exactly $424,000,000 or more on BOM's calendar grosses page as of Oct 1, 2025. Multiple sources from within the resolution window cite the figure: [Businessday NG](https://businessday.ng/life-arts/article/2025-hollywood-box-office-leaders-reflect-franchise-dominance/) cites BOM data showing $423.9M; [Koimoi](https://www.koimoi.com/box-office/lilo-stitch-north-america-box-office-disneys-1b-2025-hit-falls-behind-a-minecraft-movie/) reports $424M; [Statista](https://www.statista.com/chart/19538/highest-grossing-movies-based-on-vdeo-games) reports $424M; [ScreenRant](https://screenrant.com/lilo-and-stitch-box-office-not-beat-minecraft-domestic/) cites BOM at $423.9M. The $423.9M figure from BOM is just below $424M threshold. Some sources round to $424M, suggesting the actual BOM figure is approximately $423,900,000-$424,000,000. Given the film's theatrical run was nearly complete by September, it's possible but not confirmed that additional earnings pushed it to exactly $424M+ by Oct 1.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The most precise BOM-attributed figure is $423.9M, referenced by articles from August 20 and September 17-20, 2025. No source provides an exact BOM figure as of October 1, 2025 specifically. The film's earnings in the final weeks of September 2025 would be minimal, possibly adding a few hundred thousand dollars. A direct BOM snapshot for October 1, 2025 is not available in the search results.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable for this type of question - it's about whether a threshold is met at a specific date, not first occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: The key tension is between $423.9M (cited directly from BOM by multiple sources in August-September) and the $424M threshold. The Koimoi article (Sept 16) and Statista (Sept 5) report '$424 million', which could be rounding of $423.9M OR could reflect actual $424M+ figures from those earlier dates. If the film earned approximately $100,000+ more in late September, it would cross $424M. Given minimal late-September earnings for a film 5+ months into release, this is plausible but uncertain. Importantly, no source provides a BOM figure dated on or after September 25 that specifically shows the domestic calendar gross. The most recent BOM-sourced figure I can find is from the Businessday NG article (Sept 20) showing $423.9M as of approximately September 17.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is inconclusive about whether the exact BOM figure as of October 1, 2025 met the $424,000,000 threshold. The most precise BOM-sourced data shows $423.9M (approximately September 17, 2025). Some secondary sources round this to $424M. Given the film's theatrical run was nearly complete, any additional September earnings would be modest. However, I cannot confirm with sufficient precision whether the BOM calendar gross figure as of October 1 was $423.9M (below threshold) or $424.0M+ (at/above threshold). The difference is about $100,000 and relates to the exact BOM reporting methodology. Since direct access to the BOM page as of October 1 is not available, and the evidence spans both below-threshold ($423.9M) and at/above-threshold ($424M) reporting, this question is at the boundary of the threshold. However, given that multiple sources specifically referencing BOM data cite $423.9M through mid-to-late September (and the film would earn very little additional revenue in October), and the threshold requires at least $424.0M, I cannot definitively confirm a Yes resolution without explicit evidence of the October 1 BOM figure meeting the threshold.

question: Will Juliana Stratton be the Democratic nominee for Senate in Illinois?
description:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Democratic Primary for United States Senator from Illinois.

If no 2026 Illinois Democratic Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Illinois Democratic party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

subquestions.question: Will an independent public poll of the 2026 Illinois Democratic U.S. Senate primary released between 2026-02-12 and 2026-03-14 show Juliana Stratton in first place among likely Democratic primary voters?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful indicator because public polling shortly before the March 17, 2026 Illinois Democratic Senate primary is one of the clearest observable signals of which candidate is best positioned to win the nomination. The race appears competitive but, as of the latest cited polling before the start date, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi was ahead. An Emerson College Polling/WGN-TV poll conducted January 3–5, 2026 found Krishnamoorthi at 31% among likely Democratic primary voters, with a large undecided share and Juliana Stratton trailing well behind, indicating meaningful room for movement before voting begins. See The Hill's summary of that poll: https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5074584-krishnamoorthi-leads-illinois-senate-primary-poll/

At the same time, Stratton has important strengths that could shift the race. She is the sitting lieutenant governor and has high-profile backing from Gov. JB Pritzker. Reporting indicates Pritzker put major financial support behind a pro-Stratton super PAC, including a reported $5 million boost, giving her a plausible path to improve in late polling. See Dispatch Argus reporting: https://www.dispatchargus.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/02/02/gov-jb-pritzker-throws-lt-gov-juliana-stratton-a-5-million-lifeline-for-her-us-senate-bid/ 

The race has also featured multiple major candidate debates, including a Jan. 26 debate and a scheduled Feb. 19 WGN debate featuring Stratton, Robin Kelly, and Raja Krishnamoorthi. Debate performances and late ad spending can materially change late-primary polling, making this subquestion a timely crux rather than a restatement of the ultimate question. See The Chicago Maroon on the Jan. 26 debate: https://chicagomaroon.com/46638/news/photo-essay-democratic-senate-hopefuls-spar-during-primary-debate/ and WTWO on the Feb. 19 debate: https://www.mywabashvalley.com/news/your-local-election-headquarters/senate-democratic-candidates-to-face-off-in-statewide-debate-on-wtwo/

Sources:
The Hill - Krishnamoorthi leads in wide-open Illinois Senate Democratic primary: Poll - https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5074584-krishnamoorthi-leads-illinois-senate-primary-poll/
Dispatch Argus - Gov. JB Pritzker throws Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton a $5 million lifeline for her US Senate bid - https://www.dispatchargus.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/02/02/gov-jb-pritzker-throws-lt-gov-juliana-stratton-a-5-million-lifeline-for-her-us-senate-bid/
The Chicago Maroon - Photo Essay: Democratic Senate Hopefuls Spar During Primary Debate - https://chicagomaroon.com/46638/news/photo-essay-democratic-senate-hopefuls-spar-during-primary-debate/
WTWO - Senate Democratic candidates to face off in statewide debate on WTWO+ - https://www.mywabashvalley.com/news/your-local-election-headquarters/senate-democratic-candidates-to-face-off-in-statewide-debate-on-wtwo/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-02-12 and 2026-03-14 (inclusive), at least one independent public poll of likely voters in the 2026 Illinois Democratic primary for U.S. Senate is first released and Juliana Stratton is in sole first place in the horse-race ballot test.

It resolves No if no such qualifying poll released between 2026-02-12 and 2026-03-14 (inclusive) shows Stratton in sole first place.

Qualifying poll requirements:
1. The poll must be publicly released during the window 2026-02-12 through 2026-03-14 inclusive.
2. It must measure the Illinois Democratic primary for U.S. Senate and report results for likely Democratic primary voters or likely Democratic primary election voters in Illinois.
3. It must be conducted by an organization generally recognized as a pollster or media-sponsored survey organization, and results must be publicly available from the pollster, sponsoring media outlet, or a reputable poll aggregator/news report reproducing the topline.
4. The poll must not be an internal campaign poll or a poll released solely by a candidate campaign, party committee, or aligned PAC/Super PAC.
5. The question uses the latest qualifying poll released during the window. If multiple qualifying polls are released on the same calendar date, use the one with the latest stated release time; if release time is unavailable, any same-day qualifying poll showing Stratton in sole first place is sufficient for Yes.

Interpretation rules:
- "First place" means Stratton's reported support percentage is higher than every other named candidate's percentage in that poll.
- If Stratton is tied for first, this does NOT count; the question resolves No unless another qualifying poll in the window shows her in sole first.
- If a poll reports multiple likely-voter screens, use the primary topline identified by the pollster; if none is identified, use the most restrictive likely-voter screen.
- Polls of registered voters, adults, or generic Democrats that do not specifically identify likely Democratic primary voters do not qualify.

Primary resolution sources will be the pollster or sponsor release pages, plus reputable aggregators/news reports as needed, such as RealClearPolling (if it has the race page), The Hill, WGN, or Emerson College Polling releases. Example source types:
- Emerson College Polling: https://emersoncollegepolling.com/
- The Hill: https://thehill.com/
- WGN-TV: https://wgntv.com/
- RealClearPolling: https://www.realclearpolling.com/

If no qualifying independent public poll is released between 2026-02-12 and 2026-03-14 inclusive, resolve No.

If release timing or poll qualification cannot be determined from primary sources and credible secondary reporting is insufficient to establish this, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A late independent poll showing Stratton in first place would be strong evidence that she has overtaken her rivals and is on track to win the nomination. Conversely, if she never reaches first in public polling by March 14, that is meaningful negative evidence for her nomination chances. This is a distinct observable indicator, not merely an earlier version of the primary result.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: at least one qualifying independent public poll released 2026-02-12 to 2026-03-14 (inclusive) showing Juliana Stratton in sole first place among likely Democratic primary voters. The poll must not be internal campaign/PAC-sponsored. Observable evidence: specific poll toplines with Stratton leading all candidates and an independent sponsor.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Illinois Democratic Senate primary poll 2026 Juliana Stratton' - to find relevant polls; 2) 'Illinois 2026 Senate primary poll survey likely voters' - general poll search; 3) 'Public Policy Polling Illinois Senate March 9 2026 Stratton lead' - to investigate the March 9 PPP poll; 4) 'Illinois Senate primary poll Krishnamoorthi Stratton Kelly March 2026' - broader poll search; 5) 'Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association PAC aligned Stratton Illinois Senate' - to check sponsor independence; 6) 'Tulchin Research Illinois Senate poll February 2026' - sponsor check for Tulchin poll; 7) 'Illinois Senate poll 2026 Stratton leading Krishnamoorthi independent nonpartisan'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Polls identified within window: (A) Tulchin Research (Feb 14-19): Krishnamoorthi +16 (42% vs 26%) - Krishnamoorthi first, not Stratton; (B) PPP (Feb 23-24): Krishnamoorthi 29%, Stratton 27% - Krishnamoorthi first; (C) March 9 PPP sponsored by Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association: Stratton +2 over Krishnamoorthi - but sponsor is an aligned PAC per resolution criteria. The Chicago Tribune debate article explicitly states the 'Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association PAC backing Stratton' received contributions. This disqualifies the March 9 poll under criterion 4. No other qualifying independent poll found showing Stratton in first place.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The March 9 PPP poll shows Stratton in first (+2 over Krishnamoorthi) per [Yahoo article](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/illinois-senate-race-leading-polls-080820691.html), but the sponsor is the Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association, which the [Chicago Tribune](https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/03/09/illinois-senate-democrats-final-debate-2026/) confirms is a 'PAC backing Stratton.' This disqualifies it under criterion 4: 'poll must not be released solely by a candidate campaign, party committee, or aligned PAC/Super PAC.' No other qualifying independent poll released in the window shows Stratton in first place. Multiple sources confirm she trailed Krishnamoorthi in most polling during the window. The 19th News article states 'Stratton has sometimes led but often trails Krishnamoorthi' but identifies no specific qualifying independent poll showing her leading during the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The only poll showing Stratton in first place within the window is the March 9 PPP poll (conducted March 9, released shortly thereafter per news reports). However, this poll is disqualified due to partisan sponsorship. All other polls in the window show Krishnamoorthi in first place.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying independent public poll showing Stratton in sole first place was identified within the window. The PPP Feb 23-24 poll (within window, independent) shows Krishnamoorthi first at 29% vs Stratton 27%. The March 9 PPP poll is disqualified.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple sources confirm race tightened during the window but Krishnamoorthi maintained lead in independent polls. The 19th News article from March 13 says 'Stratton has sometimes led but often trails Krishnamoorthi' without identifying any specific qualifying independent poll in the window showing her leading. The ABC7 article notes both candidates cite 'conflicting polls' but attributes Stratton's claimed lead to the Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association poll. No qualifying independent pollster (Emerson, WGN, etc.) released a poll in the window showing Stratton first.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The window closed 2026-03-14 with no qualifying independent public poll showing Stratton in sole first place. The only poll showing her leading (March 9 PPP) was sponsored by an aligned partisan organization (Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association backing Stratton), disqualifying it under criterion 4. All independent polls in the window showed Krishnamoorthi leading. Resolution: No.

question: Will Trump announce David Malpass to replace Lisa Cook?
description:
Donald Trump recently announced he was firing Lisa D. Cook from her position on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors: https://apnews.com/article/federal-reserve-lisa-cook-trump-6fca3d2fbb54ba204cc91398e6a7b020

This market will resolve to according the next individual Donald Trump nominates or announces as a nominee to become a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors between August 26, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. If Donald Trump does not announce nominee for Fed Governor within this market's timeframe, it will resolve to "No announcement by December 31".

This market will resolve based on the first individual trump nominates within the established timeframe.

The announcement of a specific nominee will qualify toward a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether that individual is later officially nominated.

The resolution source for this market will be official information form Donald Trump or one of his official representatives, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue an order between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 that blocks Donald Trump's attempted removal of Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve Board, pending further litigation?
subquestions.background_information:
Whether Trump can actually create a vacancy is a major upstream determinant of whether he can announce any replacement at all, including David Malpass. Multiple reports in late August 2025 said Lisa Cook planned and then filed suit challenging Trump's attempt to fire her, arguing the removal was illegal and that Federal Reserve governors have statutory protection against arbitrary removal. Reuters-cited reporting said Cook filed suit on August 28, 2025 in federal district court and sought immediate relief to preserve her position while the case proceeds: https://www.inman.com/2025/08/28/fed-governor-sues-trump-over-illegal-firing/ . The Federal Reserve has publicly emphasized that Board members serve long terms and cannot be removed easily, underscoring that the legality of the firing is contested: https://apnews.com/article/federal-reserve-lisa-cook-trump-6fca3d2fbb54ba204cc91398e6a7b020 .

This is relevant to the ultimate question because a court order keeping Cook in office through October would materially reduce the chance that Trump soon announces a replacement for her seat, and therefore reduce the near-term chance that the announced replacement is Malpass. Conversely, if no such blocking order is issued, the administration may be more likely to proceed quickly with a nomination announcement. Reporting before October also identified David Malpass and Stephen Miran as possible replacements, indicating the administration is considering candidates but that the legal status of the vacancy is an important bottleneck: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-fed-governor-cook-will-sue-trump-mulls-replacement-2025-08-27/ ; https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2990230/trump-moves-fast-to-replace-fed-governor-cook .

Sources:
AP News - Trump fires Fed Governor Lisa Cook: https://apnews.com/article/federal-reserve-lisa-cook-trump-6fca3d2fbb54ba204cc91398e6a7b020
Inman - Fed governor sues Trump over 'illegal' firing: https://www.inman.com/2025/08/28/fed-governor-sues-trump-over-illegal-firing/
Reuters - US Fed Governor Cook will sue as Trump mulls replacement: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-fed-governor-cook-will-sue-trump-mulls-replacement-2025-08-27/
GuruFocus - Trump Moves Fast to Replace Fed Governor Cook: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2990230/trump-moves-fast-to-replace-fed-governor-cook
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), a U.S. federal court issues a written order in Lisa Cook's lawsuit (or a directly consolidated/successor case arising from Trump's August 2025 attempted removal of Cook) that grants temporary, preliminary, or equivalent injunctive relief that prevents the removal from taking effect during the litigation window. Examples that count include a temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction, or stay that explicitly keeps Cook in office or bars defendants from treating her seat as vacant.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying court order is issued between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

For resolution, primary sources will be the relevant federal court docket and filed orders via PACER or CourtListener. A contemporaneous official court order controls over media interpretation. If docket access is difficult, high-quality legal reporting that quotes and links the order may be used as secondary evidence, but the text of the order takes precedence.

A denial of relief does not count as Yes. Mere hearings, oral comments from the bench without a written entered order, scheduling orders, or filings by the parties do not count. An order issued before 2025-10-01 or after 2025-10-31 does not count, even if it remains in force during the window. If the case is voluntarily dismissed, mooted, or transferred during the window without a qualifying order being issued in the window, resolve No.

Proposed resolution sources:
- CourtListener federal docket search: https://www.courtlistener.com/
- PACER Case Search: https://pacer.uscourts.gov/
- Reuters legal/news coverage: https://www.reuters.com/
- AP News coverage: https://apnews.com/
subquestions.rationale: The existence of a legally valid vacancy is a key crux for whether Trump will soon announce any replacement, including Malpass. A court order blocking Cook's removal would be strong evidence against a near-term replacement announcement; absence of such relief would leave the path clearer.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: A U.S. federal court must issue a written order between Oct 1-31, 2025 that affirmatively grants temporary, preliminary, or equivalent injunctive relief (TRO, preliminary injunction, or stay) explicitly blocking Cook's removal or barring defendants from treating her seat as vacant. Denial of relief does not count. Orders issued before Oct 1 do not count even if in force during the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve removal Trump court order injunction Oct 2025' — to find any Oct 2025 court orders; 2) 'Lisa Cook lawsuit federal court blocking removal Federal Reserve Board Sep-Oct 2025' — to find the full litigation history; 3) 'DC Circuit appeals court Lisa Cook injunction upheld September 2025' — to identify all injunctive orders and their dates; 4) 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve court order October 2025 preliminary injunction' — to find any new October orders
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Sept 9, 2025: U.S. District Judge Jia Cobb issued preliminary injunction blocking Cook's removal — BEFORE the window, does not qualify. (2) Sept 16, 2025: D.C. Circuit 2-1 ruling upholding the injunction — BEFORE the window, does not qualify. (3) Oct 1, 2025: U.S. Supreme Court issued brief unsigned order deferring Trump's emergency stay application and scheduling oral arguments for January 2026 — WITHIN the window, but this is a DENIAL of Trump's request to lift the injunction (denial of relief), not an affirmative grant of injunctive relief to Cook. No new affirmative injunctive order was issued within October 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The October 1, 2025 SCOTUS order does NOT satisfy the resolution criteria. The resolution criteria explicitly states 'A denial of relief does not count as Yes.' The SCOTUS order denied the Trump administration's emergency application to stay the lower court's injunction — it is a denial of relief requested by Trump, not an affirmative grant of injunctive relief to Cook. The actual injunctive relief (preliminary injunction) was issued by Judge Cobb on September 9, 2025 — before the October 1 start date. The resolution criteria also explicitly states 'An order issued before 2025-10-01 or after 2025-10-31 does not count, even if it remains in force during the window.' Multiple sources confirm: [Law & Crime](https://lawandcrime.com/high-profile/trump-fails-for-now-to-oust-lisa-cook-from-fed-based-on-mortgage-fraud-allegation/), [The Federalist](https://thefederalist.com/2025/10/01/scotus-declines-to-halt-lower-court-blockade-on-fed-gov-lisa-cooks-removal-for-now/), [Breitbart](https://www.breitbart.com/economy/2025/10/01/scotus-lets-cook-stay-for-now/), [Redstate](https://redstate.com/smoosieq/2025/10/01/scotus-says-lisa-cook-stays-put-at-the-fed-for-now-n2194617)

question: Will Artemis II launch by February 28?
description:
If the Artemis II rocket successfully launches from its launch pad by February28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Yes”. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The outcome of any launch will be corroborated by examining official video provided by NASA (https://www.youtube.com/nasa), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

Any subsequent anomaly (e.g., an explosion) after the launch will have no bearing on the outcome. Any name change of the Artemis II with another vehicle will have no bearing on the outcome of the market.

subquestions.question: Will NASA complete an Artemis II wet dress rehearsal that includes loading cryogenic propellants into the SLS core stage at Launch Pad 39B by 2026-02-05?
subquestions.background_information:
A successful wet dress rehearsal (WDR) is a key operational milestone before launch because it tests the launch team's ability to load cryogenic propellants, run the countdown, and perform related pad operations. Multiple reports published before 2026-01-21 state that Artemis II was rolled out to Launch Pad 39B on January 17, 2026 and that NASA planned a WDR on or around February 2, 2026, or no later than February 2. CBS reported that engineers would conduct two weeks of tests culminating in a WDR on or around February 2, during which nearly 800,000 gallons of liquid hydrogen and oxygen would be loaded, and noted that this test is critical for clearing the way for launch: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nasa-artemis-ii-moon-rocket-launch-pad-february-flight/ . SciTechDaily likewise reported that the WDR was targeted no later than February 2, 2026 and that NASA might conduct multiple rehearsals if needed: https://scitechdaily.com/nasas-artemis-ii-is-on-the-launch-pad-and-the-moon-is-next/ . The Houston Chronicle also reported that NASA would conduct a WDR no later than February 2 to verify system readiness, with February launch opportunities dependent on progress: https://www.houstonchronicle.com/news/houston-texas/space/article/nasa-artemis-ii-rocket-moon-mission-20041856.php .

This is a useful crux because Artemis I suffered repeated fueling and hydrogen leak issues during rehearsal and launch attempts, so completion of a cryogenic loading rehearsal for Artemis II would be strong evidence that NASA has retired one of the main technical and procedural risks to a February launch. NASA's Artemis II mission page provides official mission context and confirms Artemis II as the first crewed Artemis test flight around the Moon: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-ii/ .

Sources:
CBS News - NASA hauls Artemis II moon rocket to launch pad for February flight - https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nasa-artemis-ii-moon-rocket-launch-pad-february-flight/
SciTechDaily - NASA's Artemis II Is on the Launch Pad and the Moon Is Next - https://scitechdaily.com/nasas-artemis-ii-is-on-the-launch-pad-and-the-moon-is-next/
Houston Chronicle - NASA's Artemis II rocket prepares for first crewed moon mission in 50 years - https://www.houstonchronicle.com/news/houston-texas/space/article/nasa-artemis-ii-rocket-moon-mission-20041856.php
NASA - Artemis II mission page - https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-ii/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if NASA officially reports that, between 2026-01-21 and 2026-02-05 inclusive, Artemis II completed a wet dress rehearsal at Launch Pad 39B that included loading cryogenic propellants into the Space Launch System core stage. "Officially reports" means a NASA press release, NASA blog update, NASA article, or NASA broadcast/post on an official NASA web property explicitly stating that the wet dress rehearsal occurred and that cryogenic propellant loading took place. Primary sources for resolution are NASA official channels, including https://www.nasa.gov/ , https://blogs.nasa.gov/ , and NASA's official YouTube or livestream pages such as https://www.youtube.com/nasa .

The question resolves No if, by 2026-02-05 23:59:59 UTC, there is no such official NASA confirmation.

Clarifications:
- The rehearsal does not need to be declared fully successful overall; partial or full completion counts so long as NASA officially confirms that Artemis II underwent a WDR and that cryogenic propellants were loaded into the SLS core stage during the window from 2026-01-21 through 2026-02-05 inclusive.
- A countdown demonstration without cryogenic propellant loading does not count.
- Loading propellant into other systems only, without the SLS core stage, does not count.
- If NASA states that the rehearsal was postponed beyond 2026-02-05, this question resolves No.
- If NASA official sources become unavailable, secondary confirmation from major spaceflight reporting that directly quotes NASA or reproduces NASA statements may be used as fallback, with preference given to Space.com (https://www.space.com/), Ars Technica (https://arstechnica.com/), or CBS News space coverage (https://www.cbsnews.com/space/).
subquestions.rationale: Completion of a cryogenic fueling wet dress rehearsal is a strong near-term indicator that pad systems, launch procedures, and the vehicle are ready for an actual launch attempt. If this milestone is missed or slips, the odds of an Artemis II launch by February 28 should fall materially.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: NASA officially reports (via nasa.gov, blogs.nasa.gov, or official NASA YouTube/broadcast) that between 2026-01-21 and 2026-02-05, Artemis II completed a WDR at Launch Pad 39B that included loading cryogenic propellants into the SLS core stage. The rehearsal need not be fully successful; partial completion counts. Key entities: Artemis II, WDR, SLS core stage, Launch Pad 39B, cryogenic propellant loading. Timing: event must occur and be officially confirmed within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'NASA Artemis II wet dress rehearsal 2026' (2026-01-01 to 2026-02-05) — to find if/when the WDR occurred. Query 2: 'Artemis II WDR cryogenic propellant loading SLS core stage Launch Pad 39B' (2026-01-01 to 2026-02-05) — to find specific evidence of propellant loading. Query 3: 'NASA Artemis II wet dress rehearsal February 2 2026 propellant loading complete' (2026-02-02 to 2026-02-05) — to confirm completion. Query 4: 'NASA blog Artemis II wet dress rehearsal February 2 OR February 3 2026 cryogenic propellant' (2026-02-02 to 2026-02-05) — to find NASA official sources. Query 5: 'NASA Artemis II WDR date January 2026 delayed postponed' (2026-01-20 to 2026-02-05) — to check for postponements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events identified: (1) WDR attempted on January 31 but DELAYED to February 2 due to cold weather (still within window). (2) WDR conducted on February 2, 2026, at Launch Pad 39B — propellant loaded, countdown ran to T-5:15 before being terminated due to hydrogen leak. NASA confirmed cryogenic propellant was loaded into SLS core stage. This is the qualifying event. No earlier qualifying event found (the January 31 attempt was scrubbed before propellant loading per cold weather delay).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: NASA official source [nasa.gov](https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/full-moon-over-artemis-ii/) (published 2026-02-03) explicitly states: 'NASA completed a wet dress rehearsal for the Artemis II test flight, successfully loading cryogenic propellant into the SLS tanks, closing out the Orion spacecraft, and safely draining the rocket.' This directly confirms: (a) WDR occurred, (b) cryogenic propellant was loaded, (c) into the SLS tanks (core stage), (d) at Launch Pad 39B (the rocket was at Pad 39B throughout). Also confirmed by NASA blog [blogs.nasa.gov](https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/missions/2026/02/03/artemis-ii-wet-dress-rehearsal-nasa-discusses-initial-results/) discussing WDR results on February 3, 2026. Multiple secondary sources (SpaceDaily, JagranJosh, NASASpaceFlight, CBS News, Space.com) uniformly confirm these facts.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The WDR began its 49-hour countdown on February 1, 2026, at 8:13 PM EST (0113 UTC February 2). Propellant loading occurred on February 2, 2026. The countdown was terminated at T-5:15 on February 2-3, 2026. NASA's official blog post discussing initial results was published on 2026-02-03. The NASA image article confirming the WDR was published on 2026-02-03. The exact timestamp of propellant loading into the core stage is approximately February 2, 2026, during the daytime hours EST, which is well within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The WDR conducted on February 2, 2026, is the first (and only) qualifying occurrence within the window. The January 31 attempt was scrubbed before propellant loading due to cold weather. No other qualifying WDR event was found before February 2 in the window. This is the first occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence found. All sources consistently report that (1) the WDR occurred on February 2, 2026; (2) cryogenic propellants were loaded into the SLS core stage; (3) NASA officially reported this on February 3, 2026, via nasa.gov and blogs.nasa.gov. The hydrogen leak that terminated the countdown at T-5:15 does not negate resolution, per the question's explicit clarification that 'the rehearsal does not need to be declared fully successful overall; partial or full completion counts so long as NASA officially confirms that Artemis II underwent a WDR and that cryogenic propellants were loaded.' The event occurred within the specified window (January 21 – February 5, 2026). There is no question that cryogenic propellant loading of the SLS core stage occurred. The launch was subsequently delayed to March, but that delay does not affect whether the WDR with propellant loading occurred within the resolution window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: YES. NASA officially confirmed via nasa.gov (https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/full-moon-over-artemis-ii/) and blogs.nasa.gov (https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/missions/2026/02/03/artemis-ii-wet-dress-rehearsal-nasa-discusses-initial-results/) that Artemis II underwent a WDR at Launch Pad 39B on February 2, 2026, with cryogenic propellant loading into the SLS tanks. This falls within the resolution window (January 21 – February 5, 2026). The partial termination due to a hydrogen leak does not prevent resolution, per the explicit clarification in the question criteria.

question: Will Israel annex West Bank territory in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Israel officially annexes any territory in the West Bank between September 1 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Annexation is defined as an official declaration or legal act by the Israeli government claiming sovereignty over territory in the West Bank they were not claiming at the time of this market's creation.

Qualifying examples of annexation include the 1980 Jerusalem Law, and the Golan Heights Law, however instances where Israeli settlers claiming administrative control over land in the West Bank without a formal annexation will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Israeli government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Israel's Cabinet or Security Cabinet publicly approve, between 2025-09-02 and 2025-10-02, a formal decision or resolution that explicitly calls for applying Israeli sovereignty to any part of the West Bank?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term cabinet-level decision explicitly endorsing the application of Israeli sovereignty in the West Bank would be a strong precursor to any later legal annexation, because formal annexation in Israel would likely require prior executive backing before legislation or other legal acts are advanced. As of late August and early September 2025, multiple media outlets reported that Israeli officials were considering annexation in response to moves by several countries to recognize a Palestinian state, and that the issue was expected to be discussed at a security-cabinet meeting. Reuters-syndicated reporting said the idea would be discussed by Israel's security cabinet and that the scope and timing of any measure remained unclear, implying the process was still upstream of actual annexation steps. See Al-Monitor's Aug. 31 report: https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2025/08/israel-mulls-west-bank-annexation-response-moves-recognise-palestine and Taiwan News' Sept. 1 pickup of the same Reuters reporting: https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/news/6151606

Separately, the Knesset reportedly passed a non-binding motion in July/August 2025 calling on the government to apply sovereignty over the West Bank, but that motion did not itself change legal status. This makes a subsequent Cabinet or Security Cabinet decision especially informative: it would represent movement from symbolic parliamentary signaling toward executive action. Middle East Eye reported on Sept. 1 that a July parliamentary motion was non-binding and did not alter the legal status of the territory, while also describing annexation discussions among senior officials: https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/israel-tells-us-unfolding-plans-annex-west-bank. PNN similarly reported that the prior Knesset proposal was declarative and intended to pave the way for future government steps: https://english.pnn.ps/news/71027

Official Israeli government announcements are typically published by the Prime Minister's Office or government press channels. The PMO news page is therefore a natural primary source for whether a cabinet body has publicly approved such a step: https://www.gov.il/en/pages/prime-ministers-office and https://www.gov.il/en/departments/news/?OfficeId=f9fbf5ca-5d2b-4d30-8d76-6fddccfb8f6e

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-02 and 2025-10-02 (inclusive), the Israeli Cabinet or Security Cabinet is publicly reported by an official Israeli government source as having approved a formal decision, resolution, or government statement that explicitly uses terms equivalent to "apply Israeli sovereignty" or "extend Israeli law/sovereignty" to any territory in the West Bank (including Area C, settlements, the Jordan Valley, or named West Bank areas).

Primary resolution source: an official Israeli government publication or press release, especially from the Prime Minister's Office or Gov.il, such as https://www.gov.il/en/departments/news/?OfficeId=f9fbf5ca-5d2b-4d30-8d76-6fddccfb8f6e or https://www.gov.il/en/pages/prime-ministers-office

A Yes requires a public indication that a cabinet body approved such a step; mere discussion, consideration, agenda-setting, or unofficial leaks do not count. Fallback criteria: if no official government publication is available or accessible, the question may resolve Yes based on a consensus of at least three credible major news outlets reporting that the Cabinet or Security Cabinet approved such a decision during the window. subquestions.rationale: A public cabinet-level approval to apply sovereignty would be a major upstream step toward annexation, without being annexation itself. evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Israeli Cabinet OR Security Cabinet publicly approves a formal decision/resolution explicitly using terms equivalent to 'apply Israeli sovereignty' or 'extend Israeli law/sovereignty' to any West Bank territory. ALL candidates were rejected because none constitute a formal cabinet-level approval of sovereignty — all were discussions, proposals, considerations, or rejections.
