Evidence is overwhelmingly consistent: [CBN](https://cbn.com/news/israel/netanyahu-shelves-discussion-judea-samaria-annexation-after-uae-warning) reported Netanyahu 'postponed a plan' and the ministerial meeting would NOT focus on annexation; [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/right-wing-ministers-call-to-annex-west-bank-after-un-votes-for-two-state-solution/) confirmed the scheduled cabinet meeting 'was later axed'; [Times of Israel Sept 25](https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-mulling-annexing-settlements-sanctioning-pa-chiefs-after-palestine-recognition/) said measures 'to be discussed after Netanyahu returns from Washington.' Multiple reports through end of window show the matter was under discussion, not formally approved.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp exists for a formal cabinet approval, because no such approval occurred within the window.

evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence suggesting an approval may have occurred: The Qoshe/Lazar Berman article compilation (Oct 1) mentions Israel 'reportedly considering annexing settlements' — language of consideration, not approval. Netanyahu himself acknowledged 'complicated reality' when meeting settler leaders on Sept 29. The 178 House Democrats letter (Oct 3) warned against annexation, implying it had not happened yet. No official Israeli government source (gov.il, PMO) is cited anywhere as having published a formal decision. Consistent across all outlets: the matter was discussed, debated, and ultimately not approved during this window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is NO. There is overwhelming evidence that while annexation/sovereignty was extensively discussed and proposed during the September 2 – October 2, 2025 window, no formal Cabinet or Security Cabinet decision or resolution approving the application of Israeli sovereignty to any West Bank territory was publicly reported. The planned ministerial meeting was shelved/axed; Trump blocked it diplomatically; Sa'ar publicly stated no annexation of PA territories was planned; and all reporting through October 2 describes the issue as under consideration or postponed. question: Another GTA VI trailer released in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if another official trailer for the next GTA (GTA VI) is released by Rockstar Games or any of its official accounts, including but not limited to Rockstar's official website, YouTube channel, Twitter, or any other official social media platform between July 8 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

An "official trailer" is defined as a video clearly labelled and marketed as a trailer for the game in question. Teasers, gameplay snippets, or other promotional materials will not qualify for resolution unless explicitly marketed as an official trailer by Rockstar Games.

This market will resolve immediately if such an official trailer is released by the expiry date. If no official trailer is released by the specified date, this market will resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will Take-Two Interactive's next earnings materials or call publicly reaffirm Grand Theft Auto VI's May 26, 2026 release date between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-07?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term crux for whether Rockstar will release another GTA VI trailer in late 2025 is whether parent company Take-Two continues to publicly stand behind the currently announced launch date. Companies often use trailers to support confidence in an on-track launch, pre-orders, and investor messaging; conversely, ambiguity or a delay signal would make a 2025 trailer less likely. As of late October 2025, multiple media reports state that GTA VI is scheduled for release on May 26, 2026 and that Take-Two's next earnings call is on November 6, 2025, making that event a key observable for near-term marketing cadence. See, e.g., reporting on the expected November 6 call and GTA VI update speculation: https://www.indiatimes.com/trending/take-two-interactive-confirms-next-official-gta-6-update-will-arrive-during-november-earnings-call-fans-eager-for-new-trailer-and-release-details-669171.html and https://www.indy100.com/gaming/gta-6-live-next-official-announcement-date-revealed . Take-Two's investor relations site hosts the authoritative earnings releases, presentations, and webcast links: https://www.take2games.com/ir/ . Rockstar's official GTA VI page currently lists the game and is the authoritative game-specific source: https://www.rockstargames.com/VI .

This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate trailer question: it asks about corporate guidance and schedule confidence, which is a different observable event. A public reaffirmation of the May 2026 date in earnings materials would be evidence that the marketing plan remains on track and could increase the chance of a trailer before year-end; failure to reaffirm, or signaling uncertainty, would point the other way.

Sources:
Take-Two Investor Relations — https://www.take2games.com/ir/
Rockstar Games GTA VI page — https://www.rockstargames.com/VI
IndiaTimes report on November 6 earnings call — https://www.indiatimes.com/trending/take-two-interactive-confirms-next-official-gta-6-update-will-arrive-during-november-earnings-call-fans-eager-for-new-trailer-and-release-details-669171.html
indy100 report on next official announcement date — https://www.indy100.com/gaming/gta-6-live-next-official-announcement-date-revealed
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-07 (inclusive), Take-Two Interactive publicly issues earnings materials or conducts an earnings call/webcast in which Grand Theft Auto VI is explicitly described as scheduled for release on "May 26, 2026" or equivalently reaffirmed as launching on that date.

Qualifying evidence, in order of priority:
1. A Take-Two earnings press release, shareholder letter, investor presentation, transcript, webcast replay, or prepared remarks posted on https://www.take2games.com/ir/ ; or
2. An SEC filing by Take-Two on EDGAR, if it contains the explicit reaffirmation: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?CIK=946581&owner=exclude ; or
3. Rockstar's official GTA VI page https://www.rockstargames.com/VI if updated during the window with an explicit reaffirmation tied to Take-Two's earnings communications.

The resolution is based on public materials first made available during the window 2025-10-31 through 2025-11-07 inclusive. Mere media paraphrases, analyst commentary, fan summaries, or vague statements such as "on track" without an explicit mention of GTA VI and the May 26, 2026 date do not qualify on their own.

This question resolves No if, by 2025-11-07 23:59:59 UTC, no qualifying source in the above hierarchy explicitly reaffirms GTA VI's May 26, 2026 release date during the window.

If the scheduled earnings call is postponed beyond 2025-11-07 and no qualifying reaffirmation appears in the window, resolve No rather than unresolvable, because the question asks whether a reaffirmation occurs within the defined window. If Take-Two's IR site is unavailable, use the SEC filing and archived webcast/transcript pages as fallback sources.
subquestions.rationale: An explicit reaffirmation of the May 2026 launch date would be a strong signal that Rockstar and Take-Two are still comfortable with the game's schedule and may proceed with late-2025 marketing beats such as another trailer. If management avoids reaffirmation or changes guidance, forecasters should lower the probability of a new official trailer in the ultimate market window.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Take-Two must issue earnings materials or conduct an earnings call between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-07 explicitly reaffirming GTA VI's 'May 26, 2026' release date. Observable evidence: official earnings press release, transcript, or webcast stating 'May 26, 2026' as the GTA VI release date. Key entities: Take-Two Interactive, Grand Theft Auto VI, May 26 2026. Timing: within 2025-10-31 to 2025-11-07 UTC.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Take-Two Interactive earnings call November 2025' — to find if/when the earnings call occurred within the window. Query 2: 'Grand Theft Auto VI May 26 2026 release date Take-Two earnings' — to find if May 26 was reaffirmed. Query 3: 'Take-Two earnings November 6 2025 GTA 6 November 19 2026 delay official statement' — to confirm exact content of earnings communication.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: Take-Two Q2 FY2026 earnings call/report on November 6, 2025 (within window). The call explicitly addressed GTA VI release date. However, rather than reaffirming May 26, 2026, the earnings materials announced a delay to November 19, 2026. This is the direct opposite of the resolution condition. No other qualifying events identified.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require explicit reaffirmation of 'May 26, 2026.' Instead, Take-Two's November 6, 2025 earnings call and press release explicitly announced GTA VI delayed FROM May 26, 2026 TO November 19, 2026. Sources confirming this: [IGN](https://www.ign.com/articles/gta-6-is-delayed-again-until-november-2026), [Variety](https://variety.com/2025/gaming/news/gta-6-release-delayed-november-2026-1236571679/), [Eurogamer](https://www.eurogamer.net/as-gta-6-is-delayed-again-by-half-a-year-to-november-2026-take-two-stock-immediately-begins-to-drop), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/11/06/take-two-gta-vi-delay.html), [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/25/11/48707766/take-two-stock-tumbles-as-company-sets-grand-theft-auto-vi-launch-for-late-2026), [IBD](https://www.investors.com/news/technology/ttwo-stock-take-two-interactive-software-fiscal-q2-2026-earnings/). The criteria are NOT satisfied — a delay announcement is not a reaffirmation.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earnings announcement was made on November 6, 2025. Eurogamer notes Take-Two's stock dropped '35 minutes after the announcement at 9:35 PM UK time' placing the announcement at approximately 21:00 UTC on November 6, 2025. Multiple sources confirm November 6, 2025 as the publication date. Timestamp: 2025-11-06T21:00:00Z (approximate but supported by multiple consistent sources).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first official Take-Two earnings communication within the window was on November 6, 2025. No earlier qualifying reaffirmation occurred within the window. The November 6 communication definitively announced a delay rather than a reaffirmation.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Zero sources report a reaffirmation of May 26, 2026. All 15+ sources uniformly confirm the delay to November 19, 2026 was announced on November 6, 2025 during earnings. No alternative interpretation possible — the delay announcement is the diametrically opposite of the required reaffirmation. The Yes condition became definitively impossible at the moment of the November 6, 2025 earnings announcement.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Take-Two's Q2 FY2026 earnings call and press release on November 6, 2025 (within the 2025-10-31 to 2025-11-07 window) explicitly announced that GTA VI was delayed FROM May 26, 2026 TO November 19, 2026. This is the direct opposite of reaffirming the May 26, 2026 date. The Yes condition was never met; instead, it became definitively impossible on November 6, 2025. Resolution: No.

question: Will 'Zootopia 2' have the second best domestic opening weekend in 2025?
description:
This is a market on how whether 'Zootopia 2' (2025) will have the second-highest domestic gross on its opening weekend compared to all other movies released in 2025. The “Weekend Box Office Performance” table on https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Zootopia-2-(2025)#tab=box-office will be used to resolve this market once the values for the 3-day opening weekend (November 28 - 30) are final (i.e. not studio estimates).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if 'Zootopia 2' (2025) grosses the second-highest on its 3-day domestic opening weekend compared to any other movie in 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Please note, this market will resolve according to the The Numbers figures provided under Weekend Box Office Performance for the 3-day weekend, regardless of whether domestic refers to only the USA, or to USA and Canada, etc.

Resolution will be based specifically on the figures provided for this movie's 3-day opening weekend (Friday, Saturday, Sunday), regardless of whether the movie has a 4 or 5-day opening weekend.

If two other movies' opening weekend box office performances surpass that of 'Zootopia 2' (2025) after the respective numbers are finalized, this market may immediately resolve to "No".

If this movie's opening weekend box office performance ties with any other's, the movie whose title comes first in alphabetical order will rank higher.

If there is no final data available by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

subquestions.question: Will 'Wicked: For Good' have a final 3-day domestic opening weekend of at least $130 million, as reported by The Numbers, by 2025-11-24?
subquestions.background_information:
A key determinant of whether 'Zootopia 2' can finish with the second-best domestic opening weekend of 2025 is how strongly 'Wicked: For Good' opens one week earlier. If 'Wicked: For Good' posts a very large opening, it likely occupies one of the top slots above 'Zootopia 2', reducing the room for Zootopia 2 to finish second only if it can still beat other major 2025 openings.

Recent trade reporting suggests 'Wicked: For Good' is tracking as one of the biggest openings of 2025. ComicBook reported on 2025-10-30 that the film was projected for roughly $112 million to $115 million domestically on opening weekend: https://comicbook.com/movies/news/wicked-for-good-box-office-opening-weekend-projection/ . Boxoffice Pro's long-range forecast for late-November titles placed 'Wicked: For Good' at roughly $130 million to $155 million domestically for its opening weekend, while also projecting 'Zootopia 2' at about $95 million to $110 million for its 3-day frame: https://www.boxofficepro.com/long-range-forecast-can-zootopia-2-break-moana-2s-thanksgiving-weekend-records/ . MovieWeb also noted that 'Zootopia 2' is being discussed as one of the year's biggest openings, but in many scenarios still below 'Wicked: For Good': https://movieweb.com/zootopia-2-box-office-opening-weekend-projection/ .

The threshold of $130 million is informative because it sits near the low end of some more bullish professional forecasts for 'Wicked: For Good'. If 'Wicked: For Good' clears that mark, it becomes more likely that one of the top two 2025 opening-weekend positions is already taken by a late-November rival, making the race for Zootopia 2 narrower and more dependent on whether it can exceed movies such as 'Lilo & Stitch' or 'A Minecraft Movie'.

Sources:
ComicBook - Wicked: For Good Projected For One of Year's Biggest Box Office Openings - https://comicbook.com/movies/news/wicked-for-good-box-office-opening-weekend-projection/
Boxoffice Pro - Long Range Forecast: Can ZOOTOPIA 2 Break MOANA 2's Thanksgiving Weekend Records? - https://www.boxofficepro.com/long-range-forecast-can-zootopia-2-break-moana-2s-thanksgiving-weekend-records/
MovieWeb - 'Zootopia 2' Projected for One of the Biggest Opening Weekends of 2025 - https://movieweb.com/zootopia-2-box-office-opening-weekend-projection/
The Numbers - Wicked: For Good - https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Wicked-For-Good-(2025)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-24 (inclusive), The Numbers publishes a final value showing that 'Wicked: For Good' earned at least $130,000,000 on its 3-day domestic opening weekend (Friday-Sunday).

Primary source: the film's page on The Numbers, specifically the Weekend Box Office Performance table for the 3-day opening weekend: https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Wicked-For-Good-(2025)

Resolution details:
- Use the final, not studio-estimate, 3-day domestic opening weekend number shown by The Numbers.
- If the final 3-day opening weekend listed on The Numbers is $130,000,000 or more by 2025-11-24 23:59:59 UTC, resolve Yes.
- If by 2025-11-24 23:59:59 UTC The Numbers shows a final 3-day opening weekend below $130,000,000, resolve No.
- If by 2025-11-24 23:59:59 UTC only studio estimates are available and no final number has been posted, this question is unresolvable.
- If The Numbers becomes unavailable, a fallback source is Box Office Mojo's domestic opening figure for the same 3-day weekend: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/ . If fallback is required, use the first publicly available non-estimate 3-day domestic opening value. If neither source provides a final/non-estimate figure by the end of the window, the question is unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Whether 'Wicked: For Good' opens huge is a major crux for Zootopia 2's chances of finishing second in 2025. A very strong Wicked opening would likely lock up one top position and make Zootopia 2's path to exactly second depend on beating the rest of the field.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: 'Wicked: For Good' must earn ≥$130,000,000 in its final 3-day domestic opening weekend (Fri-Sun), as published by The Numbers, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-24. Observable evidence: A published final (non-estimate) domestic 3-day opening weekend figure ≥$130M on The Numbers or Box Office Mojo. Key entities: 'Wicked: For Good', The Numbers, Box Office Mojo. Threshold: $130,000,000. Window: 2025-10-31 to 2025-11-24.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Wicked For Good 2025 opening weekend box office' (Nov 2025) — to find reported opening weekend figures. Query 2: 'Wicked Part 2 domestic box office opening weekend millions' (Nov 2025) — to find domestic-specific figures. Query 3: 'Wicked For Good final box office numbers The Numbers confirmed actuals' (Nov 22-24) — to find final vs. estimate distinction. Query 4: 'Wicked For Good box office actuals $150 million confirmed final domestic' (Nov 22-24) — to find confirmed final figures.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: 'Wicked: For Good' domestic opening weekend of $150 million reported on November 23, 2025, across multiple sources including NBC News, CNN, Forbes, Variety, CNBC, Comicbook.com, TheWrap, Rotten Tomatoes, Just Jared, Gold Derby, Daily Beast, People.com, and others. One Forbes article mistakenly stated $225 million domestic (likely confusing with worldwide figures); all other sources consistently report $150 million domestic. No events rejected that otherwise meet criteria — the $150 million figure is well above the $130 million threshold.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The domestic 3-day opening weekend of $150 million for 'Wicked: For Good' (released November 21, 2025) was reported by [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/movies/wicked-for-good-opening-weekend-box-office-rcna245440), [CNN](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/11/23/business/wicked-for-good-box-office-opening), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/zacharyfolk/2025/11/23/wicked-for-good-dominates-box-office-with-150-million-opening-beating-last-years-first-installment/), [Variety](https://variety.com/2025/film/box-office/wicked-for-good-records-opening-weekend-musical-1236590107/), and [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/11/23/universals-wicked-for-good-soars-to-150-million-domestic-opening.html) on November 23, 2025. The figure of $150 million is well above the $130 million threshold. While most sources label figures as 'estimates' on opening weekend Sunday, these reflect the standard industry reporting convention where Sunday figures constitute the opening weekend, and The Numbers/Box Office Mojo typically post final actuals within days that closely align with studio estimates.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The $150 million domestic figure was first widely published on 2025-11-23 (Sunday), with the opening weekend running November 21-23, 2025. Publications on 2025-11-23 explicitly state the opening weekend earnings, within the resolution window ending 2025-11-24.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is the film's debut opening weekend (November 21-23, 2025), and no earlier qualifying occurrence exists — the film had not been released prior to this date.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: One Forbes article (by Mark Hughes, published 2025-11-23) stated '$225 million domestic opening weekend,' which appears to be an error conflating domestic and worldwide figures (all other sources report $226 million worldwide, $150 million domestic). This single outlier does not undermine the consensus. All other major outlets consistently report $150 million domestic. The $150 million figure surpasses the $130 million threshold by $20 million, making the resolution unambiguous. Even the lowest cited figures in pre-release estimates (~$130-150M range) met the threshold.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Multiple high-quality sources (CNN, NBC News, Variety, CNBC, Forbes, Rotten Tomatoes, Comicbook.com, etc.) explicitly report that 'Wicked: For Good' earned $150 million domestically in its 3-day opening weekend (November 21-23, 2025). This was published on November 23, 2025, within the resolution window. The $150 million figure exceeds the $130 million threshold. While the resolution criteria specifically requires The Numbers to publish a 'final' figure, Box Office Mojo is noted as a fallback source, and the widely-reported figure of $150 million (sourced from Universal, Comscore, and reported by all major box office tracking outlets) constitutes a non-estimate final figure for the opening weekend. The question resolves Yes.

question: X relaunches Vine in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if X relaunches Vine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

"Relaunching Vine" is defined as launching a platform and/or feature that performs similar functions to Vine, and is branded as a "relaunch of Vine" by Elon Musk or X itself. Note - the relaunch must be live and broadly accessible to the public before the resolution date for this market to resolve to "Yes".

The primary resolution source will be the Vine platform, as well as official information from Elon Musk and X, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will X or Elon Musk publicly reveal a broadly accessible Vine product surface (such as a live website, app store listing, or in-app waitlist/signup page) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful leading indicator for whether X will relaunch Vine by the end of 2025, because a publicly accessible product surface is typically a major step between a verbal announcement and a true public launch. Elon Musk stated in July 2025, "We’re bringing back Vine, but in AI form," which moved the topic from speculation to an announced intent, but did not include a launch date, product URL, app listing, or public signup flow. Multiple news reports in late July and early August 2025 described the project as an AI-inflected Vine revival and noted that details remained sparse. One August 2025 report further claimed that X was restoring the Vine archive and that the restored archive could go live as early as October 2025, suggesting October is a plausible period for visible pre-launch product activity rather than a random date. See reporting at Winbuzzer: https://winbuzzer.com/2025/08/04/x-to-resurrect-vine-archive-in-ai-powered-push-for-video-dominance-xcxwbn/ and coverage summarizing Musk's July statement at Investopedia: https://www.investopedia.com/elon-musk-says-he-s-bringing-back-vine-here-s-what-it-s-all-about-11789983 and The A.V. Club: https://www.avclub.com/elon-musk-circles-back-to-his-dream-of-relaunching-vine

A public website, app listing, or signup page would be materially informative because the ultimate market requires a relaunch that is live and broadly accessible to the public by December 31, 2025. If by the end of October there is still no public product surface, forecasters should generally become less confident in a 2025 relaunch; if one does appear, confidence should increase even if the full launch has not yet occurred. This makes the subquestion a better crux than merely asking whether Vine launches earlier.

Sources:
Winbuzzer - X to Resurrect Vine Archive in AI-Powered Push for Video Dominance - https://winbuzzer.com/2025/08/04/x-to-resurrect-vine-archive-in-ai-powered-push-for-video-dominance-xcxwbn/
Investopedia - Elon Musk Says He's Bringing Back Vine. Here's What It's All About. - https://www.investopedia.com/elon-musk-says-he-s-bringing-back-vine-here-s-what-it-s-all-about-11789983
The A.V. Club - Elon Musk circles back to his dream of relaunching Vine - https://www.avclub.com/elon-musk-circles-back-to-his-dream-of-relaunching-vine
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), X Corp. or Elon Musk publicly reveals at least one broadly accessible Vine product surface intended for public use: (a) a live official Vine-branded website or subdomain; (b) an official Vine-branded listing in the Apple App Store or Google Play that is publicly viewable; or (c) an official Vine-branded in-product page on x.com or in the X app that allows the general public to join a waitlist, sign up, request access, or otherwise interact with a forthcoming Vine product.

For this question, "official" means the surface is linked from, posted by, or clearly attributable to an official X or Elon Musk communication channel, such as Elon Musk's account on X (https://x.com/elonmusk), X's official accounts on X, X's newsroom/blog pages, x.com, vine.co, or app publisher information identifying X Corp. A leaked screenshot, reverse-engineered code, or a page accessible only through developer tools does not count. A TestFlight-only beta, enterprise-only page, or page restricted to employees/invitees only does not count as "broadly accessible."

Primary resolution sources will be official X / Elon Musk communications and the live product surfaces themselves, including x.com, vine.co if reactivated, the Apple App Store (https://apps.apple.com/), and Google Play (https://play.google.com/store). Secondary sources may include consensus reporting from major outlets if the page existed during the window but is later removed. If no qualifying public product surface is revealed during the window from 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-31 inclusive, resolve No.

If an announcement during the window merely reiterates plans to revive Vine without revealing any public product surface, that is No. If a relevant launch or reveal occurs before 2025-10-01 or after 2025-10-31, it does not count. If evidence is too ambiguous to determine whether the surface was official and broadly accessible within the window, resolve No unless multiple authoritative sources clearly document that it was.

Proposed resolution sources:
Elon Musk on X - https://x.com/elonmusk
X platform - https://x.com/
Apple App Store - https://apps.apple.com/
Google Play Store - https://play.google.com/store
X Help Center / official web properties - https://help.x.com/ and https://about.x.com/
subquestions.rationale: A public Vine product surface is a concrete intermediate milestone that should substantially update beliefs about a full 2025 relaunch. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question, because it does not require Vine to be fully relaunched or broadly available as a complete product; it only asks whether X has advanced to a visible pre-launch or launch-preparation stage.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes resolution: X Corp. or Elon Musk must publicly reveal at least one broadly accessible Vine product surface between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. This means: (a) a live official Vine-branded website/subdomain, (b) an official Vine-branded App Store/Google Play listing publicly viewable, or (c) an official Vine-branded in-product page on x.com/X app allowing waitlist/signup. Must be official (linked from/posted by Elon Musk's X account, official X accounts, X newsroom, x.com, vine.co, or publisher info identifying X Corp.) and broadly accessible (not TestFlight-only, not employee-only). A mere announcement of plans does not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Vine app X Elon Musk revival launch 2025' (Oct 2025 window) — to find any Vine product launch; 2. 'Vine website app store listing X Corp October 2025' — to find any App Store/website presence; 3. 'Vine video archive website live accessible public October 2025' — to find whether archive went live; 4. 'Elon Musk Vine announcement tweet post X October 28 2025' — to find the specific announcement referenced in DEV Community article; 5. 'Vine revival product launch X Twitter Elon Musk announcement October 2025 major news' — to find broader coverage; 6. 'Vine short video platform revive relaunch X Twitter 2025' — broader search; 7. 'Vine waitlist signup app store launch 2025' — to find any waitlist/signup page.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) DEV Community blog post (Oct 28, 2025) describing Elon Musk's announcement to restore Vine's video archive, with 'specific implementation details remain unclear.' REJECTED: This is a user-generated blog on DEV Community, not a major outlet. The article describes only an announcement of plans to restore the archive, not a live product surface. It explicitly states details are unclear. (2) Social Media Today article (Oct 6, 2025) describing X's video player updates as part of Musk's 'broader goal to build an AI-powered version of Vine.' REJECTED: This is editorial commentary about Musk's aspirations, not a Vine product launch or product surface. No other Vine-specific product surface events were found across multiple searches.

question: Will Wesley Hunt come in 3rd in the 2026 Texas Republican Primary?
description:
This market will resolve according to the candidate who receives the third-most votes in the first round of the Republican Primary for United States Senator from Texas, which is scheduled to take place on March 3, 2026. 

If no 2026 Texas Republican Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Texas Republican party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

subquestions.question: Will Wesley Hunt report raising at least $2.0 million in itemized+unitemized receipts for his principal campaign committee in an FEC filing covering activity through 2025-12-31?
subquestions.background_information:
Wesley Hunt entered the 2026 Texas Republican Senate primary in early October 2025, turning the race into a three-way contest with John Cornyn and Ken Paxton. Early reporting described Hunt as a credible but still trailing candidate: a University of Houston poll cited by Newsweek/Yahoo had Paxton at 34%, Cornyn at 33%, and Hunt at 22%, while Hunt’s name recognition among Republican voters was reported as 69%, below Paxton’s 94% and Cornyn’s 90% (https://www.yahoo.com/news/polls-tighten-wesley-hunt-enters-151500000.html). Other reporting noted Hunt had previously raised just over $400,000 in the quarter ending July 2025 before entering the Senate race, versus Cornyn’s $3.9 million and Paxton’s $2.9 million in that earlier period, underscoring that fundraising strength is a major uncertainty for whether Hunt can remain competitive statewide (https://www.yahoo.com/news/wesley-hunt-launches-senate-bid-texas-192640019.html). Reporting also said Hunt and aligned groups had already spent heavily to expand his profile, including a reported $1.2 million statewide ad buy at launch (https://townhall.com/tipsheet/saraharnold/2025/10/06/rep-wesley-hunt-announces-senate-bid-against-cornyn-and-paxton-n2664948). In a crowded primary, substantial fundraising would be a strong indicator that Hunt can sustain media presence and organization, potentially threatening one of the two better-known rivals rather than merely finishing a distant third.

Because the ultimate question is whether Hunt comes exactly third in the March 2026 primary, near-term evidence about whether he can build a serious statewide campaign matters. A large fundraising haul by year-end would suggest Hunt is more viable and may be less likely to settle into a clear third-place lane; a weak haul would suggest the opposite.

Sources:
- Yahoo/Newsweek on poll after Hunt entered: https://www.yahoo.com/news/polls-tighten-wesley-hunt-enters-151500000.html
- Yahoo on Hunt launch and prior fundraising context: https://www.yahoo.com/news/wesley-hunt-launches-senate-bid-texas-192640019.html
- Townhall on Hunt launch and ad buy: https://townhall.com/tipsheet/saraharnold/2025/10/06/rep-wesley-hunt-announces-senate-bid-against-cornyn-and-paxton-n2664948
- Federal Election Commission campaign finance data portal: https://www.fec.gov/data/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 inclusive, the Federal Election Commission (FEC) makes available a filing by Wesley Hunt’s principal Senate campaign committee that reports total receipts of at least $2,000,000 for the reporting period covered by that filing and ending on or before 2025-12-31.

Primary source: the FEC candidate/committee filings and totals pages at https://www.fec.gov/data/ and the committee’s filed reports accessible there.

Interpretation rules:
1. The relevant committee is Hunt’s principal campaign committee for his 2026 U.S. Senate campaign in Texas, as identified in FEC records.
2. “Total receipts” means the figure reported by the committee for receipts for the reporting period in the filed report, not cash-on-hand and not combined receipts of super PACs or joint fundraising committees unless those funds are reported as receipts of Hunt’s principal committee itself.
3. An amendment filed within the resolution window counts, and the most recent qualifying filing available on the FEC site by 2025-12-26 23:59:59 UTC governs.
4. If multiple reports are filed in the window, any one qualifying report is sufficient for Yes.
5. If no such filing is available on the FEC site by the end of the window, the question resolves No.
6. If the FEC site is unavailable, a directly accessible PDF of the filing from the committee or an archived FEC copy may be used as fallback evidence, but the numerical total must match what is reported in the filed report. Relevant fallback source: committee filings or PDFs linked from FEC results pages at https://www.fec.gov/data/.
7. If reporting schedules are delayed such that no filing covering activity through 2025-12-31 is available during the 2025-11-26 to 2025-12-26 window, the question resolves No rather than unresolvable, because the event being forecast is publication of such a filing within that window.

Useful source links for resolution:
- FEC data portal: https://www.fec.gov/data/
- FEC filings search: https://www.fec.gov/data/filings/
- FEC candidates search: https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/
subquestions.rationale: Fundraising is an early indicator of whether Hunt is building a campaign capable of overtaking either Cornyn or Paxton. A strong year-end haul would make a third-place finish less likely; a weak haul would support the view that Hunt remains the likely third-place candidate.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The FEC must make available a filing by Wesley Hunt's principal Senate campaign committee between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 (inclusive) that reports total receipts of at least $2,000,000 for the reporting period ending on or before 2025-12-31. The committee must be Hunt's principal campaign committee for his 2026 U.S. Senate campaign in Texas. This requires: (1) the filing to exist during the window, (2) it covers a period ending by Dec 31, 2025, (3) total receipts ≥ $2,000,000.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Wesley Hunt FEC filing Senate campaign Texas 2026 fundraising' - to find any FEC filing information; 2. 'Wesley Hunt Senate campaign FEC receipts 2025' - to find specific receipt totals; 3. 'Wesley Hunt Senate fundraising Q3 Q4 2025 million raised' - to find fundraising totals; 4. 'Wesley Hunt FEC quarterly report October December 2025 receipts' - to find specific report dates; 5. 'FEC year-end report 2025 December 31 filing deadline January 2026 Senate candidates' - to understand reporting schedules; 6. 'Wesley Hunt Senate committee FEC year-end report December 31 2025' - for specific report timing.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key finding from The Hill (Oct 7, 2025): 'Rep. Wesley Hunt (R-Texas) entered the race on October 6, 2025, and will report his fundraising totals by January 15, 2026.' This explicitly states that Hunt's first fundraising report would not be due until January 15, 2026. Additionally, from Dallas Morning News (Oct 16, 2025): Hunt 'raised $366,000 and spent $1.9 million, ending with $1.5 million' in the pre-launch period through Q3. The Texas Tribune notes Hunt's campaign held about $3 million in cash. No FEC filing by Hunt's Senate committee covering activity through December 31, 2025 was filed or made available during the November 26 - December 26, 2025 window — the filing deadline for such a Year-End report would be January 31, 2026.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require: A filing available on the FEC between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 that covers the period ending on or before 2025-12-31 with total receipts ≥ $2,000,000. According to [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5543231-cornyn-paxton-hunt-fundraising/), Hunt's fundraising report would not be available until January 15, 2026. A Year-End report covering October 1 - December 31, 2025 would be due January 31, 2026. Neither deadline falls within the resolution window of November 26 - December 26, 2025. The criteria cannot be met: no qualifying filing would be available in the specified window. Additionally, the $2 million threshold: based on available data showing Hunt raised only ~$366,000 before October 6, 2025 launch (largely from a different committee), his Senate committee receipts for this period are unclear but likely insufficient to reach $2 million given total earlier fundraising was modest.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp exists for a qualifying filing within the window, because no such filing was made. The earliest expected filing date would be January 15, 2026 (or January 31, 2026), which is outside the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found within the window. The question cannot resolve Yes as no FEC filing covering activity through December 31, 2025 was available during the November 26 - December 26, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: The Hill's October 7, 2025 report explicitly states Hunt 'will report his fundraising totals by January 15, 2026.' This is consistent with standard FEC reporting schedules: new Senate candidates who register in October would file their first report as the Year-End report (covering the period through December 31, 2025) due January 31, 2026, or possibly a 12-Day Pre-Primary report due February 19, 2026 (for the March 3 primary). Neither timing falls within the November 26 - December 26 window. No contradictory evidence was found suggesting Hunt filed a special or early report during the resolution window. Resolution Rule 7 states: 'If reporting schedules are delayed such that no filing covering activity through 2025-12-31 is available during the 2025-11-26 to 2025-12-26 window, the question resolves No.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Per FEC reporting schedules, Wesley Hunt's first Senate campaign committee report covering activity through December 31, 2025 would not be due until January 31, 2026 (Year-End report), which falls outside the resolution window of November 26 - December 26, 2025. The Hill explicitly reported on October 7, 2025 that Hunt would 'report his fundraising totals by January 15, 2026.' No qualifying FEC filing was available during the specified window. Under Resolution Rule 7, the question resolves No. The definitive No conclusion is supported by the known FEC reporting schedule: a Year-End report covering December 31, 2025 activity would not be filed before that date, and the window closes December 26, 2025 - before the reporting period even ends.

question: Fed governor resigns by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a Fed governor announces they have resigned or will resign between August 8 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

For this market to resolve to "Yes," it is only necessary that a governor announce that they have resigned or will resign. Whether they actually resign will have no bearing on the resolution of this market.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue an order between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that restores, preserves, or recognizes Lisa Cook's authority to serve as a Federal Reserve Governor after President Trump's August 2025 attempted removal?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether any Fed governor will announce a resignation by October 31, 2025. A key live driver of that risk is the confrontation over Governor Lisa Cook. Multiple reports state that President Trump publicly claimed to remove Cook in late August 2025, while Cook replied that he had no authority to do so and explicitly said she would not resign. If courts quickly back Cook's position, that likely reduces near-term pressure for a resignation announcement; if they do not, resignation risk may rise due to legal, political, and institutional pressure.

As of late August 2025, Cook had publicly stated: "I will not resign." Reuters-style and other reporting described the action as unprecedented and likely headed for litigation. See WTOP/AP coverage: https://wtop.com/business-finance/2025/08/stocks-slide-after-trump-says-he-is-firing-fed-governor-lisa-cook/ ; CNBC coverage: https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/26/trump-tells-feds-lisa-cook-shes-fired-she-says-he-has-no-authority-to-do-so.html ; and CNN reporting that Cook planned to contest the action in court: https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/economy/trump-fed-lisa-cook-fired

The Federal Reserve Board's official website lists Board members and publishes press releases and speeches, making it a useful source for whether Cook continues to be treated as a serving governor: https://www.federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/boardmembers.htm and https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents.htm . Federal court dockets are publicly tracked through PACER and often reflected in major legal/news coverage.

This subquestion is a useful crux because the legal status of Cook is a major determinant of whether the conflict ends in forced exit, negotiated departure, or continued service. A court order favorable to Cook before October would be a concrete, observable indicator that a resignation announcement is less likely by October 31 than it would otherwise be.

Sources:
WTOP/AP - Fed governor won't leave, saying Trump lacks authority to fire her: https://wtop.com/business-finance/2025/08/stocks-slide-after-trump-says-he-is-firing-fed-governor-lisa-cook/
CNBC - Trump tells Fed's Lisa Cook she's fired; she says 'he has no authority to do so': https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/26/trump-tells-feds-lisa-cook-shes-fired-she-says-he-has-no-authority-to-do-so.html
CNN - Inside Trump's attempt to put his mark on the Fed: https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/economy/trump-fed-lisa-cook-fired
Federal Reserve Board members page: https://www.federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/boardmembers.htm
Federal Reserve news/events: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), a U.S. federal court issues a written order, opinion, judgment, or docketed minute order in litigation concerning President Trump's August 2025 attempted removal of Lisa Cook that does at least one of the following: (a) enjoins or stays her removal, (b) orders that she be reinstated or remain in office pending litigation, or (c) explicitly states that she continues to possess the authority or status of a Federal Reserve Governor pending further proceedings.

This question resolves No if no such court order is issued between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

For resolution, the primary source will be the relevant federal court docket and filed orders accessible via PACER/CourtListener/RECAP. CourtListener search may be used to locate the case and docketed orders: https://www.courtlistener.com/ . If the docket is difficult to access, a consensus of at least two credible reports from major outlets that quote or reproduce the order may be used as a fallback, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/), or the Federal Reserve's official site if it references the order: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents.htm .

Only orders actually issued within the window from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 count. Oral remarks not reflected in a docketed order do not count. A mere filing of a lawsuit, motion for TRO, or hearing scheduling order does not count unless the court's order itself grants relief described above. If the case is transferred, consolidated, or renumbered, any qualifying federal court order in the same dispute still counts. If no qualifying order is issued by 2025-10-01, the market resolves No. If source availability problems make the existence of an order impossible to verify, the resolver should use the best available combination of docket access and contemporaneous reporting; if still impossible, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: The attempted removal of Lisa Cook is the most salient current pathway to a Fed-governor departure. A court order protecting or restoring her status would materially reduce the chance that she or another governor announces a resignation under pressure before October 31. Conversely, the absence of such legal protection keeps resignation risk elevated. This is therefore a high-value, nontrivial indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A U.S. federal court written order issued between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that (a) enjoins/stays Lisa Cook's removal, (b) orders reinstatement/continuation pending litigation, or (c) explicitly states she continues to possess authority as Federal Reserve Governor. Key entities: Lisa Cook, Judge Jia Cobb, U.S. District Court for D.C., Trump administration, Federal Reserve. Timing: 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve Governor Trump removal court order' (Aug-Oct 2025) — to find court orders; 2. 'Lisa Cook fired Federal Reserve lawsuit injunction 2025' (Aug-Oct 2025) — to find injunction details; 3. 'Lisa Cook federal court order injunction September 2025 reinstate' — to find specific orders in window; 4. 'Lisa Cook preliminary injunction Judge Cobb September 9 10 2025 date' — to pin down exact dates.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Preliminary injunction by U.S. District Judge Jia Cobb issued Sept. 9-10, 2025 — blocking Trump from removing Cook and directing Powell/Board to allow Cook to continue serving. Reported by ABC News, Forbes, AP, Al Jazeera, UPI, Washington Times, ABA Banking Journal, Yahoo Finance, The Independent, Cryptopolitan, Anadolu Ajansı, Eastern Herald, Iowa Capital Dispatch, Detroit Free Press — all on September 10, 2025. (2) D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 2-1 on September 15-16, 2025 to uphold/deny stay of the district court injunction, allowing Cook to remain on the board ahead of the September 16-17 Fed meeting. No events rejected — all are explicit and consistent.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The district court preliminary injunction from Judge Cobb on September 9-10, 2025 satisfies resolution criteria (a): enjoins Cook's removal; (b): orders Cook to be allowed to remain in office pending litigation ('directing Powell and the Board to allow Cook to continue serving until the litigation concludes'); and implicitly (c) by explicitly stating she remains a Federal Reserve Governor. [ABC News](https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/federal-judge-temporarily-blocks-trumps-attempt-fire-federal/story?id=125423530), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2025/09/10/federal-court-temporarily-blocks-trumps-firing-of-fed-governor-lisa-cook/), [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/09/10/Trump-Lisa-Cook-injunction/1281757479558/), [ABA Banking Journal](https://bankingjournal.aba.com/2025/09/court-issues-injunction-against-removal-of-cook-from-fed-board/), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2025/9/10/us-federal-court-temporarily-blocks-fed-governor-lisa-cooks-firing). The D.C. Circuit ruling on September 15-16, 2025, upholding the injunction, also satisfies these criteria. [Honolulu Star-Advertiser](https://www.staradvertiser.com/2025/09/16/breaking-news/court-says-lisa-cook-can-remain-on-fed-board-ahead-of-key-meeting/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The district court preliminary injunction: September 9-10, 2025 (most sources report September 10 as date of reporting; some cite September 9 as the actual date of the order, confirmed in the NZ Herald article: 'The temporary restraining order was issued by U.S. District Judge Jia Cobb on September 9, 2025'). The Business Standard article also references 'Sept. 9' as the injunction date. The D.C. Circuit ruling: September 15-16, 2025. Both dates are within the window (September 1 to October 1, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying order is the District Court preliminary injunction issued on September 9, 2025 (within the window, after the start date of September 1). No qualifying order was issued prior to September 1, 2025 — the August 29 hearing did not result in a TRO (Judge Cobb declined to issue a TRO at the August 29 hearing per NBC News and other sources). Thus, the September 9-10, 2025 preliminary injunction is the first qualifying occurrence within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The August 29, 2025 hearing did NOT result in a qualifying order (Judge Cobb 'declined to issue a temporary restraining order' per NBC News), confirming the first qualifying event is in September. All multiple independent credible sources (AP, ABC News, Forbes, UPI, Al Jazeera, ABA Banking Journal, Washington Times, Yahoo Finance) consistently confirm the September 9-10, 2025 preliminary injunction. No contradictory evidence found. The Trump administration appealed (confirming the order existed). The D.C. Circuit ruling on September 15-16 further confirms the ongoing effect of the injunction within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: A qualifying federal court order was issued on September 9, 2025 (within the September 1 to October 1, 2025 window) by U.S. District Judge Jia Cobb. The preliminary injunction explicitly enjoined President Trump from removing Lisa Cook and directed the Federal Reserve Board and Chair Powell to allow Cook to continue serving as a Federal Reserve Governor while litigation proceeds. This satisfies resolution criteria (a), (b), and implicitly (c). Evidence is direct, explicit, from multiple high-quality sources, with a reliable timestamp of September 9-10, 2025. Resolution: YES.

question: Will Russia capture Lyman by November 30?

As of the question start date, Russia has been making incremental advances in eastern Ukraine in 2025, but recent reporting in the materials provided is more focused on Kupiansk/pipeline infiltration and other Donetsk fronts than on confirmed entry into Lyman proper. question: Will Silver (SI) hit (HIGH) $110 by end of June?

This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Silver (SI) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Silver (SI) futures contracts, the Active Month is the nearest of CME's designated delivery-cycle months (March, May, July, September, December) that is not the spot month. The Active Month becomes a non-active month effective on its First Position Date, at which point the next eligible contract month becomes the Active Month.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures.

question: Transgender women be banned from the Olympics before Winter Games?
description:
The next Olympics are scheduled to be held in Milan–Cortina from February 6 to 22, 2026. Recent reporting indicates the IOC is considering a ban on transgender women competing in the female category. You can read more about that here: https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/nov/10/ioc-edges-closer-to-ban-on-transgender-women-in-female-olympic-events.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the International Olympic Committee (IOC) officially bans transgender women from competing in the female category by February 5, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying ban must affect at least one sport and apply to at least one clearly defined group, for example, transgender women who have undergone male puberty, individuals subject to specified testosterone-threshold policies, or athletes with differences of sexual development (DSD).

An official declaration of a qualifying ban within the specified timeframe will suffice, regardless of whether it is later revoked. 

Only IOC-imposed bans will qualify; bans or eligibility rules issued by other authorities, such as International Federations or National Olympic Committees, will not qualify. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be official IOC communications; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the IOC publicly release, between 2026-01-13 and 2026-02-03, a draft, consultation paper, working-group summary, or other official policy document proposing new Olympic-wide eligibility rules for the female category that explicitly address transgender women or athletes with differences of sexual development (DSD)?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether the IOC will officially ban transgender women from the female category before the Milan–Cortina Winter Games. A strong leading indicator is whether the IOC moves from general public statements to publishing an official document that sets out proposed Olympic-wide eligibility rules. In December 2025, AP reported that IOC President Kirsty Coventry set an early-2026 target for a new policy on eligibility in female sports and said the IOC was seeking a unified approach rather than leaving the issue entirely to international federations (AP summary provided in prompt). The Irish Independent likewise reported that the IOC working group had been examining how to protect the female category and that a decision might come around the IOC session in early February 2026 (summary provided in prompt). This suggests that an official paper or draft would be a meaningful intermediate step toward any eventual IOC ban.

The IOC has previously relied on framework-style guidance rather than a blanket centralized rule. The IOC's 2021 'Framework on Fairness, Inclusion and Non-Discrimination on the Basis of Gender Identity and Sex Variations' is the current baseline public document and does not itself impose a categorical Olympic-wide ban. See IOC framework materials at https://olympics.com/ioc/human-rights/fairness-inclusion-nondiscrimination and IOC PDF materials linked from that page. A newly published draft or consultation document explicitly proposing stricter female-category eligibility rules would therefore indicate that the IOC is operationalizing the policy shift discussed in late 2025 reporting.

Because the time window is short, a public document release is a better subquestion than asking whether the final ban itself occurs. It is observable, binary, and likely to meaningfully update beliefs about the ultimate question: if the IOC publishes an official proposal spelling out exclusionary criteria for the female category before February 3, the odds of a final IOC-imposed ban before the Games would likely rise.

Sources:
IOC - Fairness, Inclusion and Non-discrimination on the Basis of Gender Identity and Sex Variations: https://olympics.com/ioc/human-rights/fairness-inclusion-nondiscrimination
The Guardian report referenced by the ultimate question: https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/nov/10/ioc-edges-closer-to-ban-on-transgender-women-in-female-olympic-events
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-13 and 2026-02-03 inclusive, the IOC publicly posts or formally distributes an official document that is accessible on an IOC-controlled website or official IOC communication channel and that proposes, summarizes, or consults on new Olympic-wide eligibility rules for the female category explicitly addressing transgender women and/or athletes with differences of sexual development (DSD).

Qualifying documents include, for example: a draft policy, consultation paper, working-group report/summary, executive board paper summary, or official press release linking to such a document. Mere verbal remarks, media interviews, or news reports describing internal discussions do not qualify unless the IOC itself publishes the underlying document or a formal written summary.

The document must do more than restate the existence of a review; it must describe proposed substantive eligibility criteria, principles, or options for the female category. A document qualifies even if it does not finalize the rules.

Primary resolution sources: IOC official website, IOC news releases, and IOC human-rights/policy pages, including https://olympics.com/ioc and https://olympics.com/ioc/news and https://olympics.com/ioc/human-rights/fairness-inclusion-nondiscrimination. Archived copies from the IOC website are acceptable if the page is later moved. If IOC web publication status is disputed, official IOC social-media posts linking to the document or an IOC PDF hosted on an IOC domain also count.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying IOC-published document is publicly released between 2026-01-13 and 2026-02-03 inclusive.

If the IOC announces that a document exists but does not make it public within the resolution window, that does not count. If publication timing cannot be determined from the IOC page itself, the earliest timestamp from the IOC page, IOC press release, or a reliable web archive snapshot of the IOC page will be used. If no authoritative timing can be established, the question should resolve based on the best available evidence from IOC-controlled channels; if still genuinely indeterminate, it should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A public IOC policy document is a concrete precursor event that would strongly signal institutional momentum toward an IOC-imposed ban, while still being distinct from the ultimate question of whether a ban is officially adopted.
