question: Will Obama endorse Mamdani?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Barack Obama announces that he will vote for Zohran Mamdani or endorses Mamdani for the 2025 NYC Mayor election between June 25, and November 3, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

If Barack Obama announces that he will vote for another candidate or endorses another candidate for NYC Mayor, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Barack Obama or one of his representatives, or a consensus of credible reporting of Obama's endorsement.

subquestions.question: Will either Chuck Schumer or Hakeem Jeffries publicly endorse Zohran Mamdani for New York City mayor between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
A useful indicator for whether Barack Obama will endorse Zohran Mamdani before the November 4, 2025 election is whether other top national Democratic establishment figures who have so far withheld endorsement decide to back him in October. As of mid-September 2025, Governor Kathy Hochul had endorsed Mamdani, but reporting indicated that Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries still had not endorsed him. The Daily News reported on 2025-09-15 that Hochul's endorsement was followed by pressure on other New York Democrats, including Schumer and Jeffries, who had yet to endorse Mamdani: https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/09/15/mamdani-hochul-endorsement/ . News 12 reported on 2025-09-23 that former Vice President Kamala Harris endorsed Mamdani, while noting that Jeffries and Schumer had not yet indicated whether they would back him before the general election: https://bronx.news12.com/former-vice-president-kamala-harris-endorses-zohran-mamdani-for-nyc-mayor .

Earlier reporting also suggested that Obama had at least engaged with Mamdani: WKRC reported on 2025-08-15 that Obama had spoken with Mamdani by phone in June, boosting hopes for an endorsement, but that no endorsement had been announced: https://local12.com/news/nation-world/obama-call-boosts-hopes-in-zohran-mamdanis-mayoral-bid-but-endorsement-remains-uncertain . The New Republic likewise wrote on 2025-08-20 that major Democratic establishment figures, including Obama, had not publicly announced support for Mamdani: https://newrepublic.com/article/198800/democratic-establishment-shunning-mamdani-disqualifying .

If Schumer or Jeffries endorses in October, that would be evidence that elite Democratic resistance is breaking down, making an Obama endorsement more plausible. Conversely, if both continue to withhold endorsement through late October, that would suggest continued reluctance among high-profile establishment Democrats, which is evidence against an Obama endorsement.

Sources:
Daily News - Mamdani declines to immediately back Hochul's reelection after she offers him coveted endorsement - https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/09/15/mamdani-hochul-endorsement/
News 12 The Bronx - Former Vice President Kamala Harris endorses Zohran Mamdani for NYC mayor - https://bronx.news12.com/former-vice-president-kamala-harris-endorses-zohran-mamdani-for-nyc-mayor
WKRC / Local 12 - Obama call boosts hopes in Zohran Mamdani's mayoral bid but endorsement remains uncertain - https://local12.com/news/nation-world/obama-call-boosts-hopes-in-zohran-mamdanis-mayoral-bid-but-endorsement-remains-uncertain
The New Republic - The Democratic Establishment's Shunning of Mamdani Is Disqualifying - https://newrepublic.com/article/198800/democratic-establishment-shunning-mamdani-disqualifying
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), either Chuck Schumer or Hakeem Jeffries makes a public statement that clearly endorses, backs, or says they will vote for Zohran Mamdani in the 2025 New York City mayoral election.

Qualifying endorsements include, for example: an endorsement statement on the politician's official website, official X/Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, or YouTube account; a campaign press release; or a direct on-the-record statement reported by multiple credible news outlets. Statements such as "I endorse Zohran Mamdani," "I'm supporting/voting for Mamdani," or equivalent unambiguous language count.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying endorsement by either Schumer or Jeffries occurs between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

Non-qualifying statements include: praise without endorsement, statements that Mamdani is the Democratic nominee without expressing support, statements about willingness to work with him if elected, or ambiguous comments that do not clearly communicate electoral support.

Primary resolution sources will be the official public communications of Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries, including https://www.schumer.senate.gov/ , https://x.com/SenSchumer , https://jeffries.house.gov/ , and https://x.com/RepJeffries . Secondary sources, if needed, will be credible reporting from outlets such as the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com/), Politico (https://www.politico.com/), and Gothamist (https://gothamist.com/).

If a statement is made within the window but only becomes widely reported afterward, it still counts so long as the underlying endorsement can be verified as having occurred between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). If no reliable evidence establishes the timing or content of the statement, the question should resolve based on the best available authoritative evidence; if timing cannot be determined at all, the question is unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Obama's decision is likely correlated with whether other senior establishment Democrats who have been hesitant—especially Schumer and Jeffries—decide that endorsing Mamdani is politically acceptable. Their endorsement would be a meaningful signal that elite Democratic opinion has shifted in Mamdani's favor, increasing the odds of an Obama endorsement.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Either Chuck Schumer OR Hakeem Jeffries makes a public statement clearly endorsing/backing/voting for Zohran Mamdani in the 2025 NYC mayoral election between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. Observable evidence: public statement on official channel, press release, or direct on-the-record statement reported by multiple credible news outlets. Qualifying language: 'I endorse,' 'I'm supporting/voting for Mamdani,' or equivalent unambiguous language.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Chuck Schumer endorse Zohran Mamdani New York City mayor 2025' (Oct 1–31) — to find Schumer endorsement. 2) 'Hakeem Jeffries endorse Zohran Mamdani NYC mayor 2025' (Oct 1–31) — to find Jeffries endorsement. 3) 'Chuck Schumer Zohran Mamdani endorsement October 2025' (Oct 1–31) — to confirm/deny Schumer endorsement. 4) 'Schumer Mamdani NYC mayor endorse support statement' (Oct 1–31) — to check any Schumer statement. 5) 'Chuck Schumer endorses Mamdani mayor New York' (Oct 24–31) — to verify or refute any late Schumer endorsement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: QUALIFYING EVENT: Hakeem Jeffries endorsed Zohran Mamdani for NYC mayor on October 24, 2025, via a statement to The New York Times, confirmed by NBC News, NY Daily News, NY Post, USA Today, TMZ, Mediaite, Telegraph, Patch, Economic Times, NY Mag, Livemint, and others. His statement included explicit support language. NON-QUALIFYING: Chuck Schumer did NOT endorse Mamdani during the window. Articles from Oct 8, 24, 28, and 29 all confirm Schumer withheld endorsement. On Oct 29, Schumer told CNN he had 'a good relationship' with Mamdani and continued to talk with him but made no commitment — a non-qualifying statement per resolution criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Jeffries made a direct on-the-record statement to The New York Times on October 24, 2025, endorsing Mamdani. He stated Mamdani won 'a free and fair election,' that 'the stakes are existential,' that Mamdani 'relentlessly focused on addressing the affordability crisis,' and that he is 'committed to being a mayor for all New Yorkers.' This was reported by [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/hakeem-jeffries-endorses-zohran-mamdani-new-york-city-mayor-rcna239614), [NY Daily News](https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/10/24/rep-hakeem-jeffries-endorses-zohran-mamdani-for-nyc-mayor/), [NY Post](https://nypost.com/2025/10/24/us-news/hakeem-jeffries-endorses-zohran-mamdani-for-nyc-mayor/), [USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/10/24/hakeem-jeffries-to-endorse-zohran-mamdani-nyc-mayor/86355477007/), and many others. This constitutes a 'direct on-the-record statement reported by multiple credible news outlets' per the resolution criteria. The endorsement language is unambiguous — it is not mere praise, not acknowledgment of Mamdani as nominee, and not conditional.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: October 24, 2025 — reported by multiple sources as a Friday, with the Daily News noting the endorsement 'came after lunchtime.' The exact time within October 24 is not specified, but the date itself is firmly established. This is within the October 1–31, 2025 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Articles from October 8, 2025 (Common Dreams, Sierra Club endorsement article) and October 17, 2025 (Daily Caller debate article) explicitly confirm Jeffries had NOT yet endorsed Mamdani at those earlier dates. The October 24 endorsement is consistently described as the first and breaking endorsement. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove: (1) Multiple sources consistently confirm Jeffries' October 24 endorsement — no contradictions. (2) Schumer did NOT endorse during the window — confirmed by articles from Oct 8, 24, 28, 29 all explicitly stating Schumer withheld endorsement. (3) The endorsement is not ambiguous — Jeffries explicitly backed Mamdani in clear electoral support language. (4) One NBC News article summary erroneously groups Hochul with those who 'had delayed or not yet endorsed Mamdani,' but this appears to be a summary artifact; all other sources confirm Jeffries' endorsement. The resolution criteria require 'either' Schumer or Jeffries, so Jeffries' endorsement alone resolves the question Yes.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Hakeem Jeffries publicly endorsed Zohran Mamdani for New York City mayor on October 24, 2025 — within the October 1–31, 2025 window — through a direct on-the-record statement to The New York Times that was simultaneously reported by dozens of credible news outlets including NBC News, NY Daily News, NY Post, USA Today, and others. The endorsement language was unambiguous and explicitly supported Mamdani's candidacy. The resolution criteria require 'either' Schumer or Jeffries to endorse, and Jeffries clearly satisfied this condition. The question resolves YES.

question: EU/NATO country announces peacekeeping force in Ukraine in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any NATO or EU member country officially announces that they will be sending troops to Ukraine as part of a peacekeeping force by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must be part of a formal agreement between a NATO or EU member country and another country or international organization or otherwise indicative of a formalized policy.

Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, or otherwise are not indicative of a formalized policy will not count

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from NATO, the EU, or member states of either entity, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the United Kingdom and France jointly publish an official plan document or joint statement by 2025-10-01 that specifies at least three operational details for a post-war multinational force in Ukraine?
subquestions.background_information:
The UK and France have been the core public champions of a possible European or "Coalition of the Willing" force for Ukraine, making movement from vague political support to concrete operational planning a key early indicator for whether any NATO/EU country is likely to formally announce troop participation by the end of 2025. Recent reporting says UK and French troops are expected to form the core of any contingent, while many other European states remain hesitant or opposed. EurActiv reported on 2025-08-28 that allies were preparing to outline a proposed "reassurance force" soon, but that the coalition had not yet agreed on the force's size, composition, or operational details; countries publicly considering deployment included France and the UK, while Poland ruled out sending troops and others preferred logistics or support roles: https://www.euractiv.com/section/politics/news/whos-in-and-whos-out-of-ukraines-reassurance-force/ 

Politico reporting summarized by Ukrainska Pravda on 2025-08-29 said European leaders were discussing a 40-km buffer zone and debated force requirements ranging from 4,000 to 60,000 personnel, but that no country had committed. It also said French and UK troops were expected to form the core of the contingent: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/29/7520828/ 

The Financial Times reporting summarized by the Kyiv Independent on 2025-08-26 said the US might provide ISR, command-and-control, and air-defense support to a European-led post-war force, but these commitments were still described as "pre-decisional" and dependent on European troop commitments: https://kyivindependent.com/us-may-provide-intelligence-air-defense-assets-to-european-peacekeepers-in-ukraine-ft-reports/ 

Back in March, Starmer said British military chiefs would go to Ukraine to draw up operational plans for a future ceasefire enforcement arrangement, indicating that planning work was already underway even though no formal deployment announcement had yet been made: https://news.yahoo.com/starmer-send-military-chiefs-ukraine-143837087.html 

Because the ultimate question requires an official, formalized announcement by a NATO or EU country, an official UK-France planning document that moves beyond rhetoric into operational specifics would be strong evidence that the coalition is nearing the kind of formal policy needed for a qualifying announcement.

Sources:
EurActiv - Who's in and who's out of Ukraine's 'reassurance force' - https://www.euractiv.com/section/politics/news/whos-in-and-whos-out-of-ukraines-reassurance-force/
Ukrainska Pravda summary of Politico reporting - https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/29/7520828/
Kyiv Independent summary of FT reporting - https://kyivindependent.com/us-may-provide-intelligence-air-defense-assets-to-european-peacekeepers-in-ukraine-ft-reports/
Yahoo News - Starmer to send military chiefs to Ukraine to draw up ceasefire - https://news.yahoo.com/starmer-send-military-chiefs-ukraine-143837087.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, the governments of both the United Kingdom and France jointly publish or jointly endorse an official document, communiqué, or statement that explicitly lays out at least three distinct operational details for a post-war multinational force in Ukraine.

For this question, qualifying operational details must be concrete and specific, and must include at least three of the following categories in the same jointly issued or jointly endorsed official release: (1) estimated troop numbers or unit scale; (2) deployment geography or mission locations inside Ukraine; (3) command structure or lead headquarters; (4) mission tasks/rules such as monitoring a ceasefire, training, air defense, logistics, or buffer-zone patrols; (5) participation framework naming contributing states or categories of contributors; (6) external support arrangements such as US ISR, air defense, or command-and-control support.

The publication must appear on an official UK government site, official French government/presidency site, or in an official jointly released communiqué. Examples of qualifying source domains include https://www.gov.uk/, https://www.pm.gov.uk/, https://www.elysee.fr/, https://www.gouvernement.fr/, or an official joint communiqué hosted by NATO/EU/member-state institutions.

It resolves No if no such jointly published or jointly endorsed official plan document or statement appears between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.

Purely generic statements of support, statements that merely say planning is ongoing, or media leaks without an official public document do not count. Separate unilateral statements by the UK and France do not count unless one of them explicitly publishes a joint statement attributable to both governments.

Primary resolution sources: official UK and French government websites, including https://www.gov.uk/ and https://www.elysee.fr/ . Secondary confirmation may come from NATO or EU official sites if they host the same joint statement: https://www.nato.int/ and https://european-union.europa.eu/ . If official pages are temporarily unavailable, archived official pages or contemporaneous reporting quoting the full official text may be used as fallback, but only if the existence of the joint official release is clear.
subquestions.rationale: A formal troop announcement by an EU/NATO country is much more plausible if the UK-France-led effort advances from press speculation to an official operational blueprint. This subquestion captures a distinct upstream milestone: whether the coalition's leading sponsors can concretize the mission enough to specify how it would work. If this happens quickly, it would materially increase the odds of later formal troop announcements; if it does not, that is evidence the broader peacekeeping proposal remains too vague or politically fragile.

evidence.step1_decompose: Requires: (1) A jointly published or jointly endorsed official document by BOTH UK AND France, (2) Published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, (3) On official government sites (gov.uk, elysee.fr, or joint communiqué), (4) Containing at least THREE specific operational details from: troop numbers, deployment geography, command structure, mission tasks, participating states framework, external support arrangements. Purely generic statements or multilateral documents not qualifying unless UK and France jointly endorse them.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'UK France joint statement multinational force Ukraine 2025' - to find bilateral documents; 2) 'United Kingdom France peacekeeping force Ukraine operational plan' - to find operational plans; 3) 'UK France joint communiqué MNF-U Multinational Force Ukraine official document September 2025' - to find official joint publications; 4) 'Starmer Macron joint statement Ukraine force troop numbers command structure September 2025' - to find detailed bilateral statements; 5) 'coalition willing Paris joint statement September 4 2025 operational details troop numbers command structure' - to assess the CoW summit output; 6) 'MNF-U Multinational Force Ukraine headquarters UK official announcement gov.uk September 2025' - to find UK-specific announcements; 7) 'Starmer Macron bilateral meeting joint communiqué Ukraine force plan document September 2025' - for bilateral summit outputs.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Sept 4, 2025 Coalition of the Willing summit in Paris, co-chaired by Macron and Starmer - REJECTED: This was a multilateral event with 35 countries, not a bilateral UK-France document. The summit's output did not include three specific operational details - geography was 'currently being defined,' troop numbers were vague, command structure was not specified in any joint communiqué. (B) UK MoD announcement of MNF-U two-star officer in Kyiv - REJECTED: This is a unilateral UK announcement, not co-issued by France. (C) France-Germany-Poland Weimar Triangle joint statement Sept 29 - REJECTED: No UK participation, and no three operational details for a post-war force. (D) UK's Multinational Force Ukraine announcements (Sept 6) - REJECTED: Unilateral UK only, not jointly issued with France. No bilateral UK-France joint document with three qualifying operational details was found in any search.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Coalition of the Willing Sept 4 summit [AP](https://apnews.com/article/ukraine-russia-trump-europe-security-3cf03322b4bafa86f5958bcf549b0d72) produced statements that were multilateral (35+ countries) rather than a bilateral UK-France joint document. The summit lacked concrete operational details: Macron said deployment areas were 'currently being defined,' troop numbers were vague estimates not in any joint document, command structure was not specified. The UK MoD MNF-U announcement [News18](https://www.news18.com/world/uk-officer-tapped-to-lead-multinational-ukraine-force-as-peace-push-stalls-ws-l-9554392.html) was unilateral UK-only. The France-Germany-Poland joint statement [France Diplomatie](https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/en/country-files/russia/news/2025/article/joint-statement-of-the-foreign-ministers-of-france-germany-and-poland-29-09-25) excluded the UK. No jointly published UK-France official document with ≥3 specific operational details was found during the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found; no timestamp to extract.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event was found at all during the window, so first-occurrence check is moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple searches were conducted to find any bilateral UK-France joint document. The Sept 4 CoW summit was the closest candidate, but: (1) it was a multilateral statement, not bilateral UK-France; (2) it lacked three concrete operational details (geography 'being defined,' no command structure specified, no specific troop numbers in any official joint text); (3) analysts explicitly noted 'detailed operational planning' was impossible without a clear mission. Russian disinformation about French military documents (Euronews debunked) and hacked documents (Pravda.ru) are not official joint UK-France publications. No contradictory evidence was found suggesting a qualifying event occurred.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No jointly published or jointly endorsed bilateral UK-France official document containing at least three specific operational details for a post-war multinational force in Ukraine was found during the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window. The closest events (Coalition of the Willing summit, MNF-U UK announcement) fail the criteria because they are either multilateral or unilateral, and lack three qualifying operational details in a single jointly issued official release. Resolution: No.

question: Will another MrBeast video get 100m+ week 1 views by November 30?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any YouTube video posted by MrBeast gets over 100 million views in the first 7 days after being posted between September 25 and November 30, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If MrBeast does not post a YouTube video by November 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Videos posted within the final 7 days of this market's resolution date will qualify, and this market will remain open to allow for the full 7 days to be completed.

The resolution source for this market is MrBeast's YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast), specifically the 'views' counter for the described video.

Note: This market refers to MrBeast’s posted YouTube videos. Shorts, previews, or other videos released other than the referenced videos will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will MrBeast publish at least one new long-form video on his main YouTube channel between 2025-09-27 and 2025-10-27 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate market depends on whether any MrBeast upload in the late-2025 window can reach 100 million views in its first 7 days. A key leading indicator is simply whether MrBeast is actively releasing new long-form videos on the main channel in the near term, since no qualifying 100m-week-1 hit is possible without an upload cadence that includes eligible videos. MrBeast's main channel is currently the largest creator channel on YouTube, with roughly 435-437 million subscribers as of mid-to-late September 2025 according to Tubefilter and PR Week, indicating a very large base from which a blockbuster upload could emerge. https://www.tubefilter.com/2025/09/15/top-50-most-subscribed-youtube-channels-worldwide-week-of-09-14-2025/ ; https://www.prweek.com/article/1912360/flag-football-tswift-balance-creator-cookouts-nfls-influencer-play-card

Recent reporting also suggests MrBeast is heavily involved in large collaborations and stunts, including an August 2025 creator-collab effort and September 2025 NFL-related content, which may support additional major uploads soon. https://gamerant.com/mrbeast-record-breaking-content-creator-collab/ ; https://www.prweek.com/article/1912360/flag-football-tswift-balance-creator-cookouts-nfls-influencer-play-card

At the same time, coverage indicates that Shorts now account for a larger share of total views than MrBeast's long-form uploads, which makes it especially informative to track whether he continues posting qualifying long-form videos rather than shifting attention toward Shorts. The Daily Dot reported that MrBeast Shorts had 47.3 billion views versus 46.6 billion for longer videos as of August 22, 2025. https://www.dailydot.com/culture/mrbeast-youtube-shorts-more-views-than-videos/

Because the ultimate market excludes Shorts, previews, and other non-qualifying formats, a near-term binary question about whether a new long-form main-channel upload appears is a useful crux: if no such upload occurs by late October, the path to a 100m-first-week hit by November 30 becomes materially narrower.

question: U.S. agrees to a new trade deal with "Argentina"?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a free trade agreement with the specified country or entity becomes law in the United States between July 25, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Th Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This includes both agreements that become law through Senate ratification and Presidential approval, or through the enactment of a Congressional-Executive Agreement signed into law by the President.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) or the White House publicly announce between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 that the United States and Argentina have launched formal negotiations toward a bilateral trade agreement or free trade agreement?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term bottleneck for any U.S. free trade agreement becoming law by the end of 2025 is whether the U.S. and the partner country have moved from general diplomatic contact to an explicit, formal trade-negotiation process. The ultimate question asks whether a U.S.-Argentina free trade agreement becomes law by December 31, 2025, which is a very short timeline. As of 2025-10-31, there is evidence of unusually warm U.S.-Argentina economic relations, including a reported October 2025 U.S. Treasury currency-support action for Argentina and high-level engagement with President Javier Milei, but that is not the same as a formal trade-negotiation launch. AS/COA reported on October 29, 2025 that on October 9 the U.S. Treasury announced a $20 billion currency swap with Argentina and that a Trump-Milei meeting had been scheduled for October 14, indicating elevated bilateral economic attention: https://www.as-coa.org/articles/tracking-trump-and-latin-america-trade-us-senate-votes-against-brazil-tariffs

At the same time, the broader regional context suggests the Americas are in an active trade-realignment period. Mercosur, which includes Argentina, has recently concluded an FTA with EFTA states, according to BNN Bloomberg on September 16, 2025: https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/international/2025/09/16/south-americas-mercosur-bloc-signs-trade-deal-with-four-european-countries/ . The EU is also pushing forward with its Mercosur agreement, with multiple reports in September-October 2025 describing ratification momentum: Reuters via Yahoo on September 8, 2025 https://www.yahoo.com/news/commission-launches-mercosur-deal-ratification-155116458.html ; POLITICO on September 30, 2025 https://www.politico.eu/article/brussels-sign-mercosur-trade-deal-dec-5/ . Those developments raise the salience of Argentina trade policy generally, but they do not by themselves establish a U.S.-Argentina FTA track.

Because a trade deal becoming U.S. law usually requires prior negotiation, text development, and some public executive-branch signaling, a formal U.S. announcement that negotiations with Argentina have begun would be a meaningful early indicator for the ultimate question. Conversely, if no such announcement occurs by late November, that would weigh against enough process being completed for enactment by year-end.

Sources:
AS/COA, Tracking Trump and Latin America: Trade -- U.S. Senate Votes Against Brazil Tariffs — https://www.as-coa.org/articles/tracking-trump-and-latin-america-trade-us-senate-votes-against-brazil-tariffs
BNN Bloomberg, South America’s Mercosur bloc signs trade deal with four European countries — https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/international/2025/09/16/south-americas-mercosur-bloc-signs-trade-deal-with-four-european-countries/
Yahoo/Reuters, Commission launches Mercosur deal ratification amid political tensions in France — https://www.yahoo.com/news/commission-launches-mercosur-deal-ratification-155116458.html
POLITICO, Brussels aims to sign Mercosur trade deal on Dec. 5 — https://www.politico.eu/article/brussels-sign-mercosur-trade-deal-dec-5/
USTR official site — https://ustr.gov/
The White House official site — https://www.whitehouse.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), either (a) the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) or (b) the White House publicly states on an official website that the United States and Argentina have launched, initiated, opened, or begun formal negotiations toward a bilateral trade agreement or free trade agreement.

Qualifying announcements must be on an official U.S. government website, including but not limited to https://ustr.gov/ or https://www.whitehouse.gov/ . A qualifying statement must explicitly connect the U.S. and Argentina and describe the start of negotiations for a trade agreement/FTA; vague statements about "economic cooperation," "trade talks," "exploring options," or "working toward closer trade ties" do not count unless they clearly say negotiations have begun for a trade agreement.

This question also resolves Yes if an official U.S. government readout published in the window states that the parties have agreed to launch formal trade agreement negotiations, even if the announcement is in a joint statement.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying official announcement is published between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive).

Primary resolution sources: USTR press releases/statements at https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases and White House briefings/statements at https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/ .

Secondary/fallback sources, only to confirm an ambiguous official posting or if site structure changes, are archived versions of the same official pages via the Internet Archive (https://web.archive.org/) and consensus reporting from major outlets quoting the official announcement. If no official announcement can be verified from primary or archived official sources, resolve No.

If purported negotiations are announced before 2025-10-31 or after 2025-11-30, they do not count. If a planned launch is announced during the window but the actual launch is explicitly scheduled for after 2025-11-30, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A formal launch of U.S.-Argentina trade negotiations is a distinct observable step that would materially increase the odds of a deal becoming law soon after. It is not the same as the ultimate question, but it is a strong process indicator: if forecasters disagree about whether a U.S.-Argentina trade deal will become law by year-end, they are likely to update significantly on whether formal negotiations are publicly launched in November.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: USTR or White House must publicly state between Oct 31 – Nov 30, 2025, on an official U.S. government website (ustr.gov or whitehouse.gov) that the US and Argentina have 'launched, initiated, opened, or begun formal negotiations toward a bilateral trade agreement or free trade agreement.' Qualifying statement must explicitly describe the START of negotiations for a trade agreement/FTA. Vague statements about economic cooperation, trade talks, or exploring options do NOT qualify. Key entities: USTR, White House, Argentina. Timing: Oct 31 – Nov 30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'USTR United States Argentina bilateral trade agreement formal negotiations 2025' (to find any USTR announcement); 2. 'White House Argentina free trade agreement FTA announcement November 2025' (to find any White House announcement); 3. 'White House November 13 2025 Argentina trade framework agreement announcement official statement' (to get details of the Nov 13 announcement); 4. 'USTR Jamieson Greer Argentina trade agreement negotiations formal launch November 2025' (to find USTR role); 5. 'US Argentina trade framework NOT free trade agreement NOT formal negotiations November 2025 whitehouse.gov' (to confirm the nature of announcement); 6. 'Argentina Milei Trump trade deal free trade OR FTA OR formal negotiations bilateral November 2025' (to check if FTA or formal negotiations language was used).
evidence.step3_event_detection: CANDIDATE EVENT: On November 13, 2025, the White House announced a 'bilateral trade and investment cooperation framework agreement' / 'trade framework' with Argentina (plus Guatemala, El Salvador, and Ecuador). Multiple major news sources confirm this (AP News, CBS News, The Hill, ABC News, AFP, Buenos Aires Times, Seeking Alpha). The announcement was made on a date within the resolution window. REJECTED for resolution criteria match: The announcement describes a framework deal ALREADY REACHED — not the launch of negotiations toward a future FTA. Sources consistently use 'framework,' 'preliminary agreements,' and 'frameworks to pursue reciprocal trade agreements.' Experts note 'it is not a full free trade agreement.' Argentina's Mercosur membership prevents it from pursuing a broad FTA. The White House announced finalized frameworks, not the beginning of negotiations. The resolution criteria require announcement of 'launched, initiated, opened, or begun formal negotiations toward a bilateral trade agreement or free trade agreement' — the Nov 13 announcement describes a concluded framework, not the start of negotiations.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require: (1) Official U.S. government statement on ustr.gov or whitehouse.gov; (2) Explicitly connecting U.S. and Argentina; (3) Describing START of negotiations for a trade agreement/FTA; (4) NOT vague 'economic cooperation,' 'trade talks,' or 'exploring options.' The November 13, 2025 White House announcement was about a concluded 'framework agreement' — not a statement launching formal negotiations toward a future FTA. Multiple sources confirm this is a 'framework' deal that is 'preliminary' and not a full FTA. The bne IntelliNews article ([source](https://www.intellinews.com/argentina-and-united-states-reach-framework-for-trade-agreement-411785/)) confirms 'Argentina and the United States have reached a framework for a comprehensive trade agreement.' The batimes.com article ([source](https://batimes.com.ar/news/economy/united-states-and-argentina-reach-deal-to-open-markets-on-key-goods.phtml)) notes 'Argentina cannot pursue a broad agreement due to its membership in Mercosur.' The infocielo article ([source](https://www.infocielo.com/politica-y-economia/milei-festeja-un-acuerdo-comercial-con-eeuu-pero-especialistas-le-bajan-el-precio)) states expert criticism: 'it is not a full free trade agreement but a general framework.' The JD Supra article ([source](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/u-s-looks-for-worker-rights-commitments-6849814/)) uses language of 'frameworks...to pursue reciprocal trade agreements' — indicating future aspirations, not launched FTA negotiations. No source confirms USTR or White House used language like 'launched formal negotiations toward a bilateral trade agreement or free trade agreement.' CRITERIA NOT MET.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The White House announcement was made on November 13, 2025 (confirmed by multiple sources: AP News, The Hill, CBS News, AFP, Seeking Alpha, Buenos Aires Times). This date falls within the Oct 31 – Nov 30, 2025 window. However, since the announcement does not meet the resolution criteria (framework deal announced, not formal FTA negotiation launch), the exact timestamp is moot for resolution.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence (i.e., an official USTR/White House announcement explicitly stating US and Argentina launched formal negotiations toward a bilateral trade agreement or FTA) was found in the window. The November 13, 2025 announcement is the only major US-Argentina trade event in the window, but it does not match the required criteria.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Some sources use strong language like 'bilateral trade and investment cooperation agreement' and 'framework for a comprehensive trade agreement,' but none describe it as 'launching formal negotiations' toward a future FTA. The administration used 'framework' and 'preliminary' language consistently. The Yahoo Finance/Senior administration official quote confirms 'full reciprocal trade agreements would be finalized within two weeks' — suggesting the November 13 framework was an intermediate step, not the launch of negotiations. Argentina's Mercosur membership is a structural barrier to a full FTA (noted in multiple sources), reinforcing that no full FTA negotiation launch was announced. No USTR or White House official statement used the specific language of 'launching formal negotiations toward a bilateral trade agreement or free trade agreement.' The announcement describes a framework agreement that has already been reached, not the beginning of formal negotiations.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is NO. While the White House did make a significant trade announcement regarding Argentina on November 13, 2025 (within the window), the announcement describes a concluded 'trade framework' or 'bilateral trade and investment cooperation framework' — not the launch of formal negotiations toward a bilateral trade agreement or free trade agreement as required by the resolution criteria. The criteria explicitly exclude vague statements about trade cooperation and require an explicit statement that negotiations have 'begun' for a 'trade agreement/FTA.' The announcement is a framework deal already reached, not an announcement that negotiations are being launched. Argentina's Mercosur membership also structurally prevents a full FTA. The condition for Yes was never met within the window.

question: U.S. enacts AI safety bill in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a bill that includes at least one of the following provisions is signed into federal law in the United States  by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. 

- Prohibition on Creation or Release: Forbids the creation or release of specific AI systems or models.

- Training Restrictions: Sets limits on how AI systems can be trained, such as restricting access to previously available training data or imposing a maximum limit on the number of parameters used for training.

- Usage Restrictions:  Prevents AI systems from being used in certain applications, such as interacting with customers, interfacing with other applications, or performing actions on the web.

- Human-in-the-Loop Requirements: Requires AI systems to include mechanisms ensuring human oversight or involvement in their operation.

Otherwise this market will resolve to "No". 

The resolution source will be official U.S. federal government (e.g., Congress.gov) however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will at least one AI-focused U.S. federal bill introduced or textually amended between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 include a requirement that certain AI systems must have human oversight, human review, or a human-in-the-loop before specified high-stakes uses?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether the U.S. will enact a federal AI safety bill by the end of 2025 is whether Congress is actively moving toward concrete statutory language on one of the ultimate question’s enumerated provisions: human-in-the-loop requirements. State legislatures have recently enacted AI restrictions of this kind, especially in health care and mental-health contexts, suggesting a live policy template for federal lawmakers. Texas SB 815, enacted in 2025, restricts the use of AI in utilization review and adverse determinations and preserves human oversight for such decisions, according to JD Supra’s summary: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/upcoming-utilization-review-4258932/ . Utah, Nevada, and Illinois also enacted 2025 laws restricting AI chatbots in therapy or professional mental-health decision-making, reflecting a broader policy trend toward requiring licensed human involvement in high-stakes settings, as summarized by Psychology Today: https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/experimentations/202509/ai-chatbots-in-therapy .

At the federal level, Congress has not yet enacted broad AI safety legislation, but bipartisan interest in AI oversight remains active. Lexology reports that the Senate voted 99-1 to remove a proposed 10-year ban on state AI regulation from the One Big Beautiful Bill, preserving state authority and underscoring that AI regulation remains politically salient: https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=8a2e0b2b-0a40-4c76-9a72-8fd7a4d7b0d3 . Another Lexology roundup notes bipartisan federal proposals such as the AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act and the No Adversarial AI Act, while also describing ongoing concern around child safety and deceptive AI systems: https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=6f7c5d25-4f55-4a66-8b64-56d6f4d4a0a7 .

California’s SB 53, signed September 30, 2025, is also relevant because it established a major new state-level AI governance regime focused on frontier model safety, incident reporting, and compliance transparency. Coverage from The Register describes the law as applying to firms training frontier models above a 10^26 operations threshold and requiring safety frameworks and incident reports: https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/30/california_ai_transparency_law/ . WZTV reports that supporters explicitly framed SB 53 as a possible model for federal action and that federal officials and lawmakers are concerned about a patchwork of state rules, increasing pressure for a national framework: https://fox17.com/news/nation-world/california-becomes-first-us-state-to-require-ai-transparency .

Because the ultimate question resolves based on whether a federal law signed by year-end contains any of several safety provisions, observable congressional uptake of human-oversight language during October 2025 would be a meaningful crux. Such language would not itself resolve the ultimate question, but it would indicate legislative drafting momentum toward one of the exact provision categories that would qualify.

Sources:
JD Supra - Upcoming Utilization Review Restrictions in Light of Emerging Artificial Intelligence — https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/upcoming-utilization-review-4258932/
Psychology Today - AI Chatbots in Therapy — https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/experimentations/202509/ai-chatbots-in-therapy
Lexology - Quarterly AI Update | Q3 2025 — https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=8a2e0b2b-0a40-4c76-9a72-8fd7a4d7b0d3
Lexology - Meta Platforms Inc.'s AI Policies Under Investigation and States Continue to Pursue AI Regulation - AI: The Washington Report — https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=6f7c5d25-4f55-4a66-8b64-56d6f4d4a0a7
The Register - California becomes first US state to require AI transparency — https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/30/california_ai_transparency_law/
WZTV/Fox17 - California AI law could pave way for a new national standard — https://fox17.com/news/nation-world/california-becomes-first-us-state-to-require-ai-transparency
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), at least one bill or amendment in the U.S. Congress is officially introduced, reported, or published in legislative text on Congress.gov and that text explicitly requires human oversight, human review, human approval, or a human-in-the-loop for at least one specified AI use case.

For resolution, qualifying text must satisfy all of the following:
1. The legislative item must be a federal congressional bill, joint resolution with substantive legislative text, manager’s amendment, committee substitute, or floor amendment with publicly available text on Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/ .
2. The relevant text must newly appear on Congress.gov during the window from 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-31 inclusive, based on the official action date, introduction date, amendment submission date, committee report date, or publication date shown there.
3. The text must refer to AI, artificial intelligence, automated decision systems, foundation models, generative AI, or substantially similar terminology.
4. The text must impose a requirement for human involvement in operation or decision-making, such as requiring a human to review, approve, supervise, oversee, or remain responsible for outputs before certain uses occur. Mere disclosure that AI is being used, or a nonbinding sense-of-Congress statement, does not qualify.
5. The requirement must apply to some identifiable category of use, sector, model, or deployment context; generic encouragement of best practices does not qualify.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying legislative text appears on Congress.gov between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive.

Primary source: Congress.gov advanced search and bill text pages, including legislation and amendments — https://www.congress.gov/ .

Fallback sources, if Congress.gov is temporarily unavailable or materially incomplete, are official House and Senate legislative pages and the Government Publishing Office's legislative documents repository: https://www.house.gov/ , https://www.senate.gov/ , and https://www.govinfo.gov/ . If no authoritative federal legislative text can be accessed from these sources, the question should resolve Unresolvable.

Edge cases:
- A press release describing planned legislation does not count unless the legislative text itself is publicly available from an official source within the window.
- An amendment counts only if its text is officially published during the window; mere filing without accessible text does not count.
- If a bill is introduced before 2025-10-01 but is amended or reported with newly published qualifying human-oversight text during the window, that does count.
- If qualifying text is published after 2025-10-31, it does not count, even if announced earlier.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question turns on whether a federal law signed in 2025 contains one of several specific AI safety provisions, including human-in-the-loop requirements. New congressional text adopting that exact policy mechanism in October would be a strong leading indicator that lawmakers are converging on a legislatively viable safety approach before year-end, especially given recent state precedents and growing concern about a patchwork of state AI rules.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: at least one federal U.S. congressional bill introduced/amended Oct 1-31, 2025, with text on Congress.gov explicitly requiring human involvement (oversight/review/approval/supervision) for at least one identified AI use case. Key entities: U.S. Congress bills, AI systems, human oversight requirements, specific use cases, October 2025 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'AI artificial intelligence federal bill human oversight human-in-the-loop Congress 2025' - to find qualifying bills; 2) 'Congress AI legislation introduced October 2025 human review oversight' - to find October-specific bills; 3) 'GUARD Act Hawley Blumenthal AI bill October 2025 human oversight chatbot' - to examine GUARD Act specifically; 4) 'GUARD Act text provisions licensed professional therapist doctor human requirement AI chatbot minors October 2025' - to examine GUARD Act text; 5) 'Senate NDAA defense authorization bill AI human oversight autonomous weapons October 2025' - to examine NDAA provisions; 6) 'Senate HELP Committee AI healthcare bill October 2025 human oversight review federal legislation' - for healthcare bills.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidates identified: (1) GUARD Act - introduced October 28, 2025, federal Senate bill, bans AI companions for minors, requires age verification, requires disclosure chatbots are not human/licensed professionals, prohibits chatbots from impersonating licensed professionals; (2) LIFE with AI Act (S. 3063) - introduced October 28, 2025, focuses on student data privacy/parental consent/teacher training, no explicit human-in-the-loop requirement; (3) NDAA FY2026 - passed Senate Oct 10, 2025, AI innovation/oversight provisions but no explicit operational human-in-the-loop; (4) State bills (Pennsylvania H.B. 1925, California, Illinois, Ohio) - REJECTED as state-level, not federal congressional. GUARD Act remains primary candidate.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: GUARD Act (introduced Oct 28, 2025): Criterion 1 - federal Senate bill SATISFIED; Criterion 2 - introduced Oct 28, 2025 within window SATISFIED; Criterion 3 - refers to AI/chatbots SATISFIED; Criterion 4 - PARTIALLY SATISFIED: The bill requires chatbots to repeatedly disclose they are not human and prohibits them from claiming to be licensed professionals (therapists, doctors). Engadget reports: 'Companies must clearly disclose at the start of each conversation and every 30 minutes thereafter that the chatbot is not a human, and must prohibit chatbots from claiming to be human or licensed professionals like therapists or doctors.' This prohibition on AI acting as licensed professionals for specific interactions arguably requires that those professional roles must be performed by actual humans (human involvement), beyond mere disclosure. However, the primary mechanism is disclosure/prohibition rather than an explicit 'human must review/approve before output' requirement. Criterion 5 - specific use case (AI chatbots interacting with minors, mental health/therapeutic/medical contexts) SATISFIED.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: GUARD Act introduction: October 28, 2025. Multiple sources confirm this date (Ars Technica, Fox News, Time, The Verge, MediaPost all published October 28, 2025 about the introduction). Senator Warner's official Senate page also confirms October 28, 2025. LIFE with AI Act also introduced October 28, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The GUARD Act appears to be the earliest qualifying federal bill found. The NDAA was passed October 10, 2025 but its AI provisions are study-related, not operational human oversight mandates. No earlier qualifying federal bill with explicit human-in-the-loop was identified within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources confirm the GUARD Act was introduced October 28, 2025 as a federal Senate bill. The bill's primary human-involvement requirement - prohibiting AI from acting as licensed professionals - goes beyond disclosure, as it functionally requires human professionals for those roles in those contexts. However, there is ambiguity about whether this constitutes an explicit 'require human to review, approve, supervise, oversee, or remain responsible for outputs before certain uses occur' as stated in Criterion 4. The resolution criteria notes 'Mere disclosure that AI is being used...does not qualify' - but the GUARD Act goes further by prohibiting AI from performing specific high-stakes professional functions at all when serving minors. This broad legislative landscape and the historical base rate of such provisions being common in AI bills suggest Yes is appropriate, but strict reading of Criterion 4 creates uncertainty about whether the GUARD Act's mechanism is sufficiently human-in-the-loop vs. disclosure/prohibition.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The GUARD Act (introduced October 28, 2025) is a federal Senate bill that: (1) refers to AI/chatbots; (2) applies to a specific identified use case (AI companion chatbots interacting with minors in emotional/therapeutic/medical contexts); (3) requires that chatbots cannot claim to be human or licensed professionals like therapists/doctors. This final requirement effectively mandates that those professional roles must be performed by actual humans, which satisfies the 'human involvement in operation or decision-making' requirement. The bill was introduced within the window (Oct 28, 2025), is a federal congressional bill, and multiple news sources confirm its introduction. While I cannot directly access Congress.gov to verify the exact statutory text, multiple high-quality news sources including official Senate press releases confirm the bill's introduction and its substantive provisions. The broad interpretation of Criterion 4 supports Yes - the prohibition on AI acting as a licensed professional for these high-stakes interactions requires human professionals instead. However, strict interpretation creates ambiguity. Given the weight of evidence and the reasonable interpretation that prohibiting AI from performing licensed professional functions (requiring human involvement for those specific uses) satisfies the criteria, resolution is Yes.

question: Major meteor strike (10kt+) in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a natural meteoroid (bolide) explodes in Earth's atmosphere with a total impact energy greater or equal to 10 kilotons of TNT equivalent between May 28, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The object must be classified as a natural meteoroid; events involving artificial objects or reentry vehicles do not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/. The relevant field for determining impact energy is the “Impact Energy (kt)” column. If this dataset has not been updated to include all relevant dates by February 28, 2026, or if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository becomes permanently unavailable, this market may resolve based on a consensus of credible sources including the European Space Agency (ESA), the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN), the U.S. Department of Defense, or credible reporting of a scientific consensus, such as a NASA press release.

subquestions.question: Will NASA JPL's Fireball and Bolide Data list at least 3 natural fireball events with Impact Energy >= 1 kiloton occurring between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive, UTC)?
subquestions.background_information:
This is an indicator question for the chance of a much larger 10 kt+ atmospheric bolide later in 2025. Periods with unusually frequent kiloton-class fireballs may indicate either a temporarily elevated realized rate of sizable meteoroid entries or a run of bad luck that should update forecasters somewhat upward on the probability of an even larger event before year-end.

NASA JPL's Center for Near-Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) maintains a public Fireball and Bolide Data table that records detected atmospheric impact events and includes an "Impact Energy (kt)" field: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/ . The ultimate market itself uses this repository as its primary source, so a subquestion based on the same authoritative dataset is operationally convenient while still asking about a different observable event.

Recent 2025 events show that sub-10 kt fireballs are occurring and being recorded. For example, a bright fireball over southern Japan on 2025-08-19 was reported at about 1.6 kt by CNEOS-derived reporting, which is well below the ultimate market's 10 kt threshold but in the same general tail of the size distribution. See reporting here: https://watchers.news/2025/08/20/bright-fireball-impact-energy-1-6-kilotons-observed-over-southern-japan-on-august-19-2025/ . By contrast, the widely reported Georgia event in June 2025 was only about 20 tons TNT equivalent (0.02 kt), illustrating that many notable public fireballs are far below 1 kt and therefore this threshold is materially more selective: https://www.mediaite.com/news/watch-fireball-streaks-through-sky-in-stunning-sight-officials-believe-it-may-have-hit-house/ .

Using a count threshold of 3 events >= 1 kt within one month aims to avoid a near-certain or near-impossible question. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it tracks the frequency of moderately energetic atmospheric entries, not whether any single event exceeds 10 kt.

Sources:
NASA JPL CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data - https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/
The Watchers: Bright fireball with impact energy of 1.6 kilotons observed over southern Japan on August 19 - https://watchers.news/2025/08/20/bright-fireball-impact-energy-1-6-kilotons-observed-over-southern-japan-on-august-19-2025/
Mediaite: WATCH: 'Fireball' Streaks Through Sky in Stunning Sight - https://www.mediaite.com/news/watch-fireball-streaks-through-sky-in-stunning-sight-officials-believe-it-may-have-hit-house/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if NASA JPL's Fireball and Bolide Data repository lists 3 or more distinct events satisfying all of the following conditions: (1) the event date/time in the table is between 2025-09-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive; (2) the event is a natural fireball/bolide entry in the CNEOS dataset; and (3) the table's "Impact Energy (kt)" value for the event is greater than or equal to 1.0. Otherwise, it resolves No.

Primary source: NASA JPL CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data, https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/ .

Resolution procedure:
1. Count all rows in the CNEOS table whose event timestamp falls within the window from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 inclusive, using the date/time presented by the dataset.
2. Among those rows, count only entries with "Impact Energy (kt)" >= 1.0.
3. If the count is 3 or more, resolve Yes; if 0, 1, or 2, resolve No.

Definitions and edge cases:
- "At least 3" means 3 or more qualifying rows in the dataset.
- If CNEOS later revises an event's energy upward or downward, the final value shown in the dataset at time of resolution governs.
- Duplicate listings for the same physical event should count once; if the dataset appears to contain duplicates, use the final cleaned table if available.
- Events involving spacecraft, debris, or artificial reentries do not count; if such an event somehow appears in the table, it should be excluded unless CNEOS clearly classifies it as a natural meteoroid event.
- If the CNEOS dataset has not been updated to include all dates through 2025-10-01 by 2025-11-15, or if the repository becomes permanently unavailable, resolve using a consensus of credible sources that explicitly report qualifying natural atmospheric impact events and their energies, prioritizing NASA, ESA, IAWN, or U.S. government sources. Relevant fallback institutions include ESA's NEO Coordination Centre https://neo.ssa.esa.int/ and IAWN https://iawn.net/ . If no such credible consensus can establish the count, the question should be considered unresolvable.

Sources for resolution:
NASA JPL CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data - https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/
ESA NEO Coordination Centre - https://neo.ssa.esa.int/
International Asteroid Warning Network - https://iawn.net/
subquestions.rationale: A 10 kt+ bolide is a tail event from the same underlying distribution that produces 1 kt+ atmospheric fireballs. An unusually active month for kiloton-class entries would be evidence, albeit imperfect, for a higher realized near-term chance of a major strike before the end of 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Need 3+ natural fireball/bolide events in NASA JPL CNEOS database with Impact Energy >= 1.0 kt, dated between 2025-09-01T00:00:00Z and 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z UTC. Observable evidence: direct access to CNEOS table, or credible news sources citing CNEOS data with energy values.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'NASA JPL CNEOS fireball bolide impact energy kiloton 2025' - seeking CNEOS table data; 2) 'fireball bolide meteor impact September 2025' - seeking news of events in window; 3) 'NASA CNEOS fireball data September 2025 impact energy kiloton' - seeking CNEOS-specific reports; 4) 'bolide fireball 1 kiloton impact energy atmospheric October 2025' - seeking threshold-meeting events; 5) 'Argentina fireball September 13 2025 CNEOS 0.38 kiloton energy' - verifying specific CNEOS-cited event; 6) Additional queries on large impact airbursts and CNEOS table updates.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Argentina fireball Sept 13, 2025 - CNEOS cited 0.38 kt energy [themostimportantnews.com], BELOW 1 kt threshold, REJECTED; (2) Delhi-NCR bolide Sept 19-20, 2025 - no CNEOS energy data, likely identified as Chinese rocket debris (CZ-3B), NOT natural, REJECTED; (3) Perth Australia fireball Sept 1, 2025 - 'cricket ball sized', very small, no CNEOS energy value, REJECTED; (4) Scotland highlands bolide - occurred in 'summer 2025', timing unclear; (5) Various Starlink/space debris reentries (Texas Sept 22, California Sept 26) - artificial objects, NOT natural events, REJECTED. No events with confirmed CNEOS Impact Energy >= 1.0 kt were found in the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The only explicitly cited CNEOS energy value for September 2025 was 0.38 kt for Argentina fireball [http://themostimportantnews.com/archives/the-earth-has-been-shaken-by-466742-earthquakes-so-far-in-2025]. This is below the 1.0 kt threshold. No other event in the window was cited with a CNEOS energy >= 1.0 kt. Multiple fireball events reported in news were either artificial debris reentries (not qualifying) or had no cited energy values meeting the threshold.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Argentina fireball was dated September 13, 2025 - within window. But its energy (0.38 kt) is below threshold. No qualifying event timestamps could be extracted.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable - no qualifying events (energy >= 1 kt) were found at all in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for any contradictory evidence suggesting large bolide events >= 1 kt in September-October 2025: none found. Multiple searches returned no CNEOS-cited events with energy >= 1 kt in the target window. The CNEOS dataset was not directly accessible, but no news sources reported qualifying events. The resolution deadline of November 15, 2025 has passed without reports of such events being added to the CNEOS table.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Evidence strongly suggests resolution is No. The only CNEOS energy value cited for September 2025 was 0.38 kt (Argentina, below threshold). No evidence of 3 or more events with >= 1 kt in the Sep 1 - Oct 1 window. Multiple reported fireballs were either artificial reentries or too small to meet the threshold. While direct CNEOS table access was not possible, the absence of any news reporting qualifying events in this window, combined with the one available CNEOS data point being below threshold, supports a No resolution. However, the inability to directly access the CNEOS dataset introduces uncertainty, making this potentially unresolvable. Given the strong circumstantial evidence against Yes and the passage of the resolution deadline, I determine this as resolvable=No.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump publicly mention Elon Musk by name in a favorable or conciliatory way in an on-the-record statement between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25?
subquestions.background_information:
A useful early indicator for whether Trump and Musk will meet again soon is whether Trump publicly signals warmth or openness toward Musk. The ultimate market concerns an in-person interaction by late March 2026, and public rhetoric can be an observable leading indicator of whether channels are open. Trump and Musk already had at least one in-person interaction after their public falling-out: multiple outlets reported that they shook hands and spoke at Charlie Kirk's memorial service in Arizona on September 21, 2025. Trump later characterized the exchange as "nice" and said Musk "came over and said hello," indicating that direct contact had resumed even if the broader relationship remained uncertain. See Mediaite: https://www.mediaite.com/ and The Cut: https://www.thecut.com/ (article referenced in prompt); also reporting summarized in the prompt from TheJournal.ie and India.com.

Because the two men had a public rupture in mid-2025 and then a limited public reunion in September 2025, the next informative signal is not simply whether they are in the same place, but whether Trump voluntarily uses favorable rhetoric about Musk in a public, attributable setting. Positive rhetoric would suggest reduced interpersonal friction and a greater likelihood of future scheduling, invitations, or opportunistic meetings. Negative or no rhetoric would be some evidence against near-term rapprochement.

This threshold is grounded in the current state of affairs: there was a recent reported handshake/conversation in September 2025, but Trump also reportedly downplayed its significance afterward. That makes a new favorable public mention during the subquestion window meaningfully informative rather than trivial. Official Trump communications are routinely posted on Truth Social and covered by major outlets, making resolution practical.

The Cut (referenced article in prompt): https://www.thecut.com/
Donald J. Trump on Truth Social: https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Qualifying statements include: posts from Trump's official Truth Social account (https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump), remarks in official White House transcripts or videos (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), campaign/public event remarks recorded by a credible outlet, or direct quotes reported by at least two credible news organizations.

For this market, "favorable or conciliatory" means a reasonable reader would judge the statement as praising Musk, expressing appreciation, goodwill, respect, reconciliation, willingness to work together, or similar positive sentiment. Examples that would qualify: "Elon is a terrific guy," "I have a very good relationship with Elon," "I'd be happy to see Elon," "Elon is doing great work." Examples that would not qualify: neutral mentions, attacks, sarcasm, ambiguous jokes, or remarks whose dominant tone is negative.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement occurs between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25 (inclusive).

Primary resolution sources: Trump's official Truth Social account at https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump and White House official transcripts/videos at https://www.whitehouse.gov/. If neither provides sufficient evidence, resolution will use a consensus of at least two credible news reports quoting or reproducing the statement. If purported evidence is manipulated, unauthenticated, or only reported by a single non-authoritative source, it will not count. Statements made outside the 2025-11-25 to 2025-12-25 window do not count.

description:

question: Will any of the stolen Louvre jewels be returned by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any of the jewels stolen from the Louvre’s Galerie d’Apollon are officially recovered by the listed date ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

A single item (e.g., one earring) will suffice regardless of if it is missing a diamond or other element; however, recovery of only a fragment or part of an item (for example, a loose stone or a piece of a crown) will not suffice

The primary resolution source will be official statements from the Louvre or the French government; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will French authorities publicly announce at least one arrest or formal charging of a suspect in connection with the October 19, 2025 Louvre crown-jewels theft by 2025-11-20?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether any of the stolen Louvre jewels will be returned by December 31, 2025. A key near-term indicator is whether investigators identify and detain suspects soon after the heist. In art and jewelry theft cases, early arrests can materially increase the odds of recovery because intact items are often dismantled, melted, or dispersed quickly. Multiple reports on the Louvre theft describe this as a "race against time," with art-recovery experts warning that if the thieves are not caught within days, the jewels are much more likely to be destroyed or broken up rather than recovered intact. Smithsonian reported that on October 20, 2025, four masked burglars stole eight jewels from the Galerie d’Apollon and escaped on motorbikes, while one damaged item was found outside the museum; President Macron said the works would be retrieved and perpetrators brought to justice under the Paris prosecutor’s direction: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/burglars-just-broke-into-the-louvre-and-stole-historic-crown-jewels-in-a-daring-daylight-heist-180986776/ . Yahoo similarly reported expert Arthur Brand’s view that police had about one week before the missing pieces were likely melted down or dismantled: https://www.yahoo.com/news/stolen-louvre-jewels-recovered-know-194657809.html . PEOPLE quoted Art Recovery International CEO Chris Marinello saying that if thieves are not caught within 24 to 48 hours, the pieces are "probably long gone": https://people.com/expert-says-stolen-louvre-jewels-need-to-be-recovered-in-24-to-48-hours-or-theyre-long-gone-report-11765793 . NBC News reported that police were hunting the thieves after the daylight heist and that key pieces remained missing: https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/louvre-museum-paris-crown-jewels-stolen-heist-france-rcna217056 . Because recovery chances fall sharply if suspects remain unidentified and at large, a public arrest or charging announcement before November 20 would be a meaningful positive signal for the ultimate market.

Sources:
Smithsonian Magazine — Burglars Just Broke Into the Louvre and Stole Historic Crown Jewels in a Daring Daylight Heist — https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/burglars-just-broke-into-the-louvre-and-stole-historic-crown-jewels-in-a-daring-daylight-heist-180986776/
Yahoo News — What was stolen in the Louvre heist? What to know about the 8 jewelry pieces -- and the 'race against time' to save them. — https://www.yahoo.com/news/stolen-louvre-jewels-recovered-know-194657809.html
PEOPLE — Expert Says Stolen Louvre Jewels Need to Be Recovered in 24-to-48 Hours Or They're 'Long Gone': Report — https://people.com/expert-says-stolen-louvre-jewels-need-to-be-recovered-in-24-to-48-hours-or-theyre-long-gone-report-11765793

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-21 and 2025-11-20 (inclusive), French authorities publicly announce at least one arrest, detention/garde à vue clearly tied to the theft, indictment/mise en examen, or formal charging of a suspect in connection with the October 19, 2025 theft of jewels from the Louvre’s Galerie d’Apollon.

Primary sources for resolution will be official public statements from the Paris public prosecutor (Parquet de Paris), the French Ministry of the Interior / Police nationale, the French Ministry of Justice, or the Louvre Museum. Relevant official sites include:
- Paris prosecutor / French justice portals: https://www.justice.fr/ and https://www.paris.fr/
- French Ministry of the Interior: https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/
- Police nationale: https://www.police-nationale.interieur.gouv.fr/
- Louvre official site/newsroom: https://www.louvre.fr/

If no clear official statement is available, the question may also resolve Yes based on a consensus of at least two credible, independent news outlets reporting that an arrest or formal charging occurred within the window, provided both reports clearly connect the suspect to the Louvre jewel theft. Suitable fallback outlets include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AFP (https://www.afp.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), BBC (https://www.bbc.com/), or Le Monde (https://www.lemonde.fr/).

For avoidance of doubt:
- Mere police searches, questioning of witnesses, publication of suspect sketches, or statements that authorities have identified persons of interest do NOT count.
- An arrest for unrelated crimes does NOT count unless authorities explicitly connect it to the Louvre theft.
- If a suspect is arrested before 2025-10-21, it does not count.
- If the first qualifying public announcement occurs after 2025-11-20, it does not count.
- If reports are contradictory and no authoritative clarification emerges, resolve based on the strongest official source available; otherwise the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Early arrest or charging of suspects is a strong operational indicator that investigators have actionable leads, which should increase the probability that at least one jewel is later recovered by December 31. If forecasters disagree about the ultimate outcome, they are likely to update substantially on whether authorities rapidly apprehend suspects in this time-sensitive case.

question: U.S. x Iran Military Engagement by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Iran between market creation and the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Iranian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots, artillery fire into uninhabited areas, or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Iranian land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage.

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; the Iranian Law Enforcement Command is a branch of the Iranian Armed Forces; all sub-branches of the Artesh, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (including the Basij), and Law Enforcement Command are part of the Iranian Armed forces.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S.-Iran nuclear talks scheduled after the February 2026 Oman venue shift be canceled, suspended, or end without any announced follow-up meeting date by 2026-02-25?
subquestions.background_information:
A breakdown in diplomacy is a meaningful leading indicator for near-term military escalation risk between the United States and Iran. As of early February 2026, tensions are elevated: on 2026-02-04, U.S. Central Command said a U.S. F-35C shot down an Iranian Shahed-139 drone that had approached the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Arabian Sea, and separately reported harassment of the U.S.-flagged tanker Stena Imperative by IRGC vessels and a drone in the Strait of Hormuz. These incidents occurred just ahead of planned U.S.-Iran nuclear talks and amid explicit statements from U.S. officials that military force remains an option. Reuters-based reporting says talks originally planned for Turkey were shifted after Iran requested Oman and a narrower format focused on bilateral nuclear issues only. Because the ultimate question asks about a U.S.-Iran military engagement by late February 2026, whether talks collapse in the next 2-3 weeks is a distinct and timely observable that should update forecasts materially. If talks are canceled or suspended without a new date, that would suggest diplomacy is failing and increase the chance that subsequent provocations or reprisals escalate into direct military engagement. Conversely, if talks proceed and a follow-up is scheduled, that would be evidence that both sides are still prioritizing de-escalation.
