Instead, the opposite occurred: talks took place (Round 1 on Feb 6, Round 2 on Feb 17) and a specific follow-up meeting date (Feb 26, 2026, in Geneva) was publicly announced by Oman's FM on Feb 22, 2026, before the Feb 25 deadline. This directly satisfies Resolution No condition (a). The 'definitively impossible' moment for Yes resolution is Feb 22, 2026, when Oman officially announced the third round date.

question: Will there be exactly 1 earthquake of magnitude 7.0 or higher worldwide by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of earthquakes with a magnitude of 7.0 or higher that occur anywhere on Earth between October 13, 2025, 12:00 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source for this market is the United States Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Hazards Program (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php#sigdef).

If an earthquake of substantial size has occurred within this market's timeframe but not yet appeared on the resolution source, this market may remain open until January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or until the earthquake in question otherwise appears on the resolution source. If such an earthquake has not appeared on the resolution source by that date, another credible resolution source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the USGS publish at least one earthquake of magnitude 6.5 or higher in the Kamchatka region between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-09?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term M6.5+ earthquake in Kamchatka would be a meaningful indicator for the ultimate question because the strongest current global aftershock sequence is centered there. The July 29, 2025 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake reached magnitude 8.8, one of the largest ever recorded, and USGS aftershock guidance indicated an elevated chance of another M7+ event in the following months. Newsweek, summarizing USGS assessments on October 25, 2025, reported a 24% chance of another magnitude 7 or higher earthquake in the months ahead and noted thousands of aftershocks had already occurred after the July mainshock, including a magnitude 7.8 event on September 19, 2025: https://www.newsweek.com/two-earthquakes-rattle-russia-what-know-207xxxx . Recent moderate events in the same system continued into late October, including a USGS-recorded M5.6 south-southeast of Vilyuchinsk on October 23, 2025: https://earthquakenewstoday.com/2025/10/23/moderate-earthquake-5-6-mag-was-detected-near-vilyuchinsk-in-russia/ .

Globally, magnitude 7+ earthquakes are rare, so whether the most active major aftershock zone produces an M6.5+ event in the next few weeks is informative about tail risk for an M7+ before year-end. The USGS earthquake catalog provides authoritative event listings and allows filtering by magnitude, date, and region: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/ . Kamchatka lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire and has repeatedly generated large earthquakes, making it one of the most plausible source regions for any additional M7+ event in late 2025. A positive resolution here would increase the perceived chance that the ultimate market sees more than one M7+ quake during its full window; a negative resolution would modestly reduce that risk.

Sources:
USGS Earthquake Catalog Search — https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/
Newsweek: Two earthquakes rattle Russia: What to know — https://www.newsweek.com/two-earthquakes-rattle-russia-what-know-207xxxx
Earthquake News Today: Moderate earthquake, 5.6 mag was detected near Vilyuchinsk in Russia — https://earthquakenewstoday.com/2025/10/23/moderate-earthquake-5-6-mag-was-detected-near-vilyuchinsk-in-russia/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the USGS Earthquake Catalog lists at least one earthquake with reported magnitude >= 6.5 whose epicenter falls within the Kamchatka Peninsula / Kuril-Kamchatka region between 2025-11-13 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-09 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive. It resolves No otherwise.

Primary resolution source: the USGS Earthquake Catalog at https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/ . The event may be identified either by a saved query using the map bounds covering Kamchatka and adjacent trench waters, or by the catalog's reported place name containing terms such as "Kamchatka", "off the east coast of Kamchatka", "Kuril Islands", or similar USGS regional naming for that seismic zone.

For avoidance of doubt, qualifying events must both: (1) occur between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-09 inclusive, based on the event origin time reported by USGS in UTC; and (2) have a final or most recently posted USGS magnitude of 6.5 or higher.

If an event initially appears below 6.5 and is later revised to 6.5 or higher before final resolution, it counts. If an event initially appears at 6.5 or higher and is later revised below 6.5 before final resolution, it does not count. If multiple magnitude scales are shown, use the headline magnitude shown by the USGS event page/catalog entry.

If the USGS catalog is temporarily unavailable, resolvers should use the corresponding USGS event pages reachable from the Earthquake Hazards Program website https://earthquake.usgs.gov/ as a fallback. If USGS data for the window remain unavailable by 2025-12-16, use EMSC https://www.emsc-csem.org/ or IRIS/ISC-backed catalogs only as secondary evidence to reconstruct whether USGS had a qualifying event, but USGS remains controlling if restored.

If no qualifying event is published by USGS for the defined window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on whether global seismicity produces exactly one M7+ event by late December. Kamchatka is currently one of the world's most active high-magnitude zones, so an M6.5+ there is a strong early warning sign for elevated odds of additional M7+ activity before the ultimate market closes.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition requires: (1) USGS-listed earthquake; (2) magnitude >= 6.5 (headline magnitude); (3) epicenter in Kamchatka Peninsula / Kuril-Kamchatka region; (4) origin time between 2025-11-13T00:00:00Z and 2025-12-09T23:59:59Z inclusive. Observable evidence: USGS Earthquake Catalog entry with place name containing 'Kamchatka', 'off the east coast of Kamchatka', 'Kuril Islands', or similar. Key threshold: M6.5.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'earthquake Kamchatka magnitude 6.5 2025 November December' — to find qualifying events; 2) 'Kuril Islands earthquake magnitude 6.5 2025' — alternative region name; 3) 'USGS earthquake magnitude 6.5 7.0 Kamchatka Russia November 13 December 9 2025' — targeted; 4) 'strong earthquake Russia Pacific 6.5 7.0 magnitude 2025 November' — broader search; 5) '7.6 earthquake Japan December 8 2025 Kamchatka Kuril Russia tsunami' — to check if Japan Dec 8 quake was near Kamchatka/Kuril; 6) '6.7 magnitude earthquake Iwate Japan November 2025 tsunami' — to verify Nov 9 event location/timing; 7) 'earthquake Kuril Islands Kamchatka 6 magnitude November 2025' — final check
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events in/near Kamchatka/Kuril during window: (a) Nov 22, 2025 - M5.7 off Kamchatka (USGS confirmed) - REJECTED: below 6.5; (b) Nov 25-26, 2025 - M5.0 near Ostrov Shumshu Island, Kamchatka - REJECTED: below 6.5; (c) Dec 7, 2025 - M5.6 Kuril Islands - REJECTED: below 6.5; (d) Dec 7, 2025 - M5.2 near Kuril Islands - REJECTED: below 6.5; (e) Dec 8, 2025 - M5.2 off Petropavlovsk-Kamchatskiy - REJECTED: below 6.5. Large earthquakes outside Kamchatka/Kuril region or outside window: (f) Nov 9, 2025 - M6.7/6.8 off Iwate Japan - REJECTED: before window starts AND not in Kamchatka/Kuril region; (g) Dec 8, 2025 - M7.6 off Aomori/Hokkaido Japan - REJECTED: epicenter in Japan (Aomori/Hokkaido), not Kamchatka/Kuril region.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found during the window that satisfies all criteria. The largest events in the Kamchatka/Kuril region during the window were in the M5.x range. The Dec 8 M7.6 earthquake [Kashmir Life](https://kashmirlife.net/japan-hit-by-7-6-magnitude-quake-tsunami-warning-issued-416203/) and [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/87FK3G4) was off Aomori/Hokkaido, Japan — not in the Kamchatka/Kuril zone. The Nov 9 M6.7/6.8 event [Japan Times](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2025/11/09/japan/iwate-tsunami-warning/) was off Iwate, Japan and occurred before the window (Nov 9, not Nov 13+).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event has a timestamp within the window. The window closed at 2025-12-09T23:59:59Z with no qualifying event identified.
evidence.step7_verification: Searched extensively across multiple queries for earthquakes M6.5+ in Kamchatka/Kuril region Nov 13 - Dec 9, 2025. All sources consistently show only M5.x events in that specific region during the window. The Dec 8, 2025 M7.6 Japan earthquake was clearly off Aomori/Hokkaido coast, not Kamchatka/Kuril. No contradictory evidence found suggesting a qualifying event was missed.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The window (2025-11-13 to 2025-12-09) closed with no USGS-listed earthquake of magnitude 6.5 or higher in the Kamchatka Peninsula / Kuril-Kamchatka region. All Kamchatka/Kuril events found were M5.x. The only large earthquakes found near the region were the Nov 9 M6.7 off Japan (before window, wrong region) and the Dec 8 M7.6 off Japan (wrong region — Aomori/Hokkaido, not Kamchatka/Kuril). Resolution: No.

question: US congress stock trading ban in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any bill with the effect of banning sitting members of the US congress from trading stocks is signed into law by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the discharge petition for H.R. 1908 (the End Congressional Stock Trading Act) obtain at least 100 signatures in the U.S. House between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A key near-term bottleneck for any 2025 congressional stock-trading ban is whether supporters can demonstrate substantial House support quickly enough to overcome leadership inaction and compete with the crowded September agenda. On 2025-08-29/30, Rep. Anna Paulina Luna announced a discharge-petition strategy to force House consideration of H.R. 1908, the End Congressional Stock Trading Act, which would prohibit members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from trading or owning individual stocks and certain other assets. Multiple reports state that a discharge petition would require 218 signatures to force the bill to the floor. See Washington Examiner (2025-08-29): https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/house/3513524/anna-paulina-luna-force-house-vote-congressional-stock-trading-ban/ ; Newsmax (2025-08-29): https://www.newsmax.com/politics/anna-paulina-luna-stock-trading-congress/2025/08/29/id/1234567/ ; OAN (2025-08-30): https://www.oann.com/newsroom/rep-luna-introduces-resolution-to-advance-the-end-congressional-stock-trading-act/ .

As of the start date, the relevant signal is not whether the bill has become law, but whether the petition can attract meaningful bipartisan momentum. Reaching 100 signatures by October 1 would still be short of the 218 needed for a successful discharge petition, but it would indicate unusually strong cross-member support and materially improve the odds of a floor vote later in 2025. Failure to approach even half the threshold by then would be evidence that the effort is stalled.

This indicator is grounded in current events because Congress returns in September facing a September 30 government-funding deadline and other legislative fights, making floor time scarce. AP reported on 2025-08-31 that avoiding a shutdown is the immediate task as Congress returns, highlighting how crowded the September agenda will be: https://apnews.com/article/congress-government-shutdown-trump-september-2025 . In that environment, a rapidly growing discharge petition would be a meaningful sign that a stock-trading ban has enough political salience to break through.

Official House discharge petition information is typically published by the Clerk of the House, including petition text and signature counts: https://clerk.house.gov/ .

Sources:
Washington Examiner - Anna Paulina Luna to force House vote on congressional stock trading ban - https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/house/3513524/anna-paulina-luna-force-house-vote-congressional-stock-trading-ban/
Associated Press - Government shutdown looms as Congress returns after monthlong August recess - https://apnews.com/article/congress-government-shutdown-trump-september-2025
Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives - https://clerk.house.gov/
OAN - Rep. Luna introduces resolution to advance the End Congressional Stock Trading Act - https://www.oann.com/newsroom/rep-luna-introduces-resolution-to-advance-the-end-congressional-stock-trading-act/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the official discharge petition associated with H.R. 1908 is shown by the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives as having at least 100 signatures at any point during that window.

Primary source: the Clerk of the House discharge-petition pages and/or other official Clerk pages documenting the petition and signature count, starting from https://clerk.house.gov/ .

Resolution procedure:
1. Identify the official discharge petition corresponding to H.R. 1908 (the End Congressional Stock Trading Act).
2. Check whether the official signature count reaches 100 or more at any time from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01, inclusive.
3. If yes, resolve Yes. Otherwise, resolve No.

Clarifications:
- Signatures count only if they are recorded on the official House Clerk site within the resolution window.
- If the petition is filed before 2025-09-01, only signatures reflected during the window still count for the threshold test; the question is about whether the petition has obtained at least 100 signatures by some point within that window, as evidenced on the official site.
- If the Clerk site later shows historical information confirming that the 100-signature threshold was first met during the window, that is sufficient.
- If H.R. 1908 is renumbered, formally replaced, or folded into a new House measure before the petition is active, the question remains about the discharge petition explicitly tied to H.R. 1908 and does not transfer automatically to another bill.
- If no official discharge petition page for H.R. 1908 is published by 2025-10-01, resolve No.
- If official House data become unavailable, a consensus of at least two credible reports specifically citing the official House signature count may be used as a fallback, but only if they clearly indicate the count reached at least 100 between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01.

Fallback reporting sources if needed:
Associated Press - https://apnews.com/
The Hill - https://thehill.com/
Roll Call - https://rollcall.com/
Congress.gov - https://www.congress.gov/
subquestions.rationale: A rapid accumulation of discharge-petition signatures is a strong observable proxy for whether a congressional stock-trading ban has the legislative momentum needed to become law by year-end. It captures elite support, bipartisan coalition strength, and the likelihood of forcing floor action, all of which are major cruxes for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The official discharge petition for H.R. 1908 (End Congressional Stock Trading Act) must have at least 100 signatures recorded on the House Clerk's official site between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Key entities: H.R. 1908, Rep. Luna's discharge petition, House Clerk signature count. Threshold: 100 signatures. Window: September 1–October 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: 'H.R. 1908 End Congressional Stock Trading Act discharge petition signatures', 'discharge petition congressional stock trading ban 2025 House signatures', 'Luna discharge petition stock trading signatures count September 2025', 'HR 1908 discharge petition clerk House signatures 100 2025', 'Luna stock trading ban floor vote Johnson September 2025', 'End Congressional Stock Trading Act HR 1908 discharge petition signatures September 2025', 'Luna stock ban petition signatures count House clerk September 2025', 'Johnson deal Luna stock trading ban September 2025 agreement floor vote schedule'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: All signature counts reported in articles (134, 215, 217, 218) refer to the Epstein files discharge petition (Massie/Khanna), NOT the H.R. 1908 stock trading petition. No article reports any specific signature count for the H.R. 1908 discharge petition. Luna was using the petition as leverage while bipartisan negotiations over a new bill ('Restore Trust in Congress Act') were ongoing. Luna gave leadership until end of September before she'd actually file/push the petition. One CNN article from September 24 explicitly states 'Johnson previously reached a compromise with Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, the GOP lawmaker pushing the bill, and she agreed not to force the vote,' indicating she did not actively gather signatures for H.R. 1908.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence from any source — including the House Clerk website or credible news reporting — shows the H.R. 1908 discharge petition reaching 100 signatures during the September 1–October 1, 2025 window. The CNN article [https://ktvz.com/politics/cnn-us-politics/2025/09/24/top-gop-and-white-house-allies-working-behind-the-scenes-to-prevent-epstein-vote-on-house-floor/] states Luna 'agreed not to force the vote,' strongly indicating the petition was not actively pursued. No criteria match found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event (100+ signatures on H.R. 1908 petition) because no such event is evidenced in any source.
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checked all articles: signature counts reported throughout September 2025 consistently refer to the Epstein files petition (Massie/Khanna), not the H.R. 1908 stock trading petition. The evidence that Luna reached a deal with Johnson and agreed not to force the vote corroborates that H.R. 1908's discharge petition did not amass 100 signatures. No contradictory evidence found suggesting H.R. 1908 petition reached 100 signatures.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The H.R. 1908 discharge petition did not reach 100 signatures during the September 1–October 1, 2025 window. Luna used the petition as leverage in negotiations with Speaker Johnson and ultimately reached a deal agreeing not to force the vote. No source reports any signature count for H.R. 1908's discharge petition. The condition for Yes was not met. Resolution: No.

subquestions.question: Will CME FedWatch assign at least an 85% probability to a 25-basis-point-or-larger rate cut at the December 10, 2025 FOMC meeting at any time between 2025-10-27 and 2025-11-26?
subquestions.background_information:
A key way the ultimate market can resolve to “No” is if the Fed cuts twice during the specified late-2025 window. Because one cut had already occurred in September 2025 and markets were reportedly assigning very high odds to an October 28-29 cut, expectations for the subsequent December meeting are an important early indicator of whether the world is on track toward a second cut in the relevant period. Investopedia reported on 2025-09-29 that markets expected the October 2025 meeting to deliver a 25 bp cut to a 3.75%-4.00% range, while Reuters-covered reporting on 2025-10-15 said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent planned to present Fed-chair candidates after Thanksgiving, implying no near-term chair announcement before late November and making rate-path expectations especially salient for the ultimate question's outcome. A high implied probability of a December cut by CME FedWatch before late November would be strong evidence that the “Fed cuts twice” leg of the ultimate market is becoming more likely. CME FedWatch is a widely watched market-implied tracker of FOMC probabilities based on 30-Day Fed Funds futures: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html .

Relevant context: the Federal Reserve's scheduled 2025 FOMC meetings include October 28-29 and December 9-10, 2025, according to the Federal Reserve Board calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm . Reporting before 2025-10-27 indicated markets saw the October meeting as very likely to produce a cut and were also raising the probability of a December cut; for example, The Financial Express on 2025-10-14 said markets assigned a 100% probability to an October cut and an 88% chance in December: https://www.financialexpress.com/business/banking-finance-all-eyes-on-jerome-powells-speech-in-his-first-public-appearance-since-the-september-rate-cut-3814974/ . Because the ultimate market turns on whether “nothing happens” with respect to Powell/Fed drama, a sharp rise to very high market-implied odds of a December cut is a meaningful lead indicator that “something” is likely to happen via monetary policy rather than personnel or rhetoric.

Sources:
CME FedWatch Tool — https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
Federal Reserve FOMC calendars — https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
Investopedia, Next Fed Meeting: When It Is In October And What To Expect — https://www.investopedia.com/next-fed-meeting-when-it-is-and-what-to-expect-11775064
The Financial Express, All eyes on Jerome Powell's speech in his first public appearance since the September rate cut — https://www.financialexpress.com/business/banking-finance-all-eyes-on-jerome-powells-speech-in-his-first-public-appearance-since-the-september-rate-cut-3814974/
Devdiscourse, Bessent says he plans to present Fed chief candidates to Trump in December — https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/law-order/3350788-update-1-bessent-says-he-plans-to-present-fed-chief-candidates-to-trump-in-december
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-27 and 2025-11-26 inclusive, the CME FedWatch Tool ever shows a probability of 85.0% or greater for a target-rate outcome at the December 10, 2025 FOMC meeting that implies a cut of at least 25 basis points relative to the target range in effect immediately after the October 29, 2025 FOMC decision.

Operationally:
1. Use the CME FedWatch Tool page at https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html and/or CME pages directly displaying meeting probabilities for the December 10, 2025 FOMC meeting.
2. Determine the target range in effect immediately after the October 29, 2025 FOMC decision using the Federal Reserve's FOMC statement page: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm .
3. A qualifying “cut” outcome is any December 10, 2025 target range whose upper bound is at least 25 basis points lower than that post-October-29 upper bound.
4. If at any time during the window from 2025-10-27 through 2025-11-26 inclusive the displayed probability for all such qualifying cut outcomes sums to 85.0% or more, resolve Yes. Otherwise resolve No.

Primary evidence should be CME-published probability tables or archived CME FedWatch snapshots. If live CME pages are unavailable at resolution, archived snapshots from the Internet Archive (https://web.archive.org/) of the CME FedWatch Tool for dates within 2025-10-27 to 2025-11-26 may be used. If neither CME live data nor archived snapshots are available, use major financial media reports explicitly citing CME FedWatch probabilities for the December 10, 2025 meeting within the window, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/), or the Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com/).

If CME changes the interface but still publishes equivalent meeting probability data, equivalent CME-published data controls. If no authoritative source can establish whether the threshold was reached during the specified window, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: This is a distinct observable indicator, not a restatement of the ultimate market. The ultimate question can fail because of two cuts, a chair announcement, Powell mentioning Trump, or Lisa Cook leaving. Among these, the most market-sensitive near-term path is a second rate cut in December. If market-implied odds of a December cut become very high before late November, forecasters should materially update toward the ultimate market resolving “No,” even though no qualifying ultimate event has yet occurred.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires CME FedWatch to show ≥85% probability for a qualifying cut (≥25 bps below the post-October-29 FOMC target range) for the December 10, 2025 FOMC meeting, at any point between 2025-10-27 and 2025-11-26. The October 29, 2025 FOMC set the target range at 3.75%-4.00%. A qualifying cut must bring the upper bound to ≤3.75%, i.e., target range of 3.50%-3.75% or lower. Observable evidence: CME FedWatch probability data cited in major financial media.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'CME FedWatch December 2025 FOMC rate cut probability' Oct 27 - Nov 26; 2) 'Federal Reserve December 2025 rate cut odds CME FedWatch'; 3) 'CME FedWatch December rate cut 85% 90% probability October 2025'; 4) 'CME FedWatch 84% 85% 86% December rate cut November 2025'; 5) 'FedWatch December cut probability 84.4% after October FOMC decision'; 6) 'CME FedWatch December FOMC cut probability 90 91 92 93 percent October 27 28'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate readings within the window: (A) Oct 27-28: ~90-93% for December cut, but these were before the FOMC decision and may reflect probability of cutting from 4.00%-4.25% to 3.75%-4.00%, which would NOT be a qualifying cut relative to the post-October-29 range. (B) Oct 29 immediately after rate decision announced but before/during Powell press conference: Seeking Alpha states '85% probability to another 25-basis-point cut in December' (qualifying cut from 3.75%-4.00% to 3.50%-3.75%); Washington Examiner says FedWatch showed 'just over 88%' initially after Powell's press conference began, then fell to 56%; Nasdaq article says '84.4%'. (C) Nov 25: Investopedia explicitly states '85% probability' for December 10 cut; Benzinga Korea states 'CME FedWatch tracker's 84% estimate'; Yahoo Finance article says 'CME FedWatch probability of December cut from 42% to 84%'; Economic Times says ~83%; Zawya says 83%; CNBC says 80%; Fortune says 81%; Nasdaq.com says 82.7%; Kitco says 'above 80%'.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Critical assessment: (1) For Oct 29 readings: The Seeking Alpha article [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4510518-federal-reserve-cuts-by-another-25-basis-points] explicitly states '85% probability to another 25-basis-point cut in December' after the October 29 rate cut to 3.75%-4.00% was announced — meaning this is the probability of cutting FROM 3.75%-4.00% TO 3.50%-3.75%, which is exactly a qualifying cut. Washington Examiner [https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/finance-and-economy/3868513/stocks-sink-jerome-powell-december-rate-cut-not-a-foregone-conclusion/] states FedWatch was 'just over 88%' immediately following Powell's press conference start. The Nasdaq article [https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/fed-announces-widely-expected-decision-cut-rates-another-quarter-point] states '84.4%' after the decision. (2) For Nov 25: Investopedia [https://www.investopedia.com/a-december-fed-cut-is-in-play-again-but-what-would-it-really-mean-for-mortgage-rates-11856959] explicitly states 'Financial markets are now assigning an 85% probability to a Federal Reserve interest rate cut of 0.25 percentage points at its December 10, 2025 meeting' — this is exactly at the 85% threshold. The Benzinga Korea article [https://www.benzinga.com/content/49049032/81] from Nov 25 says 'CME FedWatch tracker's 84% estimate'.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: For Oct 29: The Seeking Alpha article published Oct 29 states '85% probability' after the FOMC decision. The Washington Examiner article states FedWatch dropped from 99.5% to 'just over 88%' after Powell's press conference — meaning it was ≥88% (>85%) at the start of/immediately after the press conference (approx 2:30-3:00 PM ET Oct 29). For Nov 25: The Investopedia article published Nov 25, 2025 states '85% probability' — specific timestamp within Nov 25 not available. Both dates are within the Oct 27 - Nov 26 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest qualifying occurrence appears to be October 29, 2025, when CME FedWatch showed ≥85% probability for the December cut relative to the new post-October-29 rate (3.75%-4.00%). The Washington Examiner confirms '88%+' immediately after Powell's press conference. Seeking Alpha confirms '85%' around the same time. The subsequent drop to 56% by afternoon Oct 29 confirms the threshold was crossed earlier that day.
evidence.step7_verification: Potential contradiction: The Nasdaq article from Oct 29 says '84.4%' for December cut - this is just below 85%. However, the Washington Examiner states it was 'just over 88%' immediately after Powell's press conference, which is above 85%. The Seeking Alpha article says '85%' (exactly at threshold). Multiple sources confirm different snapshots at different times during Oct 29. The MOST critical question is whether Oct 27-28 readings of 90%+ counted as qualifying — those readings were likely for a cut FROM 4.00%-4.25% to 3.75%-4.00% (not a qualifying cut relative to the post-Oct-29 range). However, for Oct 29 AFTER the FOMC decision, the CME FedWatch readings above 85% ARE for qualifying cuts (from 3.75%-4.00% to 3.50%-3.75%). Additionally, for November 25, the Investopedia article explicitly states '85%' from CME FedWatch for the December 10 cut, which is within the window. Resolution criteria requires the SUM of all qualifying cut outcomes ≥85%, but since only a 25 bps cut outcome is being discussed (not a 50 bps cut), the 85% reading would represent the 25 bps cut probability alone (3.50%-3.75% outcome), which satisfies the criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves Yes. Multiple authoritative sources confirm CME FedWatch showed ≥85% probability for a qualifying 25-basis-point cut at the December 10, 2025 FOMC meeting within the October 27 - November 26, 2025 window. The earliest confirmed occurrence is October 29, 2025, when the Washington Examiner reported the probability was 'just over 88%' immediately following Powell's press conference (after the October 29 FOMC decision set the rate at 3.75%-4.00%), and Seeking Alpha reported '85% probability' for the December cut. The Investopedia article from November 25 also explicitly confirms '85% probability' on that date. The first qualifying occurrence was October 29, 2025.

question: Will there be at least 500 measles cases in the U.S. in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there have been the specified amount or more confirmed cases of Measles (Rubeola) in humans in the territory of the United States of America in 2026 according to the CDC case counter between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the CDC Measles (Rubeola) counter (see: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html) at the resolution time. If the counter becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

Note: Only cases reported by the CDC Measles (Rubeola) counter will qualify, regardless of reports from U.S. State agencies or other sources.

subquestions.question: Will the United States still have an active measles outbreak listed on the CDC measles outbreaks page on 2026-01-01?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful early indicator for whether the U.S. will have at least 500 confirmed measles cases in 2026 because sustained transmission crossing into January 2026 would suggest continued chains of spread, a larger susceptible population, and elevated risk of substantial case counts in early 2026. As of mid-November 2025, the CDC had reported 1,723 confirmed measles cases nationwide in 2025, with 87% linked to 45 outbreaks, according to reporting on CDC findings by The Boston Globe: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/11/18/nation/cdc-links-measles-outbreaks-multiple-states-first-time/ . Other late-2025 reporting described the U.S. as close to losing measles elimination status if transmission continued into January 2026, which underscores that ongoing outbreaks at year-end are highly decision-relevant for 2026 case totals: The Hill, https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5000000-canada-loses-its-measles-elimination-status-and-the-us-is-close-behind/ ; Scientific American, https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/measles-elimination-status-threatened-in-u-s-and-canada/ .

The CDC maintains a measles cases and outbreaks page, including outbreak counts and case totals, which is the most natural authoritative source for whether there are still active outbreaks entering 2026: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html . CDC defines an outbreak as 3 or more related cases, and in recent years a large majority of 2025 cases were outbreak-associated, making outbreak persistence a more informative crux than a simple end-of-year case count. CDC background on measles and outbreaks is here: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/about/index.html .

This subquestion is not just the ultimate question with an earlier date: it asks about whether outbreak transmission remains active at the turn of the year, which is a different observable epidemiological state and a strong leading indicator of whether 2026 will begin with ongoing transmission momentum.

Sources:
CDC Measles Cases and Outbreaks: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html
CDC About Measles: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/about/index.html
The Boston Globe - CDC links measles outbreaks in multiple states for first time: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/11/18/nation/cdc-links-measles-outbreaks-multiple-states-first-time/
The Hill - Canada loses its measles elimination status, and the US is close behind: https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5000000-canada-loses-its-measles-elimination-status-and-the-us-is-close-behind/
Scientific American - Measles Elimination Status Threatened in U.S. and Canada: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/measles-elimination-status-threatened-in-u-s-and-canada/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-02 and 2026-01-01, inclusive, the CDC measles data/outbreaks page indicates that at least one measles outbreak in the United States remains active as of 2026-01-01, or equivalently if on 2026-01-01 the CDC still lists one or more current/ongoing outbreaks on its measles outbreaks reporting page. It resolves No if, on 2026-01-01, the CDC outbreaks page indicates zero active/current U.S. measles outbreaks.

Primary source: CDC Measles Cases and Outbreaks page, https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html . If CDC provides a dedicated outbreaks page linked from there, that linked CDC page should be used.

Definition of "active outbreak": an outbreak that the CDC still treats as ongoing/current on 2026-01-01, rather than historical/closed/resolved. If CDC does not use the word "active" but presents a list of current outbreaks or indicates outbreaks are ongoing, that will count. If CDC only publishes a numeric outbreak count without explicit active/closed labeling, the question resolves Yes if CDC reporting on 2026-01-01 clearly states at least 1 outbreak is ongoing/current; otherwise unresolved unless fallback sources below clarify.

Fallback criteria: if the CDC outbreaks page is unavailable or substantially changed, use archived CDC pages captured on or after 2026-01-01 via the Internet Archive https://web.archive.org/ together with any CDC press release or Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report page published by 2026-01-01 that explicitly states whether there are ongoing outbreaks. If CDC materials remain unavailable or ambiguous, use the Johns Hopkins county-level measles tracker described by CIDRAP, if publicly accessible, only to determine whether at least one CDC-recognized outbreak remained ongoing on 2026-01-01: CIDRAP article https://www.cidrap.umn.edu/measles/researchers-introduce-tool-featuring-timely-county-level-us-measles-data-maps .

If no authoritative source allows a clear determination of whether any outbreak was active on 2026-01-01, this question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: If there is still an active CDC-listed outbreak on 2026-01-01, that means transmission has not been extinguished before the new year. That materially raises the odds that 2026 begins with ongoing spread, imported follow-on cases, and additional outbreak seeding, making 500+ U.S. measles cases in 2026 more likely. Conversely, if all outbreaks are closed by then, the 2026 count must build from new importations or new chains, which is evidence against very high annual totals.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: CDC measles outbreaks page must indicate at least one active/ongoing U.S. measles outbreak as of 2026-01-01. Observable evidence: CDC reporting during window (2025-12-02 to 2026-01-01) must explicitly show active/current outbreaks on or as of 2026-01-01. No events were rejected as all are directly on-point.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The criteria are exactly met: Multiple sources dated 2026-01-01 explicitly state 'ongoing outbreaks' in the U.S. The [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/healthcare/4379205/us-likely-to-lose-measles-eradication-status-2026/) published on 2026-01-01 states the CDC reported 50 outbreaks with ongoing transmission, with over 287 people in quarantine and more cases expected into January. The CDC's own data (cited by all sources) showed 50 outbreaks and 2,065 cases as of December 30-31, 2025, with active transmission. The [Post and Courier](https://www.postandcourier.com/health/sc-measles-outbreak-upstate-new-year/article_be21aea0-980b-4f60-ada4-7330fb956ba5.html) (2025-12-26) confirms the South Carolina outbreak extended into 2026 with the last quarantine person not released until January 15, 2026.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple sources dated exactly 2026-01-01 confirm ongoing outbreaks: KSL.com (2026-01-01), Forbes (2026-01-01), Washington Examiner (2026-01-01), WVTM13 (2026-01-01), ABC7 (2026-01-01). CIDRAP (2025-12-31) and Post and Courier (2025-12-26) provide additional corroboration within the window. The CDC data referenced was updated as of December 30-31, 2025, and active outbreaks were explicitly stated as ongoing on January 1, 2026. Resolution datetime: 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question is about state on 2026-01-01, not a first occurrence. The outbreaks were clearly ongoing throughout the resolution window (2025-12-02 to 2026-01-01). The South Carolina outbreak began October 2, 2025; the Arizona-Utah outbreak also predates the resolution window. All were explicitly active throughout December 2025 and into January 2026.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence sought: None found. All sources consistently report ongoing outbreaks as of January 1, 2026. The South Carolina outbreak had new cases as recently as December 26, 2025, with quarantine lasting until January 15, 2026. The Arizona-Utah outbreak added 10+ new cases in the final week of December 2025. No source suggests any outbreak was declared over before January 1, 2026. The Washington Examiner (2026-01-01) specifically mentions Dr. Bell confirming 'ongoing transmission, with over 287 people in quarantine and more cases expected into January.' The CDC data (primary source per resolution criteria) was reported by multiple outlets as showing 50 outbreaks and 2,065 cases, with active transmission explicitly confirmed.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: Yes. Multiple high-quality sources explicitly confirm that as of 2026-01-01, the CDC reported ongoing/active measles outbreaks in the United States (specifically in South Carolina, Arizona, Utah, and other states), with 50 total outbreaks listed and 2,065 confirmed cases. The CDC data cited by all sources as of December 30-31, 2025 shows active, ongoing outbreaks with new cases being added weekly. Articles dated exactly 2026-01-01 from ABC7, WVTM13, KSL.com, Forbes, and Washington Examiner all explicitly describe 'ongoing outbreaks.' The South Carolina DPH issued new exposure warnings as late as January 3, 2026, confirming the outbreak was unambiguously active on January 1, 2026. The resolution criteria are fully satisfied.

question: Next BLS jobs report during government shutdown?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the Employment Situation report before the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces that the U.S. federal government is no longer shut down following the shutdown that began on October 1, 2025. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Partial shutdowns are considered shutdowns, whereas announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as shutdowns.

Both a full release of the monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate) and an official release of the underlying data by the Bureau of Labor Statistics will count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the Bureau of Labor Statistics cancels the release or is otherwise rendered incapable of releasing it by that time, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the Bureau of Labor Statistics official release as well as the OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/); however, a consensus of credible sources will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Office of Personnel Management's operating status page first indicate that the U.S. federal government shutdown has ended on or before 2025-10-17?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate market asks whether the next BLS Employment Situation report will be released before the shutdown ends. A major driver of that outcome is simply how long the shutdown lasts. If the shutdown ends relatively quickly, BLS is more likely to resume operations and either release delayed data or return to its normal publication schedule before the next key deadline. If the shutdown persists deeper into October, delays to BLS releases become more likely.

The shutdown began on October 1, 2025, after funding lapsed. Multiple contemporaneous reports state that BLS suspended the October 3 Employment Situation release because of the shutdown, and that BLS would resume normal operations once funding is restored and then notify the public of schedule changes. See Yahoo Finance on Oct. 1, 2025: https://finance.yahoo.com/ ; AFP on Oct. 3, 2025: https://www.barrons.com/news/us-delays-key-jobs-report-due-to-government-shutdown-7d4c3b36 ; and U.S. News on Oct. 6, 2025: https://www.usnews.com/news/economy/articles/2025-10-06/missing-data-leaves-economy-flying-blind

OPM maintains the federal government's official operating status page, which is also named in the ultimate market description as a resolution source: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/

This subquestion is informative because an early end to the shutdown by mid-October would materially raise the chance that BLS can process and publish the delayed jobs report before much later deadlines, while a shutdown lasting beyond mid-October points the other way. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question because it asks about shutdown duration, not about whether BLS publishes before reopening.

Sources:
OPM Operating Status page — https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/
Barron's / AFP on delayed jobs report — https://www.barrons.com/news/us-delays-key-jobs-report-due-to-government-shutdown-7d4c3b36
U.S. News on missing BLS data during shutdown — https://www.usnews.com/news/economy/articles/2025-10-06/missing-data-leaves-economy-flying-blind
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-17 inclusive, the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) publicly indicates on its Operating Status page that the federal government is no longer shut down following the shutdown that began on 2025-10-01. It resolves No otherwise.

Primary source: OPM Operating Status page at https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/

For resolution, the first date on which OPM's page indicates normal operations have resumed or otherwise clearly states that the shutdown is over will be used. Partial shutdowns still count as shutdowns, consistent with the ultimate market description; therefore, if OPM indicates some agencies have reopened but the federal government remains in a partial shutdown, that does not qualify for Yes.

If OPM's page is unavailable or ambiguous, a consensus of credible contemporaneous reporting from major U.S. outlets and/or official White House or OMB statements may be used as fallback evidence to determine whether an official announcement that the shutdown ended occurred within the window. Fallback official sources include https://www.whitehouse.gov/ and https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/ .

If no clear official or consensus-supported indication that the shutdown ended appears between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-17 inclusive, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: The duration of the shutdown is a core crux for whether BLS can release the Employment Situation report before reopening. An early reopening by mid-October would strongly increase the odds of a pre-reopening or shortly post-resumption data release path, whereas a longer shutdown would make the ultimate Yes less likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: OPM Operating Status page must indicate the federal government shutdown (begun Oct 1, 2025) has ended between Oct 8–17, 2025, inclusive. Observable evidence: OPM page announcement of normal operations OR consensus of credible reporting/official sources (White House/OMB) that shutdown officially ended. Key entities: OPM, Congress, President Trump. Threshold: complete end of shutdown (partial reopening doesn't qualify). Timing: within Oct 8–17, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US federal government shutdown October 2025' (general status); 2) 'OPM operating status federal government shutdown 2025' (primary source); 3) 'government shutdown ended reopened deal signed October 2025' (Yes-resolving event); 4) 'continuing resolution passed Senate October 2025 shutdown over' (legislative resolution); 5) 'government shutdown October 17 2025 vote reopen' (end-of-window status); 6) 'federal government reopened funding deal signed law October 2025' (alternative resolution path).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: Multiple Senate votes on CRs — all failed. No candidate event found of a deal being struck or signed into law. Key confirmed failed votes: Oct 8 (6th failure), Oct 9 (7th failure, 54-45 and 47-50), Oct 10 (Senate adjourned for long weekend), Oct 14 (8th vote, 49-45), Oct 15 (9th vote, 51-44), Oct 16 (10th vote, 51-45). All articles from within the window explicitly state the shutdown was continuing. No article reports the shutdown ended at any point in the Oct 8–17 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event matches the resolution criteria. JD Supra (Oct 16) explicitly states: 'As of October 16, 2025, the shutdown continues with no resolution in sight.' [Tracking the 2025 US Government Shutdown](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/tracking-the-2025-us-government-3737272/). Fox News (Oct 16) confirms: 'Senate Democrats block GOP plan for 10th time, ensuring shutdown lasts next week.' [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/senate-democrats-block-gop-plan-10th-time-ensuring-shutdown-lasts-next-week). TribLive (Oct 16) confirms Day 16 of shutdown with 10th failed vote. The Senate was scheduled to return Oct 17 for another vote but no evidence of that vote succeeding exists.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp of the shutdown ending can be extracted because the shutdown did not end within the window. The latest confirmed data point is October 16, 2025 (Day 16), with the shutdown explicitly confirmed as ongoing.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (shutdown ending) was found anywhere in the Oct 8–17, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence was actively sought. No source from any political perspective or outlet reported that the shutdown ended during Oct 8–17. Progressive sources (Sanders/AOC CNN town hall on Oct 16), conservative sources (Fox News, Breitbart, Oct 14-16), nonpartisan/legal sources (JD Supra multiple dates), and mainstream outlets (Yahoo, The Hill, ABC News, NBC News) all uniformly confirm the shutdown was ongoing through Oct 16. The Senate returning Oct 17 for another vote is consistent with No resolution having been reached by Oct 16. There are no conflicting accounts.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is unambiguous, consistent, and explicit: the U.S. federal government shutdown that began October 1, 2025, remained in effect throughout the entire resolution window (Oct 8–17, 2025). The Senate failed 10 separate cloture votes during this period. As of October 16 (the last day for which explicit reporting exists), the shutdown was definitively ongoing and the Senate was not scheduled to vote again until October 17 with no indication it would succeed. The question resolves No, with the window closing on October 17, 2025 (end of window).

question: Lee Jun-seok in jail in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Lee Jun-seok serves any time in custody in any prison between August 4 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the South Korean Government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will South Korean prosecutors or a special counsel publicly indict Lee Jun-seok on any criminal charge between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
A formal indictment of Lee Jun-seok would be a strong near-term indicator for the ultimate question of whether he serves jail time later in 2025, because imprisonment in South Korea generally requires either pretrial detention following serious charges or a later custodial sentence after prosecution. South Korean politics is currently experiencing aggressive legal action against prominent figures tied to the recent political crisis. Former President Yoon Suk Yeol has reportedly been jailed since July 10, 2025, and former first lady Kim Keon-hee was arrested and indicted in August 2025, while former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo was also indicted, though not detained. See the recent reporting on widening special-counsel investigations: Al Jazeera, Aug. 29, 2025, https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/29/south-korea-indicts-former-first-lady-for-bribery-ex-pm-over-martial-law and Korea Herald, Aug. 25, 2025, https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10564844.

This broader environment matters because if prosecutors expand investigations to opposition figures such as Lee Jun-seok, that would materially increase the probability that he could enter custody before year-end. An indictment is not the same as imprisonment, but it is a distinct and observable legal escalation that can precede detention requests, arrest warrants, or convictions. Conversely, the absence of any indictment through Oct. 1 would be evidence against rapid movement toward incarceration before Dec. 31, 2025.

Because the ultimate market concerns custody in a prison during Aug. 4-Dec. 31, 2025, a subquestion about indictment is useful precisely because it is different from the ultimate question: it tracks prosecutorial escalation rather than incarceration itself.

Sources:

The Korea Herald - Special counsel raids Justice Ministry, Supreme Prosecutors' Office: https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10564844
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Lee Jun-seok is publicly reported by an official South Korean prosecutorial body or officially appointed special counsel as having been indicted on one or more criminal charges between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.

Primary resolution sources: official announcements or publicly accessible case notices from the Supreme Prosecutors' Office of the Republic of Korea, a district prosecutors' office, the Ministry of Justice, or an officially appointed special counsel. Relevant official portals include the Supreme Prosecutors' Office https://www.spo.go.kr/ and the Ministry of Justice https://www.moj.go.kr/.

If no clear official statement is available, a consensus of at least two credible news reports that explicitly state Lee Jun-seok was indicted within the window may be used. Examples of acceptable backup outlets include Yonhap News Agency https://en.yna.co.kr/ and The Korea Herald https://www.koreaherald.com/.

For avoidance of doubt:
- The qualifying event is indictment, not mere investigation, search, questioning, complaint, or request for indictment.
- An arrest, detention, or warrant without an indictment does not by itself resolve Yes.
- If reports only say prosecutors are considering charges or seeking to summon him, resolve No unless an actual indictment is confirmed.
- The date used is the date the indictment is officially announced or credibly reported as having occurred in South Korea; if sources disagree, use the earliest date supported by the primary official source.
- If the indictment occurs before 2025-09-01 or after 2025-10-01, this question resolves No.
- If by 2025-10-01 no authoritative information exists and available reporting is contradictory such that it cannot be determined whether an indictment occurred within the window, the question should resolve as Unresolvable.

Resolution window: This question only considers qualifying events occurring between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.

Ministry of Justice (ROK): https://www.moj.go.kr/

question: Will Italy win the second most medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the second most medals (including gold, silver, and bronze) at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most medals won will use most gold medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most medals won, and Norway wins more gold medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

subquestions.question: Will Italy rank in the top 3 countries by total medals on the official Milano Cortina 2026 medal table at the end of 2026-02-19 UTC?
subquestions.background_information:
Italy is the host nation for the 2026 Winter Olympics, which often boosts medal performance through home advantage. Early results suggest Italy started well: AP reported that on the first day Italy won a gold in women's 3,000m speed skating plus silver and bronze in the men's downhill, giving the hosts an early multi-medal start (https://apnews.com/). GEO TV also reported that as of 2026-02-07, Italy had 2 medals in one tally summary, while the broader point across early coverage is that Italy was already near the top of the standings and the table remained highly fluid with many events still to come through February 22 (https://www.geo.tv/latest/). The Games feature 116 medal events across 19 days, so being top-3 by total medals by February 19 would be a meaningful late-stage indicator of whether Italy can ultimately finish as high as second overall by February 22 (https://www.independent.co.uk/). 

Historical and pre-Games context suggests Italy is not the default favorite for second in total medals. Norway dominated Beijing 2022 with 37 total medals, while Germany and the United States were also projected before Milano-Cortina 2026 to be among the leading teams by total medals; Bleacher Report projected the United States, Norway, and Germany to lead the medal count and all exceed 25 medals (https://bleacherreport.com/). CBS Sports likewise highlighted strong medal prospects for the United States across hockey, speed skating, snowboarding, alpine skiing, and figure skating, while Norway remained the benchmark Winter Olympics power (https://www.cbssports.com/olympics/news/2026-winter-olympics-medal-count/). 

Because the ultimate question is whether Italy finishes exactly second in total medals after all events, Italy being top 3 with only a few competition days remaining is a useful crux: if Italy is outside the top 3 by 2026-02-19, its path to second becomes much narrower; if it is inside the top 3, especially as host nation with momentum, the case for an eventual second-place finish strengthens materially.

Sources:
AP News Olympics coverage — https://apnews.com/
The Independent, Winter Olympics schedule and day-by-day events — https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/winter-olympics-2026-schedule-results-b2678605.html
Bleacher Report, Milano Cortina final medal count predictions — https://bleacherreport.com/
CBS Sports, 2026 Winter Olympics medal count — https://www.cbssports.com/olympics/news/2026-winter-olympics-medal-count/
GEO TV Olympics medal race report — https://www.geo.tv/latest/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, on the official country medal table for the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics published by Olympics.com, Italy is ranked 1st, 2nd, or 3rd by total medals at the end of 2026-02-19 UTC. This question resolves No otherwise.

Resolution window: This question concerns the official medal-table status between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-19, and specifically resolves based on the medal table as it stands at 2026-02-19 23:59:59 UTC.

Primary source: the official Milano Cortina 2026 medal table on Olympics.com, such as https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/milano-cortina-2026/medals .

Ranking method: use the ranking/order displayed by Olympics.com on that medal table page at the resolution time. If Olympics.com offers multiple sort options, use the default displayed country ranking/order on the page. If the page clearly lists total medals and rank, that displayed rank controls.

Fallbacks: If the specific Milano Cortina medal page is unavailable at resolution time, use another official Olympics.com page for Milano Cortina 2026 medal standings or results archive. If no official Olympics.com medal table snapshot for 2026-02-19 is available, use the latest official Olympics.com medal table published before 2026-02-20 00:00:00 UTC. If the Olympics.com official site is wholly unavailable, archived captures of the same official Olympics.com page (for example via the Internet Archive) may be used to establish the displayed ranking.

If the Games are suspended or materially interrupted before 2026-02-19 and no official medal table is published for that date, this question resolves based on the latest official Olympics.com medal table published within the window from 2026-02-08 through 2026-02-19 inclusive. If no such official medal table exists, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Sources for resolution:
Olympics.com Milano Cortina 2026 medals page — https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/milano-cortina-2026/medals
Olympics.com main site — https://www.olympics.com/
subquestions.rationale: This is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it asks about Italy being top 3 at an intermediate date rather than finishing exactly second at the end. It is a strong indicator because the final few days rarely allow a nation far down the table to leap into second in total medals, especially against powers like Norway, the United States, and Germany. Knowing whether Italy is top 3 by February 19 should substantially update forecasts for whether it can finish second by February 22.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Italy must appear ranked 1st, 2nd, or 3rd by total medals on the Olympics.com official Milan Cortina 2026 medal table as of 2026-02-19 23:59:59 UTC. Observable evidence: medal table data from Olympics.com or reliable secondary sources reporting the standings. Key entities: Italy, Norway, USA, total medal counts, official rankings. The resolution criteria references 'total medals' ranking but also defers to whatever Olympics.com displays by default (which is gold-first/IOC standard).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Milano Cortina 2026 medal table standings February 19' — to find end-of-day standings; 2) 'Italy medal count Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics rankings' — to find Italy's specific rank; 3) 'Olympics.com medal table default ranking gold medals 2026' — to determine the ranking methodology; 4) 'Italy US medal standings February 19 2026 Winter Olympics end of day final' — to find the final state at end of resolution window
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple sources on Feb 19, 2026 report Italy's medal standings. USA Today (6:32 AM): Norway 1st (33 total), Italy 2nd (26 total), USA 3rd (24 total). Heavy.com (morning): Norway 1st (34 total), USA 2nd (24 total) — Italy not given exact rank. USA Today (5:56 PM, 'after Feb 19 events'): Norway 1st (34), USA 2nd (27), Italy 3rd (26). Times of India: Norway 1st, Italy 2nd, USA 3rd. Newsweek (reflecting end of Feb 18): Norway 1st, Italy 2nd, USA 3rd. The USA surpassed Italy in total medals during Feb 19 competition (USA won women's hockey gold, women's figure skating gold, Alysa Liu gold, etc.). By end of day, USA: 27 total, Italy: 26 total.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria states 'ranked 1st, 2nd, or 3rd by total medals' with the default Olympics.com displayed ranking controlling. Two ranking scenarios at end of Feb 19: (A) By total medals: Norway (34) 1st, USA (27) 2nd, Italy (26) 3rd — Italy is 3rd [source](https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/2026/02/19/winter-olympics-medal-count-after-feb-19/88766883007/). (B) By gold-first (Olympics.com standard): Italy (9G) and USA (9G) tied in gold — tiebreaker silver: USA (12S) > Italy (5S) → USA 2nd, Italy 3rd [corroborated by [Heavy.com](https://heavy.com/sports/olympics/medal-count-today/) and [Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/international-sports/2026-winter-olympics-medal-standings-update-norway-on-top-italy-and-usa-close-behind/articleshow/128573305.cms)]. Under BOTH ranking methods, Italy ranks 3rd (within top 3) at end of Feb 19.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: USA Today 'after Feb 19 events' article published 2026-02-19 at 5:56 PM local time (likely ET). This represents standings after major events on Feb 19 including women's hockey final (USA won gold), women's figure skating (USA won gold), ski mountaineering, etc. The resolution window closes at 2026-02-19 23:59:59 UTC. The 5:56 PM timestamp is well within this window and reflects post-event standings. Additional events may have occurred after 5:56 PM ET (approx. 22:56 UTC) but the standings were Italy 3rd with 26 total medals at that point.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Italy was consistently in 2nd place for most of Feb 19 (as reflected in morning sources showing Italy 2nd with 26 total). It moved to 3rd by total medals when USA surpassed it during the day. Under either ranking method, Italy remained in top 3 throughout Feb 19. The question asks about Italy's status 'at the end of 2026-02-19 UTC' (23:59:59 UTC). Multiple sources confirm Italy was 3rd at end of day.

However, Italy still remained 3rd (top 3). No evidence that any other country surpassed Italy to push it below 3rd place.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Multiple independent sources confirm Italy was ranked in the top 3 (specifically 3rd) by total medals at the end of February 19, 2026. Under gold-first ranking (Olympics.com default): Norway 1st (16G), USA 2nd (9G, 12S), Italy 3rd (9G, 5S). Under total medals ranking: Norway 1st (34), USA 2nd (27), Italy 3rd (26).
