question: James Comey indicted before October?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any Federal or State jurisdiction of the United States formally charges or otherwise announces a criminal indictment of James Comey between July 8 and September 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

For the purposes of this market the District of Columbia and any county, municipality, or other subdivision of a State shall be included within the definition of a State.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from US governmental sources, however a wide consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will any U.S. federal law-enforcement or prosecutorial authority publicly confirm between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-23 that James Comey is the subject of an active criminal investigation?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term public confirmation that James Comey is an active criminal target or subject of investigation would be a strong leading indicator for the ultimate question about indictment before late September 2025. Indictments typically follow investigative steps such as witness interviews, document collection, grand-jury activity, or formal public statements by prosecutors or investigators. While media commentary alone is weak evidence, an official confirmation from the Department of Justice, an FBI field office, a U.S. Attorney's Office, a state attorney general, or a local district attorney would materially increase the probability of a near-term indictment.

There has already been public speculation that Comey may be under scrutiny. Fox News legal analyst Gregg Jarrett said in July 2025 that prosecutors might seek an indictment of Comey or John Brennan and that a grand jury in Washington, D.C. could be involved, though this was commentary rather than an official announcement: https://conservativenewstoday.com/gregg-jarrett-explains-why-a-dc-jury-handling-comey-or-brennan-case-might-be-a-fools-errand/ . Separately, some partisan outlets in July 2025 claimed the Trump DOJ was preparing a criminal conspiracy case involving Comey, but those reports did not constitute an official governmental confirmation and cited no charging document: https://www.russia-news-now.com/a-new-age-of-accountability-trump-doj-preps-criminal-conspiracy-case-against-russiagate-architects/ .

Official DOJ practice is that criminal investigations and charges are ordinarily announced via press releases, court filings, or public statements from the responsible office. The Department of Justice newsroom is the main central source for federal charging announcements: https://www.justice.gov/news . U.S. Attorneys' Offices also publish district-level charging announcements, for example through their press-release pages collected at https://www.justice.gov/usao/find-your-united-states-attorney . The FBI publishes major investigative announcements and public statements in its newsroom at https://www.fbi.gov/news . If authorities are moving toward an indictment of Comey in the short window relevant to the ultimate market, an official acknowledgement of an active criminal investigation is one of the most observable precursor events.

Sources:
DOJ Newsroom — https://www.justice.gov/news
Find Your United States Attorney — https://www.justice.gov/usao/find-your-united-states-attorney
FBI News — https://www.fbi.gov/news
Conservative News Today (Jarrett commentary) — https://conservativenewstoday.com/gregg-jarrett-explains-why-a-dc-jury-handling-comey-or-brennan-case-might-be-a-fools-errand/
Russia News Now report — https://www.russia-news-now.com/a-new-age-of-accountability-trump-doj-preps-criminal-conspiracy-case-against-russiagate-architects/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-23 inclusive, any official U.S. governmental source publicly states that James Comey is the subject or target of an active criminal investigation.

Qualifying official sources include: the U.S. Department of Justice (https://www.justice.gov/news), any U.S. Attorney's Office website listed via https://www.justice.gov/usao/find-your-united-states-attorney, the FBI newsroom (https://www.fbi.gov/news), a state attorney general's official website, a state or local prosecutor's official website, or an official on-the-record statement attributable to such an office and reproduced by that office.

For Yes, the official statement must explicitly name James Comey and indicate an active criminal investigation using language such as "is under criminal investigation," "is being investigated," "is the subject of an investigation," "is the target of an investigation," or functionally equivalent wording. A statement merely saying authorities are "reviewing," "looking at," or "examining" matters related to him without clearly indicating an active criminal investigation is insufficient.

This question also resolves Yes if an official filing or court proceeding published during the window explicitly states that Comey is a subject or target of a criminal investigation, even if no press release is issued.

This question resolves No if no such official public confirmation occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-23 inclusive.

If only anonymous-source media reports appear, with no official public confirmation in the window, resolve No. If an official source publishes after 2025-09-23 about events during the window, that does not count; the confirming public statement itself must occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-23 inclusive. If there is a source outage or ambiguity, a broad consensus of credible reporting quoting a named official on the record may be used as a fallback, provided the reporting clearly attributes the confirmation to an official U.S. governmental authority.

Primary resolution sources: DOJ Newsroom https://www.justice.gov/news ; FBI News https://www.fbi.gov/news ; relevant U.S. Attorney's Office pages via https://www.justice.gov/usao/find-your-united-states-attorney .
subquestions.rationale: A public official confirmation of an active criminal investigation is a meaningful precursor to indictment and is distinct from the ultimate question. It captures whether authorities are openly moving against Comey, which would sharply update the odds of an indictment before the ultimate market closes.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: (1) An official U.S. governmental source (DOJ, FBI newsroom, U.S. Attorney's Office, state AG, or equivalent), (2) publicly stating between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-23, (3) that James Comey specifically IS the subject or target of an active criminal investigation, (4) using explicit language such as 'is under criminal investigation,' 'is the subject/target of an investigation,' or functionally equivalent wording. Anonymous-source media reports are explicitly insufficient per the resolution criteria.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'James Comey criminal investigation DOJ 2025' [Sept 1-23] — to find any official DOJ statements; (2) 'James Comey subject target criminal investigation federal 2025' [Sept 1-23] — to find any official confirmation; (3) 'James Comey DOJ investigation indicted charged 2025 September' [Sept 1-23] — to find any charges or indictments; (4) 'James Comey federal probe official statement DOJ announcement September 2025' [Sept 1-23] — to find press releases; (5) 'Erik Siebert Comey investigation Eastern District Virginia 2025' [Sept 1-23] — to find any official statements from EDVA; (6) 'DOJ Justice Department Comey criminal investigation announcement statement September 2025' [Sept 1-23] — to verify any official announcements; (7) 'Comey grand jury indictment charges filed 2025' [Sept 1-23] — to find any indictments.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) ABC News report (Sept 18, republished at freerepublic.com) that Daniel Richman (Comey friend) was subpoenaed in a criminal probe examining whether Comey lied in Congress — REJECTED: This is a media report citing anonymous sources, not an official governmental confirmation. (B) Trump Truth Social posts (Sept 20-21) demanding DOJ action against Comey — REJECTED: Trump is not a law-enforcement/prosecutorial authority making an official statement about an active investigation; these are political demands. (C) Erik Siebert resignation (Sept 19-22) — media reports indicate he had doubts about evidence in the Comey probe — REJECTED: This is media reporting on Siebert's private assessment, not an official DOJ confirmation of an active investigation targeting Comey. (D) Mother Jones, Raw Story, AZ Central articles mentioning 'investigations' of Comey — REJECTED: All cite media reports/political sources, not official governmental statements. (E) No DOJ press releases, FBI newsroom posts, or U.S. Attorney's Office statements found explicitly naming Comey as subject/target of an active criminal investigation.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the candidate events satisfy the resolution criteria. The resolution criteria explicitly state: 'If only anonymous-source media reports appear, with no official public confirmation in the window, resolve No.' All evidence found consists of: media reports citing anonymous sources about a probe related to Comey; Trump political statements demanding action; reporting on Siebert's departure. No official governmental source published an explicit statement naming James Comey as the subject or target of an active criminal investigation. The Straits Times summary mentioning 'the DOJ's opening of an unspecified criminal investigation into her father' references background context and is not an official DOJ statement made during the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying official statement with a timestamp was found within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-23 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: Multiple sources confirm that as of late September 2025, the status of any Comey probe was contested even within DOJ — U.S. Attorney Siebert reportedly declined the case citing insufficient evidence, and was forced out. This actually suggests no official confirmation of an active investigation had been made. The Raw Story article from Sept 22 notes the probe was described by analyst Wittes as a 'ghost investigation' that had only 'momentarily' become flesh. This further confirms no official public confirmation meeting the resolution criteria was issued.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly shows: (1) There are media reports of a federal probe touching on Comey's potential perjury, based on anonymous sources; (2) Trump publicly demanded DOJ action against Comey; (3) The EDVA U.S. Attorney Siebert resigned amid pressure to bring charges, partly because he felt the Comey case lacked sufficient evidence; but (4) No official DOJ, FBI, or U.S. Attorney's Office statement explicitly confirmed that Comey is 'the subject' or 'target' of an active criminal investigation during the window. The resolution criteria explicitly exclude anonymous-source media reports and require an official public confirmation. The question resolves No, with the window closing at 2025-09-23.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will CME FedWatch assign less than a 50% probability to a December 2025 FOMC rate cut at the close of trading on 2025-12-05?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a market-based indicator for whether the Fed is likely to pause at its December 9–10, 2025 meeting, which is the first leg of the ultimate Dec–Jan–Mar path question. If market-implied odds of a December cut fall below 50% by early December, that would be evidence that investors increasingly expect a December pause, which in turn makes a Pause–Pause–Pause sequence more plausible.

As of late October 2025, the Fed had already cut rates at the September and October meetings, leaving the target range at 3.75%–4.00% after the October 29, 2025 decision, according to reporting summarizing the FOMC outcome and the Federal Reserve's policy stance. Several reports also emphasized that Chair Powell said a December cut was "not a foregone conclusion" and highlighted growing internal division, including dissents in opposite directions at the October meeting. See Yahoo Finance coverage from 2025-10-30: https://finance.yahoo.com/ and CNBC coverage of the October meeting context: https://www.cnbc.com/ . The Federal Reserve publishes meeting calendars and policy decisions at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm and open market policy implementation information at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm .

CME's FedWatch Tool is widely used to infer market-implied probabilities for target-rate outcomes at upcoming FOMC meetings from 30-Day Federal Funds futures. Its methodology and data page are here: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html . Because the ultimate question hinges heavily on whether December is a pause or a cut, a drop in implied cut odds below 50% by 2025-12-05 would be a meaningful early signal favoring a pause-first path rather than continued easing.

Sources:
Federal Reserve FOMC calendars: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
Federal Reserve open market operations / policy page: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
Yahoo Finance (site referenced in provided context): https://finance.yahoo.com/
CNBC Fed coverage (site): https://www.cnbc.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05 inclusive, the closing reading on 2025-12-05 of CME FedWatch for the December 2025 FOMC meeting implies that the probability of any rate cut (defined as the sum of all outcomes with an upper bound below the pre-meeting upper bound of 4.00%) is less than 50.0%.

For avoidance of doubt, because the target range after the October 29, 2025 meeting is reported as 3.75%–4.00%, a "December cut" means any December 2025 target range outcome with upper bound below 4.00%. A "December pause" corresponds to 3.75%–4.00%.

Primary source: CME FedWatch Tool, December 2025 meeting probabilities: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html

Resolver should use the probabilities displayed for the December 2025 FOMC meeting at the close of trading on 2025-12-05, U.S. time. If CME provides a downloadable or archived probability table for that date, that should be used. If multiple cut outcomes are shown, their probabilities are summed.

Fallback criteria: If the interactive FedWatch page is unavailable, resolution should use an archived CME page capture for 2025-12-05 or a CME-published table/data file showing the same probabilities. If CME ceases publication entirely before 2025-12-05 and no archived 2025-12-05 reading is available, the question should be considered unresolvable rather than inferred from news reports.

Supporting reference for current target range and FOMC meeting schedule: Federal Reserve calendar and policy pages at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm and https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm .
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends crucially on whether the Fed pauses in December rather than cutting again. Market-implied odds for the December meeting are a timely, continuously updated synthesis of incoming macro data, Fed communications, and policy expectations. If cut odds are below 50% by December 5, that is strong evidence toward a December pause and thus raises the likelihood of a Pause–Pause–Pause sequence overall.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: CME FedWatch probability of any December 2025 rate cut (any target range outcome with upper bound below 4.00%) must be LESS THAN 50% at the close of trading on 2025-12-05. Observable evidence: direct citation of CME FedWatch probabilities for December 2025 FOMC meeting on December 5, 2025. Key threshold: 50.0%. Key entities: CME FedWatch Tool, December 2025 FOMC meeting (Dec 9-10). Timing: close of trading on 2025-12-05 (within window 2025-11-05 to 2025-12-05).
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'CME FedWatch December 2025 FOMC rate cut probability' (Nov 25-Dec 5) - to find historical trajectory of probabilities; Query 2: 'Federal Reserve December 2025 rate cut odds probability December 5' (Nov 25-Dec 5) - same purpose; Query 3: 'CME FedWatch December 5 2025 rate cut probability percentage' (Dec 5 only) - to find specific December 5 readings; Query 4: 'Fed rate cut probability December 5 2025 jobs report NFP' (Dec 5-Dec 6) - to find Dec 5 specific readings; Query 5: 'Fed rate cut probability 90% December 5 2025 PCE data' (Dec 5 only) - confirmation query.

All sources are from December 5, 2025 and directly cite CME FedWatch. No events rejected — all clearly show probabilities far above 50%.

All citations are for the December 2025 FOMC meeting (December 9-10). The probability ranges from ~85% to ~90% on December 5, all far exceeding 50%. subquestions.question: Will Guyana or the Guyana Defence Force publicly report at least one new armed cross-border incident attributed to Venezuelan forces or actors firing from Venezuelan territory into Guyana between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:

Tensions are already elevated. On 2025-08-31, Guyana's military reported that a Joint Services patrol escorting election officials near the Upper Cuyuni River was fired upon from the Venezuelan side; no injuries were reported, but the incident showed that live-fire contact across the border had already occurred shortly before this forecasting window. Guyana's government has also said Venezuela has engaged in a pattern of 'illegal and aggressive actions' aimed at annexing Essequibo, including unlawful bridge construction, unauthorized overflights, and plans to hold Venezuelan elections for the disputed area despite ICJ measures ordering Venezuela not to alter the status quo. See Newsroom Guyana, 2025-05-25: https://newsroom.gy/2025/05/25/guyana-on-high-alert-as-venezuela-threatens-international-peace-and-order/

Venezuelan rhetoric has also intensified. On 2025-09-15, Venezuelan Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino López warned Guyana and Trinidad and Tobago that if the U.S. attacked Venezuela from their territory, they would 'also receive a response,' framing this as 'legitimate defense.' This subquestion is not a restatement of invasion. A reported armed cross-border firing incident is a lower-level, more observable escalation marker that would update forecasts about whether Venezuela is willing to use force against Guyana in the near term.

If an alleged incident is reported during the window but later explicitly retracted by the originating Guyanese authority before 2025-10-31, it will not count. Key elements: (1) shots actually fired, (2) origin from Venezuelan territory/waters or by Venezuelan uniformed/armed actors crossing from Venezuela, (3) official Guyanese attribution, (4) event within the October 2025 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'Guyana Venezuela armed cross-border incident shooting October 2025' — to find direct evidence of the qualifying event; (2) 'Guyana Defence Force Venezuelan forces border attack 2025' — to find GDF reports of Venezuelan military action; (3) 'Guyana Defence Force shots fired Venezuelan territory border October 2025' — targeting specific shots-fired criteria; (4) 'GDF Venezuelan soldiers crossed border fired weapons Essequibo 2025' — targeting uniformed personnel crossing; (5) 'Guyana Venezuela military incursion attack shooting border October 2025' — broader military incursion search; (6) 'Venezuelan bomb attack Georgetown Guyana October 2025 Organizacion R' — to check if bomb attack could qualify; (7) 'DPI Guyana government statement Venezuelan forces armed attack 2025' — targeting official Guyanese statements; (8) 'Guyana border Venezuela gunfire shooting incursion Essequibo October 2025' — targeting Essequibo-specific gunfire.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified during October 2025: (A) General Guyana-Venezuela border tensions: Multiple articles discuss military buildup, ExxonMobil oil production, Venezuelan territorial claims, diplomatic tensions, and Guyana acquiring French military hardware — but NO armed cross-border firing incidents reported. (B) Venezuelan bomb attack on Georgetown gas station (October 26, 2025): A Venezuelan national linked to Organización R planted a bomb at a Mobil gas station, killing a child. This was a bombing/explosive attack inside Guyana by a Venezuelan national entering by boat — but: it was NOT shots fired from Venezuelan territory into Guyana; it was a bomb, not gunfire; the actor entered Guyana and operated inside Guyana rather than firing from Venezuelan territory. Does not meet the specific criteria of 'shots fired from Venezuelan territory/waters' or 'Venezuelan uniformed personnel firing.' (C) March 2025 Venezuelan gunboat incident in ExxonMobil waters: Pre-dates the October 2025 window entirely. (D) US strikes on Venezuelan drug boats: These were US operations, not Venezuelan forces attacking Guyana. (E) Venezuelan military buildups and threats: These are troop movements and political threats, explicitly excluded by the resolution criteria. No evidence found of Venezuelan uniformed forces or armed actors firing shots from Venezuelan territory into Guyana during October 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the events found match the exact resolution criteria. The Georgetown gas station bombing ([Guyana Inquirer](https://guyanainquirer.com/keep-nation-informed-as-investigations-continue-into-deadly-terror-attack-psc-urges-govt/), [AP News](https://apnews.com/article/guyana-gas-station-attack-953752fc189a5baeb5caa11e779fe2d8)) involved a Venezuelan national but: (1) used an explosive device, not gunfire; (2) the attack occurred INSIDE Guyana (Georgetown), not from Venezuelan territory into Guyana; (3) the perpetrator entered Guyana by boat and carried out the attack locally — not from Venezuelan territory. The resolution criteria explicitly requires shots fired FROM Venezuelan territory or waters, or by Venezuelan UNIFORMED personnel crossing from Venezuela. Criminal actors (Organización R is a criminal network, not Venezuelan uniformed forces) conducting bombings inside Guyana do not qualify. The bne IntelliNews article ([Guyana-Venezuela border tensions](https://www.intellinews.com/guyana-venezuela-border-tensions-simmer-as-exxonmobil-production-continues-407114/)) discusses general tensions but reports no armed firing incidents in October 2025. No Guyanese official statement attributing shots fired from Venezuelan territory was found in any source.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with a reliable timestamp was found. The closest events (bomb attack on October 26, 2025; Venezuelan gunboat incident from March 2025) do not meet the resolution criteria.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found anywhere in the October 2025 window. N/A.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove No conclusion by: (1) searching specifically for Venezuelan uniformed forces firing into Guyana — no evidence found; (2) checking if the Georgetown bombing could qualify — it does not meet the 'shots fired from Venezuelan territory' criterion; (3) reviewing all border-related incidents reported — only general tensions, political threats, troop buildups, and the bomb attack (which doesn't qualify) were found. The absence of reporting from credible outlets that would normally cover such an event (Reuters, AP, BBC, local Guyana outlets) strongly supports the conclusion that no qualifying armed cross-border incident occurred. The articles from bne IntelliNews, OilPrice.com, and others covering the Guyana-Venezuela tensions extensively during October 2025 make no mention of any cross-border shooting incident, reinforcing the No resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence clearly points to No resolution. While significant Guyana-Venezuela tensions existed during October 2025 (military buildups, diplomatic disputes, Venezuelan territorial claims, even a Venezuelan criminal bomb attack inside Georgetown), no armed cross-border incident meeting the specific criteria — shots fired FROM Venezuelan territory/waters into Guyana or by Venezuelan uniformed forces crossing from Venezuela — was publicly reported by Guyanese authorities or two credible independent outlets during October 1-31, 2025. The window closed with no qualifying event. Resolution: No, with resolution_datetime at end of window.

question: Will Samsung release a trifold phone by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Samsung releases a phone with three foldable screens by the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

In order to be considered released, the product must be available for purchase by the general public within the specified timeframe. An announcement or unveiling alone is not sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from Samsung. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Samsung publish an official product page or newsroom post between 2025-11-12 and 2025-12-09 that states its trifold phone will be sold in at least one market in 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Samsung has already moved beyond rumor stage: the company officially showed a trifold handset at a public technology showcase in late October 2025, and credible reporting after the APEC showcase said Samsung told media it planned to bring the device to users "within this year." This makes a near-term official commercialization statement a strong indicator for whether a public release will occur by the end of the ultimate market window. See TechRadar's report on Samsung officially displaying the device at the K-Tech Showcase: https://www.techradar.com/phones/samsung-galaxy-phones/the-samsung-galaxy-tri-fold-just-got-officially-shown-off . Forbes also reported that Samsung said in an official statement to SamMobile that it planned to bring the device to users "within this year": https://www.forbes.com/sites/ewanspence/2025/11/01/samsung-galaxy-trifold-folding-phone-release-date-coming-soon/ .

Samsung's official newsroom and product sites are typically where the company posts launch announcements, availability details, and market-by-market sales timing for flagship devices. If Samsung itself publishes a dated statement before 2025-12-09 saying the trifold will go on sale in 2025 in at least one named market, that would be a strong leading indicator that an actual public release by the ultimate deadline is likely. Conversely, if no such official commercialization statement appears by then, the probability of a true public release by the deadline is lower.

Official Samsung sources that would plausibly carry such a statement include Samsung Global Newsroom and Samsung Electronics product/news pages: https://news.samsung.com/global and https://www.samsung.com/global/galaxy/ .

Sources:
TechRadar - The Samsung Galaxy tri-fold just got officially shown off — https://www.techradar.com/phones/samsung-galaxy-phones/the-samsung-galaxy-tri-fold-just-got-officially-shown-off
Forbes - Samsung Finally Unveils Galaxy TriFold And Confirms Release Date Coming Soon — https://www.forbes.com/sites/ewanspence/2025/11/01/samsung-galaxy-trifold-folding-phone-release-date-coming-soon/
Samsung Global Newsroom — https://news.samsung.com/global
Samsung Galaxy site — https://www.samsung.com/global/galaxy/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-12 and 2025-12-09 inclusive, Samsung publishes on an official Samsung-owned website a product page, newsroom post, press release, or official event recap that explicitly states that Samsung's trifold phone (a phone with two hinges / three panels, regardless of final product name) will be sold, available for purchase, or launched in at least one market during calendar year 2025.

The qualifying statement must appear on an official Samsung domain, such as Samsung Global Newsroom (https://news.samsung.com/global), a regional Samsung Newsroom site, Samsung.com product pages, or another clearly official Samsung web property. The statement must be public and accessible on the web during or after the window.

Examples that count:
- "Available in Korea starting December 2025"
- "On sale this year in China"
- "Launching in select markets in 2025"

Examples that do NOT count:
- Mere display/showcase/unveiling language with no sales timing
- Third-party media reports quoting unnamed sources
- Statements that only say "coming soon" or "within this year" unless they are newly published by Samsung within the 2025-11-12 to 2025-12-09 window and clearly refer to market availability for sale in 2025
- Developer-facing references with no consumer sales commitment

Primary sources for resolution will be official Samsung sites, especially:
- Samsung Global Newsroom: https://news.samsung.com/global
- Samsung global Galaxy pages: https://www.samsung.com/global/galaxy/
- Samsung Electronics main site: https://www.samsung.com/

If no qualifying official Samsung statement is published between 2025-11-12 and 2025-12-09 inclusive, resolve No.

If Samsung publishes ambiguous language and no reasonable determination can be made about whether it commits to 2025 sales availability, resolve No unless a later official clarification within the same 2025-11-12 to 2025-12-09 window removes the ambiguity.

If Samsung's official sites are unavailable or archived incompletely, archived copies (for example via the Internet Archive) and contemporaneous coverage from reputable outlets quoting and linking the Samsung statement may be used as fallback evidence, but only if they clearly identify an official Samsung publication within the 2025-11-12 to 2025-12-09 window.
subquestions.rationale: An official Samsung sales-timing statement is a strong near-term crux for whether a real public release will happen by the ultimate deadline. It is not the same as asking whether the phone is released; instead, it tracks whether Samsung has crossed the internal commercialization threshold of publicly committing to 2025 market availability.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Samsung must publish on an official Samsung-owned website (newsroom, product page, press release) between 2025-11-12 and 2025-12-09 a statement explicitly committing to selling/making available for purchase its trifold phone (two hinges/three panels) in at least one market during calendar year 2025. Observable evidence: an official Samsung press release, newsroom post, or product page (on news.samsung.com, samsung.com, etc.) published within the window, with explicit sale/launch language specifying a 2025 date.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Samsung trifold phone official announcement 2025 sale launch' (2025-11-12 to 2025-12-09) — to find official announcements. Query 2: 'Samsung tri-fold foldable phone product page newsroom release date' (2025-11-12 to 2025-12-09) — to find official Samsung web properties. Query 3: 'Samsung newsroom Galaxy Z TriFold official press release December 2025' (2025-12-01 to 2025-12-09) — to confirm official Samsung publication. Query 4: 'news.samsung.com Galaxy Z TriFold product page sale available purchase 2025' (2025-12-01 to 2025-12-09) — to verify official Samsung domain. Query 5: 'Samsung Global Newsroom Galaxy Z TriFold December 2025 official announcement available Korea' (2025-12-01 to 2025-12-09) — to confirm newsroom post.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: Samsung official press event in Seoul on December 2, 2025, accompanied by an official press release/newsroom post. Confirmed by multiple high-quality sources: Yahoo Finance, GSM Arena, Yonhap, 9to5Google, Engadget, Mashable, Android Authority, mensgear.net (citing 'teaser video and press release published on December 2, 2025'). The official announcement explicitly states the Galaxy Z TriFold will launch in South Korea on December 12, 2025 (within 2025), and in China, Taiwan, Singapore, and UAE before year-end 2025. Candidate event 2: Pre-window leaks/third-party reports (Nov 12-13 from Evan Blass, Chosun Daily) — REJECTED as not official Samsung statements. December 4 GSM Arena article confirms Samsung released an 'official unboxing video' — further evidence of official Samsung publications within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The official Samsung press release/announcement published December 2, 2025 (per [mensgear.net](https://mensgear.net/samsung-z-trifold/), [9to5Google](https://9to5google.com/2025/12/01/samsung-galaxy-z-trifold-specs-launch-us-confirmed/), [Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20251202002800320), [GSM Arena](https://www.gsmarena.com/samsung_galaxy_z_trifold_is_official_and_will_be_available_starting_next_week-news-70518.php), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/samsung-debuts-first-trifold-phone-052902258.html)) explicitly states: 'Galaxy Z TriFold will launch in South Korea on December 12, 2025' — a clear 2025 availability/sale date. This is the trifold phone (two hinges, three panels — confirmed by all sources). Publication date December 2, 2025 is within the 2025-11-12 to 2025-12-09 window. The statement 'Available in Korea starting December 12, 2025' directly matches the resolution criteria example 'Available in Korea starting December 2025.' Multiple outlets also cite [Blockonomi](https://blockonomi.com/samsung-stock-first-tri-fold-smartphone-debuts-as-competition-intensifies/) and [Interesting Engineering](https://interestingengineering.com/innovation/samsung-unveils-its-first-multi-folding-phone) confirming China, Taiwan, Singapore, UAE availability 'before year-end 2025.' The official Samsung press release explicitly commits to 2025 sales in at least one market (South Korea).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: December 2, 2025 — multiple independent, high-quality sources (Yonhap, 9to5Google, GSM Arena, Yahoo Finance, Engadget, Mashable, mensgear.net, GuruFocus, Market Screener, Blockonomi, Interesting Engineering, India TV News, Android Authority) all report Samsung's official press event and press release on December 2, 2025. The resolution_datetime is set to 2025-12-02T00:00:00Z as the first official Samsung publication within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying Samsung official statement within the November 12 – December 9 window exists. Pre-December 2 coverage (Nov 12-13: Yonhap citing 'industry sources,' Digital Trends citing 'Chosun report,' TechSpot citing Evan Blass leaks, The Verge citing Evan Blass, GSM Arena citing leaks) — all from third parties, not official Samsung publications. The first official Samsung publication within the window is December 2, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Digital Trends (Nov 12) headline 'Samsung's tri-folding phone could arrive in December, but you won't be able to buy it' — this referred to speculation before the official announcement and is a third-party article from before the official Samsung publication. After December 2, 2025, no source contradicts that Samsung officially committed to a 2025 sale in South Korea. The December 12, 2025 South Korea launch date is after the question window closes (Dec 9) but the ANNOUNCEMENT/commitment was made on December 2, 2025 — within the window. The resolution criteria only requires Samsung to PUBLISH a statement within the window saying it WILL BE sold in 2025, not that the actual sale occurs within the window. The official Samsung announcement on Dec 2 satisfies this.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: Yes. Samsung published an official press release and held an official press event on December 2, 2025 — within the 2025-11-12 to 2025-12-09 window — explicitly stating the Galaxy Z TriFold (a trifold phone with two hinges/three panels) would be on sale in South Korea on December 12, 2025 (in 2025), satisfying all resolution criteria. The statement appeared on Samsung's official press release (cited by multiple reputable outlets as originating from Samsung's official communications), within the required window, and explicitly commits to 2025 sales availability in at least one market.

question: Will Trump act to ban mail-in voting or voting machines in 2025?
description:
On August 18, 2025, President Donald J. Trump announced his commitment to eliminate mail-in voting and voting machines in U.S. elections, ahead of the 2026 midterms.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that inhibits mail-in voting or voting machines from use for the 2026 midterm election by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any executive action or legislation that restricts, limits, or prohibits the use of mail-in voting or voting machines in any way will qualify, even if the action is delayed, suspended, or subsequently blocked by judicial or other actions.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or DOJ publicly release, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29, a draft executive order, formal legal memorandum, or official policy document that explicitly proposes restricting mail-in voting or the use of voting machines in federal elections?
subquestions.background_information:
A useful leading indicator for whether Trump will actually act by the end of 2025 is whether the administration produces a concrete official policy artifact, not just rhetoric. Trump publicly said in August 2025 that he intended to use executive action to end mail-in voting and voting machines before the 2026 midterms, and later reiterated plans for voter-ID rules and severe limits on mail voting. Multiple reports describe the administration as planning or drafting such an order, but public reporting before 2025-11-30 appears to be centered on statements of intent rather than release of a final official text. See KOMO's report on Trump's August 18 pledge to sign an executive order to end mail-in ballots and voting machines: https://komonews.com/news/nation-world/election-officials-speak-out-as-trump-pushes-to-eliminate-mail-in-voting ; USA Today on Trump's August 30/31 Truth Social post promising an executive order on voter ID and limiting mail-in voting: https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/08/31/trump-executive-order-voter-id-mail-voting/ ; and Al Jazeera's summary of the same announcement: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/31/trump-to-order-voter-id-for-every-vote-no-exceptions .

This subquestion is informative because formal release of a draft EO, OLC/DOJ memo, or other official policy text would show the administration has moved from messaging to legally operational planning. That is a strong indicator for the ultimate question, but not identical to it: the administration could release a draft or memo and still fail to act, or act without publicly releasing such a document. The question is also grounded in the institutional reality that presidential executive actions are often preceded or accompanied by published memoranda, fact sheets, legal justifications, or Federal Register materials. The White House publishes presidential actions and statements at https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/ , and the Department of Justice posts legal and policy materials at https://www.justice.gov/ .

Sources:
KOMO News - Election officials speak out as Trump pushes to eliminate mail-in voting - https://komonews.com/news/nation-world/election-officials-speak-out-as-trump-pushes-to-eliminate-mail-in-voting
USA Today - Trump says he will issue executive order mandating voter ID requirement - https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/08/31/trump-executive-order-voter-id-mail-voting/
Al Jazeera - Trump to order voter ID for every vote, 'no exceptions' - https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/31/trump-to-order-voter-id-for-every-vote-no-exceptions
White House - Presidential Actions - https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/
U.S. Department of Justice - https://www.justice.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 inclusive, an official U.S. government source publicly releases a document that explicitly proposes restricting mail-in voting or restricting/replacing the use of voting machines in federal elections. Qualifying documents include: (a) a draft executive order, (b) a White House fact sheet or presidential memorandum describing a forthcoming order or directive, (c) a DOJ/OLC legal memorandum, guidance document, or litigation filing, or (d) a Federal Register or other official publication containing proposed executive policy language.

The document must be publicly accessible from an official government website such as the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), the Department of Justice (https://www.justice.gov/), the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/), or another .gov site, and must explicitly reference limiting, prohibiting, replacing, or otherwise inhibiting mail-in voting and/or voting machines for federal elections. Mere speeches, social-media posts, campaign statements, or anonymous-leak reporting do not qualify unless accompanied by the release of an official document.

This question resolves No if no such official document is publicly released between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 inclusive.

Primary sources for resolution: White House Presidential Actions page (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/), White House Briefing Room (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), DOJ website (https://www.justice.gov/), and Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/). If those sources are temporarily unavailable, archived copies or contemporaneous reporting from major outlets that directly link to or reproduce the official document may be used as secondary confirmation. If a document is announced during the window but only released after 2025-12-29, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Trump will actually take executive or legislative action by year-end. A publicly released draft order or formal legal memo is a concrete precursor showing administrative preparation and legal commitment, making it a strong early indicator without merely restating the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Official U.S. government source (White House, DOJ, Federal Register) publicly releases a document between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 that explicitly proposes restricting mail-in voting OR restricting/replacing voting machines in federal elections. Document must be publicly accessible from a .gov website. Qualifying types: (a) draft EO, (b) White House fact sheet/presidential memo, (c) DOJ/OLC legal memo/guidance/litigation filing, (d) Federal Register proposed policy language. Speeches, social media posts, and leak reports do NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'White House executive order mail-in voting restrictions federal elections 2025' - to find any EO on mail voting; 2) 'DOJ legal memorandum voting machines federal elections restrict 2025' - to find DOJ documents; 3) 'Trump executive order ban mail-in voting December 2025 official document released' - to find specific releases; 4) 'White House presidential action voting machines mail ballot federal election December 2025' - to find whitehouse.gov actions; 5) 'whitehouse.gov presidential actions executive order voting elections November December 2025' - to specifically check official White House actions; 6) 'Trump election integrity executive order new December 2025 voting restrictions signed' - to check for new signed orders; 7) 'DOJ OLC memorandum guidance document voting machines restrictions federal elections December 2025' - to find DOJ guidance; 8) various supplementary queries about voting machine restrictions and mail voting documents.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Trump's March 2025 EO 'Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections' - PRE-DATES the window, does not qualify; (B) Trump urging GOP governors to go 'all paper ballots' on Dec 2, 2025 - a social media post (Truth Social), not an official document; (C) DOJ confidential MOU sent to states on voter rolls - about voter registration maintenance, not mail-in voting/voting machine restrictions, AND was labeled 'confidential' not publicly released on a .gov site; (D) NDAA Section 6805 signed Dec 18, 2025 - requires penetration testing of voting machines, does not restrict/prohibit mail-in voting or voting machines, and is congressional legislation not an executive document; (E) Multiple articles from Dec 9-19 explicitly state Trump's promised EO to ban mail-in voting had NOT been issued; (F) White House press secretary indicated Trump was merely 'considering' an EO on mail-in voting. All candidates rejected as not qualifying.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No qualifying document found. Multiple independent sources explicitly state during the window that 'no [executive order on mail-in voting] has been issued' or 'has been enacted' ([Ohio Capital Journal](https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2025/12/10/repub/voting-by-mail-faces-uncertain-moment-ahead-of-midterm-elections/), [Missouri Independent](https://missouriindependent.com/2025/12/09/repub/voting-by-mail-faces-uncertain-moment-ahead-of-midterm-elections/), [ArcaMax](https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3951538), [Arkansas Advocate](https://arkansasadvocate.com/2025/12/11/repub/voting-by-mail-faces-uncertain-moment-ahead-of-midterm-elections/)). The DOJ MOU regarding voter rolls is (1) confidential, not publicly released on .gov; (2) addresses voter registration maintenance rather than restricting mail-in voting; (3) does not propose restricting or prohibiting mail-in voting or voting machines. Trump's social media posts on paper ballots are explicitly excluded by the resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event occurred. The closest potential timestamp would be Dec 18, 2025 (NDAA signing with Section 6805), but this doesn't meet criteria. No exact timestamp of a qualifying document release can be established.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the window at all, making a first-occurrence check moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Actively searched for contradictory evidence. Found no reporting indicating an official White House or DOJ document on mail-in voting/voting machine restrictions was released on any .gov website during the window. Multiple independent outlets reporting on Trump's election integrity activities during this period consistently note the absence of any such executive order. The NDAA Section 6805 (voting machine penetration testing) is the closest potential item but requires rather than restricts voting machines and is Congressional legislation, not an executive document. The DOJ MOU is about voter roll maintenance and is confidential.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. All searched evidence consistently indicates no official White House or DOJ document explicitly proposing to restrict mail-in voting or restrict/replace voting machines in federal elections was publicly released on an official .gov website during the Nov 30 - Dec 29, 2025 window. Multiple independent sources explicitly state during this period that Trump's promised executive order on mail-in voting had not been issued. The window closed without any qualifying document being released.

question: Will US GDP growth in Q3 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP "Advance Estimate" release for Q3 of 2025 scheduled for October 30, 2025.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the Atlanta Fed GDPNow model's forecast for U.S. real GDP growth in Q3 2025 be between 1.8% and 2.7% on its last update published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term nowcast of Q3 2025 GDP is one of the most direct early indicators for whether the BEA's Q3 2025 advance estimate will land in the relatively narrow 2.0% to 2.5% range. The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model is widely followed because it updates through the quarter using incoming high-frequency macro data and is explicitly designed to track the BEA's real GDP growth measure in annualized quarterly terms. The Atlanta Fed describes GDPNow as a 'nowcast' model estimate of real GDP growth based on currently available economic data: https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow. A forecast range centered near the target bracket but slightly wider (1.8% to 2.7%) is useful because nowcasts are noisy and may differ somewhat from the eventual BEA advance estimate while still being informative about whether final growth is likely to fall in the 2.0% to 2.5% band.

Current context suggests this is a meaningful crux rather than a restatement. The BEA's second estimate reported real GDP growth of 3.3% in Q2 2025, following a -0.5% contraction in Q1 2025, underscoring recent volatility in headline GDP and making a mid-2% Q3 outcome plausible but far from certain. The BEA's Q2 2025 release page reports the 3.3% annualized growth rate in the second estimate: https://www.bea.gov/news/2025/gross-domestic-product-second-estimate-corporate-profits-preliminary-estimate-and-gdp. Because Q2's strength was materially affected by trade/import dynamics, a contemporaneous nowcast for Q3 helps distinguish whether growth is settling into the low-to-mid 2% range versus remaining stronger or weakening materially.

This subquestion is grounded in current publicly available data infrastructure and resolves before the user's requested latest date of 2025-10-01. It should have meaningful value of information because forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question will often differ on whether incoming September data leave the quarter tracking near the target band.

Sources:
Atlanta Fed GDPNow: https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow
BEA Q2 2025 GDP second estimate release: https://www.bea.gov/news/2025/gross-domestic-product-second-estimate-corporate-profits-preliminary-estimate-and-gdp
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the last GDPNow forecast for 'real GDP growth (seasonally adjusted annual rate)' published on the Atlanta Fed GDPNow page between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) is greater than or equal to 1.8% and less than or equal to 2.7%. It resolves No otherwise.

Primary source: the Atlanta Fed GDPNow page at https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow . The resolver should identify all GDPNow updates posted from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 inclusive and use the chronologically last such update in that window. If the page shows a dated table or archive entry, that dated entry governs.

If the displayed figure is rounded to one decimal place, the displayed rounded figure will be used as published. If no GDPNow update is published during the window 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 inclusive, this question should resolve Unresolvable.

Fallback source: if the main GDPNow page layout changes, use the Atlanta Fed GDPNow archive or related official Atlanta Fed pages reachable from https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow that preserve the dated published nowcasts. Unofficial media summaries should not be used unless they directly reproduce an official Atlanta Fed figure and the official page is unavailable.
subquestions.rationale: GDPNow is a high-salience, quarter-specific nowcast of the same underlying concept as the ultimate question: annualized real GDP growth. Whether it is tracking near the low-to-mid 2% range by the end of September should substantially update beliefs about whether the BEA advance estimate for Q3 will land in the 2.0% to 2.5% bracket.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires identifying the LAST GDPNow forecast for real GDP growth (SAAR) published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, and checking whether that figure is ≥1.8% AND ≤2.7%. Observable evidence needed: specific dated GDPNow figures from the Atlanta Fed within the window. Key entities: Atlanta Fed GDPNow model, Q3 2025 real GDP growth, SAAR. Window: 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Atlanta Fed GDPNow forecast Q3 2025 GDP growth September' — to find all September updates; 2) 'GDPNow model estimate real GDP growth third quarter 2025' — same purpose; 3) 'Atlanta Fed GDPNow September 26 2025 3.9% GDP forecast' — to verify the Sept 26 update; 4) 'GDPNow Q3 2025 last update September 30 October 1' — to find the final update in window; 5) 'Atlanta Fed GDPNow update September 29 30 2025' — to check for any later September updates; 6) 'GDPNow forecast update October 1 2025 Q3 GDP' — to find Oct 1 update; 7) 'GDPNow 2.2% September 2 2025 Atlanta Fed Q3' — to clarify early September readings.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events found within the window: Sept 1-2 (2.2% or 3.5% depending on source/timing), Sept 4 (3.0%), Sept 10 (3.1%), Sept 16 (3.4%), Sept 17 (3.3%), Sept 24 (3.3%), Sept 26 (3.9%), Sept 30 (3.9%), Oct 1 (3.8%). The last update in the window is October 1, 2025 at 3.8%, as explicitly reported by InstaForex ('The Atlanta Federal Reserve's GDPNow model, updated on October 1, 2025, projects a slight slowdown...revising the forecast from 3.9% to 3.8%'). Multiple Oct 1 news articles (CNBC, Fortune, Breitbart, Investing.com) also cite the GDPNow as projecting ~3.9% for Q3, some possibly referencing the Sept 26 figure rather than the Oct 1 update.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The last GDPNow update within the window (Sept 1-Oct 1, 2025) was on October 1, 2025, showing 3.8%. Source: [InstaForex](https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2763148) explicitly states: 'The Atlanta Federal Reserve's GDPNow model, updated on October 1, 2025, projects a slight slowdown in U.S. economic growth for the third quarter of 2025, revising the forecast from 3.9% to 3.8%.' The figure of 3.8% is NOT between 1.8% and 2.7% — it exceeds the upper bound of 2.7%. Therefore the resolution criteria are NOT met. Additional corroboration from [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/consumer-confidence-slumps-five-month-low-inflation-jobs-outlook/761529/) and [Investing.com probability shutdown article](https://www.investing.com/analysis/probable-shutdown-adds-risk-while-us-economy-nears-economic-nirvana-200667763) citing 3.9% as of late September.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The InstaForex article published 2025-10-01 explicitly states the GDPNow was 'updated on October 1, 2025' and revised to 3.8%. The article timestamp is 2025-10-01. This is the last update within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is not about 'first occurrence' but about the LAST update in the window. The October 1 update is the chronologically latest GDPNow update within the Sept 1–Oct 1 window.
