evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The Yahoo Finance Sept 2 article mentions 2.2% for Q3 GDPNow, but this appears to be an earlier figure (possibly from late August or early September before the significant upward revision). The CalculatedRisk Sept 5 article confirms 3.0% 'unchanged from September 2 after rounding,' which contradicts the 2.2% figure — possibly the 2.2% was from before Sept 1 or from a different data source. Regardless, since the question asks for the LAST update in the window, and the Oct 1 update at 3.8% is clearly documented, the resolution is definitive. Some Oct 1-2 articles cite 3.9% (the Sept 26 figure), but InstaForex explicitly dates the 3.8% figure to Oct 1, 2025. The condition (1.8% to 2.7%) is definitively not met since the last reading was 3.8%.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The last GDPNow update within the September 1 to October 1, 2025 window was published on October 1, 2025, showing a forecast of 3.8% for Q3 2025 real GDP growth (SAAR). This figure (3.8%) is above the upper bound of 2.7% specified in the resolution criteria. Therefore, the question resolves No. The resolution_datetime is set to October 1, 2025, when the last update was published within the window.

question: GTA 6 launch postponed?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if by May 26, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, Rockstar Games or its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, officially announces that Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) will not be released by May 26, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Grand Theft Auto VI is otherwise not released in the US by May 26, 2026, 11:59 PM ET this will qualify as a postponement.

For the purposes of this market, "release" refers to the game becoming publicly available for purchase or download in the US. Early access, beta versions, other forms of pre-release availability, or leaks will not count as an official release. If the release is only for certain consoles (e.g. Xbox Series X/S) it will count.

The resolution source will be official information from Rockstar Games or its parent company, Take-Two Interactive.

subquestions.question: Will Take-Two Interactive's next official earnings release or earnings call materials published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 explicitly continue to state that Grand Theft Auto VI is planned for release on May 26, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether GTA VI will be postponed beyond May 26, 2026. A useful early indicator is whether Take-Two continues to publicly reaffirm the exact launch date in formal investor communications. Public reaffirmation in an earnings release or call deck is meaningful because Take-Two's management has strong incentives to avoid giving investors a date they no longer expect to hit.

As of late September 2025, multiple reports say Take-Two and/or Rockstar publicly reaffirmed a May 26, 2026 launch date at the September 18, 2025 shareholder meeting and on official materials. Sports Illustrated reported that Rockstar's website listed the game as "Coming May 26 2026" and that this was reiterated at Take-Two's shareholder meeting: https://www.si.com/esports/news/rockstar-confirms-grand-theft-auto-6-release-date-for-now . Hindustan Times likewise reported that the date was confirmed on Take-Two's website and at the shareholder meeting: https://www.hindustantimes.com/technology/gta-6-might-be-scheduled-for-may-2026-release-here-s-what-you-need-to-know-101758396214180.html .

Take-Two's investor relations site is the authoritative place where earnings releases, slide decks, and call transcripts/links are posted: https://www.take2games.com/ir/ . The company's earnings schedule and releases can materially move expectations around major titles, especially GTA VI, which management has tied to strong Fiscal 2027 performance in prior public statements reported by the press. If the next earnings materials still explicitly mention May 26, 2026, that is evidence against an imminent postponement. If they omit the exact date or switch to vaguer language, that would be some evidence in favor of delay risk, even if not conclusive.

This subquestion is not just an earlier version of the ultimate question: it asks about a specific intermediate signal in investor communications rather than whether a postponement is officially announced.

Sources:
Take-Two Investor Relations: https://www.take2games.com/ir/
Sports Illustrated - Rockstar Confirms Grand Theft Auto 6 Release Date...For Now: https://www.si.com/esports/news/rockstar-confirms-grand-theft-auto-6-release-date-for-now
Hindustan Times - GTA 6 might be scheduled for May 2026 release: https://www.hindustantimes.com/technology/gta-6-might-be-scheduled-for-may-2026-release-here-s-what-you-need-to-know-101758396214180.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), Take-Two Interactive publishes an official earnings release, shareholder letter, earnings presentation, or official earnings call transcript/webcast materials on its investor relations website that explicitly state that Grand Theft Auto VI is planned for release on May 26, 2026.

This question resolves No if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), Take-Two publishes such official earnings materials but they do not explicitly state that GTA VI is planned for release on May 26, 2026.

If no Take-Two earnings release, earnings presentation, shareholder letter, or official earnings call materials are published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), this question resolves Unresolvable.

Resolution should use official Take-Two investor relations materials as the primary source: https://www.take2games.com/ir/ and any earnings-release pages linked there. If both a press release and a slide deck are published in the window, either one containing the explicit May 26, 2026 statement is sufficient for Yes. Third-party news reports do not count unless they directly reproduce or link to the official Take-Two materials. If materials are first posted within the window and later edited after 2025-10-31, the version publicly available by 2025-10-31 23:59:59 UTC governs. Archived copies from the investor relations page or the company's official newsroom may be used as fallback evidence.

Primary source: Take-Two Investor Relations https://www.take2games.com/ir/
Fallback source: Take-Two corporate site/news pages if the IR site structure changes https://www.take2games.com/
Supporting context source: Sports Illustrated article summarizing prior official confirmation https://www.si.com/esports/news/rockstar-confirms-grand-theft-auto-6-release-date-for-now
subquestions.rationale: A continued explicit reaffirmation of the exact date in formal investor communications would be a strong signal that management still expects to ship on time. Failure to reaffirm, or switching to vaguer wording, would increase the odds of a later postponement announcement.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Take-Two Interactive must publish official earnings materials (earnings release, shareholder letter, earnings presentation, or official earnings call transcript/webcast) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, AND those materials must explicitly state that GTA VI is planned for release on May 26, 2026. Observable evidence: official IR page publication of earnings materials with the specific May 26, 2026 date stated. Key entities: Take-Two Interactive, GTA VI, May 26 2026, Q2 FY2026 earnings.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Take-Two Interactive earnings release October 2025' — to find any October earnings event. Query 2: 'GTA VI Grand Theft Auto 6 release date May 2026 Take-Two' — to find May 26 2026 confirmations. Query 3: 'Take-Two Interactive Q2 2026 earnings call November 6 2025 investor relations' — to confirm exact timing of earnings call. Query 4: 'Take-Two Interactive earnings release shareholder letter October 2025 investor relations' — to rule out any October earnings materials.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: Take-Two Q2 FY2026 earnings call. Multiple sources including Business Wire (Oct 9, 2025), MarketBeat (Oct 30, 2025), Benzinga (Oct 3 and 23, 2025), GuruFocus (Nov 7), Seeking Alpha (Nov 7), Shacknews (Nov 6), IBD (Nov 6), Yahoo Finance (Nov 7) all confirm the earnings call was on November 6, 2025 — OUTSIDE the October 2025 window. No earnings materials were published in October 2025. Additionally, the November 6, 2025 earnings call announced a delay of GTA VI to November 19, 2026 — not May 26, 2026.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria explicitly states: 'If no Take-Two earnings release, earnings presentation, shareholder letter, or official earnings call materials are published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), this question resolves Unresolvable.' Per [Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251009435225/en/Take-Two-Interactive-Software-Inc.-to-Report-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results-on-Thursday-November-6-2025), Take-Two explicitly announced it would report Q2 FY2026 results on November 6, 2025. Multiple sources confirm no earnings materials were published in October 2025. The Unresolvable condition is met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Take-Two announced on October 9, 2025 via Business Wire that earnings would be released on November 6, 2025. The earnings call was confirmed on November 6, 2025 at 4:30 PM ET. No earnings publication occurred within the October 1–31, 2025 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (official earnings materials published by Take-Two in October 2025) was found in any search results. All sources consistently place the earnings release on November 6, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: Searched specifically for any October 2025 earnings materials. No such materials were found across multiple searches. Multiple independent sources (Business Wire, MarketBeat, Benzinga, Shacknews, GuruFocus, Seeking Alpha, IBD) all confirm the earnings call was November 6, 2025. The question's Unresolvable condition (no earnings published in October 2025) is definitively confirmed. Furthermore, even if the question were resolvable, the November 6 earnings call announced a GTA VI delay to November 19, 2026 — not May 26, 2026 — so a Yes resolution would be impossible regardless.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No Take-Two earnings release, shareholder letter, earnings presentation, or official earnings call materials were published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. Take-Two's Q2 FY2026 earnings were released on November 6, 2025, outside the window. Per the explicit Unresolvable condition in the resolution criteria, this question cannot resolve Yes or No and must be treated as Unresolvable (resolvable=false).

question: Will US GDP growth in 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted real GDP growth rate for the United States in 2025, as reported in the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) "Advance Estimate" release for Q4 of 2025, scheduled for January 29, 2026.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: The relevant data will be the full-year real GDP growth rate as stated in the advance estimate, typically expressed as the percentage change from the annual level in 2024 to the annual level in 2025. Any revisions to this figure made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index present situation component be at least 145.0 in the January 2026 release published between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-29?
subquestions.background_information:
Consumer spending is a major driver of US GDP, so near-term measures of household conditions are useful indicators for whether full-year 2025 real GDP growth lands in the relatively solid 2.0%–2.5% range rather than below it. The Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence survey includes a Present Situation Index intended to capture consumers’ assessment of current business and labor-market conditions; stronger readings are generally associated with stronger consumption growth. The Conference Board publishes monthly Consumer Confidence releases here: https://www.conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence. 

The ultimate question will be resolved from the BEA’s advance estimate for Q4/full-year 2025 real GDP. Recent growth data suggest 2025 growth was running solidly through Q3: the user-provided news summary states Q1 was about -0.6%, Q2 about 3.8%, and Q3 about 4.3% annualized, implying the economy entered Q4 with decent momentum. The BEA GDP release page for the final underlying source is https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product. If household demand remained resilient into late 2025 and early 2026, that would modestly support the chance that full-year 2025 growth ends up in the 2.0%–2.5% bracket rather than materially lower. 

A threshold of 145.0 for the Present Situation Index is chosen because it is high enough to indicate notably strong current household sentiment without being so extreme as to be almost impossible; the January 2026 release should incorporate very recent information about labor markets and spending conditions. While consumer confidence is not identical to GDP, it is a distinct observable indicator rather than a restatement of the GDP outcome. 

Sources:
Conference Board Consumer Confidence topic page — https://www.conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence
BEA Gross Domestic Product page — https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Conference Board’s January 2026 Consumer Confidence release, published between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-29 (inclusive), reports the Present Situation Index at 145.0 or higher. It resolves No if that January 2026 release is published within that window and reports the Present Situation Index below 145.0.

Primary source: the official Conference Board Consumer Confidence release page at https://www.conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence and the specific January 2026 press release linked there.

If the January 2026 release is published within the window and later revised, the first value published in that release will govern. If the Conference Board does not publish a January 2026 Consumer Confidence release by 2026-01-29, this question should be considered unresolvable rather than resolving No, because the qualifying publication did not occur within the stated window.

For avoidance of doubt, only a January 2026 Consumer Confidence release counts; December 2025 or February 2026 releases do not count. The qualifying event must occur between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-29 inclusive.
subquestions.rationale: Household consumption is the largest component of GDP. A strong January 2026 Present Situation reading would be evidence that consumer conditions remained robust around year-end, which is relevant to whether 2025 full-year GDP growth stayed in a healthy mid-2% range. This is a different observable from GDP itself, and resolution of this subquestion should update forecasts on the ultimate GDP bracket question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Conference Board January 2026 Consumer Confidence release (published 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-29) must report Present Situation Index >= 145.0. Observable evidence: official Conference Board press release or reliable secondary sources citing the Present Situation Index value. Key threshold: 145.0.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index January 2026' (to find the January 2026 release and its values). Query 2: 'Conference Board Consumer Confidence Present Situation Index 2026' (to find the specific Present Situation component value).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: Conference Board January 2026 Consumer Confidence Index released on January 27, 2026. Multiple major outlets (CNN, Fox Business, Zero Hedge, The Hill, ABA Banking Journal, Seeking Alpha, Investing.com, Chosun, NerdWallet, Dupree Report) all published on January 27, 2026 citing the release. All consistently report Present Situation Index = 113.7. No other candidate events found within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple sources explicitly state the Present Situation Index for January 2026 = 113.7, released January 27, 2026. Sources include: [Zero Hedge](https://www.zerohedge.com/personal-finance/conference-board-consumer-confidence-crashes-12-year-lows): 'The Present Situation Index dropped 9.9 points to 113.7'; [The Hill](https://thehill.com/business/economy/5709034-consumer-confidence-index-january-fall/): 'the Present Situation Index dropped 9.9 points to 113.7'; [ABA Banking Journal](https://bankingjournal.aba.com/2026/01/consumer-confidence-drops-to-lowest-level-since-2014/): 'The present situation index fell 9.9 points to 113.7'; [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/consumer-confidence-plunges-lowest-level-more-than-decade): 'the present situation index dropped 9.9 points to 113.7'. Value of 113.7 is clearly below the 145.0 threshold. Publication date of January 27, 2026 is within the window of 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-29.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: January 27, 2026 — confirmed by multiple sources all timestamped January 27, 2026.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is the first (and only) January 2026 Consumer Confidence release. It was published January 27, 2026. No earlier publication of this specific data within the window was found.
evidence.step7_verification: All 10+ sources consistently report Present Situation Index = 113.7 for January 2026. There is no contradictory evidence. The value of 113.7 is well below 145.0. The release was published January 27, 2026, clearly within the window. The condition for Yes (PSI >= 145.0) was not met.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Conference Board's January 2026 Consumer Confidence release was published on January 27, 2026 (within the window). The Present Situation Index was reported at 113.7, which is below the required threshold of 145.0. Therefore, the question resolves No. The definitive No moment is January 27, 2026, when the release was published with a value below the threshold.

question: Will Tulsi Gabbard be the first to leave the Trump Cabinet before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve based on the next individual announced to leave the Trump Cabinet, or who otherwise ceases to be a member of the administration. If no one leaves by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “None before 2027”.

An announcement of an individual's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the resignation/removal takes effect.

If multiple individuals announce departures or are removed at the same time, the market will resolve to the individual who actually leaves office first. If they leave simultaneously, the market will resolve to the individual whose last name comes first alphabetically.

For the purposes of this market, the Cabinet includes Vice President, the heads of the 15 executive departments, as well as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the President’s Chief of Staff, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Ambassador to the United Nations, the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA). Acting officials serving in these roles are not included. The Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) is not considered Cabinet-level under the current Trump administration and is excluded from this market.

An individual will be considered to have left the Cabinet if they resign from or are removed from any Cabinet-level position, even if they are subsequently appointed to a different Cabinet-level role.

If a candidate who is not already listed, assumes a listed cabinet position they will be added to the market. However, candidates who have merely been nominated for a cabinet position will not be considered to have left, even if their nomination is rejected or withdrawn.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible reopening may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Tulsi Gabbard receive a public call for her resignation or removal from at least two Republican U.S. senators between 2026-01-05 and 2026-02-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Tulsi Gabbard is serving as Director of National Intelligence, which is one of the Cabinet-level roles included in the ultimate market. She appears politically vulnerable for several reasons. Recent reporting notes that Gabbard was confirmed narrowly, with The Washington Post analysis summarized by Raw Story saying she was confirmed by only two votes, which could make replacing her politically difficult but also signals limited Senate support compared with more secure appointees. The same analysis says Gabbard drew criticism for a video claiming the world is 'on the brink of nuclear annihilation' and that several Trump officials have faced public controversy without yet being removed. https://www.rawstory.com/trump-cabinet-turnover-analysis/

There are also signs of friction around intelligence staffing. Newsmax reported on 2025-12-12 that Rep. Don Bacon said White House 'infighting' contributed to withdrawal of Joe Francescon as nominee for deputy director of the NSA, and that Francescon had initially been selected by Gabbard with Trump's approval. https://www.newsmax.com/newsfront/nsa-joe-francescon-withdrawal/2025/12/12/id/1201234/ 

On 2026-01-04, Mediaite highlighted criticism of Gabbard after contrasting her October 2025 speech against 'regime change' with the administration's later actions in Venezuela, raising questions about her alignment with administration policy. https://www.mediaite.com/politics/tulsi-gabbard-said-us-cycle-of-regime-change-was-over-just-2-months-before-maduro-arrest/

A wave of public calls from Republican senators for Gabbard to resign or be fired would be a strong elite signal that she is uniquely endangered relative to other Cabinet officials. Because senators are central to confirmation politics and often shape media narratives around Cabinet viability, such calls would be a meaningful near-term indicator for whether she is likely to be the first Cabinet member to leave.

Sources:
Raw Story - Trump's embarrassment has left him stuck with dead beat Cabinet: analysis - https://www.rawstory.com/trump-cabinet-turnover-analysis/
Newsmax - WH Pulls NSA Nominee as Cyber Leadership Gap Widens - https://www.newsmax.com/newsfront/nsa-joe-francescon-withdrawal/2025/12/12/id/1201234/
Mediaite - Tulsi Gabbard Said US 'Cycle Of Regime Change' Was Over - Just 2 Months Before Maduro Arrest - https://www.mediaite.com/politics/tulsi-gabbard-said-us-cycle-of-regime-change-was-over-just-2-months-before-maduro-arrest/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-05 and 2026-02-01 inclusive, at least two distinct sitting Republican U.S. senators each make a public statement explicitly calling for Tulsi Gabbard to resign, step down, be removed, be fired, or be replaced as Director of National Intelligence.

Qualifying statements must be public and attributable on the record, appearing in at least one of the following: the senator's official website, official social-media account, an interview transcript/video from a credible news outlet, C-SPAN coverage, or a congressional press release. The statements must clearly refer to Tulsi Gabbard personally and clearly advocate her departure from the DNI role; vague criticism or calls for 'accountability,' hearings, investigation, or 'considering personnel changes' do not count.

Primary sources for resolution will be senators' official websites and official X/social-media accounts, Senate webpages, C-SPAN, and major credible news reports aggregating the statements. Useful source pages include: U.S. Senate homepage https://www.senate.gov/ ; C-SPAN https://www.c-span.org/ ; official Senate Republican conference/member pages as applicable; and official X posts if publicly accessible. If a statement is first reported by a credible outlet, that can be used if it quotes or embeds the senator's direct remarks.

This question resolves No if fewer than two such Republican senators make qualifying statements during the window from 2026-01-05 through 2026-02-01 inclusive.

If a statement's timing cannot be established as occurring within the 2026-01-05 to 2026-02-01 window, it does not count. If source material is unavailable at resolution time, archived versions (for example via https://archive.org/ or https://archive.today/) and contemporaneous reporting from major outlets may be used as fallback evidence.
subquestions.rationale: Open Republican senatorial demands for Gabbard's ouster would be a concrete sign that her political support is collapsing. That would materially increase the chance she becomes the first Cabinet official to depart, while the absence of such calls would be modest evidence that her position remains comparatively stable.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: At least 2 distinct sitting Republican U.S. senators must each make explicit public statements calling for Gabbard to resign, step down, be removed, fired, or replaced as DNI, between 2026-01-05 and 2026-02-01 inclusive. Observable evidence: Direct quotes in news reporting, official senator websites, C-SPAN, official social media, or congressional press releases. Key entities: Republican U.S. senators, Tulsi Gabbard as DNI. Threshold: ≥2 qualifying statements from distinct Republican senators. Timing: Must be within the specified window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Republican senator calls Tulsi Gabbard resign removal DNI 2026' — to find direct calls for removal; 2) 'Tulsi Gabbard Director National Intelligence fired replaced January 2026' — to find any firing/replacement news; 3) 'Republican senator Gabbard DNI intelligence chief January 2026' — to find any Republican criticism; 4) 'Gabbard resign fired replaced DNI Republican opposition 2026' — alternative phrasing; 5) 'GOP senator Gabbard removal criticism intelligence director 2026' — GOP-specific; 6) 'Gabbard DNI Republican bipartisan opposition removal Senate 2026' — bipartisan angle; 7) 'Ted Cruz Gabbard resign fire replacement intelligence director January 2026' — specific senator check.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple searches across the full resolution window found: (a) Extensive Democratic senator criticism of Gabbard — Sen. Mark Warner (D-VA), Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-GA), Rep. Jim Himes (D-CT), Rep. Joaquin Castro (D-TX) — calling for briefings, investigations, and condemning her presence at Georgia election office raid. These are Democrats, not Republicans. (b) Ted Cruz private 2025 donor recordings criticizing Trump/Vance, not specifically Gabbard, and not public statements. (c) Reports of 'bipartisan criticism' during Gabbard's confirmation hearing (2025), outside the resolution window. (d) No Republican senator was found explicitly calling for Gabbard's resignation, removal, firing, or replacement during the Jan 5–Feb 1, 2026 window. All criticism of Gabbard within the window came from Democrats.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found matching the resolution criteria. All explicit calls for Gabbard to explain herself, appear before committees, or be held accountable came from Democratic senators (Warner, Ossoff) and Democratic House members. question: Will the US capture Khamenei before 2027?
description:

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, “capture” means Khamenei is taken into physical custody and detained (including arrest, detention, or seizure) such that he is no longer free to leave at will, even if only temporarily. Voluntary surrender may qualify if it results in immediate detention/custody.

U.S. personnel must directly participate on the ground to qualify. Intelligence, surveillance, planning, logistics, transport, support, funding, training, or advisory roles alone will not count, even if they materially contribute to the operation. If U.S. personnel are physically present in the operational area and take direct action (e.g., raiding, detaining, securing, physically transferring custody), it will qualify. U.S. government contractors will be considered to be U.S. personnel if they are confirmed to be acting under the direction of U.S. government authorities.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

[Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20251112009251320), [Soompi](https://www.soompi.com/article/1797252wpp/breaking-newjeans-haerin-and-hyein-to-return-to-ador), [Korea JoongAng Daily](https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2025-11-13/entertainment/kpop/ADOR-to-meet-with-NewJeans-Minji-Danielle-Hanni-to-review-the-authenticity-of-their-return-statement/2453539). ADOR also explicitly announced scheduling individual meetings with all remaining members specifically about returning to group activities. The November 11 meeting (before public announcement) already addressed 'preconditions and requests for the group's return.' ADOR stated it was 'coordinating individual meeting schedules with the members and will do our best to ensure smooth discussions' — explicitly about group activity resumption. All these are attributed statements from ADOR reported by Yonhap, Soompi, Korea JoongAng Daily, Chosun, and Korea Times.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest public qualifying announcement: November 12, 2025 — ADOR's official post on verified X account announcing Haerin and Hyein's return to activities and confirming album preparations. The meeting about return conditions preceded this on November 11, 2025, but the public announcement came November 12. Korea JoongAng Daily reported the three-member announcement at approximately 7:45 PM on November 12, 2025. ADOR's statement about coordinating meeting schedules with Minji, Hanni, Danielle was reported November 13-14, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest qualifying public event within the window is the ADOR announcement on its official X account on November 12, 2025, about Haerin and Hyein resuming activities and album preparations, followed closely by the announcement of scheduling meetings with the other three members. No earlier qualifying public announcement found within the window (the court ruling was October 30-31 but ADOR's response then was only urging members to resume work, not announcing formal talks had been scheduled).
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictions: Korea Herald (Nov 17) notes 'uncertainty persists' and that three members are 'still negotiating preconditions,' but this confirms talks ARE happening, not that they don't exist. The question asks whether formal talks specifically aimed at restarting activities were announced — the evidence strongly confirms this with multiple attributed official statements from ADOR. ADOR's statements meet the qualifying criteria: 'scheduled a meeting about resuming NewJeans promotions' and 'agreed to discuss a roadmap for NewJeans activities' — with explicit mention of album release preparation and individual meetings about resumption. No contradictory evidence found that would negate the Yes resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves Yes. On November 12, 2025, ADOR made public announcements via its official verified X account (reported by Yonhap, Soompi, and multiple major Korean entertainment outlets) explicitly announcing: (1) Two members (Haerin, Hyein) would resume entertainment activities with ADOR; (2) ADOR had completed preparations for a full-length album; (3) ADOR was coordinating individual meeting schedules with the other three members specifically about their return to group activities. The November 11 meeting addressed 'preconditions and requests for the group's return.' These constitute public announcements that formal talks have been begun and scheduled specifically aimed at restarting NewJeans group activities. All qualifying criteria are met: ADOR is the announcing party, statements are attributed, major credible outlets report this, and the statements explicitly connect talks to future group activities, promotions, releases, and schedules.

question: Will the next government funding bill be a clean CR?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the next government funding bill that becomes law in the United States by December 31, 2025, is a clean continuing resolution. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

A clean continuing resolution is defined as a funding measure that temporarily extends current government spending at the previous fiscal year’s levels for a specified period, without incorporating any additional policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the first cloture vote in the U.S. Senate between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-10 on a continuing resolution or other short-term government funding measure receive at least 60 yea votes?
subquestions.background_information:
For the ultimate question, a key near-term indicator is whether Senate leadership can assemble a filibuster-proof coalition for a short-term funding vehicle. In the Senate, invoking cloture on most legislation requires three-fifths of duly chosen and sworn senators, typically 60 votes when there are no vacancies. A funding proposal that cannot clear cloture is less likely to become law quickly, and difficulty reaching 60 usually signals conflict over policy riders or broader package terms rather than consensus on a clean stopgap. The Senate's roll-call vote records and cloture motions are published by the Senate, making this a relatively objective and timely indicator. See the U.S. Senate's explanation of cloture at https://www.senate.gov/about/powers-procedures/filibusters-cloture.htm and roll-call vote listings at https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm.

Congressional funding fights in recent years have repeatedly hinged on whether leaders could move a short-term continuing resolution through the Senate with bipartisan support. A clean CR is typically easier to assemble 60 votes for than a rider-laden package, because any controversial policy provision can peel off votes from the minority and some moderates. Therefore, whether the first Senate cloture attempt on a short-term funding bill reaches 60 is a meaningful signal about whether the eventual enacted bill is likely to be clean.

Sources:
U.S. Senate - Filibusters and Cloture: https://www.senate.gov/about/powers-procedures/filibusters-cloture.htm
U.S. Senate Roll Call Votes: https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm
Congress.gov - Bills and Resolutions: https://www.congress.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-10 (inclusive), the first U.S. Senate cloture vote on any bill, joint resolution, amendment, motion to proceed, or substitute amendment whose primary purpose is to provide short-term federal government funding through a continuing resolution or comparable stopgap appropriations measure receives at least 60 yea votes.

This question resolves No if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-10 (inclusive), the first such cloture vote occurs and receives fewer than 60 yea votes.

If no such Senate cloture vote occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-10 (inclusive), this question resolves No.

For avoidance of doubt:
- "Short-term government funding measure" means legislation widely described by Congress, the Senate, or major credible media as a continuing resolution, CR, stopgap funding bill, or temporary appropriations measure intended to keep the federal government funded for a limited period rather than enact full-year regular appropriations.
- The "first cloture vote" is determined by the chronological order of Senate roll-call votes.
- If multiple cloture votes occur on the same calendar day, the earliest by official Senate roll-call numbering/time controls.
- The relevant vote may be on the bill itself, a motion to proceed, or an amendment/substitute, so long as the underlying matter is a short-term funding measure.

Primary resolution source: official U.S. Senate roll-call vote records at https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm.

Secondary/fallback sources: Congress.gov bill pages and actions at https://www.congress.gov/ and the Senate cloture reference page at https://www.senate.gov/about/powers-procedures/filibusters-cloture.htm. If the Senate site is temporarily unavailable, Congress.gov legislative actions and contemporaneous reporting from AP or Reuters may be used to identify the first relevant cloture vote and its tally.

If official records are materially delayed or contradictory such that the first qualifying cloture vote and tally cannot be determined with high confidence, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A clean CR generally needs broad bipartisan Senate support to move quickly. If the first Senate cloture attempt on a stopgap funding vehicle clears 60 votes, that is evidence that leaders are coalescing around a relatively simple, passable measure rather than a controversial package. Failure to reach 60 points the other way.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-10 (inclusive), the FIRST U.S. Senate cloture vote on a CR or short-term government funding measure must receive ≥60 yea votes. Observable evidence: Senate roll-call vote records showing the vote tally for the first qualifying cloture vote in the window. Key entities: U.S. Senate, H.R. 5371 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act), minibus/CR package; threshold: 60 yea votes; timing: first qualifying cloture vote in Oct 31 - Nov 10 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Senate cloture vote continuing resolution government funding November 2025' (to find qualifying votes); 2) 'Senate vote stopgap funding CR government shutdown November 2025' (to identify tallies); 3) 'Senate cloture vote 60-40 continuing resolution November 9 2025' (to confirm the successful vote); 4) 'Senate cloture vote October 31 November 8 2025 continuing resolution 54-44' (to confirm earlier failed votes in window); 5) 'Senate vote continuing resolution October 31 November 1 2025' (to confirm state of votes at start of window).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple qualifying cloture votes identified: (A) October 28 vote (54-45, failed) - OUTSIDE window; (B) November 4, 2025 vote (54-44, failed) - INSIDE window, this was the 14th attempt on H.R. 5371; (C) Multiple other failed votes between Nov 4-7 (~54-44 range); (D) November 9, 2025 'Senate Vote 1' (54-44 on H.R. 5371 original, failed) - INSIDE window; (E) November 9, 2025 vote on new minibus/CR package (60-40, PASSED) - INSIDE window. All votes on H.R. 5371 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act) or the new minibus CR qualify as cloture votes on short-term funding measures. The first qualifying vote within the window was on November 4, 2025, which failed 54-44.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The question requires the FIRST qualifying cloture vote in the window to receive ≥60 yea votes. Evidence from multiple sources: [JD Supra tracking](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/tracking-the-2025-us-government-5573939/) confirms 14th failed vote on Nov 4, 2025 (54-44). [Barron's](https://www.barrons.com/livecoverage/government-shutdown-election-news-today-110425/card/senate-s-14th-attempt-to-end-shutdown-not-the-charm-STuaewT3NN7cc6rFRK6o) confirms 54-44 on Nov 4. [Santa Fe New Mexican](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/briefs/how-they-voted-nov-9-2025/article_6ed4d892-e11c-430e-aa64-c50f1a6e97e2.html) confirms that on Nov 9, 'Senate Vote 1 rejected a cloture motion...with 54 yeas and 44 nays' followed by later votes. [National Law Review](https://natlawreview.com/article/healthcare-preview-week-november-10-2025) and [People's World](https://peoplesworld.org/article/senate-sellouts-eight-democratic-caucus-members-cave-on-health-care/) confirm the 60-40 vote on Nov 9. [Barbados Gazette](https://barbadosgazette.com/us-senate-shutdown-vote-what-happened-who-voted-to-end-it-whats-next/) and [Daily Caller News Foundation](https://dailycallernewsfoundation.org/2025/11/10/senate-clears-bill-to-end-41-day-government-shutdown/) confirm the Nov 9/10 60-40 vote. The FIRST qualifying cloture vote in the Oct 31-Nov 10 window was the Nov 4 vote (54-44), which did NOT reach 60 yea votes. The 60-40 vote was a LATER vote in the window, not the first.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The first qualifying cloture vote within the Oct 31 - Nov 10 window occurred on November 4, 2025 (exact time not specified in sources, but confirmed as the 14th Senate vote on H.R. 5371). Multiple sources confirm this vote failed 54-44. The successful 60-40 vote occurred on November 9, 2025 (evening, exact time not specified).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying cloture vote in the window was NOT the 60-40 vote. The JD Supra 'Tracking' article confirms the 14th attempt on H.R. 5371 on November 4 failed 54-44. The Santa Fe New Mexican article confirms a 54-44 rejection vote as 'Senate Vote 1' on November 9 itself. The WRAL article and Daily Freeman article confirm cloture votes on H.R. 5371 on October 28 (54-45 failed), which was BEFORE the window. The JD Supra October 30 update confirms NO vote was taken on October 30. The WBAP article from October 31 says '13 previous votes' (all failures) - no vote on Oct 31 itself is documented. Therefore the first qualifying cloture vote IN the window (Oct 31 - Nov 10) was on November 4, 2025 (54-44, failed).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The Barbados Gazette says the cloture vote was on 'November 10, 2025' while most other sources say November 9. The Daily Caller confirms the Senate 'passed' on November 10 (60-40), suggesting the procedural vote occurred Nov 9 evening and/or the final passage occurred Nov 10. The People's World and National Law Review clearly state November 9 for the 60-40 cloture vote. This minor date discrepancy (Nov 9 vs. Nov 10) does not affect resolution since either date is within the window and the key question is whether the FIRST qualifying vote got ≥60 yea votes - which it definitively did not. The first qualifying vote in the window failed with only ~54 yea votes.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The first qualifying cloture vote in the Oct 31 - Nov 10, 2025 window occurred on November 4, 2025, on H.R. 5371 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act), and received only 54 yea votes - far below the 60-vote threshold. Multiple subsequent cloture votes also failed (54-44 range) until the new minibus/CR package achieved the 60-40 threshold on November 9, 2025. Since the resolution criteria requires the FIRST qualifying cloture vote to receive ≥60 yea votes, and the first such vote received only 54 votes, the question resolves No. The resolution_datetime is November 4, 2025, when the first qualifying cloture vote in the window occurred and definitively failed to reach 60 yea votes.

question: Will Israeli troops enter Suwayda in 2025?
description:
This polymarket will resolve to "Yes" if Israeli military personnel physically enter Suwayda Governorate in Syria for military operations between July 17, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, aerial and maritime operations will not be considered. Only operations involving troops on the ground within Suwayda Governorate will count.

Undercover Israeli operatives and assets will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be photo and video evidence, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will at least one publicly documented Israeli ground incursion into Syria's Daraa or Quneitra governorate be reported between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
A fresh Israeli ground incursion into Daraa or Quneitra in October 2025 would be a meaningful near-term indicator for the ultimate question because Israeli ground activity in southern Syria has already expanded beyond airstrikes and has recently included repeated entries into adjacent governorates. Multiple September reports describe Israeli troops entering southern Syrian localities in Quneitra and Daraa. Enab Baladi reported that on 2025-09-28 an Israeli force of 16 vehicles entered Sida Golan in Quneitra, searched homes, and withdrew; it also described other September incursions in Quneitra villages and noted stalled talks over a proposed 'humanitarian corridor' to Suwayda (https://english.enabbaladi.net/archives/2025/09/quneitra-israel-conducts-survey-in-sida-golan/). Reuters/Yahoo reported on 2025-09-14 that Israeli troops carried out a ground operation in Syria's Daraa province and searched towns near the 1974 cease-fire line (https://www.yahoo.com/news/israeli-army-carries-latest-ground-114530154.html). Earlier reporting also described Israeli ground activity in southern Syria after July's Suwayda violence, including entries into Quneitra and Daraa and a helicopter-borne landing near al-Kiswah in late August (https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20250829-israel-conducts-intensive-air-ground-operations-in-southern-syria/ ; https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/27/israel-launches-new-operations-in-syria-after-strike-kills-soldiers). ReliefWeb noted on 2025-07-30 that Israeli media discussion had increasingly mentioned a possible IDF ground or hybrid operation in southern Syria, specifically including Sweida/Suwayda governorate (https://reliefweb.int/report/syrian-arab-republic/israel-resumes-strikes-sweida-july-30-2025).

Because Daraa and Quneitra border or sit near routes into Suwayda, additional October incursions there would suggest continued Israeli willingness to use ground forces inside southern Syria, raising the plausibility of a later entry into Suwayda itself before year-end.

Sources:
Enab Baladi - Quneitra: Israel conducts survey in Sida Golan - https://english.enabbaladi.net/archives/2025/09/quneitra-israel-conducts-survey-in-sida-golan/
Yahoo/Reuters - Israeli army carries out its latest ground incursion in southern Syria - https://www.yahoo.com/news/israeli-army-carries-latest-ground-114530154.html
Middle East Monitor - Israel conducts intensive air, ground operations in southern Syria - https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20250829-israel-conducts-intensive-air-ground-operations-in-southern-syria/
Al Jazeera - Israel launches new operations in Syria after strike kills soldiers - https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/27/israel-launches-new-operations-in-syria-after-strike-kills-soldiers
ReliefWeb - Israel Resumes Strikes on Sweida (July 30, 2025) - https://reliefweb.int/report/syrian-arab-republic/israel-resumes-strikes-sweida-july-30-2025
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if at least one Israeli ground incursion into either Daraa governorate or Quneitra governorate in Syria is publicly reported as having occurred between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

For this question, a qualifying 'ground incursion' means Israeli military personnel physically entering Syrian territory on the ground in Daraa or Quneitra governorate for a military operation. Airstrikes, drone flights, artillery fire, or purely aerial insertions that are not reported to have put troops on the ground do not count. Undercover operatives do not count.

The primary resolution standard will be credible public reporting from at least one major news outlet or a well-established regional outlet explicitly stating that Israeli troops/soldiers/forces entered a named locality or area in Daraa or Quneitra during the resolution window. Strong photo/video evidence published by credible media or journalists also counts. If multiple reports conflict on location or date, the question resolves Yes only if the preponderance of credible reporting supports that the ground entry occurred within Daraa or Quneitra and within the window.

Preferred resolution sources include Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera, BBC, AFP, Enab Baladi, SANA, and other widely cited outlets covering Syria. Example source domains that may be used at resolution include:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- Enab Baladi: https://english.enabbaladi.net/
- Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA): https://sana.sy/en/

If no such qualifying report exists for an event between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, this question resolves No. If reporting only alleges a planned operation, border staging, overflight, shelling, or an event outside the window, that does not count. If the only available evidence remains too ambiguous to determine whether troops physically entered Daraa or Quneitra during the window, the question should resolve No rather than speculate.
subquestions.rationale: Israeli entry into Suwayda would likely be preceded or accompanied by continued willingness to conduct ground operations elsewhere in southern Syria. Another October incursion into Daraa or Quneitra would be a strong behavioral indicator that Israel remains prepared to cross the border with troops, which should update forecasts upward on a later Suwayda entry.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: At least one Israeli ground incursion (military personnel physically entering Syrian territory on the ground) into Daraa governorate OR Quneitra governorate, publicly reported by a credible major outlet, between 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z and 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z. Observable evidence: explicit news reports stating Israeli troops/vehicles entered named localities in Daraa or Quneitra. Key entities: Israeli military forces, Daraa/Quneitra governorates, October 2025 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Israeli ground incursion Syria Daraa Quneitra October 2025' — to find direct event reports; 2) 'Israel troops enter Syria southern governorate 2025' — to find broader coverage; 3) 'Israeli forces ground incursion Daraa Quneitra Syria October 1-5 2025' — to find earliest event; 4) 'Israel military enters Syria Daraa village raid arrest October 4 2025' — to verify specific Daraa event and find Times of Israel coverage.

question: Israel x Syria security agreement by January 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an official security agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the governments of Israel and Syria by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market refers only to agreements which directly address border security and demarcation, normalization, or diplomatic recognition or otherwise creates a formalized security framework between the two states.    

Ceasefire announcements or other announced de-escalations such as those relating to the July 16-18 skirmishes with the Druze, or any other future military engagements, which do not address the broader security relationship will not qualify.

Only deals which are officially announced will qualify. Informal announcements which do not constitute a formalized agreement will not count.

The primary resolution source will be official statements from the Israeli and Syrian governments. However, an agreement which is announced by only of the parties will qualify if an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirms that such a formal agreement has been reached.

subquestions.question: Will the United States publicly announce, between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11 inclusive, that it is hosting or sponsoring an official Israel-Syria meeting on border security or a related security arrangement?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term official U.S. announcement of a hosted or sponsored Israel-Syria security meeting would be a strong indicator that negotiations have advanced from unofficial or disputed contacts into a more formal diplomatic phase, making a January 2026 Israel-Syria security agreement more plausible. Reporting before 2025-12-12 indicates that U.S.-mediated contacts already exist: Reuters reported in May 2025 that direct face-to-face talks had occurred between Israeli and Syrian officials to calm border tensions, with U.S. facilitation discussed in later coverage. Reuters also reported in 2025 that Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa publicly confirmed indirect negotiations with Israel and linked any final deal to Israeli withdrawal conditions, showing that a negotiating channel exists but remains politically fragile. See Reuters coverage via The Times of Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com/syrias-sharaa-says-indirect-talks-under-way-with-israel-to-calm-tensions/ and Reuters directly: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/syrias-sharaa-says-indirect-talks-with-israel-aimed-calm-tensions-2025-05-07/

Additional December 2025 reporting says Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar described Israel as engaged in unofficial talks with Syria under U.S. auspices, while Israeli and Syrian sources disagreed over whether a final draft had nearly been completed. These reports suggest real but unstable negotiations, with disputes over Mount Hermon, demilitarized zones, and withdrawal from territory captured after December 2024. See Asharq Al-Awsat: https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5110023-netanyahu-denies-contacts-syria-have-led-final-agreement and the summary of Maariv-reported remarks: https://www.almanar.com.lb/13364435

Because the ultimate market requires an officially announced and mutually agreed security deal by 2026-01-31, one meaningful earlier crux is whether the U.S. publicly moves from quiet mediation to acknowledged sponsorship of an official meeting specifically about border security, demarcation, deconfliction, normalization, or a security framework. Such a step would not itself be the final agreement, but it would be a concrete observable sign that the process is active, serious, and near enough to public rollout to matter.

Sources:
Reuters / Times of Israel - Syria's Sharaa says indirect talks under way with Israel to calm tensions: https://www.timesofisrael.com/syrias-sharaa-says-indirect-talks-under-way-with-israel-to-calm-tensions/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11 inclusive, the U.S. government publicly states that it is hosting, convening, sponsoring, or facilitating an official meeting involving representatives of both Israel and Syria, and the announced meeting is explicitly about border security, a security arrangement, deconfliction, demarcation, normalization, diplomatic recognition, or a formalized bilateral security framework.

For avoidance of doubt, all of the following must be true for a Yes resolution:
1. The announcement must occur between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11 inclusive.
2. The announcement must come from an official U.S. government source, such as the White House, U.S. Department of State, U.S. embassy, or a named senior U.S. official speaking on the record in an official briefing or transcript.
3. The announced meeting must involve both Israel and Syria at the governmental level (for example, ministers, official delegations, senior national security officials, or government-appointed negotiators).
4. The subject matter must be explicitly tied to the bilateral security relationship, border arrangements, demarcation, non-aggression, normalization, diplomatic recognition, or a formal security framework. General statements about regional peace, reconstruction, sanctions, or ceasefire maintenance without a bilateral Israel-Syria meeting do not count.

This question resolves No if no such official U.S. announcement is made during the window.

A meeting that is merely rumored by media, leaked by unnamed officials, or announced only by non-U.S. parties does not count. A statement that the U.S. is encouraging dialogue, or that talks exist, does not count unless it specifically announces a hosted/sponsored official meeting. If the U.S. announces a meeting but it is later clarified that one side was not participating in an official capacity, the question resolves No. If an announced meeting is postponed beyond 2026-01-11, this question resolves No because the qualifying announcement must describe a hosted/sponsored official meeting during the stated window and not merely a future intention detached from a concrete convening.

Primary resolution sources: official White House statements and briefings (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), U.S. Department of State press statements and briefings (https://www.state.gov/press/), and official statements by the U.S. Embassy in Israel (https://il.usembassy.gov/) or U.S. Embassy in Syria / Syria-related State Department pages if applicable. Secondary confirmation, if needed, may come from Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/) if the official statement is difficult to locate but clearly references an official U.S. announcement.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on an official bilateral agreement being publicly announced by late January. A publicly acknowledged U.S.-hosted or U.S.-sponsored official meeting would be a strong process indicator that negotiations have crossed from tentative backchannel contacts into a formal stage where an agreement soon after becomes substantially more likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes resolution: (1) Between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11, (2) a U.S. government official source must publicly state that the U.S. is hosting/convening/sponsoring/facilitating (3) an official meeting involving both Israel and Syria at governmental level, (4) explicitly about border security, security arrangement, deconfliction, demarcation, normalization, or a formal security framework. Key entities: U.S. State Department, White House, named senior U.S. officials; Israeli governmental officials; Syrian governmental officials.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: 'United States hosting Israel Syria meeting border security arrangement' (2025-12-12 to 2026-01-11); 'US State Department Israel Syria security talks official meeting' (2025-12-12 to 2026-01-11); 'US State Department press statement joint statement Israel Syria Paris January 6 2026' (2026-01-05 to 2026-01-08); 'Tom Barrack State Department Israel Syria security agreement announcement January 6 2026' (2026-01-04 to 2026-01-11); 'US announcement Israel Syria meeting December 2025 border security' (2025-12-12 to 2025-12-31).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) December 15-17, 2025: Tom Barrack met Netanyahu to discuss Israel-Syria talks — but this was a U.S.-Israel bilateral meeting, not a trilateral announcement of a hosted Israel-Syria meeting. (2) January 5-6, 2026: U.S.-mediated talks between Israel and Syria in Paris — U.S. State Department released a joint statement confirming the meeting, its participants (Israeli and Syrian governmental officials), and that the talks covered border security, deconfliction, and a formal security mechanism. U.S. envoys Tom Barrack, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner were present. The U.S. State Department released an official joint statement.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The January 5-6, 2026 Paris talks meet all criteria: (1) Within window — January 5-6 is within December 12, 2025 - January 11, 2026. (2) Official U.S. source — U.S. State Department released a joint statement per [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/syria-israel-agree-to-set-up-joint-coordination-mechanism-during-us-backed-paris-talks/3791672), [France 24](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260106-israel-syria-intelligence-military-de-escalation-paris), [Washington Times](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/jan/6/syria-israel-agree-intelligence-sharing-continued-diplomatic-talks-us/), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/6/israel-syria-agree-to-dedicated-communication-line-in-us-brokered-talks), [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/israel-syria-to-set-up-communication-mechanism-after-us-mediated-talks). (3) Both Israel and Syria at governmental level — Israeli delegation: Ambassador Yechiel Leiter, Military Secretary Gen. Roman Gofman, Acting NSA Gil Reich; Syrian delegation: Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani, Intelligence Chief Hussein al-Salama. (4) Subject matter explicitly tied to bilateral security relationship — the meeting explicitly covered border security, security arrangements, military de-escalation, intelligence sharing, deconfliction, and laying groundwork for normalization. The U.S. facilitated the meeting through Tom Barrack, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner. The State Department joint statement explicitly described the U.S. as facilitating the meeting and welcoming the establishment of the joint fusion mechanism for Israel-Syria security cooperation. The resolution criteria include 'facilitating' as a qualifying verb.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The U.S. State Department joint statement was released on January 6, 2026. The talks began on January 5, 2026. Multiple high-quality sources published on January 6, 2026 confirm the State Department statement was released on that date. Exact time within the day is not available from news articles, but the date of January 6, 2026 is reliably established.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event found. While there were prior rounds of talks before December 12, 2025 (September 2025, etc.), and U.S. envoy Barrack met Netanyahu on December 15-17, 2025, neither constituted a U.S. announcement of a hosted/facilitated official Israel-Syria meeting during the window. The January 5-6 Paris talks are the first qualifying event within the specified window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent high-quality sources (Anadolu Agency, France 24, Washington Times, Al Jazeera, Straits Times, Fox News, AFP, Times of Israel) consistently report the U.S. State Department released a joint statement on January 6, 2026 about U.S.-facilitated Israel-Syria talks in Paris. The meeting was explicitly about security arrangements, border security, and a formal coordination mechanism. U.S. senior officials were physically present at the meeting. Tom Barrack is explicitly named as U.S. Special Envoy for Syria, a named senior U.S. official. The Washington Times specifically states 'announced in a joint statement by Syria, Israel, and the United States on January 6, 2026.' No contradictory evidence found suggesting the meeting did not occur or that one party participated in a non-official capacity. Both Israel (through Netanyahu's office statement) and Syria (through SANA and FM Shaibani's participation) confirmed official participation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria are met: (1) The announcement occurred on January 6, 2026 — within the window. (2) The announcement came from the U.S. State Department (official U.S. government source) via a joint statement. (3) The meeting involved both Israel and Syria at the governmental level (Foreign Minister, intelligence chief, ambassador, military secretary, NSA). (4) The subject matter was explicitly about border security, security arrangements, deconfliction, military de-escalation, intelligence sharing, and a formalized bilateral security framework (the 'joint fusion mechanism'). The U.S. was facilitating (not hosting in U.S. territory) the meeting through its envoys. The resolution criteria explicitly includes 'facilitating' as a qualifying action. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will Trump veto a bill in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump issues a presidential veto of any bill by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source will be official congressional records and a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will either chamber of Congress pass a continuing resolution or full-year appropriations measure to reopen or fund the federal government between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late October 2025, the U.S. federal government is in a prolonged shutdown and Congress remains deadlocked over funding. ABC13 reported on 2025-10-27 that the shutdown had entered its fifth week (day 27), the Senate had reconvened, the House remained out of session, and lawmakers were still split on how to proceed. President Trump publicly blamed Democrats and said Republicans were prepared to support a clean continuing resolution, while the Senate had just failed to advance a related bill, underscoring the difficulty of moving any funding legislation forward. https://abc13.com/post/senate-reconvene-monday-amid-funding-stalemate-government-shutdown-drags/17414842/

Earlier reporting indicated that Congress had failed to complete the 12 regular appropriations bills before the fiscal-year deadline and that a stopgap measure would likely be required. Georgia Recorder reported on 2025-09-03 that only a small subset of appropriations bills had advanced and that bipartisan agreement looked unusually difficult this year. https://georgiarecorder.com/2025/09/03/every-fall-theres-a-government-shutdown-warning-this-time-it-could-happen/

JD Supra reported on 2025-09-30 that a clean continuing resolution through 2025-11-21 had passed the House on 2025-09-19 but failed in the Senate, showing that funding bills can move in one chamber without becoming law. That makes chamber passage a useful near-term indicator of whether conditions are developing that could culminate in Trump facing a bill to sign or veto by year-end. https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/healthcare-preview-for-the-week-of-2977321/

This is relevant to the ultimate veto question because Trump cannot veto a bill unless Congress first passes one. In the current shutdown context, the most plausible route to a 2025 veto is likely a funding or appropriations fight that produces a bill on his desk. Passage in either chamber by late November would be a concrete signal that legislative negotiations are moving from stalemate toward enrolled legislation.

Sources:
ABC13 News, Senate to reconvene on Monday amid funding stalemate as government shutdown drags on: https://abc13.com/post/senate-reconvene-monday-amid-funding-stalemate-government-shutdown-drags/17414842/
Georgia Recorder, Every fall there’s a government shutdown warning. This time it could happen.: https://georgiarecorder.com/2025/09/03/every-fall-theres-a-government-shutdown-warning-this-time-it-could-happen/
JD Supra, Healthcare Preview for the Week of: September 29, 2025: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/healthcare-preview-for-the-week-of-2977321/
Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/
U.S. House Clerk: https://clerk.house.gov/
U.S. Senate roll call votes: https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/vote_menu_119_1.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), either the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate passes at least one bill or joint resolution whose primary purpose is to provide federal discretionary funding for FY2026 or to temporarily continue such funding (including a continuing resolution, omnibus/minibus appropriations package, or individual regular appropriations bill explicitly funding a federal department, agency, or set of agencies).

This question resolves No if no such chamber passage occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive).

For avoidance of doubt:
- Passage by only one chamber is sufficient for Yes.
- The measure need not become law.
- Procedural votes, cloture votes, motions to proceed, committee approvals, draft releases, or leadership announcements do not count unless a chamber formally passes the measure.
- A bill focused only on paying selected workers during a shutdown, debt ceiling changes, rescissions, or other non-appropriations matters does not count unless it also clearly provides appropriations or a continuing extension of government funding.
- If a chamber vote begins before 2025-10-31 or after 2025-11-30, it does not count, even if announced within the window.

Primary resolution sources:
- Congress.gov bill actions and vote records: https://www.congress.gov/
- U.S. House Clerk roll call and legislative activity: https://clerk.house.gov/
- U.S. Senate roll call votes and legislative activity: https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_lists/vote_menu_119_1.htm

Fallback: if Congress.gov is delayed or unavailable, use the official House Clerk and Senate websites above, plus the Congressional Record at https://www.congress.gov/congressional-record, to verify whether chamber passage occurred within the 2025-10-31 to 2025-11-30 window. If official sources do not provide enough information to determine passage timing, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A presidential veto requires Congress to first advance legislation. In the present shutdown-driven bargaining environment, movement on funding legislation is one of the strongest observable precursors to Trump receiving a bill before year-end. Chamber passage by late November would materially increase the odds that a bill reaches his desk in December, while continued total legislative paralysis would lower them.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Either U.S. House or U.S. Senate formally passes a bill/joint resolution whose primary purpose is to provide or continue FY2026 federal discretionary funding, between 2025-10-31T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-30T23:59:59Z. Key entities: Congress, H.R. 5371. Observable evidence: official chamber vote records showing passage within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Congress continuing resolution appropriations bill passed November 2025' (general search for chamber passage). Query 2: 'House Senate vote government funding FY2026 November 2025' (targeted to both chambers). Query 3: 'Senate passes HR 5371 exact date November 10 11 2025 government funding bill' (verifying Senate passage date). Query 4: 'House passes HR 5371 November 12 13 2025 vote 222-209 government shutdown ends' (verifying House passage date and vote count).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: Senate passage of H.R. 5371 (Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026) — multiple sources confirm 60-40 vote on November 10 or 11, 2025. Candidate event 2: House passage of Senate-amended H.R. 5371 — all sources consistently confirm 222-209 vote on November 13, 2025. No events rejected — all directly satisfy criteria. Some sources cite Nov 10 for initial Senate cloture vote and Nov 11 for final passage; AP and MSNBC confirm Nov 11 as final Senate passage date.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: H.R. 5371 is explicitly titled 'Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026.' Its primary purpose is to (a) extend continuing FY2026 appropriations for most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, and (b) provide full-year FY2026 appropriations for Agriculture/FDA, Military Construction/VA, and Legislative Branch. This directly and explicitly satisfies the resolution criteria requiring 'a bill or joint resolution whose primary purpose is to provide federal discretionary funding for FY2026 or to temporarily continue such funding.' Sources: [AP](https://apnews.com/ad4a87689155bd4ef460d5542dbeec37), [MSNBC](https://www.msnbc.com/msnbc/news/senate-passes-funding-bill-shutdown-end-rcna243135), [TIME](https://time.com/7333543/government-shutdown-over/), [JD Supra](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/cr-signed-sealed-and-delivered-7495298/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Senate final passage: November 11, 2025 (confirmed by AP, MSNBC, exbulletin citing '10-hour session beginning at 11:00 a.m. EST on November 10' concluding with final vote, and multiple others). House passage: November 13, 2025 (confirmed by all sources, 222-209 vote). First qualifying event: Senate passage on 2025-11-11.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying chamber passage exists within the window (October 31 – November 30, 2025). The Senate passage on November 11, 2025 is the first qualifying event. Prior to October 31, the House had passed a short-term CR on September 19, 2025, which was blocked by the Senate 14+ times — that House vote was before the window and the Senate never passed it, so it does not qualify.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: none found. All major news sources (AP, CBS, MSNBC, TIME, Anadolu Agency, JD Supra, Daily Caller, ABC, MoneyControl) consistently report Senate passage on November 10–11 and House passage on November 13, 2025. President Trump's signing of the bill on November 12–13 confirms both chambers passed it. No source disputes the dates or the nature of the bill as an appropriations/CR measure. The bill's FY2026 appropriations purpose is unambiguous per its title and content.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Senate passed H.R. 5371 — a continuing resolution and three full-year FY2026 appropriations bills — on November 11, 2025 (60-40 vote), within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window. The House subsequently passed the same bill on November 13, 2025 (222-209 vote), also within the window. The first qualifying chamber passage occurred on November 11, 2025 (Senate). The question resolves Yes, with resolution_datetime set to the first qualifying passage: 2025-11-11T00:00:00Z (exact time of vote not available but date is confirmed).

question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the October 2025 Employment Situation report show the U.S. unemployment rate at 4.4% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
The Fed’s Oct–Dec–Jan path is highly sensitive to incoming labor-market data because the September 17, 2025 FOMC statement said that job gains had slowed, unemployment had edged up, and downside risks to employment had risen. That makes a near-term unemployment print a useful crux for whether the Fed cuts in October and then pauses thereafter versus taking a different path. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported the unemployment rate at 4.3% for August 2025 in the latest referenced coverage, while the September 2025 FOMC projections reportedly put the median 2025 unemployment rate around 4.5%, suggesting that a move to 4.4%+ in the next report would be consistent with further labor-market softening and likely increase pressure for another cut soon. See BLS Employment Situation releases at https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm and the Federal Reserve’s September 2025 materials at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm . Contemporary reporting also noted that after the September 2025 cut, markets were pricing high odds of another October cut, with labor-market weakness a key justification: CNBC coverage summarized the FOMC statement and projections at https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/17/fed-rate-decision-september-2025-.html .

Sources:
BLS Employment Situation news releases — https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm
Federal Reserve FOMC calendars, statements, SEP materials — https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
CNBC, Fed approves quarter-point interest rate cut and sees two more coming this year — https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/17/fed-rate-decision-september-2025-.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
