It resolves No if that release reports the unemployment rate below 4.4%.

Primary source: the Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation release at https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm . The unemployment rate should be taken from the headline national unemployment-rate figure in that release (Table A or equivalent summary text).

If BLS republishes or revises the figure later, the initially released value in the first Employment Situation report published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 will govern. If no BLS Employment Situation release is published during that window, this question should be considered unresolvable. If the BLS release format changes, the resolver should use the official BLS national U-3 unemployment rate stated in the release or linked release tables for that publication date.
subquestions.rationale: A higher unemployment reading by late October would be a strong near-term signal that labor-market deterioration is continuing, which would increase the odds of an October cut and shape expectations for whether the Fed then pauses or continues easing. It is a different observable event from the ultimate question itself and directly informs the macro conditions driving the policy sequence.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A BLS Employment Situation release published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 showing the U-3 unemployment rate at 4.4% or higher. The resolution criteria explicitly states: 'If no BLS Employment Situation release is published during that window, this question should be considered unresolvable.' Key entities: BLS Employment Situation report (September 2025 reference month), headline U-3 rate, 4.4% threshold, October 1-31, 2025 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'BLS Employment Situation report October 2025 unemployment rate' — to find the actual release; 2) 'Bureau of Labor Statistics jobs report unemployment October 2025' — alternative phrasing; 3) 'government shutdown end BLS jobs report released October 2025' — to check if shutdown ended and report was released; 4) 'September 2025 unemployment rate BLS report released' — to find if report was eventually released; 5) 'government shutdown ended October 2025 Congress spending bill' — to find if shutdown ended; 6) 'BLS jobs report released September unemployment rate after shutdown' — to find post-shutdown release; 7) 'government shutdown ended deal reached October 30 31 2025' — to find last-minute resolution; 8) 'BLS Employment Situation report October 31 2025 unemployment release' — final window search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) BLS was scheduled to release September Employment Situation on October 3, 2025 (first Friday of October) — REJECTED: shutdown prevented release. (B) BLS CPI data was partially released during shutdown for Social Security COLA purposes — REJECTED: This is CPI not Employment Situation. (C) Chicago Fed estimates of unemployment (4.34-4.35%) released Oct 27 — REJECTED: Not an official BLS Employment Situation release. (D) ADP private payroll data — REJECTED: Not BLS Employment Situation. No qualifying BLS Employment Situation release was found in the October 1-31, 2025 window. Multiple sources from October 28-30 confirm shutdown was still ongoing on day 29-30, BLS had not released employment data, Senate had rejected funding bills 13 times.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires 'the first BLS Employment Situation release published within that window.' Multiple explicit sources confirm no such release occurred: [CNBC Oct 3](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/03/shutdown-jobs-report-economy.html) reports BLS did not release jobs report due to shutdown; [altoonamirror.com Oct 21](https://www.altoonamirror.com/news/local-news/2025/10/govt-shutdown-pa-jobless-data-limbo/) confirms BLS website had not been updated since October 1; [bakercityherald.com Oct 30](https://bakercityherald.com/2025/10/23/missing-federal-jobs-report-leaves-oregon-employment-department-businesses-in-the-dark/) confirms BLS failed to release September 2025 jobs report; [FOX21 Oct 29](https://www.fox21news.com/top-stories/federal-reserve-cuts-rates-for-second-time-as-shutdown-stalls-key-data/) confirms BLS had not released employment data as of October 29; [politomix.com Oct 30](https://politomix.com/npr/2302003/federal-government-still-shut-down-means-across/) confirms government still shut down as of October 30, no resolution; [MSNBC Oct 30](https://www.msnbc.com/msnbc/news/senators-leave-town-shutdown-pain-rcna240949) confirms Senate adjourned for the week October 30 without resolution, shutdown on track to become longest in U.S. history. evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No BLS Employment Situation release timestamp exists within the October 1-31, 2025 window. The shutdown began October 1, 2025, and was still ongoing as of October 30-31, 2025 (day 30). The Senate adjourned without resolution on October 30, 2025. evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checked across multiple independent sources: CNBC, The Hill, RISMedia, Washington Examiner, altoonamirror.com, bakercityherald.com, FOX21 News, MSNBC, CBS News, Newser, kscj.com all confirm the shutdown was ongoing throughout October 2025 and the BLS Employment Situation report was not released. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question is UNRESOLVABLE. The resolution criteria explicitly states: 'If no BLS Employment Situation release is published during that window, this question should be considered unresolvable.' The evidence conclusively shows that no BLS Employment Situation report was published between October 1-31, 2025, due to a federal government shutdown that began October 1 and remained ongoing through at least October 30-31, 2025 (its 30th day). The government did not reopen and the BLS did not release employment data during this window. The next scheduled BLS release date was November 7, 2025 (outside the window), and even that was uncertain due to the ongoing shutdown. Therefore: resolvable=false.

question: Will TikTok be banned in 2025?
description:
On April 4, 2025, President Trump signed an executive order extending the delay of enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, which prohibits TikTok in the United States, until September 17, 2025 (see: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/06/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay/)

This market will resolve to "Yes" if a U.S. government ban that prohibits access or use of the TikTok app by the majority of Americans in the United States becomes legally enforceable for any amount of time between July 24, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

If Trump’s executive order delaying enforcement of the ban expires or is removed without TikTok coming into compliance with U.S. laws and regulations, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether enforcement action is taken by the U.S. government.

If TikTok is sold to another entity in such a way that it comes into compliance with U.S. laws and regulations this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will President Trump issue a new executive order or presidential memorandum between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that explicitly extends, pauses, or otherwise delays enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act against TikTok beyond September 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question turns on whether a legally enforceable U.S. ban on TikTok takes effect at any time in late 2025. A key near-term indicator is whether the administration chooses to delay enforcement again rather than allow the existing deadline to bite. The White House states that President Trump signed a presidential action further extending the TikTok enforcement delay, with the current delay running to September 17, 2025, under the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act framework. See the White House presidential action: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/06/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay/

Reporting before 2025-09-01 indicates Trump publicly said he was open to a fourth extension and that "very substantial American buyers" were being lined up, but that Chinese approval might not arrive in time. Reuters reported these remarks on August 22, 2025: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-says-he-would-probably-extend-tiktok-deadline-again-if-no-deal-reached-2025-08-22/ . This makes a further extension a live and highly relevant crux: if another delay is issued, that is strong evidence against an actual enforceable ban materializing in 2025; if no further delay is issued, the probability of the ultimate market resolving Yes rises materially.

This is not a restatement of the ultimate question because it asks about a distinct observable policy action by the President, not whether a ban becomes legally enforceable. It is grounded in current events: there have already been multiple delays, and the next key date is September 17, 2025. The White House also launched an official TikTok account in August 2025, underscoring the administration's mixed posture toward the app and making another delay more politically plausible. Example coverage: Anadolu Ajansı, August 20, 2025, https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/white-house-joins-tiktok-as-president-trumps-deadline-for-potential-ban-gets-closer/3663839

White House - Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay - https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/06/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay/
Reuters - Trump says he would probably extend TikTok deadline again if no deal reached - https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-says-he-would-probably-extend-tiktok-deadline-again-if-no-deal-reached-2025-08-22/
Anadolu Ajansı - White House joins TikTok as President Trump's deadline for potential ban gets closer - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/white-house-joins-tiktok-as-president-trumps-deadline-for-potential-ban-gets-closer/3663839
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the White House publishes an executive order, presidential memorandum, or other formal presidential action that explicitly states that enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (or enforcement against TikTok under that law) is extended, delayed, paused, stayed, or otherwise deferred beyond September 17, 2025.

This question resolves No if no such formal presidential action is published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

For a Yes resolution, the action must be an official presidential action published by the White House or Federal Register and must explicitly concern delaying or extending enforcement timing. Mere public statements, press briefings, social media posts, or anonymous-source reporting that an extension is planned do not count unless followed by an official published action within the window.

Primary sources for resolution:
- White House presidential actions page: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/
- Federal Register presidential documents: https://www.federalregister.gov/presidential-documents/executive-orders

Fallback sources, if publication timing is unclear or pages are unavailable:
- White House briefing room/search pages: https://www.whitehouse.gov/
- Federal Register main site search: https://www.federalregister.gov/
- Consensus of credible reporting from Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/ and AP News: https://apnews.com/

If an order is signed within the window but first published only after 2025-10-01, the question should resolve based on the official signing date stated in the document. If no official document with a clear signing date is available, use the first public release date from the White House or Federal Register. If the administration takes some novel legal step functionally equivalent to a delay but not labeled an executive order or memorandum, it counts only if an official federal government document clearly states that enforcement is being delayed beyond September 17, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: A further presidential delay is one of the strongest short-term indicators against TikTok being banned in 2025. It directly measures the administration's willingness to keep non-enforcement in place, which would make the ultimate Yes outcome less likely even before any final sale or compliance decision.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the White House must publish a formal executive order, presidential memorandum, or other formal presidential action explicitly stating that enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (or TikTok enforcement under that law) is extended, delayed, paused, stayed, or otherwise deferred beyond September 17, 2025. Observable evidence: Official White House or Federal Register publication of such a document within the window. Key entities: President Trump, TikTok/ByteDance, the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act. Threshold: The action must be formal and explicit (not merely a statement or social media post). Timing: Must be published September 1–October 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump executive order TikTok enforcement delay extension September 2025' — to find if an EO was issued in the window. Query 2: 'TikTok ban deadline September 17 2025 extension' — to find if the Sept 17 deadline was extended. Query 3: 'Trump executive order Further Extending TikTok September 16 2025 White House signed' — to verify signing date. Query 4: 'whitehouse.gov further extending tiktok enforcement delay presidential action September 16 2025' — to confirm official White House publication.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event identified: An executive order titled 'Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay' was published on the White House presidential actions page (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/09/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay-9dde/) on September 16, 2025. This order explicitly extends the enforcement delay for the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act as applied to TikTok until December 16, 2025. Multiple independent sources corroborate this event: White House, StreetInsider, Social Media Today, Boston Globe, CNET, Mondaq, AV Club, and others all report the same executive order signed on September 16, 2025. No events were rejected.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The executive order 'Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay' [White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/09/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay-9dde/) explicitly: (1) Is a formal executive order, (2) Published on the White House presidential actions page, (3) Explicitly extends enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (PAFCA) as applied to TikTok, (4) Extends the deadline to December 16, 2025 — clearly beyond September 17, 2025, (5) States 'The enforcement delay specified in section 2(a) of Executive Order 14166 of January 20, 2025 ... is further extended until December 16, 2025.' [Social Media Today](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/trump-signs-fourth-executive-order-to-keep-tiktok-in-US/760325/). All criteria are explicitly and exactly satisfied.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The White House published the presidential action on September 16, 2025, as evidenced by the URL path '/2025/09/' and the publication date of September 16, 2025 reported by the White House source and multiple media outlets. Multiple sources published on September 16, 2025 report the order was signed and issued that day. Some sources date the event as September 16, others as September 17 (possibly due to time zone differences), but the White House source itself shows a publication date of September 16, 2025. This date is within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No sources contradict the existence of this executive order. No sources claim the order was NOT issued within the window. Multiple completely independent sources (White House directly, AP-cited outlets, Reuters-cited outlets, major newspapers like Boston Globe) all confirm the same event with the same details. The order text is directly quoted ('The enforcement delay specified in section 2(a) of Executive Order 14166 of January 20, 2025 ... is further extended until December 16, 2025') in multiple reports. The White House URL itself confirms the document's existence and publication. No alternative interpretations are plausible.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves YES. President Trump signed an executive order titled 'Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay' on September 16, 2025, which was published on the White House presidential actions page (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/09/further-extending-the-tiktok-enforcement-delay-9dde/). This executive order explicitly extended enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act as applied to TikTok until December 16, 2025 — beyond the September 17, 2025 deadline. This event occurred within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window, satisfies all resolution criteria exactly, and is confirmed by the White House publication itself and numerous independent credible sources.

subquestions.question: Will the University of Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment preliminary October 2025 reading be below 55.0?
subquestions.background_information:
Trump’s late-2025 approval is plausibly sensitive to near-term consumer sentiment, because voters often reward or punish presidents based on perceived economic conditions. Recent reporting indicates Trump is significantly underwater on economic issues: a September 2025 report cited polling showing 53% disapproval on his handling of the economy and only 30% approval on cost of living, while Silver Bulletin put his overall approval around 44.1% and disapproval around 51.7% as of September 10, 2025. https://wmt.radio/news/030030-donald-trump-approval-rating-sees-change-on-crucial-issue/ ; https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin

Consumer sentiment has already shown weakness during tariff-related market stress earlier in 2025. In April, the University of Michigan preliminary consumer sentiment index fell to 50.8, described as its lowest level since the COVID-19 pandemic. https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-nate-silver-tariffs-2058569 ; https://www.sca.isr.umich.edu/

A reading below 55.0 in the preliminary October release would indicate continued depressed consumer sentiment close to recessionary-pessimism territory, which would be evidence against a material rebound in Trump’s approval by December 31. Conversely, a rebound above that threshold would modestly support the case that approval could finish above its current ~44% level. The threshold is informative because sentiment was 50.8 in April and has been a closely watched macro-political indicator, so 55.0 is neither trivial nor extreme given 2025 conditions. https://www.sca.isr.umich.edu/ ; https://www.theconversation.com/polling-shows-donald-trumps-ratings-are-poor-but-they-could-be-worse-263951

subquestions.background_information:
Maria Margarita Rojas was announced by Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in March 2025 as having been arrested for allegedly providing illegal abortions and operating clinics unlawfully in the Houston area. The attorney general's office described the case as a test of Texas's post-Roe criminal abortion enforcement and said Rojas was charged with performing illegal abortions and practicing medicine without a license. See the AG press release: https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/news/releases/attorney-general-ken-paxton-announces-arrest-houston-area-abortionist-and-crackdown-clinics

By October 2025, multiple major outlets reported that Rojas faced 15 felony counts, including 3 counts tied to allegedly performing illegal abortions and 12 counts for unlicensed medical practice, and that she had pleaded not guilty. CNN reported that eight additional people linked to the clinics had also been arrested or indicted, indicating the state was expanding rather than abandoning the prosecution: https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/08/us/texas-illegal-abortion-clinics-arrests/index.html . ABC17's writeup similarly said Rojas was the first person charged under Texas's Human Life Protection Act and that the clinics had been barred from operating during the case: https://abc17news.com/news/national-world/cnn-national/2025/10/08/eight-people-charged-in-connection-with-clinics-providing-abortions-illegally-texas-attorney-general-says/

A near-term legal indicator for eventual guilt is whether the trial court rejects a defense attempt to knock out the abortion-related counts before trial. If a motion to dismiss, quash, or otherwise invalidate those counts is denied, that suggests the prosecution has survived an important procedural challenge and that the case remains on track toward adjudication. Conversely, if all abortion-related counts are dismissed or quashed, that would strongly cut against the ultimate market resolving Yes.

Texas criminal case events are commonly reflected in county court dockets and filings. Because reporting indicates the case is in Waller County, public docket updates from Waller County district court or the Waller County District Clerk are likely to be the most authoritative source, with credible legal reporting as backup.

subquestions.question: Will Statistics Canada report that Canada's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate was at least 7.2% in the Labour Force Survey release published between 2025-12-24 and 2026-01-23?
subquestions.background_information:
The Bank of Canada's March 2026 rate decision will depend heavily on whether economic slack is growing enough to justify renewed easing. Labour-market deterioration is one of the clearest near-term indicators for that. Recent reporting indicates the BoC cut its policy rate to 2.25% on 2025-10-29, then held at 2.25% on 2025-12-10 while saying the current rate was 'about the right level' but that the next move could be either a hike or a cut depending on incoming data and trade developments. Reuters/press coverage of 2025 data described the labour market as soft, with unemployment having risen to around 7.1% in late 2025 and job losses concentrated in trade-sensitive sectors. See CBC on the September 2025 decision and labour-market weakness: https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/bank-of-canada-interest-rate-sept-17-1.7331965 ; and Bank of Canada materials for the December 2025 hold and meeting schedule: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/core-functions/monetary-policy/key-interest-rate/

Statistics Canada is the authoritative source for Canada's Labour Force Survey and unemployment rate. A January 2026 Labour Force Survey release falling within this window would give forecasters fresh evidence on whether labour-market slack is worsening enough to make a March cut more likely. A reading at or above 7.2% would suggest further softening relative to the roughly 7.1% level reported in late 2025, which would generally lean dovish for the BoC. Labour Force Survey releases are published by Statistics Canada in The Daily and in labour-force tables: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/index-eng.htm and https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/subjects-start/labour_

Statistics Canada labour topic page — https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/subjects-start/labour_
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Preferred data source within the release is the national seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for Canada. If The Daily article links to accompanying tables, those official Statistics Canada tables may be used to confirm the figure. An alternative official Statistics Canada labour-force page may also be used if the Daily page format changes: https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/subjects-start/labour_

If Statistics Canada publishes more than one Labour Force Survey release during the window, the question resolves Yes if any such release in the window reports 7.2% or higher. If no Labour Force Survey release is published by Statistics Canada between 2025-12-24 and 2026-01-23, this question resolves No. Revisions published after 2026-01-23 do not count unless they were already publicly released within the window. Non-Statistics Canada sources are not sufficient except to locate the official Statistics Canada release.
subquestions.rationale: A weaker labour market is a direct input into BoC easing decisions. If unemployment rises further by January, forecasters should update toward a higher chance of a March 2026 25 bps cut; if unemployment stays lower, that supports the view that the BoC remains on hold at 2.25%.

question: U.S. fertility rate up in Q2 2025?
description:
The CDC reported a general fertility rate of 54.5 births per 1,000 women aged 15–44 for Q1 2025 (see: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm). 

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the initial reported rate for Q2 2025 exceeds 54.5, according to the CDC's Vital Statistics Rapid Release series. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

If the CDC does not release general fertility rate data for Q2 2025 by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Resolution will be based on the first published estimate for Q2 2025, regardless of any subsequent revisions.

The resolution source will be the CDC’s Vital Statistics Rapid Release.

subquestions.question: Will the CDC Vital Statistics Rapid Release natality dashboard display an initial Q2 2025 U.S. general fertility rate above 54.5 births per 1,000 women aged 15–44 by 2025-09-16?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a near-term process indicator for the ultimate market because the ultimate question resolves from the CDC's first-published Q2 2025 general fertility rate (GFR). As of the information provided in the ultimate question, the CDC reported a GFR of 54.5 for Q1 2025 on its Vital Statistics Rapid Release natality dashboard. The same dashboard is the stated resolution source for the ultimate market, so whether the CDC posts a Q2 2025 reading by mid-September is highly relevant to whether the ultimate question can resolve Yes before its deadline. See the CDC natality dashboard: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm

The CDC's quarterly natality dashboard presents recent provisional fertility and birth data, including the general fertility rate for women ages 15–44. Because the ultimate question depends on the first published Q2 2025 estimate, an early-release question about whether that estimate appears and exceeds 54.5 before 2025-09-16 is informative: if Yes, the ultimate market is very likely to resolve Yes; if No because no estimate appears by then, that increases the chance the ultimate market resolves No due either to a lower/equal estimate or to non-release by its deadline. The dashboard and related Vital Statistics Rapid Release pages are here: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr.htm and https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm

Recent CDC annual data also show the broader backdrop is one of low fertility. The CDC reported a 2024 general fertility rate of 53.8 births per 1,000 women aged 15–44, an all-time low, which indicates that a Q2 2025 reading above 54.5 would represent a meaningful short-term uptick relative to the recent annual level. See NCHS/CDC reporting summarized in the July 2025 release: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db537.htm

Sources:
CDC Vital Statistics Rapid Release Natality Dashboard — https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm
CDC Vital Statistics Rapid Release program page — https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr.htm
CDC/NCHS Data Brief on 2024 births and fertility — https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db537.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-16 inclusive, the CDC Vital Statistics Rapid Release natality dashboard first displays a Q2 2025 U.S. general fertility rate (defined by CDC as births per 1,000 women aged 15–44) that is strictly greater than 54.5. It resolves No if, by 2025-09-16 23:59:59 UTC, either (a) the dashboard displays an initial Q2 2025 GFR of 54.5 or lower, or (b) no Q2 2025 GFR has been published on the dashboard.

Primary resolution source: CDC Vital Statistics Rapid Release natality dashboard, https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm

If the dashboard is temporarily unavailable, resolvers should use an archived CDC page capture from the same URL or a CDC/NCHS page announcing the quarterly natality estimate under the Vital Statistics Rapid Release program: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr.htm

For avoidance of doubt, the relevant value is the first published Q2 2025 estimate appearing on the CDC source during the window 2025-09-01 through 2025-09-16 inclusive; later revisions do not affect resolution. If a qualifying Q2 2025 value is first posted after 2025-09-16, it does not count for this subquestion.
subquestions.rationale: This is not just the ultimate question with a shorter date; it asks about an earlier observable event: whether the CDC has posted a qualifying Q2 estimate by a specific near-term date. That event is a strong crux because the ultimate market can only resolve Yes if such an estimate is published and exceeds 54.5, and delayed publication by mid-September materially raises the chance of an ultimate No.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The CDC Vital Statistics Rapid Release (VSRR) natality dashboard at https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm must publish a Q2 2025 U.S. general fertility rate (GFR) value strictly greater than 54.5 births per 1,000 women aged 15–44, and this must happen for the first time during the window 2025-09-01 through 2025-09-16. No article or source reports Q2 2025 GFR from the CDC VSRR natality-dashboard.htm specifically. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The resolution criteria allow for No if either (a) the Q2 2025 GFR ≤ 54.5 OR (b) no Q2 2025 GFR was published on the VSRR natality dashboard by 2025-09-16. question: Will Eric Adams join Trump administration by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump officially nominates or appoints Eric Adams to his administration by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The Trump administration includes individuals formally appointed or nominated by Donald Trump to roles within the U.S. federal government, such as Cabinet members, Executive Office staff, senior policy advisors, ambassadors, or White House staff whose appointments are publicly announced by official government channels.

Nominations will qualify even if the individual is not confirmed.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Eric Adams publicly announce that he is ending or suspending his 2025 New York City mayoral campaign between 2025-09-06 and 2025-10-06?
subquestions.background_information:
A key obstacle to Eric Adams joining the Trump administration by the end of 2025 is that, as of early September 2025, Adams is still running for reelection as New York City mayor. Multiple reports say Trump advisers have discussed offering Adams a federal role, potentially including an ambassadorship, as part of an effort to reshape the NYC mayoral race. The New York Times-reported plan was summarized by CNBC on 2025-09-05, which said close advisers to President Trump were working on a plan to nominate Adams as U.S. ambassador to Saudi Arabia if he abandoned his long-shot reelection bid: https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/05/new-york-mayor-eric-adams-to-make-important-campaign-announcement-as-trump-nomination-floated.html

Other contemporaneous reporting said talks were underway over a possible Trump administration role for Adams, with unnamed sources describing active conversations between Trump advisers and Adams' team: https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3831113 and https://nypost.com/2025/09/03/us-news/eric-adams-white-house-in-talks-over-potential-trump-admin-job/

A further New York Post report on 2025-09-05 said Trump adviser Steve Witkoff had floated Adams for the Saudi ambassadorship and that Trump wanted Adams to drop out of the race soon: https://nypost.com/2025/09/05/us-news/top-trump-adviser-floats-eric-adams-for-saudi-arabia-ambassadorship/

Because these reports frame a federal appointment as contingent on Adams stepping aside from the mayoral race, a public campaign withdrawal or suspension would be a strong near-term indicator that negotiations are serious and that the probability of a later Trump appointment has risen materially. Conversely, if Adams stays in the race through early October, that would be evidence against an imminent federal landing spot.

Sources:

Qualifying announcements include, for example:

subquestions.rationale: Whether Adams exits the NYC mayoral race is a distinct observable event, not the same as joining the Trump administration. It is a plausible crux because current reporting suggests a federal appointment is being discussed partly as an inducement for Adams to step aside. A withdrawal or suspension would substantially increase the odds of a later Trump nomination or appointment by removing a major political constraint.

question: Apple AirTags 2 priced below $30 USD at release?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the standard edition of the AirTag 2 launches at $29.99 or less. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the pre-tax launch price in USD of the standard edition of the AirTag 2 as listed on the official Apple Store website or Apple’s retail pricing in the United States on the first official day of its release.

If the price differs between configurations, this market will resolve according to the lower price of the version that includes the full standard AirTag 2 model with no additional features, accessories, or services.

A qualifying product must be named "AirTag" and be recognized as a successor to the original AirTag product, similar to the relationship between iPhone 14 and iPhone 15. A new AirTag product released without a number, under a designation other than AirTag 2 will qualify if it retains the original functions of the AirTag and expands on them in such a way that it is clear that this product is a successor.

In order to be considered released, the product must be available for purchase by the general public within the specified timeframe. An announcement or unveiling alone is not sufficient.

If the AirTag 2 is not released by June 30, 2026, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official Apple Store (online or retail pricing), however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Apple continue listing the current single AirTag at $29.00 on the U.S. Apple Store at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether the successor AirTag launches below $30. A useful leading indicator is whether Apple preserves the original AirTag’s $29 U.S. list price through September 2025 rather than preemptively repricing or discontinuing it. If Apple keeps the incumbent product at $29 during the rumored AirTag 2 launch window, that is evidence Apple is comfortable with $29 as the key entry price point for the category and may be more likely to keep the successor at or below that level.

As of late August 2025, multiple reports describe the current AirTag’s official single-unit price as $29 and 4-pack price as $99 in the U.S. CNET states that the current AirTag “sells for $29 each or $99 for a four-pack” while discussing AirTag 2 rumors: https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/apple-airtag-2-rumors-new-features-and-possible-release-date-leaked/ . Apple’s own AirTag product page historically lists the single AirTag at $29 and 4-pack at $99 on the U.S. store: https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-airtag/airtag .

There are also signs of heavy third-party discounting ahead of the rumored successor launch. 9to5Toys reported Amazon selling single AirTags for $22.99 and a 4-pack for $69.99 on 2025-08-25, while noting the standard list price remained $29/$99: https://9to5toys.com/2025/08/25/apple-airtag-4-pack-70-single-23/ . Such discounting may indicate channel inventory clearance, but it does not by itself imply Apple will lower official launch MSRP for the successor.

Meanwhile, several outlets report that AirTag 2 may debut at Apple’s September 2025 event and is expected to retain a similar outward design while adding range/privacy improvements, which makes pricing continuity especially relevant. 9to5Mac says the new tag will “look similar to the current model”: https://9to5mac.com/2025/08/27/new-airtag-2-is-coming-very-soon-with-these-rumored-features/ . Mashable India and other outlets cite Mark Gurman’s reporting that the device is “nearly ready” for a September launch: https://in.mashable.com/tech/98929/apple-airtag-2-rumoured-for-september-launch-alongside-iphone-17-series .

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the official U.S. Apple online store lists the current-generation single AirTag for purchase at a pre-tax price of exactly $29.00 or $29.99 USD.

This question resolves No if, throughout the entire window from 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the official U.S. Apple online store never lists the current-generation single AirTag for purchase at a pre-tax price of $29.00 or $29.99 USD.

Primary source: the official U.S. Apple Store product page for AirTag, or successor archived snapshots of that page if the live page changes or is removed: https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-airtag/airtag .

Primary archival fallback: Internet Archive Wayback Machine snapshots of the Apple Store page captured during the resolution window: https://web.archive.org/ .

Additional fallback sources, only if the Apple Store page becomes unavailable and no archive snapshot exists for the relevant dates: credible contemporaneous reporting that explicitly states the official Apple U.S. list price and cites Apple pricing directly, such as MacRumors (https://www.macrumors.com/) or 9to5Mac (https://9to5mac.com/).

- Third-party retailer prices (e.g., Amazon, Best Buy) do not count.
- Promotional discounts, education pricing, carrier bundles, Apple Card offers, or trade-in offers do not count unless the base official Apple U.S. list price itself is $29.00 or $29.99.
- If Apple replaces the page with a new product page but still offers the original/current AirTag for purchase at the qualifying price during the window, that counts as Yes.
- If the product is unavailable for purchase but the Apple Store still clearly lists the official price on a product page during the window, that counts.
- If evidence is insufficient to determine whether the Apple Store listed the qualifying price at any point in the window, the market should resolve based on the best available archived evidence; if no reliable evidence exists at all, it should be considered unresolvable.

Continued $29 official pricing would modestly favor a below-$30 AirTag 2 launch; a move away from that price point would point the other way.

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a federal government funding lapse or shutdown remain in effect at any time on October 10, 2025, causing the Bureau of Labor Statistics to operate under shutdown contingency procedures?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term driver of whether BLS might stop regularly reporting payroll and other major releases in 2025 is whether a federal shutdown actually persists long enough to interrupt BLS operations. Multiple pre-October 1 reports say the Department of Labor's contingency plan states that if the government shuts down, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) will "suspend all operations," "all active data collection activities for BLS surveys will cease," and economic data scheduled during the lapse will not be released. This directly affects the scheduled Employment Situation report, CPI, PPI, and other releases. See reporting from UPI on Sept. 29, 2025: https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/09/29/government-shutdown-jobs-report-bls/ and Anadolu Ajansı on Sept. 29, 2025: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-wont-release-key-economic-data-if-government-shuts-down-report/3680064

Fortune also reported that a shutdown lasting more than a few days would halt BLS data collection and scheduled releases, including the monthly jobs report due in early October and potentially the Oct. 15 CPI if the lapse extends beyond the first week: https://fortune.com/2025/09/28/government-shutdown-jobs-report-fed-rate-cuts-bls-cpi/ . Reuters reporting carried by other outlets likewise described the Labor Department contingency plan as warning that key economic data releases would halt during a lapse in appropriations: https://www.yahoo.com/news/govt-shutdown-suspend-bls-delay-211500123.html

This is not the same as the ultimate question. A shutdown still would not by itself satisfy the ultimate market's "ceases regular publication" standard if releases are merely temporarily delayed and later resume. But whether a shutdown is still in effect by Oct. 10 is a meaningful crux because a persistent lapse makes missed releases, data-collection degradation, and later publication disruptions substantially more likely.

Sources:
UPI - BLS won't release jobs report Friday if the government shuts down - https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/09/29/government-shutdown-jobs-report-bls/
Anadolu Ajansı - US won't release key economic data if government shuts down: Report - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-wont-release-key-economic-data-if-government-shuts-down-report/3680064
Fortune - A government shutdown would delay the jobs report at a critical time - https://fortune.com/2025/09/28/government-shutdown-jobs-report-fed-rate-cuts-bls-cpi/
Yahoo Finance - Govt. shutdown would suspend BLS, delay key labor data - https://www.yahoo.com/news/govt-shutdown-suspend-bls-delay-211500123.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive), a federal government funding lapse/shutdown is in effect at any time on 2025-10-10 and BLS is operating under shutdown contingency procedures on that date.

For resolution, use the following hierarchy:
1. An official U.S. Office of Management and Budget (OMB), White House, or Department of Labor/BLS statement indicating that a lapse in appropriations or shutdown remains in effect on 2025-10-10, or that BLS remains subject to shutdown contingency operations. Relevant official sites include https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/ , https://www.dol.gov/ , and https://www.bls.gov/ .
2. If no single official statement is sufficient, a consensus of at least two credible reports from major outlets stating on or after 2025-10-10 that the shutdown/lapse remained in effect on that date and that BLS was under shutdown procedures. Example sources include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), and major national newspapers.

Resolves No if, by 2025-10-10, appropriations are in force and BLS is no longer operating under shutdown contingency procedures for all of that date, or if official/consensus reporting shows no shutdown was in effect on 2025-10-10.

If there is a brief intraday lapse on 2025-10-10 that is officially recognized as a shutdown/lapse in appropriations and BLS is under contingency procedures for any part of that date, resolve Yes. If evidence is genuinely contradictory and no consensus can be established from the above sources, resolve using the preponderance of official statements; if still impossible, the question is unresolvable.

Resolution window: only events occurring between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive) count toward resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A persistent government shutdown is one of the clearest near-term causal pathways to interrupted BLS publication. Knowing whether a shutdown is still active by Oct. 10 helps distinguish between a brief procedural scare and a materially elevated risk of missed releases, degraded data collection, and possible escalation toward the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: A federal government funding lapse/shutdown must be in effect at any time on October 10, 2025 (within the Oct 1–Oct 10 window), AND the BLS must be operating under shutdown contingency procedures on that date. Observable evidence required: official/credible reports explicitly confirming (1) shutdown in effect on Oct 10, and (2) BLS under contingency/shutdown procedures on Oct 10. Key entities: U.S. federal government, BLS, OMB. Key threshold: shutdown must be in force on Oct 10; BLS must be under contingency procedures on that date.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'federal government shutdown October 2025' (Oct 1–10) — to find confirmation of shutdown start and duration. Query 2: 'government funding lapse appropriations October 2025' (Oct 1–10) — to find lapse details and BLS impact. Query 3: 'government shutdown ended reopened October 10 2025' (Oct 8–12) — to check if shutdown ended before Oct 10. Query 4: 'Bureau of Labor Statistics BLS shutdown contingency October 2025' (Oct 1–12) — to find BLS-specific shutdown status. Query 5: 'government shutdown still ongoing day 10 October 10 2025' (Oct 9–11) — to confirm shutdown was ongoing on Day 10.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Government shutdown started October 1, 2025 at 12:01 a.m. — confirmed by AP, NBC, ABC, CNBC, FOX5 DC, Investopedia, and many others. (2) Shutdown still in effect on October 10, 2025 (Day 10) — confirmed by CNN, ABC News, Yahoo News, CBS News, Straits Times, BSS News, Benzinga, USA Today. (3) BLS halted all operations on October 1 when funding lapsed — confirmed by CNBC, Yahoo Finance, HuffPost, Washington Examiner, Morningstar, etc. (4) On October 10, BLS announced it would recall limited staff for CPI report only, but confirmed ALL OTHER operations remain suspended — confirmed by Investing.com UK, New York Post, Zero Hedge, Yahoo Finance, KRDO, Cryptopolitan. No candidate events found suggesting shutdown ended before or on Oct 10. No contradictory events identified.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Criterion 1 (Shutdown in effect on Oct 10): [CNN](https://us.cnn.com/politics/live-news/government-shutdown-news-10-10-25) explicitly reports 'Government shutdown reaches tenth day' on Oct 10, 2025. [ABC News](https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/federal-workers-paychecks-impacted-government-shutdown-continues/story?id=126401170) confirms 'government shutdown enters its 10th day on October 10, 2025'. [Yahoo News](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/federal-government-shutdown-enters-day-105551171.html) confirms 'federal government shutdown entered its 10th day on Friday, October 10, 2025'. Criterion 2 (BLS under contingency procedures on Oct 10): [Investing.com UK](https://uk.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-to-release-september-inflation-data-despite-shutdown-93CH-4300183) published Oct 10, 2025 states 'ongoing government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025, after funding lapsed' and BLS 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services.' [KRDO](https://krdo.com/news/2025/10/10/latest-inflation-data-to-be-released-this-month-despite-government-shutdown/) confirms 'BLS had halted all operations since October 1, 2025, when funding lapsed, with only one employee working full-time on contingency plans.' [ABC17NEWS](https://abc17news.com/money/cnn-business-consumer/2025/10/09/latest-inflation-data-to-be-released-this-month-despite-government-shutdown/) confirms 'BLS halted all operations on October 1 when federal funding lapsed.' Both criteria are explicitly satisfied on October 10, 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple articles dated October 10, 2025 explicitly confirm: (1) shutdown was in effect on that date (Day 10); (2) BLS was operating under shutdown contingency procedures. Specific timestamp: October 10, 2025 (entire day). The shutdown began at 12:01 a.m. October 1, 2025, and was still in effect on October 10, 2025 with no resolution before or on that date. The next Senate vote was scheduled for October 14, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying occurrence is October 1, 2025, when the shutdown began and BLS halted all operations. The question asks about any time on October 10, 2025 — the shutdown was in effect for the entirety of that day (Day 10 of the shutdown). No earlier qualifying occurrence is needed as the question resolves based on the state on October 10, specifically.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence: No articles found indicating the shutdown ended before October 10, 2025. All sources from October 10 explicitly state it was Day 10 of the shutdown. The next Senate vote was scheduled for October 14, 2025, confirming no resolution on or before October 10. The BLS recalling limited staff specifically for CPI report on October 10 does NOT indicate normal operations resumed — BLS explicitly stated 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services,' confirming contingency procedures remained in effect. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Both criteria for Yes resolution are explicitly and unambiguously satisfied: (1) The federal government funding lapse/shutdown was in effect on October 10, 2025 (Day 10), as confirmed by CNN, ABC News, Yahoo News, CBS News, and multiple other major outlets; (2) BLS was operating under shutdown contingency procedures on October 10, 2025, with operations halted, most employees furloughed, and all regular data releases suspended, as confirmed by Investing.com UK, KRDO, New York Post, Zero Hedge, and Yahoo Finance articles dated October 10, 2025. Resolution: Yes.

question: Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes be impeached 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the the Federal Senate (Senado Federal) votes to proceed with any impeachment of Minister of the Supreme Federal Court of Brazil Alexandre de Moraes by December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the results of the first such vote the Senate undertakes (e.g., if the Federal Senate decides to vote on the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes and it fails to pass, this market will resolve to "No").

This market will resolve to "Yes" as soon as the Senate successfully votes to proceed with this impeachment, regardless of the impeachment's outcome.

If it becomes impossible to impeach Alexandre de Moraes while he is in his role as Minister (e.g., he resigns) and the "Yes" condition has not yet been met, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the government of Brazil, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the President of the Federal Senate formally place on the Senate agenda, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, any request for impeachment of STF Minister Alexandre de Moraes for consideration by the Senate plenary or the Mesa do Senado?
subquestions.background_information:
A key bottleneck for any impeachment of an STF minister is not merely the filing of petitions, but whether the Senate leadership chooses to advance one procedurally. Multiple impeachment requests against Alexandre de Moraes have reportedly already been filed; one August 2025 report described a new filing as roughly the 30th such request against him, indicating that filing alone has not been sufficient to create a credible path to impeachment. https://www.breitbart.com/latin-america/2025/08/07/brazil-tries-to-impeach-for-the-30th-time-judge-who-put-jair-bolsonaro-under-house-arrest/

Recent reporting also indicates that after U.S. sanctions on Moraes and rising political pressure, the Senate president still declined to hold an impeachment vote, which suggests Senate agenda-setting is a highly informative near-term indicator for the ultimate question. https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/7IY7YV5R4JH7XJ4N4YQX6I3G6I/

The political environment is unusually salient. The U.S. Treasury sanctioned Moraes on 2025-07-30 under the Global Magnitsky framework, increasing international and domestic controversy around him. https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0174

At the same time, Brazilian right-wing groups were reported to be planning mass demonstrations for 2025-09-07 demanding Moraes's impeachment, making the first month of September a natural window to watch for institutional follow-through. https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/7IY7YV5R4JH7XJ4N4YQX6I3G6I/

Because the ultimate market resolves on a Senate vote to proceed, an earlier procedural signal is whether Senate leadership moves any impeachment request onto the formal agenda or formally submits it for consideration by the relevant Senate governing body. That event is distinct from the ultimate question but strongly related: if the Senate president still refuses to schedule or docket the matter during a period of peak attention, the odds of an impeachment vote by year-end likely fall.

Sources:
Brazil Tries to Impeach--for the 30th Time--Judge Who Put Jair Bolsonaro Under House Arrest — https://www.breitbart.com/latin-america/2025/08/07/brazil-tries-to-impeach-for-the-30th-time-judge-who-put-jair-bolsonaro-under-house-arrest/
Brazil's democratic quandary: How to prosecute a president — https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/7IY7YV5R4JH7XJ4N4YQX6I3G6I/
U.S. Department of the Treasury press release on sanctions against Alexandre de Moraes — https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0174
Federal Senate of Brazil (official site) — https://www25.senado.leg.br/web/atividade
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, the President of the Federal Senate or the Senate's official systems formally place on the Senate agenda, order of business, dispatches, or other official legislative processing record any impeachment request against STF Minister Alexandre de Moraes for consideration by either (a) the Senate plenary or (b) the Mesa do Senado/Federal Senate leadership body.

This question resolves No if no such formal agenda placement or equivalent official procedural advancement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.

For avoidance of doubt, the following do NOT by themselves count for Yes: (1) a new impeachment petition merely being filed or publicized; (2) speeches, interviews, or social-media statements by senators; (3) street protests; (4) media reports claiming the matter is under discussion without an official Senate record.

Qualifying evidence for Yes should come from official Senate sources such as the Senado Federal legislative portal, agenda pages, plenary agenda/order-of-the-day pages, official news releases, or official dispatch/publication records. Primary source: https://www25.senado.leg.br/web/atividade and related official Senate pages under senado.leg.br. If the Senate website structure changes, archived or successor official Senate pages may be used.

If official Senate records are unavailable or ambiguous, a consensus of at least three credible Brazilian news outlets reporting that the Senate president formally pautou, incluiu na pauta, despachou for consideration, or otherwise officially advanced an impeachment request against Moraes during the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window may be used as a fallback, provided no official Senate source contradicts that reporting. Potential secondary sources include Agencia Senado https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias, G1 https://g1.globo.com/politica/, and Folha de S.Paulo https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/.

If a qualifying action is announced before 2025-10-01 but the formal Senate record shows the agenda placement occurred outside the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window, it does not count. If the matter is scheduled and then withdrawn within the window, it still counts as Yes so long as official records show it was formally placed on the agenda during the window.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question hinges on whether the Senate will actually vote to proceed with impeachment. Formal agenda-setting by the Senate president is a necessary and highly informative precursor that is distinct from the ultimate outcome. Observing whether Senate leadership advances the matter during a period of intense public pressure should materially update forecasts about the probability of a vote by year-end.

(3) Yahoo (Sep 1): '41 senators have lined up to remove Moraes, but 54 votes are needed' — shows insufficient votes and no formal action. (4) Multiple September 2025 articles on Brazil Senate show Alcolumbre active in scrapping immunity bill and making STF requests but NO mention of formally scheduling Moraes impeachment. No candidate events for formal agenda placement within the September 1 - October 1 window were identified.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article or source explicitly confirms that Senate President Davi Alcolumbre formally placed any impeachment request against Moraes on the Senate agenda between September 1-October 1, 2025. The NZ Herald article [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/KJQ5XHZBCNCKJNZTGN72BV6B4E/] explicitly states 'a Senate president declined to hold an impeachment vote.' Multiple sources confirm only 41 senators support impeachment (insufficient for the required 54), and the Senate president was actively resisting the opposition's demands for such proceedings.

The Breitbart article (Aug 7) confirms a petition was filed in August, not formally scheduled. The September 2025 articles covering Brazilian politics focus on: Bolsonaro trial, immunity bill protests, sanctions on Moraes — but none report formal Senate scheduling of Moraes impeachment. The evidence consistently shows the Senate president (Alcolumbre) refused to formally advance impeachment proceedings.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence indicates: (1) Senate President Alcolumbre declined to formally place impeachment requests on the Senate agenda; (2) Only 41 of 54 required senators supported impeachment; (3) No official Senate record of formal agenda placement was reported by any source. The condition for Yes was never met during the window. Resolution is No, with the window closing on 2025-10-01.

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States publicly acknowledge conducting at least one new drone, missile, or air strike in Syria between 2026-01-13 and 2026-02-12?
subquestions.background_information:

This is informative for the ultimate question because if the US conducts another acknowledged strike in Syria so soon after the January 10 operation, that would be evidence of an elevated operational tempo and a greater base rate of US cross-border air/missile/drone strikes in 2026. Since the ultimate market turns on whether the US strikes the soil of 3 different countries during 2026, repeated early activity in one already-active theater increases the chance of a broader multi-country strike pattern later in the year, even though this subquestion is not itself a restatement of the ultimate question.
