Candidate Event 2: Five US CENTCOM precision strikes against ISIS targets in Syria between January 27 and February 2, 2026. Announced February 4, 2026 by CENTCOM. Sources: DVIDS (official US military), Fox News, Anadolu Agency, Epoch Times. Neither event requires inference; both are explicitly stated within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Event 1 fully satisfies criteria: (a) US military conducted an airstrike using precision munitions in Syria [AP News](https://apnews.com/article/syria-united-states-alsharaa-trump-airstrikes-9273f17f74ecffa0e0793c88642140e1), [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/us-kills-al-qaeda-affiliate-leader-bilal-hasa-al-jasim-linked-ambush-syria/), [DVIDS](https://www.dvidshub.net/news/557429/us-forces-strike-isis-targets-syria-partners-sustain-pressure); (b) officially acknowledged by CENTCOM (Adm. Brad Cooper quoted directly); (c) occurred January 16, 2026 — within the window; (d) impacted ground territory in Syria (killed a target on the ground); (e) was a new strike, not re-reporting of January 10 strikes (explicitly called 'another retaliatory strike'). Event 2 (Jan 27–Feb 2 strikes) also fully satisfies criteria: five precision airstrikes using fixed-wing, rotary-wing, and unmanned aircraft per CENTCOM announcement on February 4, 2026 [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/world/us-military-syria-carries-out-5-strikes-against-multiple-isis-targets), [DVIDS](https://www.dvidshub.net/news/557429/us-forces-strike-isis-targets-syria-partners-sustain-pressure), [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/us-says-it-carried-out-strikes-on-isis-targets-in-syria/3820536).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest qualifying event: January 16, 2026 (the date the strike occurred), with CENTCOM public announcement on January 17, 2026. This is explicitly stated in multiple sources. Fox News states: 'The strike occurred in northwest Syria on January 15, 2026' (slightly different date), while CBS News, DVIDS, and Sahara Reporters confirm January 16, 2026. The announcement by CENTCOM was made on January 17, 2026. Since the question asks for acknowledgment during the window, and the strike itself also falls within the window (after January 13, 2026), the resolution datetime is 2026-01-16T00:00:00Z (or at latest when CENTCOM announced it on 2026-01-17).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The January 16 strike is explicitly identified as a new event within the window (the question excludes the January 10 strikes). Multiple sources describe this as 'another retaliatory strike' or 'third retaliatory strike' distinct from earlier strikes. No earlier qualifying strike within the January 13–February 12 window was identified. The January 13 airstrikes mentioned in one source (Conservative Journal Review) may also qualify — stating 'The U.S. military conducted a series of large-scale airstrikes against ISIS targets in Syria on January 13, 2026, at approximately 12:30 p.m. EST.' However, the question excludes re-reporting of the January 10 strikes, and it's not clear whether the January 13 reporting refers to those same January 10 strikes or new ones. Given the ambiguity, the January 16 strike is the most clearly confirmed new qualifying event within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No source disputes that the January 16 strike occurred within the window or that it was a new strike. The question specifically excludes re-reporting of 'January 10, 2026 Syria strikes' — the January 16 strike is explicitly described as a new, separate targeting of Bilal Hasan al-Jasim. Multiple high-quality sources agree. The January 27–February 2 strikes are also confirmed by CENTCOM and multiple outlets. No conflicting evidence found. The strikes clearly used aerial/drone/missile means (precision munitions from fixed-wing, rotary-wing, and unmanned aircraft) and impacted Syrian ground territory.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is Yes. The United States publicly acknowledged conducting new airstrikes in Syria within the specified window (January 13 – February 12, 2026). The first qualifying event is a U.S. CENTCOM airstrike on January 16, 2026, in northwest Syria, killing Bilal Hasan al-Jasim — announced on January 17, 2026 by CENTCOM and widely reported by AP News, CBS News, Fox News, AFP, and others quoting named US officials. This is a new strike (distinct from January 10 strikes), uses qualifying modalities (aerial precision munitions), impacted Syrian ground territory, and falls squarely within the resolution window. Additionally, five more strikes were conducted January 27–February 2, 2026, further confirming Yes. Resolution datetime set to 2026-01-17T00:00:00Z (when CENTCOM publicly announced the January 16 strike).

question: Will Trump try to fire another Fed Governor by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump publicly and unequivocally announces that he is removing another Fed Governor before their term is up, or takes formal action toward doing so, such as issuing a directive or formal request between August 25 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30, will Donald Trump publicly announce a nominee to fill Lisa Cook’s Federal Reserve Board seat or any other Federal Reserve Board of Governors seat?
subquestions.background_information:
A key near-term indicator for whether Trump will try to remove another Fed governor is whether he moves quickly to capitalize on his attempted removal of Lisa Cook by naming a replacement. Multiple late-August reports said Trump had already attempted to fire Governor Lisa Cook and was seeking to reshape the Fed Board. CNN reported on 2025-08-28 that Trump had fired Cook, that Cook planned to contest the move in court, and that Trump selected Stephen Miran as a potential replacement while saying, “We’ll have a majority very shortly.” https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/economy/trump-federal-reserve-lisa-cook The Inquirer likewise reported that Trump announced Cook was fired “effective immediately,” that Cook rejected the removal, and that Trump had also appointed Stephen Miran to a vacant Fed board seat. https://www.inquirer.com/politics/nation/trump-fires-fed-governor-lisa-cook-20250827.html Reuters/Yahoo reported that the legal fight over Cook’s status could determine whether Trump can add another member to the Fed’s seven-member Board, potentially increasing his influence over monetary policy. https://www.yahoo.com/news/trumps-firing-fed-governor-cook-204305515.html

This matters because a public nomination would be concrete evidence that the White House expects or intends to create and use additional Fed Board vacancies. If Trump announces a nominee for Cook’s seat very quickly, that would suggest he is treating governor removals as politically and legally viable, which should raise the odds of another removal attempt before 2025-10-31. By contrast, if no nominee is announced by the end of September, that would be some evidence of caution, legal uncertainty, or political difficulty.

The Fed Board normally has seven seats. Reporting before 2025-09-01 indicated that one vacancy already existed following Adriana Kugler’s resignation, and Trump’s move against Cook was widely understood as an effort to create another opening and secure a friendlier majority on the Board. CNN said advisers believed a replacement could help Trump gain influence ahead of the September policy meeting. https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/economy/trump-federal-reserve-lisa-cook

Sources:
CNN: Inside Trump's attempt to put his mark on the Fed — https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/economy/trump-federal-reserve-lisa-cook
The Philadelphia Inquirer: Trump moves to fire Fed governor, aiming to control central bank — https://www.inquirer.com/politics/nation/trump-fires-fed-governor-lisa-cook-20250827.html
Yahoo/Reuters: Trump's firing of Fed Governor Cook could be blocked by US judge — https://www.yahoo.com/news/trumps-firing-fed-governor-cook-204305515.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 inclusive, Donald Trump or the White House publicly announces a specific nominee for (a) the Federal Reserve Board seat allegedly vacated by Lisa Cook, or (b) any other specific seat on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors.

Qualifying announcements include: a White House press release; a Truth Social post or other official Trump statement naming the nominee; or formal transmission of the nomination to the U.S. Senate recorded by Congress.gov or the Senate.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 inclusive.

For avoidance of doubt:
- Mere media speculation that Trump is considering candidates does not count.
- Statements that Trump “plans to nominate someone soon” do not count unless a specific person is publicly named as nominee.
- Announcing a nominee for Fed Chair alone counts only if the announcement is explicitly for a Board of Governors seat as well; the market is about Board seats, not only internal leadership roles.
- If the announcement occurs after 2025-09-30, it does not count.
- If a purported announcement is later denied by the White House the same day, resolver should rely on the clearest final official statement as of 2025-09-30.

Primary resolution sources: White House announcements at https://www.whitehouse.gov/, Trump official communications, and Congress.gov nominations records at https://www.congress.gov/search?q=%7B%22source%22%3A%22nominations%22%7D. Secondary source: Federal Reserve Board announcements at https://www.federalreserve.gov/ and consensus reporting from Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ if needed.

If no authoritative public source remains available, a consensus of at least two independent, credible outlets reporting a named public nomination made within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-30 window may be used.
subquestions.rationale: A rapid nomination to a disputed or newly opened Fed seat would indicate that Trump is operationalizing a strategy of reshaping the Board, making another removal attempt more plausible. It is not just an earlier version of the ultimate question; it measures whether the administration is taking follow-on steps that imply confidence in and commitment to further intervention in Fed governance.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30, Trump or White House must publicly announce a specific nominee for a Federal Reserve Board of Governors seat. Qualifying events: White House press release, Truth Social post naming nominee, or formal transmission of nomination to U.S. Senate (per Congress.gov/Senate). Key: Miran nomination for Kugler seat, Lisa Cook seat, any Fed Board seat.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump Federal Reserve Board nominee nomination September 2025' - to find in-window nomination events; 2) 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve Board seat vacancy Trump nominee 2025' - to find Cook-related nomination; 3) 'Trump announces Stephen Miran Federal Reserve nomination date announcement Truth Social' - to find exact nomination date; 4) 'Trump Federal Reserve Board of Governors nominee announcement White House September 2025' - for additional in-window events; 5) 'Miran Federal Reserve nomination sent transmitted Senate August 2025 formal' - to determine formal Senate transmission date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Primary candidate: Trump announced Stephen Miran as nominee for Federal Reserve Board of Governors seat (Kugler's vacated seat) on August 7, 2025 via Truth Social — this is BEFORE the September 1 window. Secondary candidate: Formal transmission of nomination to U.S. Senate — the Senate returned from August recess on September 2, 2025, and the confirmation hearing was September 4. The committee vote was September 10, and the full Senate confirmed Miran on September 15, all within the window. A third candidate: Trump's formal signing of Miran's commission on September 16. No new/separate nomination announcement for any other seat was found within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Truth Social announcement of August 7, 2025 is the original nomination announcement — this precedes the window. However, the resolution criteria explicitly includes 'formal transmission of the nomination to the U.S. Senate recorded by Congress.gov or the Senate' as a qualifying event. Per [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/senate/3762957/white-house-senate-push-accelerate-trump-fed-nominee/), the Senate was on recess until September 2, 2025. The formal Senate proceedings (committee hearing September 4, committee vote September 10 per [Law360](https://www.law360.com/articles/2386494/trump-s-pick-for-fed-board-seat-moves-ahead-to-full-senate), Senate confirmation September 15 per [Vietnam Star](https://vietnamstar.net/u-s-senate-confirms-trump-nominee-stephen-miran-as-new-fed-governor/)) all occurred within the September 1-30 window. The formal transmission to the Senate is consistent with occurring at or shortly after Senate returned from recess (September 2), which falls within the window. Per [WBAP](https://www.wbap.com/news/senate-prepares-hearing-on-trump-fed-pick-as-cook-fights-ouster/): 'Miran...was formally nominated on August 7' — but this appears to reference the Truth Social announcement, not the formal Senate transmission. The Senate confirmation hearing on September 4 is the first formal Senate proceeding, implying the Senate received the nomination by then (i.e., within the window given the Senate's September 2 return from recess).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Original Truth Social announcement: August 7, 2025 (before window). Senate returned from recess: September 2, 2025 (within window). First Senate proceeding (committee hearing): September 4, 2025 (within window). Senate Banking Committee vote: September 10, 2025 at approximately 6:02 PM EDT (within window). Full Senate confirmation: September 15, 2025 (within window). Trump signed commission: September 16, 2025 (within window). Formal Senate transmission: likely September 2-3, 2025 (within window, when Senate returned from recess and could formally receive the nomination).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying event within the September 1-30 window would be the formal transmission to the Senate (approximately September 2-3, 2025, when the Senate returned from recess). No earlier in-window qualifying event was found — the Truth Social announcement was August 7 (before window). The committee hearing on September 4 is the first confirmed in-window event connected to the formal Senate nomination process.
evidence.step7_verification: Counter-argument: One article (WBAP, August 27) states Miran 'was formally nominated on August 7.' If the formal nomination transmission to the Senate also occurred August 7 (even if Congress was in recess), this would place the qualifying formal transmission outside the window. However, Senate procedures typically require the Senate to be in session to formally receive nominations. With Congress on recess until September 2, the formal Senate action could not have occurred before then. The nomination was publicly announced August 7 (Trump Truth Social post), but the formal Senate proceedings began in September. Additionally, there is no evidence of any denial or retraction of the Miran nomination within the September window. No contradictory evidence found. The confirmation that Miran was confirmed September 15 and sworn in September 16 is consistent across all sources.
evidence.step8_final_decision: While the original public announcement via Truth Social was August 7, 2025 (outside the window), the formal transmission of the nomination to the U.S. Senate — a qualifying event per the resolution criteria — occurred within the September 1-30 window (likely September 2-4, when the Senate returned from recess and the first committee hearing was held). The Senate Banking Committee confirmed the nomination was before them on September 4, September 10, and the full Senate confirmed on September 15. The formal legislative nomination process was conducted entirely within the September window. This satisfies the resolution criteria for a 'formal transmission of the nomination to the U.S. Senate recorded by Congress.gov or the Senate.' Resolution: Yes.

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that lowers, pauses, delays, or removes any tariffs on imports from Canada by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) or the White House announce, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, the start of a formal U.S.-Canada trade negotiation, consultation, or review explicitly aimed at modifying current U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether Trump will later lower tariffs on Canada is whether his administration opens a formal policy process directed at changing those tariffs. As of late 2025, the Trump administration has recently escalated trade restrictions on Canada rather than eased them. Reporting indicates that on August 1, 2025, Trump signed an executive order raising tariffs from 25% to 35% on goods from Canada not covered by USMCA/CUSMA, while other tariff actions and the removal of the de minimis exemption have added additional trade friction for Canadian exporters. See Pittsburgh's Action News 4 on the August 1 order: https://www.wtae.com/article/trump-tariffs-canada-delay/65506465 ; Global News on the end of de minimis and 35% non-CUSMA tariff treatment for Canadian goods: https://globalnews.ca/news/11366237/duty-free-shipping-us-ends-friday-canadian-businesses-fearful/ ; and Reuters coverage of U.S. tariff policy and official trade announcements via the White House and USTR sites: https://www.reuters.com/ .

Because the ultimate question resolves Yes if Trump later lowers, pauses, delays, or removes Canada-specific tariffs, a formal bilateral negotiation or review targeted at those tariffs would be a meaningful precursor event. Such a process would not itself lower tariffs, but it would signal political willingness to revisit them and create an administrative path for a later easing action before year-end. USTR is the principal U.S. agency for trade negotiations and publishes official notices, statements, and announcements at https://ustr.gov/ . The White House also publishes presidential statements and executive actions at https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/ and https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/ .

Sources:
USTR homepage — https://ustr.gov/
White House Presidential Actions — https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/
White House Briefing Room — https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
Pittsburgh's Action News 4, "New tariffs on Canada take effect Friday; Dozens of other countries delayed" — https://www.wtae.com/article/trump-tariffs-canada-delay/65506465
Global News, "Duty-free shipping to U.S. ends Friday. Canadian businesses are 'fearful'" — https://globalnews.ca/news/11366237/duty-free-shipping-us-ends-friday-canadian-businesses-fearful/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, either (a) the USTR or the White House publishes an official statement, press release, notice, readout, or presidential action explicitly announcing the start of a formal negotiation, consultation, working group, review, or similar bilateral process with Canada and explicitly stating that the process concerns modifying, reviewing, easing, pausing, or reconsidering current U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods; or (b) both the U.S. and Canadian governments officially confirm such a process during that window.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying official announcement is published by 2025-11-30 23:59:59 UTC.

Qualifying announcements must be official and public. Primary sources are:
- USTR news/press releases and statements: https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases
- USTR homepage: https://ustr.gov/
- White House Presidential Actions: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/
- White House Briefing Room: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- Government of Canada official trade/news releases, if needed for bilateral confirmation: https://www.canada.ca/en/global-affairs/news.html and https://www.canada.ca/en/department-finance/news.html

Non-qualifying events include: general diplomatic meetings that do not explicitly concern modifying current U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods; broad trade comments without initiation of a formal process; market rumors; commentary from unnamed officials; or negotiations solely about unrelated issues such as border security, defense, or tariffs on third countries.

If an announcement occurs within the window but is later clarified within the same window to not concern modifying current U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods, it does not qualify. If relevant official webpages are unavailable at resolution time, a consensus of at least two major outlets quoting the official announcement text directly (for example Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ and AP https://apnews.com/ ) may be used as a fallback.
subquestions.rationale: Opening a formal U.S.-Canada tariff negotiation or review would be a strong leading indicator that the administration is preparing or seriously considering a later tariff reduction. It is a different observable event from the ultimate question itself, but one that should substantially update forecasts about whether Trump will lower Canada-specific tariffs by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Between Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025, USTR or White House must publish an official statement explicitly announcing the start of a formal negotiation/consultation/working group/review with Canada explicitly aimed at modifying/reviewing/easing/pausing/reconsidering current U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods; OR both governments officially confirm such a process. Observable evidence: official press releases from ustr.gov, whitehouse.gov, or bilateral confirmation from Canadian government. Key entities: USTR, White House, Canadian government. Threshold: explicit, official, public announcement of a formal bilateral process specifically targeting modification of current U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'USTR White House formal trade negotiation Canada tariffs 2025' — to find direct qualifying announcements; 2) 'US Canada trade negotiation tariff review November 2025' — broad search for any formal process initiation; 3) 'USTR press release Canada tariff negotiation November 2025' — to specifically check USTR press releases; 4) 'White House Canada trade deal announcement November 2025' — to check White House announcements; 5) 'Trump Canada trade talks restart November December 2025' — to check if talks resumed; 6) 'Carney Trump meeting trade tariff formal announcement November 2025' — to check for any bilateral confirmation.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Trump October 31, 2025 statement declaring trade negotiations with Canada 'over' and that US 'will not restart' discussions — this is the OPPOSITE of a qualifying event and forecloses Yes. (2) Carney November 23, 2025 statement at G20 that talks will resume 'when it's appropriate' but he has no burning issue — this is not a qualifying announcement. (3) Carney-Trump casual 'exchange' around Nov 25–26 confirmed by Carney to NOT constitute formal negotiations — explicitly rejected by Carney as non-qualifying. (4) Canada's November 26 domestic steel/lumber support announcement — this is Canada acting unilaterally, not a bilateral US-Canada process, and explicitly stated 'no new formal talks are scheduled.' (5) USTR CUSMA review/comment period — this is a pre-existing mandatory review process scheduled for 2026, not a new formal bilateral process aimed at modifying current tariffs within the window. All candidates rejected as non-qualifying.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event matched the resolution criteria. [The Indian Express, Oct 31](https://indianexpress.com/article/world/trump-rules-out-restarting-us-canada-trade-talks-after-ontario-ad-row-10338745/) reports Trump confirmed 'trade negotiations with Canada are over' on October 31, 2025. [Al Jazeera, Oct 31](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2025/10/31/trump-says-us-canada-will-not-restart-trade-talks) confirms Trump announced US and Canada would not restart trade talks. [Market Screener, Nov 26](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/canada-to-implement-new-trade-financing-measures-to-protect-trade-exposed-sectors-ce7d5ed3da8af523) states 'No new formal talks are scheduled.' [TalkMarkets, Nov 24](https://talkmarkets.com/content/economics--politics/why-the-silence-on-canada-us-tariffs-negotiations?post=540141) states 'As of November 2025, no major trade negotiations are underway.' [The Star, Nov 27](https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/mark-carney-donald-trump-tariffs/article_cac49c74-9c7a-43a9-9111-4a1e5e846f9f.html) confirms Carney stated 'formal negotiations have not restarted' after a casual exchange with Trump. [ArcaMax, Nov 25](https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3930920) states 'no formal trade discussions are expected' for Carney's potential DC trip.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The definitively foreclosing event occurred on 2025-10-31, when Trump publicly declared trade negotiations with Canada 'over.' Multiple articles with publication date of 2025-10-31 confirm this. Throughout November 2025 (verified through Nov 29), no qualifying announcement was found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (formal announcement of new negotiations to modify U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods) occurred at any point in the Oct 31–Nov 30 window. The first event of the window was instead Trump's explicit foreclosure of negotiations. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence sought: No source found any official USTR or White House statement announcing formal bilateral trade negotiations with Canada during the window. All sources consistently describe talks as frozen, paused, suspended, or 'over.' The CUSMA review process (public comments, hearing) is a pre-existing mandatory multi-lateral framework review scheduled for 2026, not a bilateral process aimed at modifying current tariffs on Canadian goods as required by the resolution criteria. Canada's Nov 26 domestic measures explicitly followed 'failed negotiations with the U.S.' The only possible Carney-Trump contact was described as a casual 'exchange' explicitly NOT constituting formal negotiations.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution = No. Trump explicitly stated on October 31, 2025 (the start of the resolution window) that trade negotiations with Canada are 'over' and the US 'will not restart' them. Throughout November 2025, all reporting consistently confirms no formal bilateral process was initiated. No USTR or White House official announcement qualifying under the resolution criteria was published. Canada was instead implementing unilateral domestic protection measures and seeking talks with third-party countries (India, China, UAE). The window closed November 30, 2025 with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: Julie Masino out as Cracker Barrel CEO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Julie Masino ceases to be CEO of Cracker Barrel for any length of time between August 24 and December 31, 2025 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of Julie Masino's resignation/firing before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/firing goes into effect.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from Cracker Barrel and/or Julie Masino, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Cracker Barrel publicly announce, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, that it has appointed a new permanent President in addition to Julie Masino remaining CEO?
subquestions.background_information:
A meaningful indicator for whether Julie Masino may be removed as CEO by year-end is whether the board moves to split top leadership responsibilities or install an additional senior operator above or alongside her in day-to-day management. Cracker Barrel is already under visible pressure after its failed 2025 logo redesign and subsequent reversal. Newsweek reported on 2025-08-27 that Masino was facing calls to resign after the company abruptly scrapped the new logo following backlash and a share-price drop of more than 10% (https://www.newsweek.com/cracker-barrel-ceo-under-pressure-resign-after-logo-u-turn-2105080). The New York Post likewise reported customer and investor anger and noted criticism from activist investor Sardar Biglari and others calling for the CEO’s dismissal (https://nypost.com/2025/08/27/business/cracker-barrel-shares-jump-after-backtrack-on-logo-change-but-customers-still-want-ceo-gone/).

More recently, Cracker Barrel announced organizational changes on 2025-10-03 and said it was ending its relationship with Prophet, the consultancy associated with the rebrand. That announcement indicates the company is still actively restructuring after the backlash, making further management changes plausible. Nation’s Restaurant News reported that the company was “streamlining leadership” and quoted Masino saying that “there is more to come” as the company heads into the holiday season (https://www.nrn.com/casual-dining/cracker-barrel-ends-relationship-design-company). The Hill also reported on 2025-10-24 that Masino publicly defended the attempted logo redesign while noting the company had already reversed course and canceled remodel plans (https://thehill.com/business/5569178-cracker-barrel-ceo-explains-reason-for-attempt-to-change-logo/).

If Cracker Barrel appoints a new permanent President while Masino remains CEO, that would be an observable sign that the board is redistributing authority or adding oversight rather than immediately removing her. That would generally be evidence against near-term CEO ouster, though not decisive.

Sources:
Newsweek - Cracker Barrel CEO under pressure to resign after logo U-turn - https://www.newsweek.com/cracker-barrel-ceo-under-pressure-resign-after-logo-u-turn-2105080
New York Post - Cracker Barrel shares jump 7% after backtrack on logo change - but... - https://nypost.com/2025/08/27/business/cracker-barrel-shares-jump-after-backtrack-on-logo-change-but-customers-still-want-ceo-gone/
Nation's Restaurant News - Cracker Barrel ends relationship with design company - https://www.nrn.com/casual-dining/cracker-barrel-ends-relationship-design-company
The Hill - Cracker Barrel CEO explains reason for attempt to change logo - https://thehill.com/business/5569178-cracker-barrel-ceo-explains-reason-for-attempt-to-change-logo/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. publicly announces, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, that it has appointed or hired a new permanent executive with the title "President" of Cracker Barrel or "President and Chief Operating Officer" (or a clearly equivalent permanent role), while Julie Masino is still identified in the same announcement or in contemporaneous company materials as CEO.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement is made between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive.

For clarity:
- "Publicly announces" includes a company press release, SEC filing, or official investor-relations/newsroom posting by Cracker Barrel.
- Interim or acting appointments do not count.

evidence.step1_decompose: The exact condition for Yes: Valve Corporation must have officially announced or revealed a new Half-Life game (continuation of the series) between 2025-11-10 and 2025-12-10 (inclusive) via: (1) official Steam news hub post, (2) official trailer/teaser on Valve's YouTube, (3) official Steam store page, or (4) official public statement naming a new Half-Life title. Key entities: Valve Corporation, Half-Life series. Threshold: Official Valve action, not third-party rumor/leak/datamine. Timing: strictly within window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Valve Half-Life new game announcement 2025' (Nov 10–Dec 10) — to find direct announcement news. Query 2: 'Half-Life 3 announcement reveal Valve' (Nov 10–Dec 10) — to find specific HL3 reveals. Query 3: 'Valve Half-Life 3 officially announced confirmed December 2025' (Dec 5–Dec 10) — to find late-window official news. Query 4: 'Half-Life 3 Game Awards December 11 2025 announcement' (Dec 1–Dec 10) — to check Game Awards window boundary. Query 5: 'Half-Life 3 Steam store page revealed trailer Valve official' (Nov 10–Dec 10) — to check for official Steam presence.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (A) Valve announced Steam Machine, Steam Frame VR headset, and Steam Controller on November 12, 2025 — does NOT include Half-Life 3 announcement. (B) Multiple insider/leaker reports (GabeFollower, Tyler McVicker, Mike Straw of InsiderGaming) about a potential Half-Life 3 announcement 'within weeks' — these are third-party leaks, not official Valve announcements. ALL REJECTED: None constitute an official Valve announcement within the window. The Game Awards is December 11, which is one day OUTSIDE the resolution window (which ends December 10).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No official Valve announcement matches the criteria within the window. Sources explicitly confirming NO official HL3 announcement: [dsogaming.com](https://www.dsogaming.com/news/in-case-youre-wondering-valve-hasnt-announced-half-life-3-yet/) (Nov 12: 'Valve Hasn't Announced Half-Life 3 Yet'), [pcgamer.com](https://www.pcgamer.com/games/fps/sorry-pc-gamers-valve-isnt-announcing-half-life-3-today/) (Nov 12: 'Valve isn't announcing Half-Life 3 today'). Articles published as late as December 9, 2025 by [gamerant.com](https://gamerant.com/half-life-3-rumors-game-awards-reveal-when-bad/) and [gamesradar.com](https://www.gamesradar.com/games/events-conferences/10-predictions-for-the-game-awards-2025-half-life-3-resident-evil-requiem-and-more-on-steam-machine-please-and-thank-you/) still treat HL3 as speculative and pending a potential reveal at The Game Awards on December 11 — outside the window. No article reports an actual official Valve announcement of Half-Life 3 within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying official event was found within the window. The potential Game Awards reveal is scheduled for December 11, 2025, which is outside the resolution window (ends December 10, 2025 23:59:59 UTC).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying official Valve announcement was found at any point within the window. Every piece of evidence confirms the situation remained in the realm of rumors and speculation through December 9, 2025 (latest articles found within the window).
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality sources (PC Gamer, DSO Gaming, Game Rant, GamesRadar, IGN, Shortlist, ScreenRant) published articles within the window explicitly stating no official HL3 announcement had been made and that a potential announcement was still anticipated (speculatively) at The Game Awards on December 11, 2025 — which is outside the resolution window. No contradictory evidence found showing an official Valve announcement within the window. The question window closes on December 10, and The Game Awards (the most anticipated venue for a potential reveal) takes place on December 11.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence consistently shows that NO official Valve announcement of a new Half-Life game occurred between 2025-11-10 and 2025-12-10 (inclusive). The most anticipated potential venue (The Game Awards) was scheduled for December 11, 2025, which is outside the resolution window. question: Will Trump publicly disparage Netanyahu by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump makes any public statement in which he insults, mocks, or attacks Benjamin Netanyahu personally or professionally in a clearly negative manner by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

This includes calling Netanyahu weak, stupid, disloyal, a failure, using an insulting nickname, or using other derogatory language. Policy disagreements stated without disparaging language will not count.

Any public statement made by Trump qualifies.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump publicly claim between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24 that he had to restrain, stop, or overrule Benjamin Netanyahu on Gaza, Iran, or West Bank policy?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful indicator for whether Trump may later publicly disparage Netanyahu, because a public narrative in which Trump casts himself as the person who had to 'stop' or 'control' Netanyahu creates visible interpersonal and political friction short of direct insult. On 2025-10-24, Trump was already quoted as saying 'I stopped Netanyahu' in a TIME interview published via his site, claiming that without his intervention the Gaza war would have 'gone on for years' and reiterating opposition to West Bank annexation. That is not itself a personal insult, but it shows Trump is already willing to publicly describe Netanyahu as someone he needed to constrain. https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/2f7f6f65-4f5c-4a9d-9d4b-4f9f5e7c0c2

There are also prior reports of substantive Trump-Netanyahu tensions. In May 2025, reporting described 'sharp disagreements' over Iran strategy, with Trump preferring diplomacy while Netanyahu pushed a harder line. https://www.worthynews.com/101234-trump-netanyahu-call-reportedly-marked-by-sharp-disagreements-over-iran-strategy

Commentary in October 2025 also suggested that Trump’s Gaza policy depended on forcing Netanyahu into politically painful steps, implying a relationship where Trump may increasingly blame Netanyahu if events go poorly. https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/dealing-with-trumpian-uncertainty-and-no-cultural-boycotts/

Because the ultimate question asks about explicit public disparagement, a nearer-term crux is whether Trump escalates his public framing from 'I got him to do X' to repeated claims that Netanyahu had to be restrained or overruled. Repetition of that framing would make later personal attacks more plausible.

Sources:
Donald J. Trump - 'Trump: I Stopped Netanyahu' https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/2f7f6f65-4f5c-4a9d-9d4b-4f9f5e7c0c2
Worthy Christian News - 'Trump-Netanyahu Call Reportedly Marked By Sharp Disagreements Over Iran Strategy' https://www.worthynews.com/101234-trump-netanyahu-call-reportedly-marked-by-sharp-disagreements-over-iran-strategy
Times of Israel Blogs - 'Dealing with Trumpian Uncertainty and No Cultural Boycotts!' https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/dealing-with-trumpian-uncertainty-and-no-cultural-boycotts/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24 (inclusive), Donald Trump makes at least one public statement explicitly claiming that he had to restrain, stop, overrule, pressure, hold back, or otherwise prevent Benjamin Netanyahu from taking or continuing a course of action on Gaza, Iran, or West Bank policy.

Qualifying statements must be public and attributable to Trump directly, including: on-camera remarks, rally speeches, interviews, official statements, posts on Truth Social/X, or text/audio/video published by Trump or his official political organization. Examples that would count include formulations such as 'I stopped Bibi,' 'I had to hold Netanyahu back,' 'I overruled him on annexation,' or 'I pressured him not to attack Iran.'

Statements that only describe general policy disagreement without Trump claiming he personally restrained or overruled Netanyahu do not count. Likewise, statements made only by aides, anonymous sources, or journalists do not count unless they include a direct attributable Trump quotation published within the resolution window.

Primary resolution sources: Trump's official website/news page https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news, Trump's Truth Social account if accessible via archived/public copies, and video/interview transcripts from major outlets. Secondary confirmation may come from at least one credible report such as Reuters https://www.reuters.com/, AP https://apnews.com/, CNN https://www.cnn.com/, NBC https://www.nbcnews.com/, The New York Times https://www.nytimes.com/, or TIME https://time.com/.

If multiple credible sources quote the same Trump statement, that counts as one qualifying event. If no qualifying Trump statement occurs between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24 (inclusive), resolve No. If a claimed statement cannot be verified from public records or credible reporting, it does not count. If source material is unavailable but at least two independent credible outlets quote the statement with substantially identical wording, that is sufficient for resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A public claim by Trump that he had to restrain or overrule Netanyahu is a concrete, observable sign of deteriorating public chemistry and blame assignment. That kind of dominance-framing often precedes Trump’s transition to overt mockery or insult, making it a meaningful early indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Trump makes at least one public statement explicitly claiming he personally restrained, stopped, overruled, pressured, held back, or otherwise prevented Netanyahu from taking/continuing a course of action on Gaza, Iran, or West Bank policy. Observable evidence: direct Trump quote in video/interview/Truth Social attributing personal restraint or pressure on Netanyahu. Key timing: 2025-10-25 through 2025-11-24 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump restrain stop overrule Netanyahu Gaza Iran West Bank' (Oct 25-Nov 24); 2) 'Trump held back stopped Bibi overruled Netanyahu' (Oct 25-Nov 24); 3) 'Trump quote pushed stopped Netanyahu 60 Minutes ceasefire Gaza Qatar'; 4) 'Trump Truth Social Khamenei ignominious death Netanyahu Iran assassination veto'; 5) '60 Minutes CBS air date November 2025 Netanyahu interview'; 6) 'Trump I pushed him Netanyahu great talented guy never been pushed'

I didn't like certain things that he did, and you saw what I did about that' and 'had to push him a little bit one way or the other' regarding Gaza ceasefire and Qatar strike. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Trump's statement in the November 2-3, 2025 60 Minutes interview — 'I pushed him. I didn't like certain things that he did' — directly claims he personally pressured Netanyahu. Multiple sources describe this as Trump acknowledging pushing Netanyahu on the Gaza ceasefire and on the Qatar strike/apology. This satisfies 'pressured, held back, or otherwise prevented Benjamin Netanyahu from taking or continuing a course of action on Gaza policy.' Sources: [Zero Hedge](https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/trump-boasts-he-pushed-netanyahu-gaza-ceasefire-candid-reveal), [Al Arabiya](https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2025/11/03/trump-says-gaza-ceasefire-very-solid-warns-hamas-will-be-eliminated-if-doesn-t-disarm), [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/trump-us-will-be-involved-in-netanyahu-trial-to-help-him-out-pm-being-mistreated/), [Yahoo/Times of Israel](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/netanyahus-trial-very-unfair-trump-084857759.html), [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5585989-trump-ceasefire-israel-hamas/)

News reports covering the interview were published on November 3, 2025. Exact broadcast: November 2, 2025 (Sunday evening airing), with reporting published November 3, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This appears to be the first qualifying Trump statement within the Oct 25-Nov 24 window. No earlier qualifying statements within the window were found. The Truth Social post about Khamenei was in June 2025. The 60 Minutes interview (Nov 2-3, 2025) is the first confirmed qualifying statement.

The interview date is confirmed as November 2, 2025 (aired Sunday). No contradictory evidence found disputing these quotes. The quote explicitly claims Trump personally pushed/pressured Netanyahu on Gaza ceasefire — not merely describing general policy disagreement. This is a direct, attributable, on-camera statement.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Trump's statement on CBS 60 Minutes (aired November 2, 2025) — 'I pushed him.
