This is within the resolution window (Oct 25-Nov 24, 2025), is directly attributable to Trump, is on-camera, and is confirmed by multiple credible outlets. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will Russia enter Toretske by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Toretske by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of Toretske is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-28, will the ISW Ukraine map show Russian control, gains in the past 24 hours, advance, or infiltration in any area within 5 kilometers of the administrative boundary of Toretsk city (excluding territory inside Toretsk itself)?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a near-term military-positioning indicator for whether Russia is likely to enter Toretsk by December 31, 2025. If Russian forces establish mapped presence very close to Toretsk's city boundary, that would be strong evidence that an entry into Toretsk is becoming more likely in the final days of December.

Toretsk is in Donetsk Oblast and remains a focal point of Russian offensive efforts in eastern Ukraine. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) publishes a daily map and control layers that are also used by the ultimate question for resolution: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 . Because the ultimate market already relies on ISW map shading, a subquestion using the same map but a different geographic condition can provide an informative early signal while avoiding being merely the same question with an earlier deadline.

Recent reporting and analyst commentary indicate that Russia's 2025 advances in Ukraine have generally been incremental, attritional, and often based on infiltration tactics rather than rapid mechanized breakthroughs. ISW's August 31, 2025 assessment argued that Russian gains in 2025 were real but slower and smaller than Russian official claims, describing many advances as gradual and costly: https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-august-31-2025 . That matters here because a "near-boundary but not yet inside city limits" indicator may capture the kind of stepwise progression that often precedes entry into an urban area.

Open-source reporting in 2025 also noted repeated Russian use of infiltration methods, including pipeline-related approaches in other sectors, underscoring that Russian presence can appear first on the outskirts or in adjacent zones before a clearer urban penetration is mapped. See OilPrice.com's September 19, 2025 report summarizing such tactics near Avdiivka, Sudzha, and Kupyansk: https://oilprice.com/Geopolitics/International/Russia-Leverages-Unused-Pipelines-To-Gain-Ground-in-Ukraine.html .

The 5-kilometer threshold is intended to be close enough to matter militarily for Toretsk while still being distinct from the ultimate question, which asks whether Russia enters Toretsk itself. A positive resolution here would imply that Russian forces reached the immediate approaches to the city, increasing the probability of a subsequent mapped entry before year-end.

Sources:
ISW Ukraine map (control layers): https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 31, 2025: https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-august-31-2025
OilPrice.com, Russia Leverages Unused Pipelines To Gain Ground in Ukraine: https://oilprice.com/Geopolitics/International/Russia-Leverages-Unused-Pipelines-To-Gain-Ground-in-Ukraine.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-28 inclusive, the ISW Ukraine map at https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 shows any continuous shading corresponding to any of the following layers in an area that is (a) outside Toretsk city territory and (b) within 5.0 kilometers of the administrative boundary of Toretsk city: "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", "Assessed Russian Control", "Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine", or "Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours."

As with the ultimate market, a qualifying map change must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, the shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published. Temporary glitches or obvious map errors do not count.

For this subquestion, "Toretsk city territory" means the mapped administrative area of Toretsk as represented on standard publicly available map basemaps used with the ISW map. If any qualifying Russian shading lies partly inside Toretsk itself, that does NOT count for this subquestion, because the event must be outside the city boundary. If qualifying Russian shading lies outside the city boundary and any part of that shaded area is within 5.0 km straight-line distance of the city boundary, it counts.

Primary source for the military-control overlay is the ISW map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 . Distance and city-boundary checks should be made using the map's basemap and, if needed, corroborated using OpenStreetMap or Google Maps measuring tools: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ and https://www.google.com/maps .

If the ISW map becomes permanently unavailable before resolution, DeepStateMap may be used as a fallback for locating Russian-controlled/contested advances near Toretsk: https://deepstatemap.live/ . If both are permanently unavailable, the question should resolve based on a consensus of credible open-source mapping/reporting. If the available evidence does not allow a confident determination of whether qualifying Russian shading was outside Toretsk yet within 5 km of its boundary during the window from 2025-11-28 to 2025-12-28 inclusive, the question should be considered unresolvable.

This question resolves No if no qualifying event occurs in the window from 2025-11-28 to 2025-12-28 inclusive.
subquestions.rationale: Reaching the immediate approaches to Toretsk without yet entering the city is a classic leading indicator for an eventual urban entry. It is distinct from the ultimate question because it concerns proximity outside the city rather than control of any part of Toretsk itself. If this resolves Yes, forecasters should update upward on the chance that Russia enters Toretsk by December 31.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: ISW map shows Russian control/gains/advance/infiltration shading in an area (a) outside Toretsk city territory and (b) within 5.0 km of Toretsk's administrative boundary, between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-28, persisting through next ISW update cycle.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: 'Russian advance Toretsk area December 2025 ISW'; 'Toretsk frontline Russian control gains Ukraine map 2025'; 'Toretsk surroundings Druzhba Kostiantynivka November December 2025'; 'ISW Toretsk Russian gains infiltration December 2025'; 'Toretsk Pivnichne Zalizne Kurdiumivka 2025'; 'Toretsk captured fall Russian control 2025'; 'Toretsk battle status front line December 2025 ISW'; 'Toretsk Kostiantynivka front Russian gains south'; 'ISW assessment Kostiantynivka Toretsk surroundings'; 'near Toretsk Russian advance settlement village'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key candidate events: (1) ReliefWeb (Nov 8-14, 2025): 'one near Toretsk in Donetsk' village captured; (2) Oct 2025 General Staff reports show Toretsk sector attacks near Shcherbynivka, Pleshchiivka, Rusyn Yar, Poltavka - settlements adjacent to Toretsk; (3) Meduza Dec 12: Russian forces tightening encirclement of Kostiantynivka, with advances near settlements in the Toretsk area; (4) Dec 26: Ukrainian Border Guards destroying Russian equipment 'in Toretsk direction'; (5) RT ranks Toretsk as a Russian victory in 2025. Multiple sources indicate Toretsk itself was largely captured before/during the window, with Russian forces advancing further toward Kostiantynivka through surrounding areas.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The evidence strongly supports Russian shading outside Toretsk's boundary within 5km during the window. By late 2025, Toretsk was largely under Russian control (listed as Russian victory); fighting continued in the 'Toretsk direction' as of Dec 26. Settlements like Shcherbynivka, Rusyn Yar, Pleshchiivka - all mentioned in Ukrainian General Staff reports as attack points in the Kostiantynivka sector - are within or near the 5km zone of Toretsk. The ISW map would show Russian control shading in these surrounding areas. [Sources: reliefweb.int/report/ukraine/ukraine-war-situation-update-8-14-november-2025; charter97.org/en/news/2025/12/26/667874/; ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/4066241; rt.com/russia/629974]
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The window starts 2025-11-28. The Nov 8-14 situation report mentions a village near Toretsk was captured before the window opened. The ongoing Toretsk direction activity persisted throughout the window (confirmed Dec 26, 2025). Russian shading around Toretsk on ISW map would have been present from at least 2025-11-28 onward.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Given that Toretsk city was being fought over throughout 2025 and Russian forces were making gains in surrounding villages before the question window, Russian control shading outside-but-near Toretsk's boundary on the ISW map would have existed well before and throughout the window. No evidence contradicts this.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradiction check: Some Ukrainian sources claim resistance in the Toretsk direction, but these are consistent with Ukrainian defense of remaining pockets, not absence of Russian control in surrounding areas. The RT ranking of Toretsk as one of Russia's top battles of 2025 (already concluded by Dec 2025) and continued 'Toretsk direction' operations suggest the surrounding area shows Russian control on ISW map. The Meduza and other sources confirm encirclement dynamics around Kostiantynivka through Toretsk.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Yes. The preponderance of evidence indicates that during 2025-11-28 to 2025-12-28, ISW's map would have shown Russian control/gains in areas outside but within 5km of Toretsk's administrative boundary. Toretsk had been progressively captured throughout 2025; settlements adjacent to it (Shcherbynivka, Rusyn Yar, Pleshchiivka) were under active Russian assault and Russian control by this period. The Phoenix unit report from Dec 26 confirms ongoing Russian offensive operations in the Toretsk direction. This satisfies the resolution criteria.

question: Will Elon and DOGE cut 100-150k employees in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve based on the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) under the "All Employees, Federal" series (CES9091000001), displayed here (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001)

This market will resolve according to the decrease in the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees between the December 2024 report and the December 2025 report.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The difference will be calculated as the December 2024 value minus the December 2025 value.

The December 2024 figure will be based on the initial December 2024 BLS Employment Situation report scheduled for release on January 3, 2025, and the initial December 2025 figure will be based on the report scheduled for release on January 9, 2026. Revisions made to these figures will not be considered, only the values reported in the initial reports will be used.

The resolution source will be the BLS Employment Situation data, specifically the series CES9091000001, available at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 or the official BLS website.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Office of Personnel Management report that at least 75,000 federal civilian employees submitted deferred resignation offers or equivalent voluntary separation agreements between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30?
subquestions.background_information:
A large 2025 decline in the BLS 'All Employees, Federal' series would likely require either substantial involuntary layoffs, a large wave of buyouts/deferred resignations, or both. A near-term indicator is whether the federal government publicly reports a very large number of accepted or submitted voluntary separation offers. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is the central HR agency for the federal civilian workforce and has published governmentwide civilian employment statistics in FedScope; as of recent years, the federal civilian executive-branch workforce has been a bit above 2 million employees, so 75,000 separations would be roughly 3%+ of the workforce and therefore material for the ultimate 100k-150k cut question. See OPM FedScope employment cubes and status data: https://www.opm.gov/data/datasets/ and https://www.fedscope.opm.gov/. The ultimate market resolves using BLS series CES9091000001 ('All Employees, Federal'), available via FRED at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 and originally sourced from BLS CES. Because the final December 2025 BLS number is not available until January 2026, an official late-2025 count of voluntary federal departures is a useful leading indicator. If DOGE/Elon-driven cuts are truly on pace to reach 100k-150k by year-end, one plausible path is a very large, publicly acknowledged wave of resignations, buyouts, or deferred resignations before the end of December. Recent broader labor-data context also points to elevated uncertainty around payroll measurement and revisions, making direct personnel-action indicators more informative than extrapolating from payroll series alone. The BLS announced a preliminary benchmark revision of -911,000 jobs for the year through March 2025, underscoring data uncertainty in labor-market estimates: https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesprelbmk.htm.

Sources:
OPM Data, Analysis & Documentation Hub — https://www.opm.gov/data/datasets/
OPM FedScope — https://www.fedscope.opm.gov/
FRED: All Employees, Federal (CES9091000001) — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001
BLS Preliminary Benchmark Revision for CES — https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesprelbmk.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30 (inclusive), the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) publicly states in an official press release, official blog post, official memo posted on an official .gov website, or official testimony/document that at least 75,000 federal civilian employees submitted deferred resignation offers, accepted buyouts, or entered equivalent voluntary separation agreements under a governmentwide program during that same window or cumulatively by a date within that window.

Primary resolution sources are official OPM web pages and press releases at https://www.opm.gov/ and https://www.opm.gov/news/. If OPM publishes the figure in an official memorandum or guidance document, that also counts, provided it is hosted on an official U.S. government website ending in .gov.

The count must explicitly refer to federal civilian employees or federal workers in a way that is governmentwide or clearly broad enough to be relevant to the federal civilian workforce. Purely agency-specific figures do not count unless OPM or another official U.S. government source explicitly states they sum to at least 75,000 governmentwide. Media reports alone do not suffice unless they directly quote or reproduce an official OPM or other U.S. government source document containing the figure.

Equivalent voluntary separation agreements include programs explicitly described as deferred resignation, voluntary separation incentive payments (buyouts), or other opt-in separation programs. Involuntary layoffs, terminations, or reductions in force do not count toward this question unless the official source explicitly includes them within the reported voluntary-separation total.

If multiple official figures are published within the window, the highest clearly stated qualifying total published between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30 is used. If no qualifying official figure of at least 75,000 is published within that window, resolve No.

If an official source later retracts a figure before 2025-12-30 and replaces it with a lower figure below 75,000, the corrected figure governs. If all relevant official publications are removed and no archived official copy is available, resolver should use the Internet Archive version of the official page, if available: https://web.archive.org/. If no official or archived official source can establish the figure, resolve No rather than using unsourced media estimates.
subquestions.rationale: A very large reported wave of voluntary federal departures by late December would be strong evidence that the government is on track to post a 100k-150k year-over-year drop in federal employment in the December 2025 BLS data. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question because it tracks a different mechanism—voluntary separation program uptake—rather than the final BLS employment level itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: OPM must officially state (in a press release, blog post, memo, or testimony on an official .gov website) that ≥75,000 federal civilian employees submitted deferred resignation offers or equivalent voluntary separation agreements under a governmentwide program, within the window 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-30. Key entities: OPM, federal civilian workforce. Threshold: 75,000+ governmentwide voluntary separations. Timing: report published within window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'OPM Office of Personnel Management federal employees deferred resignation voluntary separation 75000' (Nov 30–Dec 30 2025) — to find official reports; 2) 'OPM Scott Kupor 317000 federal employees voluntary separation press release December 2025' (Nov 30–Dec 30 2025) — to find official sources; 3) 'OPM official press release deferred resignation 75000 voluntary separation December 2025' (Nov 30–Dec 30 2025) — targeted at official publications; 4) 'OPM.gov official blog post 317000 federal employees voluntary separation December 2025' — targeted at .gov sources; 5) '"deferred resignation" 144000 OR 75000 federal employees OPM official 2025' — to find specific figures
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple news articles from around December 10, 2025 report that OPM/OPM Director Scott Kupor stated approximately 144,000 federal employees opted for the deferred resignation program and ~317,000 total employees left. The figure of 144,000 well exceeds 75,000. Bloomberg Law (Dec 10) reports the OPM Director stated these on 'X (formerly Twitter).' Government Executive (Dec 10) reports OPM 'reported' these figures. ArcaMax (Dec 10) cites OPM Director Kupor. FedSmith (Dec 12) states Kupor anticipates ~300,000 would leave with 75-80% through buyout programs. However, these are all media-reported figures from social media and spokesperson statements — NOT from an identified official OPM.gov press release, blog post, or memo.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires an official OPM publication on a .gov website. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/daily-labor-report/federal-workforces-toll-after-a-year-of-doge-and-trump-317-000) states the OPM Director made statements 'on X (formerly Twitter)' — this is not a .gov publication. [Government Executive](https://www.govexec.com/workforce/2025/12/opm-says-92-fed-departures-year-were-voluntary-those-who-left-disagree/410076/) reports OPM statements but doesn't cite a specific .gov document. [ArcaMax](https://www.arcamax.com/business/businessnews/s-3948367) cites OPM Director Kupor but again through media reporting. None of the articles confirm the figures were published in an official OPM press release, blog post, or memo on opm.gov. The criteria explicitly states 'Media reports alone do not suffice unless they directly quote or reproduce an official OPM or other U.S. government source document containing the figure.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Media reports about these figures were published on December 10, 2025 (Bloomberg Law, Government Executive, ArcaMax). If official .gov sources existed, they would likely have been published on or before December 10, 2025. However, no .gov URL containing the qualifying figure was identified in any source.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying .gov publication found. The question is whether any qualifying .gov publication exists at all within the window — and the evidence does not confirm one.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove by searching for contradictory evidence (e.g., that OPM denied figures, retracted them, or published a lower figure). No retraction found. However, the fundamental problem remains: the available evidence shows these figures were communicated via social media (X) and media statements, not via official OPM.gov publications. The FedSmith article quotes Kupor's expectations (75-80% of 300,000 through buyout = 225,000-240,000) but again this is referenced through a secondary source. The resolution criteria specifically requires a .gov-hosted official document.
evidence.step8_final_decision: While there is strong evidence that OPM communicated figures well exceeding 75,000 deferred resignations (approximately 144,000 per multiple media sources citing OPM Director Kupor) during the window, the strict resolution criteria requires an official OPM publication on a .gov website — not media reports or social media posts. No evidence was found of an official OPM.gov press release, blog post, or memo containing the qualifying figure of ≥75,000 voluntary/deferred separation agreements published within the window 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-30. Since the criteria cannot be verified as met, and all available evidence fails to produce a direct .gov source, the question resolves No.

question: Pakistan strike on India by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Pakistan initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Indian territory by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Pakistani military forces that impact Indian territory (e.g., if a Pakistani missile or drone hits a target within India’s borders, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted before reaching Indian territory, as well as surface-to-air missile strikes, will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether debris lands on Indian soil or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or any operation conducted by Pakistani ground forces will not qualify as a strike under this market.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will India publicly announce between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 (inclusive) that it has intercepted or shot down at least 10 Pakistani military drones in Indian airspace or over Indian territory since 2025-10-15?
subquestions.background_information:
A renewed burst of Pakistani drone activity would be a meaningful early-warning indicator for the ultimate question, because the May 2025 crisis appears to have escalated from drone and missile attacks into broader cross-border strikes before a halt in military operations was announced. Multiple reports from May 2025 describe Pakistan launching drones and missiles toward Indian targets across several states, with India claiming many were intercepted. For example, India's Ministry of Defence said Pakistani-origin drones and missiles targeted military stations at Jammu, Pathankot and Udhampur on May 8, 2025, and that the threats were neutralised; Firstpost quoted the ministry on this point: https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/how-india-foiled-pakistans-overnight-air-attacks-with-advanced-defence-systems-and-blackouts-13888474.html . India Today reported on May 10, 2025 that Pakistan targeted 26 locations and that debris was recovered in Sirsa, Barmer, and Jalandhar: https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/pakistan-strikes-missile-debris-found-in-haryana-rajasthan-punjab-2722846-2025-05-10 . News18 likewise reported Pakistani drone incursions across 26 locations and repeated Indian interceptions: https://www.news18.com/india/indian-army-razes-terrorist-launchpads-near-loc-in-response-to-pak-drone-strikes-video-9350516.html .

The ultimate market only resolves Yes on a Pakistani drone, missile, or air strike that actually impacts Indian territory. But before such a qualifying strike occurs, a visible precursor could be a sharp rise in attempted Pakistani drone penetrations. If India is publicly reporting double-digit military drone interceptions over a one-month period, that would suggest a materially worsened cross-border aerial posture and increase the odds of eventual leakage or escalation to a successful strike before year-end. Conversely, continued absence of such reports would be some evidence against imminent aerial escalation.

This subquestion is not just the main question with a shorter deadline: it tracks attempted Pakistani aerial activity that falls short of the ultimate market's impact requirement. It therefore serves as an operational indicator of escalation pressure rather than a restatement of the end event.

Sources:
Firstpost - How India foiled Pakistan's overnight air attacks with advanced defence systems and blackouts - https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/how-india-foiled-pakistans-overnight-air-attacks-with-advanced-defence-systems-and-blackouts-13888474.html
India Today - Missile Debris Found in Indian Border States Following Pakistani Strikes - https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/pakistan-strikes-missile-debris-found-in-haryana-rajasthan-punjab-2722846-2025-05-10
News18 - Indian Army Razes Terrorist Launchpads Near LoC In Response To Pak Drone Strikes - https://www.news18.com/india/indian-army-razes-terrorist-launchpads-near-loc-in-response-to-pak-drone-strikes-video-9350516.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 inclusive, the Government of India, Indian Armed Forces, Indian Ministry of Defence, or a named senior Indian official speaking in an official briefing or statement publicly announces that at least 10 Pakistani military drones have been intercepted, neutralised, or shot down in Indian airspace or over Indian territory since 2025-10-15.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement is made by 2025-11-14 23:59:59 UTC.

For resolution, the count must refer to Pakistani drones attributable to Pakistani military forces or official Pakistani cross-border military activity; purely civilian quadcopters, smuggling drones, hobby drones, or unattributed UAV incidents do not count. The announcement may aggregate incidents across multiple days within the window, but all counted interceptions must have occurred between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 inclusive. Statements that only say drones were "spotted" or "detected" do not count unless they also say they were intercepted, neutralised, or shot down. If India announces a lower bound such as "more than 10" or "at least 10," that counts. If multiple official statements conflict, the latest official clarification by 2025-11-14 23:59:59 UTC governs.

Primary sources for resolution: official releases from the Press Information Bureau of India (https://pib.gov.in/), the Indian Ministry of Defence (https://mod.gov.in/), and official Indian Army / Indian Air Force / HQ IDS accounts or websites, including https://indianarmy.nic.in/ and https://indianairforce.nic.in/ . Secondary confirmation may come from Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/india/), AP (https://apnews.com/hub/india), or BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news/world/asia/india) if they directly quote the official Indian announcement. If no official source is archived but multiple major wire services quote the same official statement, that is sufficient.

If by the end date there is no clear public official statement meeting the threshold, resolve No. If reporting is too ambiguous to determine whether the threshold of 10 military drones was met within the stated window, resolve No rather than extrapolating.
subquestions.rationale: A surge in officially acknowledged Pakistani drone interceptions would indicate renewed cross-border aerial operations and heightened escalation risk. That would increase the chance that, before the ultimate market deadline, at least one Pakistani drone or missile penetrates defenses and impacts Indian territory, satisfying the main market.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: An official Indian government announcement (from PIB, Indian MoD, Indian Army, IAF, or named senior Indian official in official briefing) publicly stating that AT LEAST 10 Pakistani MILITARY drones were intercepted/neutralized/shot down in Indian airspace or over Indian territory, with all 10+ interceptions occurring BETWEEN 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 inclusive. Purely civilian/smuggling/hobby drones explicitly excluded. The announcement must occur within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'India intercept shoot down Pakistani military drones 2025' (Oct15-Nov14) — to find qualifying events; 2. 'India Pakistan drone interception announcement October November 2025' — to find official statements; 3. 'India official announcement 10 Pakistani military drones intercepted shot down October November 2025' — threshold-specific search; 4. 'India Ministry Defence Indian Army drones Pakistan military cross-border intrusion October 2025' — official source search; 5. 'India PIB MOD Indian Air Force Army drone intercept Pakistan military November 2025' — official source search; 6. 'Pakistan drone attack India Indian airspace shoot down October November 2025 official statement' — alternative formulation; 7. 'India official statement Pakistan military drone interception 10 drones October 2025' — threshold search; 8. 'India armed forces Pakistan UAV neutralized destroyed Indian airspace November 2025' — alternative wording search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found and assessed: (A) BSF neutralized 3 Pak drones on Oct 24 (Times of India) — DJI Mavic consumer drones used for drug smuggling, excluded per criteria. (B) BSF foiled drone-based smuggling attempts Oct 18, recovered multiple drones — civilian smuggling drones, excluded. (C) BSF reported 200 drones intercepted year-to-date as of Oct 15 — all smuggling/civilian drones, excluded, and the year-to-date count predates the window. (D) India Army references to '50 drones neutralized' and 'over 300 aerial threats intercepted during Operation Sindoor' — all refer to May 2025 conflict, outside the window. (E) Various BSF drug-drone interceptions Oct 26-Nov 5 — all civilian/smuggling drones, excluded. NO events found of official Indian announcement of 10+ Pakistani military drones intercepted within the Oct 15 – Nov 14 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article or source confirms an official Indian government announcement (from PIB, Indian MoD, Indian Army/IAF) of 10 or more Pakistani MILITARY drone interceptions in the window Oct 15–Nov 14, 2025. [Times of India, Oct 24](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chandigarh/bsf-neutralises-3-pak-drones/articleshow/124790168.cms) reports BSF neutralizing 3 Pak drones, but these are DJI Mavic commercial drones used for drug smuggling — explicitly excluded. [Hindustan Times, Oct 15](https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/chandigarh-news/bsf-seized-200-drones-287-kg-heroin-along-indo-pak-border-so-far-this-year-101760471748858.html) mentions 200 drones seized year-to-date, but all are smuggling drones and the count is prior to the window's start. [RT.com, Nov 6](https://www.rt.com/india/627429-india-army-chief-combat-drones/) references 300+ aerial threats intercepted during Operation Sindoor (May 2025), not within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found; timestamp extraction is moot. The window closes at 2025-11-14T23:59:59Z with no qualifying announcement found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence found at all within the window. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists because no qualifying occurrence exists at any point in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for: (1) Large-scale military drone attacks by Pakistan on India during Oct-Nov 2025 — none found; (2) Any official Indian statement about Pakistani military drone interceptions in this period — none found; (3) Contradictory evidence suggesting such announcements were made but suppressed — none found. The period was characterized by military exercises (Trishul, Thar Shakti) and post-Operation Sindoor rhetoric, but no active military drone exchange. The India-Pakistan ceasefire from May 10, 2025 appears to have held during this window with respect to military drone operations.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying event occurred within the window. India did not publicly announce intercepting 10+ Pakistani military drones between Oct 15–Nov 14, 2025. Drone interceptions during this period were of civilian/smuggling DJI consumer drones, which are explicitly excluded from the criteria. The only references to large-scale Pakistani military drone interceptions by India date back to Operation Sindoor in May 2025. Resolution: No. Since no qualifying announcement was ever made during the window and the window has now closed (end date Nov 14, 2025), the resolution datetime is 2025-11-14T23:59:59Z.

question: Clarity Act signed into law in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R.3633) is passed by both chambers of the U.S. Congress and signed into law by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source is Congress.gov’s legislation tracker (https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633) and other official information from the government of the United States, however other credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee hold a hearing or executive business meeting between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 at which the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R. 3633) or a Senate market-structure bill explicitly described as CLARITY-related is listed on the official agenda?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R. 3633) is signed into law by the end of 2025. As of late August 2025, the House has already passed H.R. 3633, so the key bottleneck is Senate action and then reconciliation/final passage. Congress.gov shows H.R. 3633 in the 119th Congress and is the authoritative tracker for the bill: https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633 . Reporting in July and August indicates that the Senate is the next major hurdle. JD Supra reported on July 30 that the CLARITY Act was 'currently being considered by the Senate Banking and Agriculture Committees,' with leadership aiming to finalize it by October: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/blockchain-and-digital-assets-news-and-3470180/ . Cryptonews reported on August 29 that Senator Cynthia Lummis said she hoped the bill would move through the Senate Banking Committee in September and Agriculture in October: https://cryptonews.com/news/clarity-act-has-35-chance-of-passing-in-2025-polymarket/ .

A formal Senate Banking Committee hearing or markup that specifically places CLARITY-related market-structure legislation on the agenda would be a meaningful near-term indicator because it signals the Senate is devoting scarce committee time to advancing the issue. This is not the same as asking whether the bill becomes law by an earlier date; rather, it tracks whether one of the most important procedural prerequisites is actually happening on schedule. If no such Banking Committee event occurs by October 1, that would be evidence against year-end enactment, given the limited legislative calendar and the need for subsequent Agriculture Committee, floor, and bicameral steps.

The Senate Banking Committee publishes official hearing and executive session notices on its website: https://www.banking.senate.gov/ . Committee activity is also often reflected in press releases and archived event pages. Congress.gov provides official bill status but may lag intraday committee scheduling details, so the committee website is the best primary source for this subquestion.

Sources:
Congress.gov – H.R. 3633: https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633
Senate Banking Committee website: https://www.banking.senate.gov/
JD Supra, Blockchain and Digital Assets News and Trends - July 2025: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/blockchain-and-digital-assets-news-and-3470180/
Cryptonews, CLARITY Act Has 35% Chance Of Passing In 2025: https://cryptonews.com/news/clarity-act-has-35-chance-of-passing-in-2025-polymarket/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the official website of the U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs posts an official hearing notice, hearing page, executive session notice, markup notice, or meeting agenda showing that during that window the committee held or scheduled a hearing or executive business meeting in which either (a) 'H.R. 3633', 'Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025', or 'CLARITY Act' is explicitly named, or (b) a Senate digital-asset market-structure bill/draft is explicitly described on the official agenda or official committee materials as CLARITY-related, a market-structure framework corresponding to H.R. 3633, or substantially the same legislative vehicle under Senate consideration.

Primary source: official Senate Banking Committee pages at https://www.banking.senate.gov/ . Relevant evidence may include hearing pages, executive session pages, press releases, or posted agendas on that site.

Secondary/fallback source: if the committee website is unavailable or pages are later removed, archived copies from the U.S. Senate domain or contemporaneous official committee press releases on the same domain may be used. Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/) may be used as corroboration but not as a substitute for an official committee posting if the issue is whether a hearing/meeting was officially scheduled or held.

This question resolves No if no such official Banking Committee event is posted and held/scheduled within the window from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 inclusive.

Edge cases:
- A generic crypto hearing counts only if the official agenda explicitly names H.R. 3633, the CLARITY Act, or clearly identifies the agenda item as the Senate's CLARITY-related market-structure legislation.
- Mere public statements by senators, media reports, or unofficial calendars do not count without an official Senate Banking Committee source.
- If an event is announced within the window but scheduled for after 2025-10-01, it does not count.
- If an event begins before 2025-10-01 but is postponed beyond 2025-10-01 before occurring, it does not count and should be treated as No unless another qualifying event occurs within the window.
- If available official evidence is contradictory and no authoritative committee record clarifies whether a qualifying event occurred in the window, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Resolution sources:
U.S. Senate Banking Committee: https://www.banking.senate.gov/
Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/
subquestions.rationale: Senate Banking Committee action is a central bottleneck for crypto market-structure legislation. A formal hearing or markup on CLARITY-related legislation by October 1 would be strong evidence that the Senate is on a timeline compatible with year-end enactment; failure to reach even this committee-stage milestone by then would materially weaken the case for the bill being signed into law in 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the official Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee website must post an official hearing notice/agenda/executive session showing a hearing or executive business meeting was held or scheduled in that window, with H.R. 3633, 'Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025', 'CLARITY Act', or a Senate market-structure bill explicitly described as CLARITY-related explicitly named on the official agenda. Key entities: Senate Banking Committee (not Finance or Agriculture), official website banking.senate.gov, window Sept 1–Oct 1 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Senate Banking Committee Digital Asset Market Clarity Act H.R. 3633 hearing 2025' (Sept-Oct 2025) — to find any official Banking Committee hearing on CLARITY Act; 2) 'Senate Banking Committee CLARITY Act crypto market structure hearing September 2025' — to find any official Banking hearing; 3) 'Senate Banking Committee markup vote September 30 crypto market structure bill' — to check if the planned markup occurred; 4) 'Senate Banking Committee executive session hearing agenda CLARITY Act September October 2025' — to find any official agenda posting; 5) 'Senate Banking Committee September 30 markup postponed canceled CLARITY crypto' — to confirm the markup did not happen; 6) 'Senate Banking Committee hearing official agenda digital asset October 2025' — to find any last-minute official hearing.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Senate Banking Committee roundtable on Sept 17, 2025 (Charles Hoskinson attended) — REJECTED: This was a private/informal industry roundtable, not an official hearing or executive business meeting with an official agenda; (B) Planned Senate Banking Committee markup by Sept 30 — REJECTED: Multiple sources confirm this was postponed to the week of October 20, never occurred within window; (C) Senate Finance Committee hearing on October 1 on digital asset taxation — REJECTED: Wrong committee (Finance, not Banking), and focused on taxation, not CLARITY Act market structure. No qualifying event found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that exactly satisfies: (a) held by Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee; (b) in the Sept 1–Oct 1 window; (c) officially scheduled AND held; (d) with H.R. 3633, CLARITY Act, or CLARITY-related market structure bill explicitly on the official agenda. The planned September 30 markup was confirmed postponed to October by multiple sources including [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/news-analysis/2025/09/27/state-of-crypto-shutdown-watch), [Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-government-shutdown-digital-asset-market-structure), [FXEmpire](https://www.fxempire.com/forecasts/article/xrp-news-today-blackrock-catalyst-vs-senate-delays-influence-outlook-1550397), and [CoinDesk Sept 30](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/09/30/bitcoin-steady-but-bitfinex-warns-of-downside-risks-as-government-shutdown-looms). The Forbes article from Oct 4 ([Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jasonbrett/2025/10/03/full-steam-ahead-lummis-drives-crypto-market-structure-amid-shutdown/)) confirms no markup occurred before the government shutdown on Sept 30.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The September 30 markup was definitively reported as postponed before it could occur. Multiple articles dated September 24–30 confirm it was pushed to the week of October 20. No official Banking Committee hearing/session with CLARITY Act agenda was held within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying earlier occurrence found within the September 1–October 1 window. The September 17 roundtable does not qualify (not official, no official agenda). No other official Banking Committee hearing on market structure/CLARITY Act was identified.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The Senate Finance Committee hearing on October 1 was initially confusing, but this is confirmed to be the Finance Committee (tax focus), not the Banking Committee (market structure/CLARITY focus). No contradictory evidence suggests a Banking Committee hearing actually occurred. The government shutdown beginning at midnight Sept 30/Oct 1 further confirms no Banking Committee markup occurred within the window. The Forbes Oct 4 article confirms legislative work on market structure was ongoing but no committee action had been taken — still 'full steam ahead' but no completed markup.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. The Senate Banking Committee planned a markup for September 30, 2025, on a market-structure bill explicitly described as building on the CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633), but this was postponed to the week of October 20 before it could occur. No official Banking Committee hearing, executive session, or markup was held or officially scheduled within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window with H.R. 3633, 'CLARITY Act', or CLARITY-related market structure explicitly on the official agenda. The window closed with no qualifying event.

subquestions.question: Will the MrBeast YouTube channel gain at least 8 million subscribers between 2025-09-12 and 2025-10-12?
subquestions.background_information:

As of early September 2025, multiple outlets reported MrBeast at roughly 430-431 million subscribers, including 430 million on September 3, 2025 (Benzinga: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/09/47269708/mrbeast-could-be-the-next-celebrity-to-turn-a-phone-into-a-fortune-t-mobile-us-nasdaq-tmus-amazon-com-nasdaq-amzn) and 431 million on September 5, 2025 (Yahoo Finance syndication: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/youtube-star-mrbeast-reportedly-wants-132616425.html). SocialBlade provides a widely used public tracker for YouTube subscriber counts and recent gains for major channels, including MrBeast's channel page (https://socialblade.com/youtube/c/mrbeast6000). If MrBeast adds 8+ million subscribers over this 30-day window, that would be evidence that the 500 million threshold by late 2025 is materially more reachable; if growth is much slower, the subscriber leg of the ultimate market becomes less likely to flip the outcome.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

subquestions.question: Will Romania's Ministry of National Defence report at least one new drone or missile incursion into Romanian airspace attributed to the war in Ukraine between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29?
subquestions.background_information:
Romania is one of the most plausible locations for another NATO downing of a Russian drone because it sits directly on Ukraine's southwestern border and has already experienced repeated cross-border drone incidents. Reuters reported on November 25, 2025 that Romanian and German NATO jets were scrambled after two Russian drones breached Romanian airspace, with one flying more than 100 km inland; Defence Minister Ionut Mosteanu said Romania had legal authority to shoot down such drones in peacetime under some conditions, though it did not do so in that case. Reuters also noted this was the 13th such breach since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began. See: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/romania-scrambles-nato-jets-after-deepest-ever-drone-incursion-calls-it-2025-11-25/ 

AP similarly reported a broader pattern of suspicious drone activity and confirmed that on September 10, 2025, Russian drones entered Polish airspace and some were shot down by NATO aircraft, demonstrating that airspace incursions can escalate to direct NATO countermeasures. See: https://apnews.com/ 

A fresh Romanian incursion during the subquestion window would be a strong leading indicator for the ultimate question because Romania has recently been the most active eastern-flank venue for such incidents, and another incursion would create another opportunity for NATO forces already on alert to engage. Romania's defence ministry publishes incident statements on its official website, which is an authoritative primary source for whether a qualifying new incursion was officially reported. See: https://english.mapn.ro/ 

Sources:
Reuters - Romania scrambles NATO jets after deepest-ever drone incursion, calls it Russian provocation - https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/romania-scrambles-nato-jets-after-deepest-ever-drone-incursion-calls-it-2025-11-25/
Romania Ministry of National Defence (English) - https://english.mapn.ro/
AP News - Mysterious drone flights in NATO airspace have caused alarm across Europe. Here's what we know - https://apnews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Romania's Ministry of National Defence (MAPN), in an official statement published between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 inclusive, reports at least one new incursion into Romanian airspace by a drone, UAV, missile, or similar aerial object explicitly linked to or occurring in the context of Russia's war against Ukraine. The publication date of the official MAPN statement must fall within the window from 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-29 inclusive.

Primary source: official MAPN news releases at https://english.mapn.ro/ or the Romanian-language site https://www.mapn.ro/ .

A report counts if it describes a distinct incident newly announced during the window; updates during the window about an incident first officially announced before 2025-11-30 do not count.

The question resolves No if no such qualifying official MAPN statement is published between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 inclusive.

If MAPN's site is unavailable, fallback sources are official Romanian government or presidency statements and then at least two consistent reports from major international wire services such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) or AP (https://apnews.com/) clearly attributing the incident report to Romanian defence authorities.

If available information is insufficient to determine whether a distinct new official Romanian report occurred within the stated window, resolve Unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Another official Romanian airspace incursion report would materially increase the chance of the ultimate outcome by creating a fresh, geographically plausible opportunity for NATO forces to down a Russian drone before year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official MAPN statement published 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-29 reporting a new drone/missile incursion into Romanian airspace linked to Russia's war against Ukraine. Observable evidence: MAPN press release describing an airspace breach; fallback: consistent major wire service reports attributing the report to Romanian defence authorities.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Romania Ministry Defence drone missile airspace incursion Ukraine 2025' (Nov30-Dec29); 2) 'Romania MAPN airspace violation drone December 2025'; 3) 'Romania airspace drone incursion November 25 2025 Gerbera'; 4) 'Romania drone found forest December 2025 MAPN official statement'; 5) 'Romania MAPN drone airspace incursion December 2025 official statement'; 6) 'Romania drone airspace November 30 December 2025 MAPN statement Reuters AP'; 7) 'Romania airspace violation drone incursion December 2025 RFERL fighter jets'; 8) 'Romanian airspace drone December 2025 violation incursion new'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Nov 25, 2025: Two Romanian airspace violations (#12 and #13), MAPN confirmed — REJECTED as before resolution window. (B) RFERL Dec 11 article references 'recent drone incursions into Romanian airspace' prompting jets in December 2025 — ambiguous, likely refers to Nov 25 events reported in early December. (C) Dec 21, 2025: Drone found in Romanian forest (Argeș County) — not attributed to Russia/Ukraine war by Romanian authorities; under investigation. (D) Dec 23, 2025: MAPN reported drone activity near border but explicitly confirmed NO airspace violations. (E) Dec 26, 2025: MAPN reported drone detection but explicitly confirmed NO unauthorized intrusions into Romanian airspace. (F) Express article Dec 26 cites MAPN: 'airspace violations have occurred 13 times' total since war start — same as count after Nov 25 event, confirming no new violations within window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The December 26 Express article [https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/2150622/ww3-fears-explode-nato-scrambles] cites Romanian Ministry of National Defence: 'airspace violations have occurred 13 times' since the war began — this total matches the November 25 count (13th violation). MAPN statements from Dec 23 [http://actmedia.eu/daily/new-drone-attacks-in-ukraine-near-border-with-romania-ro-alert-message-sent-to-population/117411] and Dec 26 [https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/12/26/8013481/] both explicitly confirm NO unauthorized intrusions into Romanian airspace. The RFERL Dec 11 reference to 'recent drone incursions' in 'December 2025' is ambiguous and may reflect reporting lag on Nov 25 events.

Romanian President Dan's Dec 22 statement that drones 'entering Romania's airspace pose no threat' could be interpreted as acknowledging ongoing entries, but this is not a specific MAPN incident report and is ambiguous.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All available evidence indicates no new qualifying MAPN official statement was published within the Nov 30 - Dec 29 window reporting a new Romanian airspace incursion. The total violation count remained at 13 as of Dec 26. Multiple MAPN statements within the window explicitly confirmed no airspace violations. The question resolves No.

subquestions.question: Will Taylor Swift or Travis Kelce publicly state or strongly imply that they are actively planning a wedding between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful indicator for the ultimate market because one of the three disqualifying conditions is that Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce marry before the end of 2025. As of the start date, the couple are widely reported to be engaged: multiple October 2025 entertainment reports say Swift discussed Kelce's proposal and referred to him as her fiancé, while reporting that she was prioritizing the album rollout before wedding planning. For example, NDTV reported on 2025-10-03 that Swift said on The Graham Norton Show that Kelce "crushed" the proposal and that "I want to do the album stuff first, and the wedding is what happens after in terms of planning" (https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/taylor-swift-on-how-travis-kelce-crushed-it-with-his-marriage-proposal-9175914). Because marriage is one of the explicit "Nothing Ever Happens" failure modes, a clear public indication that the couple are actively planning a wedding in late October or November 2025 would increase the odds of a wedding by year-end. This is meaningfully different from the ultimate question itself: it asks about wedding-planning signals, not whether a marriage actually occurs.

Sources:

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24 (inclusive), either Taylor Swift or Travis Kelce makes a public statement in a primary or widely cited secondary source that clearly indicates active wedding planning is underway. Qualifying examples include statements that they have started planning the wedding, have set or are narrowing a wedding date, have chosen or are touring venues, are working with a wedding planner, are sending invitations, or are making concrete arrangements for the ceremony.

Strong implication also counts if the report quotes one of them directly describing concrete planning steps, even without the exact words "planning the wedding." Mere references to being engaged, generic excitement about getting married, or vague future-oriented remarks such as "we'll get married someday" do NOT count. Unattributed tabloid speculation or anonymous-source-only reporting does NOT count unless it is subsequently confirmed in an on-record interview or statement by Swift or Kelce during the window.

Primary resolution sources, in order of priority, are direct interviews, official social media accounts, official podcast/video appearances, or official representatives' statements. Secondary sources may be used only to relay such direct statements. Preferred sources include Taylor Swift's official accounts (https://www.instagram.com/taylorswift/), Travis Kelce's official accounts (https://www.instagram.com/killatrav/), official New Heights content (https://www.youtube.com/@newheightshow), and transcripts or recordings from major outlets such as NBC, ABC, CBS, BBC, People, Us Weekly, or similar reputable outlets.

If no qualifying public statement or strongly implied concrete planning step is documented between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24 (inclusive), resolve No.

If an alleged qualifying statement is reported but no sufficiently reliable public record can be found, resolve based on the best available direct quote in a reputable outlet. If all evidence is ambiguous as to whether active planning was stated, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A late-2025 marriage is more plausible if the couple publicly move from engagement into concrete planning. This subquestion is an early observable indicator for the marriage branch of the ultimate market without merely restating whether they marry by year-end.

subquestions.question: Will a federal grand jury be reported by Reuters or the Associated Press as having heard evidence in the John Bolton investigation between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-14?
subquestions.background_information:
A grand-jury presentation would be a meaningful near-term indicator for whether John Bolton is federally charged soon, because federal indictments typically require either a grand-jury vote or, less commonly, an information following waiver in applicable cases. Reuters reported on 2025-09-26 that prosecutors were expected to present the Bolton case to a grand jury the following week, while noting internal DOJ disagreement over whether to move quickly. That makes actual grand-jury activity a concrete observable step distinct from the ultimate question itself and highly relevant to near-term charging odds. Reuters/KSL reported that senior DOJ leaders were urging swift charges and that prosecutors in the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office and DOJ National Security Division were resisting pressure, with one source saying prosecutors were expected to present the case to a grand jury next week: https://www.ksl.com/article/51373720/justice-department-pushing-for-swift-charges-against-bolton-people-familiar-say . Reporting on the August searches also indicates the investigation is criminal and active, with search warrants approved by a judge and public statements from senior officials signaling seriousness: Reuters via RTHK, https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1819852-20250823.htm .

This subquestion is not just an earlier version of the ultimate question: it asks whether a specific procedural milestone occurs, not whether Bolton is charged. If the investigation is presented to a grand jury by mid-October, that would materially increase the probability of a charge by the ultimate deadline; if not, it would tend to reduce it.

Sources:
KSL / Reuters - Justice Department pushing for 'swift charges' against Bolton, people familiar say - https://www.ksl.com/article/51373720/justice-department-pushing-for-swift-charges-against-bolton-people-familiar-say
RTHK / Reuters - FBI raids home and office of ex-Trump advisor Bolton - https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1819852-20250823.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-14 (inclusive), either Reuters or the Associated Press reports that a federal grand jury heard evidence, received a presentation, or otherwise considered the John Bolton criminal investigation/case for potential charges.

This question resolves No if no such Reuters or Associated Press report is published during the window from 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-14 (inclusive).

For purposes of resolution, qualifying language includes clear statements such as that prosecutors "presented the case to a grand jury," "a grand jury heard evidence," "the case went before a grand jury," or equivalent wording indicating actual grand-jury consideration during the window. Mere statements that prosecutors expect, plan, intend, or are pushing to present the case do NOT qualify. Mere mention of sealed court activity without explicit grand-jury consideration does NOT qualify.

Primary sources for resolution: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) and Associated Press (https://apnews.com/). If both publish conflicting accounts within the window, resolution should follow the later clarification/correction from the same outlet; if conflict remains unresolved, the question is unresolvable. If neither Reuters nor AP publishes on the matter during the window, it resolves No even if other outlets report it.

If a report published after 2025-10-14 states that grand-jury consideration occurred during the 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-14 window, that later report may be used to resolve Yes, provided Reuters or AP explicitly dates the grand-jury activity to within that window.

The AP report cited in [Deutsche Welle](https://www.dw.com/en/john-bolton-former-trump-national-security-advisor-indicted/a-74392911) and [Breitbart](https://www.breitbart.com/politics/2025/10/16/former-nsa-john-bolton-indicted-over-mishandling-of-classified-documents/) was also published Oct 16, outside the window. The MSNBC-attributed reporting (Oct 10-11) about the grand jury 'reviewing evidence for several weeks' is: (1) from MSNBC, not Reuters/AP; (2) describes ongoing review, not a specific dated event of evidence presentation; (3) only appears via secondary sources, not directly from Reuters/AP. None of the Reuters or AP reports found are within the Oct 1-14 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Reuters first reported on the Bolton indictment/grand jury on October 16, 2025. AP also first reported on October 16, 2025. These timestamps are outside the Oct 1-14 window. No Reuters or AP reporting within the Oct 1-14 window was identified.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification checks: (1) Searched multiple ways for Reuters/AP reports within Oct 1-14 window — none found. (2) The actual grand jury consideration of the Bolton case happened Oct 16 per CNN reporting (prosecutor arrived at courthouse just before 1:30pm Oct 16). (3) The MSNBC reporting from Oct 10-11 about grand jury 'reviewing evidence for weeks' is the closest to within-window activity, but it is MSNBC, not Reuters/AP, and the description is about past/ongoing activity rather than a specific dated event. (4) Multiple sources confirm Reuters and AP published about Bolton's grand jury only on Oct 16 (indictment day). (5) One Hindustan Times article from Oct 11 citing MSNBC says 'a federal grand jury in Maryland has been reviewing evidence for weeks' — but this is MSNBC-sourced, not Reuters/AP. (6) No contradiction found in the finding that Reuters and AP did not publish within the Oct 1-14 window about grand jury consideration of the Bolton case.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence shows: (1) The Bolton grand jury case was presented on October 16, 2025, outside the Oct 1-14 window. (2) Reuters published a report about the DOJ seeking to indict Bolton before a grand jury on October 16, 2025, outside the window. (3) AP also reported on October 16, outside the window. (4) While MSNBC (cited by third parties on Oct 10-12) mentioned a grand jury had been 'reviewing evidence for several weeks,' this was: (a) from MSNBC, not Reuters/AP; (b) a general description, not a specific event on a specific date within the window; (c) not itself a Reuters/AP publication. The resolution criteria are clear that only Reuters or AP publications qualify. Since no qualifying Reuters or AP report was published within October 1-14 explicitly stating actual grand jury consideration of the Bolton case, the question resolves No. The window closed with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: Will Kamala Harris endorse Mamdani?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Kamala Harris announces that she will vote for Zohran Mamdani or endorses Mamdani for the 2025 NYC Mayor election between June 26, and November 3, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

If Kamala Harris announces that she will vote for another candidate or endorses another candidate for NYC Mayor, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Kamala Harris or one of her representatives, or a consensus of credible reporting of Kamala Harris's endorsement.

subquestions.question: Will House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries endorse Zohran Mamdani for New York City mayor between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-20?
subquestions.background_information:
A key uncertainty for whether Kamala Harris will endorse Zohran Mamdani is whether prominent establishment Democrats begin publicly backing him first. Hakeem Jeffries is especially informative because he is both one of the highest-profile New York Democrats and, as of mid-July, had met with Mamdani without endorsing him. Yahoo reported on 2025-07-18 that Jeffries held an hour-long meeting with Mamdani but still had not endorsed him; the same article noted that other top Democrats, including Gov. Kathy Hochul and Sen. Chuck Schumer, also had not endorsed him yet (https://www.yahoo.com/news/hakeem-jeffries-meets-zohran-mamdani-090000000.html). This suggests Jeffries was a salient holdout rather than an automatic endorser.

At the same time, Mamdani has accumulated meaningful progressive and Democratic support. Bernie Sanders endorsed him on 2025-06-28, giving him a major boost and underscoring that he has strong support on the party's left flank (https://nystateofpolitics.com/state-of-politics/new-york/politics/2025/06/28/bernie-sanders-endorses-mamdani-in-the-mayoral-race). Rep. Adriano Espaillat endorsed Mamdani on 2025-07-18, and that report said Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Jerrold Nadler, and Nydia Velázquez had also endorsed him, indicating some consolidation among elected Democrats (https://nystateofpolitics.com/state-of-politics/new-york/politics/2025/07/18/rep--adriano-espaillat-endorses-mamdani-for-mayor).

There are also countervailing signs that establishment Democrats may hesitate. Reporting has highlighted reluctance among moderates and some officials who backed Cuomo in the primary; for example, the Queens Daily Eagle reported on 2025-07-07 that several Queens elected officials were hesitant or opposed to endorsing Mamdani, with some explicitly declining to do so (https://queenseagle.com/all/mamdani-got-queens-support-on-election-day-can-he-now-get-it-from-his-queens-colleagues). If Jeffries breaks with this hesitation and endorses, that would be a strong signal that the party establishment is coalescing around Mamdani, which would plausibly increase the odds that Harris also endorses. Conversely, continued non-endorsement by Jeffries through 2025-09-20 would be evidence that high-level Democrats remain cautious.

Sources:
