evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: (1) 'Graham Platner 2026 U.S. Senate campaign Maine' - general campaign info; (2) 'Graham Platner FEC campaign finance filing 2025' - specific filing data; (3) 'Graham Platner FEC filing campaign expenditures disbursements 2025' - disbursement details; (4) 'Graham Platner campaign spending operating expenditures $500000' - threshold-specific; (5) 'Graham for Maine FEC campaign committee disbursements report' - committee filing; (6) 'Maine Senate 2026 FEC filings campaign finance reports October November' - broader filing search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No news articles or sources identified any FEC or Maine state campaign finance filing for Graham Platner's campaign ('Graham for Maine') showing itemized expenditures for the period Oct 23–Nov 22, 2025. Key finding: A Townhall article (Nov 14, 2025) explicitly states 'no filings from Platner's campaign appear in the Senate Office of Public Records database,' confirmed by a phone operator. The campaign's treasurer (Victoria Perrone) resigned in October, and the national finance director (Ronald Holmes III) resigned Oct 31, 2025, creating compliance uncertainty. No candidate event was identified that meets the resolution criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No qualifying filing found. The [Townhall article](https://townhall.com/tipsheet/amy-curtis/2025/11/14/graham-platner-personal-financial-disclosure-report-n2666454) (Nov 14, 2025) explicitly confirmed no Senate Office of Public Records filings exist as of that date. No FEC quarterly report, amended report, or Maine state report for Graham Platner with itemized disbursements for the Oct 23–Nov 22 window was identified in any searched source.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Cannot extract a timestamp for a qualifying filing because no such filing was found in any accessible source.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at all within or outside the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Verified against multiple sources: (1) Townhall (Nov 14) confirmed no filings in Senate system; (2) Multiple sources confirmed significant staff/compliance turmoil (treasurer and finance director resignations); (3) No contradictory evidence found suggesting a compliant FEC filing with operating expenditure detail for this specific window was made publicly available by Nov 22, 2025. The resolution criteria specify: 'If no qualifying public filing with sufficient detail exists by 2025-11-22, this question should resolve Unresolvable rather than No.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria explicitly state that if no qualifying public filing with sufficient detail exists by 2025-11-22, the question should resolve 'Unresolvable' rather than 'No.' Given that: (a) no FEC or Maine state filing for Graham Platner's campaign committee with itemized disbursements for the Oct 23–Nov 22 window was found, (b) the campaign was confirmed delinquent in its disclosure obligations as of Nov 14, 2025, and (c) key compliance staff resigned during this period — there is no basis for a Yes or No resolution. The question is unresolvable.

question: Will Consensys IPO by December 31 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ConsenSys (the parent company of MetaMask) completes an Initial Public Offering (IPO) by the listed date ET, as confirmed by official company announcements and credible news sources. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The IPO refers to the first sale of stock by the listed company to the public on any recognized stock exchange.

If ConsenSys is acquired by another company that is already public, this market will immediately resolve to "No."

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will ConsenSys publicly announce or file that it has confidentially submitted a draft registration statement for a U.S. IPO between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29?
subquestions.background_information:
A confidential submission of a draft registration statement to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is a common late-stage step toward a U.S. IPO. Under the SEC's expanded confidential submission process, companies may submit draft registration statements for nonpublic review before a public filing, making an announced or reported confidential submission a strong near-term indicator that an IPO is actively progressing. SEC overview: https://www.sec.gov/corpfin/announcement/draft-registration-statement-process-faq

For ConsenSys specifically, reporting on 2025-10-31 said the company had hired JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs to lead an IPO, according to Axios as cited by Yahoo Finance, but the same reporting also said the IPO could occur as early as 2026 and that the company had 'nothing to announce at this time.' This suggests IPO preparation may be underway, but that a completed IPO by 2025-12-31 remained uncertain as of late October. Yahoo Finance summary of Axios report: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/metamask-maker-consensys-plans-ipo-175423414.html

Crowdfund Insider similarly reported on 2025-11-01 that ConsenSys was reportedly planning an IPO and working with JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs, reinforcing that there is active market speculation about a listing process rather than a completed public filing. https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/11/241365-ethereum-and-web3-focused-consensys-is-reportedly-planning-an-ipo/

A confirmed confidential submission would be materially more informative than generic IPO rumors because it would indicate that the company and its banks have moved from exploratory preparation to an actual SEC review process. That would substantially increase the chance of a near-term IPO, even if not guaranteeing pricing before year-end.

Sources:
SEC - Draft Registration Statement Process FAQ - https://www.sec.gov/corpfin/announcement/draft-registration-statement-process-faq
Yahoo Finance - MetaMask Maker Consensys Plans IPO With JPMorgan, Goldman: Axios - https://finance.yahoo.com/news/metamask-maker-consensys-plans-ipo-175423414.html
Crowdfund Insider - Ethereum and Web3 focused ConsenSys Is Reportedly Planning an IPO - https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/11/241365-ethereum-and-web3-focused-consensys-is-reportedly-planning-an-ipo/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), either: (a) ConsenSys publicly states that it has confidentially submitted, or previously confidentially submitted, a draft registration statement to the SEC for an IPO; or (b) the SEC EDGAR system shows a public filing by ConsenSys that explicitly states a draft registration statement had previously been confidentially submitted; or (c) at least two credible business/financial news outlets report during that window, citing the company, the SEC filing, or named knowledgeable sources, that ConsenSys has confidentially submitted such a draft registration statement.

This question resolves No if no such announcement, filing, or sufficiently corroborated reporting occurs between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive).

Primary resolution sources: ConsenSys official newsroom and corporate channels (https://consensys.io/newsroom), SEC EDGAR company filings search (https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/), and credible financial press such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), The Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com/), Axios (https://www.axios.com/), or Yahoo Finance reproducing/attributing such reporting (https://finance.yahoo.com/).

Definitions and edge cases:
- 'Confidentially submitted' refers specifically to submission of a draft registration statement to the SEC for IPO review, not merely hiring banks, holding analyst meetings, preparing governance changes, or planning an IPO.
- A public S-1/F-1 filing also counts as Yes only if the filing itself states that a draft registration statement had been previously confidentially submitted, because the question is about evidence that this milestone occurred.
- Rumor or single-source unsourced reporting alone does not count unless directly backed by company statements or SEC filing text.
- If reports conflict and no underlying filing or company statement is available by 2025-12-29, resolve according to the preponderance of the named primary sources above; if this still cannot be determined, the question should be treated as unresolvable.
- Events outside the window do not count. A confidential submission first reported or occurring after 2025-12-29 does not qualify.
subquestions.rationale: A confidential SEC submission is a concrete, late-stage IPO process milestone. It is not the IPO itself, but if it happens before year-end it would meaningfully increase the probability that ConsenSys is far enough along to complete an IPO soon, while failure to reach this stage by 2025-12-29 would be evidence against a 2025 IPO.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29, ConsenSys must publicly announce or file evidence that it has confidentially submitted a draft registration statement to the SEC for a U.S. IPO. Qualifying events: (a) ConsenSys official statement; (b) SEC EDGAR public filing; (c) two credible financial outlets citing company, SEC filing, or named knowledgeable sources. Key distinction: 'planning' or 'preparing for' an IPO does NOT satisfy criteria — only 'confidential submission' does.

No article found explicitly states ConsenSys 'confidentially submitted a draft registration statement to the SEC.'

question: Trump declares another national emergency by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump formally declares a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) between October 1, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A national emergency must actually be declared for this market to resolve to "Yes" - it will not be enough for Trump to announce an intention to declare a national emergency.

This market's resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration.

subquestions.question: Will Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, the White House Press Secretary, or President Trump publicly state between 2025-10-02 and 2025-10-31 that the administration is actively considering or preparing a national housing emergency declaration?
subquestions.background_information:
A plausible pathway to another National Emergencies Act declaration in late 2025 is a housing-related emergency. Multiple September 2025 reports said the administration was weighing such a move. Benzinga reported on 2025-09-01 that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, "We may declare a national housing emergency in the fall," while describing housing affordability as a central administration theme and discussing possible federal actions on zoning, closing costs, and tariff exemptions on construction materials: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/25/09/47182011/trump-administration-weighs-national-housing-emergency-as-costs-bite . A follow-up Benzinga report on 2025-09-17 noted Polymarket bettors pricing roughly a 34% chance of a housing emergency declaration in 2025 and cited severe affordability pressure, including mortgage rates in the mid-6% range and only 28% of listings being affordable to a median-income household: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/prediction-markets/25/09/47513922/trump-could-declare-housing-emergency-in-2025-polymarket-bettors-are-giving-it-a-34-chance-as-mortgage-distress-mounts .

This is informative because a fresh, on-record statement from senior administration officials that a housing emergency is under active consideration would be a concrete precursor signal for the ultimate question. It is not itself an emergency declaration, but it would indicate that internal deliberations are live during the period relevant to the ultimate market. Conversely, silence or walk-back from the principals most associated with the idea would be evidence against another declaration by year-end.

Current context also suggests Trump has been willing to use emergency authorities frequently in 2025. Commentary summarizing the administration's record said Trump had already declared numerous national emergencies in his second term, making another declaration more plausible than under many prior administrations. For example, RealClearPolitics summarized Fareed Zakaria's April 2025 comments that Trump had declared eight national emergencies in his first 100 days: https://www.realclearpolitics.com/video/2025/04/27/fareed_zakaria_trumps_eight_national_emergencies_in_100_days_push_boundaries_of_presidential_power.html . Separately, official White House publications show Trump continuing at least one existing national emergency in September 2025, regarding foreign interference in U.S. elections, demonstrating ongoing executive attention to NEA authorities: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/09/continuation-of-the-national-emergency-with-respect-to-foreign-interference-in-or-undermining-public-confidence-in-united-states-elections/ .

Qualifying statements must be public and documented in at least one of the following source types:
1. An official White House transcript, briefing, statement, fact sheet, or video posted at https://www.whitehouse.gov/ ;
2. An official U.S. Treasury press release, transcript, remarks page, or video posted at https://home.treasury.gov/ ;

Statements of past reporting by journalists do not count unless the official actually makes the statement in the quoted material. A statement that the administration is not considering such a declaration resolves No unless a separate qualifying positive statement occurs within the window.

Primary resolution sources will be official government websites: White House presidential actions, briefings, and transcripts at https://www.whitehouse.gov/ and Treasury remarks/releases at https://home.treasury.gov/news . question: Will Israel strike 0 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by Israel as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, as well as strikes within the West Bank or the Gaza Strip, will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the Israeli government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Israeli government or IDF announce at least one aerial strike by Israeli forces on targets in Yemen between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14?
subquestions.background_information:
A key driver of whether Israel strikes any foreign country in 2026 is whether the active Israel-Houthi exchange continues in late 2025. Yemen is especially relevant because Israel has already conducted multiple long-range strikes there in 2025, and the Houthis have continued launching missiles and drones toward Israel. On 2025-08-24/25, Israeli strikes reportedly hit targets in Sanaa including the presidential palace area, power infrastructure, and fuel facilities, according to ABC and AP reporting: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-08-24/israeli-retaliatory-strikes-hit-yemeni-presidential-palace/ and https://apnews.com/ . The Times of Israel also reported repeated Israeli retaliatory actions against Houthi targets during 2025 and noted that the IDF had struck Houthi positions 17 times by mid-September 2025: https://www.timesofisrael.com/ .

The Houthis have continued to attack Israel through 2025. Times of Israel reported repeated Houthi ballistic missile launches and drone attacks in August-September 2025, including claims that since March 18, 2025 the Houthis had launched dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com/ . LatestLY reported that on 2025-09-07, a drone launched from Yemen struck the passenger hall at Ramon Airport near Eilat, injuring one person: https://www.latestly.com/agency-news/world-news-israel-closes-airspace-at-southern-airport-after-houthi-drone-strike-6348903.html .

Because the ultimate question asks whether Israel will strike zero countries in 2026, persistence of Israeli aerial operations against Yemen in the immediate pre-2026 period is a strong indicator against a peaceful 2026. An official Israeli announcement of another Yemen strike before mid-December 2025 would suggest the conflict channel remains live and raises the chance that Israel again strikes Yemen in 2026.

question: 30-year mortgage rate below 6% by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average in the United States falls below 6.00% at any point between September 2 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If, for any reason, there is no data point for this market's resolution date on either of the sources listed below, information for the nearest previously available date will be used.

The primary resolution source for this market is Freddie Mac, specifically https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms. The data that will be looked at is the "30Y FRM" as indicated on the graph titled "Primary Mortgage Market Survey®". subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch tool show at least a 60% probability on 2025-10-01 that the Federal Reserve will cut its target rate by at least 25 basis points at the November 2025 FOMC meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
U.S. 30-year mortgage rates are heavily influenced by longer-term Treasury yields and expectations for Federal Reserve policy. While the Fed does not directly set mortgage rates, stronger market expectations for near-term rate cuts often coincide with lower benchmark yields and easier financial conditions, which can feed through to mortgage pricing. As of late August 2025, Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey reported the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage at 6.56%, down from 6.58% a week earlier and described as a 10-month low, but still well above the 6.00% threshold in the ultimate question. See Freddie Mac PMMS: https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms and the 2025-08-28 release summary: https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms/docs/20250828.pdf (if archived on the PMMS site).

A key near-term indicator for whether mortgage rates could fall below 6% by year-end is whether markets come to expect additional Fed easing soon. The CME FedWatch Tool publishes market-implied probabilities for target-rate outcomes at upcoming FOMC meetings based on 30-Day Fed Funds futures, and is widely used as a real-time gauge of rate-cut expectations: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html. If by early October markets assign a clear majority probability to a cut at the November meeting, that would be evidence favoring lower mortgage rates later in 2025.

This is not a restatement of the ultimate question because it asks about monetary-policy expectations rather than mortgage rates themselves. It is a meaningful crux because disagreement about the ultimate question may hinge on whether forecasters expect the Fed to move quickly enough to pull market rates lower by late 2025.

Sources:
Freddie Mac PMMS - https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms
CME FedWatch Tool - https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
FRED 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average in the United States - https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MORTGAGE30US
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), and specifically using the value displayed on 2025-10-01, the CME FedWatch Tool shows a probability of 60.0% or greater that the target federal funds rate after the November 2025 FOMC meeting will be at least 25 basis points lower than before that meeting.

Operationally, resolution will use the CME FedWatch Tool page for the November 2025 FOMC meeting at https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html. The relevant probability is the sum of outcome bins corresponding to a target range at least 25 bps below the pre-meeting target range, as displayed by CME on 2025-10-01.

If CME provides a direct probability for a 25 bps-or-more cut for the November 2025 meeting, that direct figure will be used. If CME only provides a distribution across target ranges, the resolver will sum all bins implying at least one 25 bps cut by that meeting.

If the CME FedWatch Tool is temporarily unavailable on 2025-10-01, the nearest previously available 2025-10-01 UTC snapshot from CME pages or CME-published data will be used. If CME permanently changes the page format or removes the tool, archived CME pages or other CME-published FedWatch materials will be used if they clearly show the same probabilities. If no authoritative CME evidence for 2025-10-01 is available, this question should be considered unresolvable rather than inferred from news commentary.

Fallback context source: Federal Reserve FOMC calendar https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

question: Trump enacts a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to establish a de minimis tax exemption on cryptocurrency transactions by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If the tax exemption only applies for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a member of Congress publicly introduce a federal bill creating a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether Trump will enact a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026 is whether the policy advances to the bill-introduction stage in Congress during December 2025. Recent reporting indicates that this idea is active but not yet enacted. Senator Cynthia Lummis was reported in October 2025 as 'working on' legislation to exempt small crypto transactions from capital gains taxes, with a reported structure of a $300 per-transaction exemption and a $5,000 annual cap; those reports also note that similar efforts had failed earlier in 2025 during reconciliation negotiations. See Cryptonews (2025-10-09): https://cryptonews.com/news/working-on-it-senator-lummis-backs-jack-dorseys-push-for-a-bitcoin-tax-exemption/ and Decrypt (2025-10-09): https://decrypt.co/289746/jack-dorsey-cynthia-lummis-bitcoin-tax-relief-block-btc-payments

Industry pressure also appears substantial. On November 20, 2025, more than 60 crypto organizations reportedly urged President Trump to support tax changes including a small-transaction exemption, with reported thresholds around $600. See Coinspeaker: https://www.coinspeaker.com/66-crypto-orgs-call-trump-tax-clarity/ and CoinCentral: https://coincentral.com/cryptos-christmas-wish-to-the-white-house-act-now-on-regulatory-clarity/

Additional November reporting suggests crypto policy advocates were directly lobbying House tax-writers and the White House for 'quick wins' including a de minimis exemption, with suggested thresholds in the $200-$600 range. See TechStory (2025-11-22): https://techstory.in/crypto-titans-court-d-c-in-push-for-sweeping-tax-overhaul/

Bill introduction is not the same as enactment, but it is a meaningful crux because enactment by the end of 2025 becomes much more plausible if lawmakers have moved from informal advocacy and letters to an actual legislative text with a sponsor. Since the ultimate question allows either a law or executive action, bill introduction is not sufficient for a Yes on the ultimate market, but it is strong evidence that the policy has concrete political momentum.

Sources:

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), a bill is formally introduced in either chamber of the U.S. Congress whose text would create a federal de minimis tax exemption for at least some cryptocurrency or digital-asset transactions by U.S. taxpayers.

For this question, 'formally introduced' means the bill receives an official bill number and appears on Congress.gov during the resolution window. Primary source: Congress.gov bill search and bill pages, https://www.congress.gov/

For this question, a qualifying bill must explicitly provide that gains, disposition, exchange, or use of qualifying cryptocurrency/digital assets below a stated threshold are excluded, disregarded, or exempted from federal tax reporting or tax liability. The exemption may apply to all crypto assets or only specific classes of crypto assets; either counts. The bill may include caps, anti-abuse rules, annual limits, or aggregation rules and still qualify.

A bill does not qualify if it only addresses staking, mining, wrapping, lending, broker reporting, retirement-plan access, securities treatment, or other crypto tax topics without a small-transaction de minimis exemption.

Resolution procedure:
1. Check Congress.gov for bills introduced between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 inclusive: https://www.congress.gov/
2. Confirm the bill text or official summary shows a de minimis exemption for crypto transactions.
3. If Congress.gov is unavailable or materially delayed, use the official House Clerk or Senate legislative pages plus the sponsoring member's official congressional press release as fallback sources: https://clerk.house.gov/ and https://www.senate.gov/ .

This question resolves No if no such bill is formally introduced during the window from 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-29 (inclusive).

If a member only announces plans, circulates a discussion draft, posts on social media, or issues a press release without formal introduction during the window, that does not count. If a bill is introduced before 2025-11-30 or after 2025-12-29, it does not count. If source records are too incomplete to determine whether formal introduction occurred within the window, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Sources for resolution:
Congress.gov - https://www.congress.gov/
House Clerk - https://clerk.house.gov/
U.S. Senate - https://www.senate.gov/
subquestions.rationale: A formally introduced bill is a concrete, observable step beyond lobbying, rumors, or broad pro-crypto rhetoric. If such a bill appears in December 2025, it would significantly increase the odds that Trump could sign a qualifying measure quickly or that the administration is coordinating around the policy. If no bill is introduced despite intense industry lobbying and prior public support, that is evidence against near-term enactment.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A bill must be formally introduced (receive an official bill number, appear on Congress.gov) between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29, with text creating a federal de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency or digital-asset transactions below a stated threshold. Key entities: U.S. Congress members, any chamber. Observable evidence: bill number (H.R. or S. prefix), Congress.gov listing, bill text with de minimis exemption provision.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Congress bill cryptocurrency de minimis tax exemption 2025' - to find any qualifying bills; 2) 'federal legislation digital asset tax exemption small transactions introduced December 2025' - to find formal introductions; 3) 'Digital Asset PARITY Act formally introduced Congress.gov bill number December 2025' - to check formal introduction status; 4) 'PARITY Act discussion draft not formally introduced Congress bill number assigned' - to verify draft vs formal status; 5) 'Virtual Currency Tax Fairness Act de minimis crypto bill introduced December 2025' - to check other potential bills
evidence.step3_event_detection: Primary candidate: Digital Asset PARITY Act, circulated December 20, 2025 by Reps. Max Miller (R-OH) and Steven Horsford (D-NV). Contains a de minimis exemption (proposed Section 139J) for stablecoin transactions under $200. However, multiple authoritative sources (CoinDesk, Coingape, TechStory, Blockonomi, Analytics Insight, Crowdfund Insider) explicitly state the bill was only a 'discussion draft' and had NOT been formally introduced with an official bill number. No other qualifying bills identified.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The PARITY Act contains a qualifying de minimis exemption for stablecoin cryptocurrency transactions under $200 - which satisfies the substantive criteria ('The exemption may apply to all crypto assets or only specific classes of crypto assets; either counts'). However, the formal introduction requirement is NOT met. [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2025/12/22/u-s-bipartisan-lawmakers-draw-up-tax-bill-with-stablecoin-and-staking-relief): 'The bill is a discussion draft and has not yet been formally introduced as legislation.' [Coingape](https://coingape.com/rep-max-miller-unveil-crypto-tax-bill-includes-de-minimis-rules/): 'The legislation has not yet been formally introduced.' [TechStory](https://techstory.in/house-lawmakers-unveil-bipartisan-parity-act-to-overhaul-crypto-taxes/): 'The draft is currently under discussion and has not yet been introduced in the House.' Resolution criteria explicitly state: 'If a member only announces plans, circulates a discussion draft, posts on social media, or issues a press release without formal introduction during the window, that does not count.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The PARITY Act discussion draft was circulated on December 20, 2025. No formal introduction date exists because no bill number was assigned during the window. Therefore, a reliable timestamp for a qualifying formal introduction cannot be extracted.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No formally introduced qualifying bill was identified at any point in the resolution window (2025-11-30 to 2025-12-29).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Some sources (Yahoo Finance, BeInCrypto, Brave New Coin) use language such as 'introduced the Digital Asset PARITY Act' without specifying it was only a draft. However, the more technically precise sources (CoinDesk, Coingape) explicitly clarify it was a discussion draft not formally introduced. No source provides a bill number (H.R. or S. designation). The resolution criteria require the bill to 'receive an official bill number and appear on Congress.gov during the resolution window,' which is not evidenced by any source. Note that the resolution criteria also exclude bills addressing staking/mining without a de minimis exemption, but this is moot given the formal introduction issue.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Digital Asset PARITY Act, which does contain a qualifying de minimis stablecoin exemption, was only circulated as a discussion draft during the resolution window. Multiple authoritative sources explicitly confirm it was NOT formally introduced (no bill number assigned, not on Congress.gov). The resolution criteria explicitly exclude discussion drafts. No other qualifying formally-introduced bill was identified during the window. The question resolves No, with the window closing on 2025-12-29.

question: Russia x Ukraine buffer zone agreement by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an agreement on an official buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "buffer zone" is defined as a neutral or otherwise militarily restricted area that lies between the territories of Russia and Ukraine and is intended to reduce or manage conflict between them.

A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. It is sufficient that the agreement explicitly demonstrates mutual intent to suspend offensive military action within the designated zone, for example, by stipulating the withdrawal of heavy artillery, armored vehicles, etc.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the buffer zone is established formally by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, announcements of a partial implementation, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A mutual agreement on a buffer zone will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of potential subsequent violations of such an agreement.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a broad consensus of credible media reporting stating an official agreement regarding a buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will either the Russian government or the Ukrainian government officially announce, between 2025-10-13 and 2025-11-12, support for a geographically defined demilitarized, buffer, or security zone to separate Russian and Ukrainian forces?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term precursor to a formal Russia-Ukraine buffer-zone agreement would be at least one side publicly endorsing the concept of a geographically defined militarily restricted area. The ultimate market requires an official agreement by both sides, but unilateral official support would be a meaningful intermediate signal that the idea has entered formal negotiating space.

As of early October 2025, available reporting suggests momentum toward a settlement was weak rather than strengthening. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said on 2025-10-08 that momentum from the Alaska meeting on a Ukraine settlement had 'already run out,' indicating that a negotiated framework was not obviously advancing at that time (Azeri Press Agency, 2025-10-08: https://apa.az/en/america/russian-foreign-ministry-momentum-for-ukraine-settlement-has-run-out-483145). At the same time, the European Parliament adopted a resolution on 2025-10-07/09 urging fewer restrictions on Ukraine's use of Western weapons against military targets inside Russia, which points toward continued military escalation rather than deconfliction arrangements such as a buffer zone (European Parliament resolution page: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/B-10-2025-0423_EN.html; related reporting: https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/10/9/615374/). A Foreign Affairs article from 2025-10-07 argued for 'snapback' guarantees to enforce a cease-fire, underscoring that any cease-fire or separation arrangement would likely need explicit security mechanisms to be credible (Foreign Affairs: https://www.foreignaffairs.com/ukraine/snapback-solution-ukraine).

Because there is no clear evidence in the supplied materials that either Moscow or Kyiv had already officially endorsed a bilateral buffer zone immediately before 2025-10-13, an official unilateral endorsement during the following month would be a substantial update toward the ultimate question resolving Yes by year-end.

Sources:
APA.az - Russian Foreign Ministry: Momentum for Ukraine settlement has run out — https://apa.az/en/america/russian-foreign-ministry-momentum-for-ukraine-settlement-has-run-out-483145
European Parliament motion/resolution B10-0423/2025 — https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/B-10-2025-0423_EN.html
Charter97 reporting on European Parliament urging strikes on Russian territory — https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/10/9/615374/
Foreign Affairs - A Snapback Solution for Ukraine — https://www.foreignaffairs.com/ukraine/snapback-solution-ukraine
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-13 and 2025-11-12 (inclusive), either of the following occurs:
1. An official Russian government source or official Ukrainian government source publicly states support for creating a geographically defined demilitarized zone, buffer zone, security zone, separation zone, or equivalent militarily restricted area between Russian and Ukrainian forces; OR
2. An official statement from either government says it has proposed such a zone in negotiations, provided the statement identifies the zone as geographically delimited and intended to restrict military activity or separate forces.

For Yes resolution, the statement must come from an official source such as the Kremlin, the Russian Foreign Ministry, the Russian Defense Ministry, the President of Ukraine, the Ukrainian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense, or an official government transcript/website/social-media account. Mere commentary by legislators, anonymous officials, pundits, or foreign governments does not count.

The statement must refer to a geographically defined zone or line-area arrangement. Generic support for a 'cease-fire,' 'truce,' 'de-escalation,' or 'peace talks' without mention of a demilitarized/buffer/security/separation zone or equivalent restrictions on forces in a defined area does not count.

This question resolves No if no qualifying official announcement is made between 2025-10-13 and 2025-11-12 (inclusive).

Primary resolution sources: official government websites and readouts, including Kremlin.ru (http://kremlin.ru/), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation (https://mid.ru/), the President of Ukraine official site (https://www.president.gov.ua/), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine (https://mfa.gov.ua/), and the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine (https://www.mil.gov.ua/).

Secondary/fallback sources: if official source pages are inaccessible, broad consensus reporting from Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/), AP News (https://apnews.com/hub/russia-ukraine), BBC News Europe (https://www.bbc.com/news/world/europe), or major Ukrainian/Russian outlets quoting the official text directly may be used to establish whether such an official announcement occurred within the window.

If a purported proposal is reported only as a leak, rumor, or contingent plan without an official public statement in the 2025-10-13 to 2025-11-12 window, it does not count. If the announcement occurs outside that window, this question resolves based only on events within that window.
subquestions.rationale: A formal bilateral buffer-zone agreement by 2025-12-31 is unlikely to emerge without at least one party first officially endorsing the concept of a geographically defined separation mechanism. This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question because it asks about unilateral official signaling, not a mutual agreement. A Yes outcome would be a strong leading indicator that buffer-zone language has entered serious diplomacy; a No outcome would suggest the year-end agreement remains less likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: An official statement from Kremlin, Russian MFA/MoD, Ukrainian President, Ukrainian MFA/MoD publicly supporting creation of a geographically defined demilitarized/buffer/security/separation zone between Russian and Ukrainian forces, or proposing such a zone in negotiations (with geographic delimitation and force-restriction purpose), between 2025-10-13 and 2025-11-12 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Russia Ukraine demilitarized zone buffer zone official announcement 2025' (Oct 13–Nov 12) — to find direct announcements; 2. 'Ukraine Russia security zone separation zone ceasefire negotiations official statement' (same window) — to find negotiation proposals; 3. 'Lavrov buffer zone Ukraine Russia official statement October 2025' — to examine Lavrov statements; 4. 'Kremlin Putin buffer zone demilitarized security zone Ukraine proposal 2025' — to check Kremlin statements; 5. 'Miroshnik ZNPP Zaporozhye nuclear buffer zone Russian foreign ministry November 2025' — to examine Miroshnik statement; 6. 'Russia Ukraine peace negotiations demilitarized zone geographically defined separation forces proposal official November 2025' — broader search; 7. 'Putin Russia demands buffer zone Ukraine border map Medvedev territory negotiations 2025' — to check leaked demands.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate 1: Lavrov (TASS, Oct 26-27) said Russia controls territories 'beyond Donbass and Novorossia because it needs a buffer zone' — explaining existing territorial control, not proposing a new geographically defined separation zone between forces. Candidate 2: Miroshnik (TASS, Nov 11) said establishing 'a buffer zone around the [Zaporozhye nuclear] plant' would stop Ukrainian attacks — this is about nuclear plant safety, not separating Russian/Ukrainian military forces. Candidate 3: Russia's non-paper/memo reported by Financial Times (Oct 31) allegedly demanded a buffer zone on Ukraine's side — but this was a reported leak/non-paper, not a public official announcement. Candidate 4: Various referenced security zones in the leaked 12-point Coalition of the Willing plan — explicitly not an official document. Candidate 5: Zelensky/EU statements about current line of contact as ceasefire starting point — these are generic ceasefire/truce statements, not buffer zone proposals. None of these clearly satisfy all criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Lavrov's buffer zone statement [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2035295): This is from an official source (Russian Foreign Ministry via TASS), within the window (Oct 26), and uses the term 'buffer zone.' However, it describes Russia's *existing* territorial control as fulfilling a buffer zone function, not an official proposal for a new, geographically defined demilitarized/buffer/security zone intended to separate forces as part of a peace arrangement. The resolution criteria require 'support for creating a geographically defined demilitarized zone... between Russian and Ukrainian forces.' Lavrov's statement does not propose or announce support for the *creation* of such a zone. Miroshnik's ZNPP statement [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2042167): While from an official MFA source and within the window (Nov 11), this refers to a nuclear safety buffer zone around a specific power plant, not a militarized separation zone between forces broadly. The leaked Russian memo with a buffer zone demand is reported only as a leak/non-paper, not a public official statement. No qualifying official announcement found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No event fully matching the criteria was identified. The closest candidates — Lavrov's Oct 26-27 statement and Miroshnik's Nov 11 statement — do not satisfy all resolution criteria (geographically defined zone between forces; official public support/proposal for creation of such zone).
evidence.step7_verification: Extensive search found no official public statement from Kremlin, Russian MFA/MoD, Ukrainian President, Ukrainian MFA or MoD explicitly proposing or supporting creation of a geographically defined demilitarized/buffer/security zone between Russian and Ukrainian forces during Oct 13–Nov 12, 2025. The diplomatic discourse centered on ceasefire at current contact lines, Russia's 'demilitarization' demands (referring to Ukraine's entire military capability, not a specific separation zone), and nuclear plant safety. The 12-point peace plan mentioning 'security zones' was explicitly noted as not an official EU/Ukrainian document. Russia's leaked demands were not publicly announced in an official statement.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying official announcement was identified within the Oct 13–Nov 12, 2025 window. The Lavrov buffer zone statement explains existing Russian territorial control rather than proposing a formal separation zone; the Miroshnik ZNPP statement refers to nuclear plant safety rather than force separation; the leaked Russian memo was not a public official statement. All other references either involve generic ceasefire proposals, commentary by non-qualifying sources, or events outside the window. Resolution: No.

question: Will Lionel Messi announce his retirement in 2025?
description:
This polymarket will resolve to "Yes" if Lionel Messi officially announces his retirement from club soccer by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

To resolve "Yes", the announcement must clearly state that Messi is retiring from club-level professional soccer. The announcement must come from Messi himself or his official representatives.

Retirement from international soccer alone will not qualify. 

The retirement must be intended to take effect immediately or prior to the start of the next club season following the announcement.

The primary resolution source will be official statements from Lionel Messi. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Inter Miami CF publicly announce between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that Lionel Messi has signed a contract extension or new playing contract with the club beyond the end of the 2025 MLS season?
subquestions.background_information:
A key driver of whether Lionel Messi retires from club soccer in 2025 is whether he plans to continue playing for Inter Miami beyond the current season. Multiple reports before 2025-09-01 stated that Messi's current Inter Miami contract runs through the end of the 2025 MLS season and that renewal talks are ongoing. ESPN reported on 2025-08-19 that both Luis Suárez's and Messi's contracts with Inter Miami conclude at the end of the 2025 MLS season, and that conversations between the club and Messi over an extension are ongoing: https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/45811137/luis-suarez-retire-lionel-messi-inter-miami-future-tbd . Sportskeeda similarly reported on 2025-08-27 that Messi's entourage said his focus is currently on Inter Miami and that he is reportedly negotiating a new contract with the club: https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/news-as-today-the-only-certainty-lionel-messi-s-entourage-provide-update-future-argentina-ahead-fifa-world-cup-2026 .

This makes a near-term contract extension announcement a strong indicator against a 2025 retirement from club soccer. If Inter Miami publicly confirms Messi will remain under contract beyond the 2025 season, that would materially reduce the likelihood that he announces retirement from club soccer during 2025. Conversely, the absence of such an announcement by early October would not prove retirement is coming, but would leave more room for end-of-season retirement scenarios.

Inter Miami regularly publishes official news releases on its website, which is an authoritative source for player contract announcements: https://www.intermiamicf.com/news . MLS club transactions and roster updates are also often reflected in official league channels: https://www.mlssoccer.com/ .

question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield dip below 3.9% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 10-year yield is lower than the listed value for any date between February 24 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch tool show a greater than 65% implied probability on any day between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-17 that the target range for the federal funds rate will be lower after the December 17, 2025 FOMC meeting than before it?
subquestions.background_information:
A key driver of the 10-year Treasury yield over short horizons is the market’s expectation of near-term Federal Reserve policy. If markets become more confident that the Fed will cut rates at its December meeting, that would generally support lower Treasury yields, including the 10-year, and make a dip below 3.9% in late 2025 more plausible. Reuters reported on 2025-11-13 that the 10-year Treasury yield was around 4.09% and that the probability of a December cut had fallen materially from earlier levels, with Fed officials signaling caution ahead of the December 17–18 meeting. Reuters also noted that the two-year yield was around 3.58%, reflecting market sensitivity to expected Fed easing. https://www.yahoo.com/finance/news/us-10-treasury-yields-priced-050617820.html

Recent market commentary also suggests shifting December-cut expectations have been moving Treasury yields. On 2025-11-14, market reports noted the 10-year yield holding above 4.1% as the implied probability of a December cut fell to roughly 50%, indicating that repricing of Fed expectations and 10-year yields remains tightly linked. https://www.investing.com/rates-bonds/u.s.-10-year-bond-yield-news ; https://www.tradingview.com/symbols/TVC-US10Y/

The CME FedWatch tool is a widely used public source for implied probabilities of target-rate outcomes based on 30-Day Federal Funds futures. A rise above 65% for a lower target range after the December 2025 meeting would be a meaningful sign that markets are leaning back toward near-term easing, which would be a relevant early indicator for whether the 10-year yield can fall below 3.9% before year-end. CME documents the methodology and publishes meeting-by-meeting implied probabilities here: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html

Sources:
Reuters/Yahoo Finance - US 10-year Treasury yields priced for no inflation surprises, set to rise modestly: https://www.yahoo.com/finance/news/us-10-treasury-yields-priced-050617820.html
CME Group - CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
Investing.com - U.S. 10-year Bond Yield news: https://www.investing.com/rates-bonds/u.s.-10-year-bond-yield-news
TradingView - US 10Y yield overview: https://www.tradingview.com/symbols/TVC-US10Y/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any time between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-17 (inclusive), the CME FedWatch Tool shows an implied probability greater than 65.0% that the target federal funds rate range after the December 17, 2025 FOMC meeting will be lower than before that meeting. In practice, this means the sum of probabilities assigned by CME FedWatch to target-rate outcomes below the pre-meeting target range exceeds 65.0% for the December 17, 2025 meeting on at least one calendar day in the resolution window.

Primary source: CME FedWatch Tool, December 2025 meeting page or equivalent published table/archive: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html

If CME provides only discrete target-range probabilities, the resolver should sum all outcomes that imply a lower target range than the range in effect immediately before the December 17, 2025 meeting. If CME changes the display format but continues publishing equivalent implied probabilities, the equivalent published CME probabilities should be used.

Fallback sources: CME Group methodology or meeting-specific pages, if the main FedWatch landing page changes: https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/quikstrike/cme-fedwatch-tool-user-guide.html and relevant CME interest-rate futures pages at https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates.html

If CME FedWatch becomes unavailable for the entire period from 2025-11-17 to 2025-12-17 and no authoritative CME archival or equivalent CME-published probability table can be located, this question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Near-term Fed easing expectations are one of the most direct observable drivers of Treasury yields over a one-month horizon. A clear increase in the implied probability of a December rate cut would materially raise the chances that the 10-year yield declines enough to dip below 3.9% before year-end.

question: Lisa Cook out as Fed Governor by February 28?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Lisa Cook announces her resignation or otherwise ceases to be a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors for any period of time between December 8, 2025, and February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only official announcements of Cook's resignation or removal before her term is scheduled to end, made by either Cook or the Board of Governors, will qualify. Announcements from Trump or his administration will not alone qualify.

Temporary absences or attempts at termination which do not actually remove Cook from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be information from the U.S. Government however a consensus of credible reporting will also suffice.

subquestions.question: Between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08, inclusive, will a U.S. federal court issue an order in Lisa Cook's case that explicitly restores, preserves, or recognizes her authority to continue exercising the powers of a Federal Reserve Governor pending final resolution of the litigation?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether Lisa Cook will be out as a Fed Governor by late February 2026. A key near-term crux is whether the courts materially validate her continued status on the Board after President Trump’s August 2025 purported removal attempt. Multiple reports state that Trump announced Cook’s removal in August 2025, but Cook immediately said he lacked authority to remove her and that she would continue serving; her lawyer said they would challenge the action in court. Reuters reported that Cook said, “I will not resign” and “will continue to carry out my duties,” while the White House and Fed indicated the dispute would likely be resolved through legal channels: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/federal-reserve-governor-lisa-cook-says-trump-has-no-authority-fire-her-2025-08-26/ . AP likewise reported Cook’s refusal to resign and noted that Fed governors are generally understood to be removable only for cause, making litigation central to the dispute: https://apnews.com/article/federal-reserve-lisa-cook-trump-fired- . CBS News noted analysts viewed the dispute as likely to reach the courts and potentially affect whether Trump could change the Board’s composition before future Fed decisions: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-lisa-cook-fed-governor-fired-leverage-over-fed-board/ .

This makes an early court order a strong indicator. If a federal court issues a preliminary injunction, temporary restraining order, declaratory relief, or similar order expressly preserving Cook’s authority to act as a governor pending litigation, that would materially reduce the chance she is actually out by February. Conversely, if no such order appears by early January, forecasters might assign a higher probability to a later removal or negotiated exit. The indicator is distinct from the ultimate question because it tracks the legal trajectory rather than Cook’s actual departure.

Sources:
Reuters - Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook says Trump has no authority to fire her - https://www.reuters.com/world/us/federal-reserve-governor-lisa-cook-says-trump-has-no-authority-fire-her-2025-08-26/
AP News - Federal Reserve official says she won't be 'bullied' by Trump into resigning - https://apnews.com/article/federal-reserve-lisa-cook-trump-fired-
CBS News - Trump's move to fire Fed governor Lisa Cook could give him leverage over Fed board, analysts say - https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-lisa-cook-fed-governor-fired-leverage-over-fed-board/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 inclusive, a U.S. federal court docket or written court order in litigation brought by or against Lisa Cook concerning her status as a Federal Reserve Governor issues an order that explicitly does at least one of the following pending further proceedings: (a) enjoins the government from treating Cook as removed; (b) states that Cook remains a member of the Board of Governors; or (c) restores/preserves her ability to perform the official powers or duties of a Federal Reserve Governor.

This question resolves No if no such order is issued between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 inclusive.

Qualifying orders include a temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction, stay, declaratory order, or equivalent written order from a U.S. District Court, Court of Appeals, or the U.S. Supreme Court, so long as the text expressly preserves or recognizes Cook’s authority to continue serving pending litigation. Mere scheduling orders, briefing orders, oral comments from judges not reflected in a written order, or filings by parties do not qualify.

Primary resolution sources will be official federal court records via PACER/CourtListener/RECAP and any publicly available written order. If the docket is not easily accessible publicly, authoritative reporting that quotes the operative language of the order from major outlets such as Reuters or AP may be used as a fallback. Relevant source portals include PACER: https://pacer.uscourts.gov/ ; CourtListener: https://www.courtlistener.com/ ; Reuters legal/news coverage: https://www.reuters.com/ ; AP News: https://apnews.com/ .

If multiple orders issue within the window, any one qualifying order is sufficient for Yes. If an order is issued within the window but is immediately vacated within the same window, the question still resolves Yes because the criterion is issuance of a qualifying order during the stated period. If no litigation concerning Cook’s Board status is filed or no written ruling is issued by 2026-01-08, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: The most important short-run driver of whether Cook is actually out by late February is likely the legal status of Trump’s attempted removal. A court order preserving her authority would be strong evidence against her being out by the ultimate deadline, while the absence of such protection would leave removal pressure more salient.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Between December 9, 2025 and January 8, 2026, a U.S. federal court must have issued a written order in litigation concerning Lisa Cook's status as Federal Reserve Governor that explicitly: (a) enjoins the government from treating Cook as removed, (b) states Cook remains a member of the Board of Governors, or (c) restores/preserves her ability to perform official powers/duties of a Federal Reserve Governor. The order must be issued WITHIN the window (not merely remain in effect from a pre-window order). Key entities: Lisa Cook, Federal Reserve Board of Governors, Trump administration. Timing: December 9, 2025 to January 8, 2026 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve Governor fired removed lawsuit court order' (Dec 1-Jan 8) - to find any court orders in the window; 2. 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve Supreme Court order remain board January 2026' - to find the October 1 SCOTUS order details; 3. 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve court order December 2025 January 2026' - targeted within-window search; 4. 'Trump v Cook Supreme Court new order December January 2026' - to detect any new within-window orders; 5. 'Lisa Cook fired removed Federal Reserve court order December 2025' - targeted within-window search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key events found: (1) U.S. District Court (Judge Jia Cobb) issued preliminary injunction in September 2025 allowing Cook to stay - BEFORE window. (2) D.C. Circuit upheld injunction September 15, 2025 - BEFORE window. (3) Supreme Court issued unsigned order on October 1, 2025 allowing Cook to remain pending oral arguments in January 2026 - BEFORE window. (4) Within window (Dec 9-Jan 8): No new court orders were identified. All sources consistently describe Cook as continuing to serve based on the October 2025 SCOTUS order, with oral arguments for Trump v. Cook scheduled for January 21, 2026 (after window closes). Lisa Cook voted at the December 10, 2025 FOMC meeting, confirming she was still serving. One Hindu BusinessLine article mentioned 'The Court also allowed the firing of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook' but this appears erroneous and contradicted by all other sources. Rejected candidates: The October 1, 2025 SCOTUS order, the September 2025 D.C. Circuit ruling, and the September 2025 District Court injunction all fall OUTSIDE the question window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No court order within the December 9, 2025 - January 8, 2026 window has been identified that meets the criteria. The existing orders (District Court preliminary injunction, D.C. Circuit ruling, October 1 SCOTUS order) were all issued BEFORE December 9, 2025. Multiple sources from within the window confirm: Cook was still serving as a result of the October 2025 SCOTUS order; oral arguments were scheduled for January 21, 2026 (after window closes); no new qualifying order was issued in this period. [AP News](https://apnews.com/article/supreme-court-trump-executive-power-firings-boards-e45b572f8140ffcdfacbe82ba0b896ef); [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/03/federal-reserve-powell-face-challenges-in-2026.html); [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/supreme-court/supreme-court-new-term-trump-tariffs-birthright-citizenship-fed-rcna249340); [Quartz](https://qz.com/lisa-cook-scotus-fed-stay); [Zero Hedge](https://www.zerohedge.com/political/3-key-supreme-court-cases-watch-early-2026)
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The October 1, 2025 Supreme Court order is clearly established by multiple sources. No new qualifying order was issued between December 9, 2025 and January 8, 2026. The next significant legal action in Cook's case was the January 21, 2026 oral arguments at the Supreme Court - outside the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable - no qualifying event was identified within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: One article (Hindu BusinessLine, January 6, 2026) states 'The Court also allowed the firing of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook,' but this appears to be either an error or describing future events post-window, as it is contradicted by all other reporting (10+ major sources from the same period) which consistently state Cook was still serving on the Fed Board and oral arguments were scheduled for January 21, 2026. The December 10, 2025 FOMC monetary policy statement explicitly lists 'Lisa D. Cook' as voting in favor of the rate cut, confirming she was still serving as a Board member within the window. No source reports any new court order within the December 9, 2025 - January 8, 2026 window. The existing stay/injunction protecting Cook remained in force throughout the period as a carry-over from pre-window orders, but no new qualifying order was issued within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question asks specifically whether a qualifying court order was ISSUED between December 9, 2025 and January 8, 2026. The evidence clearly establishes: (1) All qualifying orders protecting Cook (District Court injunction, D.C. Circuit ruling, Supreme Court October 1, 2025 order) were issued BEFORE the question window. (2) No new qualifying court order was issued within the December 9, 2025 - January 8, 2026 window. (3) The next relevant judicial action was oral arguments scheduled for January 21, 2026, after the window closes. (4) Cook continued serving during the window solely based on the October 2025 pre-window orders. Therefore, the question resolves No.

question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between October 30 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Poland's Armed Forces Operational Command or Romania's Ministry of National Defence publicly report at least 3 separate scrambles of military aircraft in response to Russian aerial attacks on Ukraine between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
A useful leading indicator for a direct Russian strike on NATO territory is the tempo of near-border Russian aerial operations that already force NATO members to react militarily. In September 2025, Polish and allied jets were scrambled during a large Russian strike on Ukraine involving hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles, underscoring that Russian attacks near NATO borders can rapidly create spillover risk. NewsGram reported that on 2025-09-20 Polish and allied aircraft were activated amid a mass Russian attack on Ukraine, while Polish air defenses and radar systems were put on maximum readiness: https://www.newsgram.com/world/2025/09/20/nato-jets-scramble-amid-mass-russian-attack-on-ukraine . Similar reporting described repeated Polish/NATO scrambles and recent drone incidents affecting Poland and Romania: https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2025/09/03/russia-drone-missile-ukraine/5401756900340/ and https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/russia-ukraine-war-putin-drones-missiles-poland-nato-fighter-jets-scrambled-2644000-2025-09-20 .

The underlying Russian strike volume has also risen sharply. Euronews reported that on 2025-10-17 Russia launched more than 300 drones and 37 missiles at Ukraine's energy infrastructure: https://www.euronews.com/2025/10/17/russia-batters-ukraines-energy-grid-with-drone-and-missile-strikes . On 2025-10-30, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform reported 705 total aerial targets in one night, including 653 drones and 52 missiles, with many impacts across Ukraine: https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3940000-ukraines-air-defenses-down-623-drones-and-missiles-out-of-705-launched.html . More large barrages increase the chance of navigation errors, deliberate probing, or debris-causing incidents near NATO airspace; they also raise the chance that NATO fighters are repeatedly scrambled. A month with 3 or more officially reported scrambles by Poland and/or Romania would signal an unusually elevated level of operational friction along NATO's eastern flank, making the ultimate question more likely.

Sources:
NewsGram - NATO Jets Scramble Amid Mass Russian Attack On Ukraine - https://www.newsgram.com/world/2025/09/20/nato-jets-scramble-amid-mass-russian-attack-on-ukraine
UPI - 1 killed, 5 hurt as Russia launches aerial assault on Ukraine - https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2025/09/03/russia-drone-missile-ukraine/5401756900340/
India Today - Poland in tension, scramble fighter jets with NATO as Russia attacks - https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/russia-ukraine-war-putin-drones-missiles-poland-nato-fighter-jets-scrambled-2644000-2025-09-20
Euronews - Russia batters Ukraine's energy grid with drone and missile strikes - https://www.euronews.com/2025/10/17/russia-batters-ukraines-energy-grid-with-drone-and-missile-strikes
Ukrinform - Ukraine's air defenses down 623 drones and missiles out of 705 launched - https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3940000-ukraines-air-defenses-down-623-drones-and-missiles-out-of-705-launched.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), there are at least 3 separate calendar dates on which either (a) Poland's Armed Forces Operational Command (Dowództwo Operacyjne Rodzajów Sił Zbrojnych, typically via official website or official X account) publicly states that Polish and/or allied military aircraft were scrambled / were operating in Polish airspace in response to Russian long-range aviation, missile, or drone attacks on Ukraine, or (b) Romania's Ministry of National Defence publicly states that Romanian military aircraft were scrambled / airborne in response to Russian aerial attacks near Romanian airspace.

Count rules:
1. Multiple posts or articles about the same country's response on the same UTC date count as one scramble date.
2. A report must attribute the action to an official Polish or Romanian government/military source.
3. Reports of mere heightened readiness, radar activation, or air-defense alert without aircraft scrambling / military aircraft airborne do not count.
4. NATO aircraft from allied states count only if the official Polish or Romanian source says they were operating in that country's airspace in response to the attack.
5. If one incident begins before midnight and continues after midnight, count it on the date identified by the official source; if unclear, use the first publication date from the official source.

Primary resolution sources:
- Poland Armed Forces Operational Command official site: https://www.wojsko-polskie.pl/dorsz/
- Poland Armed Forces Operational Command official X account: https://x.com/DowOperSZ
- Romanian Ministry of National Defence news portal: https://english.mapn.ro/
- Romanian Ministry of National Defence Romanian-language portal: https://www.mapn.ro/

Secondary / corroborating sources if needed:
- Reuters world news: https://www.reuters.com/world/
- Associated Press world news: https://apnews.com/hub/world-news

If by 2025-12-07 no authoritative public information is available to determine the count, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Repeated official scrambles by front-line NATO states are an observable sign that Russian strike patterns are creating acute spillover risk near alliance territory. A high scramble count indicates sustained Russian operations close enough to NATO borders to trigger military response, which should materially raise the probability of an actual Russian aerial impact on NATO territory before year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, there are at least 3 separate calendar dates on which either (a) Poland's Armed Forces Operational Command publicly states Polish/allied military aircraft were scrambled in response to Russian attacks on Ukraine, or (b) Romania's Ministry of National Defence publicly states Romanian military aircraft were scrambled in response to Russian aerial attacks near Romanian airspace. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All 5 events explicitly involve aircraft scrambles (not mere readiness). The threshold of 3 qualifying dates is met by Romania alone (Nov 4, Nov 22, Nov 25), plus Nov 20 shared, and Poland Nov 29.

evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: First qualifying event in the window is Romania's MoND-confirmed scramble on November 4, 2025. No earlier qualifying event within the Oct 31-Nov 30 window was found.
evidence.step7_verification: Romania's Ministry of National Defence is explicitly cited as the source in all Romania scramble articles (Nov 4, Nov 20, Nov 22, Nov 25). Polish defense officials/military confirmed Poland scrambles (Nov 20, Nov 29). The Nov 20 article (KESQ/CNN) explicitly states 'Poland scrambles fighter jets in its airspace.' The Nov 29 Newsweek article quotes Polish military statement about actions 'aimed at securing the airspace.' Count rule 1 (same country, same date = one date) is respected — all 5 events are on different calendar dates, all within the window. Count rule 3 (no mere readiness without aircraft) is satisfied — all involve actual scrambles/aircraft airborne. Threshold of 3 separate dates is clearly exceeded (at least 5 qualifying dates identified).

Poland's armed forces confirmed scrambles on November 20 and November 29. The threshold of 3 qualifying dates is definitively exceeded (minimum 5 qualifying dates). Resolution: Yes.

subquestions.background_information:
Drobysheve lies just east-northeast of Karpivka, and Russian progress into or through Karpivka would be a meaningful operational indicator for whether Russian forces are closing the western/northwestern approach needed to secure Drobysheve’s remaining contested area. A move into Karpivka would suggest that Russian forces are not merely conducting temporary infiltration in the Drobysheve area but are broadening and consolidating local control.

The ultimate market is based on ISW map shading at a specific intersection inside Drobysheve. ISW’s mapping distinguishes between assessed Russian control/advance/gains and mere infiltration; this matters because recent reporting has highlighted that Russian claims of capture can be exaggerated and that infiltration does not always translate into durable control. ISW has recently pushed back on inflated Russian territorial claims, including claims by Gerasimov, emphasizing that some reported advances lacked supporting evidence: https://charter97.org/en/news/2026/1/28/627711/ . ISW’s own mapping products and legend are hosted here: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 .

Recent reporting specifically claimed that Russian forces were 'completing the capture of Drobysheve' and advancing in the nearby Lyman/Sloviansk axis, but these claims came from Russian or pro-Russian sources and should be treated cautiously as signals rather than facts: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/01/27/ . Another report claimed an enemy group in Drobysheve had been trapped and destroyed, again reflecting Russian official statements rather than neutral confirmation: https://tass.com/politics/ . Because of this uncertainty, an adjacent-settlement indicator like Karpivka is useful: if ISW itself starts shading Karpivka red, that would be a stronger sign that Russian pressure around Drobysheve is translating into map-confirmed control.

This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question because it concerns a different location. It is an early indicator: Russian-confirmed expansion into Karpivka before late February would raise the odds that the specific Drobysheve intersection is captured by February 28, while failure to do so would be evidence against rapid nearby consolidation.
