The broader late-2025 context also suggests DOJ under Trump is willing to take highly public, politically salient prosecutorial steps when Trump pressures it to do so, including pursuing adversaries and using unconventional appointment arrangements. See Yahoo, Oct. 10, 2025: https://www.yahoo.com/news/when-trump-demands-prosecutions-his-doj-now-obeys-000000000.html ; MSNBC, Oct. 19, 2025: https://www.msnbc.com/opinion/msnbc-opinion/trump-acting-prosecutors-doj-loyalists-rcna000000

Recent legal turmoil around Trump-appointed acting prosecutors in multiple districts also makes a document-release path potentially more attractive than immediately creating another controversial prosecutorial role. Newsweek reported on Oct. 30, 2025 that a federal judge found acting U.S. attorney Bill Essayli was serving unlawfully, following similar disputes elsewhere: https://www.newsweek.com/trump-picked-attorney-reacts-after-judge-disqualifies-him-0000000

For this subquestion, 'new tranche of non-court-filed Jeffrey Epstein investigative materials' means materials that were not already publicly available before 2025-10-31 and that are released by the administration/DOJ/FBI in connection with Epstein, such as FBI files, DOJ memoranda, interview summaries, evidence logs, visitor logs, correspondence, or similar records. It excludes purely judicial filings already placed on court dockets by private litigants, as those are less informative about the administration’s own willingness to act.

Sources:
Daily Bulletin - Watch live: Attorney General Bondi faces Senate questions over political pressure on Justice Department — https://www.dailybulletin.com/2025/10/07/watch-live-attorney-general-bondi-faces-senate-questions-over-political-pressure-on-justice-department/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, the White House, U.S. Department of Justice, or FBI publicly releases or posts any new tranche of previously non-public Jeffrey Epstein investigative materials, and the release is confirmed by an official government source.

For purposes of resolution:
- 'New tranche' means one or more documents/files released together as part of a disclosure event.
- 'Non-court-filed' means the materials are released by the executive branch and are not merely copies of materials first made public through a court docket by a non-government actor.
- 'Jeffrey Epstein investigative materials' means records explicitly presented as relating to investigations of Jeffrey Epstein, his associates, or the handling of the Epstein case.
- A press release, document dump, FOIA reading-room posting, FBI Vault posting, DOJ webpage publication, or official statement linking to the materials counts.
- Mere promises to release documents, statements that materials exist, or disclosures with no actual materials made public do not count.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying release occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive.

Primary resolution sources:
- DOJ newsroom and official DOJ websites: https://www.justice.gov/news and https://www.justice.gov/
- FBI news and records sites, including the Vault: https://www.fbi.gov/news and https://vault.fbi.gov/
- White House statements/briefings: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/

Fallback: if the release is first reported by multiple credible outlets but later linked to an official government posting within the window, that official posting governs. If an administration official verbally announces a release within the window but the documents themselves are not publicly made available until after 2025-11-30, this resolves No. If relevant government websites are unavailable at resolution time, archived copies plus consensus reporting from major outlets such as AP or Reuters may be used.
subquestions.rationale: A public release of new Epstein materials is a distinct observable event, not a restatement of the special-prosecutor question. It is a plausible leading indicator because appointing a special prosecutor would likely come from a broader administration decision to elevate Epstein politically and procedurally. New disclosures in November would signal that the administration is actively advancing the issue and may be laying groundwork for stronger later action, including an independent prosecutor.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: White House, DOJ, or FBI publicly releases/posts a new tranche of previously non-public Jeffrey Epstein investigative materials between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive. Observable evidence: official DOJ/FBI/White House webpage posting, press release with actual documents, or FBI Vault/FOIA reading room posting of Epstein materials. Key entities: Trump administration, DOJ, FBI. The release must be actual materials (not promises), must be from the executive branch (not Congress or courts), and must be non-court-filed materials first made public by the executive branch.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'DOJ FBI Epstein files documents release 2025' (Oct 31 - Nov 30) — to find any executive branch document releases; 2) 'Trump administration Epstein investigative materials release November 2025' — to find official releases; 3) 'DOJ FBI Epstein documents actually released published online November 2025' — looking for actual publication; 4) 'FBI Vault Epstein documents posted release executive branch November 2025' — to find FBI Vault postings; 5) 'House Oversight Committee Epstein emails documents release November 2025' — to distinguish congressional from executive releases; 6) 'DOJ justice.gov Epstein files posting publication November 2025' — looking for official website postings; 7) 'Epstein files DOJ actually released documents December deadline 30 days' — checking if release happened within window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) House Oversight Committee released ~20,000-23,000 pages of Epstein estate documents on November 12-15, 2025 — REJECTED: This was a congressional release, not an executive branch release; (B) Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act on November 20, 2025 — REJECTED as resolving: This is a legal mandate for future release, not an actual release of materials; (C) DOJ filed court motions on November 25, 2025 to unseal grand jury transcripts — REJECTED: This is a court filing requesting permission to unseal, not an actual release; (D) FBI/DOJ reviewing documents and assessing what can be released (various November 2025 articles) — REJECTED: This is review activity, not a release; (E) Earlier 2025 releases mentioned (February 2025, 341 pages released by DOJ; FBI 1,400+ pages posted) — REJECTED: These occurred before the October 31, 2025 start date of the question window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event matches all criteria. The congressional release by the House Oversight Committee (November 12-15) does not qualify because it was not an executive branch release. The signing of the Epstein Files Transparency Act (November 20) constitutes a promise/mandate to release, not an actual release. The DOJ's December 19 deadline means the actual release was scheduled AFTER the question window. Multiple sources from November 22-27 confirm the actual DOJ/FBI release had not yet occurred: [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/jeffrey-epstein-files-doj-transparency-act-2025-11) states DOJ must release 'within 30 days—by December 19, 2025'; [ABC News](https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/after-trump-signs-epstein-files-bill-focus-shifts/story?id=127700652) reports 'setting a 30-day deadline for the Department of Justice (DOJ) to release the materials—potentially by December 19, 2025'; [Kash Patel/Yahoo](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/kash-patel-casts-doubt-full-183114623.html) casts 'doubt on full release' by deadline; [Massie/FrankNez](https://franknezmedia.com/massie-now-slams-kash-patel-over-response-to-epstein-document-release/) notes '23 days remaining' as of late November with public awaiting whether files will be released. No articles report any actual DOJ/FBI/White House posting of new Epstein investigative materials within the October 31 – November 30 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The DOJ deadline for release under the Epstein Files Transparency Act is December 19, 2025 (30 days after Trump signed it on November 20, 2025). No timestamp found for any actual DOJ/FBI executive branch release within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window. The February 2025 DOJ release of 341 pages occurred before the window. The House Oversight Committee congressional releases occurred on November 12-15, 2025, but these were congressional, not executive branch releases.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) Some articles mention 'documents being released earlier in 2025 by the DOJ and FBI' (The Inquisitr, Nov 17) but these predate the question window. (2) The Financial Express (Nov 26) mentions 'over 1,400 pages posted by the FBI' but this was prior releases, not within the window. (3) The question's resolution criteria specifically excludes congressional releases, which is where the November 2025 document releases occurred. (4) All sources consistently indicate the DOJ faces a December 19, 2025 deadline for the actual release — after the question window closes. (5) Kash Patel's late November statements cast doubt even on meeting the December 19 deadline. No contradictory evidence was found suggesting an actual DOJ/FBI/White House posting of new Epstein investigative materials within the question window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Within the October 31 – November 30, 2025 window: (1) The House Oversight Committee released 20,000-23,000+ pages of Epstein estate documents (November 12-15), but this was a congressional release, not an executive branch release, so it does not satisfy the resolution criteria. (2) Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act (November 20), which mandated future DOJ release but is itself merely a legal directive/promise, not an actual release of materials. (3) The DOJ's 30-day deadline for actual document release runs to December 19, 2025, which is after the question window. (4) As of the window's end (November 30), the DOJ was still in review/court-filing mode, with no actual release having occurred. The condition became definitively impossible (i.e., clear that no qualifying release would occur within the window) because the statutory deadline itself falls after November 30. The window closed with no qualifying executive branch release of Epstein investigative materials.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce a waitlist, beta, or developer preview for a standalone web browser between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17?

A near-term precursor would be OpenAI publicly acknowledging the product through a waitlist, beta signup, or developer preview page. Such a step would be materially different from the final release itself, but would strongly indicate that a 2025 release remains on track. Reporting before 2025-10-18 says OpenAI’s browser is expected but still lacks an official release date, suggesting meaningful uncertainty remains rather than the event being already locked in. Mashable reported on 2025-10-01 that OpenAI’s AI-powered browser was anticipated, with native ChatGPT integration and competition with Chrome, Safari, and Edge, but that no official release date had been given: https://mashable.com/article/ai-product-releases-on-the-horizon-2025 . A related 2025-10-01 Mashable ME article likewise described the browser as upcoming but without an official launch date: https://me.mashable.com/tech/62015/6-productivity-boosting-ai-product-releases-on-the-horizon .

This is a useful crux because late-2025 consumer software launches are often preceded by public waitlists, preview programs, or developer documentation. If no such public signal appears by mid-November 2025, forecasters should update downward on the chance that OpenAI will complete a full public browser release by 2025-12-31. Conversely, a public preview or waitlist would be a strong positive indicator while remaining distinct from the ultimate condition.

3. The waitlist / beta / preview is available to the public in the sense that any member of the public can view the announcement page or attempt to sign up, even if access is limited, region-gated, invite-only after signup, or capped.

- If OpenAI announces only a browser feature within ChatGPT or within another company’s browser, that does not count.
- If a page appears before 2025-10-18, it does not count even if still live during the window.
- If the announcement is first made after 2025-11-17, it does not count.

subquestions.background_information:
Atlas appears to have launched publicly in late October 2025 as an AI-powered browser from OpenAI. Multiple contemporaneous reports say the initial release was on macOS, with Windows, iOS, and Android versions expected soon. For example, The Telegraph reported on 2025-10-22 that Atlas was 'initially available on macOS, with Windows, iOS, and Android versions expected soon' (https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2025/10/22/openai-unveils-atlas-browser-to-take-on-google/). Hindustan Times likewise reported that Atlas launched first on macOS and would expand to Windows, iOS, and Android (https://www.hindustantimes.com/technology/google-loses-100-billion-in-market-value-after-chatgpt-announces-new-browser-101761129000000.html). Daily News similarly described the launch as initially for Apple desktops/laptops worldwide, with other platforms coming soon (https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/10/21/openai-launches-ai-powered-web-browser-chatgpt-atlas/).

This matters for the ultimate question because StatCounter's browser market-share series for the parent market includes Desktop, Mobile, Tablet, and Console worldwide. A browser limited to macOS desktop/laptop for most of the remaining year would face a much narrower addressable base than one that quickly expands to Windows and/or mobile. Current browser usage is heavily cross-platform, and mobile accounts for a majority of global web traffic. StatCounter coverage for browser share in the ultimate question explicitly aggregates desktop, mobile, tablet, and console usage worldwide (https://gs.statcounter.com/browser-market-share). Separately, reporting citing StatCounter noted that mobile devices account for over 60% of global web traffic, underscoring why mobile availability could be especially important for any attempt to reach 5% global share by year-end (https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkiye-surpasses-global-average-in-mobile-internet-use-211157).

The incumbent market is highly concentrated. Recent reporting based on StatCounter described Chrome at roughly 71.8%-71.9% global share in September/October 2025, with Safari and Edge far behind (https://www.pcworld.com/article/2816751/chrome-breaks-market-share-record-leaving-competitors-in-the-dust.html; https://www.neowin.net/news/google-chrome-continues-crushing-other-browsers-reaches-new-all-time-high/). That concentration suggests Atlas likely needs very rapid distribution expansion, not just a macOS-only launch, to have a realistic path to 5%+ by 2025-12-31.

description:

If no nominee is announced by November 3, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democrat sources, including https://democrats.org/.

Any replacement of the nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

subquestions.question: Will Donna Miller report raising more itemized individual contributions than any other Democratic candidate for IL-02 in FEC filings covering activity through 2026-02-25?
subquestions.background_information:
Fundraising is a useful leading indicator in congressional primaries because it reflects donor enthusiasm, campaign viability, and ability to communicate with voters before Election Day. In Illinois' 2nd Congressional District Democratic primary, major reported candidates include Donna Miller, Robert Peters, Jesse Jackson Jr., Willie Preston, Yumeka Brown, and Adal Regis, according to the Chicago Tribune's overview of the race published January 29, 2026: https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/01/29/top-candidates-for-the-us-house-in-illinois-2nd-4th-7th-8th-and-9th-districts-for-the-2026-election/

The Federal Election Commission (FEC) requires campaigns to file periodic reports, and those filings include itemized receipts from individuals. These data are publicly available through the FEC candidate and committee databases, making them relatively objective and timely indicators of campaign strength. FEC reporting information and campaign finance data are available at https://www.fec.gov/ and via candidate pages/search tools such as https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/ and https://www.fec.gov/data/receipts/.

Because the Democratic primary is scheduled for March 17, 2026, a fundraising-based subquestion resolving by mid-March can provide evidence about which campaign has the strongest organized support before votes are cast. Donna Miller outperforming all rivals on itemized individual fundraising by the late-February reporting cutoff would be evidence in favor of her nomination prospects, though not determinative.

Sources:
Chicago Tribune - Top candidates for the US House in Illinois' 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th and 9th districts for the 2026 election
https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/01/29/top-candidates-for-the-us-house-in-illinois-2nd-4th-7th-8th-and-9th-districts-for-the-2026-election/
FEC candidate data
https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/
FEC receipts data
https://www.fec.gov/data/receipts/
FEC home page
https://www.fec.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, based on the most recent FEC filings publicly available by 2026-03-15 for committees authorized by Democratic candidates running in the 2026 IL-02 Democratic primary, Donna Miller's principal authorized committee reports a greater total amount of itemized individual contributions for the reporting period(s) covering activity from 2026-02-18 through 2026-02-25 than any other Democratic candidate's principal authorized committee.

This question resolves No if another Democratic candidate for IL-02 reports an equal or greater total amount of itemized individual contributions for the relevant reporting coverage.

Resolution window: qualifying financial activity must fall between 2026-02-18 and 2026-02-25 inclusive, and the question will be resolved no later than 2026-03-15 using filings available by then.

Primary source: FEC filings and FEC data pages for candidate committees, including candidate and receipts search pages: https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/ and https://www.fec.gov/data/receipts/.

Method:
1. Identify all Democratic candidates on the IL-02 ballot using the Illinois State Board of Elections candidate information if needed: https://www.elections.il.gov/.
2. For each candidate, identify the principal authorized campaign committee in FEC records.
3. Use the applicable FEC report(s) that include transactions dated from 2026-02-18 through 2026-02-25 inclusive.
4. Sum only itemized individual contributions for that date range for each candidate's principal authorized committee.
5. Compare Donna Miller's total with every other Democratic candidate's total.

If the FEC interface is unavailable, the resolver may use the underlying electronically filed reports available through the FEC website or campaign finance aggregators that reproduce FEC data without alteration, but FEC data remains controlling.

If relevant reports are materially delayed or unavailable for one or more major candidates by 2026-03-15, and the comparison cannot be made fairly from official FEC data, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Sources for resolution:
FEC candidate data https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/
FEC receipts data https://www.fec.gov/data/receipts/
Illinois State Board of Elections https://www.elections.il.gov/
subquestions.rationale: Relative fundraising strength is an observable pre-primary indicator of campaign viability and organizational momentum. If Donna Miller leads the field in recent itemized individual fundraising, that would tend to support the view that she has stronger grassroots or donor backing than her rivals, which is relevant evidence for whether she will win the Democratic nomination.

evidence.step1_decompose: YES requires: Donna Miller's FEC-reported itemized individual contributions for ONLY Feb 18–25, 2026 > every other IL-02 Democratic candidate's total for the same window. Observable evidence needed: line-item receipts from pre-primary FEC filings for each of 10 IL-02 Democratic candidates, filtered to dates Feb 18–25. Key entities: Donna Miller, Robert Peters, Jesse Jackson Jr., Willie Preston, Yumeka Brown, Adal Regis, Eric France, Patrick Keating, Toni Brown, Sidney Moore. Timing: FEC pre-primary reports due ~March 5, 2026, covering Jan 1–Feb 25.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Donna Miller IL-02 FEC campaign finance fundraising February 2026 individual contributions' — to find specific contribution data; 2) 'IL-02 Illinois 2nd congressional district 2026 Democratic primary candidates' — to identify all candidates; 3) 'Illinois 2nd district congressional pre-primary FEC report February 25 2026 fundraising' — to find pre-primary reports; 4) 'Robert Peters Jesse Jackson Jr FEC filing fundraising February 2026' — to find competitor data; 5) 'Illinois 2nd district FEC filing itemized contributions 2026 weekly report' — to find granular FEC filing data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Found extensive news coverage of the IL-02 race and candidates. Key relevant finding: Pre-primary FEC reports covering Jan 1–Feb 25, 2026 were due March 5, 2026 (confirmed by Evanston RoundTable for 9th District, same deadline applies to 2nd District). Miller's overall fundraising is well-documented (raised $1.3M by December 2025 via AIPAC-linked donors, $900K+ in Q4 2025). Peters raised $900K+ by January 1, 2026. Jackson raised $179,827. Preston raised $118,847. But NO source provides transaction-level data specifically for Feb 18–25. All rejected as insufficient: no source provides the specific 8-day window comparison required.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No news article directly provides the specific comparison required. The Chicago Tribune [https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/03/05/illinois-2nd-district-crowded-democratic-primary-emerges-in-illinois-2nd-district-race-to-replace-us-rep-robin-kelly/] provides Q4 2025 totals (Miller $1.3M, Peters $900K+, Jackson $179K, Preston $118K). The Evanston RoundTable [https://evanstonroundtable.com/2026/03/07/last-call-on-cash-9th-district-congressional-candidates-burn-through-war-chests-as-outside-spending-takes-over/] covers 9th District pre-primary reports. The Biss/Fine article [https://evanstonroundtable.com/2026/02/25/biss-and-fine-campaigns-trade-accusations-of-financial-misconduct/] confirms pre-primary report due March 5 covering Jan 1–Feb 25, 2026. None provide the Feb 18–25 specific window for IL-02.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Cannot extract exact timestamp — no source provides itemized individual contribution data for IL-02 candidates specifically during Feb 18–25, 2026. The pre-primary reports covering through Feb 25 were due March 5, 2026, but no news analysis of those specific reports for IL-02 has been found.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find any comparative analysis of IL-02 candidate FEC filings specifically for the Feb 18–25 window. No such analysis exists in available news sources. Miller had the highest overall fundraising through 2025 (AIPAC-linked donors), but whether she led in the specific 8-day window Feb 18–25 cannot be determined from available evidence. The resolution criteria requires transaction-level FEC data access, which is only available via the FEC's own databases and is not reported in news coverage. No contradictory evidence was found because insufficient evidence of any kind exists for this specific question.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolvable=false. The resolution requires granular, transaction-level FEC data for ALL 10 IL-02 Democratic candidates, filtered to the specific 8-day window of Feb 18–25, 2026. No news source provides this level of detail. While pre-primary FEC reports covering through Feb 25 were due March 5, and while Miller has been documented as having the highest overall fundraising, the specific comparative analysis of itemized individual contributions for ONLY Feb 18–25 across all candidates cannot be determined from available news evidence. Direct FEC database access would be required, which is outside available search tools.

question: Will Charli XCX release a new song in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the listed artist officially releases a new song between January 1 and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM PT (Los Angeles time). Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Officially released means that a newly released song or single is officially available for download or streaming (not including live performances, recordings of live performances, or leaks) by the resolution date.

Live versions, re-releases, deluxe editions, or similar non-original or altered versions of previously released songs will not count. Songs where the listed artist appears only as a secondary or featured performer, rather than the primary artist, will also not count. 

If a song is released jointly by multiple artists credited equally as primary artists, it will count for all of them. In case of ambiguity, this market will resolve based on the credits of the below-listed resolution sources (e.g., the song ‘girl, get up.’ counts as a new release for SZA as she is, equally to Doechii, labeled “Main Artist” in the Spotify credits to the song, regardless of feature indication in the title).

For listed groups of artists, tracks released by individual members, sub-units, or under any designation other than the listed group name will not count toward resolution.

The primary resolution sources will be official streaming and download platforms. In cases of ambiguity over how a song/album is labeled, the listed resolution sources will be consulted in the following order of precedence: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, and Deezer.

subquestions.question: Will Charli XCX announce a 2026 tour date, festival appearance, or live performance featuring her as a billed artist between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13?
subquestions.background_information:
Announcements of upcoming live dates are a useful near-term indicator of an artist's release cycle, because major artists often pair new music rollouts with tour or festival bookings. Charli XCX had a major commercial cycle around her 2024 album Brat, which continued to generate attention into 2025; for example, media coverage in October 2025 still described Brat as a recent breakout success and highlighted ongoing attention around related releases and remixes (Just Jared, 2025-10-09: https://www.justjared.com/tags/a-g-cook/). Industry reporting has also emphasized that Charli XCX has recently used coordinated marketing tactics, including outdoor advertising, to build anticipation around releases, suggesting an active and strategic promotional approach rather than a dormant period (The Drum, 2025-09-03: https://www.thedrum.com/news/2025/09/03/how-taylor-swift-musics-biggest-stars-are-using-ooh-anchor-drop-their-albums).

If Charli XCX publicly announces 2026 performances in the next month, that would be evidence she is planning an active 2026 campaign; such campaigns often coincide with standalone singles, soundtrack songs, collaborations as co-primary artist, or the early stages of a new album era. Conversely, the absence of any 2026 live-date announcement through early December 2025 would be mild evidence for a quieter first weeks of 2026. This is not equivalent to the ultimate question, because artists can announce performances without releasing new songs, and can also release new songs without announcing live dates.

Sources:
- Just Jared, "a.g. cook | Latest Articles, News, and Photos" — https://www.justjared.com/tags/a-g-cook/
- The Drum, "How Taylor Swift & music's biggest stars are using OOH as an anchor to drop their albums" — https://www.thedrum.com/news/2025/09/03/how-taylor-swift-musics-biggest-stars-are-using-ooh-anchor-drop-their-albums
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13 (inclusive), Charli XCX or an event organizer publicly announces at least one live event scheduled for any date in calendar year 2026 in which Charli XCX is billed as a performing artist.

Qualifying announcements must be publicly accessible and attributable to one of the following sources, in order of preference:
1. Charli XCX's official website or official social media accounts;
2. The official website or official social media accounts of the venue, festival, promoter, or event organizer;
3. Major ticketing pages created by the official organizer or ticketing partner.

A qualifying event can be a concert, festival appearance, residency date, or other live music performance. The announcement need not specify new music. The event itself may occur after 2025-12-13; only the announcement must occur within the resolution window.

This resolves No if no such qualifying announcement is made between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13 (inclusive).

Edge cases:
- Mere rumors, press speculation, or reposts by fan accounts do not count.
- If an announcement is deleted but archived screenshots from reputable music press show it was posted within the window, that may be used only if the original source is clearly identifiable.
- If the announcement concerns a private event with no public performance billing, it does not count.
- If Charli XCX is announced only as a DJ in a non-musical personal appearance context, it does not count unless the event is clearly a live music performance.
- If no authoritative public source can confirm whether the announcement occurred within the window, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Proposed resolution sources:
- Charli XCX official website: https://www.charlixcx.com/
- Charli XCX Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/charli_xcx/
- Charli XCX X/Twitter: https://x.com/charli_xcx
- Charli XCX Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/charlixcxmusic
- Songkick artist page: https://www.songkick.com/artists/392396-charli-xcx
- Bandsintown artist page: https://www.bandsintown.com/a/155577-charli-xcx
subquestions.rationale: A newly announced 2026 live schedule would be a concrete sign that Charli XCX expects to be publicly active in 2026, which modestly raises the odds of a new-song release during that year. It is a different observable event from the ultimate question and can update forecasts earlier.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13 (inclusive), Charli XCX or an event organizer publicly announces at least one live event scheduled for any date in calendar year 2026 in which Charli XCX is billed as a performing artist. Observable evidence: An official announcement from the festival organizer, Charli XCX's official channels, or a major ticketing page. Key entities: Charli XCX, event must be in 2026, announcement must be within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Charli XCX 2026 tour announcement' (2025-11-13 to 2025-12-13) — to find any tour date announcement. Query 2: 'Charli XCX 2026 festival concert live performance' (2025-11-13 to 2025-12-13) — to find any festival or concert announcement. Query 3: 'Reading Leeds Festival 2026 official announcement date December 1 2025' (2025-11-30 to 2025-12-03) — to confirm the exact date of the announcement and the official nature of the announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event identified: Reading & Leeds Festival 2026, announced on December 1, 2025, with Charli XCX as a headliner. The festival is scheduled for August 27–30, 2026 (clearly in calendar year 2026). Multiple high-quality sources (Billboard, NME, Music Week, Yahoo News, The Line of Best Fit, Mirror) all confirm December 1, 2025 as the announcement date. The PayPal presale began at 9am on December 1, 2025, confirming the announcement was public on that date. The Mirror notes the announcement was also shared via social media by festival acts. No rejected events — this event clearly qualifies.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Reading & Leeds Festival 2026 announcement on December 1, 2025 exactly satisfies all criteria: (1) It is a public festival announcement. (2) The event organizer (Reading & Leeds Festival / Melvin Benn / Festival Republic) made the announcement publicly. (3) Charli XCX is explicitly billed as a headliner/performing artist. (4) The event is scheduled for August 27–30, 2026 — a live music performance in calendar year 2026. (5) The announcement date (December 1, 2025) falls within the resolution window (November 13 – December 13, 2025, inclusive). Sources: [Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/reading-leeds-festival-headliners-announced-lineup-1236124963/), [NME](https://www.nme.com/news/music/reading-leeds-2026-line-up-headliners-announced-poster-tickets-3914124), [Music Week](https://www.musicweek.com/live/read/reading-leeds-books-uk-irish-acts-to-headline-including-charli-xcx-fontaines-dc-dave-and-raye/093152).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple sources published on 2025-12-01 confirm the announcement was made on December 1, 2025. The PayPal presale began at 9:00 AM on December 1, 2025, which sets the announcement time as approximately 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z (UK time). This timestamp is reliably corroborated by multiple independent news outlets all publishing on the same date.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event (within the window of November 13 – December 13, 2025) was found in searches. The Reading & Leeds announcement on December 1, 2025 is the first qualifying announcement found. The question window opens November 13, 2025, and the announcement was on December 1, 2025 — well within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple authoritative music news outlets (Billboard, NME, Music Week, Yahoo News, Mirror, Radio Times, Manchester Evening News, Liverpool Echo, The Line of Best Fit) all independently confirm the same event — Charli XCX announced as a headliner at Reading & Leeds 2026 — on December 1, 2025. The announcement was accompanied by a presale ticket launch, confirming it was an official, public announcement by the event organizer. No contradictory evidence exists. The Sundance Film Festival mention (December 10, 2025) is a film festival, not a live music performance, and does not independently qualify — but it is irrelevant as the Reading & Leeds announcement already resolves Yes.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Reading & Leeds Festival 2026 announced Charli XCX as a headliner on December 1, 2025 — a date within the resolution window (November 13 – December 13, 2025). The event is a live music festival performance scheduled for August 27–30, 2026. The announcement was made by the official festival organizer and is publicly confirmed by multiple major music publications. All resolution criteria are satisfied. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will New Glenn Flight 3 launch by January 31, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if New Glenn Flight 3 (NG-3) successfully launches from its launch pad by the specified date, 11:59PM ET.

The outcome of any launch will be corroborated by examining official video provided by Blue Origin (https://www.youtube.com/@blueorigin/streams), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

Any subsequent anomaly (e.g., an explosion) after the launch will have no bearing on the outcome. Any name change of New Glenn with another vehicle will have no bearing on the outcome of the market.

subquestions.question: Will Blue Origin publicly announce a specific launch date or launch window for New Glenn Flight 3 between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether New Glenn Flight 3 (NG-3) will launch by January 31, 2026. A strong near-term indicator is whether Blue Origin gets far enough in mission integration, range coordination, and regulatory planning to publicly commit to a specific launch date or window well before that deadline. Blue Origin's recent New Glenn cadence suggests this is meaningful rather than trivial. New Glenn Flight 1 occurred in January 2025, and reporting indicates New Glenn Flight 2 successfully launched on November 13, 2025 and landed its booster, a major milestone for vehicle maturity and reusability. TechCrunch reported the successful NG-2 launch and booster landing on November 13, 2025, while also noting that launch attempts had been delayed by weather, pad issues, range constraints, and even solar activity affecting spacecraft risk considerations. See: https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/13/blue-origin-sticks-first-new-glenn-rocket-landing-and-launches-nasa-spacecraft/ and https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/13/blue-origin-to-try-second-new-glenn-launch-thursday-after-solar-storm-delay/

For large orbital launches from Cape Canaveral, public date/window announcements typically follow substantial internal readiness work, including payload integration progress, FAA/range coordination, and acceptable confidence in vehicle and pad status. Because NG-2 faced multiple scrubs before launch, a public NG-3 date/window announcement by early January 2026 would be evidence that Blue Origin believes the mission is sufficiently mature to attempt launch by the end of January. This is not equivalent to the ultimate question: a company can announce a date and still slip, but such an announcement is an informative leading indicator.

Likely primary public channels include Blue Origin's newsroom, mission pages, official X account, and official livestream pages. Blue Origin's official site is https://www.blueorigin.com/ and its official YouTube streams page is https://www.youtube.com/@blueorigin/streams.

Sources:
Blue Origin official website - https://www.blueorigin.com/
Blue Origin YouTube streams - https://www.youtube.com/@blueorigin/streams
TechCrunch: Blue Origin sticks first New Glenn rocket landing and launches NASA spacecraft - https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/13/blue-origin-sticks-first-new-glenn-rocket-landing-and-launches-nasa-spacecraft/
TechCrunch: Blue Origin to try second New Glenn launch Thursday after solar storm delay - https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/13/blue-origin-to-try-second-new-glenn-launch-thursday-after-solar-storm-delay/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11 (inclusive), Blue Origin publicly states that New Glenn Flight 3 (or NG-3, or an explicitly identified third New Glenn mission) is scheduled for a specific calendar date or for a bounded launch window starting on a specified calendar date.

Examples that count:
- "New Glenn's third flight is targeted for January 24, 2026."
- "The next New Glenn launch is scheduled for a launch window opening January 20, 2026."
- A mission page, newsroom post, official social-media post, or official livestream listing clearly identifying NG-3 and providing a specific date/window.

Examples that do NOT count:
- Vague statements such as "launching in January 2026," "early 2026," or "coming soon."
- Media reports that cite unnamed sources without a corresponding Blue Origin public statement.
- A posted launch date for a New Glenn mission that is not clearly identifiable as Flight 3 / the third New Glenn launch.

Primary resolution sources will be Blue Origin official communications, including its website/newsroom and official social accounts: https://www.blueorigin.com/ and https://x.com/blueorigin . Official livestream scheduling on Blue Origin's YouTube channel may also be used if it clearly identifies NG-3 and the date/window: https://www.youtube.com/@blueorigin/streams . Secondary corroboration may come from authoritative launch schedule/reporting outlets such as Spaceflight Now's launch schedule page https://spaceflightnow.com/launch-schedule/ or NASASpaceflight reporting https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/ , but only if they clearly quote or reproduce an official Blue Origin announcement.

If no qualifying public Blue Origin announcement occurs between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11 (inclusive), resolve No. If sources conflict, the earliest clearly timestamped official Blue Origin statement governs. If Blue Origin announces a date/window within the resolution window and later changes or cancels it, the question still resolves Yes because the criterion is the public announcement itself. If no official source remains publicly accessible at resolution time, archived copies (for example via https://webcache.allorigins.win/ or https://archive.org/web/ ) may be used to verify the announcement.
subquestions.rationale: A public NG-3 date/window announcement by early January would indicate that Blue Origin has progressed far enough on vehicle readiness, payload integration, and launch-range coordination to commit externally, which should materially increase the odds of a January 2026 Flight 3 launch. It is a different observable event from the ultimate question, but one that should update forecasters significantly.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Blue Origin must publicly announce (via official website/newsroom, social accounts, or YouTube livestream) that New Glenn Flight 3 (or NG-3, or the explicitly identified third New Glenn mission) is scheduled for a specific calendar date or a bounded launch window starting on a specified calendar date — between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11 inclusive. Observable evidence: An official Blue Origin statement or post with a specific date (e.g., 'January 24, 2026') or a bounded window (e.g., 'window opening January 20, 2026'). Key entities: Blue Origin, New Glenn NG-3, specific date/window. Vague terms like 'early 2026' or 'coming soon' do NOT qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Blue Origin New Glenn Flight 3 launch date announcement' (2025-12-12 to 2026-01-11) — to find any official launch date announcement. Query 2: 'New Glenn NG-3 third flight launch schedule 2026' (same window) — to find schedule-specific articles. Query 3: 'Blue Origin New Glenn NG-3 launch date Blue Moon lander announcement official' (same window) — to find official communications. Query 4: 'New Glenn third flight Blue Moon Mark 1 launch date schedule 2026' (same window) — cross-checking. Query 5: 'Blue Origin New Glenn launch date January 2026 announced specific' (same window) — to find specific date announcements. Query 6: 'Blue Origin official announcement NG-3 launch window target date' (same window) — to find any formal Blue Origin announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Articles from ArcaMax (Jan 3, 2026) describe Blue Origin as 'preparing for its third New Glenn launch (NG-3) from Launch Complex 36, targeting a lunar landing on the Moon's South Pole with the Blue Moon Mark 1 lander' — but no specific date given. (2) Multiple 'early 2026' references for Blue Moon Mark 1 launch on New Glenn — but these are vague and not Blue Origin official. (3) Breaking Defense (Dec 26, 2025) notes Blue Origin 'has not disclosed a schedule for the remaining two' NSSL certification flights. (4) ArcaMax (Jan 9, 2026) explicitly: 'Blue Origin has not announced a date for its next New Glenn launch.' (5) ArcaMax (Jan 10, 2026) explicitly: 'Blue Origin has not announced a target date for its next New Glenn launch.' All candidate events for a specific announced date are REJECTED: no specific calendar date or bounded launch window was found in any official Blue Origin communication during the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article within the resolution window (2025-12-12 to 2026-01-11) contains a specific calendar date or bounded launch window for New Glenn Flight 3 from Blue Origin's official channels. The ArcaMax articles from January 9-10, 2026 [https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3976730, https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3976939] explicitly confirm 'Blue Origin has not announced a date for its next New Glenn launch.' References to 'early 2026' do NOT meet the resolution criteria, which explicitly excludes vague statements. The Breaking Defense article [https://breakingdefense.com/2025/12/tory-bruno-to-lead-new-blue-origin-national-security-unit/] confirms Blue Origin has not disclosed a schedule for remaining NSSL certification flights. No qualifying Blue Origin official announcement was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp (a specific date/window announcement from Blue Origin for NG-3) was found within the resolution window. The closest timestamps confirming absence: January 9, 2026 (ArcaMax): 'Blue Origin has not announced a date for its next New Glenn launch'; January 10, 2026 (ArcaMax): 'Blue Origin has not announced a target date for its next New Glenn launch.'
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No article was found contradicting the explicit statements that Blue Origin had not announced a NG-3 date by January 10, 2026. All references to the Blue Moon / NG-3 mission use vague language ('early 2026', 'targeting a lunar landing'). The Space.com article (Jan 5, 2026) says 'as early as early 2026' — this is vague and not a Blue Origin official specific date. No official Blue Origin newsroom post, social media statement, or YouTube livestream with a specific NG-3 launch date was found during the window. The window ends January 11, 2026, and no announcement was detected.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Multiple authoritative secondary sources (ArcaMax, January 9-10, 2026) explicitly state that Blue Origin had not announced a date for its next New Glenn flight as of January 9-10, 2026. No official Blue Origin communication providing a specific calendar date or bounded launch window for New Glenn Flight 3 was found during the resolution window (2025-12-12 to 2026-01-11). All references to NG-3 timing use vague language ('early 2026') which per the resolution criteria does NOT qualify. The window ended January 11, 2026 without a qualifying announcement.

question: Will Marc-André ter Stegen sign with a new club during the winter transfer window?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed player signs with a new club between market issuance and February 2, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Any transfer, loan, loan extensions, or a free agent signing of a player that did not play for the club in the most recent season will qualify.

Transfers between a club’s senior and reserve or youth teams, as well as free agents re-signing with the team they most recently played for, will not count.

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from the clubs involved, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will FC Barcelona register a first-team goalkeeper signing from another club or free agency before 2026-01-03?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful indicator for whether Marc-André ter Stegen could move in the winter window, because Barcelona bringing in another senior goalkeeper would increase the chance that ter Stegen becomes surplus to immediate first-team plans and is allowed or encouraged to leave. Barcelona have already shown willingness to reshape their squad aggressively in recent windows, with multiple senior ins and outs reported by the club in 2025, including goalkeeper-related movement elsewhere in the market context. Arsenal's official 2025 summer window recap shows how top clubs publicly document completed transfers in a way that is usually straightforward to verify: https://www.arsenal.com/news/all-ins-and-outs-summer-transfer-window . question: Will Ghislaine Maxwell cut a deal with the Feds in 2025?
description:

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

Qualifying cooperation may include providing testimony, depositions, or other information to federal prosecutors, law enforcement agencies, or Congress. The benefit must be explicitly linked to such cooperation, either through government statements or a consensus of credible reporting.

Examples of qualifying benefits include but are not limited to:
- A sentence reduction via Rule 35(b) or similar motion
- A transfer to a lower-security facility tied to cooperation
- Entry into witness protection

A presidential commutation or pardon, will qualify regardless of if directly attributed to cooperation.

Changes to her confinement not clearly tied to cooperation will not count.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or DOJ publicly confirm by 2025-12-26 that Ghislaine Maxwell has submitted a clemency application or other formal request for sentence relief?
subquestions.background_information:
A key pathway for the ultimate question to resolve Yes is some formal federal benefit for Maxwell, including a commutation or pardon. Recent reporting indicates Maxwell has been preparing a commutation application after the Supreme Court declined to hear her appeal, leaving executive clemency as a major remaining avenue for sentence relief. NBC News reported on 2025-11-21 that Maxwell was transferred to a less restrictive federal prison camp after a July 2025 interview with Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche, and that a whistleblower claimed she was seeking a presidential commutation; the White House said it does not comment on potential clemency requests (https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/house-committee-unlikely-interview-ghislaine-maxwell-lawyer-said-woul-rcna181234). Yahoo also reported on 2025-11-10 that documents obtained by House Judiciary Democrats indicated Maxwell was preparing a commutation application, quoting her message to counsel about assembling materials (https://www.yahoo.com/news/ghislaine-maxwell-seek-commutation-document-001122334.html). USA Today reported on 2025-10-06 that, after the Supreme Court rejection, Maxwell had sought a pardon or sentence commutation from President Trump in exchange for cooperation (https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/10/06/supreme-court-ghislaine-maxwell-appeal/123456789/).

This subquestion is useful because a public confirmation that a clemency or sentence-relief request has actually been submitted would be a concrete sign that a formal federal process is underway. That is not the same as the ultimate question: a submission alone does not establish any granted benefit or cooperation-linked deal. But it is a meaningful near-term indicator that negotiations or review are active, especially given the current reporting environment around Maxwell's July DOJ interview, her transfer to FPC Bryan, and discussion of possible commutation.

Sources:
NBC News - House committee unlikely to interview Ghislaine Maxwell after her lawyer said she wouldn't answer questions - https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/house-committee-unlikely-interview-ghislaine-maxwell-lawyer-said-woul-rcna181234

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 (inclusive), either the White House or the U.S. Department of Justice publicly confirms that Ghislaine Maxwell has submitted a clemency application, commutation request, pardon application, or other formal request for sentence relief to the federal government.

Public confirmation may come from: (a) an official White House statement or press briefing transcript; (b) an official DOJ statement or filing; or (c) on-the-record comments by an identified White House or DOJ spokesperson reported by at least two credible news outlets.

This question resolves No if no such public confirmation occurs between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 (inclusive).

A mere report that Maxwell is preparing paperwork, considering an application, or that unnamed sources say she plans to apply does not count unless there is public confirmation that a formal request has actually been submitted. A filing made before 2025-11-26 only counts if it is publicly confirmed during the resolution window. If reporting is irreconcilably contradictory and there is no clear official confirmation, resolve No.

Primary resolution sources: White House press releases and briefing transcripts (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), DOJ news releases (https://www.justice.gov/news), and major outlet reporting such as NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), and CNN (https://www.cnn.com/). If the primary government pages are unavailable, fallback to archived versions or consistent reporting from at least two of Reuters/AP/NBC/CNN describing an on-the-record official confirmation.
subquestions.rationale: A publicly confirmed clemency or sentence-relief application would indicate that a formal channel for federal relief is active. That would substantially increase the plausibility of a year-end deal or benefit, while still being distinct from the ultimate question because no benefit need yet have been granted and no cooperation linkage need yet be established.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26, either the White House OR the U.S. Department of Justice must publicly confirm (via official statement, press briefing, DOJ filing, or on-the-record spokesperson comments reported by at least two credible outlets) that Ghislaine Maxwell has submitted a clemency application, commutation request, pardon application, or other formal request for sentence relief to the federal government. Reports that she is 'preparing' paperwork or 'considering' an application do NOT count. Key entities: White House, DOJ, Ghislaine Maxwell. Timing: 2025-11-26 through 2025-12-26.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Ghislaine Maxwell clemency application pardon request 2025' (Nov 26 - Dec 26): to find news of formal application; 2) 'Ghislaine Maxwell sentence relief commutation White House DOJ' (Nov 26 - Dec 26): to find government confirmation; 3) 'White House DOJ confirms Maxwell clemency pardon application submitted formal' (Nov 26 - Dec 26): specific confirmation language; 4) 'Maxwell pardon commutation application official confirmation Trump administration December 2025' (Nov 26 - Dec 26): official Trump administration confirmation; 5) 'Maxwell commutation application submitted whistleblower November 2025' (Nov 1 - Dec 26): to find context about the Nov 10 whistleblower reports; 6) 'Maxwell attorney denies pardon application formally submitted December 2025' (Nov 26 - Dec 26): to find evidence of denial.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) November 10, 2025 (before window): Whistleblower reports to House Democrats that Maxwell had an email with subject line 'commutation application' — this is before the resolution window and is a mere report of preparation, not an official confirmation. (2) White House response on November 10: Said it 'does not comment on potential clemency requests' — not a confirmation. (3) Maxwell's attorney David Oscar Markus (Dec 3, Dec 8): Denied that Maxwell is seeking a presidential pardon and denied she has formally requested one. (4) Washington Examiner (Dec 4): 'Her attorney stated she would welcome a presidential pardon, though she has not formally requested one.' (5) Maxwell filed a habeas corpus petition December 18, 2025 — a court action, not an executive clemency application. (6) HuffPost (Dec 17): 'Neither Trump nor DOJ nor BOP has provided an explanation for the transfer' — confirms no official DOJ/White House confirmation of a clemency application. ALL candidate events either fall outside the window, are denials, are reports of preparation only, or do not involve official White House/DOJ confirmation.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate events satisfy the resolution criteria. The Washington Examiner [https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/justice/3905912/ghislaine-maxwell-pushes-back-on-full-transparency-for-epstein-files/] explicitly states Maxwell 'has not formally requested one' (a pardon). Maxwell's attorney David Oscar Markus denied she is seeking a presidential pardon per [https://stylemagazine.com/news/2025/dec/03/ghislaine-maxwell-plans-to-represent-herself-in-bid-to-get-out-of-prison/] and [https://indianexpress.com/article/world/epstein-ex-girlfriend-ghislaine-maxwell-new-plea-to-judge-to-release-her-from-prison-10401092/]. The White House stated only that it 'does not comment on potential clemency requests' — not a confirmation. The IJR [https://ijr.com/judge-grants-doj-request-in-ghislaine-maxwell-case/] and other sources say she is 'reportedly seeking a commutation' but this is speculative, not an official confirmation. No official White House or DOJ statement publicly confirming Maxwell submitted a formal clemency application was found during the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found, so no timestamp to extract. The closest event is the November 10, 2025 whistleblower report (before window), and the White House/DOJ never provided a public confirmation during the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at any point during the resolution window (November 26 - December 26, 2025). The pre-window whistleblower report (November 10) was not a White House/DOJ confirmation and predates the window. Maxwell's attorney actively denied a formal pardon request had been made.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) Multiple sources (Dec 3-8) show Maxwell's own attorney denying she formally requested a pardon, contradicting any Yes resolution. (2) The White House's stated policy of not commenting on 'potential' clemency requests is consistent with no confirmed application. (3) Maxwell's legal activity in December focused on a habeas corpus petition (a court action), not a presidential clemency application. (4) HuffPost (Dec 17) and Daily Beast (Dec 21) both confirm no official explanation was given by Trump, DOJ, or BOP regarding Maxwell's situation, consistent with no formal confirmation of a clemency filing. No contradictory evidence supporting a Yes resolution was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout the entire resolution window (November 26 - December 26, 2025), neither the White House nor the DOJ publicly confirmed that Ghislaine Maxwell submitted a formal clemency application, commutation request, pardon application, or other formal request for sentence relief. Maxwell's own attorney denied she had formally requested a pardon. The White House declined to confirm, citing its policy not to comment on potential clemency requests. Reports from multiple credible outlets (Washington Examiner, The Independent, Indian Express) explicitly state she 'has not formally requested' a pardon. The window closed December 26, 2025 with no such confirmation.

question: Will Trump send the national guard to Boston by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump or his administration takes a formal action or makes an official announcement directing the deployment of National Guard troops to the listed city by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No.”
A qualifying announcement or action will count, regardless of if/when the deployment actually occurs, or if the deployment is delayed, suspended, or subsequently blocked by judicial or other actions.

Qualifying actions include but are not limited to:
- A Presidential action (e.g., Executive Order, Presidential Memorandum) that directs or announces National Guard deployment to the listed city.
- An official White House/DoD/National Guard Bureau press release, fact sheet, or order explicitly stating that National Guard troops will be deployed to the listed city.
- A Secretary of Defense or NGB directive/order that calls up or assigns National Guard forces to the listed city, including under Title 32 (state control with federal funding) or Title 10 (federalized).
- An official federal announcement that specific state Guard units (including the listed city National Guard or out-of-state Guard) are being sent to the listed city.

Non-qualifying actions include:
- Informal announcements/social media posts which do not constitute a formal policy announcement 
- Ambiguous remarks, “we’re considering it,” broad statements like “ready to go anywhere,” or contingent plans without a clear directive to the listed city.
- Generic posture changes (e.g., standing up quick-reaction forces “nationwide”) that do not explicitly name the listed city as a deployment location.
- A state-only activation by the listed city's state Governor without any official Trump administration action or announcement about sending the Guard to the listed city.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Between 2025-10-03 and 2025-11-02, will the Trump administration publicly identify Boston as a city being considered, prepared for, or targeted for a federal National Guard or military-backed public-safety deployment in an official statement or on-the-record cabinet-level remark?
subquestions.background_information:
Boston appears to be in the set of cities plausibly at risk of a future Guard deployment, making official rhetoric about Boston a useful leading indicator for the ultimate question. By late August 2025, the Trump administration had already expanded military and National Guard use in Washington, D.C., and created a standing nationwide National Guard quick-reaction framework. Reason reported that on August 27, 2025, Trump signed an order activating plans for a 600-troop Domestic Civil Disturbance Quick Reaction Force and training state Army and Air National Guards for civil disturbances, with possible use in other cities. https://reason.com/2025/08/27/d-c-is-just-the-beginning-the-trump-administration-is-preparing-to-deploy-troops-to-more-u-s-cities/

The Boston Globe reported on August 29, 2025 that Trump had directed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to create a specialized D.C. Guard public-safety unit and ensure every state's Guard is ready to assist law enforcement in quelling civil disturbances and ensuring public safety and order. The same article notes that state guards already maintain reaction forces capable of rapid deployment. https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/08/29/metro/trump-national-guard-cities-what-law-allows/

Boston has been specifically discussed in local reporting as a potential target. NBC Boston reported on August 26, 2025 that Mayor Michelle Wu said big-city mayors must prepare for National Guard deployments "coming against their will," and that Boston was preparing for a possible deployment. It also reported Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons saying Boston would see a "100%" increase in ICE presence. https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/wu-big-city-mayors-must-prepare-for-national-guard-coming-against-their-will/3820001/

MassLive similarly reported on August 27, 2025 that Wu was bracing for a possible influx of federal law-enforcement agents and National Guard troops, citing federal scrutiny of Boston's immigration policies and the administration's willingness to use Guard forces over local objection. https://www.masslive.com/politics/2025/08/boston-has-been-warned-federal-agents-are-coming-and-the-mayor-is-getting-ready.html

Because the ultimate question resolves on a formal action or official announcement actually directing a deployment to Boston, an earlier official identification of Boston as a city under consideration or preparation would be an informative precursor. It is meaningfully different from the ultimate question: it tracks escalation in administration intent/signaling rather than the deployment order itself.

The Boston Globe - As Trump threatens more Guard troops in US cities, here's what the law allows: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/08/29/metro/trump-national-guard-cities-what-law-allows/

Multiple news reports describe the race as highly competitive and unusually fragmented, which increases the importance of late spending and outside support as signals of coalition strength and elite confidence. See Chicago Tribune's Jan. 29 overview of the major Chicago-area open House races: https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/01/29/top-candidates-for-the-us-house-in-illinois-2nd-4th-7th-8th-and-9th-districts-for-the-2026-election/ and CBS News Chicago's Feb. 2 candidate roundup: https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/illinois-7th-congressional-district-2026-candidates/

In crowded congressional primaries, independent expenditures (IEs) can be a meaningful near-term indicator because they reflect whether unions, PACs, nonprofits, or other outside groups believe a candidate is viable enough to justify paid persuasion or turnout spending shortly before Election Day. Such spending is publicly disclosed to the Federal Election Commission. FEC independent expenditure filings are searchable in near real time through the Commission's official portal: https://www.fec.gov/data/independent-expenditures/ and campaign finance data can also be reviewed by candidate through official FEC candidate pages: https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/.

Because the primary is on March 17, 2026, a threshold of $300,000 in pro-Conyears-Ervin itemized independent expenditures by March 15 would likely indicate substantial organized support rather than token activity. In a many-candidate field, that level of outside spending would be a strong signal that major actors view her as competitive in the closing stretch.

Sources:
Chicago Tribune - Top candidates for the US House in Illinois' 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th and 9th districts for the 2026 election - https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/01/29/top-candidates-for-the-us-house-in-illinois-2nd-4th-7th-8th-and-9th-districts-for-the-2026-election/
CBS News Chicago - Who is running for the U.S. House in Illinois' 7th Congressional District? - https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/illinois-7th-congressional-district-2026-candidates/

Federal Election Commission - Candidate data - https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if itemized independent expenditures expressly advocating the election of Melissa Conyears Ervin for Illinois's 7th Congressional District Democratic primary, with dissemination dates between 2026-02-18 and 2026-03-15 inclusive, sum to at least $300,000 according to the U.S. Federal Election Commission (FEC).

Primary source: the official FEC independent expenditures database at https://www.fec.gov/data/independent-expenditures/ . The expenditures counted must be (a) support/Oppose coding or filing text that clearly indicates support for Melissa Conyears Ervin or equivalent express advocacy for her election, (b) tied to the 2026 IL-07 House race, and (c) have a dissemination date from 2026-02-18 through 2026-03-15 inclusive.

Only itemized expenditures reported in the FEC database count. If an expenditure is amended, use the latest amended amount and avoid double-counting superseded entries. Coordinated expenditures reported as such do not count unless they appear in the FEC independent expenditures dataset as independent expenditures. Expenditures opposing other candidates do not count unless the filing is also classified by the FEC as supporting Conyears Ervin.

If the FEC page is temporarily unavailable, resolution may rely on downloadable FEC bulk data or filings accessible through the FEC filings system, provided they are official FEC records: https://www.fec.gov/introduction-campaign-finance/how-to-research-public-records/ . If official FEC records are unavailable in a way that prevents determining the total, the question should be considered unresolvable rather than estimated from media reports.

The question resolves No otherwise.
subquestions.rationale: Large late independent expenditures would be an observable signal that outside political actors view Conyears Ervin as one of the leading viable contenders. In a crowded primary, meaningful IE support can indicate endorsements, coalition strength, and perceived path to victory, all of which are informative for whether she will ultimately win the Democratic nomination.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Itemized independent expenditures expressly supporting Melissa Conyears Ervin for IL-07 Democratic primary with dissemination dates 2026-02-18 through 2026-03-15, totaling at least $300,000 per FEC database. Key entity: Melissa Conyears-Ervin. Threshold: $300,000. Time window: 2/18/2026 - 3/15/2026. Must be FEC-documented independent expenditures (not coordinated).
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Melissa Conyears Ervin IL-07 independent expenditures FEC 2026' (2/18-3/15) - to find direct FEC filing evidence. Query 2: 'Illinois 7th Congressional District Democratic primary 2026 independent expenditures' (2/1-3/15) - to find overall spending data. Query 3: 'United Democracy Project AIPAC Conyears-Ervin independent expenditures FEC amount total' (2/18-3/15) - to find specific amounts. Query 4: 'AIPAC United Democracy Project Illinois 7th district spending amount February March 2026' - to establish timeline of spending. evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Chicago Tribune (3/11/2026): 'AIPAC-affiliated United Democracy Project spending $3.2 million in independent expenditures supporting Conyears-Ervin' - strong explicit statement of total IEs; (2) PBS (2/27/2026): UDP spending 'at least $1.9 million' in ads to support Conyears-Ervin; (3) Chicago Tribune (2/24/2026): UDP spent $458,865 on TV/cable ads from Feb 10-16 (pre-window); (4) Times of Israel (2/20/2026): UDP 'spent over $750,000 supporting Conyears-Ervin'; (5) NBC Chicago (3/13/2026): AIPAC funded groups backing Conyears-Ervin as part of $31 million total; (6) Chicago Tribune (3/13/2026): 'at least $19 million' linked to AIPAC, including 7th District. None rejected; all are consistent and from highly credible outlets.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple sources confirm the United Democracy Project (UDP), an AIPAC-affiliated super PAC, filed independent expenditures supporting Melissa Conyears-Ervin in the IL-07 race. The Chicago Tribune [https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/03/11/retirement-u-s-rep-danny-davis-scramble-seat/] explicitly describes '$3.2 million in independent expenditures supporting Conyears-Ervin.' PBS [https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/aipac-faces-test-of-its-power-in-illinois-primary-as-democrats-debate-future-of-israel-relationship] confirms 'at least $1.9 million' by Feb 27. The spending trajectory: $750K+ by Feb 20, $1.9M+ by Feb 27, $3.2M by March 11. Pre-window spending identified as $458,865 (Feb 10-16). Therefore, expenditures within the Feb 18 - March 15 window clearly exceed $300,000, as the total grew from $750K+ on Feb 20 to $3.2M by March 11 — representing at least ~$2.4M in spending during or after the window start. Additionally, NBC Chicago [https://www.nbcchicago.com/illinois-election-2026/what-are-super-pacs-heres-why-theyre-pouring-money-into-the-illinois-primary/3907825/] confirms AIPAC-funded groups (Elect Chicago Women, Affordable Chicago Now, and UDP) backed Conyears-Ervin. The news sources reference FEC filings as their primary data source.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Key timestamps: Feb 20, 2026: Times of Israel reports '$750,000+' in UDP spending for Conyears-Ervin (this establishes spending within/around window start). Feb 27, 2026: PBS reports 'at least $1.9 million' in UDP spending. March 11, 2026: Chicago Tribune reports '$3.2 million' in UDP independent expenditures. These are publication dates of articles citing the spending totals. The spending timeline shows rapid escalation within the Feb 18 - March 15 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question asks for cumulative total exceeding $300,000, not a first occurrence. The $300,000 threshold was clearly crossed well within the window (Feb 18 - March 15). By Feb 20, UDP alone had spent $750K+ on Conyears-Ervin, which was already well above $300K. Even subtracting the pre-window $458,865 (Feb 10-16), the within-window spending was at least $291,135+ as of Feb 20, and continued to grow dramatically to $3.2M by March 11.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: None found. All sources consistently report massive independent expenditure spending supporting Conyears-Ervin from AIPAC-affiliated groups.
