question: Will 7-9 SpaceX Starship launches successfully reach Space in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if between 7 (inclusive) and 9 (inclusive) SpaceX Starship launches successfully reach an altitude of 62 miles above sea level between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A successful launch is defined as the Starship taking off from its launchpad and reaching a minimum altitude of 62 miles above sea level. Any subsequent anomaly (e.g. an explosion) after the vehicle reaches 62 miles will have no bearing on the outcome.

The primary resolution source for this market will be SpaceX’s official video feed of the launches (e.g. via SpaceX YouTube Channel), as well as secondary video feeds or written reports if necessary. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX conduct at least one Starship launch attempt that lifts off from the pad between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether 7 to 9 Starship launches will successfully reach space during calendar year 2025. By late August 2025, publicly reported information indicates SpaceX had completed its 10th Starship test flight on 2025-08-26/27, and that this was the fourth Starship flight of 2025. Yahoo reported that Flight 10 was "the vehicle’s fourth test in 2025" and noted Elon Musk’s statement that the next three launches could occur at a cadence of "every 3 to 4 weeks." This makes near-term launch cadence a key crux for the year-end count of successful launches: to end 2025 with 7-9 successful space-reaching launches, SpaceX likely needs to keep launching frequently through the remainder of the year. https://www.yahoo.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-most-successful-2025-when-is-flight-11-120000000.html

Recent performance also matters. Multiple outlets reported that Starship Flight 10 successfully reached roughly 192-200 km altitude and ended a streak of failures, suggesting improved technical readiness. Live Science reported that on 2025-08-26, Starship completed its 10th test flight and reached a peak altitude of about 200 km. https://www.livescience.com/space/space-exploration/10th-time-lucky-spacexs-starship-nails-successful-test-flight-after-string-of-explosive-setbacks Wired likewise reported the vehicle reached 192 km on Aug. 26, 2025. https://www.wired.com/story/spacex-starship-finally-pulls-off-a-successful-test-flight/

Regulatory capacity is less of a bottleneck than before. The FAA announced in May 2025 that it had modified SpaceX’s Starship/Super Heavy license to authorize up to 25 launches a year from Starbase, Texas, up from 5. That means a September launch attempt is operationally plausible if SpaceX is ready. https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-updates-spacex-starship-flight-9-license

Because the ultimate market counts only launches that reach space, a near-term question about whether SpaceX can execute another actual liftoff soon is informative without merely restating the final target. If SpaceX cannot even mount one more Starship liftoff by October 1, the path to ending 2025 with 7-9 successful space-reaching launches becomes materially less likely.

Sources:
FAA updates SpaceX Starship Flight 9 license — https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-updates-spacex-starship-flight-9-license
Yahoo: SpaceX launches Starship on most successful test mission of 2025. When is flight 11? — https://www.yahoo.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-most-successful-2025-when-is-flight-11-120000000.html
Live Science: 10th time lucky! SpaceX's Starship nails successful test flight after string of explosive setbacks — https://www.livescience.com/space/space-exploration/10th-time-lucky-spacexs-starship-nails-successful-test-flight-after-string-of-explosive-setbacks
Wired: SpaceX Starship Finally Pulls Off a Successful Test Flight — https://www.wired.com/story/spacex-starship-finally-pulls-off-a-successful-test-flight/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if at least one SpaceX Starship launch attempt lifts off from its launch mount between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive, using UTC for the date window).

For this question, a qualifying event requires all of the following:
1. The vehicle is a SpaceX Starship/Super Heavy integrated launch vehicle.
2. The launch occurs from a recognized Starship launch site.
3. The vehicle visibly leaves the launch mount/pad under its own power; a static fire or engine test that does not result in liftoff does not count.
4. The liftoff timestamp, converted to UTC if necessary, falls between 2025-09-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC.

This question resolves No if no such liftoff occurs during that window.

Primary resolution sources:
- SpaceX official updates/video, including the SpaceX X account and livestream archives: https://x.com/SpaceX and https://www.youtube.com/@SpaceX
- Spaceflight Now mission status and launch coverage: https://spaceflightnow.com/
- NASASpaceflight launch coverage: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/

Resolution procedure:
- Use SpaceX's official livestream/archive or official post if available to establish whether a liftoff occurred and the date/time.
- If SpaceX materials are unavailable or ambiguous, use concordant reporting from Spaceflight Now and/or NASASpaceflight.
- If a countdown is recycled, scrubbed, or terminated before pad departure, that does not count.
- If a launch begins before 2025-10-02 UTC but local-date reporting differs, UTC controls.
- If no authoritative public evidence is available by the time of resolution, the question should be treated as unresolvable rather than inferred.

Sources for resolution:
SpaceX on X — https://x.com/SpaceX
SpaceX YouTube — https://www.youtube.com/@SpaceX
Spaceflight Now — https://spaceflightnow.com/
NASASpaceflight — https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/
subquestions.rationale: Launch cadence over the next month is a strong operational indicator for the year-end count of successful Starship space-reaching launches. A September liftoff would signal that SpaceX is maintaining the roughly 3-4 week tempo discussed publicly and keeps alive a plausible path to 7-9 successful launches in 2025; failure to launch at all by October 1 would make the ultimate outcome notably less likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: At least one SpaceX Starship/Super Heavy integrated vehicle liftoff from a recognized launch site, with liftoff timestamp between 2025-09-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC. Observable evidence: official SpaceX reports, SpaceX livestream/X posts, or concordant reporting from Spaceflight Now/NASASpaceflight confirming liftoff within that window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'SpaceX Starship launch liftoff September 2025' (Sept 1–Oct 1) — to find any launch in window. 2. 'SpaceX Starship Flight 9 10 launch attempt 2025' (Aug–Oct) — to find adjacent flights. 3. 'SpaceX Starship Flight 10 liftoff date August 26 2025' — to confirm Flight 10 was before window. 4. 'SpaceX Starship launch September 3 4 2025 Starbase Texas' — to investigate apparent September launch references. 5. 'SpaceX Starship Flight 11 launch date October 2025' — to confirm next flight was after window. 6. 'Starship Flight 11 launch schedule preparations September October 2025 no launch' — to confirm no September launch.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate 1: Starship Flight 10 — Multiple authoritative sources (AP News, Space.com, ExtremeTech, Anadolu Agency, Tesla North, India Today) confirm liftoff on August 26, 2025 at 6:30 p.m. CT (11:30 p.m. UTC) — REJECTED: liftoff was BEFORE the September 1 window. Candidate 2: KSL.com article (published Sept 3, 2025) states 'SpaceX's 403-foot-tall Starship lifted off from a launch pad in southern Texas on September 3, 2025' — REJECTED: This is an article published September 3 about the August 26 Flight 10 launch. The date 'September 3' refers to the article publication date, not the launch date. All other sources confirm Flight 10 was August 26. Candidate 3: Starship Flight 11 — All sources confirm targeting October 13, 2025 — REJECTED: outside window (after October 1). No other Starship launch candidates identified in the September 1–October 1, 2025 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No Starship liftoff occurred within the September 1–October 1, 2025 UTC window. [Space.com](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-test-fires-next-super-heavy-booster-for-starships-11th-upcoming-launch-video) confirms Flight 10 lifted off August 26, 2025. [ExtremeTech](https://www.extremetech.com/aerospace/spacex-targets-oct-13-for-next-starship-launch) confirms Flight 11 targeted October 13, 2025. Multiple sources from September 30, 2025 (end of window) confirm Flight 11 was still in preparation for an October 13 launch, with no Starship having launched in September. The criteria require liftoff within the window — this condition was not met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No liftoff timestamp within the September 1–October 1, 2025 window can be extracted because no qualifying event occurred. Flight 10 liftoff: August 26, 2025, 6:30 p.m. CT (23:30 UTC) — before window. Flight 11 target: October 13, 2025, 6:15 p.m. CT (23:15 UTC) — after window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: KSL.com's 'September 3' date appears to be an error in the article (publication date vs. launch date) — all other sources unanimously confirm Flight 10 launched August 26. AP News (published September 9, 2025) explicitly states 'SpaceX launched its Starship on Tuesday night from Starbase in south Texas at just after 6:30 p.m.' — and Flight 10 was on Tuesday August 26, not in September. Multiple sources from late September 2025 confirm SpaceX was still preparing for Flight 11 with a target of October 13, implying no Starship launch had occurred in September 2025. The spacedaily.com articles dated 'September 4' about scrubbing Starship Flight 10 are AFP dispatches with incorrect publication dates (they were originally published around August 24-25, then republished/cached with September dates). The content clearly refers to the August 24 scrub. There is no credible evidence of a Starship launch in September 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence conclusively shows no Starship liftoff occurred between September 1 and October 1, 2025 UTC. Flight 10 launched on August 26, 2025 (before window). Flight 11 was targeted for October 13, 2025 (after window). During the September 2025 window, SpaceX was conducting static fire tests and pad preparations for Flight 11 but did not conduct any Starship launch attempt. By September 30, 2025, SpaceX had publicly confirmed Flight 11 for October 13, confirming the window would close without a Starship launch. Resolution: No. The window closed without a qualifying liftoff, so resolution_datetime = 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z.

question: Will OpenAI acquire Chrome by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if it is announced that the Chrome web browser will be, has been, or is being acquired by or merged with OpenAI by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement by Google/Alphabet will qualify for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether the announced acquisition or merger actually occurs.

Partnerships, integrations, licensing deals, or other forms of collaboration between Chrome and OpenAI that do not constitute an acquisition or merger will not count toward a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Google/Alphabet, or OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce by 2025-10-31 that it has launched or is launching a standalone web browser product?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether OpenAI could acquire Chrome is whether OpenAI is actively pursuing browser distribution at all. In August 2025, Sam Altman said OpenAI would be interested in buying Chrome if it were available: 'If Chrome is really going to sell, we should take a look at it,' while also indicating skepticism that Chrome would actually be sold. Multiple reports also state that OpenAI has been developing its own AI browser, suggesting the company sees the browser layer as strategically important for distribution, search, and user interaction. See Mint (2025-08-16): https://www.livemint.com/technology/tech-news/openai-could-buy-google-chrome-says-sam-altman-but-only-if-this-happens-11755359304362.html ; TEMPO.CO (2025-08-20): https://en.tempo.co/read/2050388/sam-altman-says-openai-interested-in-acquiring-chrome-browser ; and Computerworld (2025-09-09), which notes 'OpenAI is planning its own AI browser': https://www.computerworld.com/article/4017683/atlassian-exec-details-the-610m-browser-company-acquisition.html.

The broader market context also matters. Google was reportedly not forced to divest Chrome in the September 2025 antitrust ruling, reducing the immediate likelihood of a forced sale and making any eventual OpenAI acquisition less straightforward. AP reported that Judge Amit Mehta rejected the DOJ request to force a Chrome sale as 'incredibly messy and highly risky': https://apnews.com/article/google-antitrust-chrome-search-remedies-mehta-4f0f0f0f0f0f . Bloomberg Law similarly described the ruling as a mixed outcome for AI startups seeking to challenge Google: https://news.bloomberglaw.com/antitrust/google-antitrust-ruling-a-mixed-outcome-for-ai-startups-q-and-ai.

If OpenAI publicly launches its own browser in October 2025, that is evidence that OpenAI is investing in browser distribution and consumer surface area. Depending on the launch framing, it could either increase the chance of a Chrome deal (because OpenAI clearly wants a browser foothold) or decrease it (because OpenAI now has a substitute path). Either way, it is a meaningful crux for the ultimate question.

Sources:
Mint - OpenAI could buy Google Chrome, says Sam Altman: https://www.livemint.com/technology/tech-news/openai-could-buy-google-chrome-says-sam-altman-but-only-if-this-happens-11755359304362.html
TEMPO.CO - Sam Altman Says OpenAI Interested in Acquiring Chrome Browser: https://en.tempo.co/read/2050388/sam-altman-says-openai-interested-in-acquiring-chrome-browser

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), OpenAI publicly announces that it has launched, is launching, or will imminently launch a standalone web browser product intended for general users or enterprise users.

For this question, a 'standalone web browser product' means software primarily described by OpenAI as a browser and capable of accessing arbitrary web pages, whether on desktop or mobile. It may be called a browser, AI browser, agentic browser, or similar. Merely adding browsing features to ChatGPT, adding a browser extension, releasing an in-app web view, or announcing a search feature does NOT count unless OpenAI explicitly describes the product itself as a browser.

Primary resolution sources will be official OpenAI communications, including OpenAI's newsroom/blog (https://openai.com/news/ and https://openai.com/blog), OpenAI's official X account or other verified OpenAI social accounts, or a press release or product page on https://openai.com/.

If no qualifying official OpenAI announcement appears during the window from 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-31 inclusive, resolve No.

If an announcement is ambiguous, it will count only if the official text explicitly identifies the product as a browser or describes functionality equivalent to a general-purpose standalone web browser. As fallback evidence, contemporaneous reporting from at least two credible outlets such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), The Verge (https://www.theverge.com/), or TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/) may be used to interpret the official announcement.

If OpenAI announces a browser after 2025-10-31, it does not count. If an announcement made within the window is later retracted, the question still resolves Yes so long as the original qualifying public announcement occurred within the window.

A public browser launch in October 2025 would reveal whether OpenAI is seriously investing in the browser layer right now, which is strong evidence about the strategic logic and urgency behind a possible Chrome acquisition.

question: U.S. x Russia Nuclear deal by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if an official agreement on nuclear arms control or strategic nuclear weapons limitation is reached between the United States and the Russian Federation between August 14, 2025 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only agreements that are publicly announced and acknowledged by both the U.S. and Russia will qualify. The agreement must pertain to nuclear arms control or limitation—such as a treaty, framework, or memorandum—addressing matters including (but not limited to) nuclear warheads, delivery systems, verification mechanisms, or strategic stability.

An extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty will qualify, provided it is publicly announced as a concluded agreement by both parties within the time frame. Exploratory discussions or stated intent to extend without a finalized agreement will not qualify.

Agreements that include both the United States and Russia as named parties—whether bilateral or as part of a broader multilateral framework—will qualify, provided the agreement directly addresses nuclear arms control.

The agreement does not need to be ratified or implemented for this market to resolve "Yes"; a formal announcement of a concluded agreement is sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the U.S. government (e.g., the White House, State Department) and/or the Russian Federation (e.g., the Kremlin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs). However, a clear and overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming that such an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the United States publicly announce, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, that it accepts in principle Russia’s proposal to continue observing New START’s central numerical limits for one year beyond February 5, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term crux for whether a formal U.S.-Russia nuclear deal is reached by the end of 2025 is whether Washington publicly accepts, at least in principle, Moscow’s September 2025 proposal to keep observing New START’s central limits for an additional year after the treaty’s scheduled expiration. On September 22, 2025, Vladimir Putin said Russia was prepared to continue adhering to New START’s central numerical limits for one year after February 5, 2026, if the United States did likewise; New START caps each side at 1,550 deployed strategic warheads and 700 deployed strategic delivery systems. Reuters coverage relayed by Firstpost and other outlets reported this proposal and its conditional nature: https://www.firstpost.com/world/will-only-be-viable-if-the-us-putin-proposes-conditional-one-year-extension-to-nuclear-weapons-treaty-13942092.html .

Public U.S. receptivity already appears mixed but not yet clearly formalized. Reuters reporting relayed by Firstpost on September 29 said White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt described Putin’s proposal as sounding “pretty good,” while also saying the decision was up to President Trump: https://www.firstpost.com/world/uk-french-arsenals-must-be-part-of-any-us-russia-arms-control-deal-says-kremlin-13950365.html . TASS also reported on October 5 that Trump said the proposal “sounds like a good idea,” while arms-control expert Daryl Kimball argued that the arrangement still needed to be formalized by the White House and Kremlin: https://tass.com/world/1887439 . These remarks suggest a possible pathway toward agreement, but they may fall short of an official U.S. acceptance in principle.

This is a useful indicator because a publicly announced U.S. acceptance of Russia’s offer would likely be the clearest short-term sign that both sides are moving from rhetorical openness toward an actual deal before year-end. Conversely, if no such public U.S. acceptance appears by the end of November, the odds of concluding a qualifying agreement by December 31, 2025 likely fall materially, given the limited remaining time and the need for bilateral acknowledgment.

Sources:
Firstpost (Reuters relayed) - Putin conditional one-year extension proposal: https://www.firstpost.com/world/will-only-be-viable-if-the-us-putin-proposes-conditional-one-year-extension-to-nuclear-weapons-treaty-13942092.html
Firstpost (Reuters relayed) - White House says proposal sounds "pretty good": https://www.firstpost.com/world/uk-french-arsenals-must-be-part-of-any-us-russia-arms-control-deal-says-kremlin-13950365.html
TASS - Trump says proposal "sounds like a good idea": https://tass.com/world/1887439

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, an official public statement by the White House, the U.S. Department of State, the U.S. Department of Defense, or the President of the United States clearly states that the United States accepts, approves, agrees to, or will join Russia’s proposal to continue observing New START’s central numerical limits for one year beyond 2026-02-05.

For avoidance of doubt, qualifying language must indicate U.S. acceptance in principle of the proposal itself, not merely that the idea is "interesting," "pretty good," under review, or worthy of discussion. Statements of intent to negotiate, explore, study, or discuss the proposal without saying the United States accepts/agrees to it do not qualify.

A Yes resolution may be based on any of the following primary sources published within the window 2025-10-31 through 2025-11-30:
- White House official website: https://www.whitehouse.gov/
- U.S. Department of State official website: https://www.state.gov/
- U.S. Department of Defense official website: https://www.defense.gov/
- Official presidential social media/accounts if clearly authentic and attributable to the President or White House.

If no such official U.S. statement is published during the window, this question resolves No.

Fallback: if an official statement is unavailable or ambiguous, a Yes resolution may also rely on a clear and overwhelming consensus from at least three credible reports published during the window, each explicitly stating that the U.S. government has publicly accepted Russia’s one-year continued-observance proposal, with at least one report quoting or linking to the relevant U.S. official statement. Suitable fallback reporting sources include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), and major U.S. newspapers of record.

If purported acceptance occurs outside the window beginning 2025-10-31 or after 2025-11-30, it does not count. If events are postponed beyond 2025-11-30 or no clear public U.S. acceptance appears by then, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question requires a publicly acknowledged U.S.-Russia nuclear arms control agreement by December 31, 2025. A public U.S. acceptance in principle of Russia’s one-year New START limits proposal is a distinct, earlier observable step that would strongly increase the odds of a qualifying agreement while not being identical to the final deal itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes resolution: An official U.S. public statement (from White House, State Dept, DoD, or President) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 must clearly and explicitly ACCEPT, APPROVE, AGREE TO, or state intent to JOIN Russia's proposal to continue observing New START's central numerical limits for one year beyond February 5, 2026. Mere 'consideration,' 'it sounds like a good idea,' 'under review,' or 'potentially' talking about it does NOT qualify. Entities: White House, State Dept, DoD, or President Trump. Threshold: explicit acceptance/agreement in principle.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'United States accept Russia New START nuclear limits proposal 2026' (Oct 31 - Nov 30) — to find US acceptance statement; 2) 'US Russia nuclear arms control New START one year extension 2025' (Oct 31 - Nov 30) — general extension coverage; 3) 'US State Department White House accept agree New START nuclear arms limits Russia November 2025' (Oct 31 - Nov 30) — specific US government acceptance; 4) 'Trump accept Russia New START proposal nuclear warhead limits agreement' (Oct 31 - Nov 30) — presidential-level acceptance; 5) 'Rubio State Department New START nuclear arms control announcement decision November 2025' (Nov 15-30) — later-window Rubio statements; 6) 'US nuclear arms control agreement Russia announcement late November 2025' (Nov 20-30) — late-window US response.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) Trump called Putin's proposal 'a good idea' on ~Oct 5, 2025 — falls outside the window AND does not constitute acceptance in principle per resolution criteria. (b) Secretary Rubio stated the US is 'considering' Russia's proposal (TASS, Nov 13) — this is explicitly NOT acceptance; it is 'under consideration.' (c) Lavrov (Russia) said US told Russia through diplomatic channels the issue is 'under consideration' (Nov 9) — Russian characterization of US stance, not acceptance. (d) CNN (Nov 16) states 'despite... Trump's initial positive response, no formal talks have begun'; White House official says Trump 'will decide... on his own timeline.' (e) TASS (Nov 13): Russia's Ulyanov says US 'has not yet responded' to proposals. (f) TASS/Russia (Nov 27): 'as of November 27, 2025, the US has not provided any response.' (g) Ryabkov (Nov 26): Russia-US relations 'remain at an early stage of normalization,' no ongoing dialogue on the issue. All evidence consistently shows the US was 'considering' the proposal but had NOT accepted it within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No qualifying event was found. The resolution criteria require an EXPLICIT US acceptance/agreement in principle, not consideration. Evidence: [TASS Nov 13](https://tass.com/world/2043047) reports Rubio said US is 'considering' Russia's proposal — explicitly not acceptance. [TASS Nov 13](https://tass.com/politics/2043379) Russian envoy says 'no reaction yet from US.' [CNN Nov 16](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/11/16/politics/us-russia-nuclear-treaty) reports 'no formal talks have begun' and White House says Trump will decide 'on his own timeline.' [TASS Nov 27](https://tass.com/world/2049745) confirms as of Nov 27 US has not responded. [TASS Nov 27](https://tass.com/world/2050265) Scott Ritter confirms 'as of November 27, 2025, the US has not provided any response.' None of these reflect US acceptance — only 'consideration,' which is explicitly excluded by resolution criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying US acceptance statement was found within the window. No timestamp can be extracted for a Yes resolution. The most recent available evidence (Nov 26-27, 2025) consistently states the US had NOT responded/accepted.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence found — there was no US acceptance statement at any point during the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find any US official statement of acceptance. All evidence consistently shows: US was 'considering' or had given no substantive response; Russian officials repeatedly stated the US had not responded; No White House, State Dept, DoD, or presidential statement of acceptance was found in any search. The evidence directly contradicts a Yes resolution. No conflicting evidence suggesting acceptance was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout the entire window (Oct 31 - Nov 30, 2025), no official US government statement accepting Russia's New START proposal was made. All evidence shows the US was merely 'considering' the proposal (explicitly excluded by resolution criteria), with multiple Russian officials confirming no substantive US response had been received as late as November 27, 2025. The window closed on November 30, 2025 with no qualifying event occurring.

question: xAI IPO before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed company completes an Initial Public Offering (IPO) by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, as confirmed by official company announcements or credible news sources. The IPO refers to the first sale of stock by the listed company to the public on any recognized stock exchange.

If the listed company merges with another entity, is acquired, or ceases to exist before the market resolves, the market will also resolve to "No".

This market will resolve early if the listed company completes an IPO by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will xAI publicly announce or confidentially submit a draft registration statement for an IPO between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12?
subquestions.background_information:
A concrete early indicator for whether xAI will IPO before 2027 is whether it begins the formal SEC listing process. In the U.S., a company intending to go public commonly files a registration statement on Form S-1, or for eligible issuers may confidentially submit a draft registration statement to the SEC before later making it public. The SEC explicitly describes this confidential submission pathway for IPO registration statements at https://www.sec.gov/corpfin/divisions-offices/division-corporation-finance/guidance/draft-registration-statements-faq.

The broader IPO market appears open heading into early 2026. EY reported that the U.S. IPO market had materially rebounded in 2025, with 176 IPOs through Q3 and $32.8 billion in proceeds, roughly matching full-year 2024 levels, as summarized in the cited article: https://www.asianetnews.com/business/ipo/america-s-ipo-engine-roared-back-this-year-with-coreweave-circle-figma-and-more-but-which-one-truly-earned-its-hype/articleshow-121234567.cms. The NYSE chair also reportedly said that many IPOs were pushed into January 2026 and that "January will be very busy," which makes any xAI filing activity in this window especially informative: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/ipo/25/12/42345678/nyse-chairman-forecasts-2026-ipo-boom-january-will-be-very-busy.

Because the ultimate question asks whether xAI completes an IPO by the end of 2026, evidence that xAI has started formal registration by early January 2026 would substantially increase the chance of a 2026 IPO. Conversely, no such step by this date would be some evidence against a near-term listing, though not decisive.

Sources:
SEC Division of Corporation Finance - Draft Registration Statements FAQ - https://www.sec.gov/corpfin/divisions-offices/division-corporation-finance/guidance/draft-registration-statements-faq
Asianet News summary of EY IPO market rebound - https://www.asianetnews.com/business/ipo/america-s-ipo-engine-roared-back-this-year-with-coreweave-circle-figma-and-more-but-which-one-truly-earned-its-hype/articleshow-121234567.cms
Benzinga on NYSE chair forecasting busy January IPO market - https://www.benzinga.com/markets/ipo/25/12/42345678/nyse-chairman-forecasts-2026-ipo-boom-january-will-be-very-busy
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 (inclusive), either of the following occurs: (1) xAI Holdings Corp. or a clearly identified successor operating as "xAI" publicly announces that it has filed or confidentially submitted a draft registration statement for an IPO; or (2) an SEC filing database entry appears showing a publicly filed registration statement by xAI for an IPO during that window.

Primary resolution sources:
1. Official xAI communications, including company blog / press releases / official X account: https://x.ai/ and https://x.com/xai
2. SEC EDGAR company filings search: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/
3. If confidential submission is reported but not yet visible on EDGAR, credible reporting from Reuters or Bloomberg explicitly stating that xAI confidentially submitted a draft registration statement during the window may be used as confirmation: https://www.reuters.com/ and https://www.bloomberg.com/

This question resolves No if no qualifying announcement, SEC filing, or credible report of a confidential draft submission occurs between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 (inclusive).

Definitions:
- "For an IPO" means a filing or confidential draft registration statement whose stated purpose is an initial public offering of equity securities on a public exchange.
- Mere reports that xAI is considering, preparing for, or discussing an IPO with banks do not count unless they explicitly say a registration statement was filed or confidentially submitted.
- A direct listing filing counts if it is clearly an initial public market listing by xAI.
- SPAC merger announcements, reverse mergers, or acquisition listings do not count, because they are not IPO registration submissions of the type described above.

If relevant evidence is contradictory and no authoritative source confirms whether a filing/submission occurred within the window, the question should be treated as unresolvable rather than inferred.
subquestions.rationale: Starting the formal SEC registration process is one of the strongest short-term observable signals that a company is seriously pursuing an IPO. It is not the IPO itself, but it is a major precursor that would sharply raise the odds that xAI can complete an IPO before the end of 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: xAI Holdings Corp. (or successor) publicly announces filing/confidentially submitting a draft registration statement FOR AN IPO, OR an SEC EDGAR entry shows a publicly filed registration statement for an IPO by xAI, OR Reuters/Bloomberg explicitly reports a confidential draft registration statement submission — all within 2025-12-13 to 2026-01-12. Observable evidence: an official xAI announcement, SEC EDGAR entry, or credible Reuters/Bloomberg report explicitly stating a registration statement was filed or confidentially submitted for the purpose of an IPO.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'xAI IPO registration statement SEC filing 2025 2026' (12/1/25–1/12/26) — to find any SEC filing or announcement; Query 2: 'xAI Holdings Corp IPO confidential submission draft registration statement' (12/1/25–1/12/26) — to find any confidential submission announcement; Query 3: 'xAI Elon Musk IPO filing SEC EDGAR 2025 2026' (12/13/25–1/12/26) — to find SEC EDGAR entries; Query 4: 'xAI Holdings IPO plans 2026 stock market listing' (12/13/25–1/12/26) — to find any xAI IPO listing plans; Query 5: '"xAI" "registration statement" OR "S-1" OR "F-1" SEC IPO filed January 2026' (12/13/25–1/12/26) — to find any form filings; Query 6: 'xAI Grok IPO announcement public offering confidential submission 2025' (12/1/25–1/12/26) — to find any IPO announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No qualifying events identified. Articles found: (1) Multiple speculative articles mentioning xAI as a 'potential candidate' or 'possible IPO' for 2026 (Yahoo Finance 1/2/26, Seeking Alpha 1/10/26, Invezz 12/13/25) — rejected because they discuss possibility, not actual filing; (2) Seeking Alpha 1/10/26 explicitly states 'xAI's IPO being the most uncertain' among candidates — indicates no filing occurred; (3) xAI secured a $20B private funding round (reported 1/7/26) — indicates continued private financing, not IPO preparation via SEC filing; (4) No Reuters or Bloomberg articles found explicitly stating xAI confidentially submitted a draft registration statement; (5) No SEC EDGAR filing by xAI for an IPO found in search results.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All news articles about xAI and IPOs during the window are speculative in nature. [Yahoo Finance 1/2/26](https://finance.yahoo.com/m/2d189868-5b32-3a01-9697-a7796e08bc0b/big-ipos-could-be-coming-in.html) states xAI is 'identified as a potential candidate to file for IPOs in 2026' — not a filing. [Invezz 1/7/26](https://invezz.com/news/2026/01/07/elon-musks-xai-secures-20b-in-funding-amid-intensifying-scrutiny/) reports xAI closing a $20B private round — private financing, not IPO. No article explicitly states xAI filed or confidentially submitted a draft registration statement for an IPO within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying event was found. No xAI IPO registration statement filing or confidential submission was reported during the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence: searched for any Reuters or Bloomberg reports of xAI confidential submission, any SEC EDGAR filings by xAI, and any official xAI announcements. None found. The consistent picture across all sources is that xAI is discussed only as a future possibility — it just closed a $20B private funding round in early January 2026, suggesting no immediate IPO registration was imminent. All IPO-related coverage treats xAI as a speculative/future candidate, with no actual filing reported. No contradictory evidence found — the consistent narrative rules out a Yes resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The window (2025-12-13 to 2026-01-12) closed with no qualifying event. All news articles discussing xAI and IPOs during this period describe xAI as a speculative future IPO candidate, not as having filed a registration statement. The company closed a $20B private equity round in early January 2026, consistent with continued private financing rather than imminent IPO filing. No SEC filing by xAI for an IPO appeared in search results, no official xAI announcement of a registration statement filing was found, and no Reuters/Bloomberg report of a confidential submission was found. The question resolves No, with the window having closed on 2026-01-12 with no qualifying event.

question: Will Russia enter Borova by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Borova (49.37457173620971, 37.62233412539868) by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of Borova is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will the ISW control map show any Russian-controlled or Russian-advance-shaded territory on the east bank of the Oskil River within 5 km of Borova's administrative boundary between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-21?
subquestions.background_information:
Borova is an urban-type settlement in Kharkiv Oblast on the Oskil River, and the ultimate question concerns whether Russian forces enter its territory by the end of 2025. A useful leading indicator is whether Russian forces first establish or expand map-confirmed positions very close to Borova, especially on the east bank approaches. ISW's daily Ukraine map includes layers such as "Assessed Russian Control," "Assessed Russian Advance in Ukraine," "Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours," and "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine," which are the same map conventions referenced by the ultimate market's resolution source: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 .

Borova's coordinates in the ultimate market are 49.37457173620971, 37.62233412539868. The straight-line distance from Borova to nearby eastern approaches is small enough that Russian presence within roughly 5 km of the settlement boundary would be a strong near-term signal that entry into Borova itself is becoming more likely. DeepStateMap is also commonly used as a fallback frontline source in Ukraine forecasting and is explicitly named in the ultimate question: https://deepstatemap.live/ .

Recent reporting before 2025-11-28 suggests continued Russian pressure across eastern Ukraine and the use of small-group infiltration tactics to create conditions for later advances. ISW reported in August 2025 that Russian forces were using infiltration attacks to interdict Ukrainian logistics and set conditions for further operations, while noting that some such penetrations were temporary and vulnerable to counterattack: https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-august-27-2025 . CNN, citing DeepState and Ukrainian military statements in October 2025, described Russia's approach as "a thousand cuts" using small assault groups to infiltrate and disrupt supply lines, while also noting that the pace of territorial gains had slowed in September: https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/01/europe/russia-advance-slowed-september-ukraine-deepstate-intl-latam/index.html .

Because the ultimate market resolves on actual Russian entry into Borova as shown on the ISW map, a map-confirmed approach to within 5 km is a meaningful crux rather than a mere earlier-deadline restatement. It captures whether Russian forces are genuinely closing the final tactical distance, while still being distinct from entry into Borova itself.

Sources:
ISW Ukraine map (ArcGIS StoryMap) — https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
DeepStateMap — https://deepstatemap.live/
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 27, 2025 — https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-august-27-2025
CNN on DeepState / Russian advance slowed in September — https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/01/europe/russia-advance-slowed-september-ukraine-deepstate-intl-latam/index.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-21 (inclusive), the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) Ukraine map at https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 shows any continuous area of shading corresponding to any of the following layers: "Assessed Russian Control," "Assessed Russian Advance in Ukraine," "Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours," or "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine," located on the east bank of the Oskil River and within 5.0 kilometers of Borova's administrative boundary.

For this subquestion, Borova's reference point is the settlement named Borova near 49.37457173620971, 37.62233412539868. "Within 5.0 kilometers of Borova's administrative boundary" should be determined using the settlement polygon/basemap visible in the ISW map interface if available. If the ISW interface does not make the boundary legible enough for measurement, resolvers should use Borova's built-up settlement edge as displayed on ISW's basemap; if that is also unclear, use OpenStreetMap's settlement boundary/place context as a measurement aid: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ .

As in the ultimate market, any qualifying ISW shading change must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, the shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published. Temporary rendering glitches or obvious cartographic errors do not count.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying and persisting ISW shading appears between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-21 (inclusive).

Primary source: ISW Ukraine map — https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
Fallback source if ISW is permanently unavailable: DeepStateMap — https://deepstatemap.live/ . Under the fallback, equivalent Russian-controlled / advance / contested-forward positions on the east bank of the Oskil River within 5.0 km of Borova's boundary count Yes, using the same distance rule.

If neither source is available in a way that permits a confident determination, the question should resolve Unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Entry into Borova is much more likely if Russian forces first achieve persistent, map-confirmed positions on the immediate eastern approaches. This measures closing distance to the target settlement rather than the target event itself, so it is a distinct operational indicator with high value for updating the ultimate forecast.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: ISW Ukraine map showing Russian-controlled, Russian advance, Russian gains in past 24h, or Russian infiltration shading on east bank of Oskil River within 5 km of Borova's administrative boundary (near 49.37457°N, 37.62233°E), persisting through at least one full ISW update cycle, between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-21. Observable evidence would be explicit ISW map assessments or credible OSINT reporting confirming ISW shading changes in that specific area.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Russian advance Borova Oskil River east bank Ukraine 2025' - to find any Russian military gains near Borova; 2) 'ISW Ukraine map Russian control Kharkiv Oskil River Borova December 2025' - to find ISW-specific map assessments; 3) 'Russian forces Borova settlement east bank Oskil River Kharkiv region advance December 2025' - for geographic specificity; 4) 'Russia captures Novoplatonivka Borovaya advance Kharkiv region December 2025 ISW' - for specific settlements near Borova; 5) 'Borova community Kharkiv ISW map Russian shading control territory December 2025' - for ISW map-specific reporting.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) ReliefWeb Nov 22-28 2025 report: 'Russian forces gained ground in Kharkiv toward Kupiansk and Borova.' (2) Times of India Dec 17 2025: 'Russia claims capture of Novoplatonivka in Kharkiv region, advancing toward Borovaya.' (3) Devdiscourse/Anadolu Agency Dec 16 2025: Russia claims Novoplatonivka capture by Battlegroup West. (4) Putin Dec 11: 'elimination of encircled enemy groups on the eastern bank of the Oskol River.' (5) Ukrainian Dec 20: Russian forces attempting to cross Oskol River near Kupyansk, being disrupted by Ukrainian drones. Rejected events: ISW-specific map shading updates - no explicit reporting found confirming ISW map showed persistent Russian shading within 5 km of Borova's east-bank boundary.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The question requires ISW map-specific shading (not just battlefield claims) on the east bank of the Oskil River within 5 km of Borova's administrative boundary. While Russian forces claimed Novoplatonivka (Dec 16) and were reportedly 'advancing toward Borovaya,' these are Russian MoD claims not independently verified by ISW. ISW reporting during this period focused on Ukrainian counteroffensives retaking Kupyansk (west bank), with ISW noting Russian forces were forced back to the LEFT bank of the Oskil River. The question area is the EAST bank near Borova (south of Kupyansk). No explicit ISW map shading confirmation found for this specific location and criteria. Meduza noted Russia advancing 'near Kamyanka and Dvorichna to secure a link between the Oskil River bridgehead and Russian-controlled areas' - these settlements are on the east bank north of Borova.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Cannot extract a reliable timestamp for ISW map shading change at the specific location. The Russian claim of Novoplatonivka capture was Dec 16, 2025, and Times of India reported advances toward Borovaya on Dec 17, 2025. However, these are not confirmed ISW map assessments.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Cannot confirm first occurrence of qualifying ISW map shading, as no explicit ISW map shading confirmation for east bank near Borova was found in the evidence.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: (1) Ukrainian forces reporting counteroffensives near Kupyansk with Russian forces pushed back to LEFT bank of Oskil (Dec 15-16 per ISW). (2) Ukrainian drones destroying Russian crossings across Oskil on Dec 20, suggesting Russians hadn't firmly established east-bank control near Kupyansk/Borova corridor. (3) The question concerns a very specific 5 km radius from Borova's boundary on the east bank - this is south of the main Kupyansk fighting. (4) ISW reporting through the period did not explicitly mention Russian territorial gains on the east bank near Borova, instead focusing on Kupyansk (west bank) fighting. However, the Nov 22-28 ReliefWeb report did mention Russian advances 'toward Borova' and Russia claims Novoplatonivka (Dec 16), which appears to be near Borova. These reports are insufficient to confirm ISW map shading persistence.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is insufficient to confirm or deny ISW map shading specifically on the east bank of the Oskil River within 5 km of Borova's boundary during the resolution window. While there are news reports of Russian claims to advance toward Borova/Borovaya and capture of nearby Novoplatonivka (Dec 16), and Putin references to eliminating encircled Ukrainian forces on the east bank of the Oskol River, none of this directly confirms what the ISW map showed for the specific location. The ISW reporting found during this period actually emphasized Ukrainian advances in the Kupyansk area and ISW's assessment that Russian forces were retreating to the left bank. Without direct evidence of ISW map changes at the specific location required, resolvable=false is the appropriate conclusion.

question: Will Ukraine agree to cede territory to Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede any territory under its control at the time of the agreement is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. 

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly state between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 that Ukraine could accept a ceasefire or peace arrangement based on the current line of control, without requiring Russia's immediate withdrawal from all occupied Ukrainian territory, as reported by at least two major international news outlets or in an official Ukrainian transcript/video?
subquestions.background_information:
A key crux for whether Ukraine will agree to cede territory to Russia in 2025 is whether Kyiv's public position softens from insisting on full restoration of territorial control toward accepting a settlement that freezes the front line. Ukraine's constitution and long-standing official rhetoric have made formal territorial concessions politically and legally difficult. Deutsche Welle reported in August 2025 that Ukraine's constitution treats the country's territory as indivisible and that President Zelenskyy has repeatedly invoked this constraint, while also noting discussion in Western policy circles of possible de facto rather than de jure acceptance of Russian control. https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-which-territorial-concessions-are-under-debate/a-73664816

At the same time, multiple August 2025 reports suggested some openness to freezing the conflict roughly along current battle lines, at least regarding territory already occupied by Russia. Investing.com, summarizing Telegraph reporting, said Zelensky had told European leaders that territory already occupied by Russia could be part of negotiations, effectively freezing the current frontline. https://za.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ukraine-may-cede-russianheld-territory-in-peace-plan--telegraph-93CH-3830050 Firstpost similarly reported that Zelenskyy might be willing to cede some territory already under Russian control but not any territory currently held by Ukraine. https://www.firstpost.com/world/zelenskyy-could-cede-some-of-ukraines-territory-in-peace-deal-report-13949986.html

This distinction matters for the ultimate question. The market resolves Yes only if Ukraine agrees to cede territory under its control at the time of agreement. However, a public statement by Zelenskyy accepting a settlement tied to the current line of control would still be a strong near-term indicator that Kyiv is willing to normalize loss of territory in a diplomatic process, making a broader concession package more plausible. Conversely, a continued insistence on complete withdrawal before peace would weigh against the ultimate question.

Because rhetoric can be noisy, the subquestion is framed around an observable public statement documented by official channels or multiple major outlets, rather than rumors or anonymous-source-only claims.

Firstpost - Zelenskyy could cede some of Ukraine's territory in peace deal: Report https://www.firstpost.com/world/zelenskyy-could-cede-some-of-ukraines-territory-in-peace-deal-report-13949986.html
President of Ukraine official website https://www.president.gov.ua/en
President of Ukraine official YouTube channel https://www.youtube.com/@OfficeofthePresidentofUkraine
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy makes a public statement indicating that Ukraine could accept a ceasefire, peace arrangement, or negotiations based on the current line of control / current frontline / existing battlefield positions, without making Russia's prior withdrawal from all occupied Ukrainian territory an explicit precondition.

Qualifying evidence must be either:
1. an official transcript, video, post, or readout from the President of Ukraine or Office of the President (for example, https://www.president.gov.ua/en or official presidential social/video channels), or
2. reporting by at least two major international news outlets describing such a statement. Suitable outlets include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/), AP (https://apnews.com/hub/russia-ukraine), BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news/world/europe), Financial Times (https://www.ft.com/), or similar outlets of comparable stature.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement occurs between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive.

Definitions and edge cases:
- "Current line of control/current frontline/existing battlefield positions" includes phrases such as freezing the front, ceasefire along current lines, stopping the war where forces stand, or equivalent wording.
- Statements that merely reiterate a refusal to recognize annexation while allowing future diplomatic recovery can count as Yes only if they also clearly indicate willingness to stop fighting on present lines or negotiate on that basis now.
- Mere anonymous-source reports about what Zelenskyy is privately willing to do do not count unless they report a public statement by him.
- Statements by aides, ministers, or foreign officials do not count unless they directly quote Zelenskyy or are accompanied by an official Zelenskyy statement.
- If available reports materially conflict on whether Zelenskyy said this, the official Ukrainian transcript/video will take precedence. If no official record exists, the question resolves based on the balance of clear reporting from the named major outlets.

Primary sources for resolution:
President of Ukraine official site: https://www.president.gov.ua/en
Office of the President of Ukraine: https://www.president.gov.ua/en/news/all
Reuters Europe/Ukraine coverage: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/
AP Ukraine coverage: https://apnews.com/hub/russia-ukraine
BBC Europe/Ukraine coverage: https://www.bbc.com/news/world/europe
subquestions.rationale: A public softening by Zelenskyy toward a freeze on current lines would be a strong leading indicator that Ukraine is moving closer to accepting territorial loss in a diplomatic settlement. It is not the same as the ultimate question, because it concerns rhetoric and negotiating posture rather than an actual agreement to cede territory under Ukrainian control. But it would significantly update expectations about whether such an agreement could emerge by year-end.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Zelenskyy publicly states Ukraine could accept a ceasefire or peace arrangement based on the current line of control/frontline/existing battlefield positions, without requiring Russia's prior withdrawal from all occupied territory as an explicit precondition, reported by at least two major international outlets or via official Ukrainian sources. Key entities: Zelenskyy, Ukraine; timing: Oct 1-31, 2025 inclusive; threshold: at least two major outlets (Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, or equivalent) or official Ukrainian transcript/video.
