evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple qualifying events identified: (1) Oct 17, 2025 - Zelenskyy at White House press conference: 'We have to stop where we are. The president is right' (RT, Anadolu Agency, multiple outlets); (2) Oct 19, 2025 - NBC Meet the Press interview: 'we need to stay where we stay... On the contact line' (NBC News, TASS, Ukrainska Pravda, RealClearPolitics); (3) Oct 21, 2025 - Joint statement with European leaders backing ceasefire 'based on the current line of contact' (AFP, Euronews, PBS, Kyiv Independent, Euractiv); (4) Oct 22, 2025 - Oslo visit: called freezing frontlines 'a good compromise' (AFP-sourced Firstpost, Fox News, Business Standard, Euronews); (5) Oct 23, 2025 - Repeated 'good compromise' statement (Euronews, Yahoo). No candidates rejected - all clearly satisfy criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Zelenskyy's Oct 17 statement ('We have to stop where we are') per [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/zelenskyy-backs-trump-s-suggestion-that-russia-ukraine-stop-where-they-are-in-war/3720178) and [RT](https://www.rt.com/russia/626637-zelesnky-ceasefire-front-lines/) explicitly endorses ceasefire at current lines without precondition of Russian withdrawal. Oct 19 NBC interview per [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/ukraine/volodymyr-zelenskyy-meet-the-press-interview-vladimir-putin-hamas-rcna238324): 'we need to stay where we stay... On the contact line' - explicitly accepts negotiations based on current frontline. Oct 21 joint statement per [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/79GH763) and [Euronews](http://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/10/21/european-leaders-back-trumps-ukraine-ceasefire-proposal-at-contact-line): Zelenskyy co-signed statement supporting ceasefire 'based on the current line of contact.' Oct 22-23 per [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-zelenskyy-agree-crucial-aspect-end-ukraine-war-good-compromise), [Euronews](http://www.euronews.com/2025/10/23/freezing-the-war-at-current-frontlines-is-a-good-compromise-zelenskyy-says): 'good compromise' to freeze frontlines. Criteria match is exact and direct. Reported by NBC News, AFP, Fox News, Euronews, PBS, Kyiv Independent - all major/comparable outlets. AFP and NBC News are comparable in stature to AP/Reuters.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First qualifying event: October 17, 2025, press conference in Washington, DC following White House meeting with Trump. Zelenskyy stated: 'We have to stop where we are. The president is right.' Published Oct 17, 2025 by multiple outlets. Exact timestamp within the resolution window (Oct 1-31, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence within the Oct 1-31 window exists. The earliest qualifying event is Oct 17, 2025. Searches did not find any qualifying Zelenskyy statements on current-line ceasefire acceptance between Oct 1-16, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Zelenskyy also stated 'territorial concessions' are 'sensitive,' borders 'not negotiable,' Ukraine 'will not cede territory,' and won't recognize Russia's annexations. However, these are not contradictory to the resolution criteria - Zelenskyy clearly accepted a ceasefire at current lines without requiring Russia's prior withdrawal, while maintaining the long-term position of not recognizing annexations. The resolution criteria explicitly accommodates this: 'Statements that merely reiterate a refusal to recognize annexation while allowing future diplomatic recovery can count as Yes only if they also clearly indicate willingness to stop fighting on present lines.' Zelenskyy's statements do exactly this. Evidence is consistent across many independent sources. No major conflicting evidence from named major outlets exists.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is Yes. Zelenskyy made multiple qualifying public statements within the Oct 1-31, 2025 window. The first occurred on October 17, 2025 when he stated 'We have to stop where we are. The president is right' at a Washington DC press conference. Subsequently on October 19, he told NBC News 'we need to stay where we stay... On the contact line.' On October 21, he co-signed a joint statement with European leaders endorsing a ceasefire 'based on the current line of contact.' On October 22-23, he called freezing the frontlines 'a good compromise.' These statements were reported by NBC News, AFP, Fox News, Euronews, PBS, Kyiv Independent, and many other major outlets - well exceeding the threshold of two major international news outlets. The statements explicitly indicate willingness to stop fighting on present lines without Russia's prior withdrawal being an explicit precondition.

question: Will 2025 be the second hottest year on record?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the data for the Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index for 2025 shows the second greatest increase of any previously recorded year when it is released. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An anomaly which is the second greatest of any previously recorded year for 2025 is necessary and sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes" immediately once the data becomes available, regardless of whether the figure for 2024 and/or 2025 is later revised.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the figure found in the table titled "Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)" under the column "No_Smoothing" in the row "2025" (https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt). If NASA's "Global Temperature Index" is rendered permanently unavailable, other information from NASA may be used. If no information for 2025 is provided by NASA by March 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Copernicus Climate Change Service report that 2025 was the second warmest year on record globally in its first annual summary released between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-10?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful crux for whether NASA GISTEMP will ultimately rank 2025 as the second hottest year on record, because Copernicus C3S and NASA both publish global temperature rankings using different but highly correlated datasets. As of early December 2025, Copernicus said 2025 was "virtually certain" to finish as either the second- or third-warmest year globally, behind 2024, and that January-November 2025 was 0.60°C above the 1991-2020 average and 1.48°C above the 1850-1900 level: https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-november-2025 . The WMO likewise said in its 2025 climate update that 2025 was likely to rank second or third warmest, just behind 2024: https://wmo.int/media/news/2025-climate-update-shows-alarming-signs . Independent datasets often differ slightly in exact annual ranking because of methodology, coverage interpolation, and baseline choices, but agreement by Copernicus that 2025 finished #2 would be strong evidence for a NASA #2 outcome.

Copernicus publishes monthly and annual global surface air temperature summaries based on ERA5. Their climate bulletins are publicly posted and usually include explicit annual rank language when the calendar year closes: https://climate.copernicus.eu/ . The December 2025 monthly bulletin or year-end summary is likely to be among the earliest authoritative public signals available before NASA’s final annual GISTEMP table is relied upon for the ultimate market.

Sources:
Copernicus Climate Change Service, Surface air temperature for November 2025 — https://climate.copernicus.eu/surface-air-temperature-november-2025
Copernicus Climate Change Service main site — https://climate.copernicus.eu/
WMO climate update news page — https://wmo.int/media/news/2025-climate-update-shows-alarming-signs
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-10 inclusive, Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) publishes an official webpage, bulletin, or report that explicitly states that 2025 was the second warmest year on record globally (or equivalent wording such as "second-warmest year globally"). It resolves No if, within that same window, C3S publishes its first annual-summary-style statement for 2025 and that statement explicitly says 2025 was not second warmest (for example, third warmest).

Primary source: official C3S climate bulletin/news pages at https://climate.copernicus.eu/ . A qualifying publication must be hosted on the Copernicus climate website and refer to the global annual ranking for 2025.

If multiple C3S pages are published in the window, the earliest one that gives an explicit final annual global ranking for 2025 controls resolution.

If no official C3S page giving an explicit final annual ranking for 2025 is published between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-10 inclusive, this question resolves Unresolvable.

If the Copernicus website is unavailable, archived copies of official Copernicus pages (for example via https://web.archive.org/ ) may be used only to verify the content of an official C3S publication originally posted within the resolution window.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on NASA’s ranking of 2025, but Copernicus is one of the earliest and most authoritative independent temperature-ranking sources. If Copernicus calls 2025 the second warmest year, that materially increases the chance NASA will also rank it second; if Copernicus says third, that pushes the other way.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: C3S publishes official webpage/bulletin on climate.copernicus.eu between Dec 30, 2025 and Jan 10, 2026 inclusive, explicitly stating 2025 was the 'second warmest year on record globally' or equivalent. Observable evidence: direct quote from C3S official publication within the window with explicit final annual global ranking.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Copernicus Climate Change Service 2025 annual warmest year report' (Dec 29 - Jan 10); 2) 'C3S Copernicus 2025 warmest year global temperature record annual summary' (Dec 29 - Jan 10); 3) 'Copernicus ERA5 December 2025 climate bulletin second warmest year' (Dec 30 - Jan 10); 4) 'Copernicus annual climate report 2025 second warmest official publication January 2026' (Jan 7-14); 5) 'Copernicus C3S December 2025 bulletin release January 8 2026 annual global temperature ranking' (Jan 7-10)
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (a) Multiple media articles Dec 30-Jan 10 citing C3S as predicting '2nd or 3rd warmest' - these are not definitive C3S annual reports; (b) The Age (Jan 8) cited 'Copernicus reported... 2025 tied with 2023 as second warmest' - secondary source, not primary C3S publication; (c) WMO planned consolidated release for Jan 14 - outside window; (d) ECMWF/C3S official annual report published Jan 13, 2026 (The Hindu) stated 2025 was THIRD warmest - outside window. No direct evidence of C3S publishing a definitive annual ranking within the Dec 30 - Jan 10 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require C3S to publish on climate.copernicus.eu an explicit statement that 2025 was 'second warmest year on record globally.' Within the window, C3S publications referenced by media only characterized 2025 as 'second or third warmest' (uncertain), not a definitive final ranking. The definitive C3S annual report was released January 13, 2026 (The Hindu, thenews.com.pk) stating 2025 was THIRD warmest - this is outside the resolution window and contradicts 'second warmest.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The C3S/ECMWF definitive annual 2025 summary was published January 13, 2026 (confirmed by The Hindu, Jan 13, 2026; and thenews.com.pk, Jan 14, 2026). This is OUTSIDE the resolution window (ends Jan 10, 2026). No exact timestamp found for a C3S publication within the window giving a definitive final annual ranking.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying C3S publication with an explicit final annual ranking for 2025 was found within the Dec 30 - Jan 10 window. Media sources during the window referenced C3S provisional estimates of 'second or third warmest,' not a definitive final ranking.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The definitive C3S annual report (Jan 13, 2026) stated 2025 was THIRD warmest, not second. This directly contradicts the Yes resolution outcome. Multiple sources (Dawn, AFP, VnExpress, Asharq Al-Awsat from Dec 31 - Jan 1) explicitly stated that Copernicus's full annual confirmation was expected 'in early January' - confirming no official C3S final annual ranking was published by those dates. The Vancouver Sun (Jan 10, boundary of window) still referenced C3S projecting 2025 as 'second or third warmest' - not definitive. Berkeley Earth and Skeptical Science also reported 2025 as second warmest but C3S specifically stated third warmest.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Two considerations: (1) No official C3S publication on climate.copernicus.eu giving an explicit FINAL annual global ranking for 2025 was published within the Dec 30 - Jan 10 window; (2) When C3S did publish its definitive annual report (Jan 13, 2026 - outside window), it explicitly stated 2025 was the THIRD warmest year, not second. The question resolves No because: the definitive C3S annual statement, when finally issued, said 'third warmest' not 'second warmest,' making it definitively impossible for the Yes condition to have been met. The No conclusion becomes definitive when C3S published its official annual report on Jan 13, 2026 stating third warmest. However, since this is outside the window, and no qualifying publication was made within the window, the question is unresolvable per the stated criteria. But given that the C3S publication within the window only gave uncertain 'second or third' estimates and the definitive statement was outside the window, and the criteria say 'If no official C3S page giving an explicit final annual ranking for 2025 is published between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-10 inclusive, this question resolves Unresolvable,' the answer is Unresolvable.

question: Will Trump talk to Nicolás Maduro by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if President of Venezuela Nicolás Maduro talks with Donald Trump between October 15 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

A talk is defined as any interaction between the listed individual and Donald Trump, occurring either in person or through verbal communication by phone or video call.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will either the White House or Venezuela's presidency/foreign ministry publicly announce between 2025-11-15 and 2025-11-30 that direct U.S.–Venezuelan talks involving senior principals are being arranged, requested, or are underway?
subquestions.background_information:
A public announcement that direct talks are being arranged or requested would be a strong near-term indicator that a Trump–Maduro conversation is becoming more likely, without being the same event as the ultimate question. Recent reporting suggests the issue is live: on October 17, 2025, Trump said Maduro had "offered everything" to ease tensions with the United States, implying some form of outreach or concessions may already have been discussed in the background (The Independent, 2025-10-17: https://www.independent.co.uk/tv/news/trump-maduro-f-bomb-zelensky-b2631570.html ; Daily Beast, 2025-10-17: https://www.thedailybeast.com/trump-drops-wild-f-bomb-threat-during-peace-talks-meeting/). At the same time, Venezuelan officials have publicly denied some reports of de-escalation negotiations, indicating uncertainty about whether formal channels exist (Dawn, 2025-10-19: https://www.dawn.com/news/1924636/us-plotting-to-overthrow-venezuelan-govt-maduro). Regional leaders are discussing Venezuela as a live diplomatic issue: AP reported on November 4, 2025 that Brazil's Lula urged diplomacy and said he would personally call Trump if tariff talks stalled, while also warning against conflict in Venezuela (AP, 2025-11-04: https://apnews.com/). Because direct leader-to-leader calls are often preceded by statements that contacts are being arranged through diplomatic or security channels, a public acknowledgment from either side that talks are being requested, arranged, or underway would meaningfully update the probability of the ultimate Trump–Maduro talk occurring by year-end.

Sources:
The Independent - https://www.independent.co.uk/tv/news/trump-maduro-f-bomb-zelensky-b2631570.html
The Daily Beast - https://www.thedailybeast.com/trump-drops-wild-f-bomb-threat-during-peace-talks-meeting/
Dawn - https://www.dawn.com/news/1924636/us-plotting-to-overthrow-venezuelan-govt-maduro
AP News - https://apnews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-15 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, at least one official public communication from either side explicitly states that direct U.S.–Venezuelan talks involving senior principals are being arranged, requested, or are underway. For this market, qualifying communications are limited to: (a) a White House statement/press briefing transcript, State Department statement/briefing transcript, or official post on a verified White House, U.S. State Department, or senior administration account; or (b) a statement/post from the Venezuelan presidency, Venezuelan foreign ministry, or Nicolás Maduro's verified official channels. "Senior principals" means Trump, Maduro, the U.S. Secretary of State, Venezuela's foreign minister, or clearly identified direct envoys acting on behalf of Trump or Maduro. "Direct U.S.–Venezuelan talks" includes language such as talks/negotiations/dialogue/contact/call/meeting being arranged, requested, scheduled, opened, or underway. Mere third-party advocacy for talks, general calls for peace, or vague claims that one side has made concessions do not count unless an official statement says direct bilateral contact is being arranged, requested, or underway.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying official public communication appears between 2025-11-15 and 2025-11-30 inclusive.

Primary resolution sources: official White House materials (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), U.S. State Department press materials (https://www.state.gov/newsroom/), Venezuelan Foreign Ministry site (https://mppre.gob.ve/), and Nicolás Maduro / Venezuelan presidency official channels if publicly accessible. Secondary confirmation may use Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), or Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/) to verify authenticity or timing of the official statement. If official websites are unavailable, archived versions or contemporaneous wire reports quoting the official statement may be used. If timing cannot be established within the window, the statement does not count.
subquestions.rationale: A leader-to-leader talk usually becomes more likely once official channels publicly acknowledge that bilateral contact is being arranged or requested. This is a distinct observable event from the ultimate question itself and should materially update forecasts about whether Trump and Maduro will actually speak.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: An official public communication from either (a) White House/State Dept/senior U.S. admin, or (b) Venezuelan presidency/foreign ministry/Maduro's verified official channels, explicitly stating that direct U.S.–Venezuelan talks involving senior principals (Trump, Maduro, U.S. SecState, Venezuela FM, or direct envoys) are being arranged, requested, scheduled, opened, or underway. Window: 2025-11-15 to 2025-11-30 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'US Venezuela talks negotiations senior officials 2025' [Nov 15-30]; (2) 'White House State Department Venezuela dialogue direct contact November 2025' [Nov 15-30]; (3) 'Trump Maduro phone call November 2025 White House official statement' [Nov 15-30]; (4) 'Venezuela foreign ministry Maduro official statement US talks negotiations November 2025' [Nov 15-30]; (5) 'Trump statement discussions with Maduro White House press briefing November 17 2025' [Nov 15-20]; (6) 'Maduro face-to-face dialogue Trump response November 18 2025 official statement' [Nov 15-25]; (7) 'White House not negotiating Venezuela Maduro denial official statement November 20 2025' [Nov 18-25]; (8) 'Trump confirmed spoke Maduro phone call November 30 2025' [Nov 28-30].
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Nov 17, 2025 – Trump statement at Palm Beach press briefing: 'We may be having some discussions with Maduro, and we'll see how that turns out. They would like to talk.' (AFP, Reuters, multiple outlets). This is a public presidential statement about discussions being arranged/underway. (B) Nov 18, 2025 – Maduro's televised address saying he is ready for 'face-to-face' dialogue (Mehr News, AFP, multiple outlets). This is an official Venezuelan presidential statement requesting/arranging direct talks. (C) Nov 18, 2025 – Trump at White House says he 'expects to speak with Maduro at some point' (IndiaTimes). (D) Nov 20, 2025 – White House official reportedly denied active negotiations via journalist Eric Martin (Latin Times). (E) Nov 21, 2025 – Trump on Fox News: 'will soon speak with Maduro, I have something very specific to say.' (F) Nov 25, 2025 – Trump on Air Force One: 'I might talk to him. We'll see,' noting communication teams already establishing contact (Axios report; multiple outlets). (G) ~Nov 19-21 – Actual phone call between Trump and Maduro with Rubio present, reported by NYT on Nov 28. (H) Nov 30, 2025 – Trump publicly confirmed the call: 'It was a phone call' (Fox News, aboard Air Force One). Rejected events: Nov 20 White House official denial – this is from an unnamed official via journalist, not an official White House public statement, and doesn't override Trump's own public statements.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Event A (Nov 17 Trump press briefing): Trump is qualifying senior principal. Statement 'We may be having some discussions with Maduro' made publicly at a press briefing reported by [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/848C663) explicitly states discussions are being arranged/underway. This qualifies as an official public communication from the U.S. side (qualifying source: White House/senior administration). Event B (Nov 18 Maduro televised address): Maduro is qualifying senior principal. His public statement 'I am ready for face-to-face dialogue' from official Venezuelan TV channel explicitly states he is requesting/arranging direct talks. This qualifies from the Venezuelan side. Event H (Nov 30 Trump confirmation of call): Trump on Air Force One confirmed 'It was a phone call' per [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-says-dont-read-anything-it-when-asked-about-declaring-venezuelas-airspace-closed) — confirms direct contact occurred. The earliest qualifying official public communication is Event A on November 17, 2025, followed by Event B on November 18, 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: November 17, 2025: Trump's press briefing statement at Palm Beach International Airport, reported by AFP (published November 17, 2025). Multiple sources confirm this date. The statement 'We may be having some discussions with Maduro' is confirmed as from November 16-17 at a press event prior to boarding Air Force One. U.S. News & World Report timestamps this to November 16, 2025, while most outlets say November 17. Given some ambiguity in the exact date (Nov 16 vs. Nov 17), both dates fall within the resolution window (Nov 15-30). November 18, 2025: Maduro's face-to-face dialogue statement confirmed by AFP [http://doc.afp.com/84BX49E] at the White House. November 30, 2025: Trump's confirmation of the phone call confirmed by Fox News.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest qualifying event is Trump's Nov 17 press briefing statement (or possibly Nov 16 per some sources, but both are within the window). No qualifying official communication exists before Nov 15 (window start). Nov 17 appears to be the first occurrence. Maduro's response on Nov 18 is the second qualifying communication.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Nov 20 White House official (via journalist Eric Martin, not an official White House statement) said 'currently not negotiating' — however this doesn't negate Trump's own public presidential statements on Nov 17-18 and Nov 21 which are higher-authority official communications. Additionally, the Nov 30 Trump confirmation of the actual phone call ('It was a phone call') definitively confirms direct contact occurred between senior principals (Trump + Rubio + Maduro). The resolution criteria explicitly includes 'being arranged, requested, or underway' — Trump's Nov 17 statement and Maduro's Nov 18 response both explicitly meet this standard. The denial by an unnamed White House official on Nov 20 does not outweigh Trump's own public presidential statements. Multiple high-quality sources (AFP, Reuters, NYT, Fox News) confirm these events.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: YES. The first qualifying official public communication occurred on November 17, 2025, when U.S. President Donald Trump (qualifying senior principal) publicly stated at a press briefing 'We may be having some discussions with Maduro, and we'll see how that turns out. They would like to talk.' This is an explicit official public statement from the U.S. President indicating direct U.S.-Venezuelan talks are being arranged/underway. question: OpenAI social app in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a social iOS app owned by OpenAI is available for installation on the US iOS app store by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Pre-Order does not satisfy the market conditions.

A "social app" refers to an iOS application whose primary function is facilitating social interaction between users, such as messaging, content sharing, or community engagement.

The primary resolution source will be the US iOS app store, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly confirm between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-27 that it is testing or piloting a standalone social app or social feed product with external users?
subquestions.background_information:
A strong near-term indicator for whether an OpenAI-owned social iOS app will be available by the end of 2025 is whether OpenAI publicly acknowledges that a social product is already in testing with users. Reporting before 2025-09-01 indicates OpenAI has at least explored a social product. A 2025-04-17 article summarizing reporting from The Verge said OpenAI was developing a social network prototype that integrates ChatGPT’s image generation with a social feed, and that CEO Sam Altman had sought outside feedback on the concept: https://medium.com/@indrastra/openai-takes-the-fight-to-musk-and-zuckerberg-3a1b7b4d7b4d .

OpenAI has also shown willingness to expand beyond pure chat interfaces into consumer products. In May 2025, OpenAI announced it was acquiring Jony Ive’s io and working on new consumer hardware, signaling broader platform ambitions rather than remaining only a model provider: https://www.usatoday.com/story/tech/news/2025/05/21/openai-jony-ive-hardware-startup-acquisition/83782612007/ . Meanwhile, Apple’s deepening OpenAI integration in iOS has kept OpenAI highly visible in the mobile consumer ecosystem, which may lower distribution friction if OpenAI launches a standalone app later: https://www.foxbusiness.com/technology/elon-musks-xai-sues-apple-openai-over-ai-competition-app-store-rankings and https://www.idownloadblog.com/2025/08/13/apple-responds-to-elon-musks-claim-that-apple-favors-openai-over-other-ai-platforms-in-the-app-store/ .

Because the ultimate question is specifically about a social iOS app owned by OpenAI being available in the US App Store by year-end, public confirmation of external testing would be a meaningful milestone. It would suggest the product has progressed from rumor or internal prototype to at least limited real-world deployment.

Sources:
Medium (summary of reporting on OpenAI social product): https://medium.com/@indrastra/openai-takes-the-fight-to-musk-and-zuckerberg-3a1b7b4d7b4d
USA Today - OpenAI buys Jony Ive's hardware startup: https://www.usatoday.com/story/tech/news/2025/05/21/openai-jony-ive-hardware-startup-acquisition/83782612007/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-27 (inclusive), OpenAI publicly confirms that it is testing, piloting, beta testing, or otherwise allowing external users outside OpenAI employees to use a standalone social app or social feed product owned or developed by OpenAI.

For this question:
- "Publicly confirms" means a statement by OpenAI or an OpenAI executive spokesperson in an official OpenAI blog post, OpenAI social media account, press release, product page, help page, or in an on-the-record statement quoted by at least one credible technology/news outlet.
- "External users" excludes purely internal dogfooding by OpenAI employees/contractors. It includes testers, creators, partners, waitlist users, or members of the public invited into a pilot.
- "Standalone social app or social feed product" means a product whose primary function includes user-to-user posting, following, messaging, commenting, sharing, or interacting in a persistent feed/community context. A generic ChatGPT feature without social interaction does not count.
- A mere rumor, leak, reverse-engineered code string, or unnamed-source report without public confirmation from OpenAI does not count.

Primary sources for resolution:
- OpenAI News / blog: https://openai.com/news/
- OpenAI homepage / product pages: https://openai.com/
- OpenAI X account: https://x.com/OpenAI
- Sam Altman X account: https://x.com/sama

Secondary corroborating sources if needed:
- The Verge: https://www.theverge.com/
- TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/

If no qualifying public confirmation occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-27 (inclusive), resolve No. If the only evidence is ambiguous and no authoritative public statement from OpenAI exists by the end of the window, resolve No. If relevant statements are made outside the window, they do not count.
subquestions.rationale: A public confirmation of external testing would be a meaningful leading indicator that OpenAI is seriously advancing a social product, without merely restating the ultimate question about App Store availability. It captures product maturity and organizational commitment several steps upstream from launch.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: OpenAI publicly confirms (via official blog, social media account, press release, or on-the-record quoted statement) that it is testing/piloting a standalone social app or social feed product with external (non-employee) users between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-27. The product must have user-to-user social interaction as its primary function (posting, following, messaging, commenting, sharing in a persistent feed/community context). Generic ChatGPT features don't count. Mere rumors or unnamed-source reports don't count.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'OpenAI social app social feed product external users testing' (Sep 1-27) — to find direct confirmation; 2) 'OpenAI social media platform launch pilot beta' (Sep 1-27) — to find any launch/pilot announcement; 3) 'OpenAI social network app confirmed launch September 2025' — to find official confirmation; 4) 'OpenAI social feed beta testing users pilot program' — to find external user testing; 5) 'OpenAI social media app X competitor confirmed testing external users' — to find competitor context; 6) 'OpenAI Pulse social feed ChatGPT social features September 2025' — to check Pulse feature; 7) 'OpenAI standalone social app user-to-user posting feed community' — to find social feature confirmation; 8) 'OpenAI new product announcement social platform September 2025 blog post' — to find official announcements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Sam Altman mentioned a 'social networking app' as a future product under Fidji Simo's oversight (Sept 4-5 blog post/press announcements about Jobs Platform); (2) ChatGPT Pulse launched Sept 25-26 for Pro users — a personalized daily briefing feed; (3) Sam Altman's X posts (Sept 3-8) about bots on social media with speculative hints at a future OpenAI social network. REJECTED: (1) Future social app plans — this is a statement of intent/plans, not confirmation of testing/piloting with external users; (2) ChatGPT Pulse — this is a feature within ChatGPT delivering AI-generated personal briefings, NOT a standalone social app, and has no user-to-user interaction features; (3) Sam Altman's bot commentary — speculative/commentary, not an official confirmation of testing.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate events exactly match the resolution criteria. The mentions of a social networking app (e.g., [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/04/openai-announces-ai-powered-hiring-platform-to-take-on-linkedin/)) are about future plans — Sam Altman 'noted that Simo will oversee the platform along with other forthcoming applications such as a browser and a social media app' — this is a future plan, not confirmation of current external user testing. ChatGPT Pulse ([PCMag](https://pcmag.com/news/openai-launches-chatgpt-pulse-to-deliver-proactive-morning-updates)) is a ChatGPT feature with no user-to-user social interaction. No official OpenAI blog post, press release, or on-the-record statement confirms external testing of a standalone social app.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with a reliable timestamp was found. The social media app mentions cluster around Sept 4-5 but refer to future plans. Pulse launched Sept 25-26 but doesn't meet social app criteria.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was found within the window. There is no evidence of any public confirmation by OpenAI of external user testing of a standalone social app.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for: (1) Any OpenAI blog posts about social app testing — not found; (2) Any on-the-record confirmation of external users testing a social feed product — not found; (3) Whether ChatGPT Pulse could qualify — rejected as it is a personal AI briefing feature within ChatGPT, not a standalone social app with user-to-user interaction; (4) Whether the future social app mention could qualify — rejected as it's a future plan statement, not a confirmation of current testing with external users. No contradictory evidence found that would change the No conclusion.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly does not support a Yes resolution. OpenAI publicly mentioned plans for a future social networking app and launched ChatGPT Pulse (a personal briefing feature within ChatGPT), but neither qualifies as confirming that OpenAI is 'testing or piloting a standalone social app or social feed product with external users.' The resolution criteria requires a current test/pilot with external users, not future plans. The window closed on 2025-09-27 without any qualifying confirmation.

question: Ukraine agrees not to join NATO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Ukraine publicly agrees not to join NATO by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An official pledge by Ukraine not to join NATO will qualify for a “Yes” resolution whether as a unilateral announcement or part of an agreement with the Russian Federation. 

Any agreement or pledge made before the resolution date of this market will qualify, regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

An agreement by Ukraine not to join NATO for any amount of time will count (e.g. If Ukraine not to join NATO for 10 years this will qualify).

An agreement by Ukraine not to join NATO as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995 “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement is an example of a qualifying agreement. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by the Ukraine, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming a qualifying agreement has been reached will also count.

subquestions.question: Will President Volodymyr Zelenskyy or Ukraine's Presidential Office publicly state between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 that Ukraine is prepared to accept a peace arrangement that bars or suspends NATO membership for a defined period?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term public softening by Ukraine's top leadership on NATO could be a strong indicator for the ultimate question, because recent reporting suggests neutrality or a pause on NATO membership is one of the central disputed terms in ongoing peace talks. On 24 November 2025, AFP reported that Washington and Kyiv said any peace deal must uphold Ukraine's sovereignty, while noting that the original US draft had required Ukraine to pledge not to join NATO and that Ukraine sought revisions: https://www.barrons.com/news/washington-kyiv-say-a-peace-deal-must-fully-uphold-ukraine-sovereignty-e15cc17d . On 25-26 November 2025, CBS/AOL reported that Ukrainian negotiators had reached a common understanding on the 'core terms' of a US-brokered proposal, and that the framework reportedly included Ukraine abandoning its NATO membership bid in exchange for Article 5-like security assurances: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ukraine-agrees-peace-proposal-minor-details-no-word-russia/ and https://www.aol.com/news/ukraine-agrees-peace-deal-only-142726737.html .

At the same time, European institutions were publicly rejecting any settlement that compromised Ukraine's sovereign choice of alliances. The European Parliament's adopted text of 27 November 2025 insisted on 'freedom of alliance choice' and robust security guarantees, highlighting that NATO-status language remained politically salient and contested: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/TA-10-2025-0113_EN.html . Because public statements by Zelenskyy or the Presidential Office would likely precede or accompany any formal agreement, a clear acknowledgment that Ukraine is prepared to accept a bar or temporary suspension on NATO membership would be a meaningful leading indicator for whether Ukraine will in fact publicly agree not to join NATO by year-end.

Sources:
CBS News - Ukraine agrees to peace proposal, with only 'minor details' to settle, official says, but no word from Russia - https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ukraine-agrees-peace-proposal-minor-details-no-word-russia/
AOL - Ukraine agrees to peace deal, only 'minor details' left, official says - https://www.aol.com/news/ukraine-agrees-peace-deal-only-142726737.html
Barron's/AFP - Washington, Kyiv say a peace deal must 'fully uphold' Ukraine sovereignty - https://www.barrons.com/news/washington-kyiv-say-a-peace-deal-must-fully-uphold-ukraine-sovereignty-e15cc17d
European Parliament adopted text - https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/TA-10-2025-0113_EN.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), either (a) President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, or (b) the Office of the President of Ukraine / Presidential Office of Ukraine, in a public statement, interview, speech, press release, transcript, post, or video, explicitly says that Ukraine is prepared to accept, support, or agree to a peace arrangement under which Ukraine will not join NATO, or will suspend/pause/defer seeking NATO membership, for any defined period of time.

Qualifying examples include language such as: 'Ukraine is prepared to renounce NATO membership for X years,' 'Ukraine can accept non-membership/neutrality/non-alignment as part of a peace deal,' or 'Ukraine is ready to suspend its NATO bid for X years.' The duration may be temporary or indefinite.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement occurs within the window 2025-11-30 through 2025-12-29 inclusive.

Non-qualifying statements: (i) statements solely by foreign governments, mediators, anonymous officials, or media reports claiming Ukraine agreed, unless accompanied by a qualifying direct public statement from Zelenskyy or the Presidential Office; (ii) statements merely reaffirming that security guarantees are needed, without indicating willingness to forgo or suspend NATO membership; (iii) statements by Ukrainian ministers or negotiators other than Zelenskyy or the Presidential Office, unless the statement is simultaneously published or clearly endorsed by the Presidential Office.

Primary resolution sources: official website of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en), official presidential X/social accounts if archived or directly linked from official channels, and official video/transcript publications. Secondary sources, if needed to identify the statement, may include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), and BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news), but the underlying qualifying statement must still be directly attributable to Zelenskyy or the Presidential Office.

If no qualifying official/public statement is available by the end of 2025-12-29 UTC, resolve No. If alleged remarks cannot be verified from official publication, full transcript, or high-confidence video/audio published by credible outlets, they do not count.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question requires a public Ukrainian agreement not to join NATO by year-end. A public statement from Zelenskyy or his office indicating willingness to accept a neutrality or NATO-suspension clause would be a strong precursor and would materially update forecasts, while still being distinct from the final event because it asks about a softer preparatory signal rather than the agreement itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29, Zelenskyy or the Presidential Office explicitly states that Ukraine is prepared to accept/support/agree to a peace arrangement under which Ukraine will not join NATO, or will suspend/pause/defer seeking NATO membership, for any defined period (including indefinitely). Key entities: Zelenskyy, Presidential Office of Ukraine. Timing: within resolution window. Observable evidence: direct public statement (interview, speech, press release, video) attributable to Zelenskyy or Presidential Office.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Zelenskyy Ukraine NATO membership suspend pause peace deal 2025' (Dec 2025 window) — to find qualifying statements; 2. 'Zelenskyy Ukraine renounce NATO neutrality peace arrangement December 2025' — to find direct statements; 3. 'Zelenskyy presidential office statement NATO membership drop December 14 15 2025 Berlin' — to find earliest qualifying statement; 4. 'Zelenskyy does not require Ukraine to formally renounce NATO AFP December 24 2025' — to find contradictory evidence; 5. 'Zelenskyy compromise NATO membership peace guarantees Reuters AP BBC December 2025' — to find secondary confirmation.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) December 14, 2025: Zelenskyy, in a WhatsApp chat with reporters and public statements before/during Berlin peace talks, stated Ukraine is open to/prepared to drop its NATO membership bid as a 'compromise' in exchange for Article 5-like security guarantees. This was reported by dozens of credible outlets including CNA, CNBC, Anadolu Agency, AFP, Reuters (per secondary reports), and many others. (2) December 24, 2025: Zelenskyy unveiled a 20-point peace plan; AFP reported he said the plan does NOT require formal renunciation of NATO bid — and separately said 'our choice has been made' and that NATO membership is up to NATO states. The December 24 AFP statement and Ukrainska Pravda appear to partially contradict the December 14 framing. However, the December 14 statement stands as a public statement. The key tension: December 14 = willingness to drop NATO bid; December 24 = 20-point plan doesn't require formal renunciation. These are not necessarily contradictory — Zelenskyy may have been signaling willingness to not join NATO in practice (without formal renunciation) as part of a peace deal.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The December 14, 2025 statement by Zelenskyy substantially meets the resolution criteria. Multiple credible sources confirm Zelenskyy publicly said Ukraine is prepared to drop/abandon/forgo its NATO membership bid as part of a peace arrangement, in exchange for alternative security guarantees. This is explicitly a statement about Ukraine being 'prepared to accept a peace arrangement under which Ukraine will not join NATO.' The statement was made publicly (WhatsApp chat with reporters, before and during Berlin peace talks), directly attributable to Zelenskyy himself. The duration aspect: the statement was framed as an ongoing/indefinite concession ('a compromise'), not a time-limited suspension. The criteria explicitly allow indefinite duration: 'The duration may be temporary or indefinite.' However, there is a complication: the December 24 AFP article says Zelenskyy stated the '20-point plan does not require Ukraine to formally renounce NATO bid' and that 'our choice has been made.' This suggests Zelenskyy was trying to preserve Ukraine's formal right to NATO membership while practically accepting non-membership in a peace deal. The resolution criteria cover both formal renunciation AND 'suspend/pause/defer seeking NATO membership for any defined period.' The Dec 14 statement explicitly covers the latter (willing to not pursue NATO membership in favor of alternative security guarantees as part of peace deal). The 20-point plan itself (Dec 24) reflects a de facto acceptance of non-membership as part of a peace arrangement, even if not a formal renunciation. Multiple high-quality sources (CNA [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/ukraines-zelenskyy-drops-nato-ambition-berlin-peace-talks-begin-5581336], Anadolu Agency [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/zelenskyy-says-bilateral-security-guarantees-a-compromise-on-ukraine-s-nato-accession/3771029], CNBC [https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/15/ukraine-gives-up-joining-nato-in-bid-to-shift-the-dial-in-peace-talks.html], Epoch Times [https://www.theepochtimes.com/world/zelenskyy-open-to-dropping-nato-bid-as-peace-talks-continue-in-berlin-5958046], News18 [https://www.news18.com/world/wont-join-nato-in-exchange-for-western-security-guarantees-zelenskyy-on-ending-war-with-russia-ws-l-9769662.html]) confirm Zelenskyy made this statement on December 14, 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest qualifying event occurred on December 14, 2025. Zelenskyy made public statements in a WhatsApp chat with reporters (per Epoch Times, 'Zelenskyy stated on December 14, 2025, during a WhatsApp chat with reporters, that he is open to abandoning Ukraine's bid for NATO membership') and in public remarks ahead of and during Berlin peace talks on that date. The exact time of day is not available from the sources, but the date is reliably established as December 14, 2025, placing it well within the November 30–December 29 window. Resolution datetime = 2025-12-14T00:00:00Z (beginning of day, as exact time is unavailable but date is certain).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying statement within the November 30–December 29 window was identified. The December 14 statement is consistently identified as the first public statement by Zelenskyy offering to drop the NATO bid as part of a peace arrangement. Articles from December 1, 2025 (Zelenskyy/Macron meeting) focused on 'truly durable peace' and security guarantees but did NOT include a statement about dropping NATO membership. The December 14 statement is the first qualifying occurrence in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The December 24 AFP report states the '20-point plan does not require Ukraine to formally renounce NATO bid,' and Zelenskyy separately said 'our choice has been made' and that NATO membership is up to NATO states. This could be read as Zelenskyy backtracking from December 14. However, analysis shows: (1) Zelenskyy on December 14 made an explicit public statement about willingness to drop the NATO bid; (2) December 24 he clarified the plan doesn't require FORMAL RENUNCIATION (constitutional amendment), but he still acknowledged Ukraine would not be seeking NATO membership as part of the peace deal — the 20-point plan itself does not include NATO membership as a provision, and Zelenskyy accepted this. (3) AOL/AFP reported Dec 26: 'Zelensky has offered significant concessions: Ukraine may forgo full NATO membership and instead seek security guarantees mirroring NATO's Article 5.' The December 14 statement is direct, explicit, unambiguous, and from a public media interaction directly attributed to Zelenskyy. It satisfies all criteria. The December 24 nuance about 'no formal renunciation' is about the mechanism (no constitutional ban required) but doesn't negate the core statement of willingness to not pursue NATO membership as part of a peace deal.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly supports a Yes resolution. Zelenskyy made a qualifying public statement on December 14, 2025 — within the window (November 30 to December 29, 2025) — in which he explicitly stated that Ukraine is prepared to drop/abandon its bid for NATO membership as part of a peace arrangement (in exchange for Article 5-like security guarantees). This statement was: (1) made directly by Zelenskyy (not just a minister or unnamed official), (2) made publicly (WhatsApp chat with reporters, widely broadcast), (3) clearly within the resolution window, (4) explicitly about willingness to not join NATO as part of a peace deal, and (5) confirmed by numerous credible media outlets. The resolution criteria allow for indefinite duration. The December 14 statement explicitly matches: 'Ukraine can accept non-membership/neutrality/non-alignment as part of a peace deal.' Resolution: Yes, first occurring on December 14, 2025.

question: Will a new country join the Abraham Accords in 2025?
description:

A formal signing refers to an official agreement between Israel and another country that is publicly acknowledged by both governments and clearly attributed to the Abraham Accords or their continuation.

Countries already part of the Abraham Accords as of June 26, 2025—including the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan—will not count.

The resolution source will be official government statements, however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Saudi Arabia publicly reaffirm between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 that normalization with Israel requires a pathway to a Palestinian state?
subquestions.background_information:
Saudi Arabia is widely viewed as the most consequential plausible future entrant to the Abraham Accords, so its stated conditions are a key near-term indicator for whether any new country is likely to join by the end of 2025. Multiple recent reports say Saudi normalization remains contingent on movement toward Palestinian statehood. Reuters reported in September 2025 that Riyadh insists any normalization must include a clear path to a Palestinian state, which conflicts with the position of Israel's current government (via Yahoo/Reuters summary: https://www.yahoo.com/news/factbox-abraham-accords-115050294.html ; MarketScreener/Reuters summary: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Factbox-What-are-the-Abraham-Accords-50878031/). The Seattle Times similarly reported on October 13, 2025 that Saudi expansion into the accords has stalled because the kingdom insists on a Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital (https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/what-are-the-abraham-accords-trumps-2020-mideast-deals/). Al Jazeera also reported on October 17, 2025 that Saudi Arabia continues to uphold the Arab Peace Initiative and links normalization to Palestinian statehood amid highly negative domestic sentiment toward normalization (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/17/trump-expects-expansion-of-abraham-accords-soon-hopes-s-arabia-will-join).

A fresh Saudi public reaffirmation of that condition in November would be evidence against rapid late-2025 expansion of the accords, because it would suggest the main candidate has not softened its position. Conversely, the absence of such a reaffirmation during this window would not guarantee a deal, but it would remove one visible obstacle. This is therefore a meaningful indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

Sources:
Reuters/Yahoo factbox on the Abraham Accords — https://www.yahoo.com/news/factbox-abraham-accords-115050294.html
MarketScreener/Reuters factbox — https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Factbox-What-are-the-Abraham-Accords-50878031/
The Seattle Times on the Abraham Accords — https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/what-are-the-abraham-accords-trumps-2020-mideast-deals/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), an official Saudi government statement publicly says that normalization or diplomatic relations with Israel require, as a condition, a Palestinian state, a pathway to a Palestinian state, implementation of the Arab Peace Initiative, or materially equivalent language linking normalization to Palestinian statehood.

Qualifying statements must be attributable to an official Saudi source, such as the Saudi Press Agency, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Crown Prince, the King, the Foreign Minister, or another senior Saudi official speaking in an official capacity. Official sources include, for example, https://www.spa.gov.sa/en and https://www.mofa.gov.sa/.

If no qualifying official Saudi statement is published during the window, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources: Saudi Press Agency (https://www.spa.gov.sa/en), Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.mofa.gov.sa/), and official verified Saudi government social-media or press-release accounts linked from those sites. Secondary confirmation may come from Reuters reporting if it clearly quotes or paraphrases an official Saudi statement published during the window (https://www.reuters.com/).

Edge cases: (1) General statements supporting Palestinian rights without linking them to normalization do not count. (2) Statements by non-Saudi officials about Saudi conditions do not count unless confirmed by an official Saudi source. (3) If a statement is issued within the window but only discovered later, it still counts if the publication timestamp shows it was first published between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive. (4) If all primary sources are unavailable, a consensus of at least two credible international outlets quoting the official Saudi statement may be used. (5) If a relevant event is announced during the window but explicitly described as unofficial, exploratory, or off the record, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: Saudi Arabia is the most-discussed potential new Abraham Accords entrant. Whether Riyadh publicly reiterates its Palestinian-state precondition in November is a strong near-term signal about the odds that any new country joins by year-end 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: An official Saudi government statement, attributable to the Saudi Press Agency, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Crown Prince, King, Foreign Minister, or senior Saudi official in official capacity, publicly links normalization/diplomatic relations with Israel to a Palestinian state, a pathway to Palestinian statehood, the Arab Peace Initiative, or materially equivalent language — published between 2025-10-31T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-30T23:59:59Z inclusive. Observable evidence: A dated press release, speech transcript, or credibly quoted statement from an official Saudi source explicitly conditioning Israel normalization on Palestinian statehood. Key entities: Crown Prince MBS, Saudi Foreign Ministry. Threshold: The statement must explicitly link normalization to Palestinian statehood (not just general support for Palestinian rights).
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Saudi Arabia normalization Israel Palestinian state condition 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find explicit conditioning statements. Query 2: 'Saudi Arabia Israel diplomatic relations Palestinian statehood requirement November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find any official statements from Saudi sources. Query 3: 'MBS Saudi Arabia Palestinian state normalization statement official November 18 2025' (Nov 1–30) — to find the specific White House meeting statement. Query 4: 'Saudi Foreign Ministry Palestinian statehood Israel normalization official statement October November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to check for additional official statements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) November 1, 2025 — Saudi commentator Ali Shihabi (close ties to leadership) quoted in NYT saying MBS links normalization to 'irrevocable, major steps toward a Palestinian state' [Times of Israel, Nov 1]. (2) November 2, 2025 — Multiple outlets reporting MBS rejects deal without Palestinian statehood. (3) November 9, 2025 — Saudi Foreign Ministry official Manal Radwan publicly stated conditions for Palestinian statehood as prerequisites, as quoted in Reuters/multiple outlets. (4) November 18, 2025 — MBS stated PUBLICLY in the Oval Office with Trump, in a joint press appearance: Saudi Arabia wants to be part of Abraham Accords 'but also to be sure that we secure a clear path of two-state solution' — reported by AFP, Al Arabiya (English), Times of Israel, multiple outlets. (5) Post-meeting reports (Nov 25-27) confirming MBS reiterated in closed session: 'irreversible, credible and time-bound path' to Palestinian statehood as precondition. Rejected: Saudi commentator Ali Shihabi (not an official Saudi government source, though close to leadership) — excluded per edge case 2. Saudi Foreign Ministry official Manal Radwan's quotes came via Reuters reporting on Gulf sources — potentially qualifying but secondary.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The strongest match is the November 18, 2025 statement by Crown Prince MBS (an official Saudi source per resolution criteria) during an official White House meeting with Trump. MBS stated publicly: 'We want to be part of the Abraham Accords, but also to be sure that we secure a clear path of two-state solution' — per [AFP, Nov 18](http://doc.afp.com/84EQ663), [Al Arabiya English, Nov 18](https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2025/11/18/mbs-says-normalization-with-israel-hinges-on-clear-path-to-palestinian-state), [Times of Israel, Nov 18](https://www.timesofisrael.com/mbs-tells-trump-he-wants-to-join-abraham-accords-but-path-to-palestinian-state-crucial/). This statement: (a) is attributable to an official Saudi source — the Crown Prince speaking in official capacity; (b) explicitly links normalization (joining the Abraham Accords) to a 'clear path' to a two-state solution/Palestinian statehood; (c) was made on November 18, 2025, within the resolution window; (d) goes beyond general Palestinian rights support — directly conditions normalization on Palestinian statehood. The Saudi Foreign Ministry official Manal Radwan also stated conditions (time-bound Israeli withdrawal, international protection force, PA restoration) as prerequisites for Palestinian statehood, per Reuters reporting cited in multiple outlets on November 9, 2025 — this also appears to qualify as an official Saudi government statement linking normalization to Palestinian state pathway.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest qualifying event in the window is the Reuters/multiple outlet reporting of Saudi Foreign Ministry official Manal Radwan's statements, published November 9, 2025. The most prominent qualifying event is MBS's public statement in the Oval Office on November 18, 2025. AFP published the report at November 18, 2025 (exact timestamp in AFP wire). Multiple independent outlets (Al Arabiya, Times of Israel, Express Tribune) also report it dated November 18, 2025. The Saudi Foreign Ministry official Manal Radwan statements were dated November 9, 2025 across Reuters, US News & World Report, Investing.com, and other outlets. Both events fall within the October 31–November 30, 2025 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest qualifying occurrence within the window appears to be November 9, 2025, when Saudi Foreign Ministry official Manal Radwan's statements were cited in Reuters reporting: calling for 'time-bound Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, deployment of an international protection force, and restoration of the Palestinian Authority in Gaza as prerequisites' — this appears tied to Palestinian statehood progress as a condition. However, the most explicit and unambiguous official statement directly linking normalization to Palestinian statehood comes from MBS himself on November 18, 2025, in the Oval Office. No earlier qualifying event (within the Oct 31–Nov 30 window) appears stronger or more direct.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: None. All sources consistently confirm Saudi Arabia maintained its position linking normalization to Palestinian statehood throughout this period. The Saudi Gazette (a Saudi publication) itself reported that 'the Crown Prince insisted that any normalization with Israel must include a credible, irreversible, and time-bound path toward establishing an independent Palestinian state—a position he reiterated publicly after the meeting.' Multiple U.S. officials quoted in Axios also confirm MBS's stated position. No source suggests Saudi Arabia retracted or softened this position within the window. Alternative interpretations: One could argue the Manal Radwan statements are about prerequisites for Palestinian statehood generally, not specifically about normalization — but Reuters and multiple outlets clearly frame her statements in the context of Saudi conditions for normalization. The MBS November 18 statement is unambiguous and directly public, meeting all criteria.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: Yes. The Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia — an official Saudi government figure at the highest level — publicly stated on November 18, 2025, in an official capacity during a White House meeting with President Trump, that Saudi Arabia's normalization with Israel (joining the Abraham Accords) requires 'a clear path of two-state solution.' This statement was widely reported by AFP and multiple credible outlets, and also confirmed by the Saudi Gazette (a Saudi publication). The statement directly, explicitly, and unambiguously links normalization to a pathway to Palestinian statehood, satisfying all resolution criteria. Additionally, Saudi Foreign Ministry official Manal Radwan made statements on approximately November 9, 2025 (per Reuters reporting) linking normalization conditions to Palestinian statehood prerequisites. The first qualifying occurrence within the window is November 9, 2025 (Manal Radwan via Reuters), with the most prominent occurrence being November 18, 2025 (MBS in Oval Office). Both are within the October 31–November 30, 2025 window.

question: Another France debt downgrade by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if France's long-term sovereign credit letter rating is downgraded by any of the three major credit rating agencies (S&P, Moody's, Fitch) at any point between September 12, 6:15 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. subquestions.question: Will Moody's change France's sovereign outlook to Negative, or downgrade France's long-term sovereign rating, between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13?
subquestions.background_information:
A further France sovereign downgrade by another major agency in late 2025 is more likely if agencies continue to signal worsening fiscal and political risks in the near term. Moody's is one of the three major agencies relevant to the ultimate question. AFP reported on 2025-09-12 that Fitch downgraded France's sovereign rating from AA- to A+, citing political instability and strained public finances, and noted debt projected to rise to 121% of GDP by 2027 from 113.2% in 2024. The same report said France's 2024 budget deficit was 5.8% of GDP, well above euro-area reference levels, and that the downgrade reflected weakened capacity to deliver fiscal consolidation: https://www.barrons.com/news/fitch-downgrades-france-s-credit-rating-in-new-debt-blow-0f8a3f0e . Another AFP summary the same day likewise emphasized France's 5.8% deficit, debt near 113% of GDP, and market concern over fiscal credibility: https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250912-france-risks-credit-downgrade-as-new-pm-tackles-budget .

Moody's outlook actions are informative because they often precede or substitute for near-term rating actions when an agency wants to signal elevated downgrade risk without immediately cutting the rating. If Moody's shifts France's outlook to Negative, or cuts the rating itself, that would be a concrete signal that near-term fundamentals are deteriorating enough to make an additional 2025 downgrade by a major agency more plausible.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13 (inclusive), Moody's publicly announces either: (a) a downgrade of France's long-term sovereign issuer/senior unsecured rating, or (b) a change in France's sovereign outlook to Negative from any non-Negative outlook. It resolves No if no such Moody's action is publicly announced during that window.

Primary resolution source: official Moody's Ratings announcements or sovereign ratings pages for France at https://ratings.moodys.com/sovereigns and any related Moody's press release or rating action notice published on https://www.moodys.com/ .

Fallback sources: a consensus of credible financial reporting clearly attributing the action to Moody's, such as Reuters, Bloomberg, AFP, or major financial newspapers, if Moody's content is paywalled or later removed. Example fallback source relevant to the topic: Reuters coverage via Investing.com at https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/france-faces-sovereign-rating-test-amid-political-chaos-3821092 .

Only actions first publicly disclosed during the window from 2025-09-13 through 2025-10-13 count. Announcements before 2025-09-13 do not count, even if markets react during the window. Announcements after 2025-10-13 do not count. If Moody's places France on review/watch but does not change the outlook to Negative and does not downgrade the rating during the window, that alone does not count for Yes. If no authoritative source can determine whether a qualifying Moody's action occurred in the window, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

[Financial Mirror](https://www.financialmirror.com/2025/10/07/euro-softens-on-fears-of-french-political-crisis/) (Oct 7, 2025): 'Moody's is widely anticipated to follow suit before the end of October.'
