question: Will Donald Trump visit North Korea in 2025?
description:
If U.S. President Donald Trump visits North Korea between August 4 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial or maritime territory of the listed country. Whether or not Trump enters the country's airspace during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or South Korea's presidential office officially announce between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 that Donald Trump and Kim Jong Un are expected to meet in 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A formal announcement that Trump and Kim are expected to meet in 2025 would be a strong leading indicator for a possible Trump visit to North Korea later in the year, because arranging such a summit would usually require advance diplomatic agreement and public signaling. Recent reporting suggests there is some momentum but also substantial uncertainty. On August 26, 2025, Trump said he hoped to meet Kim Jong Un later in 2025 and said he had a "very good relationship" with Kim, according to reporting summarizing his White House remarks: https://www.latestly.com/world/us-president-donald-trump-says-he-hopes-to-meet-north-korean-leader-kim-jong-un-in-2025-7080638.html . Reuters-republished reporting on August 26 said South Korean President Lee Jae Myung proposed that if Trump visits South Korea for a regional forum, a meeting with Kim could be arranged later this year: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/South-Korea-s-Lee-proposes-meeting-between-Trump-and-North-Korea-Kim-later-this-year-Lee-s-offi-50937129/ .

At the same time, there are reasons to doubt near-term progress. South Korea's national security adviser said on August 29 that North Korea had been "inactive in engaging in diplomacy with South Korea or the United States" and had "not shown willingness to engage in talks": https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10556864 . That makes any official announcement of an expected 2025 Trump-Kim meeting especially informative: it would signal that a key diplomatic barrier had been overcome.

This subquestion is not a restatement of whether Trump visits North Korea. Trump and Kim could be officially expected to meet in 2025 without the venue being North Korea, but such an announcement would materially increase the odds of a visit, especially because Trump's prior Kim diplomacy has included unusual venue choices and direct leader-level engagement.

Sources:
LatestLY - US President Donald Trump Says He Hopes To Meet North Korean Leader Kim Jong Un in 2025: https://www.latestly.com/world/us-president-donald-trump-says-he-hopes-to-meet-north-korean-leader-kim-jong-un-in-2025-7080638.html
MarketScreener / Reuters - South Korea's Lee proposes meeting between Trump and North Korea Kim later this year: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/South-Korea-s-Lee-proposes-meeting-between-Trump-and-North-Korea-Kim-later-this-year-Lee-s-offi-50937129/
The Korea Herald - N. Korea appears to be inactive in engaging in diplomacy with S. Korea or US: security adviser: https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10556864
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), an official public statement from either (a) the White House / U.S. government or (b) the South Korean presidential office explicitly states that Donald Trump and Kim Jong Un are expected, planned, scheduled, agreed in principle, or likely to meet in calendar year 2025.

Qualifying examples include official press releases, briefing transcripts, pool reports, or official spokesperson statements published on WhiteHouse.gov (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), the U.S. State Department site (https://www.state.gov/), or the Republic of Korea presidential office site (https://www.president.go.kr/ or any official successor domain), provided the statement clearly indicates an expected 2025 Trump-Kim meeting.

The question also resolves Yes if Trump states via an official/verified presidential or personal account that he and Kim will meet in 2025, but only if that statement is subsequently reported or archived by an authoritative source such as the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or a consensus of Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) and AP (https://apnews.com/).

The question resolves No if no such qualifying official announcement is made between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

Important clarifications:
- The announcement need not specify the venue; it only needs to say that a Trump-Kim meeting is expected in 2025.
- Statements merely expressing hope or desire to meet, without indicating an expected/planned/agreed meeting, do not count.
- Statements from unnamed officials reported only as anonymous sourcing do not count unless later confirmed in an official public statement within the resolution window.
- If an announcement is made within the window and later canceled, the question still resolves Yes.
- If the relevant official websites become unavailable, the fallback sources will be Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) and AP (https://apnews.com/) quoting or reproducing the official statement.
- If there is no clear official statement and only ambiguous media speculation, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A publicly announced expected Trump-Kim meeting would be a major precursor to any Trump visit to North Korea. It captures whether diplomatic channels have opened enough to support leader-level engagement, without simply asking whether the visit itself happens by an earlier date.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Official public statement from White House/U.S. government OR South Korean presidential office explicitly stating Trump and Kim Jong Un are expected/planned/scheduled/agreed in principle/likely to meet in 2025. Statements of mere hope or desire do not count. Anonymous sourcing alone does not count. Entities: Trump (U.S. President), Kim Jong Un (North Korean leader), White House, South Korean presidential office. Timing: October 1-31, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump Kim Jong Un meeting 2025 official announcement White House' (Oct 1-31) — to find official announcements. Query 2: 'Trump Kim Jong Un summit planned scheduled 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find any scheduling confirmations. Query 3: 'Trump Kim Jong Un meeting scheduled confirmed APEC October 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find APEC-related confirmations. Query 4: 'White House official statement Trump Kim Jong Un meeting expected planned 2025' (Oct 1-31) — narrower official statement search. Query 5: 'Trump Kim Jong Un will meet OR agreed to meet OR confirmed meeting 2025' (Oct 1-31). Query 6: 'Trump Kim Jong Un meeting South Korea APEC Panmunjom DMZ confirmed' (Oct 28-31) — checking final days.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events reviewed: (1) October 1, 2025 — White House official tells Yonhap that Trump is 'open to talks without preconditions' and a meeting 'may very well happen' — REJECTED: This expresses possibility/hope, not an expected/planned/scheduled meeting. (2) October 14-17 — South Korean Unification Minister Chung says meeting 'could' happen at APEC — REJECTED: Speculative, from Unification Minister not presidential office, and expresses possibility not expectation. (3) October 24-25 — Senior U.S. official explicitly states meeting is 'NOT on the schedule for this trip' and 'no plans' — NEGATIVE evidence, confirms no planned meeting. (4) October 27 — South Korean presidential office deputy says meeting 'unlikely to happen soon' — NEGATIVE evidence. (5) October 28 — South Korea and U.S. confirm NOT discussing Kim-Trump meeting as agenda item — NEGATIVE evidence. (6) October 29 — Trump states he and Kim 'couldn't work out timing' for meeting — definitive confirmation no meeting planned or occurred during visit. (7) October 30 — Trump declines to meet Kim, says 'would return' — confirms no meeting in 2025 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No statement from any qualifying source (White House, U.S. government, or South Korean presidential office) explicitly confirmed that Trump and Kim Jong Un were expected/planned/scheduled/agreed in principle to meet in 2025. The White House October 1 statement ('may very well happen') [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2023449) expresses hope/possibility, not expectation. A senior U.S. official confirmed on October 24-25 that the meeting was 'NOT on the schedule' [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/79XY2CQ) [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/no-plans-for-trump-to-meet-north-koreas-kim-during-asia-tour-official/3726210). South Korean presidential office deputy stated meeting was 'unlikely to happen soon' on October 27 [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/South-Korean-presidential-aide-says-meeting-between-Trump-and-North-Koreas-Kim-unlikely-to-happen-soon). South Korea-U.S. confirmed NOT discussing Kim-Trump meeting as agenda on October 28 [Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20251028010100315). Trump himself confirmed on October 29 that timing 'didn't work out' [Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20251029009751315). None of these qualify for Yes resolution.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The definitively negative outcome was established by Trump's October 29, 2025 statement that he and Kim 'couldn't work out timing' during his South Korea visit, and confirmed by the October 30 reporting that Trump declined to meet Kim and said he would 'return' for such a meeting. The window closed on October 31, 2025 with no qualifying event having occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying 'Yes' event occurred at any point during the October 1-31, 2025 window. All candidate events either expressed mere hope/openness (insufficient under criteria) or were explicitly negative (U.S. officials confirming no meeting was scheduled).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The closest possible qualifying statement was the White House official's October 1 comment that a meeting 'may very well happen' — but this clearly expresses possibility/hope, not expectation/planning, and falls below the resolution threshold. All subsequent official statements moved further from a 'Yes' outcome, with explicit denials from U.S. officials (Oct 24-25), the South Korean presidential office (Oct 27), and Trump himself (Oct 29). No Reuters or AP article reported an official confirmed statement of a planned/expected Trump-Kim 2025 meeting. The question definitively resolves No.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Throughout October 2025, while there was significant speculation and Trump expressed personal openness to meeting Kim, no official statement from the White House, U.S. government, or South Korean presidential office ever explicitly stated that Trump and Kim were expected, planned, scheduled, or agreed in principle to meet in 2025. Multiple official statements explicitly denied any such plan. Trump's own October 29 statement confirmed the meeting did not happen, and by October 30-31, the window closed without any qualifying announcement.

question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla obtain a California DMV Autonomous Vehicle Testing Permit or Deployment Permit for driverless vehicles between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A key bottleneck for Tesla launching unsupervised FSD is regulatory authorization in major jurisdictions. California is especially relevant because Tesla is already operating a Bay Area ride-hailing service there, but reporting before 2025-09-01 indicates that service uses human drivers and that Tesla had not yet secured the permits needed for autonomous vehicle operations. Electrek reported on 2025-07-31 that Tesla's Bay Area service was powered by human drivers and that Tesla had not applied for the required California autonomous vehicle permits at that time: https://electrek.co/2025/07/31/tesla-robotaxis-are-officially-powered-by-human-drivers-as-it-launches-ride-hailing-in-bay-area/ . Breitbart similarly reported on 2025-07-29 that Tesla was awaiting regulatory approval for autonomous robotaxis in additional markets, and that California rules required an initial pilot phase: https://www.breitbart.com/tech/2025/07/29/not-so-robo-elon-musk-introduces-tesla-taxi-service-with-human-drivers-in-san-francisco/ .

In California, the DMV regulates autonomous vehicle testing and deployment permits, including driverless testing and driverless deployment. Public permit-holder lists are published by the California DMV here: https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/ . Separately, the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) regulates passenger service aspects of autonomous ride-hailing and charter-party operations, with information published here: https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/regulatory-services/licensing/transportation-licensing-and-analysis-branch/autonomous-vehicle-programs . Because the ultimate question requires broad public availability of unsupervised FSD, movement by Tesla to obtain a California driverless AV permit would be strong evidence that Tesla is progressing beyond supervised driver-assist and toward legally deployable unsupervised operation.

As of 2025-09-01, public reporting suggests Tesla is still at a supervised stage in California, making any newly granted California driverless permit during September 2025 a meaningful early indicator rather than a foregone conclusion.

Sources:
California DMV Autonomous Vehicles page https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/
California CPUC Autonomous Vehicle Programs https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/regulatory-services/licensing/transportation-licensing-and-analysis-branch/autonomous-vehicle-programs
Electrek - Tesla's Robotaxis are officially powered by human drivers as it launches ride-hailing in Bay Area https://electrek.co/2025/07/31/tesla-robotaxis-are-officially-powered-by-human-drivers-as-it-launches-ride-hailing-in-bay-area/
Breitbart - Not So Robo: Elon Musk Introduces Tesla Taxi Service with Human Drivers in San Francisco https://www.breitbart.com/tech/2025/07/29/not-so-robo-elon-musk-introduces-tesla-taxi-service-with-human-drivers-in-san-francisco/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) publicly lists Tesla, Inc. (or a clearly identified Tesla-affiliated operating entity) as having been granted either (a) a Driverless Testing Permit or (b) a Deployment Permit for autonomous vehicles in California.

This question resolves No if no such California DMV permit grant is publicly documented by 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC.

Primary source for resolution: the California DMV Autonomous Vehicles page and its linked manufacturer/permit-holder lists: https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/ .

A Tesla-affiliated entity counts only if the DMV listing clearly identifies Tesla branding or if Tesla publicly states that the permit holder is its operating subsidiary for the autonomous driving program. Acceptable supplementary confirmation sources include Tesla investor relations or newsroom pages (https://ir.tesla.com/ and https://www.tesla.com/blog), or a California DMV press release.

If the DMV site structure changes, archived snapshots from the California DMV domain or an official California press release may be used as fallback evidence. CPUC approvals alone do not count for Yes unless accompanied by a qualifying California DMV driverless testing or deployment permit, because the question is specifically about DMV AV permitting. If an application is filed but not granted within the window from 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01, the question resolves No. If the permit grant date is ambiguous, the earliest official public posting date on the DMV website or official California press release will control.

Tesla Investor Relations https://ir.tesla.com/
Tesla Blog https://www.tesla.com/blog

subquestions.rationale: A California driverless AV permit is not the same as launching unsupervised FSD, but it is a concrete, near-term indicator that Tesla is crossing an important regulatory threshold for driverless operation on public roads. If Tesla cannot secure a driverless permit even in this early window, that is evidence against rapid progress toward a broad unsupervised launch by the ultimate deadline; if it does secure one, forecasters should update upward.

question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.background_information:
A key live issue in late 2025 is whether Washington will provide the enabling commitment that European governments say is necessary for any credible Ukraine security architecture. Multiple reports before 2025-10-31 indicate that European-led security guarantees for Ukraine are being actively discussed, but that these plans are stalled without a U.S. role. CBC reported on 2025-09-04 that roughly 30 Western leaders discussed guarantees for Kyiv and that participants agreed any European military role would require U.S. security guarantees as a "back-stop," which President Trump had not yet formalized as of that date (https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/ukraine-security-guarantees-us-help-1.7320010). Foreign Policy similarly reported on 2025-09-04 that 26 countries had committed to a postwar reassurance force for Ukraine, while Trump was described as open to security guarantees but not U.S. ground troops, instead potentially considering air support (https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/09/04/ukraine-europe-troops-security-guarantees-trump-macron-starmer/). 

Ukrainska Pravda reported on 2025-08-22 that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Andrii Yermak discussed security guarantees, with working groups developing both political-legal and military components; the article says a U.S. "backstop mechanism" with air cover was specifically being worked out (https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/22/7512345/). The G7 foreign ministers also said on 2025-09-24 that they would work with the United States to provide Ukraine with "robust and credible security guarantees" (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/g7-vows-continued-support-for-ukraine-calls-for-gaza-ceasefire/3301122). 

This makes a formal U.S. announcement of a "backstop" highly relevant: it would not itself necessarily equal the ultimate Article 5-style binding security guarantee, but it would be a concrete observable step toward one. It would signal that the Trump administration is willing to move from vague support to an operational security role tied to Ukraine's defense. By contrast, if no such announcement occurs even during an active negotiation period, that is evidence against the ultimate question resolving Yes by year-end.

subquestions.question: Will the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index present situation component be at least 140.0 in the January 2026 release?
subquestions.background_information:
Consumer spending is a major driver of U.S. GDP, so near-term readings on household confidence are a useful indicator for whether Q4 2025 growth is likely to land in a moderate positive range such as 2.0%–2.5%. The provided news notes that Q3 2025 GDP growth was strong at 4.3% annualized and was powered by domestic consumption, but also that consumer sentiment/confidence had weakened late in 2025, with the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index falling and remaining well below its earlier 2025 peak. If households still report a strong assessment of current business and labor-market conditions in January 2026, that would be evidence that consumption likely held up through late Q4 rather than slowing sharply. The Conference Board publishes both an overall Consumer Confidence Index and a Present Situation Index; the latter is especially relevant for contemporaneous spending conditions. The Conference Board's consumer confidence release page is here: https://www.conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence. Historical releases and data tables are posted on that site, and major financial data aggregators such as FRED also track related confidence series: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/. The Q3 GDP context comes from the BEA release page and contemporaneous reporting that Q3 real GDP rose 4.3% annualized after shutdown-related delays: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product and https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/us-economy-grew-much-faster-than-expected-third-quarter-delayed-report-shows. The NBC New York summary also notes that consumer confidence had recently declined, making the January reading informative rather than trivial: https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/business/money-report/spending-helped-drive-4-3-economic-growth-in-third-quarter-delayed-gdp-report-shows/6348823/.

Sources:
Conference Board Consumer Confidence page — https://www.conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence
BEA GDP page — https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
Fox Business on Q3 2025 GDP — https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/us-economy-grew-much-faster-than-expected-third-quarter-delayed-report-shows
NBC New York on Q3 GDP and confidence — https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/business/money-report/spending-helped-drive-4-3-economic-growth-in-third-quarter-delayed-gdp-report-shows/6348823/
FRED homepage — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

It resolves No if that January 2026 release occurs within that window and reports the Present Situation Index below 140.0.

If the Conference Board publishes the January 2026 release within the resolution window but later revises or amends the number, the first value published in that January 2026 release will be used. If the January 2026 release is not published by 2026-01-28, this question should be considered unresolvable. If the Conference Board website is unavailable, a materially identical contemporaneous republication by a major wire service or data terminal report quoting the Conference Board January 2026 Present Situation Index may be used as a fallback, but only if it clearly identifies the January 2026 value.

Conference Board data/download portal root — https://www.conference-board.org/

subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question is about whether Q4 2025 GDP growth lands in a fairly narrow moderate-growth band. Consumer spending is the largest GDP component, and a strong January read on households' assessment of present conditions is an informative cross-check on whether spending likely remained solid through late Q4. This is not a restatement of GDP itself; it is a distinct, timely indicator tied to the main demand engine behind recent growth.

question: Foreign intervention in Gaza in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if police officers, security forces, or military personnel belonging to neither Israel nor a Palestinian entity begin an officially acknowledged police, military, peacekeeping, and/or security operation on the ground within Gaza by December 31, 2025 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The foreign personnel must physically enter the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip to qualify. Entering the maritime territory, as occurred during the US’s attempt to construct a floating pier in 2024, or entering the airspace will not qualify. 

Entering Israeli controlled buffer zones will not qualify.  

Egyptian or other forces operating solely along the Egyptian/Gaza border will not qualify regardless of if they cross the border. 

Foreign personnel carrying out individual special operations, diplomatic missions, or solely humanitarian operations will not qualify.

Qualifying deployments must involve active-duty personnel of at least one foreign state or international institution (e.g., the UN or multinational missions) who are officially sent to Gaza for an operational role (e.g., peacekeeping, convoy escort, detention, logistical support). To qualify, the deployment must occur within the specified timeframe; mere announcements will not suffice.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the UN Security Council adopt, between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15 inclusive, a resolution that explicitly authorizes or endorses deployment of a multinational or international security/stabilization/peacekeeping force inside Gaza?
subquestions.background_information:
A key bottleneck for foreign intervention in Gaza appears to be the creation of a formal legal-political framework. On 2025-10-14, Germany's foreign minister said talks were underway with Russia and China on a UN Security Council resolution backing Trump's Gaza plan, and specifically said such a legal framework was essential for deploying a multinational International Stabilization Force in Gaza. This directly links UNSC action to the plausibility of an eventual on-the-ground foreign security deployment in Gaza. See Anadolu Ajansı, 2025-10-14: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/germany-says-talks-underway-for-un-security-council-resolution-on-trumps-gaza-plan/3718011

Recent reporting also suggests that post-ceasefire plans already contemplate an international force for Gaza, but that consensus is incomplete. Asia Times reported on 2025-10-11 that the ceasefire's later phases could include a temporary International Stabilization Force and international civil administrators, though consensus remained pending. https://asiatimes.com/2025/10/the-first-day-after-the-gaza-war/

There is also precedent for foreign actors discussing operational roles around Gaza without yet entering Gaza itself. For example, the EU announced readiness to restart its civilian mission monitoring the Rafah crossing, part of broader ceasefire support, but this is border-focused and not necessarily equivalent to a foreign security operation on the ground within Gaza as defined by the ultimate question. Anadolu Ajansı, 2025-10-13: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-vows-to-restart-civilian-mission-to-monitor-border-crossing-between-gaza-egypt/3717229

This makes a UNSC resolution an informative crux: if passed, it would strongly increase the odds of an officially acknowledged foreign ground operation in Gaza by year-end; if it fails or stalls, prospects for such intervention likely fall.

Sources:
Anadolu Ajansı - Germany says talks underway for UN Security Council resolution on Trump's Gaza plan - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/germany-says-talks-underway-for-un-security-council-resolution-on-trumps-gaza-plan/3718011
Asia Times - The first day after the Gaza war - https://asiatimes.com/2025/10/the-first-day-after-the-gaza-war/
Anadolu Ajansı - EU vows to restart civilian mission to monitor border crossing between Gaza, Egypt - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-vows-to-restart-civilian-mission-to-monitor-border-crossing-between-gaza-egypt/3717229
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15 inclusive, the UN Security Council adopts a resolution that explicitly authorizes, endorses, approves, welcomes, or establishes deployment of a multinational, international, UN, or similar security / stabilization / peacekeeping force inside the Gaza Strip.

For Yes, the adopted resolution must do more than call generally for peace or humanitarian aid; it must explicitly refer to deployment of foreign or international personnel in a security, policing, monitoring, stabilization, peacekeeping, escort, protection, or similar operational role in Gaza itself.

This question resolves No if no such UNSC resolution is adopted by 2025-11-15 23:59:59 UTC.

Resolution will primarily rely on the official UN Security Council resolutions database and meeting records:
- UN Security Council resolutions search / documents: https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/content/resolutions
- UN Digital Library Security Council documents: https://digitallibrary.un.org/

Fallback sources, if needed for timing or text confirmation, are the UN News site and official Security Council press releases:
- UN News: https://news.un.org/
- UN Security Council press statements/meetings: https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/

If the Council votes on a draft but it fails, is vetoed, is postponed, or remains under negotiation without adoption during the window 2025-10-16 to 2025-11-15, the question resolves No.

If a resolution is adopted during the window but its language is ambiguous, resolution should be based on the plain text of the resolution. If the text does not explicitly connect the Council's action to deployment of an international/foreign security-type mission in Gaza, it does not qualify.
subquestions.rationale: A UNSC mandate or endorsement is one of the clearest near-term institutional prerequisites for many plausible foreign intervention scenarios in Gaza. It is not the same as the ultimate question, because it asks about a diplomatic/legal authorization step rather than troops actually beginning operations on the ground. But if it happens, it would materially raise the likelihood of qualifying foreign intervention by 2025-12-31.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question resolves Yes if the UN Security Council adopts a resolution between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15 (inclusive) that explicitly authorizes, endorses, approves, welcomes, or establishes deployment of a multinational/international security/stabilization/peacekeeping force inside Gaza. The resolution must go beyond general peace calls and explicitly refer to deployment of foreign/international personnel in a security/peacekeeping/stabilization role in Gaza itself.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'UN Security Council resolution Gaza peacekeeping force 2025' (Oct 16–Nov 15) — to find any resolution adopted in the window. Query 2: 'UNSC resolution Gaza multinational security stabilization force October November 2025' — to find specific drafts or adoptions. Query 3: 'UN Security Council Resolution 2803 Gaza November 17 18 2025' — to confirm exact date. Query 4: 'UNSC vote Gaza international stabilization force resolution adopted November 2025' — to verify adoption date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key candidate: UNSC Resolution 2803, which authorizes an International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza. Multiple sources confirm adoption on November 17, 2025 (New York time/Eastern), with 13 votes in favor and abstentions from Russia and China. The vote was scheduled for 5:00 PM New York time (22:00 GMT) on November 17, 2025. Some sources report it as November 18 due to timezone differences. During the window (Oct 16–Nov 15), there were only draft resolutions being circulated (US draft circulated Nov 4–6, Russia counter-draft Nov 14) — no adoption. No other qualifying UNSC resolution was adopted during Oct 16–Nov 15.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Resolution 2803 explicitly authorizes an International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza — this directly matches the resolution criteria. However, the adoption date of November 17, 2025 falls OUTSIDE the resolution window which closes on November 15, 2025 at 23:59:59 UTC. During the window (Oct 16–Nov 15), the US draft was circulated (Nov 4–6) and Russia introduced a competing draft (Nov 14), but NO resolution was adopted. The vote was scheduled for and occurred on November 17, 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Resolution 2803 was voted on November 17, 2025 at 5:00 PM New York time (22:00 GMT / UTC). This is November 17, 2025 at 22:00:00 UTC — after the window's close on November 15, 2025 at 23:59:59 UTC. During the window itself (Oct 16–Nov 15), multiple sources confirm no UNSC resolution on Gaza's ISF was adopted, only drafts were circulated.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying UNSC resolution authorizing an international security/stabilization force in Gaza was adopted during Oct 16–Nov 15, 2025. Resolution 2803 is the first such resolution and it was adopted on November 17, 2025 — after the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked multiple sources: The Hindu (Nov 15 article says vote scheduled for Nov 17), Digital Journal (vote at 5 PM on Nov 17), UN News live coverage (Nov 17 vote), multiple Nov 18 articles reporting adoption. France Diplomatie, Anadolu, Irish Times, RT, and Korean press all confirm Nov 17 as the vote date (New York time). The Chathamhouse article mentions 'November 17, 2025' as the adoption date. No source places adoption within the Oct 16–Nov 15 window. Russia's competing draft was introduced on Nov 14 (within window) but was not adopted. The question explicitly states: 'If the Council votes on a draft but it fails, is vetoed, is postponed, or remains under negotiation without adoption during the window 2025-10-16 to 2025-11-15, the question resolves No.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution 2803, which explicitly authorizes the International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza and fully satisfies the resolution criteria, was adopted on November 17, 2025 — two days after the resolution window closed on November 15, 2025. During the window, only draft resolutions were circulated and negotiated, with no adoption. The question therefore resolves No. The window closed on November 15, 2025 with no qualifying resolution adopted.

question: U.S. recognizes Russian sovereignty over Crimea in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. government formally recognizes Russian sovereignty over the majority of the Crimean peninsula by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Donald Trump's March 25, 2019, recognition of Israel's sovereignty over the Golan Heights is an example of a qualifying action. 

Statement of intents, or announcements of planned recognition will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Government, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of State remove or materially revise the 2018 'Crimea Declaration' from its official website between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
A meaningful early indicator of possible U.S. recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea is whether the U.S. government first backs away from its existing formal non-recognition policy. On July 25, 2018, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo issued the 'Crimea Declaration,' stating that 'the United States rejects Russia's attempted annexation of Crimea and pledges to maintain this policy until Ukraine's territorial integrity is restored.' The declaration explicitly analogized U.S. policy to the Welles Declaration on non-recognition of Soviet annexation of the Baltics. This is a standing official statement of U.S. policy and therefore a natural precursor document to watch for any reversal or softening. State Department archive: https://2017-2021.state.gov/crimea-declaration/ and current State archive copy: https://2009-2017.state.gov/r/pa/prs/ps/2018/07/284005.htm

Recent reporting indicates the issue remains live inside U.S. policy debate. The Hill reported on May 31, 2025 that former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo warned against recognizing Russian control over Crimea and specifically referenced the 2018 Crimea Declaration as the policy that should be maintained, implying that recognition had been considered by the Trump administration in 2025. https://thehill.com/policy/international/5328230-pompeo-warns-against-us-recognizing-russian-control-over-crimea/

The ultimate market requires formal U.S. recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea by the end of 2025. Such recognition would be much easier politically and bureaucratically if the administration first removed, superseded, or materially diluted the most prominent official U.S. non-recognition statement. Conversely, leaving the declaration untouched through November would be some evidence against near-term recognition.

Sources:
U.S. Department of State (2018 Crimea Declaration): https://2017-2021.state.gov/crimea-declaration/
U.S. Department of State archive copy: https://2009-2017.state.gov/r/pa/prs/ps/2018/07/284005.htm
The Hill - Pompeo warns against US recognizing Russian control over Crimea: https://thehill.com/policy/international/5328230-pompeo-warns-against-us-recognizing-russian-control-over-crimea/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of State's official website either (a) removes public access to the 2018 'Crimea Declaration' page without an equivalent replacement affirming non-recognition, or (b) publishes an official replacement, update, notice, or edited version that materially revises or repudiates the declaration's core non-recognition policy toward Crimea.

For purposes of this question, 'materially revise or repudiate' means an official State Department webpage or document stating, in substance, at least one of the following: that the United States no longer rejects Russia's annexation/sovereignty claim over Crimea; that the 2018 declaration is superseded or no longer reflects U.S. policy; or that the United States recognizes, accepts, or is prepared to treat Crimea as Russian sovereign territory. Mere website redesign, relocation to a new URL, archival migration, temporary outage, or changes to formatting/navigation do NOT qualify if the declaration remains publicly accessible or is replaced by substantially similar non-recognition language.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying removal or material revision occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30.

Primary sources for resolution:
- Current/archived State Department Crimea Declaration pages: https://2017-2021.state.gov/crimea-declaration/ and https://2009-2017.state.gov/r/pa/prs/ps/2018/07/284005.htm
- U.S. Department of State official site search / press statements: https://www.state.gov/ and https://www.state.gov/press-releases/

Fallback evidence if the webpage structure changes:
- Internet Archive Wayback Machine snapshots of the relevant State Department pages: https://web.archive.org/
- Official State Department X account for policy statements: https://x.com/StateDept

If the evidence is mixed, the resolution should follow the clearest official State Department publication issued within the window. If no authoritative official publication can establish a qualifying policy change within the window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: Formal recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea would likely require first undoing or superseding the U.S.'s existing formal non-recognition commitment. A public rollback of the 2018 Crimea Declaration is therefore a concrete, observable precursor that would strongly increase the odds of the ultimate question resolving Yes.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition for Yes: The U.S. State Department's official website must have (a) removed the 2018 Crimea Declaration page without equivalent non-recognition replacement, OR (b) published an official document on state.gov materially revising or repudiating the declaration's core non-recognition policy toward Crimea — specifically within October 31–November 30, 2025. Observable evidence would be: news reports confirming the state.gov Crimea Declaration page was removed/altered, or an official State Department press release explicitly stating the U.S. now accepts/recognizes Russian sovereignty over Crimea.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'U.S. State Department Crimea Declaration 2018 removed revised' (Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025) — to find direct evidence of webpage changes; 2) 'State Department Crimea non-recognition policy change 2025' — to find policy shift announcements; 3) '"Crimea Declaration" State Department website deleted updated November 2025' — direct website action; 4) 'United States officially recognizes Crimea Russia announcement State Department' — official recognition; 5) 'State Department press release Crimea non-recognition policy November 2025' — official statements; 6) 'Rubio State Department Crimea sovereignty recognition official statement' — statements by Secretary of State.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Reports of a leaked 28-point U.S. peace plan including 'de facto' recognition of Crimea as Russian (Nov 20–28, 2025) — REJECTED: this was a leaked/proposed plan, not an official State Department action; White House Press Secretary explicitly called all reporting 'speculative until officially confirmed.' (2) Revised 19-point Geneva plan (Nov 23–24, 2025) — REJECTED: this actually removed territorial recognition requirements, and Russia dismissed it as 'unconstructive'; no official State Dept website action. (3) Reports that US 'may' or is 'considering' recognizing Crimea (Nov 28) — REJECTED: all phrased as media speculation/leaks, not official U.S. government declarations. No candidate event found that involves the State Department actually removing or materially revising the Crimea Declaration webpage.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found explicitly states that the State Department's Crimea Declaration page was removed or materially revised. All coverage concerns ongoing diplomatic negotiations about a potential peace plan. The White House and State Department have not issued any official statement recognizing Russian sovereignty over Crimea. Putin himself was still demanding formal U.S. recognition as a precondition for talks as of Nov 27–28, indicating it had not happened. Multiple sources explicitly describe proposed recognition as a 'significant departure from longstanding U.S. policy' — implying the policy had NOT changed yet. Rubio described any peace plan as a 'living, breathing document' — still under negotiation, not finalized.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying event occurred within the window. The State Department Crimea Declaration was not removed or materially revised on any specific date within Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at all within the window, let alone a first occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification attempts to disprove the No conclusion: Multiple articles from Nov 20–29, 2025, discuss potential U.S. recognition of Crimea as part of peace negotiations, but all describe future possibilities or leaked documents, not official State Department website actions. The White House explicitly called reports 'speculative.' Russia was still demanding recognition, confirming it hadn't been granted. The revised 19-point plan removed territorial recognition. No contradictory evidence found — all sources consistently show the policy change was under discussion but never officially adopted during this window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. While there were extensive diplomatic discussions about a U.S. peace plan potentially including recognition of Russian control over Crimea, no official State Department action occurred during Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025, that would satisfy the resolution criteria. The Crimea Declaration was not removed from state.gov, and no official State Department publication materially revised or repudiated the non-recognition policy. All reports of potential recognition were based on leaked draft proposals, not official government actions, and the White House explicitly called such reporting 'speculative.' The window closed on November 30, 2025, with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: Will EJ Antoni be confirmed as BLS Commissioner in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if E.J. Antoni is confirmed as Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If Antoni’s nomination is formally withdrawn, or if the Senate rejects their nomination, this market will immediately resolve to “No”.

The Senate must confirm this nominee for this market to resolve to "Yes". Recess appointments without Senate confirmation will not count toward a "Yes" resolution.

The resolution source for this market is information from the U.S. Senate (see: https://www.senate.gov/legislative/NominationsRejectedorWithdrawn.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Senate HELP Committee hold a nomination hearing for E.J. Antoni to be Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-28?
subquestions.background_information:
A committee hearing is a meaningful near-term indicator for whether a nominee is on track for Senate confirmation, because most executive-branch nominees need to receive committee consideration before a floor vote. The Bureau of Labor Statistics sits within the Department of Labor, and labor-related nominations are typically handled by the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP), whose nominations page and hearing schedule publicly track such activity: https://www.help.senate.gov/hearings and https://www.help.senate.gov/nominations.

E.J. Antoni was nominated in mid-August 2025 after President Trump fired BLS Commissioner Erika McEntarfer. News reports before 2025-09-01 describe the nomination as controversial, with Senate Democrats publicly opposing Antoni and questioning his qualifications and views on BLS data releases. See Newsday (2025-08-16): https://www.newsday.com/business/trump-firing-data-chief-pressure-economic-numbers-upward-b6r2h8k7 and The Hill (2025-08-17): https://thehill.com/. Reporting also notes the Senate partisan balance is 53 Republicans to 47 Democrats, which makes committee and floor scheduling decisions especially relevant to Antoni’s prospects: https://coloradonewsline.com/2025/08/16/trump-taps-economist-from-far-right-foundation-to-head-agency-that-tracks-jobs-numbers/.

As of 2025-09-01, the key observable bottleneck is whether Antoni’s nomination advances into the formal Senate process via a HELP Committee hearing. question: TikTok sale announced in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if ByteDance announces their intention to sell TikTok by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to “No”.

A public announcement of the intention to sell TikTok will qualify even if a sale has not been finalized. This includes any formal declaration made by ByteDance or its authorized representatives regarding their plans to sell or transfer ownership of TikTok.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from ByteDance. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will ByteDance or TikTok publicly state between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-17 (inclusive) that they are engaged in negotiations, discussions, or a proposed transaction to divest, sell, or transfer ownership of TikTok's U.S. operations?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful early indicator for whether ByteDance will later announce an intention to sell TikTok by the end of 2025. The ultimate question is specifically about ByteDance announcing an intention to sell TikTok. A narrower but distinct precursor is whether ByteDance or TikTok publicly acknowledges active negotiations or a proposed transaction concerning TikTok's U.S. operations before the current U.S. deadline.

As of mid-2025, the U.S. government had extended the deadline for ByteDance to divest TikTok's U.S. assets to September 17, 2025. Reuters reported that President Trump signed an executive order extending the enforcement deadline by 90 days, to September 17, 2025, while the White House said the administration wanted a deal that protects U.S. national security and keeps TikTok operating in the U.S. https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-extend-deadline-bytedance-divest-tiktok-wsj-reports-2025-06-17/

There were also substantial public claims from President Trump that a buyer group existed. Reuters reported on June 29, 2025 that Trump said he had found a buyer for TikTok, describing it as a group of 'very wealthy people,' while noting the deal would likely need China's approval. https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-says-he-has-found-buyer-tiktok-2025-06-29/

However, the ultimate market resolves based on ByteDance announcing its intention to sell, not on statements by Trump or unnamed prospective buyers. That makes public acknowledgement from ByteDance or TikTok of negotiations or a proposed divestiture a meaningful crux: if ByteDance begins confirming talks or a proposed structure, that would be strong evidence that a later formal sale-intention announcement is more likely. Conversely, continued silence or denials from ByteDance close to the September 17 deadline would be evidence against the ultimate outcome.

This subquestion is not merely the main question with an earlier date. It asks about a different observable event: whether ByteDance or TikTok publicly acknowledges negotiations or a proposed divestiture process, which is often a precursor to a formal announcement of intent to sell.

Sources:
Reuters: Trump to extend deadline for ByteDance to divest TikTok to Sept. 17 https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-extend-deadline-bytedance-divest-tiktok-wsj-reports-2025-06-17/
Reuters: Trump says he has found buyer for TikTok https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-says-he-has-found-buyer-tiktok-2025-06-29/
U.S. Supreme Court case materials / background on the divest-or-ban law (general legal context) https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/24pdf/24a587_3f14.pdf
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-17 inclusive, ByteDance Ltd., TikTok, or an explicitly authorized representative of either company publicly states that they are engaged in negotiations, discussions, talks, or a proposed transaction to divest, sell, spin off, transfer ownership of, or otherwise separate TikTok's U.S. operations from ByteDance ownership.

Qualifying statements must be public and attributable to one of the following:
1. An official ByteDance or TikTok press release or newsroom post;
2. An official company social media account;
3. A named company spokesperson quoted by a credible news outlet;
4. A filing, court submission, or other official document issued by the company.

Examples of qualifying language include statements such as: 'we are in talks regarding a sale,' 'we are evaluating a divestiture proposal,' 'a transaction is under discussion,' or 'ownership transfer of U.S. operations is being negotiated.'

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-17 inclusive.

Statements by third parties alone (for example, the U.S. President, unnamed sources, potential buyers, or media speculation) do not count unless they are accompanied by an attributable public statement from ByteDance, TikTok, or an authorized representative. A flat denial of negotiations does not count as Yes. Ambiguous statements that mention 'compliance discussions' or 'regulatory engagement' without indicating negotiations or a proposed transaction to divest/sell/transfer ownership do not count.

Primary sources for resolution will be official ByteDance and TikTok communications:
- ByteDance newsroom or official site: https://www.bytedance.com/en/
- TikTok newsroom: https://newsroom.tiktok.com/
- TikTok official X account: https://x.com/TikTok

Secondary resolution sources, if needed, will be credible reporting that quotes named company representatives, such as:
- Reuters https://www.reuters.com/
- AP News https://apnews.com/
- The Wall Street Journal https://www.wsj.com/

If no authoritative public evidence is available by the end date, the question resolves No. If relevant company statements are issued within the window but become inaccessible later, archived versions or reproductions in Reuters/AP/WSJ quoting the statement may be used. If an event is only rumored within the window and not publicly acknowledged by the company until after 2025-09-17, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: A public acknowledgement by ByteDance or TikTok that sale-related negotiations are underway would be a strong leading indicator that ByteDance may later announce an intention to sell TikTok. It is distinct from the ultimate question because it focuses on an earlier precursor signal—admitted deal talks or a proposed transaction structure—rather than a formal sale-intention announcement itself.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: ByteDance Ltd., TikTok, or an explicitly authorized representative publicly states (via press release, official social media, named company spokesperson quoted by credible outlet, or official filing) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-17 that they are engaged in negotiations, discussions, or a proposed transaction to divest/sell/transfer ownership of TikTok's U.S. operations. Statements by third parties (e.g., U.S. President, Treasury Secretary, Trade Representative, Chinese officials) do NOT qualify unless accompanied by a ByteDance/TikTok statement.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'ByteDance TikTok divestiture sale negotiations US operations 2025' (Sep 1-17) — to find any company statements. Query 2: 'TikTok ByteDance sell divest US statement official September 2025' (Sep 1-17) — to find official company communications. Query 3: 'ByteDance TikTok official statement spokesperson sale divestiture September 2025' (Sep 1-17) — targeting named spokesperson quotes. Query 4: 'TikTok newsroom press release ByteDance statement negotiations transaction September 2025' (Sep 1-17) — targeting official channels. Query 5: 'TikTok ByteDance denies confirms reaction framework deal divestiture September 15 16 17 2025' (Sep 14-17) — targeting company responses to the framework deal announcement. Query 6: 'ByteDance TikTok company statement comment framework deal sale September 16 17 2025' (Sep 15-17) — final check on company responses.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) U.S.-China framework deal announced Sept 15, 2025 — all statements from U.S. officials (Bessent, Greer, Trump) and Chinese negotiator Li Chenggang. REJECTED: These are third-party statements per resolution criteria. (2) CNBC (Sept 15) explicitly noted 'TikTok has not yet responded to a request for comment.' — confirms NO TikTok company statement. (3) Gizmodo (Sept 15) noted 'Bytedance has repeatedly stated it is not interested in selling TikTok.' — prior position, not a qualifying statement in the window. (4) Trump extended deadline to Dec 16 via executive order (Sept 16) — U.S. government action, not a ByteDance/TikTok statement. No qualifying ByteDance or TikTok company statement found in any search.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No qualifying statement found from ByteDance, TikTok, or an authorized representative. Per [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/15/trump-tiktok-china.html): 'TikTok has not yet responded to a request for comment.' All public statements about the deal/framework/negotiations came from: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, President Trump, and Chinese negotiator Li Chenggang — none of whom qualify as ByteDance or TikTok representatives under the resolution criteria. Per [Gizmodo](https://gizmodo.com/trump-admin-says-framework-reached-for-u-s-owners-to-take-control-of-tiktok-2000658887): 'Bytedance has repeatedly stated it is not interested in selling TikTok.' This represents ByteDance's pre-window position, not an in-window qualifying statement.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying ByteDance or TikTok statement was found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification: Searched extensively for ByteDance/TikTok official statements. Multiple sources confirm the framework deal was announced by U.S. and Chinese government officials — not by ByteDance or TikTok. CNBC explicitly notes TikTok had 'not yet responded' as of Sept 15. Gizmodo notes ByteDance's standing position of not being interested in selling. No ByteDance newsroom post, TikTok official statement, named TikTok spokesperson quote, or company filing was found acknowledging negotiations. The resolution criteria explicitly exclude statements by the U.S. President, unnamed sources, potential buyers, or media speculation — and all found statements fall into these excluded categories.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Despite extensive news coverage of a U.S.-China framework deal announced Sept 15-16, 2025, all qualifying statements came exclusively from U.S. government officials (Trump, Bessent, Greer) and Chinese government trade negotiators — NOT from ByteDance, TikTok, or authorized company representatives. TikTok explicitly declined to comment on the framework deal (per CNBC). ByteDance's prior stated position was opposition to selling. No press release, newsroom post, official social media statement, named company spokesperson quote, or company filing from ByteDance or TikTok was found within the September 1-17, 2025 window that acknowledges engagement in negotiations or a proposed transaction to divest TikTok's U.S. operations. The window closed on September 17, 2025.

question: Trump meets Xi, Putin, and Kim by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Kim Jong Un all meet with Donald Trump between October 24, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both the listed individual and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will credible reporting by 2025-11-02 state that Donald Trump and Xi Jinping held an in-person bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 2025 APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea?
subquestions.background_information:
A Trump–Xi meeting appears to be the most concrete near-term step toward the ultimate question, because the ultimate question requires Trump to meet all three leaders, and current reporting suggests Xi is the most likely of the three to meet Trump first. Multiple pre-2025-10-25 reports say Trump is traveling to Asia and has a meeting with Xi planned or seriously discussed for late October around the APEC summit in Gyeongju. AFP reported on 2025-10-24 that Trump was beginning an Asia trip and had a "pivotal meeting scheduled on October 30 in Gyeongju, South Korea, with Chinese leader Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit." https://www.barrons.com/news/trump-heads-to-asia-and-high-stakes-meeting-with-xi-5bdac5f2

Earlier reporting also described serious preparations for such a meeting. Reuters reported on 2025-09-06 that Trump and advisers were preparing for a South Korea trip and that there had been serious discussions about a bilateral Xi meeting on the sidelines of APEC, though plans were not yet final. https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-preparing-travel-south-korea-next-month-may-meet-chinas-xi-cnn-reports-2025-09-06/

The relevance is high because a confirmed Trump–Xi in-person meeting would demonstrate that at least one leg of the required trio is completed, and it would also signal that Trump’s Asia trip successfully produced leader-level diplomacy in the region. That in turn may increase the odds of opportunistic side meetings or follow-on diplomacy involving Kim Jong Un before year-end. By contrast, if the much-discussed Xi meeting fails to happen, the path to the ultimate question becomes significantly narrower. APEC itself is a plausible venue for such a meeting; the official APEC 2025 host site identifies the Republic of Korea as host of APEC 2025. https://apec2025.kr/

Sources:
Barron's/AFP, "Trump heads to Asia and high-stakes meeting with Xi" — https://www.barrons.com/news/trump-heads-to-asia-and-high-stakes-meeting-with-xi-5bdac5f2
Reuters, "Trump preparing to travel to South Korea next month, may meet China's Xi, CNN reports" — https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-preparing-travel-south-korea-next-month-may-meet-chinas-xi-cnn-reports-2025-09-06/
APEC 2025 Korea official site — https://apec2025.kr/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-02 (inclusive), there is a consensus of credible reporting that Donald Trump and Xi Jinping held an in-person bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 2025 APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea.

For this question, an "in-person bilateral meeting" means both Trump and Xi were physically present and interacted face-to-face in a meeting described by credible sources as a meeting/talks/sit-down encounter between them. A handshake/photo-line alone does not count unless credible reporting explicitly describes it as a meeting. A phone call or video call does not count.

Primary resolution sources will be reporting from major wire services or official readouts, including Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), AFP coverage as carried by major outlets such as Barron's (https://www.barrons.com/), the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), or China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/). If at least two of these sources clearly report that the meeting occurred within the window, resolve Yes. If by 2025-11-02 no such consensus exists, resolve No.

If reporting only says the meeting was planned, expected, canceled, postponed, or may occur after 2025-11-02, resolve No. If the reporting is irreconcilably contradictory and no consensus of credible reporting emerges, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: This is a strong early indicator because Xi is the leader with the most concretely reported near-term meeting opportunity. If Trump does not complete the Xi leg during the Asia trip, the probability of meeting all three leaders by 2025-12-31 likely falls materially.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Trump and Xi Jinping held an in-person bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 2025 APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-02 (inclusive), confirmed by at least two credible major wire services or official readouts. Must be described as a meeting/talks/sit-down, not merely a handshake.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Trump Xi Jinping bilateral meeting APEC 2025 Gyeongju South Korea' (to find the primary event); 2. 'APEC summit 2025 Gyeongju leaders meeting' (to find context and corroboration); 3. 'Trump Xi Jinping meeting Busan October 30 2025 Reuters AP' (to find wire service confirmation); 4. 'Trump Xi bilateral talks APEC sidelines South Korea White House readout' (to find official readouts); 5. 'Trump Xi Jinping APEC sidelines Busan meeting confirmation Reuters AFP' (to find AFP/Reuters specific confirmation).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Clear candidate event identified: Trump and Xi Jinping held an in-person bilateral meeting on October 30, 2025, in Busan, South Korea (at Gimhae International Airport / military base), on the sidelines of the 2025 APEC summit. The meeting lasted approximately 90-100 minutes and was explicitly described as 'bilateral talks,' a 'meeting,' and a 'sit-down' between the two leaders. No events were rejected as all evidence unanimously confirms the meeting occurred.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The meeting exactly satisfies all resolution criteria: (1) In-person bilateral meeting: confirmed — both leaders were physically present at the same location for ~90-100 minutes of talks [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/82CU8NQ), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/30/trump-and-xi-land-busan-meeting-trade-and-tariffs-.html); (2) Described as a meeting/talks: explicitly called 'bilateral talks,' 'summit,' and 'meeting' by numerous sources [The Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/world/trump-seeks-trade-war-truce-with-chinas-xi-in-south-korea-talks/), [Business Times](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/international/trump-xi-meeting-ends-after-around-90-minutes-trade-talks); (3) On the sidelines of the 2025 APEC summit: multiple sources including AFP explicitly describe the meeting as 'during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit' and 'on the sidelines of the APEC summit' [SBS](https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/trump-and-xi-wrap-meeting-leaving-tight-lipped-after-albanese-calls-for-trade-truce/j4se2un93), [LiveMint](https://www.livemint.com/news/world/fantastic-relationship-tough-negotiator-despite-high-praises-trump-xi-meet-ends-with-no-comment-from-either-11761798073475.html); (4) Timing: October 30, 2025 — clearly within the resolution window of 2025-10-25 to 2025-11-02; (5) Sources: AFP directly confirmed, China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed ('in-depth communication on strategic, long-term issues'), multiple wire services (Yonhap, CNBC, Reuters photo credit) confirmed — well exceeding the two-source threshold.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The meeting took place on October 30, 2025, starting at approximately 11:00 AM Korean Standard Time (KST), which is 02:00 UTC on October 30, 2025. This is within the resolution window. The timestamp is reliably established by multiple consistent sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: This is the first and only in-person bilateral meeting between Trump and Xi during the resolution window (October 25 – November 2, 2025). No earlier qualifying occurrence exists — all sources confirm October 30, 2025 was their first meeting since Trump's return to office in January 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence: none found. All sources — AFP, CNBC, Yonhap, The Tribune, Business Times, South China Morning Post, China's MFA, and many others — unanimously confirm the meeting took place on October 30, 2025 in Busan on the sidelines of the APEC summit. No source disputes the meeting occurred. The only nuance is that the physical location was Busan (Gimhae Airport/military base) rather than Gyeongju itself, but all credible sources explicitly frame it as 'on the sidelines of the APEC summit,' which satisfies the resolution criteria. Trump departed by Air Force One after the meeting while Xi went to Gyeongju to attend the formal APEC leaders' meetings — this further confirms the bilateral meeting was a side event of APEC.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: YES. Trump and Xi Jinping held an in-person bilateral meeting on October 30, 2025, in Busan, South Korea, on the sidelines of the 2025 APEC summit in Gyeongju. The meeting lasted approximately 90-100 minutes, was explicitly described as bilateral talks/a meeting (not merely a handshake), fell within the resolution window, and was confirmed by multiple credible sources including AFP and China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, well exceeding the two-source threshold required for resolution.

question: EU sanctions on Israel by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the European Union officially imposes new sanctions of any form against Israel between September 2 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Sanctions could include measures like tariffs, trade restrictions, financial penalties, diplomatic expulsions, travel bans, restrictions on specific individuals, or any other actions that are commonly recognized as sanctions.

Sanctions against Israeli citizens or entities which do not directly target the Israeli state or members of the Israeli government will not qualify.

The passage of an official act authorizing sanctions on Israel within this market's timeframe will count toward a "Yes" resolution, regardless of if/when the sanctions come into effect.

Only the imposition of sanctions on Israel by the EU as an entity will qualify; if individual member states of the EU apply sanctions against Israel (e.g., France imposes novel trade restrictions on Israel unilaterally), it will not be sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes".

The primary resolution source will be official information from the European Union; however, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the EU Foreign Affairs Council or the High Representative publicly announce, between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03, a formal proposal for new EU restrictive measures specifically targeting members of the Israeli government or the Israeli state?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful early indicator because the ultimate market requires the EU as a bloc to officially impose new sanctions on Israel by the end of 2025. Before that can happen, one important observable step is whether EU institutions move from discussion and options papers to a formal public proposal for restrictive measures aimed at the Israeli government or the Israeli state. Such a proposal would not itself be the same as sanctions being imposed, but it would be a meaningful sign that the process has advanced.

As of summer 2025, reporting indicated that the EU External Action Service had prepared options that included suspension of all or part of the EU-Israel Association Agreement, targeted sanctions on Israeli ministers or military personnel, trade restrictions, an arms embargo, and suspension of scientific cooperation. Anadolu reported on 2025-07-05 that EU officials were preparing punitive options and that targeted sanctions on individuals were viewed as among the most politically feasible measures: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-prepares-sanctions-options-as-pressure-on-israel-grows/3622004

Euractiv similarly reported that an internal options paper existed and that the EU was fragmented on whether to proceed, with selective sanctions seen as more viable than broad trade steps: https://www.euractiv.com/section/global-europe/news/eu-to-examine-possible-measures-against-israel-over-gaza-situation/

At the informal foreign ministers' meeting on 2025-08-30, High Representative Kaja Kallas said the EU remained divided over Gaza but also indicated that concrete measures would be proposed soon. Europa's official readout of her press remarks is a primary source for this political state of play: https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/informal-meeting-foreign-affairs-ministers-press-remarks-high-representative-kaja-kallas-after_en

Euronews reported the same day that Kallas said the options paper had already been presented, that not all member states were on board, and that Denmark and some others were exploring ways to increase pressure, including trade-related ideas concerning occupied territories: https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/08/30/eu-member-states-divided-over-gaza-at-their-copenhagen-meeting

Because the ultimate question turns on actual EU sanctions by 2025-12-31, a formal public proposal for restrictive measures against the Israeli government or state during September 2025 would be a strong near-term crux. If no such proposal materializes even after Kallas' statement that concrete measures were forthcoming, that would be evidence against the ultimate outcome.
