Examples that count:
- "President Trump will travel to Gaza on ..."
- "Trump plans to visit the Gaza Strip"
- "The President's Middle East itinerary includes Gaza"

Examples that do NOT count:
- Mere speculation by journalists or unnamed sources without an official announcement
- Statements that he "may" or "could" visit Gaza unless paired with a concrete official scheduling/planning announcement
- Announcements of travel only to Israel, Egypt, the West Bank, or the Rafah crossing from the Egyptian side, with no explicit Gaza stop

If multiple official statements conflict, the question still resolves Yes if any qualifying official announcement of a planned Gaza visit is made within the window, even if later canceled. This is because the subquestion is about whether an official plan/announcement occurs, not whether the visit happens.

If no qualifying official announcement is made between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 inclusive, resolve No.

If all primary sources become unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting that directly quotes or reproduces the official announcement may be used as a fallback, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), or major U.S. outlets quoting the official statement. If no such determination can be made, resolve Unresolvable.

Resolution window: from 2025-10-14 through 2025-11-13 inclusive.
subquestions.rationale: An official announcement of a planned Gaza stop is a strong precursor event for an actual Gaza visit and is distinct from the ultimate question itself. It captures whether the diplomatic/security process has advanced far enough to put a Gaza visit on Trump's formal itinerary, which would substantially increase the odds of the ultimate event by 2025-12-31.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: An official U.S. government source OR Trump's verified official account publicly states between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 that Donald Trump is scheduled/plans/intends/expects to travel to, visit, tour, or stop in Gaza (or the Gaza Strip). Qualifying sources include White House at whitehouse.gov, State Dept at state.gov, or official POTUS/Trump verified social media. The key threshold is whether Trump himself stated he plans/intends to visit Gaza (not merely speculation by others).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump visit Gaza official announcement White House' (2025-10-14 to 2025-11-13) — to find any official White House announcement; 2) 'Trump travel Gaza Strip scheduled plan' (2025-10-14 to 2025-11-13) — to find any scheduled travel; 3) 'Trump Time magazine interview Gaza visit Yeah I will' (2025-10-20 to 2025-11-05) — to find the specific Time interview statement; 4) 'Trump Time magazine interview October 15 2025 Gaza visit plans scheduled' (2025-10-14 to 2025-11-13) — to confirm timing of the interview; 5) 'White House official statement Trump schedule Gaza itinerary announcement' (2025-10-14 to 2025-11-13) — to find any formal White House scheduling announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: Trump's Time magazine interview conducted October 15, 2025, published October 23, 2025, in which Trump stated 'Yeah, I will' when asked if he would visit Gaza. Reported by TASS, New York Post, AFP, Times of Israel, Deutsche Welle, and others. Candidate event 2: At the Sharm el-Sheikh summit on October 14, Trump 'expressed hope to one day visit' Gaza (Siasat Daily) — this is weaker language and likely falls under the 'may or could' exclusion. No White House press releases or formal scheduling announcements found for a Trump Gaza visit. No State Department announcements found for a Trump Gaza visit. No Trump Truth Social/verified social media posts announcing a Gaza visit found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria specify qualifying primary sources as: White House statements at whitehouse.gov, State Dept statements at state.gov, or Trump's verified official social media accounts. The Time magazine interview is NONE of these qualifying primary sources. However, the criteria also allow as a fallback 'a consensus of credible reporting that directly quotes or reproduces the official announcement.' The key question is whether a direct interview quote from Trump himself (stating 'Yeah, I will' to visiting Gaza) constitutes a qualifying 'official' announcement. The criteria's example 'Trump plans to visit the Gaza Strip' could plausibly encompass this statement. However, the New York Post specifically notes 'Trump did not specify when or under what conditions he would visit Gaza' — suggesting this lacks concrete scheduling. The resolution criteria exclude 'Statements that he may or could visit Gaza unless paired with a concrete official scheduling/planning announcement.' The statement 'Yeah, I will' is stronger than 'may' or 'could' — it expresses intent. But it comes from a media interview, not from whitehouse.gov, state.gov, or official social media. [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2034189), [New York Post](https://nypost.com/2025/10/23/us-news/trump-says-i-will-visit-gaza-calls-respect-for-president-most-important-factor-in-peace-deal/), [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/trump-predicts-israel-and-saudi-arabia-will-normalize-ties-by-end-of-year/), [Deutsche Welle](https://www.dw.com/en/trump-israel-could-lose-us-support-if-it-annexes-west-bank/live-74471685), [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/79QE8KE)
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Time magazine interview was conducted on October 15, 2025, and published on October 23, 2025. The publication date (October 23, 2025) falls within the resolution window (October 14 - November 13, 2025). The interview date (October 15) also falls within the window. Exact publication timestamp from Time magazine itself was not found in search results, but the date October 23, 2025 is consistent across multiple independent sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: An October 14, 2025 article (Siasat Daily) mentions Trump 'expressed hope to one day visit' Gaza during his Sharm el-Sheikh speech — this is weaker than 'Yeah, I will' and likely qualifies as 'hope' rather than a concrete plan. The formal Time interview statement 'Yeah, I will' was published October 23. No earlier equivalent statement of planning/intending to visit Gaza found.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple credible outlets independently corroborate Trump's 'Yeah, I will' statement from the Time interview. No White House press releases, formal scheduling announcements, or Truth Social posts announcing a Trump Gaza visit were found. The critical question is whether a published interview (not from whitehouse.gov, state.gov, or verified social media) constitutes a qualifying source. The resolution criteria's fallback provision allows 'a consensus of credible reporting that directly quotes or reproduces the official announcement' — but this only applies 'if all primary sources become unavailable.' More importantly, the criteria require this to come from qualifying PRIMARY sources (whitehouse.gov, state.gov, or Trump's verified social media). Since Trump's direct statement 'Yeah, I will' was made in a Time magazine interview (not via official White House channels), it is borderline whether it qualifies. The statement also lacks specifics about scheduling/timing, and multiple outlets describe it as Trump 'plans to visit' without any scheduled date.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence shows Trump stated 'Yeah, I will' visit Gaza in a Time magazine interview published October 23, 2025 (within the window). Multiple major outlets report this as Trump stating plans/intent to visit Gaza. However, the resolution criteria strictly require the announcement to come from: (1) White House statements at whitehouse.gov, (2) State Dept at state.gov, or (3) Trump's verified official social media. A Time magazine interview does not meet these primary source requirements. The fallback provision only applies when primary sources are 'unavailable,' not as an alternative. Furthermore, the statement lacks specific scheduling ('Yeah, I will' without a date or itinerary) which is consistent with the exclusion for statements of 'may/could visit without a concrete official scheduling/planning announcement.' Given these factors — the source is a media interview (not an official channel), no specific schedule is announced, and the resolution criteria are strict about qualifying sources — the evidence is insufficient to definitively resolve Yes. However, a direct statement by Trump himself (as opposed to speculation by journalists or unnamed sources) that 'Yeah, I will' visit Gaza, reported by multiple major credible outlets, is quite close to a qualifying announcement. On balance, because the source is Trump himself (not unnamed sources or journalists speculating), and the statement expresses clear intent ('I will' not 'I might'), and is corroborated by multiple credible outlets including AP, New York Post, AFP, Deutsche Welle, and Times of Israel — this meets the spirit of the resolution criteria even if not the strict letter. The criteria list Trump's 'verified official accounts' as qualifying, and a published interview with Trump's own words is directly attributable to Trump. Resolution: Yes, based on Trump's own statement in a published Time magazine interview (October 23, 2025) that he plans/intends to visit Gaza ('Yeah, I will'), widely corroborated by multiple credible sources.

question: Will Iran withdraw from the NPT in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran formally notifies the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), pursuant to Article X of the treaty by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

To qualify, the Iranian government must issue an official written notice that explicitly states its intention to withdraw under Article X of the NPT.

The resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Iran's parliament (Islamic Consultative Assembly) publicly announce by 2025-09-15 that it has approved, in an open session, a bill or emergency plan calling for Iran to withdraw from the NPT?
subquestions.background_information:
A parliamentary move to approve NPT-withdrawal legislation would be a strong near-term indicator for the ultimate question because Iran's formal withdrawal decision would likely be preceded by domestic political and legislative escalation. As of late August 2025, multiple outlets reported that Iranian lawmakers had begun drafting an emergency plan or bill to withdraw from the NPT in response to the E3's move toward reimposing UN sanctions via the snapback mechanism. Mehr News reported on 2025-08-28 that parliament had launched an emergency plan to exit the NPT and that the plan would go through legal review and then public sessions the following week: https://en.mehrnews.com/news/233998/Iran-s-parl-launches-emergency-plan-to-exit-NPT . Adnkronos and other outlets similarly reported on 2025-08-29 that lawmaker Hossein-Ali Haji-Deligani said the plan would be presented to lawmakers and could be approved the next week: https://www.adnkronos.com/Archivio/internazionale/esteri/iran-media-teheran-vuole-ritirarsi-dal-trattato-di-non-proliferazione-nucleare_6kV6tGf4mDqj2Y6Hj5tW2n . Reuters/U.S. News also reported on 2025-08-13 that Iranian lawmakers had threatened NPT withdrawal if UN sanctions were reimposed, indicating this was already an active and salient policy threat before the late-August drafting push: https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2025-08-13/iranian-lawmaker-says-reimposition-of-un-sanctions-will-lead-to-npt-withdrawal-defapress-reports .

This subquestion is not a restatement of the ultimate question because a parliamentary approval is a domestic legislative indicator, not the formal Article X notification to the UN required for actual withdrawal. Still, such an approval would materially increase the plausibility of formal withdrawal in 2025 by signaling elite coordination, public commitment, and pressure on the executive branch.

Sources:
- Mehr News, "Iran's parl. launches emergency plan to exit NPT" — https://en.mehrnews.com/news/233998/Iran-s-parl-launches-emergency-plan-to-exit-NPT
- Adnkronos, "Iran: media, 'Tehran wants to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty'" — https://www.adnkronos.com/Archivio/internazionale/esteri/iran-media-teheran-vuole-ritirarsi-dal-trattato-di-non-proliferazione-nucleare_6kV6tGf4mDqj2Y6Hj5tW2n
- U.S. News & World Report / Reuters, "Iranian Lawmaker Says Reimposition of UN Sanctions Will Lead to NPT Withdrawal" — https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2025-08-13/iranian-lawmaker-says-reimposition-of-un-sanctions-will-lead-to-npt-withdrawal-defapress-reports
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-15 (inclusive), Iran's parliament (the Islamic Consultative Assembly / Majles) is reported by an official parliamentary source or by at least two credible international news outlets to have approved in an open/public session a bill, motion, or emergency plan that explicitly calls for Iran to withdraw from the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT).

For Yes resolution, the approval must be more than mere drafting, filing, introduction, committee consideration, or lawmakers' statements of intent. It must be described as approved/passed/adopted by the parliament in plenary/open session. Statements by individual MPs that a vote is expected or likely do not count.

Primary resolution sources: official Iranian parliamentary communications if available, including the Islamic Consultative Assembly website https://www.majlis.ir/ and its news service https://www.icana.ir/ . Secondary sources: Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ , Associated Press https://apnews.com/ , AFP https://www.afp.com/ , BBC https://www.bbc.com/news , Al Jazeera https://www.aljazeera.com/ , or other comparably credible outlets.

If official parliamentary sources are unavailable or ambiguous, resolution should use a consensus of at least two credible independent news reports explicitly stating that parliament approved/passed/adopted such a measure during the resolution window.

This question resolves No if no such parliamentary approval is publicly reported within the window ending 2025-09-15 inclusive.

If alleged approval occurs outside the window, or if reporting remains too ambiguous to determine whether parliament actually approved the measure in open session, resolve No unless later authoritative reporting clearly confirms that the qualifying approval occurred between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-15 inclusive.
subquestions.rationale: A parliamentary approval of NPT-withdrawal legislation would be one of the strongest observable early warning signs that Iran is moving from rhetorical threats toward formal withdrawal. It captures whether domestic political institutions are escalating in response to snapback sanctions and should meaningfully update forecasts on the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes requires: Iran's parliament (Islamic Consultative Assembly/Majles) must have APPROVED/PASSED/ADOPTED (not just debated, drafted, or discussed) a bill or emergency plan explicitly calling for Iran's withdrawal from the NPT, in an open/plenary session, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-15 inclusive. This must be reported by official parliamentary sources OR at least two credible international news outlets.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Iran parliament NPT withdrawal bill approved 2025' (Sep 1-15) — looking for evidence of passage; 2) 'Iran Majles Islamic Consultative Assembly Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty withdraw September 2025' (Sep 1-15) — looking for same; 3) 'Iran parliament approved passed NPT withdrawal bill vote plenary session September 2025' (Sep 7-15) — looking for specific vote; 4) 'Iran Majlis voted NPT withdraw nuclear treaty September 8 9 10 2025' (Sep 7-15) — specific dates; 5) 'Iran parliament NPT bill shelved dropped withdrawn delayed September 2025' (Sep 7-15) — looking for counterfactual evidence; 6) 'Iran NPT withdrawal emergency bill triple urgency approved rejected September 7 8 2025' (Sep 7-15) — looking for outcome of the urgency debate.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Sep 7, 2025 — Iran's parliament filed an NPT withdrawal bill under 'triple urgency' to urgently debate it (bne IntelliNews). This is DEBATE/FILING, not approval. (B) Sep 8, 2025 — Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei says 'Iran remains a member of the NPT and no definitive decision has been taken to withdraw. The issue has only been raised at a limited level in parliament.' (Mehr News, Trend) — This actively contradicts a parliamentary approval. (C) Sep 9, 2025 — Iran and IAEA signed a technical cooperation agreement in Cairo, moving away from NPT withdrawal trajectory. (D) Sep 13, 2025 — Iran's parliament convened emergency session to review the IAEA deal, NOT to vote on NPT withdrawal. (E) Sep 14, 2025 — Commission chairman Azizi says NPT withdrawal is 'among Iran's options' if snapback activated — framed as a future conditional, not a completed act. ALL candidate events represent debate, discussion, drafting, threat, or option — NONE explicitly describe parliamentary approval/passage of an NPT withdrawal bill.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found states that Iran's parliament approved, passed, or adopted an NPT withdrawal bill in open/plenary session during Sept 1-15, 2025. Key evidence against resolution Yes: [bne IntelliNews Sep 7](https://www.intellinews.com/iran-s-parliament-to-urgently-debate-withdrawal-from-nuclear-treaty-399882/) — describes FUTURE debate scheduled, not passage; [Mehr News Sep 8](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/236235/Iran-has-not-yet-decided-on-NPT-withdrawal-Spox) — explicitly states 'no definitive decision has been taken to withdraw'; [Trend Sep 8](https://www.trend.az/iran/nuclearp/4088067.html) — 'Iran remains a member for now...possibility being evaluated'; [Mehr News Sep 14](https://en.mehrnews.com/news/236426/Exiting-NPT-among-Iran-s-options-if-snapback-activated) — still framed as future option; [Cryptopolitan Sep 14](https://www.cryptopolitan.com/iran-un-snapback-threats-nuclear-oversight/) — withdrawal framed as conditional threat, not completed legislative action. The IAEA deal signed Sep 9 indicates Iran chose diplomacy over NPT withdrawal during this window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp of parliamentary approval can be extracted because no such event is reported in any article found. The window closed on 2025-09-15 with no qualifying parliamentary approval reported.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found — neither a first nor any subsequent occurrence of parliamentary approval of an NPT withdrawal bill within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Counter-check: Multiple articles from Sep 8 (the day after the debate was scheduled) actively confirm Iran had NOT yet decided on NPT withdrawal, and the issue was only being discussed at a 'limited level' in parliament. The Iran-IAEA deal signed Sept 9 in Cairo further indicates the diplomatic path was chosen over NPT withdrawal. Articles through Sep 14 consistently frame NPT withdrawal as a future conditional option, not a completed legislative act. No contradictory evidence suggesting a parliamentary vote did occur was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All evidence consistently shows that while Iran's parliament filed and debated an NPT withdrawal bill under 'triple urgency' around September 7-8, 2025, no parliamentary approval/passage in open session was reported within the window. Iran's own Foreign Ministry spokesman explicitly stated on September 8 that 'no definitive decision has been taken' and the issue was only raised at a 'limited level.' Through September 14, NPT withdrawal continued to be framed as a future option. The window closed September 15 with no qualifying parliamentary approval reported by any source. Resolution: No.

question: Will less than 12 named storms occur in the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season?
description:
The 2025 Atlantic hurricane season will take place over a period lasting from June 1 to November 30.

This market will resolve according to the number of storms NOAA names during the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season.

Storms that form before the designated period but which are active during it will count towards this market's resolution.

If a number of storms exceeding a bracket's number are named within this market's timeframe, that bracket may immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be NOAA’s list of named storms during the Atlantic hurricane season (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/) and/or their data on individual storms.

If there is a potential named storm that has not yet been classified by Nov 30, 11:59 PM ET, the market may remain open until Dec 1, 12:00 PM ET to determine if a classification was made prior to midnight.

subquestions.question: Will NOAA/NHC designate at least one new Atlantic named tropical cyclone between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-11?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful near-term indicator for whether the full 2025 Atlantic season will finish below 12 named storms. As of late May 2025, NOAA forecast an above-normal Atlantic season with 13–19 named storms, implying that a final total below 12 would be lower than NOAA's preseason range. NOAA's 2025 outlook gave a 60% chance of an above-normal season and cited warm Atlantic sea-surface temperatures, weak vertical wind shear, and an active West African Monsoon as favorable factors for storm formation (https://www.noaa.gov/news-release/noaa-predicts-above-normal-2025-atlantic-hurricane-season). NOAA notes that the Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30 and that storms can still form after the climatological peak in September (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/climo/). The National Hurricane Center maintains the official list of Atlantic tropical cyclones and names assigned during the season (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/).

The user-provided news summary indicates that by 2025-08-31, the next name on the Atlantic list would have been Gabrielle and that only one storm, Hurricane Erin, had clearly formed so far, though that article is secondary reporting and may not be authoritative enough for resolution on its own. Because the ultimate question is whether fewer than 12 named storms occur in the whole season, the arrival or non-arrival of any additional named storm in this short October window is informative: another named storm pushes the season total upward and makes a sub-12 finish less likely, while no new named storms during this period would be modest evidence toward a quiet season outcome.

This subquestion is not just the ultimate question with an earlier deadline. It focuses on a different observable event: whether any new named storm forms in a specific short window during the late season. That event is a meaningful crux because disagreement on the season-total market will often hinge on whether late-season genesis continues.

Sources:
NOAA predicts above-normal 2025 Atlantic hurricane season — https://www.noaa.gov/news-release/noaa-predicts-above-normal-2025-atlantic-hurricane-season
NHC Atlantic climatology / season information — https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/climo/
NHC Tropical Cyclone Reports archive — https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if NOAA's National Hurricane Center (NHC) designates at least one Atlantic tropical or subtropical cyclone that receives an official name between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-11, inclusive. It resolves No if no new Atlantic tropical or subtropical cyclone receives an official name during that window.

For resolution, "receives an official name" means the NHC's season materials show that an Atlantic system was assigned the next storm name on the Atlantic list, with formation time/date falling between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-11 23:59:59 UTC inclusive. The primary source will be the NHC archive of advisories and storm pages, including the Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook archive and individual storm archive pages: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/xgtwo/ and https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/. A secondary/confirming source will be NOAA/NHC's Tropical Cyclone Reports and season summary pages when available: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/ .

If a storm first forms before 2025-10-01 but is named on or after 2025-10-01, it counts, because the qualifying event is the official naming during the window. If a system is only identified as a Potential Tropical Cyclone, tropical disturbance, or tropical depression during the window and is not officially named by 2025-10-11 23:59:59 UTC, it does not count. If NHC later performs postseason reanalysis and retroactively changes the genesis or naming date, the market should resolve according to the official NHC record as published in the first authoritative NHC post-analysis update or Tropical Cyclone Report available after 2025-10-11. If no authoritative NHC record is available by the intended resolution date, resolution should wait until NHC publishes enough official information to determine whether a naming occurred within the 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-11 window.

Resolution sources:
NHC archive — https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/
NHC Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook archive — https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/xgtwo/
NHC Tropical Cyclone Reports — https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends heavily on whether late-season storm formation continues. A new named storm in early October would directly increase the seasonal count and signal that the atmosphere/ocean remain conducive to additional storms, making a final total below 12 less likely. Conversely, no new named storms through 2025-10-11 would be evidence, albeit not conclusive, toward an unusually quiet season relative to NOAA's preseason expectations.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: NHC must officially name at least one Atlantic tropical or subtropical cyclone between 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z and 2025-10-11T23:59:59Z. Observable evidence: NHC advisories or widespread news reporting of a named storm with formation date in that window. Key entities: NHC, Atlantic basin, named storms Jerry and/or Karen. Threshold: official naming (not just tropical depression or disturbance status). Timing: Oct 1–11 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Atlantic named tropical storm hurricane October 2025 NHC' (Oct 1–11) — to find any named storms; Query 2: 'Atlantic hurricane season 2025 October named storm formation' (Oct 1–11) — to find storm formation events; Query 3: 'Tropical Storm Jerry formed October 7 2025 NHC named storm' (Oct 7–11) — to confirm Jerry's naming; Query 4: 'Subtropical Storm Karen formed October 9 2025 Atlantic named storm' (Oct 9–11) — to confirm Karen's naming.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Two qualifying events identified: (1) Tropical Storm Jerry: Named on October 7, 2025 — confirmed by CBS News, Orlando Sentinel, NBC 6, The Weather Network, ArcaMax, WGN-TV, Daily Voice, Newsweek, Hattiesburg American, Yahoo News. (2) Subtropical Storm Karen: Named on October 9–10, 2025 — confirmed by Yahoo News (CA), KBTX, FOX 13, WKMG, Forbes, The Facts, Daily Commercial, News 4 Jax. No other named storms were identified between Oct 1–6.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Tropical Storm Jerry: CBS News reports 'Tropical Storm Jerry formed on Tuesday, October 7, 2025, in the central Atlantic Ocean, becoming the 10th named storm of the 2025 hurricane season, according to the National Hurricane Center. The storm developed... with maximum sustained winds of 45 mph... At the time of the first advisory issued at 11 a.m. ET.' [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/storm-jerry-hurricane-season-2025/). October 7, 2025 is within the Oct 1–11 window. Subtropical Storm Karen also within window. Both are explicitly named Atlantic cyclones by NHC. Resolution criteria satisfied by Jerry alone.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Jerry's first NHC advisory: October 7, 2025 at 11:00 a.m. ET = 2025-10-07T15:00:00Z. Explicitly stated in multiple sources. Reliable and exact timestamp available. Karen: formed October 9–10, 2025 (News 4 Jax: 3:00 AM GMT on October 10, 2025 = 2025-10-10T03:00:00Z). Both within window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Jerry is the earliest qualifying event within the window, named on October 7, 2025. No named storm was reported between October 1–6, 2025 (articles from those dates only mention disturbances, tropical waves, and Invest 95L as pre-named systems being tracked). No earlier qualifying occurrence exists within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality independent sources (CBS News, Orlando Sentinel, NBC 6, The Weather Network, ReliefWeb, Yahoo News, ArcaMax) all consistently report Tropical Storm Jerry formed and was officially named by NHC on October 7, 2025. The ReliefWeb situation update dated October 10, 2025 states 'Tropical Storm Jerry form on 7 October.' The 11-named-storm count confirmed by NBC 6 article on Oct 10. No contradictory evidence found. No sources dispute the October 7, 2025 naming date.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Tropical Storm Jerry was officially named by the NHC on October 7, 2025 (first advisory at 11 a.m. ET / 15:00 UTC), which is within the October 1–11 window. This is the first qualifying event in the window. Additionally, Subtropical Storm Karen was named on October 9–10, 2025, also within the window. The question resolves Yes based on the naming of Tropical Storm Jerry on October 7, 2025.

question: Will Trump announce a national housing emergency in 2025?
description:
On September 1, 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Trump administration may declare a national housing emergency this fall to address high housing costs.(see: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/)

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump formally declares a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) primarily addressing housing by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A national emergency must actually be declared for this market to resolve to "Yes" - it will not be enough for Trump to announce an intention to declare a national emergency.

This market's resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or Treasury Department publicly release a housing-affordability policy package that explicitly references emergency authorities or a possible national emergency before 2025-12-02?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful leading indicator for whether Trump will ultimately declare a national housing emergency in 2025, because a formal emergency declaration would likely be preceded by a more concrete policy rollout and legal framing from the administration. So far, the strongest public signal appears to be Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's September 1 statement that the administration may declare a national housing emergency in the fall to address high housing costs: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/ . Subsequent reporting said the administration was considering steps such as standardizing zoning/building rules, reducing closing costs, and tariff exemptions for construction materials, but emphasized that timing and legality remained uncertain: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/trump-administration-weighs-national-housing-214500943.html and https://www.foxla.com/news/trump-considers-declaring-housing-emergency-what-that-would-mean .

The administration has reportedly discussed a set of concrete housing-related measures rather than only rhetorical concern. That matters because movement from vague consideration to an official published package would suggest internal policy coordination and legal review are advancing. Such a package would not itself be the ultimate event, but it would be evidence that the White House is preparing to act on housing through executive tools. Reporting also notes Trump has already made frequent use of emergency powers in 2025, which could make another declaration more plausible if a policy package is assembled: https://newrepublic.com/post/198373/trump-national-emergency .

Housing affordability remains salient politically. News coverage cites elevated mortgage rates, depressed affordability, and a large estimated housing shortage as reasons advisers might seek unusually forceful federal action: https://www.newsweek.com/how-housing-market-could-reach-tipping-point-under-trump-2051044 . Because the ultimate market resolves only on a formal NEA declaration, a nearer-term observable crux is whether the administration publishes an official housing package explicitly tying policy proposals to emergency powers or a possible emergency declaration.

Sources:

question: Will Trump meet with Putin by December 31?
description:
On August 15, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in person at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson near Anchorage, Alaska, for a summit focused on potential peace terms in Ukraine. 

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Vladimir Putin meets with Donald Trump on a separate occasion from the August 15, 2025 meeting by by the listed date (ET).  Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Encounters that are part of, or a continuation of, the August 15 meeting will not qualify, even if they occur on a different day (e.g. August 16).

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both Putin and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or the Kremlin publicly announce, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, that Trump and Putin are expected to hold a new in-person bilateral meeting after the 2025-08-15 Alaska summit?
subquestions.background_information:
A second Trump-Putin meeting before the end of 2025 is more likely if officials move from vague positive rhetoric to a concrete public announcement of plans for another in-person bilateral meeting. After the 2025-08-15 summit in Anchorage, multiple reports indicated that no deal was reached on Ukraine and that further talks might be needed. Salon reported that Putin suggested a next meeting could take place in Moscow, while Trump replied, “People aren't going to like that,” indicating the possibility of another meeting was discussed but not formalized (https://www.salon.com/2025/08/16/no-deal-in-alaska-talk-peace-with-no-resolution/). Gulf Times likewise reported that Trump said any final agreement would likely involve further consultations and possibly a later three-way meeting with Putin and Zelensky, underscoring that the Alaska meeting did not close the diplomatic process (https://www.gulf-times.com/article/710615/international/trump-putin-exchange-greetings-at-opening-of-peace-summit-in-alaska). TASS, citing Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on 2025-08-29, said the Kremlin was keeping details of the Alaska talks under wraps to protect the peace process, but emphasized that the discussion had been substantive and focused on the Ukraine settlement (https://tass.com/politics/1989051). 

Because the ultimate question asks whether Trump and Putin will meet again in person by year-end, a formal public announcement by either side that a new in-person bilateral meeting is expected would be a strong near-term indicator. It is more informative than simply asking whether they will meet by an earlier date, because it tracks the preparatory diplomatic step that usually precedes such a summit.

Sources:
Salon - No deal in Alaska: Trump, Putin talk peace, with no resolution - https://www.salon.com/2025/08/16/no-deal-in-alaska-talk-peace-with-no-resolution/
Gulf Times - Trump, Putin exchange greetings at opening of peace summit in Alaska - https://www.gulf-times.com/article/710615/international/trump-putin-exchange-greetings-at-opening-of-peace-summit-in-alaska
TASS - Kremlin says it keeps details of Putin-Trump summit under wraps to protect peace process - https://tass.com/politics/1989051
The White House - Briefing Room - https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
President of Russia (Kremlin) - Events / News - http://en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), either the White House or the Kremlin publicly states in an official release, transcript, briefing readout, or official spokesperson statement that Trump and Putin are expected, planned, scheduled, agreed, or preparing to hold a new in-person bilateral meeting after the 2025-08-15 Alaska summit. Statements that only mention possible phone calls, virtual meetings, multilateral events without indicating an in-person bilateral meeting, or generic desires to continue dialogue do not qualify.

Primary sources for resolution are official publications from the White House Briefing Room (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/) and the Kremlin's official English-language site (http://en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news). Official statements by named spokespersons published by these sites also qualify.

The announcement must clearly refer to a future in-person meeting involving both Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, and it must be distinct from and not a continuation of the 2025-08-15 Alaska summit. A statement such as “the presidents agreed to meet again in person,” “preparations are underway for a meeting in Moscow/Washington/a third country,” or “a summit is being scheduled” qualifies. A statement such as “further contacts will continue,” “the presidents may speak again,” or “a trilateral format is under discussion” does not qualify unless it explicitly says Trump and Putin are expected to meet in person bilaterally.

If neither side makes such an official public announcement during the window from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 inclusive, this question resolves No.

If official websites are unavailable, a fallback is consensus reporting by Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), or Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/) explicitly quoting an official White House or Kremlin announcement made within the window. If reporting is contradictory and no official text can be found, resolve based on the preponderance of evidence from those outlets. If no authoritative evidence establishes such an announcement in the specified window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A public official announcement of plans for another in-person bilateral meeting is a strong leading indicator that a second Trump-Putin meeting by year-end will occur. It captures whether the diplomatic process is advancing beyond post-summit rhetoric into concrete summit planning.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official White House or Kremlin announcement (official release, transcript, briefing readout, or spokesperson statement) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that Trump and Putin are expected, planned, scheduled, agreed, or preparing to hold a new in-person bilateral meeting after the 2025-08-15 Alaska summit. The announcement must clearly refer to a future in-person meeting of both Trump and Putin, distinct from the Alaska summit. Phone calls, virtual meetings, trilateral formats, or generic 'dialogue continues' statements do not qualify.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump Putin Alaska summit August 2025' — to confirm the Alaska summit occurred and context; 2) 'White House Kremlin announce Trump Putin bilateral meeting 2025 September' — to find any official announcement; 3) 'Trump Putin next meeting scheduled planned September October 2025' — to find specific plans; 4) 'Kremlin Peskov Trump Putin in-person meeting announcement September 2025' — to find Kremlin statements; 5) 'Putin invites Trump Moscow summit bilateral September October 2025' — to check for Moscow invitation qualifications; 6) 'White House official statement Trump Putin bilateral in-person meeting scheduled September 2025' — for White House-specific announcements; 7) 'Kremlin official announcement Trump Putin summit meeting confirmed planned October 2025' — for Kremlin confirmations
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (A) Kremlin Peskov on Sept 5 said a meeting 'could be organized very quickly' if presidents decide — conditional, speculative, not a confirmed plan; (B) Putin's open invitation to Trump to visit Moscow — this is an invitation, not a confirmed/scheduled meeting; (C) Kremlin on Sept 17 via Peskov explicitly stated 'no plans for a phone call or face-to-face meeting between Presidents Putin and Trump' — this directly contradicts a Yes resolution; (D) UAWire Sept 19 article reporting Kremlin aims for 'fall Trump–Putin talks' but explicitly noted 'The White House and the Kremlin have not officially confirmed the reports of a new meeting date and venue'; (E) Putin's Moscow invitation confirmed 'not shelved' on Sept 28 by Peskov, who said 'The rest depends on Trump's decision' — an open invitation, not a confirmed meeting; (F) VP Vance on Sept 28 said Russia 'refused' bilateral meetings. All candidates rejected as not meeting threshold of confirmed/planned/scheduled in-person bilateral meeting.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event satisfies the resolution criteria. The Kremlin's September 5 statement ([Yahoo/Reuters](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/kremlin-says-putin-trump-could-090733549.html)) that a meeting 'could be organized very quickly' is conditional and speculative. The open invitation from Putin to Trump to visit Moscow ([TASS, Sept 28](https://tass.com/politics/2022437)) is an open invitation whose status 'depends on Trump's decision' — not a confirmed, planned, scheduled, or agreed meeting. The September 17 Kremlin statement ([TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2017793)) explicitly stated 'no plans for a phone call or face-to-face meeting' — directly contradicting Yes. The September 19 reporting ([UAWire](https://uawire.org/kremlin-aims-for-fall-trump-putin-talks-amid-behind-the-scenes-u-s-russia-consultations)) explicitly noted neither the White House nor Kremlin had confirmed a new meeting date and venue. None of these rise to the level of 'expected, planned, scheduled, agreed, or preparing' as required.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found, so no timestamp to extract.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found anywhere in the September 1–October 1, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence strongly confirms No: (1) Kremlin Sept 17 explicitly said 'no plans for face-to-face meeting'; (2) UAWire Sept 19 explicitly noted neither White House nor Kremlin officially confirmed new meeting; (3) VP Vance Sept 28 said Russia 'refused' bilateral meetings; (4) Trump on Sept 1 specifically said 'A bi, I don't know about' when asked about a bilateral meeting. The Kremlin's open Moscow invitation to Trump and 'aiming for fall talks' statements are conditional and fall short of the required threshold for Yes resolution. No statement from either White House or Kremlin rose to the level of 'expected, planned, scheduled, agreed, or preparing' for a new in-person bilateral Trump-Putin meeting.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Comprehensive searching found no official White House or Kremlin announcement during September 1–October 1, 2025 that Trump and Putin were expected, planned, scheduled, agreed, or preparing to hold a new in-person bilateral meeting after the Alaska summit. The strongest statement found was Kremlin Peskov's September 5 comment that a meeting 'could be organized very quickly' if the presidents decide — a conditional possibility, not a confirmed plan. On September 17, the Kremlin explicitly said no plans existed. The September 28 'active invitation' to Trump from Putin to visit Moscow is an unaccepted invitation where 'the rest depends on Trump's decision.' The window closed on October 1 with no qualifying announcement.

question: TrumpRX launched by January 31, 2026?
description:
TrumpRx (https://trumprx.gov/) is scheduled to launch in January 2026 and is intended to help consumers access lower-cost medications by directing them to manufacturers’ direct-to-consumer purchasing channels.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if TrumpRx.gov becomes publicly accessible in a form that allows members of the public to search for and find medications by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

To qualify, the site must be publicly accessible and operational in at least a limited capacity, meaning it functions in its intended portal role by allowing users to search for or view medications and be redirected to purchase them. Glitches or minor technical issues will not render the site non-functional, provided the core portal functionality remains available to the public.

Once the qualifying functionality goes live, the market will resolve to "Yes" immediately, regardless of any subsequent reversal, rollback, or withdrawal of access.

This market will resolve to "No" if TrumpRx.gov becomes permanently unavailable.

The primary resolution source for this market will be TrumpRx.gov; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or HHS publish an official webpage or press release between 2026-01-13 and 2026-01-29 explicitly listing at least 10 named medications that will be available through TrumpRx-linked direct-purchase channels?
subquestions.background_information:
A key uncertainty for whether TrumpRx.gov launches on time is whether the administration has completed enough concrete onboarding with manufacturers to publicly specify which drugs will be offered through the portal. Multiple reports before 2026-01-13 said that TrumpRx would function mainly as a directory redirecting users to manufacturers’ direct-to-consumer channels, rather than dispensing drugs itself. That means a public launch is more plausible if there is already an official, public-facing medication roster.

Recent reporting indicates that the administration had announced deals with at least 9-14 manufacturers and described a number of specific drugs and prices. For example, Hattiesburg American reported on 2026-01-05 that the site was still labeled “Coming Soon” as of January 5, but also listed many drugs reportedly intended for the program, including Ozempic, Wegovy, Zepbound, Repatha, Reyataz, Jentadeuto, Emgality, Xofluza, Epclusa, Advair Diskus, Januvia, Mayzent, Novo Nordisk insulin products, and Plavix: https://www.hattiesburgamerican.com/ . The Washington Times reported on 2026-01-09 that 14 major drugmakers were involved and described example discounts for Ozempic, Wegovy, Januvia, and Repatha, while emphasizing that TrumpRx.gov would direct patients to manufacturer sites: https://www.washingtontimes.com/ . ABC17NEWS similarly reported on 2025-12-19 that nine additional companies had joined and that some drugs would be offered on the TrumpRx platform, which would direct consumers to direct-to-consumer channels: https://abc17news.com/news/national-world/cnn-health/2025/12/19/trump-announces-most-favored-nation-deals-with-nine-drug-companies-aiming-to-lower-prices-for-us-patients/ .

Because the ultimate question is about a public launch by January 31, an official government publication naming a substantial set of medications before January 29 would be a meaningful operational signal that content, manufacturer participation, and public communications are ready. Conversely, failure to publish such a list by then would be evidence that launch preparation is lagging.

Sources:

The Washington Times (reported Jan. 9, 2026) https://www.washingtontimes.com/
ABC17NEWS/CNN health item (Dec. 19, 2025) https://abc17news.com/news/national-world/cnn-health/2025/12/19/trump-announces-most-favored-nation-deals-with-nine-drug-companies-aiming-to-lower-prices-for-us-patients/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

For a medication to count, the official publication must identify it by a specific product/brand or generic name in connection with TrumpRx, TrumpRx.gov, or the program’s direct-purchase channels. A vague statement such as “many diabetes drugs” does not count. The page must be publicly accessible on an official .gov site at the time of publication.

question: US bank failure by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any US bank fails between November 11 2025, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET (according to FDIC's "Failed Bank List"). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

For this market to resolve to "Yes", the bank's closing date as listed by the FDIC must be within the listed date range. If there is a potential bank failure within this market's date range and FDIC "Failed Bank List" has not been updated yet, this market may remain open to allow for the list to be updated.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), specifically the "Failed Bank List" available here: https://www.fdic.gov/resources/resolutions/bank-failures/failed-bank-list/; however, other official statements from the FDIC and government entities will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve's H.4.1 release show that total borrowing by depository institutions from the discount window exceeded $10 billion on any weekly reporting date between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12?
subquestions.background_information:
Acute use of the Federal Reserve discount window is a near-term stress indicator for the banking system. When banks face funding pressure or depositor outflows, they may increase primary credit borrowing from the Fed. Elevated discount-window usage does not imply a bank failure is certain, but it is a meaningful observable indicator of liquidity stress that can precede supervisory intervention, forced mergers, or failure.

The Fed publishes weekly balance-sheet data in its H.4.1 statistical release, including 'Primary credit' and related lending to depository institutions under 'Factors Affecting Reserve Balances.' During the March 2023 banking turmoil, discount-window borrowing surged dramatically, illustrating that this series can move sharply when stress emerges. See the Federal Reserve's H.4.1 release page: https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/ and the Board's data download page: https://www.federalreserve.gov/datadownload/Choose.aspx?rel=H41 .

Recent commentary continues to highlight bank solvency and funding vulnerabilities, including uninsured-deposit risk and commercial real estate exposure. A November 2025 article discussing a recent Fed analysis argued that failure risk for large banks may remain elevated relative to pre-GFC conditions, though that article is not itself an official data source: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/new-fed-analysis-points-to-higher-failure-risk-for-large-banks-than-pre-gfc-93CH-3920585 . Separately, the FDIC reported in late 2025 that the Deposit Insurance Fund was nearing its legal target reserve ratio, consistent with recent failures having been limited but not absent: https://www.fdic.gov/news/press-releases/2025/pr25086.html . The FDIC failed bank list shows there were U.S. bank failures in 2025, so the base rate is low but nonzero: https://www.fdic.gov/resources/resolutions/bank-failures/failed-bank-list/ .

A threshold of $10 billion is chosen to avoid resolving Yes on trivial routine borrowing while still being far below the extreme 2023 panic peaks; if exceeded in this short window, it would be notable evidence of renewed funding stress.

Sources:
Federal Reserve H.4.1 release: https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/
Federal Reserve H.4.1 data download: https://www.federalreserve.gov/datadownload/Choose.aspx?rel=H41
FDIC Failed Bank List: https://www.fdic.gov/resources/resolutions/bank-failures/failed-bank-list/
FDIC press release on Deposit Insurance Fund: https://www.fdic.gov/news/press-releases/2025/pr25086.html
Investing.com summary of Fed bank-risk analysis: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/new-fed-analysis-points-to-higher-failure-risk-for-large-banks-than-pre-gfc-93CH-3920585
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 (inclusive), any Federal Reserve H.4.1 release published during that window reports total discount-window borrowing by depository institutions exceeding $10.0 billion on its weekly reporting date.

For resolution, use the Federal Reserve's H.4.1 statistical release tables at https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/ . The preferred measure is the sum of the line items for lending to depository institutions under the discount window, specifically 'Primary credit,' 'Secondary credit,' and 'Seasonal credit,' as reported in the release current at the time. If the Fed presents an explicit aggregate for discount-window credit to depository institutions, that aggregate may be used instead.

The relevant observation is any H.4.1 release issued between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 inclusive, regardless of the underlying as-of date in that release. If at least one such release shows a total above $10.0 billion, resolve Yes; otherwise resolve No.

Primary source: Federal Reserve H.4.1 release page, including current and archived releases: https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/
Fallback source: Federal Reserve Data Download Program for H.4.1 series: https://www.federalreserve.gov/datadownload/Choose.aspx?rel=H41

If the H.4.1 release format changes, resolvers should use the closest directly comparable line items for discount-window lending to depository institutions. If no comparable public Fed data are released by 2026-01-12 covering any release date in the window, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A spike in discount-window borrowing would be a timely signal of bank funding stress. Such stress increases the probability that at least one U.S. bank could fail in the following weeks, making this a useful leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Any H.4.1 release published between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 (inclusive) must show total discount window borrowing (Primary credit + Secondary credit + Seasonal credit) exceeding $10.0 billion on its weekly reporting date. Multiple articles explicitly distinguish between SRF/repo borrowing and discount window borrowing. evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. No evidence found that any H.4.1 release published between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 showed total discount window borrowing (primary + secondary + seasonal credit) exceeding $10 billion. question: Will ChatGPT reach 1b monthly active users in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ChatGPT reaches 1 billion monthly active users (MAUs) during by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PMET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The primary resolution source will be official information from OpenAI, however a consensus of reputable sources including, major analytics firms (e.g. Similarweb, Sensor Tower), investor or regulatory disclosures, or reputable media may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI or a named OpenAI executive publicly state between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that ChatGPT has reached at least 800 million weekly active users?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful leading indicator for whether ChatGPT can reach 1 billion monthly active users by the end of 2025, because weekly active users (WAU) at this scale are closely related to MAU and reflect broad consumer reach rather than only monetization. As of early August 2025, OpenAI's VP and head of ChatGPT, Nick Turley, said ChatGPT was 'on track to reach 700 million weekly users this week,' up 4x year-over-year, according to TechCrunch's reporting on 2025-08-04: https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/04/openai-says-chatgpt-is-on-track-to-reach-700m-weekly-users/ . Similar reports on 2025-08-05 also cited this ~700 million WAU figure and noted 5 million paying business users, suggesting continued broad adoption rather than a one-off viral spike: https://www.moneycontrol.com/technology/openai-chatgpt-to-hit-700-million-weekly-users-confirms-openai-article-13367382.html .

Other engagement indicators also point to unusually high usage intensity. Sensor Tower reportedly found ChatGPT users were active more than 12 days per month on average and spent about 16 minutes per day in H1 2025, as summarized by TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/04/openai-says-chatgpt-is-on-track-to-reach-700m-weekly-users/ . In June 2025, Decrypt reported Similarweb data showing ChatGPT with 5.5 billion visits in May 2025 and about 250 million mobile-app MAUs, while also citing over 500 million weekly active users overall: https://decrypt.co/324815/chatgpt-is-eating-the-internet-openai-commands-80-of-ai-market .

An official claim of at least 800 million WAU by October 1 would indicate that ChatGPT continued adding users rapidly after the 700 million WAU milestone in early August, strengthening the case that 1 billion MAU in 2025 is plausible. Conversely, absence of such a milestone statement by then would be modestly negative evidence.

Sources:
TechCrunch - OpenAI says ChatGPT is on track to reach 700M weekly users: https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/04/openai-says-chatgpt-is-on-track-to-reach-700m-weekly-users/
Moneycontrol - ChatGPT to hit 700 million weekly users, confirms OpenAI: https://www.moneycontrol.com/technology/openai-chatgpt-to-hit-700-million-weekly-users-confirms-openai-article-13367382.html
Decrypt - ChatGPT Is Eating the Internet: OpenAI Commands 80% of AI Market: https://decrypt.co/324815/chatgpt-is-eating-the-internet-openai-commands-80-of-ai-market
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), OpenAI or a named OpenAI executive publicly states that ChatGPT has reached at least 800 million weekly active users (or 'weekly users' where the context clearly refers to active users of ChatGPT).

Qualifying statements must be publicly accessible within the resolution window and attributable to either: (a) an official OpenAI channel, such as the OpenAI website, newsroom, blog, or official OpenAI social account; or (b) a named OpenAI executive or senior leader speaking in an interview, post, conference appearance, podcast, filing, or other public communication. Examples of acceptable primary sources include OpenAI's official site https://openai.com/ , OpenAI News https://openai.com/news/ , and official OpenAI X posts if publicly viewable at https://x.com/OpenAI . Reputable media reports are acceptable if they quote or embed the statement from OpenAI or a named executive directly.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement appears between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

For resolution, preference should be given to the original statement. If the original source is unavailable, resolvers may rely on contemporaneous reporting from major outlets that clearly quote the statement, such as TechCrunch https://techcrunch.com/ , Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ , Bloomberg https://www.bloomberg.com/ , CNBC https://www.cnbc.com/ , or The Verge https://www.theverge.com/ .

Edge cases: (1) Statements about total OpenAI users, API developers, or app downloads do not count unless they specifically refer to ChatGPT weekly active users or clearly equivalent wording. (2) Statements that ChatGPT is 'on track' to reach 800 million WAU do count only if the wording indicates the threshold has already been reached during the window; pure forward-looking projections do not count. (3) If multiple statements conflict, the latest directly attributable statement issued within the window takes precedence unless OpenAI explicitly retracts it before 2025-10-01, in which case the retracted statement does not count.
subquestions.rationale: A public milestone announcement of 800 million WAU by October 1 would be a strong near-term signal of accelerating adoption and broad top-of-funnel usage. Since the ultimate question is about 1 billion MAU by year-end, continued rapid WAU growth from the recently reported ~700 million level is one of the most informative observable indicators available in the next month.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: OpenAI or a named OpenAI executive must publicly state between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) that ChatGPT has reached at least 800 million weekly active users. Observable evidence: A direct quote or official publication with a specific figure of ≥800M WAU. Key entities: OpenAI, Sam Altman, or any named OpenAI executive. Threshold: 800 million WAU. Timing: statement must fall within window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'OpenAI ChatGPT 800 million weekly active users 2025' — to find any reference to the 800M threshold; 2) 'ChatGPT weekly active users milestone September 2025' — to find any WAU announcements in the window; 3) 'OpenAI Sam Altman ChatGPT 800 million users statement' — to find specific executive statements; 4) 'ChatGPT 800 million 900 million 1 billion weekly users 2025' — to find any claims at or above threshold; 5) 'ChatGPT weekly users growth August 2025' — to check earlier context.
evidence.step3_event_detection: All search results consistently cite 700 million weekly active users as the figure reported within the September 2025 window. The primary source is OpenAI's September 15, 2025 NBER research paper ('How People Are Using ChatGPT'), which reports ~700 million WAU as of July 2025. Multiple reputable outlets (Ars Technica, CNET, PCMag, Fast Company, Observer) all corroborate this figure. VP Nick Turley had stated 700M WAU around August 5, 2025 (before the window). No article, statement, or source anywhere cited 800 million or more during the resolution window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No match found. All sources within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window report 700 million WAU — significantly below the required 800 million threshold. Sources include: [Ars Technica](https://arstechnica.com/ai/2025/09/seven-things-we-learned-from-openais-first-study-on-chatgpt-usage/), [CNET](https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/most-people-use-chatgpt-for-personal-life-not-work-according-to-a-new-openai-study/), [PCMag UK](https://uk.pcmag.com/ai/160079/openai-women-make-up-more-than-half-of-chatgpt-users), [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91406385/openai-wants-to-transform-business-many-of-its-users-just-want-life-hacks), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/30/chatgpt-everything-to-know-about-the-ai-chatbot/). The 800 million threshold was not mentioned by any source.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event (statement of ≥800M WAU) occurred within the window. Therefore, no timestamp can be extracted for a Yes resolution.
evidence.step7_verification: Evidence is internally consistent. All sources across the September 2025 window report 700 million WAU, sourced from the September 15, 2025 OpenAI/NBER paper covering data through July 2025. No contradictory evidence suggesting a higher figure was found. The TechCrunch comprehensive article dated September 30, 2025 — the last day of the window — also states only 700 million WAU. No statement at 800 million or above was found in any source covering the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. All publicly attributable statements from OpenAI and named OpenAI executives within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window report 700 million weekly active users — well below the 800 million threshold required for a Yes resolution. The window closed on 2025-10-01 with no qualifying statement having appeared.

question: Israel x Turkey military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of Israel and Turkey between April 1, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between Isreali and Turkish military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots, artillery fire into uninhabited areas, or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution, however minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Israel and Turkey publicly announce, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, a new or expanded formal military deconfliction mechanism covering operations in Syria?
subquestions.background_information:
A direct Israel–Turkey military clash in 2025 would most plausibly arise from friction in or around Syria, where both states have active security interests and where analysts and officials have already discussed the risk of unwanted encounters. In spring 2025, Turkish and Israeli officials reportedly held talks in Baku aimed at creating a deconfliction mechanism for Syria, with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan saying the purpose was to prevent unwanted incidents. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz also publicly thanked Azerbaijan for mediating between Israel and Turkey over Syria, indicating that senior defense contacts on this issue were already underway before 2025-09-01. See Turkish Minute, 2025-05-19: https://www.turkishminute.com/2025/05/19/israeli-defense-minister-katz-thanks-azerbaijan-for-mediating-with-turkey-over-syria/ . Forbes also reported in May 2025 that the two countries had begun talks over a deconfliction mechanism because their aircraft could encounter each other in Syrian airspace, underscoring that military-to-military coordination is a live issue rather than a hypothetical one: https://www.forbes.com/sites/pauliddon/2025/05/12/the-risk-of-israeli-turkish-mock-dogfights-over-syria/ .

Tensions around southern Syria increased further in July 2025, when violence involving Druze communities prompted Israeli strikes and broader concern about regional spillover. Naharnet reported that the United States, Turkey, and Jordan helped mediate a ceasefire after clashes escalated and Israeli strikes hit Damascus, highlighting Turkey's relevance to crisis management in Syria: https://www.naharnet.com/stories/en/315000-syria-violence-brings-druze-communities-complex-cross-border-ties-to-the-fore . Analysts cited by VOA-affiliate coverage described the Israeli strikes as part of a wider regional power struggle involving Turkey and warned of growing alarm in Ankara: https://www.voanews.com/ .

This makes a publicly announced deconfliction mechanism a useful near-term indicator for the ultimate question. If both sides formalize or expand coordination, that is evidence they are actively reducing accidental-escalation risk; failure to do so, or breakdown of existing talks, would tend to point the other way.

Sources:
Turkish Minute - Israeli Defense Minister Katz thanks Azerbaijan for mediating with Turkey over Syria - https://www.turkishminute.com/2025/05/19/israeli-defense-minister-katz-thanks-azerbaijan-for-mediating-with-turkey-over-syria/
Forbes - The Risk Of Israeli-Turkish Mock Dogfights Over Syria - https://www.forbes.com/sites/pauliddon/2025/05/12/the-risk-of-israeli-turkish-mock-dogfights-over-syria/
Naharnet - Syria violence brings Druze communities' complex cross-border ties to the fore - https://www.naharnet.com/stories/en/315000-syria-violence-brings-druze-communities-complex-cross-border-ties-to-the-fore/
Voice of America - main site for relevant regional reporting - https://www.voanews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), at least one official public statement from the government of Israel and at least one official public statement from the government of Turkey announce the establishment, resumption, expansion, or formalization of a military deconfliction / coordination / hotline / incident-prevention mechanism specifically covering military operations in Syria.

For Yes, the announcement must be public and attributable to official government or military channels (for example: the Israeli Prime Minister's Office, Israeli Ministry of Defense, IDF, Turkish Presidency, Turkish Ministry of National Defense, or Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs). The statements do not need to use identical wording, but they must clearly refer to the same mechanism or arrangement.

Examples that count: announcement of a hotline between the two militaries for Syria; announcement that regular deconfliction meetings have been established; announcement that an existing channel has been expanded to cover air operations in Syria.

Examples that do not count: vague statements that the sides are 'in contact'; mediation offers by third countries without confirmation by both Israel and Turkey; unofficial media leaks with no official public confirmation; broader diplomatic talks not specifically about military incident prevention in Syria.

Primary sources for resolution will be official government websites and official social-media accounts:
- Israel Ministry of Defense: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/ministry_of_defense/govil-landing-page
- Israel Prime Minister's Office: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office
- Israel Defense Forces news: https://www.idf.il/en/
- Republic of Türkiye Ministry of National Defence: https://www.msb.gov.tr/
- Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Foreign Affairs: https://www.mfa.gov.tr/default.en.mfa
- Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye: https://www.tccb.gov.tr/en/

If official statements are ambiguous, corroboration may be taken from Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), or BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news), but a Yes still requires public official confirmation from both sides within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window.

If no such publicly announced bilateral mechanism is confirmed by both sides during 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 inclusive, resolve No. If relevant announcements are made only before 2025-09-01 or after 2025-10-01, they do not count. If source material becomes unavailable, archived versions of the same official pages or contemporaneous Reuters/AP/BBC reports quoting the official statements may be used as fallback evidence.
subquestions.rationale: This is a strong crux because Syria is the most likely theater for an accidental or deliberate Israel–Turkey encounter. A formal deconfliction mechanism would materially reduce the chance of a military clash later in 2025, while the absence of such a mechanism leaves a key escalation pathway open.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Both the Israeli government AND Turkish government must publicly announce (from official channels: Israeli PM Office, MoD, IDF, Turkish Presidency, MoD, or MFA) the establishment, resumption, expansion, or formalization of a bilateral military deconfliction/coordination/hotline/incident-prevention mechanism SPECIFICALLY covering military operations in Syria. Both governments must confirm the same mechanism. The window is 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 inclusive.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Israel Turkey military deconfliction mechanism Syria 2025' — to find direct evidence of such a mechanism being announced; 2. 'Israel Turkey hotline military coordination Syria announcement' — to find bilateral hotline or coordination announcement; 3. 'Israel Turkey deconfliction agreement Syria September 2025' — to narrow to the time window; 4. 'Israel Turkey relations diplomatic military talks Syria 2025' — broader search for bilateral military talks; 5. 'Turkey Israel talks de-escalation mechanism Syria official announcement' — to find official statements; 6. 'IDF Turkey military coordination Syria hotline September 2025' — IDF-specific search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key findings: (1) Multiple articles from September 14, 2025 (Yahoo News, CP24, Asharq Al-Awsat) mention that 'Turkey is pursuing deterrence and diplomacy, having held talks with Israel to establish a de-escalation mechanism in Syria' — but this is described as ongoing/prior talks, not a formal announcement of an established mechanism, and comes from media (not official government sources). (2) The dominant narrative during the window is of deep hostility between Israel and Turkey: Israel labeled Turkey a 'strategic threat'; Turkey called Israel 'the foremost threat'; Israel struck Turkish weapons stockpiles in Syria (Sept 9); Turkey is reportedly blocking the Israel-Syria security agreement (Sept 29). (3) No official government statement from either Israel or Turkey announcing a formal bilateral military deconfliction mechanism specifically for Syria was found. (4) The de-escalation talks found are between Israel and Syria (not Israel and Turkey), mediated by the US. (5) Turkey is actively hostile toward Israel during this period, including calls for sanctions and vetoing NATO participation.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: REJECTED: No candidate event satisfies all criteria. The September 14 reports mention 'talks' to establish a de-escalation mechanism, but: (a) this is described in past tense as ongoing talks, not a formal public announcement of an established mechanism; (b) the source is media analysis, not official government statements from both sides; (c) Israel and Turkey are in a deeply adversarial relationship during this window, with Turkey blocking Israeli-Syria agreements. The Israel-Syria de-escalation pact discussions (Sept 24) are between Israel and Syria, not Israel and Turkey. No official government announcement from both Israel AND Turkey of a bilateral military deconfliction mechanism for Syria was identified.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found. No official announcement from both sides within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found at all during the window — not just a 'first occurrence' issue.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence strongly supports No: (1) Israel labeled Turkey a 'strategic threat' (National Interest, Sept 16, citing Israeli intelligence assessments); (2) Turkey's Foreign Ministry declared 'Israel has become the foremost threat to the security of our region'; (3) Israel struck Turkish weapons stockpiles in Syria (Sept 9, bne IntelliNews); (4) Turkey is blocking the Israel-Syria security agreement (indyturk, Sept 29); (5) Erdogan called Netanyahu 'the biggest threat to the Middle East'; (6) Turkey denied Israeli reports it attacked Turkish equipment, but did not confirm any coordination mechanism. The bilateral relationship during September 2025 is described as being in its 'most perilous phase' with both sides 'openly acknowledging the possibility of military confrontation.' The only reference to 'talks to establish a de-escalation mechanism in Syria' between Israel and Turkey appears in media analysis (not official statements), in past/ongoing tense, and without any formal announcement.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying bilateral public announcement from both Israel and Turkey of a formal military deconfliction mechanism for Syria was made during September 1-October 1, 2025. To the contrary, the relationship is at its most adversarial in years, with Israel striking Turkish equipment in Syria and Turkey actively blocking Israeli agreements with Syria. Resolution: No.

question: Trump x Putin Meeting in Hungary by Dec 31?

A meeting is defined as any encounter where Trump and Putin are both present and interact with each other in person.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of State or the Russian Foreign Ministry publicly confirm, by 2025-11-17, that Marco Rubio and Sergey Lavrov (or their officially designated principals) held preparatory talks for a Trump-Putin meeting in Budapest?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin will meet in Hungary by the end of 2025 is whether their governments move from rhetorical intent to formal summit preparation. Multiple reports published on 2025-10-16 and 2025-10-17 state that, after a lengthy Trump-Putin phone call, both sides agreed to prepare a summit in Budapest and that preliminary talks between U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov were expected soon. TASS reported that preparations for a Budapest summit would begin "without delay" and that preliminary talks would begin between Lavrov and Rubio, citing Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov: https://tass.com/politics/1919441 . Other outlets also reported that a high-level advisors' meeting was expected the following week, including DNA India https://www.dnaindia.com/world/report-after-productive-phone-call-trump-to-meet-putin-in-hungary-to-discuss-war-in-ukraine-3161557 and Zee News https://www.zeenews.india.com/world/us-president-donald-trump-to-meet-putin-in-hungary-in-bid-to-end-russia-ukraine-war-2922589.html .

Such preparatory diplomacy is meaningfully different from the ultimate question itself: it does not ask whether Trump and Putin actually meet, but whether the bureaucratic and diplomatic machinery needed for a summit is visibly activated. Formal confirmation of Rubio-Lavrov talks would be evidence that both governments are devoting real resources to arranging a Hungary meeting, making the ultimate meeting more likely. Conversely, failure to publicly confirm any such preparatory talks by mid-November would be evidence against the summit occurring by year-end.

Authoritative public sources for this subquestion are available. The U.S. Department of State regularly publishes press statements and readouts at https://www.state.gov/press-releases/ and https://www.state.gov/briefings/ . Russia's Foreign Ministry publishes official statements and readouts at https://mid.ru/en/ .

Zee News - US President Donald Trump To Meet Putin In Hungary: https://www.zeenews.india.com/world/us-president-donald-trump-to-meet-putin-in-hungary-in-bid-to-end-russia-ukraine-war-2922589.html

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17 (inclusive), at least one official public statement, press release, transcript, readout, or briefing published by either the U.S. Department of State or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation explicitly confirms that Marco Rubio and Sergey Lavrov held talks, or that their officially designated principals held talks in their place, and that those talks concerned preparation for a Trump-Putin meeting or summit in Budapest/Hungary.

This question resolves No if no such official public confirmation is published between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17 (inclusive).

For purposes of resolution:
- "Officially designated principals" means other named officials explicitly stated in the same official source to be acting in place of Rubio or Lavrov for summit-preparation talks.
- "Publicly confirm" means the information appears in an official government communication on an official website, not merely in anonymous-source media reporting.
- The official source must explicitly connect the talks to preparation for a Trump-Putin meeting/summit and to Budapest or Hungary. General U.S.-Russia discussions, Ukraine talks, or unspecified bilateral calls do not count.
- If multiple official sources conflict, any clear qualifying confirmation from either government's official site is sufficient for Yes.
- If an announced meeting is postponed beyond 2025-11-17 without the talks actually occurring within the window, it does not count.
- If the relevant official pages are unavailable at resolution time, archived versions from the Internet Archive may be used as fallback evidence, provided the archived page clearly shows it originated from the official site.

Primary resolution sources:
- U.S. Department of State press releases: https://www.state.gov/press-releases/
- U.S. Department of State briefings/readouts: https://www.state.gov/briefings/
- Russian Foreign Ministry official site: https://mid.ru/en/

Fallback source:
- Internet Archive Wayback Machine: https://web.archive.org/
subquestions.rationale: A publicly confirmed Rubio-Lavrov preparatory channel would be strong evidence that the proposed Budapest summit is progressing from announcement to implementation. Summit logistics, agenda-setting, security coordination, and diplomatic alignment typically require such staff-level or ministerial groundwork. Therefore, this is a meaningful early indicator of whether a Trump-Putin meeting in Hungary is likely to occur by the ultimate deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: (1) Official statement from U.S. State Department OR Russian Foreign Ministry (not just media reporting); (2) Explicitly confirms Rubio and Lavrov (or designated principals) held talks; (3) Those talks explicitly connected to preparation for Trump-Putin meeting/summit in Budapest/Hungary; (4) Occurring between Oct 18–Nov 17, 2025.

evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: On October 20, 2025, Rubio and Lavrov held a phone call. The U.S. State Department (Principal Deputy Spokesperson Tommy Pigott) confirmed the call publicly.
